Twitch help

This guide holds Twitch’s own help, gathered from help.twitch.tv in November 2026. Twitch is a live streaming site, best known for games, music and talk shows. Its help is written mostly for people who stream: setting up a channel and a broadcast, chat and moderation, the Affiliate and Partner programs and how they pay, and keeping an account safe. Viewers will find the account, purchase and safety articles most useful.

Twitch’s help centre draws every page with script, so each page was drawn by Microsoft Edge before it was saved, and the gathering followed the links between articles. An article no other article links to may be missing. The categories are Twitch’s own, from the trail printed above each article. Legal pages such as terms of service are not part of the help centre and are not here.

The help text belongs to its publisher and is gathered here unchanged for accessible reading. This guide’s own arrangement and wording are available under CC BY-SA 4.0.

Affiliate Program

2k Streaming on Twitch

Upgrading to 2k (1440p) streaming offers a noticeable step up from 1080p streaming, with richer detail, improved clarity, and better performance—whether you’re gaming, making art, or just chatting. Higher quality streams unlock access to 2k Clips and VODs for you and your viewers, too.

2k streaming requires Enhanced Broadcasting and is limited to Partners and Affiliates. Trying to stream in 2k(1440p) without Enhanced Broadcasting will result in a worse streaming experience for your viewers.

For streamers who tried 2k in Beta – We’ve made big improvements to performance with added server-side transcode support, increased bitrates, and other updates. Click here to see what we’ve improved since the beta.

How to stream in 2k (1440p) on Twitch

Start streaming in 2k in 3 easy steps:
  • Make sure you meet the minimal system requirements for 2k streaming, listed in the table below.
  • Adjust your settings in OBS: In OBS 32.0 or newer, go to:
    • Settings > Video > Set canvas and output to at least 2560x1440
    • Settings > Stream > Check the “Enhanced Broadcasting” box under “Multitrack Streaming” to turn it on
  • You’re ready to stream in 2k! We recommend running a test stream during off hours to fine-tune your video settings and adjusting existing scenes as needed.

System Requirements For Optimal 2k(1440p) Streaming

Twitch Status

Affiliate or Partner

Broadcast Software

OBS Studio 32.0 (or newer)

GPU and Driver Version

  • NVIDIA GeForce 2000-series (or newer) with NVIDIA driver 550 (or newer)
  • AMD Radeon RX 6000 Series (or newer) with AMD Adrenalin 24.4.1 minimum
  • Apple M4 (or newer), Apple M1-M3 Max (or greater)
  • Intel Arc A580 (or newer)

Operating System

Windows 10/11, Linux, MacOS

Display

2560x1440 at 60fps

Upstream Bandwidth Bitrate

  • 20 Mbps no Enhanced Broadcasting added server-side transcode support.
  • 9 Mbps with Enhanced Broadcasting added server-side transcode support*

Not sure how to find information on your system requirements? Check the FAQ.

*Streamers with added Enhanced Broadcasting server-side transcode support can cut required upload bandwidth in half. Check your Advanced Broadcast Settings on the Stream Settings page in your Creator Dashboard to see if you have access to added server-side transcode support for Dual Format streams.

Set Up Tips and Troubleshooting for Streamers
  • Double check that you have the OBS version and GPU drivers that meet system requirements
  • If you’re simulcasting:
    • Set your Maximum Video Tracks to at least 3 or 4 to avoid encoder overload. To do this, go to OBS Settings > Stream > Multitrack Video > Maximum Video Tracks
    • If simulcasting to +3 different services and recording a local VOD, you may need to adjust your recording settings under Encoder Settings. If you lower the preset and increase the bitrate, your local VOD will be larger, but should maintain comparable quality. To do this, go to OBS Settings > Output > Recording > Preset > Select a Preset from the dropdown menu
  • Streaming a 2k (1440p) requires more bandwidth. If you’re experiencing frame drops, it may be because of your internet connection. You can reduce bandwidth by specifying a value for Maximum Streaming Bandwidth (used for all video tracks). To do this, go to OBS Settings > Stream > Maximum Streaming Bandwidth > Specify a minimum of 14,000 Kbps (14 Mbps).

Streamers and mods may wish to provide a chatbot command, pinned chat, or other easily accessible way for viewers to find this help article to learn more about the current capabilities and limitations of 2k streaming, ensuring they have the best viewing experience.

How will streaming in 2k impact your viewer’s watching experience?

2k streaming offers higher resolution viewing for your community, without the higher risk. 2k streaming on Twitch is powered by our Enhanced Broadcasting technology, which will automatically adjust the stream quality for users with limited bandwidth to prevent lagging and buffering, making sure all of your viewers get the best version of your stream. Since we have the data about your viewers’ bandwidth and system, we are able to make these adjustments for you to optimize your stream.

Viewers: How to watch streams in 2k (1440p) on Twitch

To see if a channel is streaming in 2k (1440p), hover over the stream and click the Settings icon on the theater to open settings. From there, select Quality to see all of the qualities available to you. If a channel is streaming in 2k, you will see 2k (1440p) in the list of qualities. Some viewers may not be able to select the 2k (1440p) quality option.

Why Can’t I see Some Qualities?

If a viewer can’t watch a stream in 2k, a message in the video quality settings menu will let them know why.

  • Location restriction: Higher resolution viewing is currently restricted in some regions. All viewers will still be able to watch in 1080p or lower. See a full list of regions with 2k viewing access here.
  • Device or settings issue: Viewers may need to update their browser or turn on hardware / graphics acceleration to see a stream in 2k. Check out the troubleshooting tips below.
  • Device or browser not supported: Certain computer set ups, TV devices, older mobile devices, and game consoles may not be able to support 2K(1440p) viewing at this time. Viewers will still be able to watch in 1080p.
  • You’re logged out: Higher resolution viewing is currently restricted to logged-in viewers. Logged-out viewers will still be able to watch in 1080p.
  • Streamer issues: If a streamer has not turned on Enhanced Broadcasting before going live, their viewers will not be able to select some quality variants and may have trouble viewing the stream. The streamer needs to end the stream and fix the issue.

If none of the above troubleshooting issues apply to you, and you’re still unable to watch the stream in 2k (1440p), try the advanced troubleshooting tips below.

Viewers: Why can’t I watch a stream in 2k on some devices? Troubleshooting
  • Update your browser, or try a different browser, such as Google Chrome
  • If you’re on Windows 10, you may need to install “HEVC Video Extensions” from the Microsoft app store
  • Enable hardware acceleration in your browser, if applicable. Hardware Acceleration (also known as graphics acceleration) allows certain computing tasks to be offloaded from your device’s CPU (central processing unit) to specialized hardware components, typically the GPU (graphical processing unit). Turning on hardware acceleration may solve issues viewing 2k (1440p) content on Twitch. To enable hardware acceleration in Twitch’s supported browsers:
    • Google Chrome (Recommended) - Settings > System > Use graphics acceleration when available
    • Mozilla Firefox - Settings > Performance > Use recommended performance settings (or make sure “use hardware acceleration when available” is checked)
    • Opera and Opera GX - Settings > System and performance> Use graphics acceleration when available
    • Apple Safari - Safari automatically manages hardware acceleration. There is no setting to enable or disable

Improvements We’ve Made to 2k Streaming Since Beta

We’ve made several improvements to the 2k Streaming experience since we first started testing in Beta. If you tried it out during beta, give 2k another try and share your feedback with us on the experience! We recommend testing it out for two to three streams before sharing feedback. Join the 2k and Dual Format Enhanced Broadcasting Discord to share your feedback and get support from staff and other 2k streamers.

  • We’ve added Server-Side Transcode Support for 2k Enhanced Broadcasting streams to offset the strain caused by client-side encoding. 2K streams use Enhanced Broadcasting, which encodes multiple quality variants from your broadcast software. To reduce strain on your system and improve performance, Twitch also provides added server-side transcode support for these streams for Partners and select Affiliates. This added server-side transcode support lets us utilize your GPU to encode the highest-resolution horizontal and vertical streams, while using server-side transcoding to fill in all the lower resolutions. Ultimately, this results in your viewers getting a higher-quality experience across all formats. Check your Advanced Broadcast Settings on the Stream Settings page in your Creator Dashboard to see if you have access to added server-side transcode support for 2k and Dual Format streams.
  • Improved viewing experience on Living Room devices (TV, Game Consoles): Viewing limitations on older living room devices has been a known limitation. The majority of our viewers are not watching Twitch on Living Room devices, but we know that negative feedback from even a few of your viewers in chat can be distracting, so we’re invested in improving this. While some limitations still persist, the team has made meaningful improvements to the experience since June 2025, and we want to know if you see the changes.
    • Please note: 2k streams still do not work for viewers watching on PS4 devices. Viewers on PS4 devices will see an error message that directs them to view your channel on a different device, but this impacts less than 1% of viewers on living room devices.
  • Clips Updates: We rolled out full 2k Clip and VOD support for 2k streams. You can now create 2k clips by using the Quick Actions button in stream manager and with third-party integrations.
  • Expanded Regions: We’ve added support for 2k viewing in a few additional countries. As a reminder, if a viewer is watching your 2k stream in a region that does not have 2k viewing support, they will still be able to see your stream in 1080p. The full list of supported 2k viewing regions can be seen here.
  • Increased Bitrates: We increased bitrates from 7.5 Mbps to 9 Mbps for 2k (1440p) HEVC and from 6 Mbps to 7.5 Mbps for 1080p AVC, when streaming in 2k using Enhanced Broadcasting on Twitch.
  • Key Bug Fixes and finalizing our full list of feature updates, like supporting 2k Clips and VODs.

Known Limitations:

  • Watching 2k streams on certain game consoles or TV apps may be limited: Watching 2k streams may not be available on select game consoles or TV apps. Viewers will still be able to watch streams in 1080p or lower on these consoles or apps.
  • Viewers watching 2k streams in certain regions may be limited to 1080p or lower. They can still see your stream, they just may be limited to lower qualities. These viewers will be notified of why they can’t see the 2k version of your stream when they click on the video quality settings.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is eligible to stream in 2k?
All Partners and Affiliates on Twitch are eligible to stream in 2k. Enhanced Broadcasting is required to enable 2k (1440p) streams, and Partners and select Affiliates will benefit from added server-side transcode support to optimize performance when streaming in 2k. Please follow the set up instructions in the article above to get started.
Is Twitch increasing bitrates for 2k?
Yes, we’ve increased the recommended bitrate from 6 Mbps for 1080p to 7.5 Mbps for 2k (1440p) stream. For streamers who configure their own settings to go above the recommended bitrate with AVC, the newer HEVC codec will allow us to deliver higher quality video at 7.5 Mbps than you would get with your existing settings today. So while the increase in bitrates is modest, the impact to your video quality will be meaningful. And, there’s no need to customize bitrate settings manually. Enhanced Broadcasting automatically configures your stream settings for you to ensure that your viewers experience the least buffering and best visual quality possible given your GPU and network.
What is added server-side transcode support?

Dual Format and 2K streams use Enhanced Broadcasting, which encodes multiple quality variants from your broadcast software. To reduce strain on your system and improve performance, Twitch also provides added server-side transcode support for these streams for Partners and select Affiliates. This added server-side transcode support lets us utilize your GPU to encode the highest-resolution horizontal and vertical streams, while using server-side transcoding to fill in all the lower resolutions. Ultimately, this results in your viewers getting a higher-quality experience across all formats.

Check your Advanced Broadcast Settings on the Stream Settings page in your Creator Dashboard to see if you have access to added server-side transcode support for Dual Format and 2k streams.

How will I know if I qualify for this additional transcode support for 2k Streams?

All Partners and select Affiliates will qualify for additional transcode support for 2k Streams using Enhanced Broadcasting. Check your Advanced Broadcast Settings on the Stream Settings page in your Creator Dashboard to see if you have access to added server-side transcode support for Dual Format streams.

Please note that this added server-side transcode support is specific to Dual Format and 2k streams that use Enhanced Broadcasting and is entirely separate from transcode support for any other regular stream. Read more about transcode support for regular streams.

Why can’t everyone have access to added server-side transcode support for 2k and Dual Format Streams?
These resources are limited. We do our best to provide additional server-side transcode support to as many 2k and Dual Format streams as possible. However, not every stream on Twitch will have this added support, and we can only guarantee it for Partners at this time. Check your eligibility status for added transcode support in stream settings.
If I qualify for transcode support, will I benefit from this transcode support on every stream?

Yes, if you qualify for transcode support, you will have the added server-side transcode support on every 2k and/or Dual Format Enhanced Broadcasting stream. It will not be available for regular non-enhanced-broadcasting streams or Enhanced Broadcasting streams that are not in 2k or Dual Format. For those streams, your standard transcode support will apply. Read more about transcode support for regular streams.

Please note: Twitch may stop providing added transcode support for your 2k or Dual Format streams for select reasons, such as if you are inactive for long periods of time or lose Partner or Affiliate status. You can always check your access to added transcode support for Dual Format and 2k streams in your Stream Settings.

I have additional transcode support but I still experienced performance issues during my stream. Why is that happening?
  • Double check your qualification by visiting your Advanced Broadcast Settings on the Stream Settings page in your Creator Dashboard.
  • Some performance issues may not be related to Enhanced Broadcasting or 2k and may be caused by temporary issues with your network provider.
Does 2k streaming always require Enhanced Broadcasting?
Yes. 2k streaming always requires using Enhanced Broadcasting, even if you have added server-side transcode support.
Will my VODs and Clips be available in 2k?
Yes. Please note that the 2k quality version of your VOD will expire 7 days after your stream, after which the 1080p quality version will be available for the remainder of your existing retention period (60 day retention for Prime, Turbo, and Partners and 14 day retention for Affiliates). Clips from 2k streams will be available in 2k quality and will not expire.
Will all of my viewers be able to watch my stream if I stream in 2k?
All viewers will be able to watch your stream, they just may not be able to see the 1440p quality and will see your stream in 1080p. Regions that currently have 2k viewing access include:
  • NA: United States, Canada
  • EMEA: Germany, Austria, Switzerland, United Kingdom, Ireland, France, Belgium, Netherlands, Luxembourg, Denmark, Finland, Norway, Sweden, Italy, Spain, Andorra, Portugal
  • MENA: KSA, UAE, Qatar, Kuwait
  • LATAM: All Latin American countries
  • APAC: Japan, Australia, and New Zealand
Why is the ability to watch streams in 2k quality limited to certain regions?
As we consider expanding access to 2k streaming on Twitch, we want to take a cautious approach that allows us to learn about the impact of 2k streaming and viewing on Twitch at scale before we consider extending 2k viewing access to more regions over time. All of your viewers will still be able to see your stream, they just may be limited to watching in 1080p or lower if watching in select regions.
Can I multistream / simulcast when streaming in 2k?

Yes. You can still stream to an existing restreaming service to enable restreaming to any other platforms in addition to streaming directly to Twitch with ERTMP. This may introduce more encoding overhead on your local system, but streamers with modern GPUs should be capable of doing this without any negative side effects.

We have also added server-side transcode support for Partners and select Affiliates using 2k streaming with Enhanced Broadcasting. This added server-side transcode support still requires Enhanced Broadcasting but lets us utilize your GPU to encode the highest-resolution horizontal and vertical streams, while using server-side transcoding to fill in all the lower resolutions. Ultimately, this results in your viewers getting a higher-quality experience across all formats. Check your Advanced Broadcast Settings on the Stream Settings page in your Creator Dashboard to see if you have access to added server-side transcode support for Dual Format and 2k streams.

How will streaming in 2k impact my system? Will it cause delays and buffering?

Modern GPUs have a dedicated chip just for video encoding, so they can handle it without slowing down your games. When you use your GPU (graphics card) for video encoding, it does not significantly affect gaming or stream performance. Even with older GPUs like the NVIDIA GeForce 900 series, our testers played fast-paced games and didn’t notice any difference in performance.

To reduce strain on your system and improve performance, Twitch also provides added server-side transcode support for Partners and select Affiliates when streaming in 2k with Enhanced Broadcasting. This added server-side transcode support lets us utilize your GPU to encode the highest-resolution horizontal and vertical streams, while using server-side transcoding to fill in all the lower resolutions. Ultimately, this results in your viewers getting a higher-quality experience across all formats. Check your Advanced Broadcast Settings on the Stream Settings page in your Creator Dashboard to see if you have access to added server-side transcode support for Dual Format and 2k streams.

Can I stream in 2k from mobile?
Most mobile streaming set ups likely do not meet the system requirements above. 2k streaming is possible on mobile with the use of 3p tools like IRLToolkit.
How do I find out what GPU and driver I have?
On Windows, right click the task bar on the bottom of your screen and open task manager. Click the icon on the left that shows a square with a squiggly line. Then click GPU to see your GPU information at the top of the task manager.
How can I find out which operating system I have?
On Windows, open the start menu and click the Windows button in the bottom-left corner of your screen. Click the Settings icon to open settings, click on “system”, and scroll down to click on “about”. Under “windows specifications” you’ll be able to find the edition and version of your Windows operating system.
Does Twitch offer 4k or AV1?
We do not offer 4k or AV1 streaming at this time. It may be something we consider down the line.
How will my viewers know if I’m streaming in 2k?
Viewers will see a 2k (1440p) source quality badge when they first land on your channel page and when hovering over the stream. Viewers can always check the source quality by clicking into the quality settings on web and mobile. Some viewers may not be able to watch your stream in 2k and will see your stream in 1080p or the next best quality available to them.

About Emote Prefix Changes

Emotes are small pictures that can be sent in chat or used around Twitch. An emote’s prefix, or code, goes just before the emote name, and is randomly generated once your channel gains access to emotes. Streamers who have completed onboarding, and Affiliates can update their prefix once every name change. Emote prefixes are randomly generated based on your new username. This article explains how to update your Emote prefix.

Partners can update their prefix once every 60 days.

On this page:

  • Updating your Emote Prefix
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Updating your Emote Prefix

As an Affiliate, if you have ever undergone a username change, you may undergo a one-time Emote prefix change to match your new username. This prefix is randomly generated based on your new username. You are eligible to do this once for every username change. To do this:

  • Head to your dashboard and click the icon to open the menu. Click Viewer Rewards, then Emotes under Subscriber Emotes. If you’re eligible to update your emote prefix, you will be able to click the Update Prefix dropdown.
  • You will be shown a preview of your new prefix when you click on Update Prefix. Click Confirm Prefix Update to accept your updated prefix.
  • You will receive a confirmation if and when your prefix is successfully updated.

Frequently Asked Questions

How often can I update my prefix?
Monetized streamers and Affiliates,may update their Emote prefix once per username change. Usernames may be changed once every 60 days.
Why can’t I choose my own prefix?
Self chosen prefixes are reserved as a Partner-only benefit.
I don’t like my new, updated prefix. Can I change it back?
No. Prefix changes are permanent. You may only update your prefix again if you change your username, you cannot revert it back to the previous one.
Can I request a new prefix by contacting Twitch Support?
Unfortunately, in this case there are no exceptions as self-chosen prefixes are reserved as a Partner-only benefit. Tell us how we can improve Affiliate/Partner benefits by sharing your feedback in UserVoice.
Why don’t I have the option to change my Emote prefix under the Subscriber Emotes in my Dashboard?
It will only appear if you are eligible to update your Emote prefix. You will be eligible for a one time change every time you have changed your Twitch username.

About Spendable Balance

Twitch offers all streamers, including those who have not yet achieved Affiliate or Partner status, access to select monetization and community building tools, including Bits, subs, emotes, badges, and Channel Points. By enrolling in Spendable Balance, qualifying streamers, Partners, and Affiliates can put the support they receive back into their own communities, or support other channels they love. Use Spendable Balance towards eligible purchases including gift subs, recurring subscriptions, Bits, and Turbo. Enrollment is always optional, and reversible.

Enrolling your payout balance into spendable earnings is a reportable tax event. Learn more.

How to Enroll in Spendable Balance

To enroll, you must meet the following criteria:

  • Complete creator onboarding, and sign the Monetized Streamer Agreement.
  • Ensure onboarding information is accurate, and you have completed a valid tax interview.

If you meet these conditions, click here to visit your Creator Dashboard payout setting.

Read each step carefully. You have successfully enrolled when you see Spendable Balance in the payout dashboard.

If you change your mind, return to your payout settings. You can opt-out from Spendable Balance at any time. Once you opt-out, you will no longer be able to use your Spendable Balance on Twitch until you enroll again.

If you already have balance: After verifying successful enrollment, you’ll see your Spendable Balance as an available payment option during checkout of eligible items. Spendable Balance can be used on Twitch on desktop, or mobile web checkout.

If you don’t yet have balance: Learn more about the features available to monetized streamers here.

Frequently Asked Questions

Where is Spendable Balance available?
Spendable Balance is available globally to all qualifying monetized streamers.
Why would I enroll in Spendable Balance?
With Spendable Balance, you can use the balance reflected on your Creator Dashboard from your Bits and subs. Spendable Balance allows you to purchase gift subs, recurring subscriptions, Bits, and Turbo to support your community and the creators you love.

If you are not yet an Affiliate or Partner, you can also choose to grow your balance and get paid out automatically once you reach Affiliate status and hit your minimum payout threshold if you prefer.

Using your Spendable Balance is completely optional, subject to the limitations in the Monetized Streamer Agreement.

How can I opt-out? What happens when I opt-out?
You can opt out from your payout settings here. When you opt out, you can no longer use your Spendable Balance towards eligible purchases on Twitch.
Am I obligated to report Spendable Balance on my taxes?
Support transferred to Spendable Balance is subject to US Informational tax reporting, meaning you may receive a tax form at the end of the year. You are obligated to ensure you’ve provided Twitch with accurate, current onboarding and tax information. A tax professional will be best suited to support you in your unique situation. Twitch cannot provide personalized tax guidance.
I am a former Twitch Partner or Affiliate– How can I check if I have balance to spend?
If you were once enrolled in the Twitch Partner or Affiliate programs, and wish to spend any accrued balance on Twitch, you must:
  • Contact Twitch Support to rejoin the Affiliate Program. Former Partners rejoin as Affiliates. If you were removed from a program by Twitch, your eligibility to rejoin may be restricted.
  • Complete onboarding, and add a successful payout method.
Can I save on payout fees when purchasing through Spendable Balance?
By purchasing using your Spendable balance, you can avoid payout fees that are usually associated with your selected payout method and conversion fees at the time of payout. Conversion fee savings are not applicable to creators in the US. Learn more about payment method fees here.
After I enroll, how soon can I spend my balance?
If you already have balance: The first time you successfully enroll in Spendable Balance, your current payout balance will be spendable. If you remove yourself from Spendable Balance, your Spendable Balance is no longer usable at checkout, effective immediately.
I’m enrolled, and just received some support, how soon can I spend it?

Affiliates and Partners only: After you successfully enroll, support events on your channel such as Bits, Subs, or Ads contribute to your Spendable Balance along the same Net 15 cycle that calculates your earnings payout, if you have elected to receive your payout.

For example*, let’s say you have $35 USD in your current payout balance. When you enroll in Spendable Balance for the first time, you should now have $35 USD available in your Spendable Balance. Now, let’s say the next time you stream, a generous soul gifts 100 subs. When will the revenue from those 100 gift subs be available in your Spendable Balance?

The answer depends on if you have chosen to receive payouts, and when in the month this support is received.

If you choose to automatically receive funds as a payout (if above payout threshold), revenue from the 100 Gift Sub support event will not be added to your Spendable Balance. Instead, that revenue will contribute to your payout balance, causing it to exceed the $50 minimum payout threshold. As a result, you will receive the entirety of your payout balance as a single payout in the middle of the next month. In this scenario, you’ll see a lock icon next to your Spendable Balance in your Payout Dashboard. This icon indicates your balance cannot be spent, as it will be included in an upcoming payment that is still being processed and finalized.

If you choose to keep funds as a Spendable Balance on Twitch, revenue from the 100 Gift Sub support event will be added to your Spendable Balance in the middle of next month.

You can manage this preference in your Creator Dashboard revenue settings.

*Example scenario (100 Gift Sub price) given assumes US-based creator and USD subscription prices.

It is expected that you may see the 100 Gift Sub event in your Earnings Analytics, even if you do not see it reflected in your Spendable Balance. Earnings Analytics provides an estimate of revenue earned throughout the current month. It is not a final statement of creator earnings.

How do I use Spendable Balance on Twitch purchases?

Choose to apply your Spendable Balance during checkout of eligible purchases. If you don’t have enough Spendable Balance to complete the purchase, you can add an additional payment method like a credit or debit card.

For recurring subscriptions and Turbo: If you choose to pay with Spendable Balance, your renewal will be charged to your Spendable Balance first. If your balance doesn’t fully cover the renewal, the remaining amount will be charged to your saved payment method. You can change how a specific subscription is charged (Spendable Balance or saved payment method) from your Subscription Management page without canceling.

Do I need to have a stored payment method (like a credit or debit card) to use Spendable Balance on Twitch purchases?
Yes, you need to have a stored payment method to use Spendable Balance for purchases, including recurring subscriptions. If your Spendable Balance doesn’t fully cover a recurring renewal, the remaining amount will be charged to your saved payment method. To add a saved payment method, see Adding a Payment Method.
Is there a limit to how much Spendable Balance can be stored?
Spendable Balance and gift card balance share a storage limit of $2,000 USD.
Is there a limit to how much Spendable Balance can be spent?
Spendable Balance and gift card balance share a spending limit of $2,000 USD per day.
Does Twitch run experiments or promotional offers with Spendable Balance?
From time to time, Twitch may test promotional offers connected to Spendable Balance, such as earning a rewards balance when you make eligible purchases using your Spendable Balance. These offers are experimental, may differ between creators, and may change or end at any time.

If you receive a rewards balance from a promotional offer, you can use it toward eligible Twitch purchases in the same way as Spendable Balance, but it cannot be paid out. Availability and terms are determined by Twitch and are subject to the applicable offer terms.

Affiliate Onboarding Guide

Congrats on being invited to the Affiliate program! This article is your companion for first-time Affiliate Onboarding. From start to finish, Affiliate Onboarding can take as little as 10 minutes, depending on verification checks.

If you have questions throughout this process, contact Twitch Support here.

What are you trying to do?

  • Complete onboarding (first time) → Follow the step-by-step guide below
  • I’m stuck on a step → See Troubleshooting: I’m Stuck
  • I don’t understand a tax form field → See Amazon Tax Information Interview Guide
  • I need to update my information → See Updating Your Information
  • I have questions about payouts → See Affiliate Program FAQ

Before You Begin

Speed up your onboarding by preparing the following information: legal name, date of birth, country of residence, desired payout method, and tax identification number (if applicable).

Congrats on completing your Path to Affiliate achievements! You’ve been invited to apply to the Affiliate program.

To begin, click your invitation. Or, visit your Creator Dashboard → Monetization → Affiliate.

Affiliate Onboarding involves three steps:

  • Enable Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)
  • Complete Your Account Detail
  • Start Earning Revenue

All three steps must be fully completed in order to begin monetizing your channel.

Already completed creator onboarding? If you previously completed your monetization setup (Set Up Tools) before receiving your Affiliate invite, Step 2 may already show as complete with your information carried over. Verify your details are correct, then proceed with Steps 1 and 3. The tax interviews and payout method in Step 3 are new — these were not part of your initial setup.

You may have monetization features enabled on a maximum of 5 accounts. If you exceed this limit, monetization features will be removed from your accounts with the least activity.

Step 1 — Enable Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)

Affiliates and Partners are required to use Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) for account security. If you already have 2FA enabled on your account, this step will show as complete and you can skip to Step 2.

If you don’t have 2FA enabled, click Enable and follow the prompts to add a phone number and verify your identity.

If you experience issues enabling 2FA (such as not receiving a verification code, or an error about your phone number being used on another account), see our Two-Factor Authentication guide for troubleshooting steps.

Once 2FA is enabled, you’ll see a green checkmark next to Step 1 and can proceed.

Step 2 — Complete Your Account Detail

Click Set Up to open the Account Detail form. Here you’ll provide your personal information and agree to the Twitch Monetized Streamer Agreement.

You’ll be asked to fill out:

  • Legal Full Name — Your first name, middle name (optional), and last name. This must match the name on your tax documents.
  • Email — Pre-filled from your account. You can edit this if needed.
  • Business Name (optional) — For business tax reporting only. Match your business name to your tax filings and payout method.
  • Country of Residence — Select your country.
  • Date of Birth — Enter your date of birth. If this field appears locked, you’ve previously verified your age with Twitch. See Date of Birth Changes to learn how to update it.
  • Monetized Streamer Agreement — Read and agree to the Twitch Monetized Streamer Agreement. If you are over 13 but under 18, your parent or legal guardian must agree on your behalf.

Common issue — mismatched details: The information you enter here (name, address, country) carries forward to your tax interviews and payout setup in Step 3. Mismatches between these areas are the most common cause of issues during onboarding. Enter your information accurately and use the same details throughout the entire process.

Issues with special characters or non-US address formats? If the form has trouble accepting your legal name with accents, hyphens, or special characters (é, ñ, ö, etc.), contact Twitch Support. You must use your legal name and address exactly as they appear on your tax documents — do not alter or change them to match the form.

Once you’ve completed all fields and agreed to the Monetized Streamer Agreement, Step 2 will show as complete with a green checkmark.

Browser autofill tip: If you use browser autofill to populate form fields, the Continue button may not appear. Try manually editing at least one character in any field to activate the button.

Step 3 — Start Earning Revenue

Click Set Up to begin. Step 3 has multiple parts:

  • Tax Interviews (one or more, depending on your region)
  • Payout Method

All items must show a completed status before onboarding is finished.

Tax Interviews

Twitch is a subsidiary of Amazon. We use certain Amazon tools to help Affiliates get paid, including the tax information forms in the onboarding process. Please refer to the Amazon Tax Information Interview Guide if you need help with the definitions for any individual field.

You’ll see one or more tax interviews listed (such as Royalty Tax Interview and Service Tax Interview). Depending on your region, you may see additional required interviews (e.g., DAC7 for EU-based streamers). Complete all interviews that appear for your account.

Click Start next to a tax interview to begin. You may be asked to re-authenticate (log in again and enter a verification code). This is normal — you’re handling sensitive personal information, so Twitch adds extra security at this stage.

You’ll then see a screen asking you to authorize Amazon Tax Central to access your account. This is expected — Twitch uses Amazon tools for tax processing.

After authorizing, you’ll be taken to the tax interview form. You’ll be asked about your tax classification, residency status, and tax identity information.

The tax interview form is managed by Amazon and may look different from Twitch. This is expected. Twitch Support cannot provide tax advice or help you fill out the form. For field-by-field guidance, see the Amazon Tax Information Interview Guide. If you need tax advice, contact a local tax professional.

Once you complete a tax interview, you’ll see a validation screen confirming your information has been received.

Exit the interview and return to the Creator Dashboard. You’ll see the completed interview marked with a green checkmark. Continue with any remaining interviews.

In some cases, a subsequent tax interview may not require you to fill out additional information if your details from a previous interview carry over. Complete whatever the form asks you to do.

Processing Timeline:

  • Tax forms typically take 24-48 hours to validate
  • In some cases, validation can take up to 72 hours (3 days)
  • If your forms are still processing after 72 hours, wait 2-3 weeks for validation to complete
  • This process cannot be expedited

If there is a problem, the interview status will update to Incomplete, Pending, or Failed. A failed status typically means the information provided could not be verified. See Troubleshooting: I’m Stuck for next steps.

Tips For Success:

  • Contact support if tax form validation is pending for more than 3 weeks. Twitch Support is unable to provide resolution for cases less than 2-3 weeks old.
  • Twitch is unable to give tax advice. If you need help filling in either tax information interview, contact your local tax professional.
  • EU residents, learn more about DAC7 requirements and how they impact you here.
  • CA residents, learn more about Canada Tax Interview requirements and how they impact you here.
Payout Method

After completing your tax interviews, click Select next to Payout Method. You may need to confirm your password before proceeding.

First, you’ll be asked to verify your information. Some fields may be pre-filled from the details you entered in Step 2. Confirm that your information is accurate.

Data consistency reminder: Ensure the name and details shown here match what you entered in Step 2 and in your tax interviews. Mismatches between these areas can cause payout issues.

Next, choose a payout method. Twitch uses a third-party payment processor for payouts. The processor charges a transaction fee each time you are paid, as well as for rejected payouts resulting from incorrect information. Fees vary by payout method. See fees here.

Available payout methods include:

  • Direct Deposit / ACH
  • Check
  • Wire Transfer
  • PayPal
  • Hold Payouts

Available methods may vary depending on your region.

Our payout processor requires a minimum balance for payout. The minimum amount for most payout methods is $50, and $100 for wire transfer. Learn more in Payout Balance FAQ.

Choose Hold Payouts if you want to control how often you are paid and consolidate transaction fees. Otherwise, you will be paid automatically with the method you select.

This section may also ask you to submit a scanned copy of your government ID such as a passport.

Onboarding Complete!

Once you’ve completed all three steps, you’ll see a “Welcome to the Affiliate fam!” confirmation. Congratulations — you can now begin monetizing your channel!

Optional Next Steps

Streamer Community Survey

You may be invited to fill out a quick Streamer Community Survey. This is optional and can be taken later from your Creator Dashboard settings. The survey helps Twitch learn more about who you are so we can source you for opportunities in the future.

Enroll in Spendable Balance

After completing onboarding, you may see an option to enroll in Spendable Balance. By enrolling, you can use your balance from creator activity to buy Bits and gift subs. This is optional and you can always change this setting later. Learn more about Spendable Balance.

Updating Your Information

If you need to update your name, address, tax information, or payout method after completing onboarding, you can edit your information directly.

Visit your Creator Dashboard → Monetization → Affiliate to view and edit your current details.

Common reasons to update your information:

  • You need to update your legal name, address, or tax information
  • You made an error in your tax interview
  • Your life circumstances changed (moved, name change, etc.)
  • You need to change your payout method

Payouts begin processing before the 15th of each month. If you need to update your payout information, it’s best to do so before the 10th of the month to avoid delays. If you have earned revenue or a payout pending and you’re unsure about timing, contact Twitch Support before making changes.

Troubleshooting: I’m Stuck

If you’re experiencing issues during onboarding, use this section to identify your problem and find a solution.

Form Won’t Submit / Getting an Error

If your form won’t submit or you’re seeing an error message, try these technical troubleshooting steps:

  • Try a private/incognito browser tab — This disables extensions and clears temporary data that might interfere.
  • Disable browser extensions — Ad blockers and privacy extensions can interfere with forms. Disable them temporarily.
  • Clear your cache and cookies — Then close and reopen your browser.
  • Try a different browser — Use Chrome, Firefox, or Edge if you’re having issues.

If issues persist after troubleshooting, contact Twitch Support.

Issues with special characters or non-US address formats? If the form has trouble accepting your legal name with accents, hyphens, or special characters, or if your address doesn’t fit US formatting, contact Twitch Support. You must use your legal name and address exactly as they appear on your tax documents — do not alter or change them to match the form.

Processing Status Confusion

If you’re waiting for your tax interview or identity verification to process:

Typical processing times:

  • Tax interview processing: 24-48 hours, up to 72 hours in some cases
  • Identity verification: 24-48 hours

When to contact support:

  • Tax interview has been processing for more than 3 weeks
  • Identity verification has been processing for more than 48 hours
  • You’re seeing an error message that won’t resolve

If you’re unsure about your processing status, contact Twitch Support.

Payout Verification Taking Longer?

If you are stuck in the payout verification step, try using an alternate payout method. If you prefer not to change the payout method, wait up to 48 hours for verification to complete. Contact support if you have been waiting more than 48 hours.

Issues With Zip Code Fields?

If you’re having trouble filling in zip code information during payout setup, this usually occurs because your payout method requires zip/postal code information that wasn’t provided in earlier steps.

You have two options:

  • Choose a different payment method that doesn’t require a zip code
  • Update your information in Step 2 to include a zip code, then return to payout setup

More Resources

Upgrading to Partner? If you’ve received a Partner invite, the process is much shorter — your account details and payout information carry over from Affiliate. See the Partner Onboarding Guide for details.

Have questions about Affiliate eligibility or requirements? See Joining the Affiliate Program.

Need help? Visit our comprehensive Affiliate Program FAQ.

Visit our Affiliate Settings Walkthrough.

Learn more about Spendable Balance.

Affiliate Settings Guide

Congratulations, new Affiliate! This article provides an overview of the various settings and customizations available to Twitch Affiliates.

Getting There

You must be an Affiliate to view Affiliate Settings.

Affiliate settings are located in the Creator Dashboard:

  • Click your avatar in the upper-right corner of twitch.tv
  • Select Creator Dashboard
  • In the left-nav menu, select Settings -> Affiliate

Onboarding

Onboarding to the Affiliate program allows you to monetize your channel. Manage or modify your payout information in this section.

Completing onboarding for the first time? Check our walkthrough here: link.twitch.tv/AffiliateOnboardingHelp

Affiliate Onboarding

To update your address or personal information (email, etc.), edit your details directly from your Creator Dashboard → Monetization → Affiliate. To redo a tax interview, use the Retake option next to the relevant interview. You do not need to restart onboarding. For more information, please see our Affiliate Onboarding Guide.

Most Affiliates should not need to redo their onboarding unless their personal information has changed.

Change Payout Method

You can change your payout method here. For information on how to do this, the payout methods we support, or general payout queries, please see our Affiliate Payout FAQ.

View Monetized Streamer Agreement

Here, you can view the Monetized Streamer Agreement. This agreement sets the terms that enable you to earn money from monetization programs such as the Affiliate program.

Subscriptions

Subscriptions are one of the monetization tools available to Affiliates and Partners. Visit your subscription settings in the Creator Dashboard under the Monetization section. Here, you can customize your subscriber benefits.

Visit Creator Camp to learn more about the monetization tools available to streamers: twitch.tv/creatorcamp/en/paths/monetize-your-content/twitch-basics/

Subscription Names

Here you can set a custom name to refer to your subscription product. This can be edited at any point, does not require approval to show immediately, and can include any characters. Explicit words and hate speech are prohibited - the Subscription name must comply with our Terms of Service and Community Guidelines.

These names appear to subscribers during checkout with some payment providers. The names also appear in a subscriber’s purchase history page.

Emotes

Uploading your first emotes? Visit our Emote Guidelines

Emotes are the language of Twitch. Your supporters can unlock custom emotes for actions such as Following, Cheering, or Subscribing to your channel.

Upload, modify, or remove emotes for your subscribers, followers, or Bits supporters here: dashboard.twitch.tv/viewer-rewards/emotes

If you have ever undergone a username change, you may use the Emote page to undergo a one-time emote prefix change to match your new username. You are eligible to do this once for every username change. For more information, please see our help article.

Subscriber Badges

You can upload custom badges to denote subscribers and their subscription length here. Unlike emotes, badges only appear in your channel and do not require manual approval before they appear to your audience. For more information about subscriber badges, please see our Subscriber Badge Guide.

Ad-Free Viewing

Toggle this option to allow subscribers to watch your channel ad free.

If you enable ad-free viewing for subscribers, your ad revenue will be calculated based only on the number of non-subscribed viewer impressions when you ran the ad. When the ad-free option is enabled, channel Subscribers will not be included in the impression counts used to calculate ad revenue. However, Turbo Subscribers who are also channel subscribers do count as ad impressions contributing towards ad revenue.

With ad-free viewing for subscribers enabled, you should only see a minimal change in ad revenue. This minimal change will be balanced by higher subscription rates as viewers see the added value of their purchase. You can also fine-tune your ad revenue by adjusting the timing and frequency of the ads you play during your streams or choosing to opt-out of offering ad-free viewing for subscribers on your channel.

Ignore Slow Mode

Toggle this option to allow subscribers to bypass slow mode. Your chat moderators will always be immune to this mode.

Subscriber-only Chat

Toggle this option to only allow subscribers to chat in your channel. This setting can also be toggled via chat commands (/subscribers and /subscribersoff) from the Affiliate or their moderators. Your chat moderators will always be immune to this mode.

Subscriber-only Archives

Toggle this option to only allow subscribers to view your past broadcasts and highlights.

Channel owners and editors may make clips from VODs when this setting is enabled. This change was made in part thanks to your feedback. Visit us in UserVoice.

Bits & Cheering

This section is located in your Monetization preferences, in the Creator Dashboard. Here, configure and customize Bits & Cheering for your channel.

Learn more about monetization tools available to your channel in Creator Camp: twitch.tv/creatorcamp/en/paths/monetize-your-content/

Minimum Bits to Cheer

This is the smallest total of Bits that a cheer must meet in order to cheer on your channel. For example, setting this to 50 would mean that the sum total of the Bits used in your channel must be equal or greater to this amount.

Minimum Bits Emote

This is the smallest individual Bit Emote that can be used to cheer on your channel. For example, setting this to 50 would mean that no individual Bit Emotes under 50 (1, 25, etc) could be used in your channel.

Enable/Disable Pins

Disable or enable pinned cheers. This setting is enabled by default.

Minimum Threshold to Pin

By default, the minimum threshold to pin is 100 Bits, or the amount selected in Minimum Bits to Cheer (whichever is higher). You can lower this setting, which will lower your Minimum Bits to Cheer.

For further info on both of these settings, please mouse over the ‘i’ icon next to each one.

Bits Tier Badges

Here you can upload, modify, or remove custom Bits badges for viewers that reach cheering milestones on your channel. Unlike your subscriber emotes, badges can only appear on your channel and do not require manual approval before they become available to your audience. Your Bits badges must abide by our Terms of Service and Community Guidelines. For more information, please see our Custom Bit Badges Guide. To upload or remove Bits Tier Emotes, head to our Emote page via Viewer Rewards -> Emotes on the left-hand sidebar.

Community

This section is located in your Monetization preferences, in your Creator Dashboard. Here, you may configure options that allow you to provide recognition and give back to supporters of your channel.

Hype Train

This menu allows you to customize various settings and enable or disable the Hype Train feature. For a full rundown of these settings, please see our Hype Train Guide.

Leaderboards

This menu provides the option to enable or disable the leaderboard that displays Top Cheerers and Top Gifters at the top of your chat.

Ads

This section is located in your Monetization preferences in the Creator Dashboard.

Ads Manager

The Ads toggle enables your ads schedule that you set within the Ads Manager. Visit your Ads Manager for easier ads scheduling during your stream, or learn more in our guide: help.twitch.tv/s/article/ads-manager

Preroll Ads

This option allows you to disable or enable prerolls when you run midroll ads on your channel.

Preroll Notifications

This toggle dictates whether or not you receive dashboard alerts when preroll ads are disabled/enabled on your channel.

For more information about preroll and midroll ads, please see our Disabling Prerolls article.

Stream Display Ads

This toggle controls whether Stream Display Ads are shown on your channel. For more information, visit help.twitch.tv/s/article/stream-display-ads

Revenue share for Advertisements

Earn up to 55% net ad revenue for running 3 minutes of ads per hour or more. Learn more about Ads Manager.

More Resources
