Amazon Tax Information Interview and IRS Annual Reporting FAQ

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

Tax Information For US Creators
Do I need Twitch’s EIN?
The tax interview is asking for your tax information, including your tax identification number. We do not require you to input Twitch’s EIN. For more information on tax identification numbers, please consult your tax advisor.
I am a U.S. individual or I represent a U.S. company. Do I need to give you my tax information?
Twitch requires all U.S. payees, including non-profit and tax-exempt organizations, to provide their U.S. taxpayer information through our short online tax interview accessible from the Dashboard. You will be required to provide your U.S. tax identification number.
  • Your nine-digit federal tax identification number is your Social Security Number (SSN),
  • Employer Identification Number (EIN), or
  • Individual Tax Identification Number (ITIN)
What is a U.S. Tax Identification Number (EIN or SSN)?
A U.S. Tax Identification Number (TIN) is issued by the IRS and can be a Social Security Number (SSN), Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN), or Employer Identification Number (EIN). For U.S. persons, this is typically an SSN (generally for individuals) or EIN (generally for companies). For non-U.S. persons, this may be an ITIN (generally for individuals) or EIN (generally for companies). For more information on tax identification numbers, please consult your tax advisor.
Why does my tax information show as invalid?
Twitch does not have insight into the details about why information is invalid, but here are some common examples:
  • Misspelling your name, not including your middle initial or middle name, or entering an incorrect Tax Identification Number (TIN) may cause tax identity information to not match IRS records.
  • Use the name and TIN that appear on your Social Security card [SSN], CP565 notice [ITIN], or CP575A notice [EIN], if applicable.
  • If you are providing an EIN, use the name that appears on the top line of the address header on your CP575A notice from the IRS if you are providing a business name.
What name should I provide during the tax information interview?
You should provide the name of the individual or organization that will report the income on an income tax return. The name on the tax forms should also agree with the name on the signed legal contract and payment information.

If you are completing the information as an organization, use the name as it appears as follows:

  • Trust – The name as it appears on the trust deed
  • Partnership – The name as it appears in the partnership agreement
  • Corporation – The name as it appears in the certificate of incorporation, or other legal document that formed the corporation
  • Other - The name as it appears on the legal document that formed the entity

You are not a “partnership” merely because you are a Partner at Twitch.

How do you determine the rate of withholding tax, if any?
The U.S. IRS requires Twitch to collect up to 30% from payments issued to non-U.S. persons who receive certain payments. Any applicable withholding tax will automatically be deducted from your payment(s).
Do I have to consent to provide an electronic signature?
Electronic signature is not required. However, if you consent to an electronic signature, you will be able to certify, sign and submit your form electronically.

If you do not provide consent, you will be required to print a hard copy of your IRS Form W-8 or Form W-9, sign with blue or black ink, and mail to the address provided.

Please note that consenting to electronic signature allows Twitch to validate your information in real-time, which generally enables you to have your tax information and account processed immediately. If you do not consent to electronic signature, it can take up to seven to ten business days after receipt of the form before processing.

When will I get my annual IRS Form(s) 1099, 1042, and/or DAC7 reporting form?

This FAQ is relevant for Twitch Affiliates and Partners only.

Consult your tax advisor with questions about required tax forms for your unique situation.

Annual Form(s) 1099 and/or the DAC7 reporting form (EU-based streamers) are available on or before January 31 of the following calendar year via snail mail as the form will be postmarked on or before January 31 and will be sent to the physical address that you have provided in your Twitch onboarding process. If you have consented to electronic delivery and successfully logged into Tax Central, on or before January 31 of the following year, you will receive an email from Twitch with instructions on how to retrieve your forms.

Annual Form 1042-S is available on or before March 15 of the following calendar year via snail mail as the form will be postmarked on or before March 15 and will be sent to the physical address that you have provided in your Twitch onboarding process. If you have consented to electronic delivery and successfully logged into Tax Central, on or before March 15 of the following year, you will receive an email from Twitch with instructions on how to retrieve your Form 1042-S.

If you have any questions about the “agent acting as an intermediary” status, please contact your tax advisor.

How do I get my annual IRS Form 1099-MISC or Form 1042-S electronically?

Manage Amazon Tax Central’s connection to your Twitch account from your account connections page at twitch.tv/settings/connections. You can read Twitch’s Privacy Policy here.

  • Click here to go to your Channel Analytics dashboard. (Or, from twitch.tv, click your portrait, select Creator Dashboard -> Insights -> Channel Analytics).
  • From your Channel Analytics dashboard, visit your payout history by clicking here or by clicking View My Payouts.
  • Click View Tax Forms.
  • Depending on the nature of your agreement with Twitch and the type of revenue you received, you may receive one (1) or two (2) separate tax forms. Many creators who earned reportable income in the form of royalty and service income will receive two (2) separate forms. These creators’ royalty income will be reported on Form 1099-MISC and their service income will be reported on Form 1099-NEC. Please download forms one at a time. Some creators may only receive one form.
  • To access these tax forms electronically, you must authorize Amazon Tax Central to access your Twitch account. If you have not done this, a pop-up will ask you to give permission. Once you have authorized Amazon Tax Central to access your Twitch account, click “Find Forms” and select the document under the Download link.
Tax Information For Non-US Creators

Providers outside of the United States may be required to complete additional tax interviews in accordance with the laws in their region.

What is a Foreign Tax Identification Number?
A foreign tax identification number is issued by your local tax authority and is used for income tax reporting purposes. Canadian individuals, for example, are given a Social Insurance Number. If your local tax authority does not issue an income tax identification number, a U.S. TIN must be provided if you wish to claim a reduced rate of withholding tax under a tax treaty. For individuals claiming treaty benefits, this is an ITIN. For non-individuals claiming treaty benefits, this is an EIN. You can apply for an ITIN or EIN with the IRS.
I am a non-U.S. individual or I represent a non-U.S. company. Do I need to give you my tax information?
Twitch requires all non-U.S. payees to provide valid taxpayer identification information by taking the tax information interview to certify your non-U.S. status by completing IRS Form W-8 or Form 8233. A taxpayer identification number (TIN) is not required unless you wish to claim a reduced rate of withholding tax.

In addition to the U.S. information provided, Providers outside of the U.S. may be required to complete additional tax interviews in accordance with the laws in their region.

General Tax FAQ
Why do I have to take online tax interviews?
Twitch requires all providers (eg. Partners, Affiliates, and streamers with onboarding complete and a signed Monetized Streamer Agreement (“MSA”) ) — including U.S. and non-U.S., non-profit or tax-exempt organizations—to provide valid taxpayer identity information in order to comply with U.S. and international tax reporting regulations.

U.S Service and Royalty tax interviews collect tax identity information on Form W-9 or W-8. Twitch is legally required to collect from creators it pays. The information collected from these tax interviews is used to determine what informational tax reporting and witholding tax may apply to a creator if they are eligible for payments, or transfers of spendable balance into creator wallet. If you do not complete the tax interview, or allow the tax interview information to expire, a default withholding tax of up to 30% may apply to your future payments, until the tax interview is completed/updated as necessary.

Creators outside of the United States may be required to complete additional tax interviews in order for Twitch to meet its international informational tax reporting obligations as required by law. These additional tax interviews appear in your the Monetization -> Affiliate/Partner/Setup -> Onboarding section of your Creator Dashboard.

How do I access or retake the interview?
If you need to retake the interview, you can log into your Twitch account. Once logged in, head to the Monetization section under your Dashboard or click here. Find the relevant tax interview and click the Retake option next to it. You do not need to restart onboarding to retake a tax interview.
My tax form says “failed”, what should I do?
If your tax form shows “failed,” this typically means the information provided could not be verified. Do not contact Twitch Support for tax issues. Instead:
  • Review the information you provided for accuracy (name, address, etc)
  • Ensure your name matches exactly what appears on your tax documents
  • Retake the tax interview with corrected information
  • For specific tax questions, consult a tax professional
I am a content partner with Twitch, does that mean I am considered a “partnership”?
The tax interview is asking whether you are an individual or a certain type of legal entity (for example, a corporation, partnership, or other legal entity type). You are not a “partnership” merely because you are a Partner at Twitch. Please evaluate whether you are answering the interview questions on behalf of yourself as an individual, or on behalf of an entity, like a corporation or partnership. If you have any questions on whether you are a “partnership”, please consult your tax advisor.
I am completing the interview for a company. Does that mean I am an “agent”?
Generally, an “agent acting as an intermediary” refers to a business or individual that will receive income on behalf of another person. Merely completing the tax interview on behalf of a company does not necessarily make you an agent. We have provided a couple of examples for your convenience:
  • Example 1: For services payments, a company (or individual) could potentially be an “agent acting as an intermediary” where they are receiving payments for services someone else is providing, as an agent for that person. However, a company (or individual) would typically not be an “agent acting as an intermediary” if they simply hire a subcontractor.
  • Example 2: For royalties, a company (or individual) would typically be considered an agent if they receive payment for the use of copyrights or content which are owned by clients of the company (or individual).
I’m a partner that hasn’t received their tax form for 2015 and beyond, what do I do?
First, make sure that you have your address up to date on the Amazon tax interview. You can retake the interview by visiting your Partner settings page.

After you have completed that, please log in to taxcentral.amazon.com with your existing account under that same email address, or create a new account under that email address if one does not already exist, click View/Edit next to one of your forms, and then finally click Contact Us at the top of the page for a number of helpful FAQs and information.

I received an email saying I needed to complete the tax interview and 30 minutes later I got an email saying my information has been completed, but I did not do anything. What does this mean?
When we introduced our automated tax identity collection process, an email was sent to all active partners. However, you already had validated tax information on file and we were able to update this in our system. When we updated the system, it triggered the second email to notify you that the interview was complete. At this time, no further action is required from you.

Important: Twitch does not provide tax guidance or support for tax form issues. For tax form failures, errors, or questions, please consult a tax professional or review this comprehensive tax guide.

Analytics Overview

Analytics empowers you with the data to understand what’s working and what’s not so you can make informed decisions about how to improve your content, grow your audience, and hit your streaming goals. The Analytics in your Creator Dashboard are spread across 6 pages designed to answer the most common questions streamers have about their performance:

Analytics

Overview page

Track your overall performance at a glance for the last 30 days, or set a custom date range to compare progress over time. Learn More or See Your Stats.

Research page

Plan your upcoming streams with the global Twitch data that is surfaced on this page. Gain insight into panels like Time to Stream to learn what is the best day and time to stream in a specific category. Learn more or View Your Stats.

Stream Summary page

After each of your streams, review a summary snapshot that includes performance stats, audience insights, top clips, progress towards achievements, and more. Learn More or See Your Summary

Achievements page

Track your progress! Learn More or See Your Achievements

Viewers

Discovery page

Understand where your viewers come from and how they discover your channel. Experiment with promoting yourself on different platforms or try some new tags and check back here to see what drives the most visits to your streams. Learn More or View Your Stats.

Engagement page

Learn how viewers engage with your content and other content across Twitch to uncover opportunities to collab with other streamers or try out a new category. Learn More or Visit Now.

Revenue

Earnings page

See how much you earn on Twitch, get a breakdown of your revenue sources, and take a look back at your payout history. Learn More or See Your Earnings

Stream data throughout your Analytics is displayed in your local time zone, with an exception to the Earnings page. Subscription data on the Earnings page is displayed in UTC to match payouts which are UTC based

Browse through these pages and share any feedback or suggestions with us on UserVoice.

What’s in My Overview Page?

Your Analytics Overview provides a top-level snapshot of your recent streams, milestones, top clips, and progress towards achievements. If you’d like to drill down into more specific info, visit other pages in your Analytics. Visit Now.

By default, your Overview will show you data from the last 30 days. Clicking the arrows on the left and right of the current date will adjust the date back or forward by 30 days. To choose a custom date range, click on the date picker in the center and select a start and end date using the calendar that pops up.

  • Achievements Progress - Achievements help streamers who want to grow transparently track their progress and stay motivated as they stream. If you’re working towards Affiliate or Partner, we’ll show the achievements relevant to those goals in the Stream Summary.
  • Top Clips - Review up to five top clips from your stream. The top clip of the stream is also included at the top of your Stream Summary. You can click on any clip to view it.
  • Stream Stats Chart - Review detailed metrics on your recent stream activity. Read on for more info.
  • Milestones - Keep track of your progress on your streamer milestones here!
The Stats Chart

This section breaks down and provides a short overview of the different parts of the Stats Chart.

Stats

Clicking on these tabs will adjust the graph to show the selected stats. Your currently selected tab will be underlined.

Clicking the arrows on the right hand side of each field allows you to display additional types of data.

If you hover your mouse over the stats bars, additional contextual information can appear. The stats available are as follows:

Average Viewers

The average number of concurrent viewers in your stream. To calculate this number, we check how many viewers there are at each point in time when you are live. The stat in the top bar is an average of this number across all the time streamed in the selected date range.

Live Views

The total views of your live streams. It does not include VOD or clip views.

Follows

The follows your channel received in the selected date range.

Subscriptions

The number of subscriptions you received. Mousing over the graph will display further information about the type of subscription, including the subscription tier and whether it is a gifted or Prime sub.

Revenue

The total revenue gained. Mousing over the graph will display a breakdown of the estimated revenue received from each source. Refunds are also included in this calculation. Learn more about your payout balance in our knowledge guide here: link.twitch.tv/PayoutBalance

Minutes Watched

The total time your live stream was watched across all of your viewers.

Time Streamed

The total time that you have broadcasted for.

Max Viewers

The maximum number of viewers that you reached across all of your streams in the selected date range.

Unique Viewers

The number of unique people who viewed your live streams across the selected date range. (If a viewer watched 3 of your streams in this time period, they would count once in this calculation.)

Raid Viewers

The percentage of your viewers that came from Raids.

Unique Chatters

The number of unique viewers who chatted across the selected date range.

Chat Messages

The total number of chat messages sent.

Clips Created

The number of clips created from your streams.

Clip Views

The total views on the clips created from your streams.

Ad Breaks

The total duration of the ad breaks that you ran during streams.

Ad Time Per Hour

The average amount of time per hour that ads were running during your streams.

Promotion Impressions

The total number of times your stream’s video card was viewed while in a promotional placement.

Promotion Clicks

The total number of times your stream’s video card was clicked while in a promotional placement.

Time Detail Selection

Clicking on the drop down menu on the right hand side of the stats graph will give you the option to choose to view the selected data in Days, Weeks or Months.

Graph

When you choose a stat from the tabs above, the graph shows how that stat changed over time for the selected date range and time detail. Mousing over each bar on the graph gives a more detailed breakdown.

Export Data

This button will allow you to download a report of your data that matches the selected graph.

Category Suggestions

Deciding what categories to stream in can be challenging, especially for creators trying to reach new viewers. Category Suggestions show you categories with favorable Avg. Viewer:channel ratios that may increase your chance of being discovered. These categories are ranked by factors such as:

  • Average hours viewed versus average hours broadcast in the past 7 days

  • Similar categories to the ones you watch

  • Estimated browse position

  • A - Whether you enjoy playing different games, or are simply trying to grow your viewership, category suggestions can help you make a decision. Suggestions are based on the previous 7 days, and should refresh daily.

    • Avg Viewers:Channels - The ratio of average viewers to the number of channels streaming in that category over the past 7 days. This excludes outliers like large Partners. The higher this ratio, the better! That means it’s a category loved by many viewers, but not streamed by many channels.
    • Avg Channels - The average number of channels that streamed in this category per day over the past 7 days.
    • Est. Browse Position - An estimate of where your stream might show up on the Browse page when sorted from high to low, based on your average viewers from the last 30 days. If you haven’t streamed in the last 30 days, there isn’t enough data and this metric will show as N/A.

  • B - Filter a wide variety of game categories by genre (pending availability)

  • C - By default, the language filter will be updated to match the broadcast language set for your stream. If we don’t detect a broadcast language for you, we’ll show you All Languages. Learn More.

  • D - Explore suggestions using the arrow keys

If you don’t wish to see Category Suggestions, you can collapse the panel by clicking the 3 Vertical Dots menu icon.

Questions Answered by Your Analytics Overview

Below your revenue information, there are several panels that try to answer common questions that you may have about your channel and statistics. These include:

What were my streams during this period?

The Streams panel displays a list of your streams during the selected date range (up to 180 days back). Clicking a stream takes you to the corresponding stream summary.

What were my top clips?

Your Top Clips panel shows your top clips sorted by view count over the selected time period. Clicking View Details will bring you to your Clips page.

Providing Feedback

To send us feedback, click the ? on the top right of the page and then click Send Feedback. We are not able to respond to all feedback, but we review every item that comes in and use it to improve your dashboard.

Frequently Asked Questions

What else can I learn with Analytics?

Dive in by visiting your Analytics, or click here for an overview.

Where can I leave feedback on Analytics?

Browse these pages and let us know your feedback or suggestions in UserVoice.

Where can I view my stats and insights for just one stream?

You can view per-stream stats and insights on the Stream Summary page.

What time zones are used on the Analytics Overview?

Stream data in your Analytics Overview is displayed in your local time zone.

Does the subscription purchase location information include Prime subs?

Yes. This information includes paid and Prime subscription purchases.

Why can’t I see subscription purchase summaries in my dashboard?

To see purchase location information creators must have enough subscriptions from at least two countries.

Why isn’t there enough data to display for category suggestions?

If you see the below error message, it is likely that:

  • You haven’t streamed enough for us to show you any data
  • You have not recently streamed in a gaming category
  • The genre you selected may be too restrictive, or you’ve encountered an unexpected error

What is an outlier, and how do you exclude it from category suggestions?

Large streams with viewership in the top 5% of a category are considered outliers, and are not factored into Avg. Viewers: Channels ratios.

Why are my category suggestions all video games?

While we know there’s no one way to stream on Twitch, we’re not able to give suggestions on non-gaming categories just yet. This may change in the future as we learn more from this experiment! To be eligible for this experiment, you must have recently streamed in a gaming category.

How do you decide what categories to suggest?

We present suggestions based on favorable viewer:channel ratios that may result in more viewership to your stream.

Can I request access to experiments?

No, sorry. Experiments are available to a limited number of channels. As we learn more about how category suggestions help you, we may expand access.

Animated Emotes

Creators will be able to upload these emotes from the Emotes page (like you do for emotes today). Here are the details you’ll need to create an animated emote:

  • The image you upload should be sized as either a single GIF for auto-resize mode (between 112x112px and 4096x4096px) or 3 GIFs (28x28px, 56x56px, 112x112px) for manual mode (when auto-resize is turned off)
  • GIF images must be square shape (e.g., same pixel height and width)
  • 1MB file size max for auto-resize mode. If using manual mode, each of the file sizes cannot exceed 512KB
  • Thumbnail for the animated emote will default to the first frame of the GIF. If you want to create a different thumbnail, this can be overridden with a custom static image (same requirements as emotes)
  • GIF images cannot be more than 60 frames
  • Must not flash or flicker more than 3 times within a 1 second period

On this page:

  • Uploading Animated Emotes
  • Easy Animate
  • Emote Slots
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Uploading Animated Emotes

With Auto-resize on, we will take 1 GIF and resize it for you. If you prefer to upload each size separately, you can toggle Auto-resize off. The upload process for animated emotes will be like the upload process for emotes today:

Auto-Resize Mode:

Auto-resize mode is the default upload experience and allows you to upload an animated .GIF between 112x112px and 4096x4096px which is then converted into all the required sizes for you. Auto-resize mode uses the first frame of each .GIF as the static image. To manually set your static image, click on Use custom thumbnails instead to upload.

Within the Enter Emote Name field, choose a name for your emote (e.g: Love). Your emote’s full code will be your emote prefix combined with your emote code (e.g.: prefix + Love = prefixLove).

Once you’ve uploaded your files and selected your code, click Upload. Your emote will be saved to your Library. If you uploaded directly into a slot, it will be assigned to that slot by default.

Manual Mode:

Deactivating auto-resize mode allows you to upload three separate sizes (28x28, 56x56, 112x112px) rather than having them automatically scaled. If the automatic conversions made via auto-resize mode are not to your liking and you want more control on each of the sizes, manual mode allows for image-by-image control for each size. Any missing images will mean your animated emote will not go live.

Within the Enter Emote Name field, choose a name for your emote (e.g: Love). Your emote’s full code will be your emote prefix combined with your emote code (e.g: prefix + Love = prefixLove).

Once you’ve uploaded your files and selected your code, click Upload. Your emote will be saved to your Library. If you uploaded directly into a slot, it will be assigned to that slot by default.

After uploading, your emote will need to be manually reviewed and approved before it’s visible to viewers. While awaiting review, it will be grayed out, shown as Pending Approval with a watch icon. Partners in Good Standing and Affiliates who meet certain criteria are eligible for instant emote upload, which means your emotes go live right away — no manual review needed. Check our Emote Guidelines for eligibility details.

Android users will see emotes animated throughout the app. We are still working to bring the animated experience to iOS users.

Easy Animate

Selecting Easy Animate allows you to apply an animation to a standard emote that you may already have. Similar to uploading a standard emote:

  • Upload a .png with a resolution between 112x112px and 4096x4096px
  • Maximum file size is 1MB
  • .png images must be square shape
  • The image must not be animated

Click the Upload icon within the square on the left-hand side to select the appropriate file. This file will then be automatically converted into our other required sizes.

Next, select an animation from the Choose Animation dropdown. The animation template will then be applied to the emote as a preview. Feel free to try them all!

Shake

Rave

Roll

Spin

Slide In

Slide Out

Within the Enter Emote Name field, choose a name for your emote (e.g: Love). Your emote’s full code will be your emote prefix combined with your emote code (e.g: prefix + Love = prefixLove).

Once you’ve uploaded your files, chosen an animation, and selected your code, click Upload. If you uploaded directly into a slot, it will be assigned to that slot by default.

After uploading, your emote will need to be manually reviewed and approved before it’s visible to viewers. While awaiting review, it will show as Pending Approval with a watch icon. Partners in Good Standing and Affiliates who meet certain criteria are eligible for instant emote upload, which means your emotes go live right away — no manual review needed. Check our Emote Guidelines for eligibility details.

As always, if you’re looking for a place to start, you still have access to our Default Emotes.

Emote Slots

There will be additional slots for animated emotes, which can be offered as tiered subscription benefits via the Emotes page. These slots cannot be used for non-animated emotes.

Partners and Affiliates earn 2 additional Tier 1 animated emote slots for 60 days if they utilize Twitch’s Alerts. If Twitch’s Alerts are not utilized on stream for 60 days, the additional emote slots are removed. Every time Twitch’s Alerts are used on stream, the 60-day countdown is reset. Learn more.

Partners

Partners can earn up to 60 animated emote slots through Tier 1 subscriptions, plus 5 animated emote slots dedicated to Tier 2 subscriptions and another 5 dedicated to Tier 3. This allows you to offer special animated emotes as a benefit of a higher tiered subscription. These slots cannot be used for non-animated emotes.

Partners can earn 2 additional Tier 1 animated emote slots for 60 days if they utilize Twitch’s Alerts. Get Started

Affiliates

Affiliates start with 5 additional slots for animated emotes. Then have the ability to unlock up to 20 total.

Affiliates can earn 2 additional Tier 1 animated emote slots for 60 days if they utilize Twitch’s Alerts. Get Started.

Frequently Asked Questions

Learn more about Bonus Animated Emotes with Twitch’s Alerts.

How do I turn off animation for animated emotes?
As a viewer, you can open chat settings (on web) or stream settings (on Android) and toggle Emote Animations to an off position. Turning this setting off on the Web experience will turn it off on Android and vice versa.
Why was my animated emote removed?
Animated emotes must follow the Twitch Terms of Service, and our Emote Guidelines. Learn more.
Why are my emotes pending?
If you don’t have Instant Upload Eligibility, all emotes are then manually checked by humans which can sometimes take a few days to be reviewed - especially when you’re uploading all your new animated emotes at once!

Artist Badge and Attribution

The Artist Badge allows creators to give artists in their community the recognition they deserve! This feature introduces the ability for creators to assign channel-specific badges to artists and the ability to attribute artists to their channel emotes.

Creators: Emote Attribution

Creators can attribute emotes on their channel to the artists who created them. Once an artist is assigned to an emote, their Twitch username is displayed, and the channel is linked in the emote details card that opens when a viewer clicks the emote in chat.

Artists who have turned off attributions will not have their username displayed on the details card of emotes they have received attributes for.

Creators can assign emote attribution when uploading a new emote or by modifying an existing emote in the Emote Manager of the Creator Dashboard.

Creators: Artist Chat Badge

The Artist Badge is another way for creators to show their support for the artists who have contributed to their channel’s brand/style. Each creator can assign up to five (5) Artist Badges to artists who have created emotes, overlays, avatars, and more for the channel.

The Artist Badge will only appear next to the artist’s username in chat on the creator’s channel who granted them the badge unless the artist hides it.

Creators can add/manage badge assignments to artists in the Role Manager of the Creator Dashboard.

Artists: Managing Attributions

Artists can control their emote attributions on a global or individual channel level. Artists can disable emote attribution on Twitch, which will prevent any creator from assigning an emote to them. Artists can also turn off emote attributions for specific channels, which would prevent that creator from assigning any emote to that artist. Managing emote attributions is done through the Emote Attribution in your account settings.

Emote attributions on Twitch are enabled by default.

Artists need to have a Twitch account to have attributions assigned to them. so consider using your Twitch profile to let others know about your work.

Frequently Asked Questions

Sections:
  • General FAQs
  • Creator FAQs
  • Artist FAQs
General FAQs

Where is the emote’s attribution displayed?

Viewers who click on an emote in chat will see the attributed artist in the emote details card.

Where is the Artist Badge displayed?

This badge is only visible on the creator’s channel who assigned the badge.

Is the Artist Badge restricted to emote artists?

We realize creators source more than emotes from artists for their channel, including overlays, avatars, and more. The Artist Badge allows creators to assign a channel level badge to up to five artists who have contributed to their channel’s brand/style.

Creator FAQs

Which emotes can I assign to artists?

Creators can attribute their subscriber, and follower emotes.

How many emote attributions do each creator get?

There is no limit to the number of artists a creator can attribute to the emotes on their channel; however, each individual emotes can only be attributed to one artist.

Can an artist be assigned to an emote and receive an Artist Badge?

Yes, an artist can be attributed to an emote and granted the Artist Badge. Artist Badges are limited to five artists per channel.

Can I assign an emote to an artist that doesn’t have a Twitch account?

No, if the artist does not have a Twitch account, they will need to create one to be able to receive emote attributions.

Artist FAQs

How do artists review their attributed emotes?

Artists can visit the Emote Attribution page in the settings to see and manage their emote attributions.

Are artists notified when they receive emote attribution or the artist badges?

When a creator attributes an emote to an artist, the artist will receive a notification on Twitch that asks them to review and approve the attribution. After an artist has been granted the Artist Badge, they will see a notification in chat the first time they visit the creator’s channel.

Can artists turn off attributions?

Yes, artists can turn off emote attributions both globally and to specific channels in their account settings.

Branded Content Guidelines

Branded content is any content produced by streamers featuring products or services based on an exchange of value, such as being paid or receiving goods or services. Sometimes these types of deals are referred to as paid product placements, endorsements or sponsorships.

Examples of branded content on Twitch include:

  • Product placements
  • Endorsements
  • Sponsored gameplay
  • Paid product unboxings
  • Channel sponsorships
  • Branded channel panels
  • Brand logo stream overlays

Branded content on Twitch is not:

  • Wearing your favorite t-shirt that happens to feature a brand or product
  • Showing off a new piece of equipment you bought for yourself
  • Talking about your favorite restaurants within your community

Remember, something of value must be exchanged between you and a third party to qualify as branded content.

To make it easy and straightforward to let viewers know a stream includes branded content, we’ve added the branded content disclosure tool to the Creator Dashboard.

If you are producing branded content on Twitch, you must

  • Use the branded content disclosure tool
  • Ensure the products or services you are promoting are permitted

We recognize that some streamers have long-term partnerships with brands, or might have incidental branding from products in the background of their stream. We do not expect streamers to use the branded content tool unless the branded content is a central and intentional element of the livestream.

Examples of when you do not need to use the branded content tool:

  • Your offline channel page has panels promoting a brand or sponsorship.
  • You have merchandise, memorabilia, or other products in your camera view but are not being paid to actively discuss or promote them.
  • You or your mods share affiliate links in response to questions from your community.
  • You mention a sponsor in passing, but are not actively promoting the product or service in exchange for payment.

As with all content on Twitch, your branded content and the brands, products, and services you represent must comply with the Twitch Terms of Service and Community Guidelines.

To ensure streamers have time to adjust to using this new tool, we will not start enforcing its use until July 1, 2023.

(1) Branded Content Disclosure Tool

The Branded Content Disclosure tool in your Stream Manager enables you to easily notify your community that your stream includes branded content. To use the disclosure tool:

  • Click Edit Stream Info in Stream Manager
  • Check Branded Content

By selecting Branded Content in Stream Manager, you will enable an automated disclosure message on your stream, and stream archives shown below.

(2) Prohibited Branded Content Categories

Some products and services aren’t suitable for promotion on Twitch because they pose a risk to members of our community.

We do not allow promotion of products and services prohibited by our Community Guidelines such as:

  • Hateful Products or Services, such as products that promote hateful stereotypes or include offensive slurs
  • Illegal Products and Services, such as selling, advertising, or trafficking drugs, firearms, counterfeit goods, or other illegal goods and services
  • Risky Gambling Products, such as promoting online slots or roulette websites
  • Unauthorized Sharing of Private Information, such as products or services to look up private information, such as phone number and home address
  • Spam, Scams, and Other Malicious Conduct, such as hacking, phishing, or malware services, or services that disrupt Twitch services (including viewbotting, fake account creation, or selling Twitch accounts)

Additionally, we do not allow the following products and services:

  • Weapons, such as firearms, explosives, and related products
  • Adult-oriented products or services, such as pornography, sexual content, or male enhancement products. Reproductive health services are allowed.
  • Tobacco and tobacco related products, such as cigarettes, e-cigarettes, vape pens, and chewing tobacco
  • Certain financial products and services, such as Initial Coin Offerings (ICOs), multilevel marketing and get rich quick schemes, and payday loans
  • Medical facilities and products, such as prescription drugs, medical trials, pharmacies, miracle cures, and drug treatment centers
  • Political content, including paid promotion of politicians, political parties, or issues of public debate
  • Cannabis-related products, including vaping and delivery

Finally, we allow branded content for certain products and services, but with some restriction, including:

  • Alcohol, products must be marked as mature content

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I know if there is branded content in my stream?
Branded content is any content on your channel that is produced for a brand for an exchange of value. The exchange of value could be monetary or through free products and services. Examples of branded content include product placements or endorsements such as sponsored gameplay or product unboxing, and sponsorships that require a brand panel on your channel page or a logo overlaid in your stream. Twitch cannot “pre-approve” your content. When in doubt ask yourself whether you have received anything of value in exchange for the content you are sharing. If the answer is no, you do not need to use the disclosure tool. There is no penalty for erring on the side of caution, and using the disclosure tool if you are unsure.
Do I have to use the disclosure tool if I have branded content in my stream?
Yes, you need to use the tool if you have branded content in your stream so we can facilitate a written disclosure to your viewers. To use the tool, click on “Edit Stream Info” in Stream Manager. Scroll down to “Branded Content” and check the checkbox.
Can I contact Twitch any other way to let them know I have branded content on my stream?
No. To disclose branded content on your stream, follow the steps outlined previously. Any other method of notifying Twitch about branded content on your stream will not be accepted. This includes emailing Twitch, or contacting Twitch via any other method.
Why do I need to disclose branded content in the stream?
When you use this tool to indicate that your stream includes branded content, we show a disclosure message on your stream informing viewers about commercial content in your stream. This standardizes the way viewers are informed of these commercial relationships, which increases clarity and transparency about why you are showing that content on your stream. Further, disclosing branded content is necessary to comply with regulations in certain jurisdictions, although using the tool will not always be sufficient to meet legal disclosure obligations (see below).
Does using the disclosure tool ensure that I have satisfied all my legal obligations regarding branded content and disclosures?
No. While Twitch’s tool may help to meet certain disclosure obligations in that it will provide a message to viewers regarding the presence of branded content on your stream, you and the brands you work with are responsible for understanding and complying with with all applicable laws and regulations for branded content, including how and when to disclose the commercial nature of the content.
What happens when I disclose my branded content?
When you declare that there is branded content in your stream by using the tool, we will automatically show a disclosure message to viewers that tells them the stream “includes paid promotion.” The disclosure message will show on screen when a viewer joins the stream and persists for 10 seconds. When you uncheck the box in Stream Manager the overlay will no longer be shown to viewers.
Does using the branded content tool impact discovery?
No. Using the branded content disclosure tool does not impact discovery, and we do not have plans to change this.
If I have panels on my offline channel page featuring branded content do I always have to have the branded content tool on?
No. You are only required to use the branded content tool if your livestream includes branded content.
Will Twitch run ads against streams that contain branded content?
Yes, ads may appear on streams that contain branded content.
What happens if I fail to disclose branded content in my streams?
If you fail to disclose branded content on your stream, we will send a warning via email. Repeated failure to disclose branded content may lead to other actions, including suspension of your account.
I work with an external platform that offers branded content activation on Twitch. Will Twitch ensure that available products on the external platforms comply with Twitch’s brand content policy?
No. You are responsible for ensuring branded content on your channel activated through any external service complies with Twitch’s branded content guidelines. However, Twitch conducts conversations with external services from time to time on this point and expects that such services adjust their offerings to align with the policy.
Do I need to use the branded content disclosure tool for content that promotes my own products and services?
No. You do not need to use the branded content disclosure tool when promoting your own products and services. However, we remind you to consider whether there remains legal or other obligations to disclose your ownership in the products or services that you promote.
Do I need to use the branded content disclosure tool if I am running a charity stream?
If you are being paid by a charity or corporate partner to fundraise you must use the branded content disclosure tool. If you are fundraising for the charity on your own, you do not need to use the tool.

Channel Points Guide for Creators

Channel Points is a customizable points program that lets streamers reward members of their community with perks, including a taste of benefits typically reserved for subscribers. It’s available to all monetized streamers.

Channel Points comes with built-in, automated rewards that streamers can customize. Streamers can also create custom rewards that they fulfill on their own, such as “choose the next channel I raid”, “set my background music”, or “make me dance on stream”.

For viewers, Channel Points are a way to be recognized for all the ways they’re already supporting the community, from watching a channel to being part of a raid. The points they earn are specific to the channel and the points accumulate automatically when they’re logged in and watch. The more support they give, the more they’ll earn.

Channel Points is a great way to get the community involved and we’re just getting started.

If you are a viewer, please check out our Channel Point article for viewers.

On this page:

  • Channel Points Setup & Management
  • Customizing your Channel Points
  • Managing Channel Point Rewards
  • Mods Can Help
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Channel Points Setup & Management

Everyone loves points and rewards! Your loyal fans will now be able to earn points from doing what they’re already doing in your channel such as watching, following, or participating in a raid. The Channel Points program will add another layer of entertainment by letting your viewers spend their points on fun rewards, some of which give them a taste of benefits typically reserved for subscribers, that seamlessly add to their community experience.

For details about the terms and conditions that apply to the Channel Points program, please see the Points Acceptable Use Policy.

Channel Points is available to all monetized streamers. You can manage your program in the Creator Dashboard. If you do not wish to have Channel Points enabled on your channel, you may disable the feature completely by toggling the Enable Channel Points option.

Currently, you’ll only be able to set up 50 rewards.

Customizing your Channel Points

Channel Points may be customized by heading to your dashboard, clicking the Hamburger icon in the top left-hand corner and proceeding to Channel Points under the Viewer Rewards section.

On this page you may customize the name of your Channel Points to reflect your brand and community. You’ll also see an option to upload a custom icon for your Channel Points that will be reflected on your channel page at the bottom of the chat window.

Managing Channel Point Rewards

Rewards can be customized via the Manage Rewards section under Channel Points in the Creator Dashboard. On this page you will see the option to add custom rewards, modify default rewards, and enable / disable both default and any custom rewards you have added.

Default Rewards

A default reward is a predefined reward such as allowing a user to choose an emote they wish to unlock or highlight a message in chat. Streamers do not need to do any additional work to fulfill these rewards, Twitch will do the heavy lifting!

When editing a default reward you may upload a reward icon and the background color of the reward panel which will be shown to the user on the reward redemption menu.

We included recommended costs for each default reward, but you can also turn on Smart Costs to automatically adjust your default rewards costs based on the size of your audience and the redemption rate of your rewards. This way, you won’t have to worry about updating your rewards costs as your audience grows. You can set your own cost or turn off Smart Costs anytime.

Custom Rewards

A custom reward is a reward which you fulfill yourself, whether it’s something as simple as giving the redeemer a shoutout, letting them join your next game or letting them choose who you raid next. For details about what can and cannot be offered as a custom reward, please see the Points Acceptable Use Policy.

Custom rewards can be added via the Manage Rewards section under Channel Points in the Creator Dashboard. Once there you will see an option to Add New Custom Reward.

Be sure to add a descriptive title and description of the custom reward so that it is clear to your community what they are redeeming. Similar to default rewards you may customize the reward icon and background color of the icon that will be displayed in the reward redemption menu on your channel page.

With custom rewards you may also require the redeemer to enter text should they need to provide additional information to you (such as who to host or what their in-game name is to invite them for example). Responses will be shown in chat, so don’t ask for or provide any personal information.

Custom rewards can also be set to have limits, allowing you to control how many claims you get during a stream. You can set a cooldown between redemptions (minimum of 1 minute, maximum of 7 days) and limit redemptions per stream or per user. You can enable all three limits for any custom reward on your channel. This is only available for rewards that are redeemable while your channel is live.

We have some icons you can get started with, as well as other Channel Points best practices in our Making the Most of Channel Points article

When a custom reward is redeemed, it will be visible in your Activity Feed on your Live Dashboard. Custom rewards redemptions are also directly integrated with Chat and Activity Feed, giving you a quick and easy way to scan what was requested in your community.

From the activity feed, you can also access your rewards queue by selecting the pop-out icon. You can use this queue to view and manage all your custom reward requests.

Mark as Complete when you’ve redeemed the request. If you choose to Reject, the points will be returned to the viewer. From here you can also Pause redemptions if you find you’re overwhelmed with requests, or you want to take a break when you’re live.

Mods Can Help

Mods can do things like: mark rewards as complete, reject rewards, refund points, report rewards as abusive, and pause redemptions for the channel(s) they moderate.

To assist streamers with Channel Points, mods need to work from the rewards queue. Open the queue in a new window by:

  • Clicking on the Channel Points reward balloon in chat.
  • Typing in /requests in chat on desktop and web.
  • Clicking on the rewards queue in chat settings under tasks.

Channel Points Predictions

With the launch of Channel Points Predictions to all monetized streamers, communities now have a new way to participate in the most exciting moments on Twitch.

On this page:

  • What are Channel Points Predictions?
  • Creator: Initial Setup for Predictions
  • Creator: Creating and Running Predictions
  • Creator: Managing and Completing Predictions
  • Viewer: How to Cast Your Prediction
  • Viewer: What to Expect
  • Viewer: Spectator Mode
  • Frequently Asked Questions

What are Channel Points Predictions?

Channel Points Predictions is a new superpower that lets creators engage their entire community while giving viewers a stake in the action of their favorite streams.

Creators or moderators (including lead moderators) set an event and its possible outcomes, and viewers use their Channel Points to predict the end result before the prediction window closes. Viewers who guess correctly will win a proportionate share of the Channel Points pool.

Viewers who cast a vote will see a temporary chat badge indicating their selected outcome during the prediction window. In addition, communities can access information such as a breakdown of all points casted, current return ratio, and the highest number of Channel Points used.

Creator: Initial Setup for Predictions

To begin running predictions, creators and mods, can use the chat command /prediction or head to the Stream Manager in the Creator Dashboard. Then, click on the + icon under Quick Actions.

Locate the Start a Prediction action, and click Add.

The Predictions Quick Action should now be visible in your Stream Manager.

You’re now ready to create your first prediction!

Predictions may result in your viewers generating high amounts of Channel Points quickly. We recommend reviewing your custom rewards and reward pricing before enabling.

Creator: Creating and Running Predictions

Moderators and lead moderators who have participated in a prediction cannot manage that prediction or select the outcome.

From the Quick Actions section in the Stream Manager, enter details on the prediction you want to run, between two and 10 outcomes possible, and the length of the voting period. Once this information is complete, you can start your prediction.

Chat Command

Creators and mods can also start a prediction using the /prediction chat command.

Once the chat command has been entered, a pop-up will allow you to enter the details of your prediction.

Creator: Managing and Completing Predictions

Managing a Prediction

Moderators and lead moderators who have participated in a prediction cannot manage that prediction or select the outcome.

You can manage your prediction in real-time from the Creator Dashboard.

Once a prediction has been set, just type /prediction to bring back the pop-up window.

Predictions can be deleted or ended before the Prediction Submission Window is up.

If you need to cancel a prediction, you will be able to do so as long as you haven’t chosen the outcome.

Complete a Prediction

To complete your prediction, select End Submissions and choose an outcome. Channel Points will then be proportionately awarded to the winning viewers.

If you do not select Complete Prediction after choosing the final outcome, points will not be allocated to viewers, and you won’t be able to start a new prediction.

Viewer: How to Cast Your Prediction

When a creator starts a prediction, viewers will see a notification at the top of the chat window. Click Predict to see the possible outcomes and cast your vote.

Viewers can also access Predictions by heading to the Channel Points store and taking action.

Viewer: What to Expect

Viewers will be able to cast their predictions during the submissions window set by the creator. See how much time is left by heading to the Predictions detail panel.

After casting their prediction, viewers will get a temporary chat badge indicating which way they voted.

Once a prediction has ended, viewers will receive a notification in the chat with information on the winning outcome and the amount of points received (or lost).

Viewer: Spectator Mode

Viewers in restricted-participation regions may now participate in Predictions without using Channel Points via Spectator Mode. Viewers participating in Spectator Mode will still receive a participation badge to display in Chat. This mode is only available to viewers in legally-restricted regions.

Spectator Mode viewers:

  • May only vote once without using Channel Points.
  • May not change their vote after it has been submitted.
  • May not win Channel Points if they predict correctly.

If all viewers in a prediction participate using Spectator Mode, 0 points will be distributed.

Only viewers and mods in restricted regions may participate in Spectator Mode at this time.

Frequently Asked Questions

Sections:
  • General FAQ
  • Creator FAQ
  • Moderator FAQ
  • Viewer FAQ
General FAQs
Are predictions available on all channels?
This feature is available to all monetized streamers. Learn more.
How long can a prediction last?
Creators will be able to set the prediction submission window between 1-30 minutes. Creators will be able to end the prediction during the day the prediction is created. If a prediction is not resolved after 24 hours, all points will automatically be returned to viewers.
Is there a maximum number of points that viewers can use?
The maximum number of points a viewer can use to participate in a prediction is 250,000 points. However, viewers can cast a prediction with as few as 10 points.
Do points round up or down when distributed (if rounding is needed)?
Points round down.
Creator FAQs
How do I start a prediction?
Use the chat command /prediction or go to your Stream Manager and add the Manage Predictions quick action.
Can I cancel a prediction?
If you haven’t resolved a prediction, you will be able to cancel it at any time. However, you will not be able to cancel a prediction after it has been resolved and points have already been distributed to participating viewers.
How many predictions can I set up at once?
You can only run one prediction at a time, but there is no limit on how many you can run and complete in sequential order during a stream.
What if I want to run a prediction with more than two options?
Predictions are limited to between two and 10 choices.
My prediction ended, but I can’t start a new one. Why?
Make sure that you have selected the outcome for your most recent prediction.
Moderator FAQs
Can mods cast predictions?
Yes, mods may cast predictions. However, any mod who participates in a prediction with points loses the ability to manage or resolve that prediction.
What happens if all mods on a channel have participated in a prediction?
If all available mods on a channel vote in a given prediction, the broadcaster will have to select the outcome. Consider this when choosing to play; the best scenario involves at least one moderator available to resolve the prediction.
Can mods play in Spectator Mode?
Mods in regions where Spectator Mode is the only form of play (Denmark, Korea, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Philippines, Poland, Quebec, Singapore, Sweden, and Turkey as well as Australia and Brazil for certain stream categories) may play in Spectator Mode. Mods in other regions must cast predictions with points to play.
Viewer FAQs
Is everyone allowed to participate in Predictions?
Viewers in Denmark, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Philippines, Poland, Quebec, Singapore, Sweden, Korea, and Turkey, as well as viewers in Australia and Brazil, for certain stream genres, can participate via Spectator Mode only due to legal restrictions in their area.
Can viewers without Channel Points participate?
Viewers without points cannot participate (except for viewers who are eligible to play in Spectator Mode). However, a quick way to earn 300 points is to follow a channel. Stick around for 5 minutes and earn 10 points! You can learn more about earning and using Channel Points here.
Do I still earn points if I predict correctly and leave the stream before the prediction is finished?
Yes, you will be greeted by a popup that you have predicted correctly and what you have won the next time you go to the creator’s channel.
Do I get my points back if the creator deletes the prediction without selecting an outcome?
Yes, points are returned if the creator does not select an outcome for the prediction.

Cheering: for Monetized Streamers

Bits are a virtual good you can use to encourage interaction with your chat. Cheering is automatically enabled for all new qualifying streamers, Partners, and Affiliates.

Curious about more of your Affiliate / Partner settings? Visit our guides!

Bits & Cheering Settings

The settings described below can be found in the Monetization section of your Creator Dashboard. To get there, click here. Or, visit Twitch and click your portrait -> Creator Dashboard -> Settings -> Monetization -> Bits & Cheering. These settings cannot be adjusted on mobile devices.

Enable/Disable Pins - Disable or enable pinned cheers. This setting is enabled by default.

Minimum Bits to Cheer - Set the minimum number of Bits needed to send a Cheer message in your channel

Setting the minimum number of Bits to send a Cheer message to 30 will mean that viewers will need to use at least 30 Bits, either in a single Cheermote, or by combining Cheermotes that add up to at least 30 Bits.

Minimum Bits Emote - Set the smallest Bits Cheermote that can be used in your channel.

Setting the minium Cheermote that can be used in your channel to 100 will mean that viewers cannot use the gray 1-99 Cheermote, and can only Cheer using the purple 100 Bit Cheermote or higher.

To reduce spam, set minimums for both settings above the default of 1. We recommend starting with the default settings for both and gradually adjust after experiencing how your chat uses Cheering. Creators with highly active chats may desire higher minimums.

Minimum Threshold to Pin - By default, the minimum threshold to pin is 100 Bits, or the amount selected in Minimum Bits to Cheer (whichever is higher). You can lower this setting, which will lower your Minimum Bits to Cheer.

Bits Tier Badges

All Bits Tier Badges are on by default, but you can manage which chat badges your channel supports. You can also upload and edit custom Bits Tier Badges for your community. This page tells you how many users have earned each of your badges.

If you’re having trouble uploading your images, visit our emote/file upload guide here.

If enabled, viewers may unlock Bits Tier Emote Rewards for Cheering amounts of Bits in your channel. These are emotes you design and set. They can be unique or the same designs as your subscriber emotes.

For more information on managing these additional Bits rewards, see our Custom Bit Badges article.

Top Cheerer Settings

Under your Leaderboard Settings, you can Enable or Disable Top Cheerer displays a list of the top weekly, monthly or all time Cheerers at the top of chat on your channel page to show that extra love to the viewers that Cheer to you.

For more information on Top Cheerer Settings, see our Leaderboards Guide.

Custom Cheermote Settings

All monetized streamers have access to default cheermotes. However, Partners can upload custom animated Cheermotes exclusive to their channel.

For more information on Cheermote Settings, visit our Cheermote Guide.

Earning Revenue From Cheering

Partners and Affiliates, check out your Bits revenue broken out in your Total Estimated Revenue in your Creator Dashboard. The revenue is listed under Cheering.

For more information on Payout, visit our FAQ.

Earning Bits From Other Bits Interactions

Partners and Affiliates may earn revenue from Bits in Extensions. You can learn more info in our Earning Bits Through Extensions article.

Qualifying streamers who are not Partners and Affiliates will see their balance reflected on their Creator Dashboard. With Spendable Balance, streamers can use their balance on their Creator Dashboard to purchase gift subs and Bits.

Alternatively, qualifying streamers who are not Partners and Affiliates can also choose to grow their balance and get paid out automatically once they reach Affiliate status and hit the minimum payout threshold.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I have to use Bits to accept donations? Can I accept donations in other ways?
Yes, creators are still free to use all existing third-party services and tools. We understand how important these services are to a creator’s livelihood and to creating interactions between creators and their communities. Our focus as an organization is making sure that our creators succeed. We believe that Cheering provides a completely new value to the Twitch community, and our goal is to take your feedback and make it a critical component to a creator’s success.
Are there restrictions on using Bits?
Yes, Bits are subject to our Acceptable Use Policy. Bits have no monetary value, so users cannot make a purchase, donate, or tip with Bits.
Can I Cheer in my own channel?
You cannot Cheer in your own channel.
Questions From Your Community
A member of my community didn’t receive Bits they purchased!

We’re sorry to hear that! Most Bits purchase delays can be resolved by refreshing the browser page, or exiting the mobile app. Depending on your payment method, a delay of a few seconds is not unusual.

If your community member is still having issues, you can send them to this troubleshooting guide. If the guide does not help, ask them to contact Twitch Support here.

A member of my community used Bits in Extensions, and it did not have the desired effect.
Your viewer can contact the Extension Developer directly! Have them view How to Contact an Extension Developer.
A member of my community says they are missing their Bits Tier Badge! What can I do?
As a first step, check your Bits Tier Badge settings to make sure that you have the badge enabled that they are missing! If this does not resolve the issue, ask them to contact Twitch Support here.
A member of my community says they should be on my Top Cheerers leaderboard. What can I do?
As a first step, check your Top Cheerers leaderboard update frequency and make sure your viewer has not fallen outside of your settings. If refreshing the page does not fix this for them, have them contact Twitch Support here.

Collaborating With Shared Hype Trains

Content in this article is most relevant for monetized streamers. Learn more.

Shared Hype Trains allow channels connected via Shared Chat to share rewards, Bits, Subscriptions, and more. To join or create a Shared Hype Train, you must be collaborating with a channel and connected in Shared Chat.

Setting Up A Shared Hype Train

To join or create a Shared Hype Train, the following conditions must be met:

  • Your channel must be live.
  • You must be in a collaboration with Shared Chat enabled. You don’t need to use Stream Together Audio/Video.
  • You must have Hype Trains enabled for your channel.
  • You must be a Twitch Affiliate or Partner.

If you see that one of your Favorite Collaborators has an active Hype Train going, you can easily request to join their session by sending a Knock. You can also open the drop-down menu next to the Knock button and click Invite to Shared Chat to start a Shared Chat with them.

Sending a Knock will allow you to connect and turn their Hype Train into a Shared Hype Train that all collaborators can participate in together. The Host of the session can invite other collaborators to join the Shared Hype Train as well.

By viewing the left-nav bar, streamers can quickly identify which of their collaborators have an active Hype Train, and initiate a Knock to join that session. This makes it easy to bring your communities together to contribute to the same Shared Hype Train!

Anyone in a collaboration can kick off a Shared Hype Train as well. Rewards are distributed to viewers based on the final level in the Shared Hype Train.

Whose Hype Train Is It Anyway? (About Hype Train Initiators)

If a Hype Train occurs in any channel that is part of Shared Chat, it occurs on all channels in the collaboration. The channel owner who kicks off a Shared Hype Train is the initiator. Shared Hype Train initiators are important for a few reasons:

  • The Shared Hype Train will remain on the initiator’s channel even if Shared Chat ends, or if other collaborators leave the session.
  • The initiator’s Hype Train kick-off threshold and difficulty settings apply to channels in the collaboration. For example, if the Initiator’s difficulty is set to Easy, then the difficulty is Easy for all collaborators throughout the duration of the Shared Hype Train.

If two or more channels start a collaboration together, each with a Hype Train already active, it converts to one Shared Hype Train. All the Hype Trains merge, and the channel with the highest level Hype Train becomes the Initiator.

The Hype Train Initiator and the Hype Train Conductor are not the same thing. Read on to see how Shared Hype Trains handle Hype Train Conductors!

Leveling A Shared Hype Train

Once a Shared Hype Train is kicked off, all qualifying support events across all channels contribute to reach higher Hype Train levels together. Learn more about how to level Hype Trains.

As the Shared Hype Train levels up, each viewer can track their contribution. The percentage displayed indicates a channel’s contribution towards the total Shared Hype Train, not a channel’s contribution to each level.

A collaboration can include up to 6 channels. Twitch will display up to 6 channels here in the order of highest to lowest % contribution.

Leaving an Active Shared Hype Train

What happens if you leave a Shared Hype Train before it reaches the end? How does it affect your community? In short, if you leave Shared Chat in a collaboration session, you also leave a Shared Hype Train. What this means depends on your role in the Shared Hype Train:

  • Initiators – If all other collaborators leave the session, the Shared Hype Train stays with your channel. If you leave the session, you end the Shared Hype Train for the other collaborators.
  • Collaborators – If you leave the Shared Chat session, your community will receive Hype Train rewards at the level of the train when it ends (which could be a higher level than when you left). You can return to the Shared Hype Train so long as it is still active.

We’ll remind Shared Hype Train initiators and collaborators the impact of leaving before they do so.

Shared Hype Train Collaborative Records and Rewards

In this section, we’ll focus on the meaningful differences in emote rewards when participating in a Shared Hype Train, compared to a solo Hype Train. For more details on solo Hype Train rewards, check out our guide here.

Collaborative Records

Shared Hype Trains feature collaborative records. As the name suggests, a collaborative record is the highest level previously achieved by a channel in any Shared Hype Train. At the end of a Shared Hype Train, channels who beat their previous collaborative record have a new high score.

Don’t worry, channels will still feature a solo Hype Train record – it’ll appear side-by-side with this new collaborative record.

Shared Hype Train Rewards

Emote rewards are distributed to viewers according to the same rules as solo Hype Trains. A few things to note:

  • If a channel leaves a Shared Hype Train before it concludes, their viewers still receive emote rewards. Those rewards are based on the highest Hype Train level achieved by all Shared Hype Train participants, regardless of when the channel leaves Shared Chat. For example, say a Shared Hype Train reaches level 5, but one of the collaborators leaves at level 2. Viewers from the departed channel receive Level 5 rewards.
  • If a channel rejoins a Shared Hype Train that reached a new level, their viewers will be automatically advanced to the current reward level, without having to start over.
  • Rewards are distributed 24 to 48 hours after the train ends.
About Shared Hype Train Conductors

Each channel will have their own conductors in a Shared Hype Train. The Hype Train Conductor badges are distributed according to the same rules as Solo Hype Trains.

Shared Specialty Trains

Oh yes…. Shared Hype Trains can include Golden Kappa Trains. Learn more about specialty trains.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is a Shared Hype Train?
Shared Hype Trains occur when 2 or more channels are joined via Shared Chat, and the conditions for a Hype Train are met. A Hype Train can go from non-shared to shared via Shared Chat, with or without Audio/Video.
What are the key differences between a solo Hype Train and shared Hype Train?
Shared Hype Trains and solo Hype Trains differ in a few key ways:
  • Shared Hype Trains tend to reach higher levels than solo Hype Trains, as contributors are shared across all Shared Chat channel participants.
  • Shared Hype Trains feature new Collaborative Records, separate from Solo Records
  • Shared Hype Trains allow collaborators to share specialty trains like Golden Kappa.
How do I manage my collaboration settings, so I am ready to participate in Shared Hype Trains?
Open Shared Chat from your chat or Stream Manager and click the Settings icon. Learn more in our Shared Chat guide.
What happens if I change my Hype Train settings while participating in a Shared Hype Train?
If you are the Shared Hype Train initiator, your threshold or difficulty setting changes applied during the Shared Hype train will take place the next time one occurs. If you are a participant, your Hype Train settings are overwritten by the settings of the Shared Hype Train initiator.
What happens if I’m in Shared Chat, but don’t have Hype Trains enabled?
If you don’t have Hype Trains enabled, you won’t be included in a Shared Hype Train. You can still participate in Shared Chat. You can enable Hype Trains during the Shared Hype Train to participate.
What happens if I disable Hype Trains while in a Shared Hype Train?
Your channel will remain in the Shared Hype Train until it ends, unless you leave Shared Chat. The next time a Shared Hype Train occurs, your channel will not be included.
What happens if the Shared Hype Train doesn’t meet its goals?
The train will end at the current level and rewards will be disbursed to contributors based on that level.
How is revenue from support events split in a Shared Hype Train?
Revenue from support events such as Subs and Bits are not split between all channels. The revenue goes to the channel in which the support event occurred.
Are there restrictions to the types of creators who can participate in Shared Hype Trains?
To participate in Shared Hype Trains, you must be a Twitch Partner or Affiliate. You must have Hype Trains enabled. You must have collaboration network settings that are open to working with other Twitch Creators.
Do Shared Hype Trains have unique rewards?
When Shared Hype Trains launched, 3 exclusive emotes were available for a limited time. These emotes are unlocked permanently for viewers who earned them, and can be used in any channel on Twitch (where the emotes are not banned).

Thanks to our emote artists: Toffeetokki (SquadUp), Tacodemuerte (JointSlay), and Maiberryart (GroupHug)!

SquadUp
