Community Goals

Content in this article is meant for Twitch Affiliates and Partners only.

Goals enable creators to set meaningful objectives for their viewers to focus their contributions around. Want to set a short-term, daily goal? How about a milestone goal for a subathon that celebrates your Partner-versary? Goals are flexible enough for you to set up the goal how you like it, while enabling a way to create hype in your community to support your stream. Click here to launch your first goal.

Creators: Setting Up Your Quick Action

To add a goal, head to the Stream Manager in the Creator Dashboard. Click on the Plus icon under Quick Actions.

Creators and editors can use the /goal chat command.

Locate the Manage Goals action, and click Add.

The Manage Goals Quick Action should now be visible in your Stream Manager.

You’re now ready to create your first goal!

Everyone can create follower goals, but only Affiliates and Partners can set additional goal types.

Creators: Creating a Goal

From the Quick Actions section in the Stream Manager, select the Manage Goals option to start creating your goal.

Once you create your goal, you’ll see a confirmation in your Stream Manager.

Customize

Customize Goals

You will need to select what goal type you want to have. Non-monetized creators can set a follower goal. Affiliates and Partners can set a follower goal along with one type of sub goal.

Goal Type

Description

Followers

Goal for new followers to your channel.

Total Subs

Goal for the total number of subscriptions made to your stream.

Total Sub Points

Goal for the total number of sub points made to your stream.

New Subs

Goal for new Prime, Gift, or Recurring subs that are purchased while a goal is active.

New Subs Points

Goal for new Prime, Gift, or Recurring sub points that are purchased while a goal is active.

New Bits

Goal for total number of Bits received while goal is active.

New Cheerers

Goal for total number of Cheerers while goal is active.

Plus Program Goal - Level 1

Goal for earning 100 Plus points while goal is active.

Plus Program Goal - Level 2

Goal for earning 300 Plus points while goal is active.

The recommended sub or follower target is based on your current sub point or follower count and are designed to help you reach a next recognizable milestone. For example, we’ll recommend 20 sub points if you have 11 sub points, or 300 followers if you have 260 followers. You can always choose to set your own goal amount to suit your… ahem, goals (no pun intended!)

Customize Description

Optionally, you can briefly describe your goal.

Copy Browser Source

When you start a goal, it will automatically appear on your channel page. You also have the option to use our browser source URL to add the goal as a real-time overlay on your stream. The preview currently shows dimensions set to 370px x 40px.

Plus Program Goals (Level 1 and Level 2) do not have a browser source option. All other goal types support browser source overlays.

You may need to adjust the aspect ratio to suit your setup (for example, try 740px x 80px).

While you can create both follower and sub goals, at this time the browser source will only render the most recent goal created. For example, if you have an active Follower goal, then create a new Sub Goal, your browser source will update to show the Sub Goal. You must create a new Follower goal for the browser source to display the Follower goal again.

Customize Progress Bar

Optionally, you can choose from 13 color combinations including the color you set for your channel. The first color circle is set to your creator color. You can set a different color for follower and sub goals.

Chat Commands

Creators and editors can also start a goal by using the /goal chat command.

Once the chat command has been entered, a pop up will allow you to enter the details of your goal.

Creators: Managing a Goal

When you start a goal, viewers will begin to see progress towards your goal increase in near real-time within your channel page, subscription user notices in chat, and your browser source overlay (if you’ve chosen to use it).

When your goal is achieved, a callout appears at the top of chat to celebrate your achievement! Follower goals will not appear in chat, but will appear if you use it as an overlay on your stream.

Once you start a goal, it will stay active on your channel until you end it or start a new one. If you’d like to modify the description or amount of your goal, you must end your current goal and start a new one.

If you achieve a goal, it will stay active on your channel and continue to increment until you decide to end it or start a new one.

Once a goal has been set, just type /goal in chat to bring back the pop up window.

Viewers: Contributing to a Goal

Viewing a goal is an easy way for you to see the impact your support can have on the creator. To find out whether a channel has an active goal, look within the Channel Page to see all active goals, or click the Subscribe button on the Channel Page.

When a viewer contributes towards a goal, all viewers will see progress towards the active goal increment within their User Notice in chat. Hover over the goal to view the description for the goal. Clicking on the goal will open a panel where you can see more details about the goal and how to contribute.

Frequently Asked Questions

FAQ Contents
  • Creator FAQ
  • Viewer FAQ
Creator FAQ
How do I start a goal?
Start a goal from the Stream Manager by enabling the Manage Goal Quick Action, or by using the /goal chat command.
How do viewers see my goal?
Once you start a goal, it will automatically appear within your channel page, sub button, and browser source overlay. Your goal will begin incrementing in real-time as viewers support your goal. New goals will temporarily appear at the top of chat to hype your community up and inform them details about the goal. When a viewer contributes towards a goal, other members of your community can see progress increase towards your goal within the chat user notice. Viewers can click the Subscribe button within the channel page to see more details about your active goals.
Can I pause a goal?
You cannot pause a goal, but you can end an active goal. If you end an active goal, your incomplete progress towards that goal is reset and you will be required to create a new goal.
Can I edit a goal?
You cannot edit an active goal. If you want to edit a goal, you must end the active goal and start a new one.
What happens if my goal is achieved?
A celebratory callout appears at the top of chat and the goal remains active on your channel. Subsequent goal actions (such as subscription purchases or follows) still increment the goal. You must decide to delete the goal or start a new goal for your existing goal to deactivate on your channel.
Will removing a goal from Quick Actions deactivate the goal?
No, the goal will still remain active even if you remove the Quick Action from your Dashboard.
Can moderators and editors access my sub goal?
Only editors can help you manage goals within the Stream Manager.
What happens to my goal during a Hype Train?
If you start or achieve a goal during a Hype Train, the two events will be merged together and the Hype Train callout will show viewers your incrementing goal in addition to the Hype Train event itself.
Why did my goal decrease after I started it?
Sub and follower goals are based on your current sub points or follower count. When subscriptions lapse or viewers unfollow, the corresponding number is deducted from your goal amount.
Why did a particular sub contribute more than 1 point to the goal?
If you choose to set your goal to track sub points, it will vary depending on the subscription’s tier. A Tier 1 subscription grants 1 sub point, a Tier 2 subscription grants 2 sub points, and a Tier 3 subscription grants 6 sub points. Where if you set your goal to track sub count, each sub is counted as 1.

For more information about the differences between sub points and sub count check out our Sub Point vs Sub Count article.

Can I have more than one goal going at the same time?
Yes, creators can set multiple goals at the same time.
If I start a sub goal mid-month will subs I already received this month count?
Yes. Sub goals are based on sub points which all active subs contribute towards.
Viewer FAQ
Can I opt-out of seeing goals in Chat?
No, we don’t support viewer opt-out of goals in chat. Goals are a shared, real-time experience that support the creator. If you are finding issues with the current experience, please report them on Uservoice.
How do I report a goal?
If you are finding issues with a goal, click the Horizontal three dots icon underneath the video player in the Channel Page. Click on report channel name . Select the report category of In channel’s goals, enter a reason, and submit your report. A member of our team will review it to see if the goal violates our policy guidelines.
How do I know if a channel has a goal?
You can see a channel’s goals within the channel page underneath the player. You can click the Subscribe button in the Channel Page to learn more details about an active sub goal on a channel. You’ll be able to see progress towards a goal appear in chat whenever someone contributes towards that goal. You can also look for the goal overlay on the stream.
What types of subs contribute to a Sub Goal?
Sub points are tied to the number of existing subscribers to a creator’s channel. Purchasing new recurring subscriptions (including Multimonth subs), or gift subscriptions or redeeming a Prime sub all award sub points and contribute to a sub goal. At the same time, because active subscriptions already contribute towards a creator’s sub point total, renewing an existing subscription or continuing a Prime or gifted sub into a paid sub do not result in additional sub points or further progress towards the goal.
Why did a sub contribute more than 1 point to the goal?
Sub goals track sub points, which vary by subscription tier. A Tier 1 subscription grants 1 sub point, a Tier 2 subscription grants 2 sub points, and a Tier 3 subscription grants 6 sub points.
If I do not renew my recurring subscription or unfollow a channel, will it decrease progress towards the goal?
Yes, if you choose not to renew your recurring subscription, no additional sub points will be contributed to the goal. Similarly, if you unfollow a channel, progress toward a follower goal will decrease.
Are goals available to mobile viewers?
Yes, viewers on Android and iOS devices will be able to see and contribute to goals.

Completing Your DAC7 Tax Interview

EU tax regulations require monetizing streamers in the European Union to complete a short tax interview.

To secure continued payouts, EU streamers must click here [Desktop browser only] to complete this tax interview in as little as 5 minutes.

EU regulations, colloquially called DAC7, require certain digital platforms, including Twitch, to report information to the EU regarding earnings generated by monetizing users. At Twitch, this concerns all monetizing streamers who reside in the EU.

Monetized EU streamers must complete a short tax interview in as little as 5 minutes. Complete the interview by November 23, 2026. If you don’t complete it by this date, your payouts will be blocked.

It’s important that monetized EU streamers understand how these regulations could impact their Twitch earnings if they do not complete this interview within the time window set by regulators. This article explains more about this regulation, how it applies to Twitch, and how simple it is to meet this regulatory requirement so streamers can remain focused on growing their community on Twitch.

Accessing the DAC7 Tax Interview

Act today! Start here to review tax interview(s)

As part of EU regulations, monetizing Twitch streamers are required to complete a 5-minute tax interview. These regulations stipulate that companies, including Twitch, must enforce penalties if they do not receive your updated information within a set time window defined by regulators. Twitch sends multiple emails and notifications to all who must complete this additional interview. Complete it by November 23, 2026 to avoid having your payouts blocked.

In general, the DAC7 tax interview should take less than 5 minutes to complete. Basic info like legal name and primary address should be pre-filled.

To Access Tax Interview(s):
  • On a Desktop browser click the link in your email or notification, or visit your Creator Dashboard -> Settings -> Monetization Settings
  • Click New DAC7 Tax Interview
  • Open and complete the interview. Twitch uses Amazon Tax Central to collect your information.

That’s it! If your interview information is accepted, the DAC7 interview status will be marked Completed, alongside your Completed Royalty and Service Tax interviews.

If there is a problem, the interview completion status will update to Incomplete, Pending, or Failed. When your tax interview fails, this typically means the information provided could not be verified. To correct this, use the Retake option next to the interview to complete it again with the correct information. You do not need to restart onboarding.

If your tax form says “failed”: Do not contact Twitch Support for tax issues. Instead, review our guide Amazon Tax Information Interview and IRS Annual Reporting FAQ for troubleshooting steps, or consult a tax professional.

Stuck? Review our onboarding walkthroughs for Affiliates and Partners, or contact Twitch Support if you need help.

Frequently Asked Questions

  • What happens if my information cannot be verified?
  • What do I do if my tax interview is not loading?
  • What if I don’t have a VAT number?
  • When entering my VAT number, what is the error “invalid code”?
  • How can I delete my account?
  • I have other questions about tax, can you help?
  • How can I tell if I am a monetized, onboarded streamer?
  • How is the DAC7 interview requirement impacted by recent announcements regarding the Monetized Streamer Agreement (Contract Migration) and Tax Withholding?
  • How often must I re-verify my information with Twitch?
What happens if my information cannot be verified?
Most streamers will be able to successfully complete required tax interview(s) in 5 minutes. If your information cannot be verified in the DAC7 tax interview, go back and closely review the information again. To correct it, use the Retake option next to the interview in your Creator Dashboard. You do not need to restart onboarding.

If you receive an error when supplying your VAT ID, make sure it matches the required formats above. If your VAT ID matches the required format above, and you continue to experience errors, please contact a tax professional.

What do I do if my tax interview is not loading?
If you experience issues loading the tax interview, please check your internet connection, or try reloading the page in a private browsing mode.
What if I don’t have a VAT number?
If VAT and TIN are the same number in your country, or you don’t have a VAT number, please tick the checkbox “I don’t have a VAT number.”
When entering my VAT number, what is the error “invalid code”?
If you receive an error “invalid code” or other error stating an Invalid VAT number, you should check whether you are registered on the EU VAT Information Exchange System (“VIES”) database. If you are not registered there, you should contact your accountant or tax adviser to resolve this issue. Amazon uses the EU VIES database to verify VAT IDs based on the verification requirements in the EU regulations.
How can I delete my account?
Click here to delete your account. Learn more about account disabling and deletion in our knowledge guide here: link.twitch.tv/DeleteYourAccount

Disabling or deleting your Twitch account does not prevent your information from being shared with EU tax authorities as per DAC7.

I have other questions about taxes; can you help?
We cannot provide individual tax guidance. You can view our tax guide here: Amazon Tax Information Interview and IRS Annual Reporting FAQ
How can I tell if I am a monetized, onboarded streamer?
A successfully monetized, onboarded Partner or Affiliate will see Completed across their Creator Dashboard onboarding settings. They will be able to see payout information in their payout history dashboard.

Affiliates must be invited to the Affiliate program after meeting a set of criteria. Partners are invited to participate in the Partner program, and in most cases, will have previously been onboarded Affiliates before becoming a Partner.

How is the DAC7 tax interview requirement impacted by recent announcements regarding the Monetized Streamer Agreement (Contract Migration), and Tax Withholding?
DAC7 is an EU regulation that Twitch is required to comply with. It is separate and does not interact with the Monetized Streamer Agreement or Tax Withholding.

Streamers must update their tax withholding every three years, or you will be subject to 30% withholding by default.

How often must I re-verify my tax information with Twitch?
Twitch will ask you to re-confirm that your tax information remains accurate every three years or 36 months. If you don’t re-verify your information by the deadline, your payouts will be blocked. You can complete the DAC7 tax interview to unblock your payouts.

More Resources

For onboarding help, visit our walkthroughs for Partners and Affiliates.

For general information on tax, view our tax guide: Amazon Tax Information Interview and IRS Annual Reporting FAQ

Content Classification Labels

We encourage streamers to stream whatever they and their communities are passionate about, as long as that content doesn’t violate our Community Guidelines. However, while content that does not violate our Community Guidelines is allowed on Twitch, not all content or topics are appropriate for everyone. In those cases, we require that streamers mark their stream with a label.

Streamers need to apply Content Classification Labels to indicate to viewers if the stream they’re about to watch contains themes related to: Mature-Rated Games; Sexual Themes; Drugs, Intoxication, or Excessive Tobacco Use; Violent and Graphic Depictions; Significant Profanity or Vulgarity; Politics and Sensitive Social Issues; or Gambling.

Twitch cannot and will not tell you in advance whether your planned content requires a specific Content Classification Label, or violates our Community Guidelines. Please remember, streamers are responsible for reviewing our guidelines and making your own content classification decisions.

How it Works for Streamers

Content Classification Labels can be added to your stream within the Edit Stream Info panel in Stream Manager.

  • Visit Stream Manager within your Creator Dashboard
  • Click Edit Stream Info
  • If this panel is not added to your Stream Manager layout, add it by clicking the drop-down menu in the top left corner, and selecting Edit Stream Manager Panels. You can also use the Edit Stream Info Quick Action.
  • Click the Content Classification field
  • Select the corresponding labels for the type of content you plan to include in your stream
  • Select Done to save your selection

Selected labels will remain and carry over stream to stream until manually changed.

Streamers are responsible for reviewing the Content Classification Guidelines and knowing which types of content need a label. If streamers fail to accurately label their streams, they will receive a warning and a label will be applied to their stream, which they can remove. Repeated violations will result in a label being locked on your channel for a period of time, but will not result in an account suspension. You can appeal any warning or lock.

Content Classification Labels & Descriptions

Twitch content is live and dynamic. We require streamers to take responsibility for accurately labeling their content, even as their stream evolves. Familiarize yourself with the Content Classification Guidelines for further information when it is appropriate to apply a label.

Name

Description

Mature-Rated Game

Games that are rated* Mature or less suitable for a younger audience

Gambling

Participating in or promoting online or in-person gambling, poker, or fantasy sports that involve the exchange of real money.

Violent and Graphic Depictions

Simulations and/or depictions of realistic violence, gore, extreme injury, or death

Drugs, Intoxication, or Excessive Tobacco Use

Excessive tobacco glorification or promotion, any marijuana consumption/use, legal drug and alcohol induced intoxication, discussions of illegal drugs

Sexual Themes

Content that focuses on sexualized activities, sexual topics, or experiences

Significant Profanity or Vulgarity

Prolonged and repeated use of obscenities, profanities, and vulgarities, especially as a regular part of speech

Politics and Sensitive Social Issues

Discussions or debates about politics or sensitive social issues such as elections, civic integrity, military conflict, and civil rights.

*If you select a game with an ESRB rating of Mature as your stream category, the Mature-Rated Game label will be automatically applied to your stream. Twitch leverages ESRB ratings to determine whether a game is considered mature for global viewers.

How it Works for Viewers

When viewers attempt to watch a stream that has a Content Classification Label applied, they will typically see an interstitial screen when they land on the channel page that lets them know the types of content in the stream they are about to watch, and must provide consent prior to viewing the stream. For certain content types (Mature-Rated Games; Significant Profanity or Vulgarity; and Politics and Sensitive Social Issues), these will be flagged only via a short on-screen overlay once the stream loads. The on-screen overlay will be available in a collapsed state in the video player for the duration of the stream.

Once a viewer has acknowledged a specific label type, they will no longer see an interstitial screen for streams labeled as including that content type, and will instead only see the on-screen overlay moving forward. Viewers will continue to see interstitial screens for the other categories (except for Mature-Rated Games; Significant Profanity or Vulgarity; and Politics and Sensitive Social Issues) until they have acknowledged each type.

Interstitial screen example On-screen overlay example

The viewer experience may vary by region in accordance with local laws. For example, in some regions, viewers will be required to log-in and confirm their age prior to viewing labeled content.

Frequently Asked Questions

Sections
  • Streamer FAQ
  • Viewers FAQ
Streamer FAQ
What happened to the “Mature Content” toggle in my Stream Settings?
Content Classification Labels replaced the former “Mature Content” toggle. You’re responsible for applying the labels that match your content whenever your stream includes the relevant themes.
If I label my stream, can I show content that is prohibited by the Community Guidelines?
No, content currently prohibited in the Community Guidelines is still prohibited even if a stream is labeled.
Can Twitch tell me in advance if my planned content needs a Content Classification Label?
No. Twitch does not provide content pre-approval, including advice on which labels to use, or any other content decisions. You must review the Community Guidelines, the Content Classification Guidelines, and decide which labels are appropriate for your content. For more information, visit our guide: About Content Pre-Approval.
If I use curse words occasionally during my stream do I need to apply the “Significant Profanity or Vulgarity” label?
No, this label only needs to be applied if you are using profanity or vulgar language in a persistent and excessive manner throughout the duration of your stream. Think cussing someone out in a game lobby, versus the occasional use of the “f-word” or a genuine reaction to a moment in a horror game. For additional examples and details on what content does or doesn’t need a label, you can refer to our guidelines.
If I smoke tobacco or drink alcohol occasionally during my stream do I need to use the “Drugs, Intoxication, or Excessive Tobacco Use” label?
Our focus here is on sustained and prolonged activity.
  • For alcohol use, sipping on a drink while streaming wouldn’t require a label, but appearing visibly intoxicated to the point you are slurring your speech, or making being drunk the focus of your stream (e.g. doing a “drunk history”) would require a label.
  • Smoking a cigarette or vape while on stream wouldn’t require a label, but intentionally drawing attention to the fact that you’re smoking, or promoting smoking would need a label.
  • Use of marijuana in any form, would require a label.

For additional examples and details on what content does or doesn’t need a label, you can refer to our guidelines.

What do you mean by “Sexual Themes”?
Examples of sexual themes include prolonged or repeated kissing of another individual or object, detailed non-educational discussions of sexual topics or experiences, and content or behavior that is very likely to elicit a mature chat conversation.

To be more direct - many ASMR practices are focused on mindfulness and are not sexual, but we consider kissing or licking a microphone to fall within Sexual Themes. Additionally, many Hot Tub streams would also fall under Sexual Themes, and will need to be labeled. Keep in mind, even when labeled, focusing on intimate body parts such as the buttocks, groin, or breasts for extended periods of time is still prohibited under our Sexual Content policy.

For additional examples and details on what content does or doesn’t need a label, you can refer to our guidelines.

How are Content Classification Labels different from tags?
Tags set the context of your stream or channel, and should be changed each time you go live. Tags are not required but can help viewers discover your stream more easily. Content Classification Labels exist to let your audience know they’re about to watch certain content types that may not be right for everyone. Viewers must consent to viewing a stream with classification labels.
What happens if I don’t label my content correctly?
Account suspensions will not be issued for incorrectly labeling a stream. If you fail to accurately label your stream, you will receive a warning via email, and a label will be applied to your stream that you can remove. Repeated failure to label content correctly may result in a label being locked on your channel for a period of time. How long depends on how many times it has happened.

Twitch Support cannot provide guidance on whether specific content requires labels. You are responsible for all content in your stream. Familiarize yourself with the Content Classification Guidelines for more details.

Can I appeal for removal of a label applied to my channel?
Yes. You can appeal any Content Classification Label warning or lock applied to your channel, no matter how long it lasts, by visiting the Appeals Portal. Please refer to your enforcement email for more information.
How will I know how long labels will be applied to my channel?
Go to the Content Classification field in your Stream Manager, where if you hover over the label that is currently applied to your channel, you will see a tool-tip detailing how long it will remain before expiring.
Can I change my selected Content Classification Labels partway through a stream?
Yes, similar to tags and streaming categories, streamers can change their selected Content Classification Labels at any point of a livestream. If a different game is selected partway through a stream, we will also automatically update whether the “Mature-Rated Game” label is selected.
Can my editors or mods help add or remove Content Classification Labels to my stream?
Editors can change the Content Classification Labels on your stream, moderators cannot.
Will the type of content I stream affect my ad revenue?
There is a possibility that the type of content that you stream could affect your ad revenue. Brands align their ads with content that reflects their brand values. The labels give advertisers more context about which types of streams they show their ads alongside. It is also possible that certain brands won’t want to run their ads alongside streams with specific types of Content Classification Labels applied. Learn more about how your ad revenue may be impacted by your content in our Advertiser-Friendly Content Guidelines.
If I apply these labels, will my channel’s discoverability be impacted?
We want to make sure the homepage, which is often the first page that viewers land on, is aligned with viewer expectations. To address this, streams that are labeled as including Drugs, Intoxication, or Excessive Tobacco Use; Violent and Graphic Depictions; Gambling; and/or Sexual Themes will not be included in Twitch Front-Page Shelves due to the visual nature of those topics. Streams labeled as including Mature-rated Games and Significant Profanity or Vulgarity; or Politics and Sensitive Social Issues will not be impacted unless the streamer has also selected one of the labels bolded above.

Streams with these labels will still be recommended in the Left Navigation Bar (Followed & Recommended Channels).

Past streams do not impact the visibility of future streams. When your stream does not include one of the CCLs listed above, it will again be eligible to be shown on homepage recommendations shelves.

In addition, viewers’ Content Display Preferences include content filtering and blurring options, and certain users have default filtering and blurring turned on for their accounts. Users under the age of 18 have content labeled with Sexual Themes; Drugs, Intoxication, or Excessive Tobacco Use; Violent and Graphic Depictions; and Gambling filtered out by default. Logged out viewers have content labeled with Sexual Themes and Gambling filtered out by default. All users have thumbnail blurring for content labeled with Sexual Themes turned on by default. These settings can be managed within the Content Display Preferences under Profile settings.

Streams with the Gambling Content Classification Label applied may not be visible in certain regions in accordance with local law.

Viewers FAQ
How do I report mislabeled content?
You can use the reporting tool to report mislabeled or unlabeled content by selecting the “Missing or Incorrect Content Classification” option. Refer to our article “How to File a User Report” for more information on how to file an actionable report. As with all user reports, they will be reviewed by a member of our moderation team before taking action. If the content is determined to need a classification label, a warning will be issued to the streamer, and the label will be applied to their stream.
Will I also see Content Classification Labels on VODs and clips?
Content Classification Labels will be automatically applied to any VODs that are associated with streams that had labels applied. Clips will also have the associated Content Classification Labels applied when viewed on web or on the iOS and Android apps.
Can I provide consent for all categories of mature content at once instead of one at a time?
At this time there is no way to consent to all types of classification labels at once, unless a stream you consent to view has every content label applied. This helps ensure you do not see content you are not expecting to see.
Is there a way for me to block all categories of content that require classification labels from my viewing experience on Twitch?
Yes, you can manage your preferences for viewing content labeled with Content Classification Labels, by visiting your Content Display Preferences.

Creator Badge Drops

View the Creator Badge Drops terms and conditions here.

Creator Badge Drops allow creators to run time-limited events where viewers can earn custom badges by subscribing, gifting subscriptions, watching the stream, or being a top supporter on the gifting leaderboard.

Viewers: How to Earn Creator Badges

What Are Creator Badge Drops?

Creator Badge Drops are custom badges that creators offer during time-limited events. When you complete a qualifying action during an active event, you’ll earn the badge and can display it in chat in that channel.

Terms and Conditions for earning badges apply. View the full Creator Badge Drops Terms and Conditions.

How Do I Know If a Creator is Running An Active Badge Event?

When a creator runs a badge event, a notice appears over chat during the event saying “Subscribe to earn Badges.” The callout shows:

  • Which custom badge(s) are available
  • What actions are required to earn them (subscriptions/gifts and/or watch time)
What Actions Unlock Badges?

Creators can set up to 3 types of Creator Badge Drops for their events:

  • Subscription/Gift Reward: Subscribe or gift a specified number of subscriptions during the event
  • Watch Time Reward (Optional): Watch the stream for a specified duration during the event
  • Top Supporter Reward (Optional): Be one of the top gifters on the event’s leaderboard by the end of the event

Viewers can earn all available badges independently during the same event.

How Does the Top Supporter Reward Work?

When a creator enables the Top Supporter Reward, a gifting leaderboard appears over chat during the event. The leaderboard shows who the top gifters are in real time.

  • The creator chooses how many top spots earn the badge (top 1, 3, 5, or 10 gifters)
  • If you reach a qualifying spot, you receive the badge immediately
  • If another viewer passes you on the leaderboard, you lose the badge until you reclaim your spot — a notice appears in chat to let you know
  • If you hold a qualifying spot when the event ends, you unlock the badge permanently!
  • Anonymous gifting does not count toward the leaderboard
Where Can I Track My Progress?

You can track your progress toward earning badges using the Drops tracker in chat. The tracker shows your current progress and what’s needed to complete the reward. You can also check progress in your Drops Inventory page. The users currently receiving the Top Supporter Reward will be shown in the Event Leaderboard.

Where Can I See My Earned Badges?

Earned badges appear in your badge collection for that specific channel. The Top Supporter badge is automatically equipped when earned. Subscription and Watch Time badges must be manually equipped. You can:

  • View them in the badge card when clicking on your username in that channel
  • Change or remove them from your displayed badges at any time
  • See claimed badges in the Drops & Rewards page under Rewards

Event badges only appear in the channel where they were earned.

Why Didn’t I Receive a Creator Badge Drop?

If you completed the qualifying action but didn’t receive the badge:

  • Verify the event was still active when you completed the action
  • Check that you met the exact requirement (correct number of subscriptions or watch time)
  • Check your Drops Inventory page - the badge may have been awarded

Creators: Setting Up Badge Events

Who Can Create Badge Events?

Creator Badge Drops is available to all monetized streamers. To get started, visit your Creator Dashboard.

How to Create a Badge Event

To set up a badge event:

  • Go to your Creator Dashboard
  • Navigate to Viewer Rewards → Creator Badge Drops
  • Click Create Event
  • Upload your badge images and configure event details
  • Set your event start and end date/time
  • Click Create Event to schedule it

Events start automatically at your selected time. You can edit or delete events until they go live. Once live, all settings are permanently locked, and the event cannot be deleted.

Event Details

When creating an event, you’ll configure the reward, how viewers earn it, and how long your event will last.

Sub/Gift Reward (Required)
  • Badge Reward Image: Upload a square PNG image (not animated, maximum 25kb file size). Recommended dimensions are at least 120x120 pixels
  • Badge Name: Up to 25 characters
  • Subscription Count: Set requirement from 1 to 100 subscriptions
  • Badge Description: Auto-generated text describing how the badge was earned
Watch Time Reward (Optional)
  • Badge Reward Image: Upload a separate square PNG image (not animated, maximum 25kb file size). Recommended dimensions are at least 120x120 pixels. This reward is separate from the reward you just set up.
  • Badge Name: Up to 25 characters (e.g., “28’ Bday”)
  • Watch Time: Set the total time a viewer must watch your stream (up to 24 hours)
  • Badge Description: Auto-generated text describing how the badge was earned
Top Supporter Reward (Optional)
  • Badge Reward Image: Upload a separate square PNG image (not animated, maximum 25kb file size). Recommended dimensions are at least 120x120 pixels.
  • Badge Name: Up to 25 characters
  • Top Spots: Choose how many top gifters earn the badge (1, 3, 5, or 10)
  • Leaderboard: A gifting leaderboard automatically appears over chat during the event, showing viewers where they stand in real time
  • Badge Description: Auto-generated text describing how the badge was earned

You must choose sub/gift reward as an option in order to enable watch time reward or Top Supporter Reward.

Event Length
  • Start Date & Time: When the event begins (uses your local time)
  • End Date & Time: When the event ends (uses your local time)
  • Maximum Duration: Events cannot exceed 28 days

Before saving, make sure your badges adhere to Twitch Badge Guidelines. Submissions in violation of these Guidelines will be rejected and may result in action against your account.

Managing Your Events

In the Creator Badge Drops dashboard, you’ll see:

  • Scheduled Events: Events that haven’t started yet (can be edited or deleted)
  • Live Events: Currently active events (view-only, but can be ended early)
  • Completed Events: Past events (view details only)

For scheduled events, you can click Edit Event to modify details or delete the event before it goes live.

For live events, click View Events to see event details and progress. All settings are locked to protect viewers’ progress, but you can End Event Early if needed. Ending an event early stops new badge claims immediately, but viewers who already earned badges will keep them.

Best Practices for Badge Events
  • Announce your badge event in advance on social media and Discord
  • Design unique, visually appealing badges that viewers will want to collect
  • Consider timing events around special streams, milestones, or celebrations (birthdays, anniversaries, marathons)
  • Remind viewers during your stream about the active event and how to earn badges

Troubleshooting

Badge Didn’t Drop After Qualifying Action

If a viewer completed the action but didn’t receive the badge:

  • Verify the event was active at the time of the action
  • Check that the qualifying action settings match what the viewer completed
  • Have the viewer check their Drops & Rewards page to confirm the badge wasn’t awarded
  • Have the viewer refresh their browser or app
Can’t Upload Custom Badge Image

If you’re having trouble uploading your badge:

  • Ensure the image is square and in PNG format
  • Verify the image is not animated
  • Check that the file size is 25kb or less
  • Ensure the badge follows Twitch Badge Guidelines
  • Try a different browser or clear your browser cache
Event Not Showing to Viewers

If your event isn’t visible to viewers:

  • Confirm the event start time has passed (events start automatically at the scheduled time)
  • Check that the end time hasn’t already occurred
  • Verify you’re currently live streaming
  • Ask viewers to refresh their page
Can’t Edit or Delete Event

Once an event goes live, all settings are permanently locked and it cannot be deleted. You can only edit or delete events that are scheduled but haven’t started yet.

Need Help?

If you’re experiencing issues with Creator Badge Drops:

  • Review the troubleshooting steps above
  • For urgent technical issues, Contact Support

Frequently Asked Questions

For Viewers
Can I earn badges from multiple creators?
Yes! You can earn event badges from different creators. Each badge is unique to that specific creator’s event and only appears in that channel.
Do event badges expire?
No. Once you earn an event badge, it’s yours to keep and display permanently in that channel. However, you can only earn the badge during the active event period. Twitch may also take down Creator Badge Drops that violate the Twitch Badge Guidelines.
What’s the difference between event badges and subscriber badges?
Subscriber badges are permanent badges that show your subscription tenure (1 month, 6 months, etc.) and evolve over time. Event badges are special limited-time badges earned by completing specific actions during creator-run events. Both can be displayed in chat.
Can I earn both the subscription badge and watch time badge in the same event?
Yes! If a creator offers multiple rewards (subscription, watch time, and/or Top Supporter), you can earn them independently during the same event.
What is the Top Supporter Reward?
The Top Supporter Reward is a badge earned by being one of the top gifters during a badge event. A leaderboard appears over chat showing the top gifters in real time. If you hold a qualifying spot when the event ends, you keep the badge permanently.
Can I lose my Top Supporter badge during an event?
Yes. The Top Supporter badge is dynamic during the event — if another viewer passes you on the leaderboard, you lose the badge until you reclaim your spot. A notice appears in chat to let you know. If you hold a qualifying spot when the event ends, the badge becomes permanently yours.
Does anonymous gifting count toward the Top Supporter leaderboard?
No. Anonymous gifting does not contribute to the leaderboard. Only non-anonymous gift subscriptions count toward your leaderboard position.
Where do I see my earned badges?
Earned badges appear in your badge collection for that specific channel. The Top Supporter badge is automatically equipped when earned; Subscription and Watch Time badges must be manually equipped. You can change or remove them from your displayed badges at any time. You can also see your earned badges in the Drops & Rewards page under Creator Badge Drops.
What happens if the creator ends an event early?
A creator can end their event early. If an event ends early, you will no longer be able to make progress toward your badge reward, or earn a badge for that event. Badges already earned before the event ended will not be affected. However, Twitch may take down or remove Creator Badge Drops that violate the Twitch Badge Guidelines.
How do I report a badge that breaks the rules?
You can report a badge directly from chat. Select the badge next to the person’s username, then select the 3 Vertical Dots icon and choose Report. The report window confirms which badge you’re reporting before you submit. To learn more, see the Twitch Badge Guidelines.
For Creators
Will this feature be available to all creators?
Creator Badge Drops is available to all monetized streamers.
Can I run multiple events at the same time?
No. Only one event can be active at a time.
Can I edit an event after it starts?
No. Once an event goes live, all settings are permanently locked and it cannot be deleted or edited. You can only edit or delete events that are scheduled but haven’t started yet.
Can I end an event early if I need to?
Yes. While an event is live, you can end it early from the View Event page. This will stop new badge claims immediately, but viewers who already earned badges will keep them. Once ended early, the event cannot be restarted.
Do I need to offer all three badge types?
No. A subscription/gift reward is required, but the watch time reward and Top Supporter Reward are both optional. You can choose to offer just the subscription badge, or any combination of the three badge types.
How does the Top Supporter leaderboard work?
When you enable the Top Supporter Reward for an event, a gifting leaderboard automatically appears over chat during the event. It shows viewers their ranking in real time based on non-anonymous gift subscriptions. You choose how many top spots earn the badge (1, 3, 5, or 10). Viewers receive the badge dynamically as they reach a qualifying spot, and lose it if they fall off — but if they hold their spot at event end, the badge is theirs permanently.

Creator Certification

Twitch Affiliates and Partners can partner with brands through the Sponsorship Portal. To help brands discover your channel, begin by filling out your Creator Profile – a professional showcase of who you are, what you stream, and what kinds of partnerships interest you.

Creator Certification is a short educational program that teaches you how to run sponsorship campaigns successfully. By completing the certification, you earn a visible badge on your Creator Profile and receive a 12-hour head-start to selected campaigns before non-certified creators. Creators who are certified are visible to advertisers in our sponsorship matchmaking tool.

Affiliates: Creator Sponsorship Certification is required to be eligible for campaign invitations. Complete the self-paced course on Creator Camp and fill out your Creator Profile to start receiving opportunities.

What Is Creator Certification?

Creator Certification is a Creator Camp educational course that covers how to run sponsorship campaigns professionally on Twitch. The course covers:

  • Sponsorships 101 — Tools and Execution: Types of sponsorships (Exclusive, Opt-in, Third-Party), how brands find creators, accepting campaigns, running campaigns, and handling unexpected situations
  • Creating Brand Suitable Content: Why brands choose creators, appropriate content during branded streams, considerations for guests, brand exclusivity rules, and language guidelines

The certification takes approximately 10–15 minutes to complete.

How to Complete Certification

  • Go to the Sponsorship Portal and look for the certification banner.

  • Click through to Creator Camp to begin the course.

  • Choose your path:

    • Full learning experience: Videos, written content with images, and quizzes
    • Test out: Skip the learning materials and go directly to quizzes

  • Complete all quizzes. You have unlimited attempts — if you answer incorrectly, the system shows the correct answer with an explanation before you continue.

  • Once complete, return to the Sponsorship Portal. Your certification status will be reflected in your Creator Profile.

To become fully Certified, you must have both a completed Creator Profile and the certification course — but you can complete them in either order.

Once certified, visit the Sponsorship Portal to see available campaigns.

Benefits of Creator Certification

  • 12-hour head-start: Receive notifications for select opt-in campaigns 12 hours before non-certified creators
  • Visible certification badge: Advertisers see your certified status in their matchmaking tool, as an indicator of credibility.

Recertification

Your certification is valid for 12 months from the date you complete it. When your certification is approaching expiration, you’ll be prompted to recertify.

If your certification expires:

  • You lose the 12-hour head-start benefit
  • Your “Certified Creator” badge is removed

To recertify, complete the certification process again in Creator Camp.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who can complete Creator Certification?
Creator Certification is available to all creators through Creator Camp. You must also complete your Creator Profile to become fully certified, but you can complete them in either order.
Is certification required to participate in sponsorship campaigns?
For Affiliates: Yes. Affiliates must be Creator Sponsorship Certified to be eligible for campaign invitations. For Partners: Certification is not required, but certified Partners receive benefits like a 12-hour head-start on select campaigns and visibility in the advertiser matchmaking tool.
How long does certification take?
The full learning experience takes approximately 10–15 minutes. If you choose the “test out” option, you can skip directly to quizzes.
What happens if I fail a quiz?
You have unlimited attempts. When you answer incorrectly, the system shows the correct answer with an explanation, then lets you continue.
How long does my certification last?
Certification is valid for 12 months. You’ll be prompted to recertify before it expires.
Can advertisers see that I’m certified?
Yes. Your certification status is visible to advertisers in the matchmaking tool as a verification badge.

Default Emotes

We know using emotes is a great way to reward and engage your community. We also know that finding an artist or creating your own emotes can be a daunting task, especially when you’re just starting out. To help you get started, we’re offering 120 emotes that you’re free to use in addition to any custom emotes you create in the future.

Library

Default emotes can be accessed from your Library from the Default Emotes tab. Selecting an emote will allow you to rename it and assign directly to your slots by clicking Assign to slot. Once assigned, you can always remove it and use it later. Feel free to add as many as you like and use the ones you like best!

Download

If you would like to create animated versions of default emotes, feel free to download them using these links below. Sets are grouped by color. For example, clicking on the yellow dog will download all of the dog emotes in yellow. You can mix and match any of the emotes and their colors, so feel free to download as many as you’d like!

You can also use these default emotes as your Bits Tier Emote Rewards, or with the Easy Animate process to create animated emotes. For information about managing Bits Tier Emote Rewards, please see our Custom Bit Badge and Emote Reward Slots guide.

Disable Pre-rolls

Streamers can now disable pre-roll ads for incoming viewers by regularly running ad breaks during their stream, allowing viewers to immediately see what’s going on.

When a streamer runs a 30 second ad break, pre-roll ads will be disabled for the next 10 minutes. When a streamer runs a 1 minute ad break, pre-roll ads will be disabled for the next 20 minutes. When a streamer runs an ad break that’s 1 minute and 30 seconds or longer, pre-roll ads will be disabled for the next 30 minutes. When a streamer runs a 3 minute ad break, pre-roll ads will be disabled for the next 60 minutes.

Streamers will see a countdown timer at the top of their dashboard which lets them know how much pre-roll free time is left. Streamers can find additional information in the Ads section on the Revenue Settings page.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why are pre-rolls disabled for a slightly longer amount of time than what my Revenue Settings page says when I run an ad break?
We disable pre-roll ads when a mid stream ad break is playing. However, a viewer coming to your stream will still see the ad you’re running. We don’t think that should count toward your pre-roll free time. So, we set the timer to include the amount of time the ad is showing, and that’s what you’re seeing.
Why am I still seeing an ad when I enter a stream that has pre-roll ads disabled?
If a streamer is running a mid stream ad break when you visit the channel, you will see the ad break.
Who can disable their pre-rolls?
All Partners and Affiliates can disable their pre-rolls by running ad breaks.
Can I still have pre-roll ads on my channel?
Yes, flexibility is important to us. There will be a toggle in your Revenue Settings page that you can use to opt in or out of this feature at any time. By default, all creators will be opted into this feature and pre-rolls will be disabled when they run ad breaks.
How will this affect the revenue I earn from ads?
While advertising revenue varies based on several factors including the number of subscribers, countries, and hours broadcast, we expect streamers running 3 minutes of ads an hour (a 3-minute ad break every 60 minutes, a 1-minute 30-second ad break every 30 minutes, a 1-minute ad break every 20 minutes, or a 30s ad break every 10 minutes) and disabling pre-rolls may earn between $1 - $2 per month per viewer. We encourage streamers to check their dashboard to understand their actual revenue.
How much pre-roll free time can I accrue?
If you already have pre-roll free time left when running an ad break, any time accrued by the latest ad break will be added to your existing pre-roll free time, to a maximum of 1 hour.
Do viewers coming from raids see pre-roll ads?
No. When a raid begins, neither the raiding creator nor their audience sees pre-roll ads upon arrival at the raided channel. Depending on the channel, some viewers can still receive mid-rolls if one is actively playing when joining via raid. Learn more about raids.

Creators may see pre-rolls when browsing channels to raid, but these do not appear once the raid begins

Drops Troubleshooting

Looking for something else? This guide covers troubleshooting Drops issues. For the basics of earning Drops, see How Drops Work. For Poké Balls, Daily Watch Progress, badge evolutions, and Pokémon Collection mechanics, see Pokémon Chat Badge Drops Campaign. For redeeming codes, see our Code-Based Drops Redemption Guide.

What Are You Trying To Do?

Choose the option that best describes your situation:

I can’t link my game account

→ I Can’t Link My Game Account

I claimed a Drop but didn’t get it in-game

→ I Claimed a Drop But Didn’t Get It In-Game

My progress bar stopped or isn’t counting

→ My Progress Isn’t Counting

I subscribed but didn’t get a Poké Ball or Great Ball

→ I Subscribed But Didn’t Get a Poké Ball

I’m under 13 or have a managed account and can’t link

→ Age Restrictions and Managed Accounts

My Daily Watch Progress disappeared

→ My Daily Watch Progress Reset

My Poké Ball isn’t opening

→ My Poké Ball Isn’t Opening

My Pokémon Chat Badge isn’t evolving

→ My Badge Isn’t Evolving
