I Can’t Link My Game Account

Problem: Twitch says “link account” but you already linked it, or the connection isn’t recognized.

Earning Pokémon Chat Badges? You don’t need to connect a game account to earn them. Watch a live channel in a participating category instead. See Where to Watch.

Step-by-Step Fix

Step 1: Find the linking page

  • Go to Twitch Drops Inventory
  • Click on a campaign
  • Click “Connect” next to the game name
  • You’ll be redirected to the game developer’s website

Step 2: Verify the connection

  • Check on Twitch: Drops Inventory should show “Connected”
  • Check on game’s website: Should show your Twitch username
  • Both must show connected - if only one does, the link isn’t complete

Step 3: If it still says “not connected”

  • Unlink your account on the game developer’s website
  • Wait 5 minutes
  • Link it again through Twitch Drops Inventory
  • Wait 15 minutes for sync
  • Refresh both pages

Step 4: Still not working after 24 hours?

Contact the game developer’s support (not Twitch Support). Provide your Twitch username and game account name.

Why contact the game developer? They control the account linking system. Twitch can’t fix connection issues on their end.

I Claimed a Drop But Didn’t Get It In-Game

Problem: You claimed the Drop on Twitch but the reward didn’t appear in your game.

Understanding Drops Delivery

Drops have 3 separate steps:

  • Earn on Twitch (you fulfill campaign requirements) ← User’s/Twitch’s responsibility
  • Claim on Twitch (you click “Claim” in Drops Inventory) ← Twitch’s responsibility
  • Deliver to game (game developer sends it to your account) ← Game developer’s responsibility

Who to contact: Twitch Support helps with Steps 1 and 2 (earning and claiming on Twitch). Game developers help with Step 3 (delivery to game).

Troubleshooting Checklist

✓ Check 1: Did you claim it on Twitch?

Go to Drops Inventory and look for “Claimed” status. If it says “Ready to Claim,” click the button.

✓ Check 2: Which game account is linked?

Many players have multiple accounts (PC, console, different regions). Verify which account is connected to Twitch. Rewards go to the linked account only.

✓ Check 3: How long has it been?

  • Most rewards: 24-48 hours
  • Some rewards: Instant
  • A few rewards: Up to 7 days

Check campaign details for specific timelines.

✓ Check 4: Where to look in-game?

  • Check your in-game mailbox
  • Check your inventory
  • Check your cosmetics/skins menu
  • Some rewards require you to “claim” them in-game

✓ Check 5: Still missing after 48 hours?

Contact the game developer’s support (NOT Twitch Support). Provide:

  • Your Twitch username
  • Your game account name
  • The Drop name
  • Screenshot of “Claimed” status from Twitch

Why contact the game developer? Once you’ve claimed on Twitch, delivery is the game developer’s responsibility. Twitch can’t add items to your game account.

My Progress Isn’t Counting

Problem: You’re watching a stream but your progress bar stopped or isn’t counting.

Troubleshooting Checklist

✓ Check 1: Are you watching a Drops-enabled channel?

Look for the “Drops Enabled” tag on the channel, a Drops banner at the top of chat, or view the participating Drops campaigns in the Drops icon at the bottom of chat. Not all channels offer Drops, even if the game has an active campaign.

✓ Check 2: Is the campaign still active?

Go to Drops Inventory and check the campaign end date. If it expired, you can’t earn more progress.

✓ Check 3: Disable ad blockers

Browser extensions that block ads can prevent progress tracking. Disable them and refresh the page.

✓ Check 4: Only one campaign at a time

You can’t earn progress toward multiple Drops simultaneously. Make sure you’re only watching one Drops-enabled stream.

✓ Check 5: Refresh the page

Sometimes progress updates after refreshing. Check your Drops Inventory to see if progress was actually counted.

✓ Check 6: Are you watching live?

VODs, replays, and clips don’t count toward Drops. You must watch live streams.

✓ Check 7: Check your internet connection

Poor internet can interrupt tracking. Make sure your stream is playing smoothly.

Still not working? Contact Twitch Support with your Twitch username, the campaign name, and which channel you were watching.

I Subscribed But Didn’t Get a Poké Ball

Problem: You subscribed to a participating channel but didn’t receive a Special Poké Ball, such as the Pokémon Night Out Themed Poké Ball.

What’s Likely Happening

Special Poké Balls earned through subscriptions follow the same eligibility rules as standard Subscription Drops:

  • The channel must be live in a participating category, and the badge window must be active (for Pokémon Night Out, October 16-24, 2026)
  • Prime subscriptions do not count
  • Renewals of an existing subscription do not count - it must be a new subscription
  • Gift subscriptions earn a Special Poké Ball for the gifter only - recipients don’t receive one
  • The subscription must be purchased while the channel is live, in the correct category, during the active campaign

See the full eligibility table in How Drops Work.

Each badge window has a limit: up to 3 Great Balls during the First Partners Campaign, and 1 Pokémon Night Out Themed Poké Ball during Pokémon Night Out (October 16-24, 2026). If you’ve already reached that limit, additional qualifying subscriptions won’t grant another Special Poké Ball.

Where to Check Your Status
  • Go to Drops Inventory to confirm whether the subscription was recognized by the campaign
  • Confirm you haven’t already reached the limit for that badge window

If your subscription meets all the eligibility requirements above, you’re within the limit for that badge window, and you still didn’t get a Special Poké Ball, contact Twitch Support with your Twitch username, the channel name, and the date/time of your subscription - this may be a bug.

Age Restrictions and Managed Accounts

Problem: You’re unable to link a third-party game account (such as an Epic Games account) to your Twitch account for Drops.

Some game developers and platforms restrict account linking for users who do not meet the minimum age requirement to use Twitch. If your third-party account is a managed account (for example, an Epic Games “cabined” account for users under 13 or the minimum age requirement in your region), you may not be able to link it to Twitch.

Why This Happens

Twitch requires users to meet a minimum age requirement to use the platform. Third-party platforms like Epic Games enforce their own age restrictions. Accounts flagged as underage or managed by a parent/guardian may be blocked from linking to external services like Twitch.

This means:

  • You cannot link a “managed” or age-restricted third-party account to Twitch
  • Without a linked account, you cannot receive Drops rewards for that game
What You Can Do
  • Check the third-party platform’s age and account requirements to understand your account status
  • If you believe your account was incorrectly flagged, contact the third-party platform’s support (for example, Epic Games Support) to resolve your account status
  • Once your third-party account is no longer restricted, you can link it to Twitch through your Drops Inventory

Twitch Support cannot override third-party account restrictions. If your issue is with the third-party platform’s account status, contact that platform’s support team directly.

My Daily Watch Progress Reset

Problem: Your progress toward a Daily Watch Progress requirement disappeared or went back to zero.

What’s Likely Happening

Daily Watch Progress resets if you don’t watch the full required number of minutes within that day’s window. For the Pokémon Chat Badge Drops Campaign, that requirement is a full 20 continuous minutes in a single day - partial progress doesn’t carry over, even if you’re only a minute or two short. This is expected campaign behavior, not an error - each day is a separate requirement, and previously completed days aren’t affected.

Where to Check Your Status
  • Go to Drops Inventory and check the campaign’s progress details
  • Look at how many of the required days you’ve completed so far
Common Causes
  • You watched part of the required 20 minutes on a day, but not all of them, before the day’s window ended
  • You started watching late in the day and ran out of time to finish that day’s requirement

Twitch Support cannot restore an expired day’s progress. This is a designed rule of the campaign, not a technical error. If you lost progress, watch at least 20 continuous minutes on a participating channel tomorrow to start a fresh day.

My Poké Ball Isn’t Opening

Problem: You earned a Poké Ball, but it hasn’t opened into a reward.

What’s Likely Happening

A Poké Ball doesn’t open automatically when you earn it. It opens once you complete the Daily Watch Progress requirement tied to that Poké Ball (see Daily Watch Progress). If you haven’t finished the required days and minutes yet, your Poké Ball is still in progress - this isn’t a bug.

Where to Check Your Status
  • Go to Drops Inventory or open the Drops & More panel in chat
  • Find your Poké Ball and check its progress indicator (for example, “Day 2 of 3” or minutes remaining today)
  • Confirm you’re watching a participating channel for the campaign
Common Causes
  • You haven’t completed all the required days yet
  • You didn’t meet today’s minute requirement, so today’s progress hasn’t counted
  • You have another Poké Ball of the same type currently active - only one Poké Ball of each type can make progress at a time
  • The badge window ended before you completed at least 1 day of progress on the Poké Ball. A Poké Ball only keeps progressing after its window ends if it already has a completed day.
  • The deadline to open it has passed. Poké Balls and Great Balls from the First Partners Campaign must be opened by October 31, 2026, and Pokémon Night Out Themed Poké Balls by November 23, 2026.

Twitch Support cannot manually open a Poké Ball or grant its contents. Your Drops Inventory and the Drops & More panel show your real, current progress. If the progress shown there indicates you haven’t met the requirement yet, that’s an accurate reflection of your status - not an error to report.

My Badge Isn’t Evolving

Problem: You’re watching participating channels, but your Pokémon Chat Badge hasn’t evolved.

What’s Likely Happening

A badge evolves only after you equip it and complete 3 days of Daily Watch Progress (20 minutes a day) on participating channels. If you haven’t finished all 3 days yet, your badge is still in progress - this isn’t a bug. See Evolving Your Badges.

Where to Check Your Status
  • Open the Drops & More panel in chat on a participating channel to check your evolution progress (for example, “Day 2 of 3”)
  • Under Watch Drops in the same panel, use Swap to confirm the badge you want to evolve is equipped
Common Causes
  • The badge isn’t equipped
  • It’s a First Partners Campaign badge (Pichu, Bulbasaur, Squirtle, or Charmander), and evolving hasn’t started yet. These badges can evolve starting October 16, 2026
  • Your badge just evolved, and you haven’t equipped its new form yet. Each new form must be equipped before it can keep evolving
  • You haven’t completed all 3 days yet, or didn’t meet today’s 20 minutes
  • You’re watching a channel that isn’t in a participating category
  • The badge is already in its final form (Pikachu, Venusaur, Blastoise, Charizard, or Gengar)
  • The evolution period has ended (badges can be evolved until January 30, 2027)

Twitch Support cannot manually evolve a badge. The Drops & More panel shows your real, current progress. If it shows you’ve completed all 3 days and your badge still hasn’t evolved, contact Twitch Support with your Twitch username and the badge name - this may be a bug.

I Got a Duplicate Reward

Problem: You received the same reward from a Poké Ball more than once.

What’s Likely Happening

Duplicate protection guarantees you’ll receive every reward in a specific pool before any reward repeats - but this only applies within that same pool. If a campaign introduces a new pool (for example, a new phase or rotation), duplicate protection starts over for that new pool and does not carry over from a previous one.

Where to Check Your Status
  • Go to your Pokémon Collection to see which rewards you’ve already earned
  • Check whether the duplicate came from the same pool as your previous rewards, or a new pool

If you believe you received a true duplicate within the same pool before earning every reward in it, contact Twitch Support with your Twitch username, the campaign name, and the reward names you received.

An Item Is Missing From My Pokémon Collection

Problem: You earned a reward, but it’s not showing up in your Pokémon Collection.

What’s Likely Happening

Rewards are added to your Pokémon Collection when you claim them - earning a reward and claiming it are two separate steps. If you haven’t claimed the reward yet, it won’t appear in your Pokémon Collection.

If your reward came from a Poké Ball, first confirm the Poké Ball fully unlocked before checking for a missing reward: unlocking requires 3 full days of 20-minute Daily Watch Progress (see Poké Balls). If you haven’t completed all 3 days yet, the Poké Ball hasn’t unlocked and there’s no reward to claim yet - this isn’t a bug.

Where to Check Your Status
  • Go to Drops Inventory and check the Poké Ball’s progress (for example, “Day 3 of 3” means it’s unlocked)
  • Look for a “Ready to Claim” status
  • Claim the reward, then check your Pokémon Collection again

Remember: your Pokémon Collection only displays rewards that are actually obtainable by you. If an item was never available to you in the first place, it won’t appear as a missing or empty slot. This is separate from Collections in Video Producer, which organize your videos into playlists.

If the Poké Ball shows fully unlocked (3 of 3 days complete) and a “Ready to Claim” reward, but claiming it still doesn’t add it to your Pokémon Collection, contact Twitch Support with your Twitch username and the reward name - this may be a bug.

I Want a Refund for My Subscription

Problem: You subscribed to earn a Pokémon Chat Badge Drops reward, but didn’t realize the requirement takes multiple days to complete, and want a refund.

What’s Likely Happening

Your subscription and the campaign reward are two separate things. Subscribing gives you the standard benefits of a subscription (emotes, badge, ad-free viewing, and any streamer-specific perks) regardless of whether you complete a Drops campaign requirement. The Special Poké Ball you earn from subscribing is an additional reward on top of your subscription - it isn’t a condition of the subscription itself.

What You Can Do

Standard Twitch subscription refund policy applies to this campaign. See Refunds on Twitch for eligibility and how to request a refund.

More Resources

  • How Drops Work — Learn the basics of earning, claiming, and tracking Drops on Twitch.
  • Pokémon Chat Badge Drops Campaign — Understand Poké Balls, Daily Watch Progress, badge evolutions, and the Pokémon Collection.
  • How to Redeem Drops Codes and Rewards — For code-based rewards that require manual entry on a partner website.
  • Creator Badge Drops — Custom badges that creators offer during time-limited events.
  • Your Drops Inventory — Check progress, claim rewards, and verify account connections.
  • Contact Twitch Support — If you’ve tried the steps above and still need help.

Earning Revenue from Bits in Extensions

Extensions make it possible for developers to create new experiences for your viewers. Eligible Partners and Affiliates can earn revenue when Bits are used within certain Extensions on their channel pages.

How It Works

  • Install and activate an Extension that has enabled Bits usage. These Extensions include the label In-Extension Bits in the Extension Manager.
  • You must have Partner or Affiliate broadcaster status and have enabled Bits on your channel to be able to use any Bits Extension features. If you are ineligible, the Bits-enabled features will be unusable on your channel.
  • Viewers must explicitly confirm their Bits usage in the Extension on each individual action.
  • When your viewers perform and confirm an action that requires Bits within the Extension on your channel page, you’ll earn 80% of 1 U.S. cent per Bit used and the remaining 20% is shared with the Extension developer. The Bits in Extensions program, including revenue share, may be adjusted from time to time or may no longer be available at Twitch’s sole discretion.
  • Both Affiliate and Partner revenue share will be paid 15 days after the first of the following month (Net 15).
  • You can track your Extensions Revenue via your Earnings Analytics under the Extensions category. Revenue generated through an Extension will not be included in the Bits category.
  • You may disable the Bits-enabled Extension features by going to the ‘Manage Permissions’ page of the extensions you have installed.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I know which Extensions enable Bits usage?
Extensions that enable Bits usage will include the label “In-Extension Bits” in the Extension Manager. Once you install, configure, and activate an Extension, it will show up on your channel page, and viewers on your channel will then be able to engage with the Extension and the community in a variety of new ways.
In which countries are Bits in Extensions available?
Bits in Extensions is available globally where Twitch is also made available. However, it is the responsibility of the Extension developer to localize any language in the Extension.
What is the revenue share to Partners and Affiliates?
Eligible Partners and Affiliates will ordinarily receive 80% of 1 U.S. cent per Bit that is used within Bits-enabled Extensions on their channel pages, and the Extension developer will receive the remaining 20%. Each Extension’s detail page states that Extension’s revenue shares.
How are experiences for Bits in Extensions fulfilled / used?
Third-party developers are responsible for delivering the experiences you get through Bits in Extensions, not Twitch. Viewers will be able to see when an Extension has Bits-enabled features and use Bits within that Extension. Note that Extensions must be installed and activated within your channel page for your viewers to use Bits in them.
Will my viewers still be able to Cheer with Bits in my channel’s chat?
Yes, your viewers’ ability to Cheer with Bits in chat and your share of the revenue Twitch receives from Cheered Bits are not affected by the Bits in Extensions program. Extensions with Bits provide complementary engagement to your channel’s experience.
What happens if I deactivate or uninstall an Extension with Bits?
If you choose to uninstall or deactivate an Extension with Bits, your viewers will no longer be able to use any persistent items exchanged for Bits in the Extension. Please avoid deactivating an Extension in a disruptive manner because it will impact your viewer’s enjoyment from their Bits usage.
Where can I find revenue information for Bits in Extensions?
You can track revenue from Bits in Extensions under Extensions Revenue via your Revenue Dashboard. It will show you the total revenue earned from Extensions.
Are Extensions with Bits available on mobile?
Yes, Extensions with Bits are available on mobile if the developer decides to support it. Extensions that are available on mobile are designated by a “Mobile” tag on the Extension Discovery page.
Are there alerts when someone uses Bits in an Extension on my channel?
Yes. Bits used in Extensions appear in the Activity Feed in your Stream Manager, showing the user and the amount of Bits used. However, if you use multiple Extensions with Bits, the Activity Feed will not indicate which Extension the Bits came from. For additional alerts or overlays, check with the Extension developer — some Extensions may offer their own notification features.
What happens if my viewer uses Bits in the Extension, but nothing happens?
Actions that are not confirmed successful by a developer will not result in a deduction from the viewer’s Bits wallet. If there is a bug, the viewer is able to contact the developer directly. All Extensions will have the developer’s support e-mail address in the Extension detail page.
Can my viewers get refunds for Bits used in Extensions?
Per our policy, Twitch does not offer returns of Bits used in Extensions. Exceptions are handled on a case by case basis - please contact Customer Support. Partners and Affiliates will have the same protections from Bits chargebacks as they do with Cheering in Chat.
What happens if I find a bug with the Extension I installed?
Please contact the developer directly. All Extensions will have the developer’s support e-mail address in the Extension detail page.
Can I disable Extension features that require Bits?
Yes, you can disable features that require Bits in an Extension by updating the permissions granted to the Extension. To manage permissions, navigate to the Manage Permissions page of the Extensions you have installed.

Emote Formatting & Instant Emote Upload Requirements

Contents in this guide apply to all monetized streamers, with some specifics for Affiliates and Partners.

This article describes the formatting requirements for your emotes, and includes details of instant emote upload eligibility. If you’re trying to learn the rules and guidelines your emotes must adhere to, visit our Safety Center.

For a guide on how to upload and manage your subscriber emotes, click here. For Bits emotes, please click here.

Rules and Guidelines

When making your emote(s), follow the requirements in our Emote Guidelines. Please read carefully.

Image size and Formatting Requirements

Some monetized streamers create their own emotes, while others hire an artist. No matter who makes the emote, there are some important things to remember when creating your emote:

Standard Emotes
  • The image must be in a .png format
  • Depending on whether you wish to use auto-resize or manual upload, you will either need a single PNG between 112 x 112px and 4096 x 4096px, or three image sizes: 28 x 28px, 56 x 56px and 112 x 112px.
  • Images must be square shape (e.g., same pixel height and width)
  • The file size cannot exceed 1MB
  • Please submit your emote with a fully transparent background. If you do not know how to make images transparent, please read this.
  • Ensure you have viewed the emote at 100% resolution to check that the art has clear lines and, if you are including words, that the letters are correct and easy to read. Make sure that lines are sharp (no unnecessary blurring or feathering)
Animated Emotes
  • The image must be in .gif format
  • Depending on whether you wish to use auto-resize or manual upload, you will either need a single square GIF (between 112x112px and 4096x4096px) or 3 GIFs (28x28px, 56x56px, 112x112px)
  • GIF images must be square shape (e.g., same pixel height and width)
  • 1MB file size max for auto-resize mode. If using manual mode, each of the file sizes cannot exceed 512KB
  • The thumbnail for the animated emote will default to the first frame of the GIF. If you want to create a different thumbnail, this can be overridden with a custom static image (same requirements as emotes)
  • GIF images cannot be more than 60 frames
  • Must not flash or flicker more than 3 times within a 1 second period

For more information on the differences between auto-resize and manual emote upload, please see our Subscriber Emote Guide for Partners and Affiliates.

Instant Upload Eligibility Requirements

Partners and Affiliates who meet certain criteria can upload their emotes without manual review by Twitch Staff. This means their emotes are live and available to the community immediately upon upload. This is a privilege that can be revoked temporarily or permanently, if a creator fails to meet one of the criteria outlined below.

Visit your Emote library to get started.

Affiliates

Emote Instant Upload Initial Eligibility

Losing Instant Upload

Regaining Instant Upload After Enforcement

Stream for at least 60 unique days over a rolling-year period. Days do not have to be sequential. Time spent streaming before reaching Affiliate status does not count towards this 60-day period.

Affiliates who receive a warning or suspension will lose access to instant emote upload.

In most cases, instant emote upload is automatically regained after 1) another period of 60 unique streaming days has passed, and 2) if the Affiliate has passed the last 60 calendar days without receiving a warning or suspension.

Certain suspensions can result in you permanently losing the ability to instantly upload emotes while you remain an Affiliate.

Partners

Emote Instant Upload Initial Eligibility

Losing Instant Upload

Regaining Instant Upload After Enforcement

New Partners unlock instant emote upload if at least 60 days have passed since the day they became Partner, and since their last warning or suspension.

Partners who receive a warning or suspension within the last 60 days lose access to instant emote upload. Depending on the severity of the suspension, they may lose this privilege permanently.

Partners may receive one warning for minor emote-related infractions without losing access to instant emote upload. Subsequent emote-related infractions (removal of an existing emote, or denial of a submitted emote) will result in loss of access to this benefit. Review the rules and guidelines for emotes on Twitch.

The ability to instantly upload emotes is lost if the Partner receives a warning or suspension. However, in most cases, instant emote upload is automatically regained after a period of 60 days has passed without an enforcement.

Certain suspensions can result in you permanently losing the ability to instantly upload emotes as a Partner.

Frequently Asked Questions

My emote was rejected. Now what?
If your emote is rejected, you should have received an email providing the general reason your emote was not approved.
You may alter your emote so it does not violate our Emote Guidelines and resubmit, or submit a different emote altogether. All emotes and their suffixes (the unique code you create during the submission process) must comply with the Emote Guidelines.
I believe my emote follows the Emote Guidelines and should have been accepted. What can I do?
If your emote was rejected, you should have received an email with information about your emote rejection. Based on the information in this email, you may alter the design and submit again. Abuse of resubmission may result in suspension of instant emote upload or other account privileges.
Can you just tell me exactly why my emote was rejected?
Our Emote Guidelines are in place to keep all streamers and viewers safe on Twitch. When an emote is rejected, we let you know the general reason that your emote does not meet our guidelines, and ask you to alter the design accordingly.
Subscriber emotes can be used globally across Twitch, so we apply our guidelines with this in mind. An in-joke, or something that seems innocent in one context can lose the important nuance of your community in the global conversation of Twitch.
What do I need to do to get my emote approved?
When your emote is rejected, a reason is included in a rejection email. If this happens, you may alter the design and submit again. If your changes adhere to the Emote Guidelines, your emote will be approved.
My emote was approved before, but is now removed. What happened?
Twitch reserves the right to review all emotes and subscriber badges and to remove content that violates our Emote Guidelines at any time, including as the guidelines are updated. If your emote was removed, you should have received an email regarding the reason why.
I lost instant upload due to a removed emote. How can I get it back?
Instant upload is available to Partners and Affiliates who meet certain criteria. For more information on how instant upload works, click here.
Why is my emote rejected, when I see more objectionable or similar content elsewhere on Twitch?
If you see any content on Twitch that you believe does not uphold our Emote Guidelines or Community Guidelines, you may report that content or channel by Filing a User Report.
Rejection of your emote does not necessarily mean approval of similar emotes. You may report any content on Twitch that you do not believe upholds our Emote Guidelines or Community Guidelines.
I am bothered by an emote showing up in my channel but it does not violate Twitch’s rules. How can I avoid seeing it?
If you do not like seeing an emote in your chatroom on your channel, but it does not violate any of our guidelines, you can still hide it from appearing in your channel by adding it to your Channel Blocked Terms. Words - including emote codes - added as Blocked Terms will appear in your chat as ***.

Emote Library

Whenever you upload an emote, it is saved within your Library. The Library allows you to save and manage your emotes independently from slots. Emotes within your library will be grayed out if they are assigned to a slot or lit up if they are available. If your emotes are pending approval, they will have a watch icon. You can have a pending emote assigned to a slot. Just note that your viewers will not be able to see it until it is approved and the watch icon disappears.

Your Emote Library

Your Library will automatically expand as you open more emote slots. As your Library of emotes expands, the ability to sort, filter, and search will allow you to quickly find the emotes you’re looking for.

This means that as a new Affiliate, you will have a standard emote Library capacity of 35 and an animated emote Library capacity of 5. Partners with all emote slots unlocked will have a standard emote Library capacity of 350 and an animated emote Library capacity of 25.

You can assign or reassign an emote from the Library to a slot by clicking on an emote and selecting Slot Assignment. The dropdown will provide a list of options for assignment. Once you’ve made your selection, the emote will be added to the end of the active emote slots for that assignment.

If the slots for a given assignment are full, the option will be grayed out. You can fix this by removing emotes from slots, which will make them unavailable to viewers but will still save them in your library should you choose to use them later. You can remove an emote from a slot either directly through the Library or by clicking on Remove from Slot on the slot itself.

At a certain point, you may reach your Library capacity, which will prevent you from uploading additional emotes until some are deleted. You can delete an emote from your Library by clicking on an emote and selecting Delete from Library. This will permanently remove the emote from your Library and any slot it is currently assigned to upon confirmation.

Frequently Asked Questions

How is my Library capacity determined?

As a new Affiliate, you have a standard emote Library capacity of 35 and an animated emote Library capacity of 5. Partners with all emote slots unlocked will have a standard emote Library capacity of 350 and an animated emote Library capacity of 25.

Can I upload multiple emotes with the same name into my Library?

Yes, but you cannot have two emotes with the same name assigned to slots at the same time. Example: You can have two “Happy” emotes in your Library, but only one of them can be assigned to your emote slots.

For Partners, are Cheermotes part of the Library?

No, Cheermotes are not supported within the library at this time due to differing upload requirements.

Enhanced Broadcasting with Multiple Encodes

When you stream to Twitch, we might create different video qualities (called “transcodes”) from your original stream. For example, if you stream in high quality 1080p, we might also make versions in 720p and 480p. This helps viewers with slow internet or older devices watch your stream without buffering.

Not all streams get Twitch-provided multiple qualities every time. However, with Enhanced Broadcasting, you can now send multiple video qualities directly from your broadcasting software (like OBS Studio, Meld, Streamlabs, or XSplit Broadcaster). This ensures your viewers always have different quality options to choose from, improving their watching experience.

Enhanced broadcasting is the technology that enables Dual Format Streaming and 2k (1440p) Streaming on Twitch by providing support for multiple client-side encodes (similar to transcodes) and automatic stream configuration. You can check your eligibility for Dual Format and 2K in your creator dashboard in Stream > Settings. Enhanced Broadcasting is required to use Dual Format and/or 2K, even if you qualify for added server-side transcode support for those streams.

We recently added server-side transcode support for Dual Format and 2k Streams using Enhanced Broadcasting to reduce strain and resolve performance issues. Learn more.

Multiple Client-Side Encodes

Transcoding is a process that creates multiple video qualities of your original high-quality streamed content. Providing multiple video qualities enables viewers experiencing poor network conditions, or those watching on older devices to watch your content without buffering. Transcodes are provided to many (but not all) Twitch streamers and are generated in Twitch datacenters. Multiple Encodes are generated directly from your source content in your broadcast software, and produce multiple video qualities, improving the experience for viewers.

Automatic Stream Configuration

Understanding complicated video settings to achieve the highest video quality can be time consuming and frustrating. By sending information about your setup to Twitch, automatic stream configuration removes the need for offline trial and error to find the correct settings. A server-side algorithm then returns the best possible configuration for broadcast software that optimizes the viewer experience given constraints in your setup.

Getting Started

To try Enhanced Broadcasting, first upgrade to OBS Studio v30.2 or XSplit Broadcaster 4.5.2406.1801 or newer. Then, enable Enhanced Broadcasting within the broadcast software settings. Use Twitch Inspector to monitor your broadcast and debug any networking issues.

Learn more about Twitch Inspector here: Guide to Using Twitch Inspector

Streaming with Enhanced Broadcasting in OBS Studio

The following instructions must be completed in OBS Studio.

  • Upgrade to OBS Studio v30.2 (or newer) by going to Help -> Check for Updates, or by downloading the newest version from OBS Project’s Download page.
  • At Settings -> Video, confirm your Base (Canvas) Resolution, Output (Scaled) Resolution, and framerate settings.

You can select a larger Canvas resolution (e.g. 3840x2160) for recording a local VOD, but the live stream’s largest video track will never be larger than the Scaled resolution. For the best performance (and the most efficient utilization of your GPU), we recommend setting them both to either 1920x1080 or 1280x720 and 60fps.

  • At Settings -> Stream, select Twitch for Service, click Connect Account (recommended), and proceed to login to Twitch. In the Multitrack Video section, check the Enable Enhanced Broadcasting checkbox.

While we recommend most streamers leave Auto checked, you can optionally configure Maximum Streaming Bandwidth or Maximum Video Tracks. These advanced options are limits you can use to constrain the amount of resources (network bandwidth and GPU encoding capacity respectively) that Enhanced Broadcasting may use. It’s important to note that these are upper limits, not a target or preference.

  • Start streaming and monitor your stream using Twitch Inspector.

If you are trying to stream in 2k (1440p) or in Dual Format, this will require extra set up. Enhanced Broadcasting is the technology that powers 2k and Dual Format streams. Learn more about how to set up Dual Format and 2k (1440p) streams.

Streaming With Enhanced Broadcasting in XSplit Broadcaster

The following instructions must be completed in XSplit Broadcaster.

  • Upgrade to XSplit Broadcaster 4.5.2406.1801 (or newer) by going to Help -> Check for Updates or by downloading the newest versions from XSplit’s Download page. Make sure that the Twitch plugin is updated to the newest version by going to Tools -> Plugin Store.
  • Go to Broadcast -> Setup a new output -> Twitch and proceed to login to Twitch.
  • In the Video Encoding -> Codec section, select NVENC H.264 (NVIDIA …) and check the Enable Enhanced Broadcasting checkbox.

While we recommend most streamers leave Auto checked, you can optionally configure Maximum Streaming Bandwidth or Maximum Video Tracks. These advanced options are limits you can use to constrain the amount of resources (network bandwidth and GPU encoding capacity respectively) that Enhanced Broadcasting may use. It’s important to note that these are upper limits, not a target or preference.

  • At the top right, confirm your Resolution and Frame rate.

  • Start streaming and monitor your stream using Twitch Inspector.

Dual Format and 2k Streaming: Benefits of Enhanced Broadcasting

Streamers using Enhanced Broadcasting can optimize their viewing experience and reach more viewers across mobile, web, and TV with Dual Format Streaming and 2k Streaming. These features both require Enhanced Broadcasting.

Dual Format Streaming allows you to send both a horizontal and a vertical version of your broadcast to Twitch at the same time. This lets you reach more viewers with an optimized experience—no matter what device they’re using. Desktop and TV viewers will continue to see your standard horizontal broadcast. Mobile viewers will see a new, full-screen vertical view when holding their phone upright, or the standard horizontal view when they rotate their device. Dual Format streaming is available to all streamers on Twitch.

2k (1440p) Streaming offers a noticeable step up from 1080p streaming, with richer detail, improved clarity, and better performance—whether you’re gaming, making art, or just chatting. Higher quality streams unlock access to 2k Clips and VODs for you and your viewers, too. 2k streaming is limited to Affiliates and Partners only.

You can stream in Dual Format and 2k (1440p) at the same time for the best viewing experience.

Added Server-Side Transcode Support: To reduce strain on your system and improve performance, Twitch also provides added server-side transcode support for these streams for Partners and select Affiliates. This added server-side transcode support lets us utilize your GPU to encode the highest-resolution horizontal and vertical streams, while using server-side transcoding to fill in all the lower resolutions. Ultimately, this results in your viewers getting a higher-quality experience across all formats. Check your Advanced Broadcast Settings on the Stream Settings page in your Creator Dashboard to see if you have access to added server-side transcode support for Dual Format and 2k streams.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who has access to Enhanced Broadcasting?
Enhanced broadcasting is available to all streamers on Twitch. Dual Format, a feature that requires Enhanced Broadcasting technology, is also available to all streamers on Twitch. 2k streaming also requires Enhanced Broadcasting and is limited to Affiliates and Partners at this time.
How much overhead is generated by multiple encodes? Does it impact my content creator tools or gameplay?

When you use your GPU (graphics card) for video encoding, it should not significantly affect gaming performance – Modern GPUs have a dedicated chip just for video encoding, so they can handle it without slowing down your games. Even with older GPUs like the NVIDIA GeForce 900 series, our testers played fast-paced games and didn’t notice any difference in performance.

However, we know it can put strain on some systems. After hearing this feedback during beta testing, we have rolled out added Server-Side Transcode Support for Enhanced Broadcasting Streams in Dual Format and 2k: To reduce strain on your system and improve performance, Twitch also provides added server-side transcode support for these streams for Partners and select Affiliates. This added server-side transcode support lets us utilize your GPU to encode the highest-resolution horizontal and vertical streams, while using server-side transcoding to fill in all the lower resolutions. Ultimately, this results in your viewers getting a higher-quality experience across all formats. Check your Advanced Broadcast Settings on the Stream Settings page in your Creator Dashboard to see if you have access to added server-side transcode support for Dual Format and 2k streams. Please note that this added support is not available for regular Enhanced Broadcasting streams and is limited to Dual Format or 2k Enhanced Broadcasting streams for qualifying users.

What renditions/qualities will multiple encodes generate and deliver to my viewers?
Automatic stream configuration optimizes for viewer experience, so it will depend. Automatic stream configuration uses various factors like screen size, broadcasting software settings, GPU/CPU models, OS/drivers version, and network speed. To balance the best viewer experience, performance impact to your system, and your available internet bandwidth, you will receive a configuration that may change every time you start streaming.
How does the viewer experience change based on my system, or environmental factors?
Every time you start streaming with Enhanced Broadcasting, automatic stream configuration chooses a configuration that optimizes for the best possible viewer experience. To make the most out of your setup, the configurations may:
  • Vary the total streaming bandwidth between 10.5 Mbps and 1.5 Mbps.
  • Vary the highest quality track’s maximum resolution from 1080p60 down to 480p.
  • Vary the number of renditions between 5 and 2.
  • Vary the selection of renditions across an expansive set of supported resolutions (1080p, 720p, 540p, 480p, 360p, 240p, and 160p).
  • Vary the video bitrate of individual renditions from 6 Mbps (e.g., 1080p AVC) down to 200 Kbps (e.g., 160p AVC).
  • Vary the framerate between high (60, 50, or 48 fps) and standard (30, 25, or 24 fps).
  • Vary the scaler algorithm to balance quality with GPU utilization (e.g., Lanczos, bicubic, and bilinear).
  • Vary video encoder settings (including codec profile, encoder preset, look-ahead window, psycho visual AQ, and number of B-frames), depending on the GPU vendor and driver version.

First-Time Chatter Highlight

Welcoming newcomers boosts engagement and encourages viewers to keep coming back to the stream. The First-Time Chatter highlight makes it easier to grow your community by helping creators and mods see who’s new to the chat.

What is First-Time Chatter Highlight

Messages from first-time chatters are now highlighted for creators in the Stream Manager in the bottom left corner view of chat.

No set up is required for the highlight to appear. The highlight is only visible to you and your mods and can be toggled off in your Chat Settings.

Mod View

Mods can view the First-Time Chatter Highlight in the Chat panel to the right of the stream.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does everyone see the First-Time Chatter Highlight in chat?

Only the creator and mods can see the First-Time Chatter Highlight.

Can I turn this feature off?

Yes, you can toggle it off in your Chat Settings.

Follower Emotes

Follower Emotes let creators grow their communities by offering viewers a fun, free benefit to hitting the “Follow” button. Follower Emote are available to all Partners and Affiliates.

Creators can select up to five emotes to populate the new free tier, accessed via the Emotes page of Creator Dashboard. Upload new emotes, reassign them from other tiers, or choose from a selection of default emotes provided by Twitch. Follower Emotes must follow all emote guidelines.

Thanks to your feedback, Follower Emotes can now be used by subscribers in any channel on Twitch. Followers who are not subscribers may continue to use Follower Emotes only within that channel itself.

On this page:

  • Managing Follower Emotes
  • Using Follower Emotes
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Managing Follower Emotes

For step by step information on how to upload your emotes, please see our Subscriber Emote Guide.

Assigning Follower Emotes

You can assign emotes to this tier from the Emotes page on the Creator Dashboard. On the left-hand sidebar, click Viewer Rewards, then Emotes. Creators with beta access will see a callout at the top of the page inviting them to populate the Follower Emotes tier.

To add emotes to the Follower tier from your Library, select Follower from the Slot Assignment drop down menu.

Managing Follower Emotes

You can rearrange, delete, reassign, and reupload Follower Emotes from the Emotes page of your Creator Dashboard or from your Library.

Using Follower Emotes

Follower Emotes can be unlocked for free by following a channel that has them available. Viewers will see a call out in Chat once Follower Emotes have been added.

Call out as seen by a viewer that hasn’t followed the channel

Call out as seen by a viewer that’s already following

Thanks to your feedback, Follower Emotes can now be used by subscribers in any channel on Twitch. Follower who are not subscribers may continue to use Follower Emotes only within that channel itself.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can Follower Emotes be used across Twitch if I subscribe to the channel where I unlocked them?

Yes! At this time, subscribers may use Follower Emotes outside the channel where they are unlocked.

Are Follower Emotes available on mobile?

Yes, Follower Emote are available on the Twitch Mobile Apps.

Who can upload Follower Emotes?

Follower Emotes can be uploaded by Partners and Affiliates.

If I subscribe to a channel but don’t follow, can I access Follower Emotes?

No, you must follow the channel in order to unlock its Follower Emotes.

How Do I Stream FAQ

Through streaming, broadcasters create a dynamic, engaging relationship with their audience. There’s no single way to stream on Twitch. This guide is intended to help you get started by answering common questions, and is not a single comprehensive guide.

For more specific help setting up your profile, customizing your channel, and optimizing your setup, visit the Go Live section of Creator Camp. For stream configuration help, view our broadcast guidelines: help.twitch.tv/s/article/broadcasting-guidelines

What is streaming on Twitch?

At its most basic, live streaming is broadcasting audio and video over the internet in real-time. At Twitch, the main information pipeline for a stream starts with you. A broadcaster sends a video stream to Twitch over the public internet using any of several tools. Your stream arrives at the Twitch ingest subsystem, where your stream is authenticated and prepared for distribution. Once your stream enters our system, Twitch beams it all over the world. Learn more at help.twitch.tv/s/article/broadcasting-guidelines

What do I need to start streaming?

All you need to start streaming is a stable internet connection and a tool that can broadcast video to the internet, also known as a video encoder. This can be a physical device like a gaming console or device (Xbox, PS4, Nintendo Switch) or software like Twitch Studio, the mobile Twitch App (iOS and Android), OBS, to name a few. To learn more, visit the Go Live section in Creator Camp!

Do I need a powerful computer to stream on Twitch?

No! Compelling content can come from anywhere. It doesn’t matter whether your video encoding device is a powerful battlestation PC, a mobile phone, game console, laptop, or a potato.

Do I need a mic and/or camera to stream?

No, you don’t need a mic or camera to stream. However, an important part of streaming on Twitch is the interaction between the streamer and audience. For more information on recommended stream hardware, visit Setting Up Your Stream Hardware in the Go Live section of Creator Camp.

Can I stream without a good or stable internet connection?

For the best experience for your viewers, a good or stable network connection is required to stream on Twitch. A stable internet connection must have adequate upload bandwidth and upload speed.

As a general practice, streamers should ensure that their upload speed is equal to the bitrate at which they have set their stream +30%. For example, attempting to stream at 6mbps (megabits per second) may require a network upload speed of at least 8mbps. Additionally, ensure that there are no other devices on the network utilizing your upload bandwidth, as that will affect your upload speed. Measure your connection’s download and upload speed, and ping time using any browser speed test tool.

For a glossary of terms including bitrate, visit Twitch Inspector Glossary.

How can I run a test stream before going live?

To help ensure that your stream will be successful, you have the ability to run a network test. Learn more in Twitch Stream Key FAQ.

What do I do if I am experiencing stuttering or buffering?

Twitch Inspector allows you to review critical health information about your stream. Learn more about Twitch Inspector here. For further information, view our Guide to Stream Health.

How do I tell if a stream problem is on my end, or Twitch?

Visit the Troubleshooting section of our Guide to Stream Health.

How Drops Work

Looking for something else? This guide covers the basics of earning Drops on Twitch. For troubleshooting (progress not counting, linking issues, missing rewards), see Drops Troubleshooting. For Poké Balls, Daily Watch Progress, and Pokémon Collection mechanics, see Pokémon Chat Badge Drops Campaign. For redeeming codes on partner websites, visit our Code-Based Drops Redemption Guide.

Drops campaigns reward you for watching or supporting your favorite channels. Rewards can be automatically delivered in-game items, redeemable codes for a partner’s website or service, or Twitch extras like unique emotes or chat badges. If a channel is participating in a Drops campaign, you will see a banner at the top of chat and a Drops icon at the bottom of chat. Interact with either to see available Drops and track your progress.

Drops are unlocked by meeting requirements set by the game developer or promotional partner, to earn a reward. Once you complete the requirement, you will be able to claim the reward. You can only gain progress toward a reward on one channel at a time. You can check on the progress you have earned towards any reward by going to your Drops Inventory page, or by using the Drops & More panel in chat. From the Drops Inventory page you can claim any unclaimed Drops rewards for up to 7 days (168 hours) after the Drops campaign has ended.

This guide covers steps on how to earn Drops rewards. Most Drops rewards are automatically added to your connected game accounts, but some campaigns provide codes to redeem on third-party company websites. Learn more: Code-Based Drops Redemption Guide.

What Are You Trying To Do?

Choose the option that best describes your situation:

I want to start earning Drops

→ How to Earn Drops (Basics)

I want to check my Drops progress in chat

→ Tracking Drops in Chat

I want to know how Event Drops work

→ Event Drops

I’m having a problem or issue with Drops

→ Drops Troubleshooting

→ Pokémon Chat Badge Drops Campaign
