How to Earn Drops (Basics)

New to Drops? Here’s how to get started:

Important: Earning Drops has 3 separate steps: (1) Earn on Twitch (User’s/Twitch’s responsibility) → (2) Claim on Twitch (Twitch’s responsibility) → (3) Deliver to game (game developer’s responsibility)

Step 1: Link Your Game Account FIRST
  • Go to Drops Inventory
  • Find the campaign you want to participate in
  • Click “Connect” next to the game name
  • You’ll be redirected to the game developer’s website to link accounts
  • Verify the connection shows on both Twitch and the game’s website

You can still claim rewards and connect your account afterwards, but linking first prevents issues.

Step 2: Watch Drops-Enabled Streams
  • Find channels with “Drops Enabled” tag
  • Watch the stream (must be live, not VOD/replay)
  • Check your progress in chat using the Drops & More panel, or at Drops Inventory
  • Remember: You can only earn progress on ONE campaign at a time
Multi-Day Requirement

Some Drops campaigns require you to watch across multiple, separate days rather than in one continuous session. Each day is its own requirement, and you need to hit that day’s minimum watch time for the day to count.

How a Day Is Counted

A “day” is a rolling 24-hour window that opens the moment you start accruing watch time toward that reward. Because the window is based on when you start watching, a single day’s requirement may span two calendar dates.

If a window closes before you’ve watched the full required minutes, those minutes are discarded. They don’t carry into your next window - but days you’ve already completed are never affected.

This is different from Watch Streaks. Watch Streaks track consecutive days of watching a specific streamer for a loyalty reward. A multi-day Drops requirement counts a total number of days and does not have to be consecutive.

Step 3: Claim Your Drop

When you meet the requirements for a Drop, we’ll notify you. If you’re in chat, click “Claim” and head to your Drops Inventory for more details.

  • Click “Claim” in the Drops & More panel in chat
  • Click the claim notification that appears in chat
  • Visit your Drops Inventory page
Step 4: Wait for Delivery

Most rewards appear in-game within 24-48 hours. Some are instant, a few take up to 7 days. Check the campaign details for specific timelines.

Two types of rewards: Most Drops are automatically delivered to your game. Some give you a code to enter on a partner website. Learn about code-based Drops.

Subscription Requirement

Some Drops campaigns require a subscription purchase instead of (or in addition to) watch time. Before you purchase a subscription to earn a Drop, know what counts:

Prime subscriptions do not count towards subscription-based Drops. Only new paid subscriptions count.

Type

Counts Towards Drops?

Prime Sub

No

Existing Subscription Renewal

No

Sub Tokens

No

New Gift Subscription (any amount, any Tier)

Yes

New 1-Month Recurring Subscription (any Tier)

Yes

New 3-Month Recurring Subscription (any Tier)

Yes

New 6-Month Recurring Subscription (any Tier)

Yes

Subscriptions must be purchased while the channel is live in the correct category, during an active Drops campaign to count.

Event Drops

Some Drops are earned by being there for a live moment, like an in-stream win or achievement, instead of by watch time. When the moment happens, everyone watching a participating channel earns the Drop at the same time. Event Drops are a surprise: there’s no notice before the moment happens, and if you aren’t watching when it does, you can’t earn that Drop later.

  • Watch live when it happens. You need to have watched a participating channel for at least 1 minute, and still be watching in the 5 minutes before the moment. At the moment, channels don’t show ahead of time whether they’re participating.
  • Claim it. We’ll notify you as soon as you earn the Drop. If your reward needs to be claimed, claim it from your Drops Inventory within 7 days. For in-game items, link your game account first, then claim.

You can’t earn an Event Drop by watching a VOD or rerun, or after the moment has passed. Missed Event Drops can’t be recovered or granted later.

Tracking Drops in Chat

You can track your progress towards Drops rewards in chat without leaving the stream. There are two ways to open the Drops & More panel:

Opening the Drops & More Panel

Option 1: Drops icon at the bottom of chat

Look for the Drops icon in the icon bar at the bottom of chat (next to the Bits and Channel Points icons). Tap or click it to open the Drops & More panel. This icon only appears if the channel has active Drops available on it.

Option 2: Banner at the top of chat

When a channel has active Drops available to earn, a banner appears at the top of chat showing a featured Drop and how many more are available. Tap or click the banner to open the Drops & More panel.

Using the Drops & More Panel

The Drops & More panel shows all available Drops on the channel, grouped by how you earn them:

  • Subscription Drops — Earned by purchasing a new subscription or gift subscription on the channel
  • Watchtime Drops — Earned by watching the stream for a set amount of time

Each Drop shows:

  • The reward you can earn
  • The game or partner offering the reward
  • Your current progress (for example, “Watch 30m to earn”)
  • An EXPIRING SOON badge if the campaign is ending

Tap a category to see more details about your progress and the available rewards in that group.

The Drops & More panel appears even if you haven’t linked your game account yet. You can track progress and claim rewards before linking, but you’ll need to link your game account for rewards to be delivered in-game.

Claiming Sub Drops

After purchasing a qualifying subscription, the Drops & More panel may not update immediately. Close the panel and look for a claim notification in chat. You can also check your Drops Inventory page to claim the reward.

The Drops & More panel in chat shows your progress on the channel you’re currently watching. To see progress across all campaigns, visit your Drops Inventory page.

Turn Off Drops Notifications

Problem: You’re getting too many Drops notifications and want to turn them off.

Option 1: Turn off all Drops notifications
  • Go to Twitch Settings → Notifications
  • Scroll to “Marketing”
  • Uncheck “Drops & Quests”
  • Click “Save Changes”
Option 2: Turn off notifications for specific channels
  • Go to the channel page
  • Click the bell icon
  • Select “None” or customize notification types

Important: Disabling notifications does NOT stop you from earning Drops. You can still participate in Drops campaigns - you just won’t get notifications about them.

Frequently Asked Questions

Check below to see if your question has been answered.

Sections:
  • Viewer FAQ
  • Streamer FAQ
Viewer FAQ
What are Drops?
Drops are rewards granted to you for participating in channels you love! Each Drop has a requirement set by the game developer. Requirements can include watch time or eligible subscription purchase(s). By meeting a Drops campaign’s requirement, you earn the Drop and the associated reward. You can check your progress any time by visiting the Drops Inventory page.
What are Creator Badge Drops?
Creator Badge Drops are custom badges that creators offer during time-limited events. When you complete a qualifying action during an active event (such as subscribing or watching for a set duration), you’ll earn the badge and can display it in chat in that channel. Creator Badge Drops appear in the Drops & Rewards panel alongside other Drops campaigns. Learn more: Creator Badge Drops.
Can I have my Twitch account connected to more than one game account?
Yes, you can connect your Twitch account to as many game accounts as you want, but you can only have one account per developer. You can connect your Twitch account to multiple different game accounts, but you cannot connect multiple accounts of a single game to one Twitch account.
How do I claim and receive a Drop?
You must meet the Drop’s requirements to earn rewards. Reward requirements can include accruing watch time in a participating channel to receive progress towards the Drop, or completing the eligible subscription purchase requirement. When you watch for the required amount of time, or complete the subscription purchase requirement on a participating channel, a claim message will appear at the top of the Twitch navigation, where you’ll be directed to the Drops Inventory page to claim your reward. If you miss the claim message, you will still be able to claim the Drop for the duration of the campaign from the Drops Inventory page.
Do I need to watch the same channel the entire time to earn Drops from a campaign?
No, you can earn progress towards a Drop on any participating channel for a campaign. For example, you can watch for a half hour on one channel and then switch to another channel and continue your progress for the Drop.

Important - You can only earn progress for one channel at a time! Watching more than one channel at the same time will not allow you to claim the Drop faster.

What is a subscription?
A subscription is a way for viewers to support their favorite Twitch streamers. When you subscribe to a channel, you are charged monthly (depending on renewal period) while gaining access to exclusive benefits. Learn more.
What devices can I use to claim Drops?
Drops supports using your PC/Mac web browser or on the Twitch app for Android and iOS to earn and claim Drops. Twitch apps on game consoles, smart TVs, and other TV apps do not support Drops at this time.
Why can’t I claim some items on the Twitch iOS app?
Drops that grant rewards for iOS apps & games do not support claiming through the Twitch iOS app at this time.
Where can I see my progress towards earning a Drop?
You can check your progress in two ways:
  • In chat: Use the Drops & More panel — tap the Drops icon at the bottom of chat or the Drops banner at the top of chat to see your progress on the current channel.
  • Drops Inventory: Visit the Drops Inventory page to see progress across all active campaigns.
Is there a schedule of Drops occurring in different games/channels?
You can see all active Drops and participating channels on the Drops campaigns page..
How can I tell if a specific game has Drops?
There are a few ways to tell:
  • On a specific channel: Look for the “Drops Enabled” tag, a Drops banner at the top of chat, or the Drops icon at the bottom of chat.
  • All Campaigns page: Check the All Campaigns page in your Drops inventory for current campaign information (including which games offer Drops, eligibility requirements, or reward details).

Game developers decide which games participate in Drops campaigns. If you’d like to see a particular game offer Drops (or want to know if an upcoming, unreleased game will offer Drops), contact the game publisher directly.

I think I got a Drop, but why hasn’t the item shown up in my game account?
The game developer is responsible for fulfilling the Drop rewards in the game and in some cases, this may take time to process. Please contact the specific game developer directly for any questions. You can do some initial troubleshooting by checking that the item has shown up on your Drops Inventory page and that your game account is linked to the correct Twitch account.
Is there a maximum number of Drops I can receive on a specific channel/all channels?
The game developer defines the limit for how many Drops you can receive and this limit will vary by campaign.
How long do I have to link my account to get my Drop rewards?
Most game developers will fulfill the reward if you link your account within 14 days of the relevant Drops campaign ending. If the reward is only usable for a limited time (e.g. beta event), then other time restrictions may apply.
Why can I no longer see some of the Drops items that I previously earned on my Drops Inventory page?
All Drops rewards disappear from the Drops inventory after 6 months.

All items earned from the Drops service will continue to be visible on the Drops Inventory page.

Who do I contact if I have issues with Drops?
Contact Twitch Support if:
  • You can’t earn progress toward a Drop on Twitch
  • You can’t claim a reward from your Drops Inventory
  • You didn’t receive a code after completing requirements

Contact Twitch Support here

For all other issues, contact the game developer/publisher or promotional partner. Visit our Code-Based Drops Redemption Guide to understand who can help and how to contact the right support team (Twitch or the promotional partner).

If I start on day 2 of a campaign, can I still get day 1 Drops?
It depends on the campaign. Some campaigns let you earn previous days’ Drops, others are time-limited to specific dates. Check the campaign details in your Drops Inventory.
When can I earn minutes toward the next day of a multi-day requirement?
A “day” is a rolling 24-hour window that opens the moment you start accruing watch time toward that reward - not a calendar day. Because the window is based on when you started watching, a single day’s requirement may span two calendar dates. Once that window closes (whether or not you completed it), you can start a new window by watching a participating channel again.
Do Drops expire?
Yes. Once you claim a Drop on Twitch, you usually have 7-30 days to redeem it (varies by campaign). Check your Drops Inventory for expiration dates. Unclaimed Drops expire when the campaign ends.
What happens if a campaign ends before I finish earning a Drop?
You lose progress. If you’re at 80% when the campaign ends, you cannot finish earning that Drop.
Can I pause my progress and come back later?
Yes, as long as the campaign is still active. Your progress is saved. You can watch different streams or take breaks.
As a streamer, do I earn Drops from my own channel?
No. You cannot earn viewer Drops from your own channel while streaming. You must watch other Drops-enabled channels to earn rewards.
Can viewers earn Drops by viewing reruns or VODs?
No. Only live streams are eligible for viewers to earn Drop rewards.
I was watching when the event happened. Why didn’t I get the Event Drop?
Check that you:
  • Were logged in and watching a participating channel for at least 1 minute in the 5 minutes before the moment
  • Meet the campaign’s region and age requirements
  • Linked your game account and claimed the reward within 7 days, if it’s an in-game item
If you met all of these and the Drop isn’t in your Drops Inventory, see Drops Troubleshooting. If you weren’t watching when the moment happened, the Drop can’t be recovered or granted later.
Can I find out when an Event Drop will happen?
Not currently. Event Drops are a surprise, so there’s no notice before the moment happens. The only way to earn one is to be watching a participating channel when it does.
Streamer FAQ
As a streamer, how do I turn Drops on / off for particular game sessions?
Go to your Dashboard settings. From there, click on Viewer Rewards and then Drops (or visit directly - dashboard.twitch.tv/drops) to change your opt-out preference. You can quickly turn Drops on/off through a toggle at the top of this page. You can also opt out of Drop campaigns at the individual campaign level while still participating in other Drop campaigns by other game developers.
As a streamer, why would I toggle Drops off rather than completely disconnecting my Twitch account?
Turning Drops off through your dashboard toggle will result in your viewers not being able to earn progress for Drops on your channel.You also have the flexibility to have Drops disabled on a per campaign basis, while still have Drops enabled for other campaigns by simply updating the enable toggle. Connecting or disconnecting your game developer account with Twitch will no longer impact whether your channel participates with Drops or not. Keep in mind that your Twitch and Game account link may power Drop rewards you’ve earned as a viewer and other additional features on Twitch or within a game that is unrelated to Drops.
As a streamer, how do I offer Drops on my channel for my viewers?
Game developers decide which channels are eligible to offer Drops. If they have activated Drops for all channels broadcasting their game (or yours specifically), Drops can appear on your channel for your viewers. All you need to do is make sure Drops are enabled by visiting the Drops section within your Dashboard (see Drops Streamer Home).
As a streamer, do I need to add the “DropsEnabled” tag when I’m streaming?
No. If there is an active Drops campaign for a specific game, you are streaming the game, you have opted in, set the stream category to the game, and your channel is eligible to offer the Drop campaign to your viewers, we will automatically apply the “DropsEnabled” tag to your live stream.
Can viewers earn Drops by viewing my reruns of my VODs?
No. Only your live streams are eligible for viewers to earn Drop rewards.
As a streamer, do Drops earned with a subscription requirement on my channel impact my revenue share?
No. Subscription revenue earned from Drops campaign purchases are paid out to streamers at their usual rev share rate.
As a streamer, can I see how many subscriptions to my channel came from users earning Drops with a subscription requirement?
Not directly. However, once the Drops campaign concludes, you can compare the period the campaign was active to previous periods using your Channel Analytics. This may help you understand changes in subscriptions gained over time.
As a streamer, how do I offer Event Drops on my channel?
The game developer or event organizer chooses which channels take part in an Event Drop. You can’t opt in on your own.

How to Set Your Ad Schedule

Partners and Affiliates: Click here to visit your Ads Manager.

Twitch’s Ads Manager tool allows Partners and Affiliates to set and forget their ad schedule, removing guesswork. Partners and Affiliates can use the Ads Manager to help maximize their potential ad revenue while also maintaining a positive viewing experience for their audience.

About Ads on Twitch

Ads represent an important monetization tool for streamers. Twitch Partners and Affiliates can earn a percentage of the ad revenue from ads shown on their channels, known as Net Ad Revenue Share.

Ads Manager Settings

We’ve updated the Ads Manager experience based on feedback from streamers like you. We’ve created a new ad density slider and reorganized where features are. Partners, you’ll also now see the revenue estimates that used to be part of the Ads Incentive Program!

Get Started Here!

Ads Manager

Enable this to have Ads Manager automatically schedule video ads on your channel.

Ad Minutes Per Hour

This slider determines how many minutes of ads will be run on your channel per hour. We offer a few preset settings: Low, Recommended, and High. Ad minutes at the Recommended and High settings will unlock 55% net ad revenue share. Running 3 minutes of ads will disable pre-roll video ads for incoming viewers.

Ad Length and Frequency

After choosing your total Ad Minutes Per Hour, you can adjust how long the ads are, and how frequently they appear.

Choose Automatic to let Twitch adjust ad length and frequency based on available ad demand and time of year. This helps Twitch determine the optimal settings to improve your ad revenue and viewership.

Choose Manual to choose between shorter ads that occur more often, and longer ads that occur less often.

The slider option to control Ad Length and Frequency only appears if you choose more than 3 minutes of ads per hour.

Advanced Ads Manager Settings

For more control, visit Advanced Settings.

First Ad Delay

After your stream starts, set this to determine the length of time you want Ads manager to wait before running ads.

Auto-Snooze Ads

Enable this setting to automatically snooze ads during high engagement moments, like Hype Trains. Learn more.

Ad-Free Viewing

Allow subscribers to watch content on your channel ad-free.

This can also be managed in your subscription settings.

Notifications

Enable or disable notifications, should you allow them to appear, only visible to you or your mods.

Choose to be notified:

  • 20 minutes before ad starts
  • 15 minutes before ad starts
  • 10 minutes before ad starts
  • 5 minutes before ad starts
  • 1 minute before ad starts

You can enable this for your moderators. Please note this gives Moderators the ability to snooze ads.

Additional Ads Manager Settings

Manage your Ad Formats and Notifications for all ad running.

Pre-rolls

Choose to keep pre-roll ads on your channel, or disable them.

Every 30 seconds of mid-roll ads grants your channel 10 minutes of no pre-roll ads. This means a total of 3 minutes per hour of mid-roll ads are required to remove pre-roll ads for 60 minutes.

Pre-roll Notification

Enable dashboard notifications and be alerted when pre-roll ads are enabled or disabled. For more settings on Notifications, visit Advanced Settings.

Stream Display Ads

Enable this to run Stream Display Ads on your channel. Learn more.

Revenue Share for Advertisement / Net Ad Revenue Share

View your net ad revenue share for Advertisements run on your channel.

Quick Action

For easy access to key Ads Manager settings, streamers can add to their Quick Actions in their Stream Manager. To access these Quick Actions.

  • Visit your Stream Manager
  • Click the Add icon
  • Choose the option you’d like to add to your Quick Actions

Visit your Stream Manager here.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does the new Ads Manager update or remove any features?
No it does not. This is only an update to the User Interface. We wanted to revisit your fundamental experience with Ads Manager instead of introducing new features; this was validated via user research studies and feedback we received from the community.
Are there any changes to revenue share?
There are no changes to the existing ad revenue share, nor the mechanics to unlock 55% net revenue share. Simply run at least 3 minutes of ads per hour via Ads Manager to unlock 55% net revenue share. You do not have to stream a minimum amount of hours to unlock this.
How does this work with the Plus Program?
The Plus Program is specific to recurring and gift subscriptions. Ads Manager is designed to make it easier for your community to support your content by watching ads without directly purchasing Subscriptions or Bits.
Is Ads Incentive Program going away?
Yes. With the new version of Ads Manager, the additional steps of using Ads Incentive Program are no longer needed. Revenue estimates remain available to Partners. Both Partners and Affiliates can automatically earn 55% net ad revenue by running at least 3 ad minutes per hour.
For Partners, how accurate are your forecasting tools?
Our forecasting tools leverage historical data that spans across viewership levels, categories, and regions to provide projections. As you stream and use Ads Manager more, our forecasting tools will get “smarter” and more accurate.
Can I just choose to run more display ads instead of more video ads?
Since Stream Display Ads are less interruptive than other formats, they are designed to run automatically with no control from streamers. Streamers earn the majority of ad revenue through video ads.
How can I remove pre-roll video ads from my channel?
To completely remove pre-roll video ads from your stream for an hour, you must run at least 3 minutes of mid-roll ads per hour via Ads Manager. As long as you do this, that hour will continue to reset to remove pre-roll video ads from your viewers for that streaming session.
My revenue estimate does not seem to be accurate
Revenue estimates are meant to give you an idea of potential ad revenue earnings in the following month. They are designed to give you an idea of potential ad revenue to help you make the best decisions for running ads on your channel.
Is Ads Manager an optional tool for streamers?
Yes, Ads Manager is an optional tool.
Does disabling Ads Manager remove ads from my channel entirely?
No. Disabling Ads Manager removes your chosen scheduling from the amount of ads run on your channel per hour. You can remove pre-roll ads by setting your Ads Manager to at least 3 minutes of mid-roll ads per hour.
Am I required to use Ads Manager on my channel?
Viewers will still see ads, even if you don’t enable the Ads Manager scheduler. Ads Manager allows you to control key aspects of ads per hour of streamed content, and provides other useful info.
Do pre-rolls count towards the required 3 minutes of ads per hour to disable pre-roll ads, and earn 55% net ad revenue share?
No, 3 minutes of mid-roll ads must be run per 60 minutes to unlock these things.
How often does my ad revenue refresh within my Earnings Analytics?
Ad revenue is added to your Earnings Analytics within 48 hours from your last stream.
Do channel subscribers see ads?
Monetizing streamers using Ads Manager can decide whether or not their subscribers see ads while on their channel. The choice is yours!
Do viewers with a Turbo subscription see ads?
Twitch viewers with a Turbo subscription will not see ads scheduled by the Ads Manager.
As a streamer, can I delay an upcoming scheduled ad?
You can snooze it for 5 minutes. If you’d like to cancel your entire schedule, you can always turn off Ads Manager.
How does Automatic Ad Length and Frequency know which settings are best for my channel?
We look at different metrics like revenue and viewership on each channel, so that we may select the option that is most likely to benefit streamers’ ad revenue and minimize any impact on the viewer experience. If you change your ad minutes per hour, we will adjust your ad settings dynamically. For example, if you increase your ad minutes from 3 to 4, your ad spacing/length will change.

It’s ongoing work to refine the optimal settings for your channel: we’re going to continue to experiment and improve this feature after launch, to deliver the right ad spacing and frequency combinations for your channel.

How can streamers access 55% net ad revenue share?
By setting Ads Manager to 3 minutes or more per hour, Affiliates and Partners unlock 55% Net Ad Revenue Share.

Hype Train Guide

Hype Train incoming! Hype Train is a super-sized celebration when community members unite to support a streamer they love. It challenges the community to reach epic levels of hype and rewards participants for keeping the train on track. A Hype Train will kick off when there’s a spike in support events (like subscriptions, or Bits) from different viewers, or high engagement moments in your channel, based on a threshold set by each Streamer. This activates a countdown, during which all participants earn emote rewards for supporting the channel.

Any monetized streamer can get started with Hype Trains today! Visit your Creator Dashboard.

On this page:

  • Kicking off a Hype Train
  • Participating in a Hype Train
  • Emotes, Badges, and Titles
  • About Special Train Types
  • Streamers: Setup and Management
  • Streamers: Hype Train Troubleshooting
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Kicking off a Hype Train

A Hype Train is kicked off by a spike in contributions in a channel, within a 5-minute period. These contributions can be monetary, or from high-engagement moments. A single viewer can kick off a Hype Train by gifting a large number of subscriptions at once.

Monetary support events that kick off a Hype Train include:

  • New subscription purchases on web and mobile
  • Subscribing with Prime on web and Android
  • Sharing a subscription renewal in chat (when your recurring subscription has renewed)
  • Sharing a gift-to-paid or Prime-to-paid upgrade in chat (when you have converted this subscription type to a paid recurring subscription)
  • Gifting subs (any amount)
  • Cheers of 100 Bits or more
  • Power Ups of 100 Bits or more

High-engagement moments (non-monetary support events) that kick off a Hype Train include:

  • An increase in chat activity
  • We notice more historical spenders watching

Hype Train Approaching lets you know a Hype Train is just a few contributions away. The amount of support events before a Hype Train arrives depends on the kickoff triggers customized by your streamer. Streamers can choose to opt-out of monetary support events, or high-engagement moments (non-monetary support events) – whatever works for their channel. Learn more.

After a Hype Train has ended, there is a cooldown period before another Hype Train can be kicked off. Streamers establish the length of any cooldown period via the channel settings. No matter if a Hype Train kicked off via monetary support events, or high-engagement moments, the same cooldown period is respected. Learn more.

Participating in a Hype Train

Join the fun! Click here to browse live streams where Hype Trains are happening right now!

When a Hype Train is currently active on a channel, a notification at the top of chat will give you all the details of the current Hype Train. Expand the card for details on:

  • The Hype Train’s current level
  • The channel’s highest all-time Hype Train level
  • Time remaining to get the Hype Train to the next level
  • Support event progress towards the next level
  • Unlockable Emotes if the Hype Train completes all the current levels (Learn more).
  • Who currently holds the coveted Hype Train Conductor badges (Learn more).
  • Hype Chest – Filled with your Hype Train Rewards, if you’ve contributed to support events.
Hype Train Levels and the Hype-o-Meter

Once kicked off, a Hype Train starts at Level 1. Everyone in chat has 5 minutes to help increase the Hype Train’s level and duration by filling the Hype-o-Meter with further support events. Once the Hype-o-Meter is full, the Hype Train moves to the next level. The five-minute timer resets and a new, higher Hype-o-Meter goal is applied! If the first level goal is not met, the train moves on, and no emote rewards are distributed. Try again next time!

If the Hype Train passes Level 1, Hype Train Rewards will be distributed to all contributing participants once the Hype Train concludes. The rewards you receive depend on both your individual contributions, as well as the final achieved level of the Hype Train. After the Hype Train ends, you’ll be prompted to open a Hype Chest to claim your rewards.

Hype Train Rewards: Emotes and Conductor Badges

Attention, rewards hunters - click here to browse streams where Hype Trains are happening right now!

How to Earn Hype Train Emotes

Hype Train participants can earn 1 emote per Hype Train. Emote rewards are distributed to participants based on the final level completed by the Hype Train, not total levels the Hype Train progresses. When a Hype Train completes, your Hype Chest is available. Open the Hype Chest to review your earned emotes and add them to your collection. Learn more about Hype Train Emotes below.

So, a Hype Train that completes at Level 5 will distribute an emote reward from the Level 5 emote set, and so on. Participants cannot earn duplicate emotes. If a participant has already unlocked all of the emotes in that level, they will receive one from a lower level.

A participant that Cheers 100 Bits at Hype Train level 1, and gifts a sub at level 3, will earn 1 emote from the emotes available at the final level of the Hype Train.

Emotes

Each Hype Train level, up to Level 5, has its own set of emotes. After Level 5, new permanent emotes unlock at Levels 10, 25, 50, and 100.

Hype Train Conductors

A bit of friendly competition can be good, when it comes to Hype Trains. Throughout the duration of a Hype Train, the top contributor of Bits and the top contributor of Subs are each recognized as the “Hype Train Conductors” for their respective support event categories. These two users are awarded the coveted “Hype Train Conductor badge.”

While the Hype Train is active, viewers can steal these badges from each other by contributing more support events. It is not possible for one user to hold both the Subs and Bits Conductor badges.

After the Hype Train concludes, the final Hype Train Conductors will each receive the exclusive “Hype Train Conductor” badge in chat, which is held until the next Hype Train.

After the badge is won by the next Hype Train Conductors, previous Conductors will receive a permanent badge to celebrate the accomplishment.

Current Conductor

Former Conductor

A previous Conductor can reclaim the title, but only one badge will be displayed at a time.

Streamers: Setup and Management

Streamers can set their goals, change kickoff triggers or cooldown periods, or disable Hype Trains for their channel entirely.

Visit your Hype Train Settings: dashboard.twitch.tv/monetization/community/hype-train

Enabling / Disabling Hype Train

Hype Trains are enabled by default for both Partners and Affiliates.

To Disable or Enable a Hype Train visit your Hype Train settings within your Monetization Settings.

There is a toggle next to Enable Hype Train you can toggle to enable or disable Hype Trains on your streams.

Enabling / Disabling Autopilot

To keep you focused on the fun, you can enable/disable Autopilot.

Hype Train Autopilot will dynamically adjust your Hype Train Settings (kickoff triggers, level goals/difficulty, and cooldown period) to help you earn more support from each Hype Train.

Manage Hype Train Autopilot in your Hype Train settings: dashboard.twitch.tv/monetization/community/hype-train

Kickoff Triggers

To change the threshold to kick off a Hype Train, visit your Monetization > Community Settings.

Locate the Kickoff Threshold. Hype Train Kickoff triggers fall into two categories. First, support events (monetary). Move the slider to select between 2 and 25 events to start your Hype Train.

High-engagement moments (non-monetary) are a second type of Hype Train trigger. You can opt-out of this Hype Train trigger by disabling the setting toggle. When this setting is enabled, a Hype Train will kick off on your channel if we detect an increase in channel activity.

Support events must each come from a different viewer to kick off a Hype Train.

Level Goals

To change the difficulty of a Hype Train on your channel you will need to go to your Monetization > Community Settings.

You will find a dropdown menu in the Level Goals section where you can select the difficulty of your hype goal. There are five difficulty levels: Easy, Medium, Hard, Super Hard, and Insane.

Cooldown Period

To change the cooldown period between Hype Trains you will need to go to your Monetization > Community Settings.

In the Cooldown Period section you will find a dropdown menu where you can select the amount of time that should pass before another Hype Train can begin. It can be set between 1 and 8 hours in hour increments.

Your cooldown settings are respected no matter which Hype Train Kickoff Triggers you have enabled.

Customization

To customize the visual appearance of Hype Trains on your channel, you will need to go to your Partner / Affiliate Settings under the Hype Train section.

In the Customization section you will find an emote selector, which allows you to choose among your existing subscription emotes, your Bits tier emotes, or Twitch global emotes.

The emote you select will replace the default Pogchamp emote in animations that appear in the Hype Train public callout on your channel. You can view how the experience will appear to your viewers in the preview section on the right.

You can also use your Profile Accent Color. You can set your Profile Accent Color to personalize your brand around Twitch and your channel elements.

About Special Train Types

Some special train types can appear randomly on any monetized streamer’s channel in lieu of a regular Hype Train.

Mythic Train

The Mythic Train is an ultra-rare specialty Hype Train. When a Mythic Train appears, it is announced with a distinct banner in chat, showing three possible golden emotes to earn.

All viewers who contribute to a Mythic Train will receive one of three golden emotes. The golden emotes to earn are selected at random, and revealed when the train ends. Everyone who contributed receives the same emote. The Mythic Train must reach at least Level 2 for emotes to be granted.

Other details:

  • The golden emote is available for 24 hours after the Mythic Train ends. After 24 hours, the emote is no longer available
  • Contributors also receive regular Hype Train emotes in addition to the golden emote
  • Mythic Trains can appear both on the Twitch mobile app, and desktop Twitch
  • Mythic Trains can appear in Shared Hype Trains
  • Possible Mythic Train golden emotes include PogChamp, CoolCat, and WutFace
Golden Kappa Trains

The golden Kappa Train can be noted on approach by its distinct banner in chat. Viewers will receive the Golden Kappa emote regardless of what level they contributed at, so long as the Hype Train reaches at least Level 1.

Other details:

  • The Golden Kappa emote is available to viewers who participated in a Golden Kappa Train for 24 hours. Viewers can see the emote in their emote picker, and can use it on any channel.
  • Depending on your kickoff settings, a Hype Train Approaching notification appears in chat when your community is within just a few actions of kicking off a Hype Train. We’ll let you know if the next Hype Train is a Golden Kappa Train.
  • Golden Kappa Trains can appear both on the Twitch mobile app, and desktop Twitch.
  • Contributors also receive regular Hype Train emotes in addition to the golden emote
Treasure Trains

A Treasure Train can be noted by its distinct banner in chat. After reaching Level 2 of the Treasure Train, a 35% discount will be unlocked on purchases of 5 or more Tier 1 single-month gift subscriptions.

Terms and Conditions apply: Treasure Train channel discount is a limited time offer available only for the duration a chat panel banner announces the Treasure Train offer is open. Discount applies only to purchase of 5 or more Tier 1 single-month gift subscriptions when offer is available. Cannot be combined with other offers or discounts. Offer is non-transferrable and has no cash value.

You can opt-out of discounted gift subscriptions in your Creator Dashboard. Opting out will prevent Treasure Trains from appearing on your channel.

Community Train (Experiment)

The team is currently experimenting with a new type of rare Hype Train called a Community Train. At level 2, this train rewards viewers who didn’t contribute to the Hype Train with Hype Train emote rewards anyway. The higher level Community Train achieved, the more non-participating viewers receive the Hype Train emote reward. This feature is currently being tested and may not be available in all channels.

Community Rewards are separate from contributor rewards. All contributors still receive their emote rewards as usual. See FAQ for more details.

How Many Viewers Receive Community Rewards?

The number of non-contributors who receive rewards increases with the Community Train level:

  • Level 2: % of non-contributors (minimum 1 recipient)
  • Levels 3-10: Percentage increases with each level
  • Levels 11-14: Percentage continues to increase
  • Level 15+: Up to 25% of non-contributors

Even if the percentage calculation results in less than 1 viewer, at least 1 eligible viewer will always receive Community Rewards when the Community Train reaches Level 2 or higher.

How Are Recipients Selected?

Recipients are randomly selected from all eligible viewers present in the channel when the Hype Train ends. You’ll receive the same notification as contributors when you receive Community Rewards, and you can open your Hype Chest to claim your emotes.

Which Emotes Do Community Reward Recipients Receive?

Community Reward recipients receive emotes from the same level set as contributors, based on the final level the Hype Train achieved. If you’ve already unlocked all emotes from that level, you’ll receive one from a lower level (just like contributors).

Streamers: Hype Train Troubleshooting

Below are some tips for how to get the most out of Hype Train on your channel.

The Hype Train Happens too Often

Hype Trains that occur frequently can remove the excitement of the event for your viewers.

If you feel the Hype Train is disrupting the flow on your channel or reducing the excitement associated with such events consider increasing the cooldown period to create longer breaks between Hype Trains, increasing the kickoff Threshold to make it more difficult to start a Hype Train, or both.

The Hype Train Doesn’t Happen Enough

If you feel the Hype Train isn’t happening enough for your channel, consider decreasing the cooldown period, decreasing the kickoff Threshold, or both.

The Hype Train Levels are Not Being Completed

If viewers are constantly unable to complete levels in the Hype Train it may become discouraging for them to try.

If your viewers are unable to complete levels of the Hype Train you may want to consider decreasing the Difficulty to an easier setting for your viewers.

The Hype Train Doesn’t Seem to be as Exciting in Long Streams

If you have longer streams, and the Hype Train is happening often, it can cause fatigue for your viewers.

If this is the case, consider extending the cooldown period for your longer streams.

The Hype Train Happened “Randomly” Without Anyone Subscribing or Cheering

Hype Trains can kick off without monetary support, if you have enabled “High-Engagement Moments” in your Hype Train settings. If you wish to limit Hype Train trigger events to monetary support, you can do so in your Hype Train settings.

High-Engagement Moments Hype Train triggers respect your cooldown settings.

Frequently Asked Questions

Check below to see if your question has been answered.

Sections:
  • Streamer FAQ
  • Viewer FAQ
Streamer FAQ
What is a Hype Train?
Hype Train is a super-sized celebration when community members unite to support a streamer they love. It challenges the community to reach epic levels of hype and rewards participants for keeping the train on track. A Hype Train will kick off when there’s a spike in support events (such as subscriptions or use of Bits) in a channel, based on a threshold set by each Streamer. This activates a countdown, during which all participants earn emote rewards for supporting the channel.
How do I change the threshold to kick off a Hype Train?
You can use the slider in your Partner Settings under the Hype Train section to choose a threshold between 2 and 25 events.
What are level goals and how do I change them?
Level goals are the required amount of support needed to complete each level.

You can change the level goals by selecting the difficulty you want from the dropdown menu in your Partner / Affiliate Settings under the Hype Train section.

How do I change the length of the cool down period?
The cooldown period is referred to as the period of time when a Hype Train ends and a new Hype Train begins. You can change that period of time via a dropdown menu located in your Partner / Affiliate Settingsunder the Hype Train section.
What if I don’t set custom values for all of these things?
At launch, your Hype Train experience will be set to unique Twitch-defined settings based on the level of support you receive in your channel. You can change these settings at any time.
Are there benefits to selecting the highest difficulty level?
When you challenge your community by selecting the “Super Hard” or “Insane” difficulty levels, participants will be eligible to unlock one of five bonus caboose emotes.
Can I opt-out or opt-in of the Hype Train on my channel?
Yes. This feature will be automatically enabled on your channel at launch, with default settings customized to your channel. You can choose to turn it off at any time through your Partner / Affiliate Settings under the Hype Train section.
As a Partner or Affiliate, can I earn Hype Train rewards in my own channel?
Yes, when rewards are distributed there is a chance you can earn rewards in your own channel.
Who is this feature available for?
Partners and Affiliate channels.
How is this better than an organic support train?
Hype Train adds new features that augment these natural community moments:
  • A distinct kickoff mechanism to communicate the beginning of a support event.
  • Visual status of the Hype Train in a community highlights area.
  • Community rewards to incentivize participation.
  • Support goals and Hype Train levels to game-ify the experience and drive participation
Can I kick a Hype Train off myself?
No, these events are intended to celebrate organic spikes in support to your channel. We’ve heard from streamers that one of the key benefits of this feature is that you don’t have to intervene directly to help build hype in your channel, so we want to make this as hands-off as possible.
Can I still get Hype Train emotes?
Yes! At the end of the Hype Train, you will receive a Hype Train emote based on the level your community completed.
Can a Hype Train start at any time?
After a Hype Train ends, the channel will be subject to a cooldown period based on settings that you can control in your channel settings.
Are all support events worth the same?
No. The Hype-o-Meter will fill up more for larger support actions. For example, if someone gifts 25 subs to the community, that will fill the Hype-o-meter a lot more than a single subscription or a Cheer of 100 Bits.
Can I block or report Hype Train Conductors?
Yes, the same moderation tools available for Chatters will be available for Hype Train Conductors displayed in the Hype Train notification card, including blocking, reporting, and banning.

Similar to chat, these options will be available by clicking the viewer’s username.

If I use this, will I look like a sellout?
As with Subs and Bits, we are providing this feature as a tool to help you gain support from your community and for the community to have fun in the process. Our goal in creating an organic kick off mechanism is to let the feature happen naturally, without any direct intervention from you, in order to limit the feeling of “selling out” by directly asking for contributions. That said, we know this feature won’t be for every community, so you can turn it off at any time if you feel it’s not contributing positively to your stream.
Is the Hype Train supported in third-party software?
Yes! Hype Train events are available to third-party APIs. View technical details here:
  • Helix: dev.twitch.tv/docs/api/reference/#get-hype-train-events
  • Eventsub: dev.twitch.tv/docs/eventsub/manage-subscriptions/
Viewer FAQ
How do I start a Hype Train?
A Hype Train automatically kicks off when there is a spike in Bits or Subscription activity in a channel. This typically requires support events from several different viewers, though a single viewer can trigger a Hype Train by gifting a large number of subscriptions at once. The specifics of this threshold are customized by your streamer.

Learn more about support events here.

Can I start a Hype Train on my own?
In most cases, you will need the help of others to kick off a Hype Train. However, a single viewer can start a Hype Train by gifting a large number of subscriptions at once. The number of support events required is specified by the streamer.
Is there a minimum support amount to participate in the Hype Train?
Any subscription, gift, or community gift counts toward the Hype Train Hype-o-meter. A Cheer must be at least 100 Bits to help kick off a Hype Train.

Cheers of any size will count toward the Hype-o-Meter during the Hype Train, but to earn emote rewards requires a cumulative Cheer of 100 Bits or more.

Once a Hype Train ends can we start another one?
Not right away. Following a Hype Train there’s a cooldown period unique to each channel based on streamer settings.
I Cheered, but didn’t get an emote?
Cheers of 100 Bits or more are required to kick off a Hype Train, or to earn Hype Train rewards. However, if a Hype Train is ongoing, Cheers of any amount will contribute towards the next level.
Can I keep the emotes I collect?
Generally, yes (except as described below). When a user participates in a Hype Train, they’ll receive the emotes corresponding to the number of Hype Train levels completed and can use those emotes across Twitch. To keep things interesting, we refresh Hype Train emotes every few months, which may result in some emotes no longer being available.
Do I need to renew my subscription during the Hype Train to make it count?
No. You can renew your subscription at any time, then share your subscription renewal notification during a Hype Train to make it count toward train progress.
If I make a large contribution, could I fill up multiple levels, or is it capped at the current level?
Large contributions can fill up multiple levels at once, and could even complete the Hype Train if it’s big enough to fill the hype-o-meter for all levels. If this happens, the level five timer will continue counting down the full five minutes to allow time for others to contribute and earn emote rewards.
If someone fills up all of the levels at once, is the Hype Train just over?
Not right away. Once the final level is filled, the Hype Train will continue until the timer ends to let other viewers get in on the hype.
How will I know a Hype Train is going on?
You will see a notification at the top of chat that will tell you that a Hype Train is in progress, the current level of the train, the time left in the level, and the progress made to complete that level as presented in the Hype-o-Meter.
Why should I participate in a Hype Train?
While a normal Cheer or Subscription supports the streamer, unlocking certain benefits, and allows your contribution to stand on its own, participating in a Hype Train makes your support part of a larger community event that collectively celebrates and supports the creator you love. The larger community event provides its own excitement to the channel. We think there’s value both in letting your support speak for itself, and in making it part of a larger support celebration within the community.

We’re excited that Hype Train now makes those large community support events more distinct and rewarding for viewers.

Could a Hype Train start at anytime?
After a Hype Train ends, there is a cooldown period during which another Hype Train cannot be activated to avoid creating noise in the channel. This cooldown period is unique to each channel based on streamer settings.
What if I participate in a Hype Train, then have to leave before the rewards are distributed?
You’ll still receive your emote reward if the level is satisfied, even if you’re offline.
If I cheer or subscribe during a Hype Train, will it still be applied to the contribution leaderboard?
Yes. Any support actions made during a Hype Train will contribute to all existing benefits, including Cheer/Gifter badges, leaderboards, and Channel Point accrual
Can I participate in a Hype Train when I am banned or suspended?
No. If you can’t chat, Cheer, or subscribe, you can’t participate in a Hype Train.
How many emotes can I win by participating in a Hype Train?
You can win 1 emote at the completion of each Hype Train.
What if I have all the emotes for the highest level we completed?
If you have been awarded all the emotes for the highest level the Hype Train completes, you will then receive an emote that you have not yet received from a lower hype level. If you have all emotes for all of the lower levels you will not receive an emote.
Can I participate while on mobile?
Yes! Hype Trains are visible on mobile, and all support on mobile, including Cheers and subscriptions, will contribute to a Hype Train.

Prime subscriptions are not available on iOS devices at this time.

(Experiment only) I didn’t contribute to the Hype Train but received rewards. Why?
Starting at Hype Train Level 2, some viewers who didn’t contribute can receive Community Rewards. If you were watching when the Hype Train ended and were randomly selected, you’ll receive emote rewards even without contributing. This feature is currently being tested and may not be available in all channels.
(Experiment only) How are Community Reward recipients chosen?
Recipients are randomly selected from eligible viewers present in the channel when the Hype Train ends. The number of recipients increases with higher Hype Train levels, starting at 1% of non-contributors at Level 2 and capping at 25% at Level 15 and above.
(Experiment only) What Hype Train level is needed for Community Rewards?
Community Rewards begin at Hype Train Level 2. The higher the level achieved, the more non-contributors will receive rewards. At least 1 eligible viewer will receive rewards at Level 2, with the percentage increasing up to 25% of non-contributors at Level 15 and above.
(Experiment only) Do Community Rewards affect contributor rewards?
No. Community Rewards are separate and additional. All contributors still receive their emote rewards as usual. Community Rewards do not reduce or change what contributors receive.

Legendary Emotes

Note: This guide is for viewers in the United States and Germany.

Legendary Emotes are rare versions of Twitch Global Emotes, like Kappa or PogChamp, that you collect by supporting streamers. You get emotes when you subscribe to channels and complete Watch Streaks (if the creator has enabled Legendary Emotes). There are 40 total emotes to collect initially, and we may add to or refresh emotes occasionally. Every Legendary Emote you unlock is yours to keep, and you can use it in any chat on Twitch.

Availability: Legendary Emotes are currently available to viewers in the United States and Germany, on channels where the feature is enabled. If you reside in any other country, you won’t be able to unlock Legendary Emotes.

What Are Legendary Emotes?

Legendary Emotes are special versions of Twitch Global Emotes that you can unlock through various behaviors, such as subscribing or maintaining watch streaks on channels. Like all Global Emotes, they work in any chat across Twitch.

Each Legendary Emote comes in four rarities, from most to least common: Uncommon, Rare, Epic, and Divine. You don’t need to collect a lower rarity version of an emote before you collect a higher rarity version. For example, you can get the Epic version of a Kappa emote before the Uncommon version.

The launch Legendary Emotes collection includes versions of popular global emotes like Kappa, LUL, and PogChamp.

Learn more about Global Emotes and how to use emotes.

How to Get Chests

There are two kinds of chests:

  • Premium Emote Chests, which come with Subscription purchases, gifts, and renewals
  • Emote Chests, which come with Watch Streaks

Anyone eligible to participate can get started on collecting Legendary Emotes. You can collect either kind of chest. There are up to 40 emotes that you can collect. Emotes are delivered through chests, which have different probabilities for emotes of different rarities. See Duplicates and Bonus Chests.

To check whether a channel has Legendary Emotes enabled, open the emote picker in that channel’s chat. If you see your Legendary Emotes collection progress, that channel has the feature enabled.

Premium Emote Chests (Earned Through Subscriptions)

You receive Premium Emote Chests for each Subscription you buy or gift, or that renews:

Subscription

Premium Emote Chests

Tier 1

1

Tier 2

2

Tier 3

5

Additional details:

  • Renewals: While Emote Chests are part of Twitch subscription benefits, you’ll get Premium Emote Chests each time a recurring subscription renews, including subscriptions you started before Legendary Emotes launched.
  • Multi-Month Subscriptions: You get 1 Premium Emote Chest each month of your subscription. For example, a 6-month Tier 1 subscription gives you 1 Premium Emote Chest a month for 6 months. If you bought a multi-month subscription before Legendary Emotes launched, you get a chest for each month that starts after launch.
  • Prime Subscription: You get 1 Premium Emote Chest when you use your monthly Prime Subscription on a channel.
  • Gift Subscriptions: You get 1 Premium Emote Chest for each Gift Subscription you purchase. Gift recipients do not get chests.
Emote Chests (Watch Streaks)

You get 1 Emote Chest every 30 days by completing a 5-day Watch Streak. From time to time, we’ll also give out extra bonus Chests for longer streaks. Learn more about Watch Streaks.

Opening Chests and Your Emote Collection

When you get a chest, a notification appears in chat.

You can open the chest right away, or save it for later. If you don’t open the chest right away, you can find your unopened chests in your Emote Collection.

To get to your Emote Collection, open your emote picker by tapping the emote icon in chat, then open your Emote Collection. Here, you’ll find unopened chests and see your progress through the current collection.

After you open a chest, the Legendary Emote you unlocked appears in your emote picker, ready to use.

Chest Probabilities

Each chest holds one Legendary Emote. You can’t choose which emote you receive. The probability of receiving an emote of a specific rarity depends on the type of chest you open.

Divine guarantee: You’re guaranteed to get at least 1 Divine emote in every 50 chests you open.

Duplicates and Bonus Chests

If you open a chest, and it contains a Legendary Emote you already have, it counts as a duplicate. Every 10 duplicates you get gives you a bonus Premium Emote Chest, which opens automatically. After each chest you open, the summary shows how close you are to your next bonus chest.

Collections and Refreshes

Every Legendary Emote you unlock is yours to keep. You can keep using it even after it’s no longer available to others via chests.

The Legendary Emotes you can unlock are offered as a collection that’s available for a limited time. Twitch may refresh the collection with new Legendary Emotes. When the collection refreshes, Twitch automatically opens any chests you haven’t opened yet and adds those emotes to your Emote Collection, so you don’t lose them.

Didn’t Get a Chest?

If you expected to receive a chest, and it isn’t in your Emote Collection, check the following:

  • Browser extensions. Some browser extensions replace the Twitch emote picker, which can hide your Emote Collections. Temporarily turn off your browser extensions, or open Twitch in a private (incognito) window, and check again. Learn more.
  • Your country. Legendary Emotes are only available to viewers in the United States and Germany, on channels where the feature is enabled.
  • Your purchase. Check that the Subscription purchase or renewal completed in your purchase history. You can also check the email associated with your Twitch account to see if you have received an invoice.
  • Multi-Month Subscriptions. You get 1 chest each month of your subscription, not all at once when you buy it.
  • Watch Streaks. You can get one Emote Chest every 30 days for a 5-day Watch Streak. If you got one in the last 30 days, you can get another one after the 30 days are up.
  • Unopened chests. Chests you haven’t opened stay in your Emote Collection until you open them, or the collection refreshes.

If you’ve checked all of these items, and your chest still is missing, contact Twitch Support. Include details about which Subscription or Watch Streak should have given you the chest.

Information for Creators

Legendary Emotes are Global Emotes, so viewers who collect them can use them in your chat like any other Global Emote. Your viewers get Premium Emote Chests when they subscribe to your channel or gift subscriptions; they get Emote Chests when they complete Watch Streaks.

Legendary Emotes respect AutoMod rules, so if you have chosen not to allow certain emote codes in your chat, they shouldn’t appear.

Legendary Emotes are available to viewers only in the United States and Germany. So, if your audience includes viewers outside these areas, they won’t be able to earn Legendary Emotes.

Frequently Asked Questions

Where do I find my chests and Legendary Emotes?
Open your Emote Collection via the emote picker to view Chests you have not opened and the Legendary Emotes you have collected.
Why are Legendary Emotes currently available only in the United States and Germany?
We wanted to get streamer and viewer feedback before expanding Emote Chests to our entire Community. Based on feedback, we may expand availability to additional locations.
What happens to chests I haven’t opened when a collection ends?
When the collection refreshes, Twitch opens your unopened chests automatically, and adds those emotes to your Emote Collection. You don’t lose them.
Can I choose which Legendary Emote I get?
No. Each chest holds one Legendary Emote, and you can’t pick which. You’re guaranteed at least 1 Divine emote in every 50 chests you open, and every 10 duplicates of any rarity give you a bonus Premium Emote Chest. See Chest Probabilities for how likely each rarity is from each type of chest.
How often do I get an Emote Chest?
You get Premium Emote Chests for each subscription purchase, gift, or renewal on channels where Legendary Emotes are enabled. You get 1 Emote Chest every 30 days by completing a 5-day Watch Streak on channels where Legendary Emotes are enabled.
What happens if I receive a Legendary Emote I already collected?
It counts as a duplicate. Every 10 duplicates gives you a bonus Premium Emote Chest, which opens automatically.
Can I prevent Legendary Emotes from being used in my channel?
Yes. If you don’t want viewers to use Legendary Emotes in your channel, add the emote names to your channel’s blocked terms.
I subscribed before Legendary Emotes launched. Do I get chests?
Yes. You get Premium Emote Chests starting with your first renewal after launch, or the first month of a multi-month subscription that starts after launch. You don’t get chests for months before launch.
I’m missing a chest. What should I do?
Check the steps in Didn’t Get a Chest? If a chest is still missing, contact Twitch Support.

Local Subscription Pricing

Subscription prices on Twitch are set by Twitch and adjusted to better reflect the cost of living where a subscriber lives. Creators cannot set the base price of their subscriptions. This pricing model enables creators to build global communities by making subscriptions more accessible to viewers around the world. Local subscription pricing applies to the following subscription types:

  • Tier 1, Tier 2 and Tier 3 subscription levels
  • Community Gift subs
  • Single Gift subs
  • Multi-month subscriptions

Regardless of the local price, all subscribers receive the same benefits. Benefits include subscriber badges, custom emotes, subscription anniversary notifications, and access to other subscriber perks the streamer has enabled (such as ad-free viewing, or subscriber-only chat).

Custom and Turbo subscriptions, as well as Bits prices, are not affected by local subscription pricing.

Which countries have local pricing?

Local subscription pricing is available in most countries worldwide. Subscription prices are adjusted based on local purchasing power and economic conditions. For a complete list of countries and their current subscription prices, visit the Local Subscription Pricing by Country page.

How does local subscription pricing impact creator revenue?

Creator subscription revenue is directly related to the price subscribers pay in their local currency. When a viewer subscribes from a country with local subscription pricing, the creator receives a proportional share of that subscription price based on their revenue share agreement with Twitch.

For example, if a Tier 1 subscription costs $5.99 USD in the United States but is priced lower in another country to match local purchasing power, the creator’s revenue from that subscription will reflect the lower price point. Your revenue share percentage remains the same regardless of the subscriber’s location.

You can view your subscription revenue breakdown by country in your Creator Dashboard under Channel Analytics to understand where your subscribers are located and how local pricing affects your overall revenue.

Supporting your community

Local subscription pricing makes it easier for viewers around the world to support your channel. You can encourage subscriptions by:

  • Setting subscription goals to motivate your community
  • Promoting gift subscriptions through leaderboards
  • While live, shouting out subscriber benefits like custom emotes and ad-free viewing
  • When live, announcing subscriber milestones and anniversaries as they appear in your activity feed

For more tips on growing your subscriber base, visit Creator Camp.

If you have questions about local subscription pricing, contact Twitch support.

Payout Details FAQ

Content in this article is intended for Twitch Partners and Affiliates only.

Changing your payout method can solve a number of issues including rejected payment, or payments that are stuck beyond standard processing time. You may also wish to hold your payments until such time you are ready for them.

What is standard payout processing time? Learn more.

What do I do when a payout is rejected? Learn more.

Changing Your Payout Method

Change your payout method in your Affiliate or Partner Settings. Select Change Payout Method.

To access or edit this section you must confirm your password and have two-factor authentication enabled.

Page 1 - If you are only changing your payout method, skip past the grayed-out fields. You cannot change your address, name, or other details when changing your payout method. To update this information, edit your details directly from your Creator Dashboard → Monetization → Affiliate or Partner. You do not need to restart onboarding.

Page 2 - Change your payout method. You can also opt to Hold Payments from this screen.

US Creators

Eurozone Creators (SEPA)

To avoid delays with payout, update your payout method as early in the month as possible. Any changes to your contact and payment information made after the 8th of the month will not be reflected in the current month’s payout. Changing your payout method will render you unpayable until the process is complete.

Changes made to your payment method take effect immediately but will not be reflected in your next payment unless you have submitted your changes before the 8th of the month.

A new lower $50 payout minimum is available with payout method set to ACH/direct deposit, eCheck/local bank, PayPal, or check. The payout minimum balance required for wire transfer will remain $100 due to fees deducted.

Supported Payout Methods

Here are the payout methods we support. Processing time and fees can vary, so consider these options carefully.

  • ACH (3-5 days): This deposits your payout directly into your bank account, making it one of the fastest methods. It is available for US residents only.
  • Local Bank Transfer / SEPA Transfer (1-2 days): This deposits your payout directly into your bank account, making it one of the fastest methods. It is available for Eurozone residents only. Creators who select this method and choose to be paid in EUR can avoid currency exchange fees.
  • Local Bank Payout Method or eCheck (1-4 days): A convenient method for non-US/non-Eurozone Affiliates. This option allows you to have the payout converted from USD to your local currency for a fee. The exchange rate is the wholesale rate (similar to the exchange rate charged by an ATM).
  • PayPal (1-2 days)
  • Check: This traditional method usually takes the longest to reach you.
  • Wire Transfer (1-3 days): When using this method, you will usually incur an extra fee by your bank. In the case of international wires, there is often an additional fee if the payout must be converted to your local currency.

Learn More about fees associated with each payment method.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are currency exchange fees?
If you choose to have your payout converted from USD to your local currency, a currency exchange fee of up to 2.5% of the transaction applies. This fee applies to both Affiliates and Partners.
How do I avoid currency exchange fees?

Creators in eligible European countries who choose to get paid out in EUR via Local Bank Transfer / SEPA Transfer can avoid the currency exchange fee. To switch, update your payout method in the Onboarding Info section of your Affiliate or Partner Settings and select “Local Bank Transfer / SEPA Transfer.”

Supported countries: Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Estonia, Finland, France (including French Guiana and Martinique), Germany, Greece, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Portugal (including Azores and Madeira), Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain (including Canary Islands).

When do changes to payout preferences take effect?
Any changes to your payout method will not be effective until at least seven days after submission. Any updates made to your payout method information after the 8th of the month will not be reflected in the current month’s payout.
Can I enter my payout info with Japanese, Korean, Chinese or other non-English characters?
Our system currently only accepts inputs in English. Field details, but not inputs, are provided in the following languages:
  • Spanish - es
  • German - de
  • French - fr
  • Italian - it
  • Netherlands - nl
  • Portuguese - pt-BR
  • Russian - ru
  • Arabic - ar
  • Chinese Simplified - zh-CHS
  • Japanese - ja
  • Korean - ko
How do I change my address/phone number?
Edit your details directly from your Creator Dashboard → Monetization → Affiliate or Partner. You do not need to restart onboarding. To access or edit this section you will need to have two-factor authentication enabled.
What do I do if I don’t recognize the payout details on my account?
If you receive a notification that your payout method or details have changed without your authorization, or if you don’t recognize the payout details in your payout history, your account may be compromised. If you can still access your account, take the following steps immediately to secure it:
  • Change your password - Use a strong, unique password you haven’t used elsewhere. Learn how to create a strong password.
  • Change your payout method - Visit your Affiliate or Partner Settings, select Onboarding Info, then Change Payout Method. Update it to your correct payment information.
  • Enable Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) - Add an extra layer of security to your account. Set up 2FA here.

If you’ve lost access to your account and therefore cannot take the previous steps mentioned, contact Twitch Support here. For more information on securing your account, visit this help guide.

When will I receive my revenue?
If you earned revenue within the current calendar month, it’s normal that it hasn’t been processed or paid out yet. Twitch uses a Net-15 payout schedule, which means payouts are only issued starting from the 15th of the following month — provided you meet the minimum payout threshold ($50 for most methods, $100 for wire transfer).

Example: If you earn $10 on May 3rd, that amount is only eligible for payout beginning June 15th — if you meet the payout threshold. Revenue earned this month will not be paid out this month.

If you have made edits to your tax or payout information in the middle of the current cycle, between the 6th and the 15th of the month, it may cause delays and defer your payout to the next calendar month.

What does “hold payments” mean? How long are payouts held?
If you are not ready to receive a payout, you can set your status to Hold Payments. You can release held payouts at any time. Held payouts must adhere to the minimum payout threshold($50 for most payout methods, $100 with wire transfer). These payouts are added to your regular Net 15 schedule.
What is the ABA number (eCheck, wire, ACH)?
An ABA number (also known as routing number or routing transfer number) is a sequence of nine numeric characters used by banks to identify specific financial institutions within the United States. An ABA number is used for wires and electronic automatic clearing house (ACH) transactions such as electronic funds transfer, direct deposit, direct payout of consumer bills, eChecks, tax payments, and more. Note: your ABA is not always the same as the routing number printed on your bank checks, so please contact your bank for the appropriate ABA number.

Piñata

Piñata is a new experiment where chat works together to break open a virtual piñata and unlock an emote. When a Piñata appears on a channel, viewers have 5 minutes to break it by Cheering with Bits, subscribing, or gifting subs. Bigger contributions land bigger hits and push the Piñata closer to breaking. Each hit shows a word, and the words get bolder as the hits get bigger! (Swung, Whacked, Slammed, or Smashed).

Other details:

  • If the Piñata breaks, everyone in chat gets the channel’s Piñata emote to use in any channel on Twitch for 24 hours. If the streamer hasn’t uploaded one, the reward is the Twitch default emote, FeelingGoated.
    • For Streamers: Upload your own Piñata reward emote in the Creator Dashboard. If you change your Piñata emote within 24 hours of a Piñata breaking, viewers who earned it get the new emote right away, for the rest of their 24 hours. If viewers got FeelingGoated before you uploaded your own emote, they keep FeelingGoated.
  • If the Piñata doesn’t break in time, everyone who contributed gets the GloatGoat emote instead, to use in any channel on Twitch for 24 hours.
  • For Streamers: To stop Piñatas from appearing in your channel, turn them off in your Creator Dashboard.
  • Piñatas are an experiment, so not every channel has them, and they may change or end.
  • Piñatas can appear on twitch.tv and the Twitch mobile app.

The Plus Program

The Plus Program offers two levels of enhanced subscription net revenue share rates for qualifying Affiliates and Partners:

  • Level 1: 60/40 net revenue share (“Level 1”)
  • Level 2: 70/30 net revenue share (“Level 2”)

This enhanced net revenue for subscriptions is earned in connection with recurring monthly subscriptions and gift subs. The enhanced net revenue share rate lasts for 12 months from the qualifying date; longer if the Affiliate or Partner continues to qualify.

To qualify for the Plus Program, streamers must adopt the Monetized Streamer Agreement (“MSA”) prior to meeting the qualification criteria (e.g., if you hope to qualify in October, you must adopt the MSA no later than the end of September).

How to Qualify

Plus Program qualification is granted on the 1st of each month to qualifying participants. To qualify, participants must meet certain recurring subscriber minimums for 3 months.

These recurring subscriber minimums are counted by Plus Points. Each time a recurring subscription purchase is made towards a streamer’s channel, they earn Plus Points. The Plus Program levels unlock at the following thresholds:

  • Level 1: Achieve 100 Plus Points or more for 3 consecutive months
  • Level 2: Achieve 300 Plus Points or more for 3 consecutive months
What types of subscriptions count towards Plus Points?

Recurring subscription purchases contribute to Plus Points. To qualify for the Plus Program, Partners and Affiliates must achieve 100 Plus Points or more (Level 1) or 300 Plus Points or more (Level 2) each month for 3 consecutive months.

Do different sub tiers count differently towards Plus Points?

Yes. A Tier 3 subs counts as 6 Plus Points, a Tier 2 as 2, and a Tier 1 as 1. So, more higher tier subs may help you reach Plus Program eligibility faster.

Do different sub tiers count Plus Points differently towards each level of the Plus Program?

No. Plus Points are counted the same towards each level of the Plus Program.

Recurring Sub Tier

Tier 1
