Plus Point requirements are the same for all Affiliates and Partners across the globe.

How are Plus Points calculated?

When evaluating program eligibility, the Plus Points total for a calendar month is calculated from the 1st of that month until 23:59:59 UTC (Universal Coordinated Time) on the last day of that month. On the first of each month, Plus Points reset, and you start fresh from 0 points.

Each time a subscriber purchases a subscription for your channel (whether as a recurring payment or a new subscription), Plus Points are added to your monthly total (+1 for Tier 1, +2 for Tier 2, +6 for Tier 3).

If you have more than 100 (Level 1) or more than 300 (Level 2) Plus Points by 23:59:59 UTC on the last day of the month, you have hit the required amount of Plus Points for qualification for the Plus Program that month.

For example, your viewer subscribes at Tier 1 on January 20 and continues to subscribe until April 20. You get a point on January 20 for their new subscription counting towards the month of January. You receive additional points on February 20 and March 20 (towards each respective month) every time that subscription recurs. Since the viewer’s subscription ends April 20, you wouldn’t get Plus Points on April 20.

Multi-month subscription payments are added to your Plus Points total on the viewer’s monthly subscription renewal date. So, a new purchase of a multi-month subscription counts for as many Plus Points that month as a regular monthly recurring subscription. Each month that multi-month subscription renews, it adds Plus Points as if it were a regular single-month recurring subscription.

How are Plus Points different from Sub Points?

Plus Points and Sub Points both offer a way to think about Sub Count, or the number of subscribers you currently have and weigh different subscription tiers (Tier 1 = 1 point, Tier 2 = 2 points, and Tier 3 = 6 points). However, there are some important differences.

Plus Points and Sub Points differ in what they count towards, when in a month they are calculated, and which subscription types contribute to them.

Plus Points only count towards your Plus Program qualification. Qualification is evaluated at the start of each calendar month at 23:59:59 UTC (Universal Coordinated Time) to see if you have gathered more than 100 (Level 1) or more than 300 (Level 2) Plus Points in the previous month. Plus Points include only paid recurring subs of all subscription tiers.

Sub Points count towards unlocking additional emote slots, or meeting creator goals you set. Sub points may fluctuate during a month as you gain and lose subscribers. Sub Points include paid recurring subs of all subscription tiers, including Prime sub users and gift sub holders.

Do upgrades of Prime or gift subs count towards Plus Points?

Yes, you will receive Plus Points after the initial gift sub or Prime sub period expires and the new paid recurring sub period begins. Put simply, Plus Points are awarded in the month that the viewer is charged, not in the month that a viewer commits to a Prime or gift sub upgrade.

For example, a viewer receives a one-month gift sub or uses their Prime sub towards your channel on August 13th. Even if the viewer upgrades their gift sub or Prime sub before the expiration date, you won’t receive the Plus Points until 30 days from the original gift date* or Prime sub use date. In this example, that would be on September 13th.

*Not all gift subscriptions last 30 days. 3-month and 6-month gift subscriptions are available, with 12-month packages available on certain platforms.

How does a sub tier upgrade impact Plus Points?

Viewers are charged instantly for each sub tier upgrade. Prices are not prorated. It is not recommended to upgrade a subscription tier mid-month.

Subscription tier upgrades are charged immediately at the time of upgrade and apply additional Plus Points towards the month the upgrade is committed.

For example, if a viewer upgrades their subscription from Tier 1 to Tier 2 in the middle of their subscription term, you’ll receive Plus Points for both tiers, equalling 3 Plus Points from that viewer for that month in total. In this example, the viewer is charged twice.

How does lowering sub tier impact Plus Points?

Lowering the subscription tier (Tier 3 to Tier 2 or Tier 2 to Tier 1) does not result in an immediate charge to the purchaser. The lower Plus Point value is applied in the month that the transaction completes. Remember, Plus Points are awarded in the month the subscriber is charged, not the month they commit to a lower tier

For example, a viewer purchases a Tier 2 paid recurring subscription towards your channel on August 13th. You will receive Plus Points for the Tier 2 purchase in August. If the viewer decides to update their subscription to Tier 1 in the middle of their subscription term, the viewer will be charged for the lower Tier 1 subscription when the original Tier 2 subscription benefits expire. As a result, you will receive the lower value Plus Points in the month the viewer’s new subscription term begins.

Not all paid recurring subscriptions renew every 30 days. 3-month and 6-month paid recurring subscriptions are available.

Setting Goals and Tracking Progress

In this section we’ll cover tools and features that can help you track progress towards Plus Program qualification and share your goals with your community.

Setting Goals

Affiliates and Partners may add a tracking widget that appears below their live stream.

To set up this widget, click here, or visit your Stream Manager in the Creator Dashboard.

Select Manage Goals, Plus Program, and choose a Level goal. Finally, click Share with Community, and Done.

The tracker is visible to anyone who views your channel page on web.

Tracking Progress

Track your progress towards Plus Program qualification in the Creator Dashboard. Visit your Earnings Analytics dashboard and review the Plus Program panel. Then click View Details.

I qualified for 1 or 2 months towards the Plus Program but missed a month. What’s next?

Don’t give up! If you are on track to qualify for the Plus Program, but you drop below 100 or 300 Plus Points in a month, work with your community towards qualifying the next month. Keep track of this month’s progress and your previous months through your Creator Dashboard.

Qualification months must be consecutive. If you completed 1 or 2 months prior to missing a month, you will need to start fresh and earn 3 consecutive months or the minimum of 100 or 300 Plus Points to qualify for their respective levels.

When do Plus Program dashboards reset for the next month?

Qualification is evaluated at the start of each calendar month at 23:59:59 UTC (Universal Coordinated Time) to see if you have gathered more than 100 (Level 1) or more than 300 (Level 2) Plus Points in the previous month.

Enrollment and Earnings

Congratulations on qualifying for the Plus Program! This section explains some specific enrollment scenarios.

If you continue to qualify:

How long do I remain enrolled?

When you enter the Plus Program (after 3 consecutive months of more than 100 or more than 300 Plus Points), you remain in the Plus Program for a minimum of 12 months, or longer if you continue to satisfy the qualification criteria while in the program.

In other words, any month you meet the qualification criteria (i.e., sufficient Plus Points accumulated each of the prior three months), your Plus Program end date is reset to 12 months from that date.

Two examples may help:

  • If you successfully maintain more than 100 or more than 300 Plus Points in February, March, and April, then your 12 months would start on May 1 and end April 30 the following year.
  • If you successfully maintain more than 100 or more than 300 Plus Points in each of February, March, April, and May, then you would again qualify on June 1 and you would be in the program until at least May 31 of the following year.

Can I qualify for Level 2 of the Plus Program while in Level 1?

Yes. Thanks to a Plus Program update in 2024, there are now two levels to the Plus Program. Qualifying Affiliates and Partners may move up from Level 1 (60/40 net revenue on subscriptions) to Level 2 (70/30 net revenue on subscriptions) at any time if they meet the 300 Plus Point threshold for 3 consecutive months to qualify for Level 2.

If your Plus Points drop below 100 (Level 1) or 300 (Level 2) after qualifying for either level:

After qualifying, if you drop below 300 Plus Points (Level 2) or 100 Plus Points (Level 1), you still retain the higher net subscription revenue share rate until 12 months after the date of your most recent qualification.

For example:

  • You qualify for the Plus Program on May 1, 2024 (reached more than 100 or more than 300 Plus Points in February, March, and April). In June 2024, you drop to 80 or 250 Plus Points. Regardless, your improved revenue share continues through April 30, 2025.*

You can also re-qualify. For example:

  • If you re-qualify for 3 consecutive months any time within your most recent 12-months period, your qualification extends for 12 months* following your most recent qualification date.
    • For example, if you qualify for the Plus Program on May 1, 2024 (you accumulated more than 100 or more than 300 Plus Points in February, March, and April).
    • Your initial Plus Program net revenue share period spans from May 1, 2024, through April 30, 2025.*
    • You maintain more than 100 or more than 300 Plus Points each of May, June, and July. As a result, your Plus Program qualification period extends through July 31, 2025.
    • In August 2024, you drop to 80 or 200 Plus Points. Your Level 1 or Level 2 subscription net revenue share still applies through July 31, 2025.
    • Now, in September, October, and November, you accumulate more than 100 or more than 300 Plus Points again.
    • In December 2024, you re-qualify for the Plus Program at Level 1 or Level 2.
    • Then, your most recent Plus Program qualification period continues from December 1, 2024, through November 30, 2025.*
    • This cycle of qualification and extension goes on and on.

*Provided you comply with Plus Program terms. If you have further questions, contact Twitch Support here.

Fraudulent Activity

If Twitch discovers that abuse of chargebacks, refunds, or other financial fraud has inflated your subscription count, this may affect your participation in the program. Learn more.

Any attempt to qualify for the Plus Program using other accounts, identities, or by utilizing another user’s account may result in temporary or permanent disqualification from the Plus Program.

Plus Program Glossary

Experienced Partners and Affiliates may be familiar with every word in this guide. However, some may find the below definitions useful. Please contact Twitch Support here if you have any questions about the Plus Program.

Term

Relation to Plus Program

Monetized Streamer Agreement (“MSA”)

Read more.

Plus Points

Learn more.

Recurring subscription

A recurring subscription is a paid (non-gifted, non-Prime) subscription. Plus Points are accumulated from paid recurring subscriptions.

Gift subscription

A gift subscription is a one-time purchase that can be purchased for another user. Gift subscription purchases do not contribute towards Plus Points. However, revenue from gift subscriptions is included in Plus Program enhanced net revenue for subscriptions once qualified.

Multi-month subscription

A regular, recurring subscription renews monthly for the number of months purchased. Multi-month subscriptions are available in 3- or 6-month packages and renew accordingly. Plus Points for multi-month subscriptions are awarded each month of the multi-month subscription.

Prime subscription

Prime subscriptions are a benefit of Prime Gaming that provides a token that may be used for a one-month subscription to a channel of the token-holder’s choice. Prime subscriptions do not contribute Plus Points.

Subscription tier(s)

Subscriptions can be purchased at different price levels or “tiers.” Higher priced tiers offer additional benefits, which may include additional emote unlocks for subscribers and badge flair, as determined by the channel owner.

Earnings Analytics

Located in your Creator Dashboard, this page shows you detailed estimates of your revenue, and Plus Program progress.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I tell my community that I’m part of the Plus Program?
Yes. You are welcome to talk about the qualification criteria, the program’s benefits, and whether you’ve qualified.
Why don’t Prime subs count for Plus Points?
Prime Subs are a benefit of Prime Gaming. The Prime Gaming benefit allows viewers to receive subscription benefits and support streamers, but a Prime Sub is not a recurring subscription. For the Plus Program, we are focused on subscriptions sold by Twitch (e.g., recurring paid subs and gift subs).
How long do Plus Program progress widgets take to complete updating each month?
On the 1st of the month, we begin calculating how many Plus Points you earned by 23:59:59 UTC on the last day of the month. This process can take up to 12 hours past 23:59:59 UTC to complete. If you would qualify into the Plus Program this month, your enhanced subscription net revenue share will apply to revenue earned during this up to 12-hour period. Additionally, your Subscribers panel in Earnings Analytics will update to reflect your new net revenue share at any time during this 12-hour period. Once this calculation completes, you should receive a notification by email of any adjustments.
I have Premium Partner terms. Are there any Plus Program benefits that aren’t included in my agreement?
No. All the benefits of the Plus Program are included in the Premium Partner agreement.
Latin America Plus Program Update
Who is eligible for these updated requirements?
Monetizing streamers based in the following countries in LATAM are eligible: Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, Panama, Peru, Puerto Rico, Paraguay, El Salvador, Uruguay, and Venezuela.
How will you determine what country I am in?
We use a number of factors to determine where streamers are based including information provided during onboarding, IP location, and tax reporting information.
What happens if I move out of Latin America after I qualify?
If you have qualified for the Plus Program while residing in Latin America and later move to another location you may be required to re-qualify for the Plus Program. Please note that falsifying information in an attempt to take advantage of geo-based qualification criteria will lead to account suspension.
Why are there separate eligibility requirements for LATAM?
As we evolve the Plus Program, we continuously monitor representation in the program and the unique obstacles creators in specific regions face. Cultural nuances and economic realities in LATAM can make it difficult for creators of similar size to meet Plus program requirements compared to those in other regions. Given this, we saw an opportunity to better support creators in LATAM by making higher revenue shares more accessible to them.
Will you be updating the Plus Program requirements in other regions?
At this time, LATAM is the only region where we’re updating criteria, but we may consider other markets in the future. We have consistently made updates to the Plus Program since it was announced in 2022, and we will continue to evaluate how we can make it more impactful for more streamers moving forward.
Will my Dashboard be updated if I am eligible?
Yes, your Dashboard will be updated to allow you to track your progress to the Plus Program.
Viewers on Twitch tend to watch creators based on language, not region, so why doesn’t this change apply to creators in Spain?
This change is based on specific purchasing behaviors in Latin America, which differ from those in other Spanish-speaking regions like Spain. We’re currently focused on addressing the unique challenges faced by LATAM creators and will continue to evaluate other regions as needed.

Plus Program Qualification Abuse Criteria

Click here to learn more about the Plus Program!

To block bad actors from bypassing the eligibility requirements of the Plus Program, we are clarifying which actions would be considered abuse and disqualify streamers from eligibility.

Paid subs used to qualify for the Plus Program must be from individual, real accounts, and may not undermine the integrity of this program or Twitch systems. Any attempt to qualify for the program by using other accounts, identities, or by utilizing another user’s account may result in temporary or permanent disqualification from the Plus Program. Continued or widespread abuse may result in removal from the Partner program.

Per our Community Guidelines, you may not:

  • Engage in viewership tampering (such as artificially inflating follower or live viewer stats)
  • Buy, sell, or share user accounts, services, or features
  • Defraud Twitch or others

In addition, in order to qualify for the Plus Program you may not:

  • Pay any other person or entity to subscribe to your channel
  • Create, or have others create, multiple accounts subscribing to your channel for the purpose of qualifying for this program
  • Engage in any cheating, hacking, botting, or tampering that gives you an advantage in qualifying for this program

Mass refunds or chargebacks of paid subs on your channel post-qualification may also result in your disqualification from the program.

We understand that sometimes streamers are victims of account takeover, fraud, or viewbotting directed by a bad actor. To avoid penalizing these streamers, we take steps to detect which specific parties are responsible for the abusive actions. We also want to provide an opportunity for streamers to share more context with us. In any case where a Partner or Affiliate feels that they have been unfairly disqualified, they may appeal the decision via the Help Portal at Contact Us.

Purchasing Gift Subscriptions

Whether you are a streamer looking to reward one of your loyal viewers with a subscription to your channel or just looking to gift a friend a subscription to one of their favorite channels; we’ve got you!

Learn more about upgrading and managing gift subs, gifting subscriptions on mobile, and gift subs for creators

On this page:

Gifting Through Chat

You can gift through chat to a specific viewer, or the community.

Gift to a Specific Viewer

To gift to a specific viewer in chat, begin by clicking or tapping the recipient’s username in chat, and opening their user card.

From here you may begin the process by clicking Gift a Sub. Select a subscription tier and number of months to gift to the recipient. To gift anonymously, tick the option.

You will then be taken to the checkout page to pay for your gift subscription.

If Gift A Sub is grayed out, it’s likely the viewer is already subscribed! They might be sporting a sub badge.

3-month, 6-month, and 12-month gift subscriptions are only available for Tier 1 gift subscriptions at this time.

Gift to the Community

Type “/gift” in chat + an amount between 1 and 100. This purchase method cannot be done anonymously.

Gift ’Em All (Experiment)

Gift ’Em All is a new experimental feature, allowing users to purchase a gift sub for every eligible follower currently watching a channel, up to the current maximum of 1000 Subs. Eligible followers are not currently subscribed to a channel. The feature is available from time-to-time in a small number of channels and users as we experiment. Purchasing gift subs with Gift ’Em All can only be done on Twitch in a desktop browser.

We do our best to catch everyone, but there are a variety of reasons why an eligible follower might not receive a gift sub purchased this way:

  • Lag between when the gifter begins, and completes the process
  • Some latency processing new followers or users joining and leaving the channel

Gift Through the Support Panel

If you don’t wish to gift subs through chat, you can use the Support Panel. The Support Panel contains additional options and information.

Gift to a Specific Viewer

To gift a sub to a specific user, begin the gifting process from the Support button on a channel. Click Gift A Sub (subscribers) or Subscribe -> Gift A Sub (non-subscribers). Select the option to gift a specific viewer.

Search for a Twitch ID. Be sure your selection is accurate, as you cannot change this later in the process.

Now, you may choose to gift a Tier 1, 2, or 3 subscription. Choose the number of months to gift. You may also choose to gift anonymously.

If the Gift A Sub button is grayed out, it’s likely the viewer is already subscribed. They might be sporting a subscriber badge.

3-, 6-, and 12-month gift subscriptions are only available for Tier 1 gift subscriptions at this time.

Gift to the Community

If you do not wish to gift to a specific user, you can gift a number of gift subs to an entire community.

Completing Your Purchase

During checkout, take special note of your Purchase Summary. Here, you will note the Tier, amount, and price of the gifts you are making to an individual or a community.

The Subtotal will show the base price of your gift subscriptions. In some geographies, we may add additional tax in the checkout process if applicable.

Complete the checkout process by adding a payment method. Once your payment has been completed the gift subscription will be received by your grateful recipient!

After you have added a payment method to Twitch, you can get back to the stream as quickly as possible by using 1-click checkout to complete your purchases.

Rewards & Anonymous Gifting

To recognize your support, we created a Sub Gifter Badge that appears when you gift a sub. This badge stays visible for as long as any gift sub you have given is active, and disappears when your gifted subs expire. If you gift another sub, the badge will reappear.

As you purchase more gift subs in the channel, your badge levels up. Just like your subscriber badge, if you ever lose your Sub Gifter Badge for any reason, your progress will be waiting for you when you come back.

Learn more about chat badges.

Keep your support lowkey by disabling the option to show progressive gift badges. Manage this setting. (Note: disabling this option will prevent you from showing up on the “Top Gifters” Leaderboard.)

Anonymous Gifting If you don’t wish to be recognized, you can enable anonymous gifting. Gift Subs purchased using anonymous gifting do not contribute towards your badge or leaderboard progress.

Learn more about leaderboards.

Learn more about Hype Trains and Anonymous Gifting in our guide: Hype Train Guide

Frequently Asked Questions

Where can I buy gift subs?

Gift Subs can be purchased on the web, or the Twitch Mobile App (iOS and Android).

You may purchase 3-month or 6-month subscriptions for users on the web. 12-month gift sub packages are only available on web, and only for specific viewers. Multi-month gift subscriptions are not yet supported on the Twitch mobile apps.

Gift Subs are Tier 1 by default. Gift Subs in Tier 2 and Tier 3 are available for purchase on some devices in single-month amounts.

Can I gift a subscription using my Prime sub?
No, Prime subs cannot be used to gift a subscription to another user.
Will people see if I have gifted someone a subscription?
Yes, an alert will be sent to chat at the time of the subscription notifying the streamer and chat of your gift subscription to another user. If you do not see the alert due to lags in the stream/chat, try refreshing your browser tab. To gift without sharing your username, select the Gift Anonymously checkbox when you are choosing your gift recipient(s) or purchasing a community gift.
I tried to gift a community some multi-month subs, but ended up purchasing a sub for myself. What happened?

Multi-month community gift subs are not available for purchase. You can only purchase multi-month subscriptions for a specific viewer.

When you open the Support Panel on a channel while not subscribed, the Gift a Sub button is in gray next to the Subscribe button. If you select multi-month options above, make sure that you intend to purchase for yourself and that you are not intending this purchase as a Gift Sub!

What payment options are available for gift subscriptions?
The checkout flow follows the same flow for self subscriptions so all of the beloved payment methods you use will be available to purchase gift subscriptions for other users.
Can I purchase a bulk amount of gift subs to multiple specific users?
No, sorry. At this time, bulk purchases for gift subs are distributed to the community at large, not specific users.
Can I gift someone a Tier 2 or Tier 3 sub?
Yes, you can gift a subscription at all three tiers using community gifting, or gifting to a specific user. Tier 2 and Tier 3 gifting is not available on mobile devices.
I tried to give someone a sub, and the Gift a Sub button is grayed out. Why?
If someone is already Subscribed or Banned in the channel, they cannot receive Gift Subs in that channel. Banned users cannot send Gifts in channels where they are banned.
Can I gift someone a higher Tier sub? My friend has a Tier 1 sub and I want to gift them a Tier 3 sub.
Upgrades are not currently available through Subscription Gifting
Can I gift someone a recurring sub?
Yes! On the web, you may purchase 3, 6, or 12 months of subscription for a specific user at Tier 1 subscriptions only.
Are gifted subscriptions refundable?
No. All purchases are final.
How are gift recipients chosen when I Gift to the Community?
We use an algorithm to help us select gift recipients starting with eligible viewers in chat, then followers, mods, and other factors that identify members of a community. Our algorithm also avoids giving trolls subs. We are constantly improving our algorithm to detect this behavior.
Can I choose all of my gift recipients when gifting to the community?
Not at the moment, but you’re not the first person to ask! We love hearing feedback and will look into incorporating it into future improvements.

Additional Terms & Conditions for Bonus Gift Subscriptions

Bonus gift subscription of 1 community subscription will be added to each purchase of 5 new community gift subscriptions. Bonus subscriptions will be in the same Tier as those purchased. Cannot be combined with Sponsored Subscriptions discounts. Offer ends on date stated in channel chat banner or when bonus subscription limit stated in channel chat banner has been reached, whichever is sooner.

Secondary Accounts and the DJ Program

The DJ program is for creators who primarily stream themselves mixing pre-recorded music in a DJ set as the focus of their live stream. You can be a DJ no matter how frequently you stream. This article is for those who may consider it their part-time job to DJ.

DJ: Do I Need a Secondary Account?

No, a second Twitch account is not required in order to participate in the DJ Program. As a first step, familiarize yourself with the DJ Program Terms and how their application may affect your stream to determine if you may benefit from creating a secondary DJ program account.

When combined with an understanding of the DJ Program Terms, the below example scenarios may help you make an independent decision:

  • You are an Affiliate or Partner who primarily streams a variety of content. You are interested in streaming Twitch DJ sets part-time, but do not plan to make streaming Twitch DJ sets the focus of your channel’s content. In this example, creating a secondary DJ account may be a good step for you.
  • You are an Affiliate or Partner who primarily streams Twitch DJ sets. This is the focus of your channel’s content and live streams. In this case, you may decide creating a secondary DJ account is not necessary.

Twitch cannot make this decision for you, and will not provide specific advice.

DJ: How to Request Affiliate or Partner Status on a Secondary Account

This process requires two separate support tickets — one filed from each Twitch account. This is how Twitch verifies that you own both accounts.

Before You Begin

Make sure you have completed all of the following:

  • You are an existing Affiliate or Partner who has signed the Monetized Streamer Agreement (“MSA”) and completed the Path to Affiliate or Path to Partner achievements
  • You have created a secondary Twitch account
  • You have added 2-Factor Authentication to the secondary account
  • You have enrolled the secondary account in the DJ Program
  • You have access to the email addresses used to create both accounts
  • You have access to both Twitch accounts
Ticket 1: From Your Existing Affiliate or Partner Account
  • Log in to your existing Affiliate or Partner account
  • Open a Twitch Support ticket
  • Choose Category → DJ, Sub-Category → Secondary Linked Account
  • In the description, include the username of your secondary DJ account
  • Submit the ticket
Ticket 2: From Your New Secondary DJ Account
  • Log out and log in to your secondary DJ account
  • Open a second Twitch Support ticket
  • Choose Topic → General, Category → DJ Program, Sub-Category → Secondary Linked Account
  • In the description, include the username of your existing Affiliate or Partner account
  • Submit the ticket
What Happens Next

After receiving both tickets, Twitch Support will verify the identity and ownership of both accounts. You will receive a response in the ticket filed from your Affiliate or Partner account.

Secondary Accounts, Community Guidelines

If you do choose to create a secondary DJ account, and link it to an existing Affiliate or Partner account, bear in mind that any enforcement history from the existing account is applied to the secondary account as well. All conduct on your secondary account is treated as if it were done on your existing Affiliate or Partner account.

Opting Out with a Secondary Partner Account

What happens if I opt out of the DJ program?
If your secondary account was granted Partner status as part of the DJ Program, opting out ends the Partnership on that account. Your secondary account will be downgraded to Affiliate status 30 days after you opt out. If you change your mind, simply reply to the notice you receive within 30 days, and let us know you’d like to stay in the DJ Program.

If your secondary account was granted Affiliate status as part of the DJ Program, your Affiliate status will be retained if you opt out.

More Resources

  • DJ Program Terms
  • DJ Program FAQ
  • About DJ Program Music Costs and 1-Year Subsidy
  • How to Opt-Out of the DJ Program

Sponsored Subscriptions

As we have seen from the success of our annual SUBtember discounts, discounted subscriptions can help our streamers grow their communities and earn more revenue. We are now offering brands the ability to reach new audiences by sponsoring promotions of recurring and gift subscriptions for individual channels. These discounts can be activated any time of the year, and not just during the month of September.

Sponsored Subscriptions is an additional feature that a brand can choose to add to their Sponsorship campaign on Twitch. When a campaign includes sponsored subscriptions, the brand will discount a set number of subs for a set duration. This is normally between one to three hours long. Sponsored Subscriptions are triggered in the Sponsorships Tool in quick actions.

Streamers will receive their standard net revenue share from the discounted price of recurring or gift subs purchased during the campaign. While this will potentially result in lower net subscription revenue from those subs, compared to a revenue share from a typical subscription revenue, streamers will also receive an additional “Sponsorships” payout for participating in a Sponsored Subscription campaign.

When a Sponsored Subscription is live on your channel, it is accompanied with a channel skin and your community will see:

  • The frame and ribbon surrounding the video player.
  • Above chat (on web)
  • Branding in your channel information
  • Follower promotion on the left navigation bar (on web)

Additional Terms & Conditions for Sponsored Subscription Discounts

Sponsored subscription discounts apply only to Tier 1 single-month community gift subscriptions, the first month of new paid recurring Tier 1 monthly subscriptions, or the first month of Prime or gift subscriptions converted to paid recurring Tier 1 monthly subscriptions. Not applicable to existing recurring subscriptions; subscriptions canceled and then repurchased during the duration of the campaign; or Prime or gift subscriptions that are not being converted to paid. Offer not available on Twitch mobile apps and cannot be combined with other offers or discounts.

Frequently Asked Questions

What if I have an opportunity to use Sponsored Subscriptions with my brand partner?
If you have a brand partner that is interested in activating Sponsored Subscriptions they can reach out to visit this page for more information. twitch.tv
What do I have to do to set up Sponsored Subscriptions on my channel?
You activate it through the Sponsorship Tool in your Stream Manager.
Who in my community will see Sponsored Subscriptions?
All viewers watching your Twitch channel on web will see Sponsored Subscription assets and may be eligible to purchase discounted recurring and gift subscriptions.
Can I turn Sponsored Subscriptions off during my stream?
If you need to take down the ongoing Sponsored Subscription you can click cancel in the Sponsorship Tool. This will reset your progress and allow you to start over. The subs already purchased as part of the promotion will still count and be deducted when you start over.
Can I run ads when I have Sponsored Subscriptions running?
Yes. You can run video ads like you normally would. The above-chat assets will disappear while a viewer is watching a video ad and reappear when the ad has finished running.
Will the discount apply when the subscription renews for recurring subscriptions?
No, the discount only applies to the first term of the subscription.
Can my existing subscriber cancel their sub and purchase a discounted subscription?
No, only viewers not currently subscribed are eligible to subscribe at a discount. However, existing subscribers are still eligible to purchase gift subscriptions.
What happens if my channel hits the maximum number of discounted subscriptions?
The promotion will automatically turn off and any future subscription purchases will be full price. The above chat and subscription window promotional banners will be replaced with “Sold Out” versions.
Are T2, T3 or multi-month subscriptions eligible for discounts?
No. T2, T3, and multi-month subscriptions are not in scope for this promotion at this time.
What types of gift subscriptions are available?
Only T1, single month, community gift subscriptions are available and only when selecting preset amounts (see below, only offers within the purple box are eligible). Custom quantities and single gift subs direct to other users are not eligible.

Sponsorship Portal Overview

Affiliates and Partners can earn through brand sponsorships on Twitch. Affiliates must complete Creator Certification to be eligible for campaign invitations.

Affiliates: You must be Creator Certified to be eligible for campaign invitations. Complete the self-paced course on Creator Camp to get certified and start receiving opportunities.

Sponsorship Portal Walkthrough

A completed Creator Profile increases your chances for receiving sponsorship opportunities.

To visit your Sponsorship Portal, click here. Or navigate from your Creator Dashboard: select Monetization → Sponsorships in the left navigation (1).

The first time you visit your Sponsorship Portal you’ll be asked to sign the portal terms. The portal terms apply to all sponsorships you accept and run through this portal.

From the top tabs (2), you can switch between:

  • Browse — View available campaign invitations
  • Manage — Track your active and completed campaigns
  • Creator Profile — Set up your profile so brands can discover you

Your Browse page shows three types of sponsorship opportunities:

Exclusive Campaigns (3)

Brands that have chosen you specifically for their campaigns on Twitch. Before you accept, review the invitation and agreement to understand what the brand expects of you.

Open-Invite Campaigns (4)

Campaigns available on a first-come, first-serve basis. Before you accept, review the invitation and agreement to understand what the brand expects of you.

Third-Party Campaigns (5)

Sponsorship opportunities sourced from our third-party partners, including Wehype. These opportunities appear directly in your Sponsorship Portal — you don’t need to create a separate account or visit an external site. For more information, see Third-Party Campaigns on Twitch.

Accepting a Campaign

If you have been selected to participate in a campaign, you’ll receive an email and onsite notification. The invitation will include the campaign fee, breakdown of your deliverables, and campaign dates.

From the invitation, you can click through to review the full invite with more in-depth details on the campaign. Review all the details and ensure you understand what the brand expects of you before accepting the campaign. Twitch offers various campaign formats for sponsorships, so please review carefully to ensure the campaign works for you. The formats are:

  • Flat fee: You earn a set revenue upon completion of the campaign.
  • Completed Viewers: A performance-based campaign where you earn revenue based on your viewership during the sponsorship.
  • Affiliate Marketing: You earn revenue based on referrals from your viewers.

“Affiliate Marketing” is a general advertising industry term for campaigns paid on referrals. It does not refer to the Twitch Affiliate Program.

Open Invitation campaigns are on a first-come first-serve basis where there are limited spots that may fill up before you are able to accept. If that is the case, we will show the campaign as no longer available in your dashboard.

A campaign’s deliverables can consist of one or more of the sponsorship features we have: Channel Skins, Streamer-read Ads, or Sponsored Subscriptions.

Running a Campaign

General guidelines for your participation in Sponsorships as a Twitch creator are as follows. For detailed guidance, see the Branded Content Guidelines.

  • Review the Sponsorship Invitation: The brand will include detailed campaign information in the Sponsorship Invitation. Review it thoroughly to ensure you can meet the requirements and complete the campaign successfully.
  • Use the Sponsorship Tool quick action on your Stream Manager page to run your campaign. If the campaign has game or category requirements, those will be called out in the Tool, and you’ll be unable to start the campaign until you have them set accordingly.
  • Make Required Disclosures: We will automatically apply the “includes paid promotion” disclosure on your channel but please ensure you verbally disclose the sponsor at the start of the campaign periodically thereafter. If other disclosures are required, they will be stated in the Sponsorship Invitation.
  • Set AutoMod to level 2 or higher.
  • Complete all Campaign Deliverables on time: Repeatedly failing to complete campaigns may impact your ability to receive future campaign offers.

To start your live campaign, head over to your Stream Manager and add the new ‘Sponsorship Tool’ to your quick actions. This is the tool from where you will be able to start each deliverable.

Each deliverable will need to be individually triggered by you during the campaign. If there are any considerations for the campaign that require a specific setup before starting the stream, like requiring you to stream in a specific category, this will be highlighted here. You won’t be able to start the campaign until the setup is correct according to the requested deliverables.

Campaign Assist

Campaign Assist gives you real-time tips while you’re live with a sponsorship. Tips help you stay on top of the brand talking points and content requirements you agreed to when you accepted the campaign. If you miss something, like a required talking point in an ad read, you can course-correct while you’re still live instead of finding out after the campaign is over. Campaign Assist is in its testing phase, and we’re still improving it.

  • Where tips appear: As dismissible notifications in your Activity Feed and in the Sponsorship Tool in your Stream Manager quick actions.
  • Dismissible, but always on: You can dismiss a tip, but Campaign Assist can’t be turned off. If a tip flags a missed requirement, fix it while you’re still live.
  • Only you see tips: Nothing changes for your viewers.
  • Campaign requirements only: Campaign Assist checks against the requirements in your Sponsorship Invitation. It doesn’t give guidance on your tone, personality, or creative direction.
  • How it works: Campaign Assist monitors your stream using additional automated systems, some of which use AI.
  • Your payout: Tips help you meet your campaign requirements so you can earn your full payout. A tip on its own doesn’t change your earnings. A person reviews every alert before it counts as a violation. How you’re paid still depends on your campaign format (see Accepting a Campaign).

Completing a Campaign and Getting Paid

You can see all your ongoing campaigns in the Sponsorship Portal under the manage tab and under completed campaigns in the completed tab.

Revenue for any campaigns completed from the Sponsorship Portal* will be visible on your revenue dashboard within a week of completion. All campaigns will go through moderation before they are paid out.

*This does not apply for any third-party campaigns you complete. Third-party campaign payouts are handled by the respective third-party partner.

Stream Display Ads

We’re continually improving the ad experience for viewers on Twitch. Enjoy your favorite streamers with even less ad disruption with Stream Display Ads.

What are Stream Display Ads

Stream display ads (SDAs) are 15-second video ads that appear on channels before or during a live stream. Viewers are able to see and hear creators while these ads are displayed.

Viewers may see multiple variations of Stream Display Ads. There is no ad revenue difference to monetized streamers based on the type of stream display ad shown.

Lower-third

The lower-third Stream Display Ad appears below the video player.

We’re bringing Stream Display Ads to mobile! Much like on desktop, viewers will now see lower third stream display ads under the video player in portrait mode in the app. This means more ad revenue to monetizing streamers who stay opted in!

Turbo Subscribers do not see Lower-third Stream Display Ads. Streamers continue to earn from ads missed by Turbo Subscribers.

Skyscraper

The skyscraper unit renders between the live stream and chat.

Turbo Subscribers do not see Skyscraper Stream Display Ads. Streamers continue to earn from ads missed by Turbo Subscribers.

Mirror-C

Mirror-C Stream Display Ads appear between the live stream and chat.

Turbo Subscribers do not see Mirror-C Stream Display Ads. Streamers continue to earn from ads missed by Turbo Subscribers.

Provide feedback via UserVoice!

Enabling Stream Display Ads

Streamers can enable or disable Stream Display Ads in their Ads Manager. Using Ads Manager, streamers can manage the density and duration of ads.

Opting out of Stream Display Ads means you are opting out of a less disruptive ad experience for your community. Creators can opt out of Stream Display Ads shown on their channel via the Creator Dashboard. Navigate to Settings > Partner / Affiliate > Ads.

Experiments

Experimental features may alter or disappear without warning.

Starting in December 2022, we’re experimenting with an update to Stream Display Ads (SDAs) to make them even less interruptive. Select viewers will notice an update to SDAs as seen in the examples below.

New/Experimental Stream Display Ads

Headliner

The Headliner is a display ad that shows on the homepage of Twitch.tv. Now, we’re bringing that same Headliner experience to the Following page within the Twitch mobile app for iOS and Android. This is a part of our ongoing work to provide less interruptive ad experiences for viewers while adding value to brands.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why are we experimenting with Stream Display Ads?

Ads are important to Twitch, and to our community. We’ve heard the feedback that ads are too interruptive, and we want creators to have the opportunity to earn additional income via advertising while building their communities, without the interruption that comes with standard video ads.

Where can creators find Stream Display Ad revenue?

Revenue earned for Stream Display Ads will be added to creators’ normal monthly payout. Ad revenue, found in channel analytics in the creator dashboard, will include both video ad and Stream Display ad revenue.

Can viewers close or minimize Stream Display Ads while they are showing?

No, viewers won’t be able to close or minimize the ads for the time period they are shown.

How long is each Stream Display Ad?

The amount may fluctuate as we learn about what works best, and as demand for these ads changes.

Will subscribers see Stream Display Ads?

Stream Display Ads will follow the same rules creators have set for their channels. So, if a creator offers ad-free viewing for subscribers, Stream Display Ads will not be shown to subscribers.

Will running Stream Display Ads contribute to pre-roll free time?

No, Stream Display Ads won’t contribute to pre-roll free time at launch.

What is the Headliner?

Headliner consists of a display ad placement on the Twitch homepage and the Following tab of the Twitch mobile app.

Will I earn a revenue share from Headliner?

These ads will not show up on individual channels; as a result, streamers will not receive a share of ad revenue from Headliner.

Why don’t I see a Headliner on the Twitch homepage and mobile app every day?

When advertisers purchase the Headliner display ad placement, their ads will show on both the Twitch.tv homepage, and the Following tab within the Twitch mobile app.

If an advertiser does not purchase the Headliner display ad for a specific day, then there will be no ad shown on that day.

Stream Recaps

Your Stream Recap is a shelf of Clips from your latest stream, shown on your channel page. Clips you and your channel editors make while you’re live are added automatically, so viewers who missed your stream can catch up. You can review, edit, or add to your Recap at any time. Stream Recaps are available to anyone who streams on Twitch.

Stream Recaps aren’t the same as your annual Twitch Recap, a once-a-year look back at your time on Twitch.

The Recap shelf on channel pages is available on every platform. Recaps on the home screen are available on the Twitch mobile app.

Viewers: Where to Find Stream Recaps

Stream Recaps let you catch up on streams you missed from the channels you watch.

Channel Page

Visit a streamer’s channel page on any platform to see Recaps from their recent streams. Clips play in the order they happened during the stream.

Home Screen (Twitch Mobile App)

On the Twitch mobile app, Recaps from channels you follow appear on your home screen.

If a channel’s latest stream doesn’t have enough Clips, its Recap shelf is hidden.

Streamers: How Your Recap Is Created

While you’re live, you and your channel editors can make Clips of your stream. These Clips are added to your Recap in the order they happened, and your Recap appears on your channel to viewers about an hour after your stream ends. Your stream must be at least 1 minute long, and your Recap can include up to 25 Clips.

There’s nothing to post. Each stream gets its own Recap, and your Recaps stay on your channel page.

Reviewing and Editing Your Recap

From your Stream Summary, review the Clips available for your latest Recap. You can filter by:

  • Clips I’ve made
  • Editor Clips
  • Community Clips

You can add or remove Clips, and change your Recap’s title. By default, your Recap’s title is the title of your stream. Once your Recap is posted, if you edit a Clip in your Recap, the changes appear right away. If you delete a Clip, it’s removed from your Recap.

To review your Recap before it appears on your channel, open your Stream Summary on the web or in the Twitch mobile app. In the mobile app, you can also tap the + button in the bottom navigation and select Review and Edit Recap. After your Recap is posted, this option is called Edit Recap.

Turning Off Automatic Clip Inclusion

Automatic inclusion is on by default. To change it:

  • Go to Creator Dashboard > Settings > Stream.
  • Under Clips Settings, find Automatically include Clips created by me or my editors in Recaps.
  • Turn the toggle off.

With the setting off, Clips aren’t added to your Recap automatically. To add a Clip yourself, select it in your Clips Manager and choose Add to Recap. In the Twitch mobile app, you can also tap the + button in the bottom navigation bar to build your Recap.

Who Can Add Clips to Your Recap?

Clips made by you and your channel editors are added to your Recap automatically. Clips made by viewers (Community Clips) aren’t added automatically, but you can add them yourself with Add to Recap.

Any Clip you add must come from the stream your Recap covers.

Frequently Asked Questions

How are Clips added to my Recap?
Clips made by you and your editors while you’re live are added automatically, in the order they happened. Your Recap appears on your channel about an hour after your stream ends. Community Clips made by viewers aren’t added automatically, but you can add them yourself.
Can I edit my Recap?
Yes, at any time. Your Recap is always on your channel page, so there’s no separate posting step. Review and edit it from your Stream Summary.
How many Clips can my Recap include?
Your Recap shows up to 25 Clips. When you review your Recap, you’ll see every eligible Clip from the stream, so you can choose which ones to include.
Does my Stream Recap expire?
No. Each stream’s Recap stays on your channel page.
Can I remove a Clip from my Recap?
Yes. Remove it while reviewing your Recap. If you delete the Clip itself, it’s also removed from your Recap.
Do I need to be an Affiliate or Partner to have a Stream Recap?
No. Anyone who streams on Twitch can have a Stream Recap.
Do Stream Recap Clips help recover a Watch Streak?
Yes. Watching Clips in a Recap from a stream you missed can help recover your Watch Streak, but Recap Clips don’t show the Watch Streaks icon.
Is a Stream Recap the same as my Twitch Recap?
No. Your Twitch Recap is a once-a-year, personalized summary of your time on Twitch. A Stream Recap is a shelf on your channel page with Clips from one of your streams.

If you’re experiencing issues with Stream Recaps, contact Twitch Support.

Streamer Achievement Program

The Streamer Achievement Program recognizes the monumental efforts streamers put into building their communities. Eligible creators may redeem one Bleed Purple Statue per milestone per channel at 5 million, 50 million, and 250 million Hours Watched. In this guide, learn how to redeem your statue, and who is eligible to receive the Bleed Purple Statue.

For advice and support growing your channel, visit Creator Camp today!

What is the Streamer Achievement Program?

The Streamer Achievement Program recognizes streamers who have dedicated their careers to building a community on Twitch. It strives to recognize the extraordinary achievements of our streamers who consistently show up with immense passion for their viewers and dedication to the art of streaming. Affiliates and Partners who meet the minimum Hours Watched requirements are eligible for redemption of a Bleed Purple Statue.

How Do I Redeem a Bleed Purple Statue?

To redeem a Bleed Purple Statue, your channel must be an Affiliate or Partner that has signed the Monetized Streamer Agreement (“MSA”) AND:

  • Have achieved any of the 5 million, 50 million, or 250 million Hours Watched Achievements. (Learn more)
  • Must not have a current enforcement on your account. (Learn more)
  • Reside in an eligible country for shipping (Learn more)

Click here to track your progress towards each Hours Watched Achievement.

Eligible Affiliates and Partners may redeem one statue per achievement per channel:

  • Bleed Purple Statue in Purple – 5 million Hours Watched
  • Bleed Purple Statue in Marble – 50 million Hours Watched
  • Bleed Purple Statue in Chrome – 250 million Hours Watched

Achievements update your progress every 24-72 hours. Hours Watched tracking starts from 2015 to present.

If you meet the above criteria, you can redeem a Bleed Purple Statue from your Achievements page.

Do not show your unique redemption code to anyone. To prevent accidentally sharing your redemption code with viewers, we disallow code redemption while your channel is live.

Once you receive your code, you will sign into our redemption portal. You may be asked to authenticate your Twitch account.

Shipping & Delivery

Once the Bleed Purple Statue is available to redeem in your Achievements page, you may request it be shipped to you at any time. The code will not expire.

Take care when filling out your shipping information, as address and legal name cannot be updated after submission. Any special characters (traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, etc) and unique alphanumeric characters (Ü, é, ñ, etc) should be avoided.

After you redeem your statue(s), a confirmation will be sent to your email. A tracking number will be sent to your email once your statue(s) have shipped.

After you complete your shipping & delivery information, you can expect your shipment to arrive in 2-8 weeks.

If your country is not selectable as a pre-listed option when filling out your shipping information, you may select Other only if your country is not one of inelligible countries listed below.

Ineligible Shipping Countries

The list of eligible shipping destinations is subject to change at any time without prior notice. We do our best to keep this information current, but availability may be updated based on local regulations, carrier restrictions, or internal policy changes.

If the country you select is not available for shipping at the time your order is processed, our team will contact you to provide an update and discuss available options.
