Frequently Asked Questions

What are Hours Watched?
Hours Watched (or minutes watched), is the total time your live stream was watched, across all your viewers. This metric can represent sustained effort building communities over varying lengths of time. It recognizes a streamer’s achievements regardless of audience size, or number of subscribers or followers.

In a simplified example, imagine a theater filled with 100 people. If a play or performance lasts 1 hour, 100 hours have been watched – 1 hour per audience member. In terms of your stream, if you stream for 1 hour to 100 people, you have gained 100 hours watched. Similarly, if you stream for 1 hour to 10 people, you have gained 10 hours watched. Stream 9 more times at 1 hour each to the same audience size, you have gained a total of 100 hours watched. In this way, a streamer who consistently puts in time and effort to create engaging content over a long period of time can achieve a high level of hours watched, even if they do not have a high number of current viewers.

Hours watched only accrue on live streams, and so does not include VOD content. Viewers must be actively watching your live stream to contribute towards hours watched.

Who can receive a Bleed Purple Statue?
To redeem a Bleed Purple Statue, you must:
  • Be a Twitch Partner or Affiliate who has signed the Monetized Streamer Agreement
  • Meet 5 million, 50 million, or 250 million hours watched
  • Must not have a current enforcement on your account
  • Reside in an eligible country for shipping
  • Redeem the reward via the redemption portal.
I’m not a Partner or Affiliate, but I completed one of the Hours Watched achievements. Am I still able to redeem my statue?
No. In order to claim a Bleed Purple Statue, you must have signed the Monetized Streamer Agreement (“MSA”) by participating in our Affiliate or Partner program.
What if I can’t access my account to claim my reward?
If you’re having trouble accessing your account or claiming your achievement reward, contact Twitch Support here for help right away.
If I change my account username, can I have my Bleed Purple Statue physical plaque updated?
No. Bleed Purple Statues are awarded one per account, per achievement. If you change your Twitch account username, the statue will not be resent.
Do Bleed Purple Statue physical plaques support localized display names?
The physical plaques on the Bleed Purple Statues support alphanumeric characters only. If your channel uses a localized display name, your plaque will use a lowercase, English version of your localized display name.
I dropped the Bleed Purple Statue and it broke! Can I get a new one?
Uh-oh, sorry to hear that! At this time, we’re not able to replace any statues that are broken accidentally.
My Bleed Purple Statue was lost or stolen. What do I do?
Yikes! Let’s get you a new one. Contact Twitch Support here right away.

Any replacement items require a signature for delivery.

My Bleed Purple Statue arrived damaged or broken. What do I do?
Oh no! Please take a picture, and contact Twitch Support here right away.

Any replacement items require a signature for delivery.

Can I sell my Bleed Purple Statue for monetary value?
No. The Twitch Bleed Purple Statue(s) is intended to celebrate your hard-earned accomplishment; therefore, it is for personal use only and may not be sold or otherwise transferred to anyone else. Bleed Purple Statue recipient(s) who violate this policy are subject to disciplinary action, at Twitch’s sole discretion, that includes, but is not limited to, forfeiture of the Bleed Purple Statue(s), ineligibility for future Twitch Bleed Purple Statue(s), and possible Twitch account suspension.
My Bleed Purple Statue is heading to the wrong address / there is an error in my Bleed Purple Statue address. What do I do?
Once the Bleed Purple Statue is requested, the shipping information you provided (address and legal name) cannot be updated.

Streamer Shouts

This guide is for streamers. Streamer Shouts is a way to engage with your viewers after your stream ends. Once you go offline, send a personal Shout to viewers from your stream, celebrating the moments and milestones that made it special, delivered straight to their Shouts.

Are you a viewer who received a Shout? Shouts are personal messages from streamers to their community. See For Viewers to find, react to, and manage notifications for Shouts.

Streamer Shouts is available to some streamers and their communities. Availability can’t be requested.

How to Send a Shout

After your stream ends, you can send a Shout from the Twitch website or the mobile app. Either way, you’re sending the same Shout.

  • Open Shouts. On the Twitch website, select the Shouts icon at the top of the page, then select Send a Shout. If viewer groups are waiting for a Shout, the button shows how many, for example Send a Shout (2). In the mobile app, go to Activity, select the Shouts tab, then select Send a Shout.
  • Under Who would you like to reach?, select a viewer group. Each group shows how many viewers are in it, and some are marked RECOMMENDED.
  • Under What would you like to say?, write your Shout, then select Send Shout. You’ll see Shout sent! when it goes out.

You can send Shouts without worrying about spamming your community. Twitch has protections in place for each viewer, working together with their individual notification settings, to keep them from getting too many notifications. And with smart notifications, each notification reaches a viewer in one place (on-site, mobile, or email) instead of all three.

Viewers in that group receive your Shout. On the Twitch website, they find it under Received when they select the Shouts icon. In the mobile app, it’s in the Shouts tab on the Activity screen.

You can always check if you have any pending Shouts to send by checking your Action Items in Creator Dashboard.

Once you send a Shout, track its performance from your Shouts tab (under Activity on mobile), or the Shouts page in your Creator Dashboard. There, you can view all the Shouts you’ve sent to your community and review how they are performing. On the Twitch website, you can also find the Shouts you’ve sent by selecting the Shouts icon, then Sent.

  • Viewers reached
  • Open rate
  • Reaction rate
  • Clip view rate

View aggregated insights into your Shouts performance over time and their impact on your channel on the Shouts page in your Creator Dashboard.

Customize Your Reaction Emotes

Viewers react to your Shouts with the same emotes they use to react to your Clips. You can swap the preset emotes for your own channel emotes in the Clip Reactions section of your Stream settings in the Creator Dashboard. The emotes you choose become the reaction options for your Clips, Stories, Recaps, and Shouts. For step-by-step instructions, see Streamers: How to Customize Your Reactions.

Who Can I Send a Shout To?

You can send Shouts to viewer groups that Twitch builds from activity on your channel. Depending on your recent streams, you may see these groups:

Viewer group

Who’s in it

Raid Welcome

Viewers who joined your stream from a recent raid

Back in the Mix

Viewers who recently tuned back into your stream

Follow Anniversary

Viewers celebrating their follow anniversary

First Time Chatters

Viewers who chatted for the first time in your stream

New Followers

Viewers who followed your channel in the last week

New Subscribers

Viewers who subscribed to your channel in the last week

Recent Chatters

Viewers who participated in chat in the last week

Regulars & More

A mix of your engaged followers and ones you haven’t seen in a while

You can then send customizable notes with Clips attached to these viewer groups, personalizing them to match your voice and the moment.

You can’t request specific viewer groups to be added to your list.

Tips for Great Shouts

  • Keep it personal — an impactful Shout references something specific: a moment from the stream, or a milestone those users helped you hit
  • Keep it casual — this is a quick, warm gesture in your own voice, not a formal message
  • Write it yourself — a personal message will always land better than a generic one

Keep in mind that your Shouts are subject to Twitch’s Community Guidelines and Terms of Service.

Submit Feedback

Your participation and feedback help us make Shouts better for every streamer. You can submit feedback on this feature using Twitch UserVoice.

If you encounter issues with Shouts, contact Twitch Support.

For Viewers

Shouts are personal messages that streamers send to their community after a stream ends.

  • Find your Shouts: on the Twitch website, select the Shouts icon at the top of the page, then Received. In the mobile app, go to Activity, then the Shouts tab. Shouts don’t expire, so you can revisit them anytime.
  • React to a Shout: you can react to a Shout, but you can’t reply to it.
  • Turn Shouts notifications on or off: use the toggle on your Notifications Settings page.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can viewers reply to my Shout?
No. Viewers receive your Shout but can’t reply to it. They can react to your Shout, and you can see those reactions on the Shouts you’ve sent.
Is there a limit to how many Shouts I can send?
You can send 1 Shout per viewer group per day, except Regulars & More, which you can Shout once a week. After you send a Shout to Regulars & More, the group stays in your list, grayed out, until you can send to it again. For other groups, check back a day after your last stream.
Do my Shouts expire? How long can viewers see them?
Shouts do not expire. Once delivered, viewers can revisit your Shout anytime.
Can I schedule Shouts in advance?
No. If eligible, you can only write and send a Shout a day after your last stream, and cannot schedule it for a future time.
How is this different from the /shoutout chat command?
These are two completely different features. The /shoutout chat command is used during a live stream to celebrate other creators and redirect your community to their channel. Streamer Shouts are sent after your stream ends, directly to your own viewers, as a personal acknowledgment delivered to their Shouts.
Why can’t I send any Shouts?
As a streamer, not every stream will result in Twitch recommending that you send a Shout; some streams may not generate eligible viewer groups. When a viewer group is available, you will be able to send a Shout to that group. Streamer Shouts is also available to some streamers only, and availability can’t be requested.
Can my Shout be hidden or removed?
People you’ve blocked or banned don’t receive your Shouts. If someone reports a Shout and Twitch Safety takes action on it, the Shout is removed.

Sub Points vs Sub Count vs Plus Points

There are several features on Twitch like Emote Slots or Community Goals that use Sub Count or Sub Points. Partners and Affiliates may qualify for the Plus Program if they maintain more than 100 or more than 300 Plus Points for 3 consecutive months. It’s good to know the difference between Sub Points, Sub Count, and Plus Points.

Subscriptions

Some of the terminologies used for how subscriptions are counted can be a bit confusing. So let’s take a look at what some of the main terms mean and their use on Twitch.

Sub

Description

New Subs

Are used for the community goals feature. These are any new Prime, gift, or recurring subs that are purchased while a goal is active.

These goals always start from 0 (e.x. 0/100).

Total Sub Count

This is used for the community goals feature. It is the total number of subscriptions a creator has at any given point.

The goal starts from their current number (e.x. 788 / 1000).

Sub Points

Subscriptions come in 3 tiers. Each tier is worth a different amount of points. These are called sub points.

Plus Points

To qualify for the Plus Program, Partners and Affiliates must maintain a minimum of 100 or a minimum of 300 Plus Points for three consecutive months. Recurring subscriptions come in 3 tiers. Each tier is worth a different amount of points. Learn more about Plus Points and the Plus Program here.

Plus Point Goals

Share your Plus Program progress with your community by adding a tracker to your channel page. Affiliates and Partners can visit their Stream Manager to get started.

Plus Points goals are separate from Community Goals.

Sub Count

This is the total number of subscriptions to your channel, regardless of tier or subscription type.

Prime Sub

This is a free subscription token you receive monthly and may use to subscribe for one month to a Twitch channel of your choice. You receive this benefit to your Twitch account, if you have Prime Gaming.

Recurring Sub

This is a paid subscription that will renew based on the length of the subscription purchased (i.e monthly, every 3 months, or every 6 months).

Only recurring subscriptions count towards Plus Program qualification. Learn more.

Gifted Sub

This is a subscription purchased by one person or entity and given to others for use as a channel subscription.

Sub Points vs Sub Count

It is important to know the difference between what Sub Points are and what the Sub Count is, and what each are used for. You can find your Sub Points and Sub Count information in the Creator Dashboard within the Insights section on your Channel Analytics.

Sub Points

Sub Points are gained with each subscription a streamer gets. The subscription’s tier will determine the number of sub points that subscription is worth.

Subscription tiers grant different benefits based on which tier you have. Check out our guide on subscriptions for more information.

Subscription Tier

Sub Points

Tier 1

1 point

Tier 2

2 points

Tier 3

6 points

You can lose Sub Points if a subscription is not renewed or the tier is changed to a lower tier.

Sub Count

Prime, gift, or recurring subs are all counted as one (1) sub towards the Sub Count. This is just the number of subscriptions to the channel.

Plus Points

Learn more about the Plus program

Plus Points are used to measure qualification for the Plus Program. For a Partner or Affiliate channel to qualify forthe Plus Program, it must maintain a total of more than 100 or more than 300 Plus Points for three consecutive months.

Frequently Asked Questions

What type of subs count towards sub count?

Prime, gift, or recurring subs all count towards the sub count.

What type of subs count towards sub points?

Prime, gift, or recurring subs all count towards the sub count. However, if the gift or recurring sub is a Tier 2 or Tier 3 subscription, it will be worth more sub points than a Tier 1 subscription.

What is the difference between Plus Points goals, and Community / Creator Goals?

Plus Points goals and Community Goals are similar in that they allow you to track progress towards a goal. Both appear under your channel page. However, Community Goals integrate with Twitch’s Alerts, allow you to set up a browser source URL, and can be set up via chat by streamers or editors. Plus points goals are separate from Community Goals.

How soon should the Plus Points goal tracker update after a successful qualifying subscription purchase?

If a viewer contributes subscriptions towards your Plus points goal, the tracker may not update for two hours.

What type of subs count towards Plus points?

Recurring subs of all tiers count towards Plus points. Learn more.

Can I lose sub points?

Yes, you can lose Sub Points if a subscription is not renewed or the tier is changed to a lower tier. For emote slots, once a milestone has been reached, the corresponding emote slot is unlocked permanently and will not be lost if the sub point total subsequently drops.

For more information about emote slots please check out our article on Emote Slots.

Subscriber Badge Guide

Content in this guide is relevant to all monetized streamers. Learn more.

When someone subscribes to your channel, they will get a subscriber chat badge that is automatically displayed next to their name when they participate in your channel’s chat. As your subscribers accumulate time subscribed to your channel (3-months, 6-months, etc), they’ll reach milestones that you can customize with further badges to thank them for their continued support.

Your earliest subscribers will also get a special badge - a Founders Badge. Founders Badge is a subscriber badge that will be exclusively available to the first 10 prime or paid subscribers for non-Partner monetized channels and first 25 prime or paid subscribers for Partner channels.

Subscriber Badge Guidelines

Our Twitch Community Guidelines and Terms of Service apply to subscriber badges, Creator Badge Drops, and emotes.

Specific content prohibited from use in badges, emotes or emote codes are listed below. Subscriber badges, Creator Badge Drops, and subscription prefix codes must also comply with these conditions, which prohibit the following:

  • Nudity, and obscene or sexually suggestive content.
  • Drugs or drug paraphernalia.
  • Hate speech, racist, derogatory, and harassing words or imagery.
  • Explicit words or gestures.
  • Images of single letters (subscriber badges may have single letters if it represents the brand of the channel).
  • Violations of Twitch Brand Assets.
  • Violations of any third party intellectual property or privacy rights, such as copyrights, trademarks, or rights of publicity. Remember, these may be subject to DMCA take-downs or other requests for removal by the rights holders.

For further information on guideline enforcement, please see the Frequently Asked Questions section below.

Subscriber Badge Requirements

  • You must upload the image in three different sizes: 18px x 18px, 36px x 36px, and 72px x 72px.
  • The image must be uploaded in the PNG format.
  • The image must have a transparent background.
  • The file size cannot exceed 25kb.
  • The image must comply with Twitch Community Guidelines, Terms of Service, and DMCA Guidelines.

Managing Your Subscriber Badges

To manage your badges, head to your dashboard. From there, click the Hamburger to open the menu and click Monetization, then Subscriptions. Here, select Subscriber Badges.

On this page, you can add, change or remove your subscriber badges. The default subscriber chat badge is a star. While you are welcome to keep the default badge, it is highly recommended that you upload your own subscriber chat badge to personalize your channel.

Monetized streamers begin with badge slots up to 1 year. Partners begin with badge slots up to 10 years. As your tenure grows, you will unlock more badge slots. You will unlock one year of badge slots longer than your current monetization tenure with Twitch.

You cannot upload a custom founders badge for your channel.

How to upload a custom subscriber badge
  • Go to the Monetization section of your Dashboard.
  • Navigate to the Subscriptions section.
  • Click Subscriber Badges.
  • Here, choose the badge you’d like to modify by selecting it from the dropdown menu beneath Manage Badges.
  • Click the + symbol on each size to upload 3 identical images in the sizes specified by the uploader:
  • Click Save Changes.

To delete a badge once it has been uploaded, click Delete Badge next to the badge you’d like to delete after selecting it on the dropdown menu.

Badge Flair

Badge flair is a special flair overlaid over the top of a Tier 2 or Tier 3 subscriber’s subscription badge. Badge flair allows your viewers to stand out in chat and be recognized for their strong financial support towards your channel.

Managing Your Badge Flair

You can find the option to enable, customize or disable badge flair on your channel on your Subscription Badges page of your Monetization preferences, underneath the Manage Badges section.

To enable or disable badge flair, click the toggle at the top of the Badge Flair panel. We’ve provided a default badge flair for each tier for you to use, pictured below.

This is the default badge flair for Tier 2 subscribers.

This is the default badge flair for Tier 3 subscribers.

You may also upload your own, custom badge flair. Please keep in mind these requirements when creating a flair:

  • You’ll need six images in total:
    • Tier 2 Flair: 18 x 18px, 36 x 36px, and 72 x 72px.
    • Tier 3 Flair: 18 x 18px, 36 x 36px, and 72 x 72px.
  • Your flair must be uploaded in the PNG format, have a transparent background, and the file size cannot exceed 25kb.
  • Your flair must comply with the Twitch Community Guidelines, Terms of Service, and DMCA Guidelines.

To upload a custom badge flair:

  • Click the Upload Custom Flair box.
  • Under the Tier 2 and Tier 3 sections, click the + icon on each box to upload the appropriately sized file (from left to right, 18 x 18px, 36 x 36px and 72 x 72px).
  • Preview your badge flair in the Flair Preview section. You can change which badge is shown with your flair in the preview by using the dropdown menu underneath Manage Badges.
  • Click Save Changes.

In order for your badge flair to go live on the site, you’ll need to upload all of the required images under the Tier 2 and Tier 3 sections.

To delete your custom badge flair, click the Delete Custom Flair button.

Frequently Asked Questions

Badge Flair
Can I disable badge flair on my channel?
Yes. To enable/disable badge flair, navigate to the Subscriber Badges page in the Subscriptions section of your Monetization preferences in your Creator Dashboard. Click the toggle next to Badge Flair.
Will my viewers be able to disable their badge flair?
Yes. Viewers will be able to disable their badge flair globally via their Chat Settings. For more information, please see our How to Subscribe help article.
Will my viewers be informed that badge flair is offered on my channel?
Yes. When on the subscription page, badge flair will be listed as a Tier 2/Tier 3 benefit for your channel.
Can I upload a custom badge flair for my channel?
Yes! You can upload a custom flair for your Tier 2 and Tier 3 subscribers. To do so, head over to your Subscriber Badges page in the Subscriptions section of your Monetization preferences, in your Creator Dashboard. Then, tick the Use Custom Flair box. For more information about the requirements for custom flair images or the upload process, please see the Managing Your Badge Flair section of this article.
Do I need to upload a custom sub badge in order for my Tier 2 and Tier 3 subscribers to have access to badge flair?
Yes. Badge flair cannot be used with the default sub badge.
Can I put my flair beneath my sub badge instead of over the top?
We only support badge flair overlaid on top of your sub badge, although you can design around it to make it appear as if it’s underneath.
Moderation & Safety
Will my subscriber badges be available for my subscribers immediately upon uploading?
Yes. Unlike Emoticons, badges will only appear in your channel and therefore do not require manual approval before they appear to your audience.
My subscriber badge disappeared and now I only see the default star. What happened?
You should have received an email regarding the reason why your badge has been removed (check your spam filter). If you did not, simply file a ticket via help.twitch.tv to inquire (Partners, please be sure to log in to ensure your Partnership status is noted for expedited assistance). Remember that all badges must comply with the badge and emoticon guidelines. To resolve this, you may alter the badge so that it does not violate any of these rules, or submit a different badge altogether.
I think a badge violates Twitch’s rules. How do I report it?
You can report a subscriber badge directly from chat. Select the badge next to the person’s username, then select the 3 Vertical Dots icon and choose Report. The report window confirms what you’re reporting, for example, “You are reporting [username] for their Subscriber badge.” Select Report Subscriber Badge to submit. To learn more about reporting, see Filing a User Report. Violations of third-party rights should be reported by the rights holders.

Subscriber Emote Guide

Available to all monetized streamers, emotes are a great way to customize your channel and rewards your subscribers and cheerers. Members of the Twitch Affiliate and Partner programs get some additional perks. Learn more here.

This article provides an overview of how to manage your emotes.

For information on emote rules, guidelines and formatting requirements see Emote Guidelines.

How to Manage Your Emotes

To manage your emotes, head to your dashboard. On the left-hand sidebar, click Viewer Rewards, then Emotes, then Subscriber Emotes.

Here you will find a list of your current emotes grouped by tier, as well as your current emote prefix and the progress you’ve made towards unlocking your next emote. Partners also have access to Animated Emotes as a Tier 1 subscriber benefit.

If you do not have an emote prefix, you’ll need to set one before you can upload or manage emotes on this page.

To upload an emote, click the + button under the desired tier. Once uploaded, your emote will be added to the slot and saved to your Library so that it can be used later should you decide to remove it from the slot in the future. You can also upload directly into your Library instead of a specific slot by clicking on Upload New. Emotes uploaded directly to your Library will not be active until you assign them to an open slot.

You can upload a Standard emote in one of two ways.

The upload process for Animated emotes can be found here.

Auto-Resize Mode

Auto-resize mode is an easy, streamlined way to upload your emotes. To upload your emote, you’ll need a single square image file between 112x112px and 4096x4096px that is under 1MB in size. This file will then be automatically converted into our other required sizes.

  • Click the Upload icon within the square on the left-hand side to select the appropriate file. Your emote will automatically be converted into the required sizes.
  • Within the Emote Code field, choose a name for your emote (e.g: Love). Your emote’s full code will be your emote prefix combined with your emote code (e.g: prefix + Love = prefixLove).
  • Once you’ve uploaded your files and selected your code, click Upload Emote. Your emote will be saved to your Library. If you uploaded directly into a slot, it will be assigned to that slot by default.

Manual Mode

If the automatic conversions made via auto-resize mode are not to your liking and you want more control on each of the sizes, disabling auto-resize mode allows you to upload three separate sizes (28x28, 56x56, 112x112 px). This manual mode allows for image-by-image control for each size. Please note that the three sizes you supply for each emote must be of the same image and must each be under 100KB.

  • Disable the Auto-resize toggle and click the Upload icon within each square to select the appropriately sized file (specified underneath the box) for each.
  • Within the Emote Code field, choose a name for your emote (e.g: Love). Your emote’s full code will be your emote prefix combined with your emote code (e.g: prefix + Love = prefixLove).
  • Once you’ve uploaded your files and selected your code, click Upload Emote. Your emote will be saved to your Library. If you uploaded directly into a slot, it will be assigned to that slot by default.

After uploading, your emote will need to be manually reviewed and approved before it’s visible to viewers. While awaiting review, it will show as Pending Approval with a watch icon. Partners in Good Standing and Affiliates who meet certain criteria are eligible for instant emote upload, which means your emotes go live right away — no manual review needed. Check our Emote Guidelines for eligibility details.

Rearranging Emote Slots for Active Emotes

Once emotes are uploaded, you can rearrange their positions within each tier by dragging and dropping or manually typing in the desired number. Rearranging your emote positions will affect the order that emotes are displayed on the site.

To rearrange your emotes with drag-and-drop:
  • Mouse over the desired emote.
  • Click and hold down the mouse button and drag the emote ahead of, in between, or after any other emotes within a given tier.
  • Release to save changes.
For manual rearrangement:
  • Click on the slot number of an emote and type in the desired position.
  • Hit enter to save changes.

Active emotes can only be rearranged within the same tier. For example, a Tier 1 emote cannot be dragged and dropped into Tier 2. If you’d like to change an emote’s tier, you can do so using your emote Library.

Removing an Emote from an Active Slot

  • Click on the Remove from Slot icon for the emote you would like to remove.
  • Agree to the prompt to Remove Emote.

Your emote will be removed from the slot but will still be accessible for reassignment later from your emote Library.

Emote Tips and Ideas

We’ve provided some tips and best practices for making your own emotes to help you maximize the experience of using emotes on your channel.

If your emote is based on a photo, ensure that the image has good lighting. A perfectly good emote slot is wasted with a photo of your face that was taken in such poor lighting that you have blue skin and no one can make out your expression.

Link your emotes (even vaguely) together by style, color, or have them all done by the same artist. This creates a streamlined, professional look and adds to your overall brand appeal.

Consider that a simple image can often be the most pleasing to the eye. Since you only have 28px to work with, too much detail or too many words can clutter the emote, making it look messy and hard to understand.

If you want memes, base your emotes on memes generated by your own community. Be original! Be YOU. This will cause your emote to have staying power beyond the short lifespan of most general internet memes, because it is based on your channel and your community can feel closer to the source of the meme.

Monitor the popularity of your emotes as time goes on. Are most of your emotes getting used about the same, but perhaps a couple of them are rarely used? Consider replacing them with something new!

Try running emote ideas and samples by your community so you do not miss an opportunity for feedback prior to upload. Ask them what they would love to see and what they would not use much. You have your very own focus group at your fingertips, so utilize that!

Will my emotes be available for my subscribers to use immediately?
Your emote will need to be manually reviewed before it’s available on the site. However, Partners in Good Standing and Affiliates who meet certain criteria are eligible for instant emote upload — your emotes go live right away without manual review. See our Emote Guidelines for details.
Can I change my emote prefix?

If I previously left the Affiliate Program and rejoined will I get a new emote prefix?
