Subscriber Streams

Subscriber Streams give streamers the option to host a stream for their most dedicated community members: subscribers, VIPs, and moderators. Subscriber Streams are a great way to show appreciation to your core community, and thank them for their support.

During a Subscriber Stream, anyone can access your channel for a free preview, and each stream is automatically tagged via Twitch’s native tagging system for easy discoverability.

Subscriber Streams are available today for all qualifying Affiliates and Partners.

On this page:

  • How can I share my feedback?
  • As a Streamer, how can I get access?
  • What are the requirements?
  • How do I start a Subscriber Stream?
  • What do Subscriber Streams look like for me as a viewer?
  • What kind of content can be streamed on Subscriber Streams?
  • Best Practices for Subscriber Streams
  • Frequently Asked Questions

How Can I Share My feedback?

Have you used Subscriber Streams as a broadcaster or viewer? Do you have any feedback or requests to improve the feature? We encourage you to please take a short survey and share your thoughts with us. Thanks in advance!

Take the Survey

As a Streamer, How Can I Get Access?

Subscriber Streams are available to creators who meet the minimum requirements. Access to this feature will be removed for channels that violate the Twitch Terms of Service and Community Guidelines.

What Are the Requirements?

The minimum requirements to broadcast a Subscriber Stream are:

  • Must be a Twitch Affiliate or Twitch Partner.
  • Must have broadcast at least 90 unique days as Affiliate or Partner
  • Must not have violated Twitch Community Guidelines in your last 90 unique broadcast days. This means that if your channel received a suspension, you would need to broadcast on 90 different days without another violation to be eligible again.

How Do I Start a Subscriber Stream?

Manage audience settings before going live in the Creator Dashboard on web.

If your channel is eligible, you will see the option to change Audience on your Creator Dashboard. To begin your Subscriber Stream:

  • Visit your Creator Dashboard.
  • Select Subscribers under the Audience section of your Stream Information tab.
  • Moderators and VIPs are able to view Subscriber Streams by default. If you wish to remove their access, uncheck their respective checkboxes in the Audience section.
  • Begin your stream.

Please note that you will not be able to set a stream as a Subscriber Stream while broadcasting live. You will need to go offline before editing your Audience selection.

You must select the All Subscribers option under the Audience Dashboard setting before beginning your stream.

Subscriber Streams will be automatically tagged on creation with the tag Subscriber Stream. Viewers can use the Twitch search bar or browse directory filters to quickly find and navigate to this content when it’s live.

What do Subscriber Streams look like to Viewers?

As a viewer, Subscriber Streams open up a new form of unique interaction between you and your favorite content creators on Twitch.

If you are not a current subscriber of a channel broadcasting a Subscriber Stream, you can still tune in for a free preview. You will be notified when your free preview has expired. A free preview is available daily for each channel broadcasting a Subscriber Stream.

For example, if Streamer X and Streamer Y were to broadcast Subscriber Streams on two consecutive days, you would have a free preview for both of their streams on both days.

If your free preview expires and you wish to get involved and support the streamer, you can subscribe at any time. If you are a Prime member, you may use your monthly free Prime subscription to subscribe to any channel and gain access to current and future Subscriber Streams on that channel for the duration of your subscription.

Receiving a gift sub also unlocks the ability to view Subscriber Streams.

You may need to refresh the page after subscribing in order to gain access.

If you notice content violating Twitch’s Terms of Service and Community Guidelines in a Subscriber Stream, please file a channel report. Instructions on how to file a report can be found here.

What Kind of Content Can Be Streamed on Subscriber Streams?

Subscriber Streams are not private streams. They are smaller, personal broadcasts available only to your subscribers, Moderators, and VIPs. Whether or not your content is streamed to everyone or your core supporters, the rules are the same. All content must follow Twitch’s Terms of Service and Community Guidelines. Subscriber Streams are not a free pass to avoid those rules and guidelines.

If you notice content violating Twitch’s Terms of Service and Community Guidelines in a Subscriber Stream, please file a channel report. Instructions on how to file a report can be found here.

Please also note that content you publish under Subscriber Stream VODs and / or streams are still subject to DMCA Guidelines.

Best Practices for Subscriber Streams

When planning your Subscriber Stream, consider:

  • Update Your Title (Strongly Encouraged) - You may wish to update your stream title to indicate that it’s for subscribers by prefixing your title with [Subs Stream]. This helps new viewers, and your audience understand what is going on.
  • Subscriber Only Public Chat (Optional) - You can also restrict your public chat to subscribers only using the /subscribers chat command. This will allow your subscribers to chat among themselves, but those messages are also viewable by non-subscribers. For more information on chat commands, see this article.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do VODs work for Subscriber Streams?

After a Subscriber Stream, the corresponding VOD will be automatically available for Subscribers. This is regardless of whether the Subscriber-only archives setting in your Dashboard settings is toggled on or off.

If you so choose, you can edit permissions on individual Subscriber Stream VODs via the Video Producer tab of your dashboard.

How do Clips work for Subscriber Streams?

Clips can still be created during a Subscriber Stream and shared during and after the stream. Clips created from Subscriber Streams will not have any restrictions placed on them. If you do not wish for Clips to be shared you may moderate your Clips accordingly in the Clips Manager.

How can I get access to start a Subscriber Stream?

The option to begin Subscriber Streams will be available to all qualifying Affiliates and Partners. For more information see this section of the article.

Which platforms can I broadcast Subscriber Streams from?

At this time, all qualifying Partners and Affiliates can start a Subscriber Stream on web via their Creator Dashboard.

Which platforms can I watch a Subscriber Stream on?

At this time, all logged in viewers can access Subscriber Streams on web, the Twitch desktop client, and the Twitch app on iOS and Android devices.

How does Twitch address inappropriate content on Subscriber Streams?

The trust and safety of our viewers is of the utmost importance to us at Twitch. That doesn’t change with Subscriber Streams. Streamers that incur violations will have their ability to start Subscriber Streams removed.

Streamers who wish to use this feature need to meet our minimum requirements, and like all content on Twitch, viewers can report violations of Twitch’s Terms of Service and Community Guidelines in a Subscriber Stream, please file a channel report. Instructions on how to file a report can be found here.

Can I set my Subscriber Stream to be only for Tier 2 and / or Tier 3 Subscribers?

Not at this moment in time, Subscriber Streams are currently for all subscribers of all subscription tiers.

Will Subscriber Streams stop me from completing my Affiliate “Path to Partner” Achievement?

No, we understand that by broadcasting Subscriber Streams your overall CCU may be lower. As such, we do not wish to penalize Affiliates that wish to create custom content for their loyal subscribers.

Will VIPs and Channel Moderators have access to Subscriber Streams?

VIPs and Channel Moderators will be included in Subscriber Streams by default. Streamers have the option of removing VIPs and/or moderators from their Subscriber Stream from their go-live dashboard.

Can I use my monthly Prime subscription to view a Subscriber Stream?

Yes, if you use your monthly Prime subscription to subscribe to a channel you will be able to view that channel’s Subscriber Streams until expiration.

If I receive a Gifted Subscription, can I view Subscriber Streams?

Yes, a Gifted Subscription to a channel will allow you to view that channels Subscriber Streams until expiration.

I was just made a VIP or Channel Moderator for a Subscriber Stream that is in-progress, but I can’t see the video.

Streamers have the option of including VIPs and moderators in their Subscriber Streams. If they’ve done so and you became a VIP or Channel Mod while the Subscriber Stream was live, please refresh your browser to gain access.

Why didn’t I receive a notification for a channel broadcasting a Subscriber Stream?

Notifications for Subscriber Streams will only go out to subscribers of a channel.

I heard one of my favorite channels was doing a Subscriber Stream, why can’t I see it in the directory?

Subscriber Streams will only show in Browse for logged in users.

I’m a Partner and I don’t see the Audience selection on my stream info. Why is that?

The Audience selector will only be visible to Partners who have Channel Subscriptions available on their channel. For example, non-revenue Partners will not see this option. Even if the feature is visible, you must still meet the minimum requirements (see above) to use Subscriber Streams.

Will I be able to use Squad Streams while broadcasting a Subscriber Stream?

Yes, you will be able to use Squad Streams while broadcasting a Subscriber Stream. If a viewer is not subscribed to the other broadcaster(s) you’re streaming with, the viewer will see a free preview of their channel(s) within the Squad Stream display.

Does my time prior to becoming an Affiliate count toward my 90 unique broadcast days?

No. In order to broadcast a Subscriber Stream, you must have broadcast on 90 unique broadcast days as an Affiliate or Partner without a Terms of Service violation.

Third Party Campaigns on Twitch

Features described in this page are for Twitch Affiliates and Partners only.

Affiliates must complete Creator Sponsorship Certification to access sponsorships on Twitch, including third-party campaigns.

Access And How-To

To find third-party opportunities and offers available to you:

  • Navigate to your Creator Dashboard.
  • Click on Monetization in the left navigation menu.
  • Click on Sponsorships.

Click on one of the available campaigns to visit the related third-party webpage, where you can review the offer and accept the campaign.

Campaign Support

All third-party campaigns visible in the sponsorships tab are sourced and handled by third parties. If you are having any issues, please contact their support team.

Wehype Support

The best way to access Wehype support is to check the Wehype Support Center (Creator FAQ), which has answers to most common questions. If you still need help, you can reach out directly via email.

You can contact Wehype support by:

  • Email: support@wehype.com
  • Support Center (Creator FAQ): help.wehype.com/en/collections/1382472-creator-faq
  • Discord: If you are already a member of the Wehype Discord, ask for help in the dedicated support channel. To keep the community safe from bots, Wehype does not share a public invite link; all creators receive an exclusive invite to the server upon signing up to Wehype.
  • X (Twitter): You can follow Wehype on X, but avoid sending DMs for support requests, as this is not an official support channel and your message may be missed. Please use the support email instead.

Further resources around Wehype’s terms of service and payments can be found in the Wehype Creator Terms of Service.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I get access to the third-party campaigns on Twitch?
Third-party campaigns are managed and executed through our third-party partners. Depending on their current campaigns, the supply of these may look different depending on your broadcast region and/or language. Make sure you are signed up with the relevant third-party partner and have linked your Twitch account on their website. Also, be sure to enable sponsorships emails in your Email Notification Settings.
Can I see the sponsorship payout before accepting?
All offers should be transparent on what your potential payout is. As long as you meet the campaign requirements, you will get paid what was on the offer.
How will I be compensated for completing the campaign?
You will be paid via your third-party account. It will not be part of your Twitch payout.
Are these third-party campaigns only on Twitch?
Campaigns from third parties displayed on Twitch are selected for you, but are not exclusive to Twitch.
Are you sharing any more data with third parties if I accept these campaigns?
When you connect your Twitch account to a third party, the account linking process discloses the data shared between the companies. We do not share any additional data as part of this experience beyond what is covered in the account connection disclosure you agree to when connecting your accounts.
I’m a Twitch Partner or Affiliate with access to one of these third parties. Why do I not see any opportunities in my dashboard?
The opportunities available on creator dashboards are determined by which creators the third-party partner chooses to target. If you do not see any offers, please reach out to their support.

Twitch Affiliate Program FAQ

This FAQ addresses some of the common questions asked about the Affiliate Program.

Joining the Affiliate Program

What is the Affiliate Program?
The Twitch Affiliate program allows qualified streamers to monetize their channel. Being an Affiliate unlocks new tools to help you build your audience.
What are the requirements to join the Affiliate Program?
The requirements to join the Affiliate Program are:
  • Reach 25 Followers
  • Stream for 4 Hours
  • Stream on 4 Different Days
  • Reach an Average of 3 Viewers (on 4 different days)*

*Reach a minimum of 3 average viewers over any 4 stream days in the last 30 days. Days below 3 average viewers don’t count against you.

All four achievements must be fully completed to be invited to the Affiliate program. Track progress towards your Affiliate Program invite via the Achievements section of your Creator Dashboard.

You will be invited to the Affiliate Program via email, and Twitch notification. It can take a few days after your channel becomes eligible to receive an invite.

To get started as an Affiliate or Partner, you need to turn on Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) on your account. Learn how to turn on 2FA here.

Achievement data can sometimes take 24-48 hours to sync with your dashboard data. Don’t worry if follower count, average viewers, or hours streamed achievements don’t update immediately!

I met the requirements. What’s next?
Congrats! Within 24-48 of completing your final requirement, you should receive an invitation to apply to the program via email, and in your Creator Dashboard.
I’m under 18, can I still sign up?
Yes, if you are over the age of 13. Your parent or guardian will need to agree to the terms of the Monetized Streamer Agreement (“MSA”), so make sure you have them with you when you go through the application. For more information about monetization and minors, see our Guide for Parents and Educators.
How do I check my progress towards the Affiliate Program?
Check your progress towards the Affiliate Program by navigating to your Achievements Analytics. Once your channel qualifies to join the program, you’ll be able to do so by clicking the button that appears on your Path to Affiliate achievement.
How do I complete my Affiliate Onboarding?
For a full overview on the Onboarding process, please see our Affiliate Onboarding Guide.

For further information on joining the Affiliate Program and the features the program offers, please see our help article.

Can I have Affiliate status on multiple accounts?
Yes, you can have Affiliate status on up to 5 accounts maximum. Each account must meet the Affiliate requirements independently and complete separate onboarding. If you exceed the 5-account limit, monetization features will be removed from your accounts with the least activity. Learn more about the 5-account limit.

Benefits Questions

Learn more about the community-building and monetization tools available to Affiliates here.

Onboarding Questions

In which countries is the Affiliate program available?
The Affiliate program is available globally. This means you can apply for the Affiliate program no matter where you live.
Can I be a Partner and an Affiliate?
No.
What do I do if I decide to change my information after onboarding, such as my payout type or my address?
You don’t need to start over. To update your account details (such as legal name or country) or change your payout method, edit your information directly from your Creator Dashboard → Monetization → Affiliate. To change your tax information, retake the relevant tax interview using the Retake option next to it.

Updating your information doesn’t reset your channel earnings history. Payout timing can be affected by when in the month you make changes, so if you have a pending payout or you’re unsure about timing, contact Twitch Support before making changes. To avoid delays, make changes as early in the month as possible, ideally before the 10th. Changes made after the 8th of the month may not be reflected in the current month’s payout.

For detailed guidance, see Updating Your Information in the Affiliate Onboarding Guide.

Cannot start the Affiliate onboarding flow? Or having trouble opening tax forms?
Try the following:
  • Please disable any add-ons/extensions on your internet browser
  • Please replicate the issue in an incognito window/private browsing mode while your browser extensions are disabled.
  • If disabling your browser’s extensions prove ineffective, please clear your browser’s cache and cookies to improve loading. It is very important to clear both cache and cookies! You’ll need to log into your account again after clearing these.
  • Please try a different browser entirely
  • Please attempt these steps using a different network.
I’m having issues filling in the zip code during onboarding. What should I do?
Some payout methods require a zip/postal code. If the payout method you chose requires one, you may be unable to complete your payout setup without it.

Solution: Select a payout method that doesn’t require a zip code (such as PayPal or eCheck/local bank). This lets you complete onboarding without entering this information.

If you must use a payout method requiring a zip code: Retake the tax interview that applies to you (for example, the Royalty or Service Tax Interview) and include your actual zip/postal code when you complete it. In your tax interviews, each completed interview has a Retake option. Do not enter fake or placeholder information. Use your legal address exactly as it appears on official documents.

If you’re unable to enter your legal zip code due to form validation issues, contact Twitch support.

What monetization features do Affiliates have access to?
Learn more about the community-building and monetization tools available to Affiliates here.
How many accounts can have monetization features enabled?
You may have monetization features enabled on a maximum of 5 accounts. If you exceed this limit, monetization features will be removed from your accounts with the least activity. Learn more.
How do I leave the Affiliate Program?
To request offboarding from the Affiliate Program, contact Twitch Support. You must verify your identity before this request can be processed. Once offboarding is complete, all features related to your Affiliate status are removed from your channel, including Subscriptions, Bits and Cheering, ad revenue, custom subscriber emotes, and subscriber badges. Any active subscriptions towards your channel are cancelled. Subscribers are notified that their subscription has been canceled, but are not told the reason for the cancellation.

If you voluntarily leave the Affiliate Program, you can contact Twitch Support to rejoin. If you were removed from the program by Twitch, your eligibility to rejoin may be restricted.

If you also want to delete your Twitch account, this is a separate, permanent action. Learn more about deleting your account.

What happens to my account status after I leave the Affiliate Program?
Your offboarding request is processed and confirmed right away, but it may take some time for the change to fully reflect across your account. If your Creator Dashboard still shows Affiliate status after 24 hours, contact Twitch Support.
Can I stop earning money while keeping my Affiliate status?
Yes. If you want to stop being paid without leaving the Affiliate Program, set your payout method to Hold Payouts from your Payout Onboarding dashboard. Your earnings will accrue in your account and your Affiliate status and all features remain active. You can switch back to an active payout method at any time to resume receiving payouts.
What’s the difference between setting my payout method to Hold Payouts and leaving the Affiliate Program?
Setting your payout method to Hold Payouts pauses your payouts while keeping your Affiliate status, monetization features, and existing subscriptions active. Leaving the Affiliate Program removes Affiliate status and monetization features from your channel entirely, and cancels active subscriptions to your channel. If you only want to stop receiving payments for now, use Hold Payouts instead of leaving the program.
What happens to my unpaid earnings when I leave the Affiliate Program?
If you’ve reached the payout threshold ($50 for most users) and your payout method is valid, we will issue payment to you on the next payout cycle. If your payout method isn’t valid, we’ll hold your balance until you update to a valid payout method. If your unpaid accruals haven’t reached the payout threshold, no payout will be issued. That balance remains on your account. To receive a payout, you’ll need to rejoin as a Twitch Affiliate or Partner and your accruals need to reach the payout threshold.
If I create a new channel with the same email, do I need to set up payouts again?
Yes. Each channel requires separate Affiliate onboarding, even if they use the same email address. You’ll need to complete the full onboarding process (tax forms, payout method, Monetized Streamer Agreement) for each channel. Remember, you can have monetization features enabled on a maximum of 5 accounts.

Revenue Questions

How is the subscription revenue I receive determined?
The standard subscription revenue split for Affiliates is 50/50 between you and Twitch. Eligible creators may qualify for enhanced rates through the Plus Program. As explained in the Monetized Streamer Agreement, there are certain costs, taxes, and fees that must be accounted for before you receive subscription revenue. Before the 50/50 split takes place, deductions are made from the full price of a subscription, including taxes, payment processing fees, bank fees, currency conversion fees, etc. After the split takes place, we still account for required tax withholding, which is reflected in the payout you ultimately see on your dashboard. Twitch does not set or control the rates or fees, and they vary from region to region and by each subscriber’s payment method.

For a detailed breakdown of factors that can affect your revenue, see Earnings Analytics FAQ. For all other questions about your revenue and payout, please see our guide When Am I Getting Paid.

How come my payout keeps failing?
Ensure your payout information is valid. For PayPal, it is important both country information, real name and PayPal email account matches information provided to PayPal directly.

For answers on rejected payouts, visit the Rejected Payout FAQ.

Are there any payout threshold settings?
Your channel must accrue at least $50 with most payout methods or $100 with wire transfer before each payout is eligible to be initialized.
Why am I seeing a reduction in my payout?
This could be a result of how your tax interview questionnaire was filled out. Please go back to the tax form to ensure all information is filled out properly.

For questions on your payout balance, visit Payout Balance FAQ.

When do I get paid by Twitch?
Your channel must accrue at least $50 with most payout methods or $100 with wire transfer before each payout is eligible to be initialized.

Payouts are made 15 days after the end of the month of revenue being earned. This is called Net15 (payment within 15 days after the end of the month). For example, if you earn at least $50 with most payout methods or $100 with wire transfer on April 5th, the payout will be initiated 15 days after April 30th, which is May 15th.

Example calculation: Revenue earned in April → Payout initiated on May 15th → Funds arrive in your account 1-5 days later (depending on payout method).

After the payout is initiated and depending upon the payout method, it may take several days for payouts to settle within your bank. Eligible payout methods for the $50 threshold include ACH/direct deposit, eCheck/local bank, PayPal, and check.

Learn more in our guide When Am I Getting Paid.

What does Net15 mean?
Net15 means payment is initiated within 15 days after the end of the month in which you earned revenue. This is an industry-standard payment term.

How to calculate your payout date:

  • Identify the month you earned revenue (e.g., April)
  • Find the last day of that month (e.g., April 30th)
  • Add 15 days (e.g., April 30th + 15 days = May 15th)
  • Add 1-5 days for your payout method to process (e.g., May 15th + 3 days = May 18th)

Example: You earn $50 on April 10th. Your payout will be initiated on May 15th (15 days after April 30th). If you use PayPal, funds typically arrive 1-2 days later, around May 16th-17th.

Why do I see my ad revenue fluctuate from month to month even though I have the same number of viewers?
Demand from advertisers fluctuate over time, this fluctuation may result in a variation in your ad revenue earnings as a result.
I ran an ad break, why isn’t it showing up in my Earnings Analytics page?
Ad revenue you earn from ads typically shows up in your Earnings Analytics page after 2-3 days. Click here to visit your Earnings Analytics.
What is CPM?
CPM (Cost Per Mille) is an industry standard term that refers to an amount paid for one thousand views of an advertisement.
Why is my payout taking so long?
Typically, the following payout methods are paid out within the following time frame. This is not a guarantee.

Payout Method

Timing

Direct Deposit / ACH (U.S Only)

3-5 Days

eCheck/Local Bank

1-4 Days

PayPal

1-2 days

Check

1-2 Weeks

Wire Transfer

1-3 days

Hold Payouts

N/A

For details on payout timing, visit our help article When Do I Get Paid? for more details.

The Plus Program

[January 2024] Can Affiliates Join the Partner Plus Program?

For more details on each of the below changes, visit our blog.

Starting May 1, 2024, the Plus Program will be open to Affiliates. Affiliates who earn a total of 100 Plus points or more for 3 consecutive months will qualify for a net revenue share of 60/40 from paid recurring subscriptions and gift subscriptions. Affiliates who earn a total of 300 Plus points or more for 3 consecutive months will qualify for a net revenue share of 70/30.

Twitch Stream Key FAQ

Also known as “authorization key”, your stream key uniquely identifies your stream as it enters the Twitch ingesting subsystem. Streaming encoders require your unique stream key to authorize your stream so you can go live. Unless it is reset, you should not need to re-enter your stream key into your encoding software each time you go live.

Finding Your Stream Key

Stream keys are assigned by Twitch. Retrieve your stream key from the Creator Dashboard (Settings icon -> Stream)

Never share your stream key with anyone. Don’t show your stream key on stream!

Using Your Stream Key

To stream, you need a few things: a stable internet connection, and a hardware or software encoding device.

Your software encoder (OBS, Twitch Studio, eg) requires a stream key. This essentially gives the encoder permission to stream to your Twitch account. Follow the instructions in each streaming encoder to add your stream key to your account!

Streaming from the Twitch App on iOS or Android does not require a stream key.

Refreshing Your Stream Key

You may reset your stream key at any time from the same place it is found in your Stream Settings. Refreshing your stream key changes your key for yourself only, and does not invalidate any Authorized Streamers.

Your stream key is reset each time you change your password to protect your account details. Occasionally in cases of account takeover (ATO), Twitch may reset your password and stream key for you.

Authorized Streams

Broadcasters who need to allow multiple accounts to broadcast to their channel can utilize the guest stream key feature.

In short, we do not recommend sharing your stream key with anyone. However, some channels may need to be jointly run.

To add authorized broadcasters to your channel, visit Permissions in your Stream settings in the Creator Dashboard.

Select People who can stream to your channel. Enter their email. Be sure you send the correct email.

The recipient will receive a guest stream key formatted like live_sub_[streamkey]

Removing an authorized stream account is the only way to invalidate a guest key. Refreshing your stream key changes it for yourself only, and not your authorized streamers.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is RTMP? What is an RTMP URL or broadcast URL?
RTMP is live video protocol used by Twitch to stream video. Learn more in our Twitch Inspector Glossary.

Each broadcast uses an RTMP URL that has the following format:

rtmp://TWITCH-INGEST-SERVER/app/STREAM-KEY

A breakdown of what this means:

  • rtmp:// - This is the Real-Time Media Protocol, which is an industry standard for moving video around a network
  • TWITCH-INGEST-SERVER - This is the ingest server from Twitch that you are connecting to, and identifies a specific Twitch server that receives this broadcast stream; e.g., live.twitch.tv. The valid values of ingest-server are listed in our recommended ingest endpoints: help.twitch.tv/s/twitch-ingest-recommendation. Most broadcasters do not need to manually set their Twitch ingest server.
  • STREAM-KEY - Covered in this guide, this is known as your authorization key that uniquely identifies your stream.

Never share your stream key with anyone else. Doing so could compromise your channel.

Twitch Teams

Teams are a way to unite and connect streamers. For example, the stream team on Twitch will look like this:

On a team’s page, members are displayed on the left-hand member list, with live channels at the top. Members who are live will also be featured in the team’s video player and will show the team’s description below the player.

Only Twitch Partners can create and manage teams. If a Twitch Partner creates a team, they can transfer ownership of that team to an Affiliate or regular (non-monetized) user. After this transfer process, that Affiliate or regular (non-monetized) user can manage the team, but they cannot request further ownership transfers.

HOW TO JOIN A TEAM

  • After you receive a team invitation, go to the Channel Settings section of your dashboard.
  • Click Featured Content.
  • Scroll down to the section named My Teams.
  • Select Accept on the team invite to join that team.

Team invites can expire. If you don’t have any active invites or current teams, you won’t be able to see the My Teams section on the Featured Content tab.

HOW TO CREATE A TEAM

Only Partners may create a team. To request a new team, Partners will need to open a ticket while logged in to their Partner Account. In your ticket, please provide the following information:

  • Team Page URL (i.e., www.twitch.tv/team/teamname):
  • Team Display Name:
  • Twitch account to own/edit:

Partners are limited to the creation of two teams. Deleting or transferring the ownership of a team does not allow for further creation requests.

Partners may transfer ownership of their team to other Partners, or to non-Partners. A non-Partner may include Affiliates, or non-monetized regular users. The Affiliate or regular user will have all team ownership powers of the Partner that created the account, except for requesting new teams or requesting ownership transfers. Only Partners can request ownership transfers. If a non-Partner owner needs to transfer ownership, the request will be denied by Twitch Support.

Only one account can own and edit a Twitch Team, and cannot change the URL once set. While only Partners can create a team, they can put any account in the owner/editor role. To request a change in ownership, the current owner must be a Partner and will need to Contact Support.

HOW TO EDIT/MANAGE A TEAM

EDITING TEAMS FOR TEAM OWNERS

Once you set up your team page, you can view and edit it by navigating to the My Teams section of your Channel preferences on your dashboard.

To edit your team, click on the Edit button of the team you wish to edit. This will take you to the Team Dashboard which will have the following options:

Option

Description

Revenue:

Here you will see the revenue generated by your team members if they have chosen to share this information with you.

Stats:

Here you will see the channel stats of your team members if they have chosen to share this information with you.

Members:

Here you can invite or remove members from your team.

Featured Channels:

Here you can choose channels to feature when none of your team members are currently live. You do not need to invite a channel to your team to feature them.

Settings:

You can change your team’s display name, public description, logo, banner, and background image here.

TEAM SETTINGS FOR TEAM MEMBERS

Once you have joined a team, you will be able to view and edit your team settings by navigating to your My Teams section under the Channel and Videos tab of your Channel Settings. You will have the following options:

Option

Description

View your team:

Click on the team’s name that you wish to view, and that will take you to the team page.

Stats:

If checked, this option will share your channel’s statistics with the team owner.

Revenue:

If checked, this option will share your channel’s revenue information with the team owner.

Main:

If checked, this option will feature that team’s display name in your channel info below your stream category. You can only choose one team to be your main team, but you can change your main team at any time.

Remove:

This option is the trash can icon; click this if you want to remove yourself from a team.

Twitch Unity Guilds Program Overview

Twitch Unity Guilds are open to Affiliates! Learn more.

What are Twitch Unity Guilds?

Imagine a space where creators who share your identity, your experiences, and your passion for streaming come together to lift each other up. That’s exactly what Twitch Unity Guilds are all about!

Launched in 2023, Twitch Unity Guilds are creator communities backed directly by Twitch — with dedicated funding and official branding — designed to give underrepresented voices a protected, empowering home to learn, share, inspire, and grow. Whether you’re a seasoned streamer or just starting out, there’s a place for you here.

Meet the Guilds

We’re proud to be home to four incredible communities:

  • Twitch Black Guild
  • Twitch Latin Guild
  • Twitch Women’s Guild
  • Twitch Pride Guild

When you join a Unity Guild, you’re not just getting a membership — you’re getting a daily connection to people who get it. Each Guild has its own Discord server where members come together every day to:

  • Learn — Discover tips, tools, and resources to level up your stream
  • Get inspired — Hear stories and see success from creators just like you
  • Have real conversations — Build genuine relationships with a community of like-minded peers

Ready to find your people? Your Unity Guild is waiting. Apply now.

How to Apply

Membership Eligibility

Members may apply to join more than one Guild, provided they meet all eligibility requirements for each.

To be eligible for membership, applicants must:

  • Be a Twitch Partner or Affiliate
  • Be in good standing with Twitch within the last 90 days (No TOS/CG Violations)
  • Have been active on Twitch within the last 30 days
  • Complete the Streamer Survey (located on your Dashboard)
  • Identify with the community they are applying to join (Black, Woman, Latin American, or LGBTQIA+)
  • Be at least 18 years of age

If you meet all of the requirements above, you’re ready to apply. Apply here.

Affiliate membership was implemented thanks to your feedback!

Frequently Asked Questions

I applied to the Twitch Unity Guilds but haven’t received a response. When should I expect to hear back?
Thank you for your interest in joining the Twitch Unity Guilds! Due to the high volume of applications we receive, we’re only able to contact applicants who have been selected to join. If you haven’t heard from us within 6 months of submitting your application, you’re welcome to reapply. We appreciate your patience and continued interest in our community.
Why are the Unity Guilds limited to the current selection?
Our current focus is on strengthening and expanding our existing Unity Guilds while providing the best possible support to the creators already within these communities. We recognize the importance of intersectionality and are committed to supporting guild members in creator-led identity programming for communities that do not have a respective guild. As the program continues to grow and evolve, we may explore additional guild categories in the future. However, deepening our commitment to our current guilds and ensuring all members feel supported across their diverse identities remains our priority at this time.
Can I join more than one Twitch Unity Guild?
Absolutely! You’re welcome to join any Unity Guild that aligns with your identity. We celebrate the intersectionality of our creators and encourage you to participate in all the guilds where you feel a sense of belonging and community.
Are there any requirements or expectations for Unity Guild members?
While there are no strict activity requirements, we encourage members to actively participate in guild programming, engage with fellow guild members, and contribute to the supportive community environment we’ve built. Members should uphold Twitch’s Community Guidelines and represent the values of inclusivity and collaboration that Unity Guilds stand for.
Under what circumstances might someone be removed from a Unity Guild?
We’re committed to maintaining protected, inclusive, and supportive spaces for all Unity Guild members. Removal from a guild may occur if a member violates Twitch’s Community Guidelines, engages in behavior that harms other guild members or the broader community, or repeatedly fails to uphold the values of respect and collaboration that Unity Guilds represent. Our goal is always to support our creators while ensuring Unity Guilds remain welcoming spaces for everyone.
Can I apply to the Twitch Unity Guilds if I am suspended on Twitch?
No, creators who are currently suspended on Twitch are not eligible to apply for or maintain membership in Unity Guilds. Unity Guilds are built on the foundation of Twitch’s Community Guidelines and Terms of Service, and all members must be in good standing with the platform. This means maintaining an active account without any active suspensions or violations. If your suspension is temporary, you’re welcome to apply once it has been lifted and your account is fully restored. We encourage all creators to familiarize themselves with Twitch’s Community Guidelines and Terms of Service to ensure they understand the expectations for participation on the platform and within Unity Guilds. Our goal is to maintain protected, inclusive spaces where all members can thrive, and this requires everyone to uphold the standards that make Twitch a welcoming community for creators and viewers alike.
How can I get involved with a Unity Guild?
There are many ways to actively participate and contribute to your Unity Guild community! Members can get involved by joining conversations in the dedicated Discord spaces, attending virtual and in-person events throughout the year, collaborating with fellow guild members on content and streaming projects, participating in guild-led programming and workshops, or even creating your own events that bring the community together. We also encourage experienced creators to serve as mentors or volunteers to support newer members in their growth journey. The more you engage with your guild, the more you’ll benefit from the connections, opportunities, and sense of community that Unity Guilds provide. Your participation helps strengthen the entire guild and creates a more vibrant, supportive space for all members.
How often are applications open? Will applications ever be open to my language/region?

Applications for Twitch Unity Guilds are typically open year-round, with occasional brief closures (usually no longer than a week) for processing and review. Currently, Unity Guilds support the following languages: Japanese (Women’s Guild) and Spanish and Portuguese (Latin Guild).

We’re actively exploring options for expanding Unity Guilds to additional languages and regions as we continue to build protected, inclusive spaces for creators around the world.

Twitch’s Charity Tool for Creators

Twitch’s Charity tool is available to Affiliates and Partners only.

Twitch’s charity tool makes setting up a charity stream easy for Affiliates and Partners, which you can do straight from your Creator Dashboard in just a few easy steps.

Twitch does not take a cut of the donations. All funds raised, excluding payment processing fees, will be donated to the charity according to PayPal Giving Fund’s policies.

Check out our Charity Fundraising page on our Creator Camp for more helpful information on doing charity streams.

If you are a viewer, please check out our Twitch’s charity tool for Viewers. If you are a charity, please check out our Twitch’s charity tool for Charities.

Choose Your Charity

Start by going to your Creator Dashboard and selecting the Charity option from the left menu.

Under the Discovery tab, you’ll be able to search for and select which charity you want to support from tens of thousands of options around the world. Once you find the charity, click the Create Fundraiser button on the charity’s card.

Using the category and country filters while leaving the search field empty will return charities that match your filter criteria.

To appear in the charity tool, charities must be enrolled with the PayPal Giving Fund. Learn more.

Create Campaign

Once you select a charity and click Create Fundraiser, you’ll be taken to a campaign creation page. Here you can see details about the charity being fundraised for.

You have the option to set a goal for your fundraiser. Select the Edit icon next to the goal. Select the amount you want to set as your community’s goal. Your goal can be increased at any time before or during the campaign, but it cannot be decreased.

When setting your goal, remember that every amount raised counts! So try to set a realistic goal for your community to reach. If your goal is achieved during the charity stream, consider increasing it to keep the support going!

Starting Your Fundraiser

Affiliates and Partners can start their fundraiser by clicking on the Start Fundraiser button in the Charity section of your Creator Dashboard under the My Fundraisers tab. Only one campaign can be active at a time. You’ll receive a confirmation at the top of this page when your fundraiser has been activated.

Activity Feed

You’ll be able to filter on and see the donations in your activity feed. Check the option to display Charity Donations.

Once selected, donations will show up in your Activity Feed for you to be able to see who and how much they donated.

This helps you not miss a donation if you are wanting to acknowledge donations made.

About Charity Goals

When you create your campaign, a goal and progress bar automatically appears at the top of chat. Unlike Community Goals, you cannot edit these goals without ending your charity campaign.

Managing Campaigns

When you click Save Fundraiser, it will appear as a draft campaign in your campaign management page. This page enables you to manage active, inactive, and draft campaigns. You can see the status of each campaign, the charity name, the date it was activated, the fundraising goal set, and the total amount raised.

About Charity on Mobile

Viewers watching your stream from the Twitch Mobile App won’t see the option to donate to charity, or progress towards your fundraising goal. Viewers can access the donation flow on mobile by using this link

[twitch.tv](https://www.twitch.tv/charity/CHANNELNAME)

It does require you to sign-in to Twitch.

We’re still working on bringing the charity tool to the mobile app. Streamers should feel free to distribute the Twitch charity tool donation link above to viewers who may be on mobile.

We share the name of your Twitch channel to PayPal Giving Fund with each donation sent so charities can see you’ve raised funds with them. No other personal information is shared.

Starting Your Fundraiser

To begin your fundraiser, click the Start Fundraiser button in the Charity section of your Creator Dashboard under the My Fundraiser tab. Only one campaign can be active at a time. You’ll receive a confirmation at the top of this page when your fundraiser has been activated.

Pausing Your Fundraiser

Once a fundraiser is started, you can pause it. To do so, choose Stop from the My Fundraisers tab. When you are ready to start the fundraiser again, click Restart.

Deleting or Ending Your Fundraiser

To end your fundraiser, click the 3 dot menu at the end of each campaign row. Select Delete.

Deleting a campaign simply removes it from your list of fundraisers. Deleting a campaign when funds have been raised has no impact on the status of funds given; the charity will still receive the donation through the PayPal Giving Fund.

View Donations

If you want to view who has donated and how much to your fundraiser, you can do so by clicking the View Donations button within the three dots at the end of each campaign row.

A list of the donor, how much was donated, and when will be displayed.

What is the Founders Badge?

Content in this article is relevant to all monetized streamers.

The Founders Badge is a subscriber badge available exclusively to the first 10 Prime or paid subscribers of non-Partner monetized channels, and first 25 Prime or paid subscribers of Partner channels.

Here’s what it looks like:

On this page:

  • Streamer FAQ
  • Subscriber FAQ

Streamer FAQ

Can I see a list of my Founders?

Yes! Visit Subscriptions Analytics within your Revenue Analytics. Then, on your subscriptions panel, click View Details for information about your channel’s Founders, including their username, whether or not they are currently subscribed, and the date they earned their Founder’s Badge. Suspended or disabled user accounts will not appear in this panel. Partners may download a list of their Subs at this link and review their first 25 supporters.

This feature was implemented thanks to your feedback!

Why don’t I see the Founders Badge info panel in my Creator Dashboard?
The Founders Badge info panel will only appear if Founders Badges are entitled.
Which channels are eligible for the Founders Badge?
All monetized channels are eligible for Founders Badges. Non-Partner monetized channels have 10 available Founders Badges. Partners have 25 Founders Badges.
Do I have to make any change to enable a Founders Badge?
No. Founders Badges are enabled by default. Creators will not need to make any changes to their settings to unlock this badge for their eligible subscribers. Newly monetized streamers will see Founders Badges distributed in chat as viewers subscribe.
Do my Founders change if I offboard, and then re-onboard monetization programs?
No, your Founders do not change.
Can I upload a custom Founders Badge?
No. We currently do not support a customized Founders Badge. If you’d like to support this idea, make your voice heard in UserVoice.
Can I disable the Founders Badge for my channel, or for certain users?

You cannot turn off the Founders Badge feature for your channel. Viewers choose whether to display their Founders Badge or their subscriber loyalty badge.

However, you can revoke the Founders Badge from individual viewers in your Manage Founders section. This action is not reversible — if you revoke a Founder’s badge, that slot becomes available and will be assigned to the next eligible subscriber.

Does my channel get additional Founders Badge slots if I go from a monetized streamer to an Affiliate? What about if I go from an Affiliate to joining the Partner program?
Any streamer can unlock Founders Badges, regardless of Affiliate or Partner status, so long as they complete onboarding and sign the Monetized Streamer Agreement (“MSA”). When that monetized streamer joins the Affiliate program, no additional Founders Badge slots are earned. However, if an Affiliate joins the Partner program, yes, additional Founders Badge slots are unlocked! We’ll automatically notify any paid or Prime subscribers that were numbers 11 through 25.

Subscriber FAQ

How can I see if a channel has Founders Badge left to earn?
If a channel has Founders Badges to earn, you will see the badge as a benefit when you visit the Support Panel.

If you receive a gifted sub and continue that gifted sub with sub tokens, you will not be eligible to receive the Founders Badge.

Which Subscribers are eligible for the Founders Badge?
The first 10 Prime or paid subscribers of non-Partner monetized channels and first 25 Prime or paid subscribers of Partner channels will be eligible for Founders Badge. Founders Badge will display in chat only if you are a current subscriber to the channel. All subscription tiers are eligible for Founders Badge.
What is a Prime or paid subscription, exactly?
Prime members receive a free twitch.tv subscription, among other benefits, which they may apply towards a channel for 1 month of free subscription. A paid subscription is any non-gifted Tier or length of subscription you purchased on Twitch, no matter desktop or mobile.
Can I replace my Founders Badge with a Subscriber Loyalty Badge (e.g. badges that show my Subscription tenure)?
Yes. By default, we will select Founders Badge (if you have unlocked it) as your default Subscription Badge. You can decide to hide Founders Badge and show another loyalty badge by using the settings at this page.

This is a site wide setting, so if you hide Founders Badge then it will be hidden from all your qualifying channels. You cannot selectively hide Founders Badge for a specific channel.

I think I should have earned a Founders Badge, but I don’t have one.
Sorry to hear that! To earn a Founders Badge, you must be one of the first 10 subscribers to a non-Partner monetized channels, or one of the first 25 for a Partner. Make sure you haven’t swapped out your Founders Badge by accident. Feel free to contact us if you require further assistance.
Will I ever lose my Founders Badge status?
Streamers have the ability to revoke the Founders Badge from individual users. As long as the streamer has not revoked your Founders Badge, it’s yours once you’ve earned it (as long as your subscription and account are active).

If you do not renew your subscription and the streamer has not revoked your Founders Badge, the badge is still yours, but it’s not visible until you resubscribe. Click the “Chat Identity” button next to your username in chat to see if you have an eligible Founders Badge in a channel.

Your Founders Badge will be visible again once you subscribe.

I purchased a gift subscription for a user. Will that qualify me for a Founders Badge?
No. Users that gift subscriptions in the channel will not be eligible for Founders Badge. You need to subscribe to the channel and meet the eligibility criteria as mentioned above.

When Am I Getting Paid?

Partners and Affiliates are paid on or around the 15th of each month if:

  • Their account balance since the last day of the month they were last paid is over $50 for most payout methods and $100 with wire transfer (Not sure?)
  • There is no issue with their payout method or account information. (Not sure?)
  • Their payout status is Eligible. (Not sure?)
  • They have opted to receive revenue from support events as payout. (Not sure?)

Revenue earned within the current calendar month is not eligible for payout until the following month. For example, if you earn revenue on May 3rd, that amount is only eligible for payout beginning June 15th — if you meet the payout threshold.

Early each month, Partners and Affiliates receive updates regarding their due balance. Updates are sent to the email address you provided during onboarding to the Affiliate or Partner programs.

View your Payout History Dashboard for a detailed breakdown on your balance estimate. You can also review past completed, submitted or rejected payouts. Payout typically takes 3-5 business days from submission date. Payout processing time can vary. Weekends and public holidays can increase the time for you to receive a payout.

In case of rejected payout, follow the instructions in your payment rejection email. Learn More.

On this page:

  • Minimum Payout Balance
  • Payout Timing
  • Future Payouts
  • Frequently Asked Question

Minimum Payout Balance

A minimum of $50 USD is required to receive a payout. Only Affiliates and Partners can receive a payout when they exceed this threshold. This threshold applies to ACH/direct deposit, eCheck/local bank, PayPal, and check payout methods. Due to transfer fees, the processing of wire transfer payouts requires a $100 minimum balance.

Learn more about changing your payout method.

Twitch Affiliates and Partners: You’ll receive your payment on or around the 15th of each month if your status is payable, your balance exceeds $50 (most payout methods) or $100 (wire transfer), and you have opted to receive revenue from supports events as payout.

Verify that a payout is submitted to you around the 15th of each month by visiting your Payout History. Here, you may review information on submitted and processing payouts, as well as a detailed breakdown of taxes and fees.

We automatically roll your balance to the next month if you do not make over $50, or $100. We do this until the payout threshold is met. Learn more about your payout balance.

Payout Timing

Payout processing time typically takes around 10 business days from the Submitted or Paid date in your Payout History or payout email. Processing time can vary, as all banks and payout processors take different amount of times to process payments sent by Twitch.

Payout Method

Timing From Submitted Date*

ACH

3-5 Days

eCheck/Local Bank

1-4 Days

PayPal

1-2 Days

Check

1-2 Weeks

Wire Transfer

1-3 Days

Weekends and public holidays can increase the amount of time that it takes for you to receive your payout. Make changes to your payout method here.

*It is not necessary to contact Twitch Support to report an issue with a submitted payout until after this period.

Learn More about making changes to your payout method.

Future Payouts

You may be wondering when to expect your next payout.

You receive a payout once a month if your balance from your last payment exceeds the $50 or $100 threshold. If you don’t exceed the balance in a given month, we roll your balance over to the next month.

The date of the most recent payment means that you were paid out for earning over $50 or $100 before the 30th of the prior month. So, for example, if you were paid on Dec 13th, you were paid your accrued revenue after exceeding the $50 or $100 threshold through to Nov 30th.

If you were last paid on Dec 13th, you would need to begin from December 1 to the present day to see your balance for future payouts.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I see my previous payments?
Track your Payout History here.
I got an email that a payout was sent, but I haven’t received it yet.
As a first step, please check your payout history. Sometimes, a payment processor (PayPal) may notify you a payment has been sent. In reality, this notice means the processing process has begun, rather than completed.
A member of my community contributed more than what they can afford. Is there anything I can do to help?
Unfortunately, once a purchase is completed it can’t be refunded. In limited cases, customers may refer to our refund guidelines. Visit the Twitch Cares guide on suspected gambling addictions.
Someone gifted a lot of subs to my channel! When will I receive this income?
If you received this support on or before the last day of the month, the value will contribute towards your accrued balance for that month. So, if you receive a $250 sub gift on April 23rd (or any day in April), you should be paid for this plus your accrued balance in the middle of the following month.

If you receive this contribution, you may not see it reflected on your account until the next day. The Channel Analytics dashboard updates once a day. Your Estimated Pay in your Payout History Dashboard updates once a month.

What do I do if I need to make a change to my payout method?
To change your payout method, visit the Onboarding section of your Creator Dashboard. Learn more.
How do I ensure that I am still paid if I need to change my payout details?
In general, make sure that you submit your new details before the 10th of any given month. Payments begin processing before the 15th of each month. It can take some time for systems to update with your new information. Learn more.
How do I receive balance earned before I become an Affiliate or Partner?
Only Twitch Partners or Affiliates can receive a payout. If you do not qualify for these programs, and have completed onboarding, you may be able to use spendable balance on Twitch. Learn more.

2025 Twitch Recap

Your annual Twitch Recap is a personalized, retrospective look at time well spent this past year. It’s a moment to reflect, celebrate, and recognize you and the Twitch community. Twitch Recap highlights the top activities of everyone on Twitch: from streamers and moderators to viewers and even quiet lurkers. Check out the special ways you participated on Twitch this past year.

Click here to go to your 2025 Twitch Recap.

What’s in my Twitch Recap?

There are three types of Recaps: Viewer, Streamer, and Community. Depending on your activity on Twitch, you may qualify for one, two, or all three Recaps. If you receive all three, you will see these icons within the feature to navigate between them:

The Viewer Recap includes stats about your viewing activity, such as hours watched, days you visited Twitch, chats sent, and more. This personalized Recap is generated for any user who watched at least 10 hours of Twitch during the eligible window of activity.

The Streamer Recap includes stats about your channel, such as total hours watched, total number of streams, your highest concurrent viewer count, and more. Regardless of Partner or Affiliate status, this personalized Recap is generated for anyone who broadcasted at least 10 hours on Twitch during the eligible window of activity.

The Community Recap captures information about the collective Twitch community, celebrating the top moments and achievements of all users. Anyone can access the Community Recap, regardless of their watching or streaming activity.
