Sharing your #TwitchRecap

At the bottom of your personal recap, download a shareable graphic to show off your year on Twitch. Use #TwitchRecap to join the conversation and connect with others.

Leave us your feedback in UserVoice as we strive to improve this experience every year.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why do I not see a Viewer Recap?
Personalized Viewer Recaps are only available to those who watched at least 10 hours of live content on Twitch during the eligible window of activity. This minimum number of hours watched can be spread across any number of channels, and does not need to come from a single stream.
Why do I not see a Streamer Recap?
Personalized Streamer Recaps are only available to those who streamed at least 10 hours on Twitch during the eligible window of activity.
What is the eligible window of activity for the Recap?
Community, Viewer, and Streamer Recaps’ eligible window of activity occurred between October 31, 2024 and October 31, 2025.
Does the Streamer Recap include information on my Twitch streams regardless of device?
Yes, it aggregates data from all your streams, no matter the source (i.e. video game console, desktop computer, mobile device, etc).
Is there a Recap for Moderators?
Though we do not have a moderator-specific Recap, moderators should see a special section within their Viewer Recap that recognizes their contributions.
Is there a Recap for Editors?
We do not have an editor-specific Recap, and we did not include any editor-related data in the Viewer Recap. If this is something that you would be interested in seeing for future Recaps, please let us know in UserVoice.
Who can see my Recaps?
Only you have direct access to your individual Recaps. However, you are able to share an image capturing many of your achievements throughout the year – simply scroll to the bottom of your Viewer or Streamer Recaps and click the “Share” button.
Some users qualified for a special Recap Chat Badge. What were the requirements for this?
Only the top 20% of Twitch users during the eligible window of activity qualified for this unique chat badge. If you didn’t get it this time, be sure to stream, watch, chat, or engage on Twitch regularly next year.
Why am I missing data, or does my data seem inaccurate?
Only activity that occurred during the eligible window of time was reflected in the Twitch Recap. In addition, activity by users that you have blocked, that are banned from your chat, or that are indefinitely suspended from Twitch will not be reflected in your Recap(s) and vice-versa.
My Recap says that I’m in the top 10% of a category, but I think I should be higher than that. How can I get this corrected?
For this year’s Recap, we only indicate if you are in the top 10%. If more granular thresholds are something that you would be interested in seeing for future Recaps, please let us know in UserVoice.

About Auto Clips Alpha Testing

Alpha testing features described in this article will be available to channels selected by Twitch who are streaming English-language content with VODs and clips enabled. Interested streamers can join the Auto Clips Alpha waitlist from their Clips Settings.

Auto Clips is a new tool that streamers can use to help them automatically create and publish clips of the most engaging moments from their streams, helping them save time on clip creation and editing. These clips are designed to both help your current community catch up on streams they have missed, as well as help new viewers discover great content. Twitch has now opened the waitlist to join the Alpha testing of some features of Auto Clips.

Alpha Testing Availability

You can join the waitlist for Alpha testing of Auto Clips from your Clips Settings in the Stream Settings page of your Creator Dashboard today. The Alpha testing is invite-only. If you are accepted into the Alpha, Auto Clips will be enabled for your channel, and the tool will auto-create and auto-publish clips to your channel for you. You can delete any Auto Clips and turn the feature off or on at any time. The Alpha testing of Auto Clips will only be available to channels who:

  • have set their Twitch language to English
  • AND have the following stream settings enabled:
    • Store past broadcasts = ON
    • Always Publish VODs = ON
    • Enable Clips = ON
    • Auto Clips = ON

We’re actively adding additional features to Auto Clips during the Alpha, and will be expanding availability on an ongoing basis. We will notify you via email when you have been accepted into the Alpha.

Streamer Experience in Alpha

Creating an Auto Clip

You can create Auto Clips in two ways once you have enabled the feature:

  • You can say “Twitch, Clip That” or “Twitch, Clip It” during a stream to create an Auto Clip of the preceding 60 seconds.
  • Auto Clips will also help you find the most engaging moments from your stream, and auto-create and auto-publish clips with titles and captions to your channel page.

Your Auto Clips are generally viewable within 30 minutes after your stream ends.

Auto Clip Captions, Titles, & Formatting

Auto Clips helps you automatically include captions of what is being said in the clip. Captions are enabled by default for Auto Clips. You can add or remove captions on Auto Clips within 30 days of creation, just as you can for Community Clips. You can disable default captions for future Auto Clips through Creator Dashboard > Settings > Stream > Clip Settings. Auto Clips are also automatically titled using direct quotes from your stream and formatted to optimize video viewing for vertical formats. We also offer tools for you to edit and optimize your Auto Clips by adjusting the vertical cropping and customizing the titles of your clips.

Auto Clips created before July 14, 2026 have captions permanently embedded in the video and cannot be removed.

Auto Clip Notifications

Your Auto Clips are available within 30 minutes of your stream ending and you will receive both a push notification and on-site notification when your new Auto Clips have been created and published to your channel. Please ensure that you are opted into receiving notifications from “Clips of Your Channel” in the “On Twitch” and “On Mobile” setting options.

Your Clips, Your Content

You and your editors can delete your Auto Clips just like you can with other clips. During the Alpha, you can edit the clip title and portrait clip layout. Additional editing features will be available in the future. Auto Clips are your User Content under Twitch’s Terms of Service. As a reminder, you are responsible for your channel content and for complying with Twitch’s Community Guidelines and Terms of Service, including when you create clips of your content using Auto Clips.

Exporting & Downloading Auto Clips

Auto Clips can be exported and downloaded, as with your other clips. This helps you surface your most engaging content to both existing viewers and new audiences on other platforms.

Viewing Auto Clips

Your Auto Clips will appear alongside other clips on Twitch. Viewers can watch them just like any of your other clips, and under a clip’s title they will see “Auto Clip by [Streamer’s Username]” to indicate when they are viewing a clip you created using Auto Clips.

Providing Feedback on Auto Clips

You can review Auto Clips both in your Stream Summary and in your Clips Manager, where you can provide feedback on the Auto Clips or delete them. We encourage you to let us know what you think of your Auto Clips so that we can continue to improve their quality based on your feedback.

What’s Next?

During the Alpha, we’ll gather feedback from streamers to continue to improve the Auto Clips functionality and prepare for a full release. We are adding additional features for our next release, including a review flow that will allow streamers to review clips prior to publishing them. Stay tuned for updates.

Frequently Asked Questions

How does Auto Clips help you pick moments to clip?
Auto Clips runs speech-to-text on your stream and analyzes the results with the help of AI to enable you to identify and clip the most engaging moments. Examples of engaging moments include:
  • Positive sentiment and excitement from the streamer
  • Funny gameplay moments or banter
  • Entertaining interactions

Auto Clips also detects when you say “Twitch, Clip That” or “Twitch, Clip It” during your stream and makes clips of those moments.

How does Auto Clips use AI?
Auto Clips uses AI to analyze your stream content to help you create clips as described above. The AI makes quick assessments of your content and chat activity for purposes of helping you create engaging clips. The AI used for Auto Clips does not retain these assessments, or information about you or your content, and it is not trained on your content or information. You have control over your Auto Clips, just like with other clips, and can delete specific Auto Clips at any time in your Creator Dashboard or turn off the capability altogether.
Which channels are eligible for the Auto Clips Alpha testing?
The Alpha testing of Auto Clips will only be available to Twitch-selected channels who have set their Twitch language to English, who have enabled VODs and clips, and who have made their VODs public and visible to non-subscribers (you can manage whether your VODs are visible only to subscribers here). Auto Clips will not be available for channels where clips and VODs are not available. Streams in the “DJs” category are also not eligible for Auto Clips under the terms of the DJ Program.
How will I know that I’ve been accepted into the Auto Clips Alpha testing?
When you have been accepted into the Alpha testing, you will receive an email notification letting you know. Auto Clips will be enabled for your channel, and you can manage your settings on your Stream Settings page.
What should I keep in mind while using Auto Clips?
Auto Clips works best with clear stream audio. The quality of your Auto Clips may vary during streams that have heavy background noise or multiple people speaking at once. You can help Auto Clips identify more interesting moments by audibly reacting and narrating in real time. Explaining your thought process and providing consistent commentary not only helps you capture the best moments with Auto Clips, but also keeps your stream entertaining and welcoming to viewers.

About Display Names

Your display name is a change in capitalization from your username. Your display name capitalization appears most everywhere on Twitch. Unlike usernames, display names can be changed at any time.

Learn more about changing your username.

Changing Your Display Name

To change your display name:

  • Visit your Profile Settings
  • Enter the custom capitalization for your username
  • Save Changes

Localized Display Names

Those using Twitch with their website language set to Arabic, Chinese (Simplified), Chinese (Traditional), Korean, and Japanese can add a localized display name with characters from their respective languages ahead of their usernames.

Adding A Localized Display Name

To add a localized display name:

  • Change your website language Arabic, Chinese (Traditional), Chinese (Simplified), Korean, or Japanese.
  • Navigate to your Profile Settings.
  • Enter your desired localized username.
  • Save Changes

Learn more about Languages on Twitch.

This is not a name change, and affects display names only. Localized display names appear ahead of your username. Localized display names must be unique, meaning no two users can share the same localized name. Localized display names cannot mix English characters or symbols.

Removing A Localized Display Name

To remove a localized display name, change your website language to English. Then, change your display name to be the same as your username.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do localized names interact with the timing of username changes?
Display name changes can be made without cooldown. Localized display name changes can be made once every 60 days. Username changes can be made once every 60 days.
Is there a recycle period with localized display names, like there is with username changes?
No. Once you change away from a localized display name, anyone can claim that localized display name.
Can I search for localized display names?
Use search results to search for localized display names, rather than search suggestions.

Clicking search suggestion for “Go to ‘紫夜リュウジ’” when searching for a localized display name like “紫夜リュウジ” will result in an error.

To resolve this issue, use search results rather than search suggestions to find what you are looking for.

For more questions on search, learn more in our guide.

About Moderation Analytics

This feature is available to all streamers and their moderators.

The Moderation Analytics page (located in your Creator Dashboard), provides post-stream moderation analytics that give a comprehensive overview of all moderation actions taken during a stream. Using this overview, streamers and moderators can easily follow up on moderation decisions, allowing them to continue keeping their communities safe.

What’s in Moderation Analytics?

Moderation analytics provide insights into the moderation activity that occurred during a stream. Moderation analytics are available soon after a stream ends and you can browse recent moderation analytics from the last 30 streams. Moderation analytics contains the following information:

Moderated Viewers

Review a list of users who experienced a moderator action, such as being warned, timed out, banned, or had their message deleted. From here, you can easily batch report groups of problem users.

Moderated Actions

Review your total moderators active during the stream and the actions they took, including: messages deleted, users warned, users timed out, and users banned. This section only reports mod actions related to safety features.

Settings Change Log

Records of the chat mode changes made by either you or your moderators during the stream, with the option to revert the change to what they were at the beginning of the stream.

Also includes changes and additions to your list of blocked and permitted terms.

How Streamers and Moderators Access Moderation Analytics

For Streamers

Streamers can access Moderation Analytics from several locations on both Desktop and the Twitch mobile app:

  • Moderation Analytics page in the Creator Dashboard (Desktop): In the left-hand sidebar, navigate to Moderation, then Analytics.

  • Stream Summary Creator Dashboard page (Mobile and Desktop): Follow the Moderation Analytics link alongside your stream analytics.

  • Stream Summary email (Mobile and Desktop): Click the direct link included in your post-stream email

  • Mod Actions Widget in Stream manager or Mod View (Desktop): Interact with the Mod Actions widget soon after the stream ends to see a moderation summary of the latest stream. To see Analytics from earlier dates, navigate to the Analytics section of your Moderation settings.

For Moderators

Moderators can access the summary through the Mod Actions widget inside Mod View. An interactable banner appears soon after the stream goes offline with a direct link to that stream’s summary.

Moderation Analytics includes several key data points to help understand what happened during the stream. Moderators see a limited view of the data. Only the channel’s streamer can see specific action counts or detailed statistics.

Taking Action: For Streamers and Moderators

Moderation Analytics provides a useful snapshot of what happened during a particular stream, helping streamers and moderators to take more effective action.

Actions for Streamers From Moderation Analytics

  • Report Users: Easily report users in bulk who were banned during the stream.

  • Review User Profiles: Open viewer cards for users who had moderation actions taken against them.

  • Update Chat Settings: Depending on the needs of your channel, you can modify verification requirements for newcomers to speak in your channel, chat modes, and other restrictions.

Actions for Moderators From Moderation Analytics
  • Report Users: Report users in bulk who were banned during the stream.
  • Review User Profiles: Open viewer cards for users who had moderation actions taken against them.
  • Update Chat Settings: Depending on what direction the streamer provides their moderation team, you can modify some channel or chat modes, or other restrictions.

Frequently Asked Questions

How far back can I see Moderation Analytics?
You can review moderation analytics for your last 30 streams.
Can my moderators see the same information I can?
Moderators can access moderation Analytics, but they see a more limited view of the data. Only the channel’s streamer can see specific moderator action counts or other detailed statistics.
I don’t have any moderators, will I still have moderation analytics?
Yes, you will still receive moderation analytics. They will show AutoMod activity, chat restrictions, and any actions you took on the stream yourself.

Visit our Safety Center to learn more about how to build a great moderation team.

Why don’t I see a Moderation Summary for my stream?
The summary is generated after your stream ends. If you’re still live, wait until you’ve ended your stream. If you still don’t see it, make sure you have the necessary permissions and that moderation actions occurred during your stream.
What if I disagree with an action my moderator took?
Moderation analytics show you all actions taken during your stream. You can review each action, open user profiles to get more context, and reverse decisions if needed. You may wish to take this opportunity to discuss moderation guidelines with your team.

About Monetization on Twitch

Twitch provides access to features to help build your community. Additional tools, including access to monetization features, are available to streamers who qualify for, and onboard to, our additional programs.

Streamer Types and Features

Access to Twitch community-building and monetization tools can be grouped into these four categories:

  • All Streamers – Anyone with a Twitch account can start building community by going live. Some community tools require that you verify your phone number or email address. No monetization tools are available.
  • All Streamers (Monetization Setup Complete) – All streamers can gain access to most monetization tools once a streamer agrees to our Monetized Streamer Agreement (MSA) and completes onboarding. Further requirements must be met to qualify for a payout, however streamers can choose to use their Spendable Balance towards specific purchases on Twitch.
  • Twitch Affiliate – By meeting further requirements, streamers may be invited to join the Affiliate program. The Affiliate program unlocks access to additional tools and features to level up your community. Affiliates can choose to receive their earned Net Revenue as payout or use it to make eligible purchases on Twitch via their Spendable Balance.
  • Twitch Partner – Once they meet further requirements, Twitch Affiliates may be eligible to apply to the Partner program. Entry is not guaranteed. The Partner program unlocks our highest level of features, tools, and support. Like Affiliates, Partners can choose to receive their earned Net Revenue as payout or use it to make eligible purchases on Twitch via their Spendable Balance.

No matter the type of creator you are on Twitch, you must follow our Community Guidelines.

Tip: To see which features you can access, visit your Creator Dashboard.

You may have monetization features enabled on a maximum of 5 accounts. If you exceed this limit, monetization features will be removed from your accounts with the least activity. You can still stream on all accounts, but only 5 can access monetization tools at any time.

How to Complete Creator Onboarding

The following instructions are for non-Affiliate, non-Partner, non-Developer Twitch users trying to complete onboarding for the first time. If you recently qualified for Twitch Affiliate or Partner, visit our Affiliate onboarding and Partner onboarding guides instead.

Twitch Developers: Extension monetization has a separate onboarding process. If you are a developer looking to monetize an Extension, visit dev.twitch.tv for details. See our developer onboarding FAQ below for more information about eligibility.

To begin, select your profile icon in the top corner and choose Creator Dashboard. Then navigate to Monetization → Setup. Or, click here.

Step 1 – Set Up Tools

This step gives you access to streamer tools such as Channel Points, subs, Bits, emotes, and badges.

Complete the following fields:

  • Legal Full Name — Enter your first, middle (optional), and last name exactly as it appears on your tax documents. Do not alter your legal name to match the form.
  • Email — Pre-selected from your account. You can edit this if needed.
  • Business Name (optional) — For business tax reporting only. Match your business name to tax filings and payout method.
  • Country of Residence — Select your country.
  • Monetized Streamer Agreement — Click View Agreement to open and read the Monetized Streamer Agreement. You must view the agreement before you can accept it.

If you are over the age of 13 but under the age of 18, this section will ask your parent or legal guardian to agree to the Monetized Streamer Agreement for you. Your parent or legal guardian must type their full legal name, check the box, and click Agree.

Once all fields are complete, click Submit.

Step 2 – Set Up Spendable Balance (Optional)

After completing Step 1, you’ll see Step 2: Set Up Spendable Balance. This step allows you to spend your earned balance from creator activity on eligible Twitch purchases.

Click Set Up to expand the enrollment fields:

  • Royalty Tax Interview — Click Start. You’ll be redirected to Amazon Tax Central to complete your tax information interview. Click Authorize to connect your Twitch account. For detailed guidance on completing the tax interview, see our Affiliate Onboarding Guide.
  • Service Tax Interview — If you just completed the Royalty Tax Interview and it was accepted, the Service Tax Interview may not require additional information.
  • Spendable Balance — Click Enroll to opt in. Enrollment is optional and reversible. Learn more: About Spendable Balance.

After completing the tax interview, you’ll see a validation screen confirming your tax information has been received and showing your applicable withholding rate.

Enrolling in Spendable Balance is optional. Your creator tools (Bits, subs, emotes, badges, and Channel Points) are available as soon as Step 1 is complete — you do not need to enroll in Spendable Balance to start using them. However, to use that support towards other purchases on Twitch, you must complete enrollment into Spendable Balance.

After Onboarding

Once you’ve completed Step 1, your Creator Dashboard will update with new tabs under Monetization: Ads, Bits & Cheering, Community, and Subscriptions.

You can also explore your Analytics → Earnings page to track support received on your channel. The Payouts page will become relevant once you reach Affiliate status and meet the minimum payout threshold.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why did you expand access to specific community-building and monetization tools?
As we shared in our 2025 open letter, we want you to be able to take advantage of our monetization tools, whether you’re just getting your community started or have been on Twitch for a while. By expanding access to monetization tools, onboarded streamers will be able to grow their communities and receive direct patronage, regardless of their status.
Who is eligible to access monetization tools?
Monetization tools are available to streamers globally. If you’re unable to access monetization onboarding in your region, please contact Twitch Support.
How do you determine which of my accounts to de-monetize if I attempt to monetize more than 5 accounts?
You may have monetization features enabled on a maximum of 5 accounts. If you exceed this limit, monetization features will be removed from your accounts with the least activity.

For the purpose of this check, we primarily define least activity in terms of subscriptions and followers. We prioritize subscriptions: most to least active, followers: most to least active, then finally the most recently created account.

Partner accounts do not count towards the maximum of 5 monetized accounts.

Once I complete onboarding, will I automatically be eligible for a payout?
Non-Affiliate, non-Partner streamers are not eligible for payouts, regardless of whether they have reached the $50 payout threshold. Non-Affiliate, non-Partner streamers who have successfully completed onboarding to access monetization tools may use the balance reflected on their Creator Dashboard via their Spendable Balance to make eligible purchases on Twitch.
What is Spendable Balance, and how can I use it?
With Spendable Balance, you can use the balance reflected on your Creator Dashboard from your Bits and subs. Spendable Balance allows you to purchase gift subs, recurring subscriptions, Bits, and Turbo to support your community and the creators you love.

If you prefer, you can also grow your balance and get paid out automatically once you reach Affiliate status and hit your minimum payout threshold.

You can enroll via your Creator Dashboard > Monetization. Learn more.

What happens to my Spendable Balance once I’ve reached Affiliate status?
Once you become an Affiliate and have met the payout threshold, you may elect to be paid out or to use your balance via your Spendable Balance.
I’m having trouble with my zip code during monetization onboarding. What should I do?
If you’re experiencing issues with your zip code during the onboarding process, try these solutions:
  • Check your zip code format: Ensure you’re entering your zip code in the correct format for your country (e.g., 5 digits for US, postal codes for other regions).
If you continue to experience issues after trying these steps, please contact Twitch Support for additional assistance.
What happens if I complete onboarding and then become eligible for Affiliate at a later date?
Once eligible for Affiliate, you will receive an invitation email to notify you of your new status. Upon receiving this email, the only steps required for you to become an Affiliate or Partner is to:
  • Complete your Tax Interview: We require you to complete two tax interviews, one for royalty tax and one for service tax. The two forms are similar, but are used for different purposes. Both must be filled out accurately. Please refer to the Amazon Tax Information Interview Guide if you need help understanding any individual field.
  • Enter your Payout Method: Select the payout method you prefer to receive your earnings at.
  • Turn on Two-Factor Authentication (2FA): To turn on 2FA, head to your dashboard and select Achievements under the Analytics tab. From there, select “Turn on 2FA”. Learn how to turn on 2FA here.

Even if you haven’t yet met all the requirements for becoming an Affiliate, we still recommend you turn on 2FA so that you can automatically become Affiliate once eligible and to provide an extra layer of security to protect your account.

I completed creator monetization onboarding, but I can’t set up Extension monetization. Why?
Twitch developers build interactive experiences that integrate directly into Twitch channels. Developers can monetize their Extensions through Bits in Extensions, which has its own onboarding process separate from the creator monetization onboarding described on this page.

If you have already completed creator monetization onboarding (signed the Monetized Streamer Agreement and completed tax and payout setup) but have not yet reached Affiliate or Partner status, your account is not currently eligible for Extension monetization onboarding. This is because the two onboarding processes set up your account’s payout settings differently, and they cannot both be active at the same time.

What you can do:

  • Reach Affiliate or Partner status on the account. Once you qualify, Extension monetization onboarding is available. Learn more about Affiliate and Partner requirements.
  • Use a different account to complete Extension monetization onboarding, that has not yet completed creator monetization onboarding. Set up extension monetization on that account through dev.twitch.tv.
  • Contact Twitch Support if you need further assistance.
How do I remove monetization from my channel?
If you have completed creator monetization onboarding but want to remove monetization features from your channel, contact Twitch Support.
What do I do if I can’t enroll in Spendable Balance?
If you’ve completed onboarding but are unable to enroll in Spendable Balance, check the following:
  • Ensure your tax interview is complete and accepted.
  • Ensure your onboarding information is accurate and up to date.
  • If you have multiple Twitch accounts with the same tax information, this may cause a conflict.

If you’ve verified the above and still cannot enroll, contact Twitch Support for assistance.

Enrolling in Spendable Balance is optional. You can still use creator tools (Bits, subs, emotes, badges, and Channel Points) without enrolling. Spendable Balance allows you to spend your earned revenue on Twitch — it is not required to access monetization features.

About Personalized Channel Notifications

To help ensure Twitch channel notifications are relevant to you, we provide all followers four customization options to choose from for each channel they follow: Always, Personalized, Go Live Only, and Off. This experience is designed to help you stay connected to your favorite channels and communities, while having more control over what other notifications you receive.

Starting December 2025, notification settings for all channels you currently follow will be migrated to Personalized Notifications. If you have notifications enabled for the channels you follow, you will receive Personalized Notifications. If you have disabled these notifications, those settings will be respected and remain turned off. This does not impact any of your other notification settings. You can customize this setting at any time.

What are Personalized Notifications?

When you follow a new channel, the default experience for those channel notifications is Personalized.

With Personalized notifications, Twitch curates your channel notifications based on factors including your viewing preferences, how recently you’ve already received notifications, and your local time of day. The types of notifications that can be personalized include:

  • Go-Live Only: also known as live-ups, a notification sent when the streamer goes live
  • Catch Up: notifications about popular VODs, clips, and Stories from streamers you follow.
  • Updates for subscribers: When there are updates about channels you are subscribed to.

Transactional notifications, such as purchase confirmations and account related notifications will be sent separately and are not controlled by this setting.

This change allows Personalized notifications on a channel-by-channel level. Even with Personalized Notifications selected, you will still receive all account and transactional notifications.

Not receiving notifications you expect? See Where are my notifications? for troubleshooting steps.

Configuring notification preferences

You can update your preferences on the Notifications tab of your account settings. To configure individual channel notification preferences, scroll down to the section Manage Channel Notifications. You can also change these preferences on the streamer’s Channel pag, or your Followed Channels page. On the Channel page, there is a notification bell you can select to change the setting.

You can update their notifications experience on a channel by selecting one of the following options:

  • Personalized: receive select notifications for the channel, optimized based on your viewing preferences
  • Always: receive all notifications for the channel
  • Go Live Only: receive only notifications that inform you when a streamer has started a livestream
  • Off: disable notifications for the channel

What about Smart Delivery and Go-Live notifications?

Smart delivery is a notification setting that controls where notifications reach you, while personalized notifications control which notifications you receive

With smart delivery enabled, if you’re active on Twitch on desktop (twitch.tv), we send notifications there. You won’t get notifications via mobile or email. If you’re not active on Twitch on desktop (twitch.tv), we’ll send notifications via mobile, email, or both. If you don’t have smart delivery enabled, you might get the same notification up to 3 times! Learn more about smart delivery here.

For more information about Go Live notifications, see How to Use Go-Live Notifications.

Frequently Asked Questions

What’s the difference between “Personalized” and “Always”?
“Always” sends you every notification type for that channel (go-live, catch-up, subscriber updates). “Personalized” curates which notifications you receive based on your viewing habits, time of day, and recent notification frequency. If you want to ensure you never miss a notification from a channel, use “Always.”
Will I miss important notifications with “Personalized”?
Personalized notifications prioritize go-live notifications for channels you watch regularly. However, you may occasionally not receive a go-live notification if you haven’t watched that channel recently or if you’ve received many notifications already. For your absolute favorite streamers, we recommend using “Always” to ensure you receive every notification.
How does “Personalized” decide which notifications to send?
Personalized notifications use several factors including: your viewing history with that channel, how recently you’ve received other notifications, your local time of day, and your engagement patterns. The system learns from your behavior to send notifications when you’re most likely to watch.
Can I use different settings for different channels?
Yes! That’s exactly how the system is designed to work. You can set your top 5 favorite streamers to “Always,” channels you watch regularly to “Personalized,” channels you only watch live to “Go Live Only,” and channels you rarely watch to “Off.” Each channel has its own independent notification setting.
How long does it take for setting changes to apply?
Changes to your notification settings take effect immediately. If you change a channel from “Personalized” to “Always,” you’ll start receiving all notifications for that channel right away.
Does “Personalized” affect transactional notifications?
No. Transactional notifications (purchase confirmations, account security alerts, subscription renewals) are always sent regardless of your channel notification settings. Personalized only affects channel-specific notifications like go-live alerts and catch-up content.

Achievements

Located in your Creator Dashboard, Achievements help you grow, set goals, and provide transparency into your progress towards Affiliate and Partner status.

The Achievements Page

To see your Achievements, head to your dashboard. Listed first on the page are a number of goals that help you track your progress from your first time on Twitch to applying for Partnership. Afterwards, you’ll see your in-progress achievements and completed achievements.

It Begins

For those just starting out, these achievements will help you set up and start your first stream.

Path to Affiliate

After you have the basics down, Path to Affiliate will help you track your progress toward eligibility for the Twitch Affiliate program. The Path to Affiliate includes four achievements:

  • Reach 25 followers
  • Stream for 4 hours
  • Stream on 4 different days
  • Reach an Average of 3 Viewers (on 4 different days)*

*Reach a minimum of 3 average viewers over any 4 stream days in the last 30 days. Days below 3 average viewers don’t count against you.

To be eligible for the Affiliate program, you must meet the requirements for all the achievements above within a 30-day period. So, for example, if you complete an Average of 3 viewers on day 5 and Stream for 4 hours on day 35, you won’t be eligible because you didn’t finish the achievements within the same 30 days. Instead, you’ll see a checkmark next to the achievements that you’ve completed within the required time window. For your stats over the last thirty days, click the View 30-day stats button.

Once you’ve completed these achievements, you can join the Affiliate program by clicking on the Get Started button that will appear. For help with the onboarding process, please take a look at our Affiliate Onboarding Guide.

Achievements not updating? Depending on when you earn the achievement, it can take up to 48 hours for Affiliate invites to be sent out.

Path to Partner

The Path to Partner is designed to help you track your progress towards being eligible to apply to the Twitch Partner program. The achievements are as follows:

  • 6 streams on 6 unique days with an average of 75 viewers in the last 30 days
  • 6 streams of 6 unique days with an average of 75 viewers in the last 30-60 days

To be eligible to apply to the Partner Program you must meet all three requirements from the Path to Partner achievement within the same 30-day period.

Broadcasts that do not reach a minimum average of 75 viewers will not count toward progression in the “Path to Partner.”

For the two consecutive months prior to your Partner application, you must consistently meet the minimum requirement of 75 average viewers across the above mentioned +6 individual streams per 30 day period. This means you should have 12 individual streams (6 per month) with a predictable +75 viewers per stream. As long as you meet the minimum threshold of +6 streams per 30 day period each meeting +75 viewers, additional streams during this period with lower viewership will not be counted against your application. Streamers who consistently attract +70-80 average viewers are more likely to receive an invite than streamers with viewership that fluctuates between 20 and 200.

There are certain circumstances where we may accept applications outside of these criteria. Some instances may include exceptional viewership growth or an established audience on other platforms. We also consider suspension history when evaluating applications. Please note that applying does not guarantee Partnership. Learn more.

Becoming eligible for Partner does not guarantee Partner status.

Build a Community

Completing these achievements unlocks the ability to grant VIP status to members of your community. Earn more VIP badges the more active chatters in your community. To learn more about the VIP role, please see our Managing Roles article.

Frequently Asked Questions

Will I automatically become an Affiliate or Partner after I complete the achievements in the Path to Affiliate and Partner to Partner panels?
No, completing the achievements will only make you eligible to apply for Affiliate or Partner status. You must still complete the Affiliate onboarding process or a Partner application form.
If I leave the Affiliate program and wish to return, do I need to complete the Path to Affiliate again?
If you voluntarily offboarded from the Affiliate program, your completed Path to Affiliate Achievements do not reset. To rejoin, you would need to contact support.
Do watch parties impact achievements?
Yes, watch parties contribute towards the progress of some achievements:
  • The Empire Business
  • Kind of A Big Deal
  • People Know Me
I met the criteria for an achievement but it doesn’t show as complete.
Depending on the achievement, it may take up to 48 hours for your achievement progress to show up.
In the Path to Affiliate, why did my progress in Reach 25 Followers go to zero?
The Path to Affiliate requires that you reach 25 followers. You don’t lose progress towards this goal, even if it takes a long time to achieve. However, if you don’t gain any new followers in 180 days (about 6 months), the achievement progress will drop to 0/25. This does not necessarily mean you’ve lost followers, or that you need to start over. This is how the achievement system displays inactivity. As soon as you gain a new follower, your actual progress (X/25) will be shown within 24 hours.
Is it possible for me to lose progress towards an achievement?
Yes. For example, for the achievement “Stream for 4 hours in the last 30 days,” you will lose progress if you stop streaming for 30 days. Once you’ve completed an achievement, progress will no longer be tracked. For the achievements related to Affiliate and Partner status, completing an achievement is separate from completing it within the last 30 days (indicated by a checkmark).
For achievements with time or day, what timezone do you use?
All times and time-based achievements (day, month) are in GMT and are not adjusted for Daylight Savings Time. (Remember, your viewers may be in a different timezone than you!)
Do chatbots count as viewers for the Path to Affiliate?
No. Chatbots such as Moobot and Nightbot connect only to your chat and are not counted as viewers. Because of this, they do not count toward the “reach an average of 3 viewers” achievement in the Path to Affiliate. Only people watching your stream count toward this achievement. For more on the difference between viewers and chat users, see Understanding Viewer Count vs. Users in Chat.
Some achievements mention reaching a number of viewers or chatters “at the same time.” What does that mean?
“At the same time” means within a few minutes of each other, not across your whole stream. For example, an achievement to reach 100 chatters “at the same time” requires 100 people chatting within a few minutes of one another — not 100 different chatters spread across your entire broadcast.

Age Verification on Twitch

Age verification helps us comply with local laws and create a safe, age-appropriate experience on Twitch. In some regions, you may need to verify your age using facial age estimation technology. This quick, one-time process helps keep our community safe.

How to Complete Age Verification

To comply with local laws, Twitch has minimum age requirements that vary by region. When you sign up, you need to provide your birth date. If you don’t meet the minimum age for your region, you won’t be able to create an account. Learn more.

In some regions, we use on-device facial age estimation technology to verify your age.

When You May Need to Verify Your Age
  • Creating a New Account: If you’re in an affected region, you may need to verify your age when signing up.
  • Logging In: Existing users in affected regions may be prompted to verify their age when logging in.
  • Prior to watching certain content: Existing users in affected regions may be prompted to verify their age prior to watching content labeled with certain Content Classification Labels (CCLs).
How to Complete Verification

Step 1: When prompted, you’ll see a “Verify Your Age” screen explaining the requirement.

Step 2: Complete the face scan by:

  • Allowing camera access when prompted
  • Ensuring you’re in a well-lit area
  • Removing headwear that covers your face
  • Keeping glasses on if you normally wear them
  • Following on-screen instructions for the scan

Step 3: Receive confirmation of your verification status and proceed with your Twitch experience.

To protect your privacy, Twitch and k-ID (a third-party vendor we partner with to verify your age) do not store your face scan video selfies. The video selfie used for facial age estimation is analyzed entirely on your device and will never leave it. The information you provide will be used solely for age verification purposes and will not be used for anything else.

Age Verification Troubleshooting

If you experience a technical issue with the face scan:

  • Ensure you’re in good lighting conditions
  • Check that your camera is working properly
  • Remove face coverings or accessories that might interfere
  • Try again in a different location with better lighting

If you need further assistance, please contact k-ID Support, or consult their Age Verification help resources here.

For security reasons, verification attempts are limited daily. If you exceed the limit, wait 24 hours before trying again.

Frequently Asked Questions

Sections:
  • General FAQ
  • UK FAQ
  • Australia FAQ
  • Turkey FAQ
General FAQ
Why does Twitch require age verification?
Age verification helps ensure that users meet the minimum age required to use Twitch, and also helps make sure that certain types of content are only seen by people who meet the age requirements for their region.
What happens if I don’t meet the age requirements?
If you don’t meet the minimum age required in your region to use Twitch, you will not be allowed to have an account on Twitch. Certain types of content on Twitch may also require you to meet a minimum age in your region, so if you do not meet the required age you will not be able to view that content. If you believe your estimated age is incorrect, you can appeal through Twitch Support with proper age documentation here. If your account was suspended for being under the minimum age and you are older than that age, appeal through our contact form using the “Privacy Questions” category and “Age Suspension Appeal” sub-category. Learn more in Date of Birth Changes.
Can I opt out of age verification?
No. Age verification is required by law in certain regions. If you are in an affected region, you may be prompted to verify your age when creating an account, logging in, or prior to watching certain content.
What content is age-restricted on Twitch?
In certain regions, and where required by local law, content labeled with certain Content Classification Labels (CCLs) requires age verification to access.
I am a parent and found out my child is using Twitch even though they don’t meet the minimum age requirement in our area. What should I do?
If you are a parent or a legal guardian of a child who has created a Twitch account, you can contact Twitch at privacy@twitch.tv to have the account closed and personal information deleted, or to make a data access request about that account. When notifying Twitch, please include any information, such as the username, that will aid in identifying the account. If you are not a parent or a legal guardian, please report the child through our reporting tool. You can find step-by-step information about reporting on the “Filing a Report” page. If Safety Operations finds sufficient evidence of the user being under the minimum age required to use Twitch in their area, they will indefinitely suspend the account.
What resources are there for parents of teens that want to use Twitch?
On a global level, Twitch requires all users to at least be 13 years of age. Twitch users between the ages of 13 and the legal age of adulthood in their area of residence may only use Twitch under the supervision of a parent or legal guardian. More information on how to provide a safe experience for Twitch users between the ages of 13 and 18 can be found here.
UK FAQ
I am a UK resident under the age of 18. Can I still use Twitch?
Yes, you can still continue to use Twitch but will not be able to view certain content labeled with Content Classification Labels (CCLs).
What do I do if I experience an error when trying to verify my age?
Review the error message for details. If this does not resolve the issue, please contact k-ID Support, or visit their help resources here.
What do I do if I experience crashing while trying to verify my age?
Please contact k-ID Support, or visit their help resources here.
Is my facial scan stored or shared?
No. Your facial scan is processed immediately on your device to estimate your age and is not stored or shared. The technology only confirms whether you meet age requirements.
How many times do I need to verify my age?
Age verification is a one-time process. Once verified, you will not need to verify again on that same account.
How long does the verification process take?
The facial scanning and age estimation process typically takes up to a minute to complete. Manual reviews through the Twitch Support appeal process may take longer depending on the complexity of the case. If you believe your estimated age is incorrect, you can appeal through Twitch Support with proper age documentation here.
Australia FAQ
I am an Australian resident under the age of 16. Why can’t I have a Twitch account?
In compliance with Australia’s Social Media Minimum Age (“SMMA”) law, Twitch will no longer allow Australian residents under the age of 16 to have an account. As of December 10, 2025, Australians under the age of 16 will not be allowed to create a Twitch account, and existing Twitch users under the age of 16 will have their accounts disabled on January 9, 2026.
What steps can I take to preserve my account before it is disabled?
If you have VODs on your channel that you would like to retain, we recommend that you download them prior to January 9. For more details on how to download your videos, you can refer to our help article.
What will happen to my recurring subscriptions or purchases after my account is disabled?
Any recurring subscriptions that you have purchased will not renew as of January 9, 2026 and if you have any active subscriptions (excluding gifted subscriptions) extending past January 9, they will be refunded. If you have any Bits remaining in your account on January 9, we will refund them to the payment method that was used to purchase them.
Can I re-enable my Twitch account once I turn 16 or will I have to create a new account?
Yes, once you turn 16 you can reach out to customer support to request that your account be reinstated, so that you can maintain your previous account username.
Turkey FAQ
I am a Turkish resident under the age of 15. Why can’t I have a Twitch account?
In compliance with Turkish law, Twitch will no longer allow Turkish residents under the age of 15 to have an account. Starting October 29, 2026, new users in Turkey under the age of 15 will not be allowed to create a Twitch account. Existing residents of Turkey with Twitch accounts under the age of 15 will have their accounts disabled in February 2027.
What steps can I take to preserve my account before it is disabled?
If you have VODs on your channel that you would like to retain, we recommend that you download them prior to February 2027. For more details on how to download your videos, you can refer to our help article.
What will happen to my recurring subscriptions or purchases after my account is disabled?
Any recurring subscriptions that you have purchased will not renew as of your account being disabled in February 2027, and if you have any active subscriptions (excluding gifted subscriptions) extending past the disable date, they will be refunded. If you have any Bits remaining in your account as of the disabled date, we will refund them to the payment method that was used to purchase them.
Can I re-enable my Twitch account once I turn 15 or will I have to create a new account?
Yes, once you turn 15 you can reach out to customer support to request that your account be re-enabled, so that you can maintain your previous account username.

Clips Settings

Create short, bite-sized segments of your live streams or past broadcasts with clips. Learn more about clips in our guide: link.twitch.tv/HowtoClip

Streamers control who can create clips from their stream, or disable clip creation altogether. Manage these settings and more in your Clips Settings.

Managing Clips Settings

Clips are available for channels in the DJ program, but must not contain music from the DJ Music Catalog. Clips are automatically scanned, and those detected as containing music will not be published. Additionally, DJs cannot have captions on their clips. Learn more.

To manage your Clips Settings, visit your Creator Dashboard -> Settings -> Stream.

Setting Name & Link

Description

Enable Clips

Enable the creation of clips from your stream or past broadcasts. Users who can create clips will also be able to trim, title, and edit the portrait layout of the clips they create. You can edit those clips at any time through the Clips Manager.

Any clip you or your editors have edited, featured, or shared will not be editable by anyone else.

Exclude Categories

When categories are added, clips will not be created by others while streaming in these categories.

Changes made will take effect starting on your next stream.

Followers-only

When enabled, followers must follow you for the specified amount of time before they are allowed to make clips of your channel. Choose between any followers, of if they have followed for 10 or 30 minutes, 1 hour, 1 day, 1 week, 1 month, or 3 months.

Subscriber-only

Only allow subscribers to make clips of your channel.

Clips made by subscribers can be viewed by anyone.

Let viewers upload clips to their socials

Allow viewers to directly post clips from your Twitch channel to their YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram accounts. By default, this setting is turned off.

If this setting is enabled, viewers will be able to do this under the Share button of any clip, anywhere the clip can be viewed.

Your Twitch channel name will be automatically added as a hashtag in viewers’ posts on both TikTok and Instagram. Auto-hashtagging is not supported to YouTube.

If you’ve added your TikTok and Instagram to your social links in your Channel Page, we’ll automatically tag your TikTok and Instagram handles. Learn more about adding social links to your Channel Page here.

Allow viewers to add captions

When enabled, viewers can add captions to new clips they create from your stream. Turning this setting off won’t remove captions that already exist. You can remove captions when exporting clips from Twitch.

Add captions when using “Clip That”

When enabled, clips that are created using the “Clip That” command will have captions added by default.

Featured Clips Permissions

Streamers and editors can feature clips by default. Enable other channel roles (like Moderators) to feature clips of your channel. Users will be notified when they receive permissions.

Comment Access

Manage who can comment on your clips. Comments are enabled by default with safety-first protections including AutoMod filtering, and rate limiting. You can adjust who can comment (followers, subscribers, verified users), or disable comments channel-wide. You can also disable comments on individual clips from your Clips Manager.

Learn more about Comments on Clips.

Learn how Featured Clips can boost the discovery of your channel and content here.

Frequently Asked Questions

If I’ve allowed viewers to upload clips of my channel to YouTube and TikTok, but a viewer posts a clip of mine to TikTok and YouTube that I want removed, what can I do?
You can always delete a clip associated with your channel on Twitch in your Clips Manager. To stop any other viewers from continuing to share it, you can turn off the setting that allows viewers to post your clips directly to their accounts on TikTok and YouTube. If you’ve turned this setting on, we are unable to assist in removing clips from third party sites such as TikTok and YouTube. In this case, you will need to reach out to the third party directly for further assistance.
Can I allow only certain types of viewers to post my clips to their TikTok and YouTube (e.g. subscribers)?
As of now, no. We only have the setting option to be toggled on for all viewers or toggled off for all viewers. The team is exploring adding additional settings and filters to this feature.

Comments on Clips

Viewers can comment on Twitch Clips — reply to each other, like comments, and use the channel’s emotes to join the conversation in the community’s own language. Streamers can heart comments to highlight them, and their comments are marked with a creator badge. All commenters are responsible for keeping their comments in line with Twitch’s Community Guidelines.

Comments are available on Clips only (not Highlights, Uploads, or VODs), including Recaps and clips shared within Stories. Comments are different from the chat replay that may also appear on a clip — chat replay is a read-only playback of past live chat, while comments are a new and ongoing threaded conversation anyone can participate in.

Comments are enabled by default on all clips with safety-first protections already in place. Streamers have full control to manage who can comment, disable comments on any clip or across their entire channel, and delete or moderate comments at any time in their Clips Settings. Unlike live chat, streamers are not expected to actively monitor clip comment sections — safety defaults work automatically in the background.

Comments on Clips are being rolled out gradually to all streamers. You’ll receive a notification in your Creator Dashboard when comments are enabled on your channel.

Comment Safety Defaults

Comments on Clips are built with multiple layers of safety protection that apply automatically — no setup required:

Protection

How it works

AutoMod filtering

All comments pass through your channel’s AutoMod settings and blocked terms list before posting. Comments that don’t pass your settings are silently blocked from posting. They do not go to a review queue.

Links blocked

All URLs and hyperlinks are blocked in comments.

Rate limiting

Commenters are limited to 5 comments per minute and 200 per day to prevent spam.

Bot detection

Automated accounts identified by Twitch’s systems are blocked from commenting.

Chat bans apply

Accounts banned in chat will not be able to comment.

Blocked users

Users you’ve blocked cannot comment on your clips. Their existing comments are hidden for all.

Community moderation

Everyone can downvote comments they don’t feel contribute to the discussion. Comments with a high rate of downvotes are automatically hidden from public view. Viewers can choose to reveal hidden comments. If a comment violates Twitch’s Community Guidelines, report it.

See your default setting for comment access on your channel and adjust it any time in Clips Settings.

Managing Comments (Streamers)

Disabling Comments

Channel-wide: Go to your Creator Dashboard → Settings → Stream → Clips Settings and toggle Comments off.

Per clip: Go to your Creator Dashboard → Content → Clips, open the overflow menu (3 Vertical Dots icon) on any clip, and select Disable Comments.

Disabling hides existing comments but preserves them. Re-enabling restores all comments.

You cannot moderate comments while they are hidden. Re-enable to access moderation tools.

Hearting Comments

Heart a comment to pin it to the top of the comment section with a “Liked by [your channel name]” indicator. When you heart a comment, that viewer receives a notification.

Engaging with your comment section — hearting or replying — notifies those viewers and brings them back to your clip. It’s a lightweight way to stay connected with your community between streams.

Downvoting and Reporting Comments

You, your viewers, and moderators can all downvote comments that don’t contribute to the discussion. When a comment receives a high rate of downvotes, it’s automatically hidden from public view, no streamer or moderator action required.

If a comment violates Twitch’s Community Guidelines, report it. Downvoting and reporting comments work together: Downvoting helps keep your clips’ comment section clean in real time, while reporting notifies Twitch to review.

Deleting Comments and Banning Users
  • Delete any comment on your clips. Deleting a top-level comment removes the entire reply chain.
  • Ban users from commenting directly from the comment interface. Banning applies across both comments and chat — and hides all of their existing comments.
Comment Access Settings

Manage who can comment in Creator Dashboard → Settings → Stream → Clips Settings:

  • Followers-only mode — Require a follow duration before commenting (10 minutes up to 3 months)
  • Subscribers-only mode — Restrict commenting to subscribers
  • Email/phone verification — Require verified email or phone
  • Disable comments — Turn off comments channel-wide
Viewing Comment Activity

Comment counts for each clip are visible in your Clips Manager (Creator Dashboard → Content → Clips). Select the count to jump to that clip’s comments.

Moderator Tools

Channel moderators can help manage clip comments on behalf of the streamer. For more on setting up your moderation team, see Setting Up Moderation for Your Twitch Channel.

Moderators can:

  • Delete individual comments or bulk delete up to 100 at once
  • Ban users from commenting via the comment interface

Moderators cannot:

  • Disable comments or change comment access settings
  • Heart or highlight comments

There is currently no Mod View history for deleted comments.

Chat bans and comment bans are shared — banning a user from one surface bans them from both.

Notifications

For Viewers

You receive notifications when someone replies to your comment or a streamer hearts it. Like notifications appear on-site only (no push). Notification volume is capped per day so you won’t be overwhelmed.

For Streamers

You receive notifications when viewers comment on your clips. Comments are batched and capped — you will not receive a notification for every individual comment.

Adjusting Notifications

Go to Settings → Notifications and look for comment options under the Social category. You can turn off push notifications for comments without disabling comments themselves.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why are comments enabled on my clips by default?
Comments are enabled by default so your community can engage with your content from day one. Safety protections — including AutoMod filtering, rate limits, link blocking, and bot detection — are active automatically. You can disable comments at any time in your Clips Settings.
How do I turn off comments?
Disable comments channel-wide in Creator Dashboard → Settings → Stream → Clips Settings, or per clip through the overflow menu in your Clips Manager. Disabling hides existing comments but preserves them — re-enabling restores everything.
What’s the difference between downvoting, and reporting a comment?
Downvoting hides a comment from public view once enough people downvote it. However, the comment still remains on the clip, and viewers can choose to unhide the comment. Reporting sends a comment to Twitch for review against our Community Guidelines, which can result in the comment behind removed and the commenter receiving enforcement action. If a comment violates our Community Guidelines, report it, even if you also already downvoted it.
I didn’t turn this on. Why do my clips have comments?
Comments on Clips are being rolled out gradually to all streamers. Comments are enabled by default with safety protections in place. You’ll receive a notification in your Creator Dashboard when comments become available on your channel. You can disable them at any time in your Clips Settings.
How do I stop getting comment notifications?
Go to Settings → Notifications and adjust comment options under the Social category. You can turn off push notifications while keeping comments enabled. Notification volume is already capped to prevent spam.
Can I control who comments on my clips?
Yes. In your Clips Settings, choose from: followers (with a duration you set), subscribers only, or require email/phone verification. You can also disable comments entirely.
Are comments the same as chat replay?
No. Comments are a threaded conversation on the clip. Chat replay is a read-only playback of what was said in live chat when the clip was captured. Both can appear on the same clip as separate tabs.
Do comments appear on Highlights, Uploads, or VODs?
No. Comments are only available on Clips. They also appear on clips shared within Stories, or Recaps.
Why can I comment on some Stories but not others?
You can comment on a clip when it appears in a Story. Stories without a clip do not have comments.
Can moderators manage comments?
Yes. Moderators can delete comments and ban users from commenting on channels they moderate. They cannot disable comments or change access settings.
My comment isn’t posting. Why?
Your comment may not post if: you don’t meet the channel’s access requirements; your comment contains a link; it was filtered by the channel’s AutoMod settings or blocked terms; or you’ve hit the rate limit. If commenting is restricted to specific viewers, you’ll see a message explaining the limitation.
What happens to comments if I delete a clip?
All associated comments are no longer available when a clip is deleted.
