Create an Account with Twitch

Creating an account on Twitch allows you to interact with streamers and the community via chat, follow your favorite streamers to receive alerts when they go live, and broadcast to the Twitch community from your channel.

Can’t access your existing account? If you’re having trouble logging in, forgot your password, or lost access to your email or phone number, visit our Account Access & Login Issues Guide for complete recovery options. Don’t create a new account if you’re trying to recover an existing one.

When signing up for an account, you must agree to our Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. You are held to our Community Guidelines as well. Accounts found to violate these are subject to penalty, including account suspension. Please take the time to read these documents carefully.

Ways to Create Your Account

Twitch offers multiple ways to create an account. Visit twitch.tv or download the Twitch mobile app and select Sign Up to get started.

Already have a Twitch account? If you’re trying to log in but can’t remember your username or password, see our Account Access Guide instead of creating a new account.

Traditional Signup

Create an account using your email address or phone number. You’ll choose a username, set a password, and provide your date of birth.

Social Login

Sign up quickly using an existing account from one of these providers:

  • Sign up with Google
  • Sign up with Apple
  • Sign up with Amazon

When using social login, Twitch will access your name and email address from your chosen provider. You’ll still need to choose a username and provide your date of birth to complete account creation.

Learn more about social login, including how to manage your connected accounts, in our Social Login guide.

Additional Authentication Methods

Twitch may introduce additional authentication methods in the future, such as passwordless login using biometrics or security keys. Check the signup page for the latest available options.

Account Creation Requirements

Regardless of which signup method you choose, you’ll need to provide:

  • Username: Between 4-25 characters in length. If your desired username isn’t available, you’ll need to choose another. Learn more about username policies.
  • Date of Birth: Required to verify you meet age requirements for using Twitch.
  • Verification Method: Either a phone number (mobile only, no landlines or VOIP) or email address for account verification.

When creating an account, double-check that the information provided is correct. If you lose access to your account and need to go through account recovery, having accurate information will greatly assist in that process.

Verification Process

After submitting your signup information, Twitch will send a 6-digit one-time password (OTP) via SMS or email to verify your contact information. Enter this code within 5 minutes to complete verification.

Desktop

Mobile

When signing up with your phone number, add your country code. Most phones will automatically add your country code for you; however, double-check, or you may not be able to receive text messages from us. SMS and data rates may apply.

Why Verify Your Email?

If you signed up using your phone number, we highly recommend also adding and verifying your email address. This will:

  • Provide an additional recovery method if you lose access to your phone
  • Allow us to send you notifications for channels you follow (if enabled)
  • Allow you to chat in channels that require verified email
  • Ensure you receive critical account information

Troubleshooting Common Issues

Username Not Available

If your desired username is taken, you’ll need to choose a different one. Twitch does not release inactive usernames. Learn more about username policies.

Not Receiving Verification Code

If you don’t receive your verification code within 5 minutes during signup:

  • Go back and double-check that your phone number or email address is entered correctly
  • Check your spam or junk folder if using email
  • Ensure your phone can receive SMS messages if using phone verification
  • If using Apple’s “Hide My Email” feature, check your Apple Mail junk folder
  • Wait 5 minutes - delivery can be delayed

Still not receiving codes? See our comprehensive troubleshooting guide: Not Receiving Verification Codes

Email Already in Use

If you receive an error that your email is already associated with another account, what are you trying to do?

Your Situation

What to Do

I forgot I already have an account

Use the Account Recovery Tool to find your username, then log in

I want to create a second account

See Creating Additional Accounts below - you must enable this on your first account

I disabled my old account

Deletion takes 90 days. See If You Deleted Your Account

I can’t access the old account

See the Account Access & Login Issues Guide for recovery steps and support options

Signing up with a phone number that’s already on another account? That works without any extra steps. See Using a Phone Number on Multiple Accounts.

Social Login Issues

If you’re experiencing issues with Google, Apple, or Amazon login:

  • Ensure you’re signed into the correct provider account
  • Check that the email from your social login provider isn’t already linked to a different Twitch account
  • Complete any two-factor authentication required by your provider
  • If the provider’s services are down, wait and try again later

For detailed social login troubleshooting, see our Social Login guide.

Account Recovery

Need more help accessing your account? Our Account Access & Login Issues Guide covers lost passwords, lost email/phone access, Account Recovery Tool instructions, and complete troubleshooting for all login scenarios.

If you’re having trouble accessing an existing account, visit our Account Recovery page or request a password reset.

Creating Additional Twitch Accounts

What are you trying to do?
  • I want to access my existing account — You probably don’t need a second account. Try Account Recovery to find your username, or request a password reset to the email in question — the reset email will show you which username is associated with it.
  • I genuinely want to create a second account — If you’re using the same email, follow the steps below to enable additional account creation. If you’re using the same phone number, no extra steps are needed.
  • Someone may have used my email without my knowledge — Contact Twitch Support immediately.

Additional Twitch accounts can be created at any time granted you adhere to the Terms of Service and Community Guidelines.

Email Verification

When verifying the email address on your account, additional creation of accounts with that email address becomes disabled to prevent abusive behavior against you.

If you have a verified email on your account, click Enable additional account creation in your Settings to create additional Twitch accounts; turning this on will allow you to register a single additional account.

Phone Verification

You can use the same verified phone number on more than one Twitch account. Enter the number when you sign up and verify it with the code we send. You don’t need to change any settings on your other accounts. See Using a Phone Number on Multiple Accounts.

If You Don’t Remember the Original Account Username

If you have forgotten the username associated with the other account, you can use the Self Recovery Tool to retrieve a list of the username(s) associated with your email address or phone number.

When using the recovery tool:

  • Go to twitch.tv/user/account-recovery
  • Enter your email address, or select your country code and enter your phone number
  • Click Continue
  • Click “I Don’t Know My Username”
  • We’ll email or text you a list of ALL accounts linked to it
If You Deleted Your Account

If you have deleted your other account, you should be able to automatically re-enable your account simply by logging in to it. If you cannot log into your account, we recommend that you request a password reset.

It could take a few minutes to process your request and appear in your inbox.

If you have recently requested to have your account deleted, keep in mind that the entire process will take around 90 days. You should receive an email or a text message once this has been finalized. At any point during the 90 days, if you re-enable the account by logging into it, you will be removed from the queue and need to start the deletion process from the beginning.

Frequently Asked Questions

What’s the difference between signing up with email/phone vs. social login?
Traditional signup requires you to create a password, while social login uses your existing Google, Apple, or Amazon account credentials. Both methods create a full Twitch account with the same features.
Can I add a password to my account if I signed up with social login?
Accounts created using social login cannot add a password from the settings page. A password can only be created through the Account Recovery process. Contact Support for assistance.
Can I use the same email or phone number for multiple Twitch accounts?
Phone number: yes. Verify it on each account; no settings change is needed. Email: social login does not support email addresses associated with multiple Twitch accounts. For traditional signup, you must enable “additional account creation” on the original account before using the same email elsewhere.
Why can’t I change my email or password?
If your account was created via social login, email and password changes may be restricted for security reasons. Contact Support for assistance.
I forgot which social provider I used to sign up. How can I find out?
Try each social login option (Google, Apple, Amazon), or check your email inbox for Twitch emails to identify which provider was used. You can also check Login Options in your Settings.
What should I do if I lose access to my Google, Apple, or Amazon account?
You’ll need to recover access to your provider account first. Visit Google Account Help, Apple ID Support, or Amazon Account Help for assistance.
Can I disconnect my social login from my Twitch account?
Once you add a social login, you cannot disconnect it yourself. Contact Support for assistance disconnecting a social login method.
Do I need to verify both my email and phone number?
You only need to verify one method to create your account, but we highly recommend verifying both. This provides additional recovery options and ensures you receive important account notifications.
Why does Twitch need my date of birth?
Your date of birth verifies that you meet the age requirements for using Twitch and helps us comply with legal requirements for protecting minors online.
Can I change my username after creating my account?
Yes, you can change your username from your account settings. Learn more about username changes.
I deleted my account but can’t reuse my email yet. Why?
Account deletion takes 90 days to complete. During this time, your email remains linked to the deleted account. You must wait for the deletion to finalize, or re-enable the account and enable “Additional account creation” before deleting it again. See If You Deleted Your Account. Phone numbers aren’t affected: you can add yours to another account right away.
Can my child under 13 use Twitch?
No, Twitch requires users to be at least 13 years old. For comprehensive information about age requirements, safety tools, and keeping teens safe on Twitch, see our Guide for Parents and Educators.

Digital Services Act (“DSA”)

The Digital Services Act (“DSA”) is a European Union (EU) law that requires online services like Twitch to provide a number of safety-related features to EU residents. If you are an EU resident, you may report suspected illegal content to us, and you may also appeal our decisions on those reports. If you receive an enforcement action due to illegal content, you may appeal that decision, and you may be able to utilize other legal methods for seeking redress including the out-of-court dispute settlement process established by the DSA. For the most part, user reports of illegal content under the DSA are made and processed according to Twitch’s normal procedures, and the only differences are described below.

Illegal Content Reporting & Reporter Appeals

Filing a Report

If you are an EU resident, you can report suspected illegal content through our regular reporting flow, which is described in detail in our How to File a User Report help page. When completing your report, in the “Why are you submitting this report?” section, you should select the most relevant reporting reason. If none of the listed reasons describes the illegal content you want to report, then you can select “Other Illegality.” Note that this reporting option is only for EU residents and reports will not be processed if filed from outside the EU.

In the “Tell Us More” section, please provide detailed information regarding the content that you believe is illegal, including:

  • The specific law you believe the content violates, including the country and section(s) of the law
  • Links to the specific content if available
  • The specific statements or a description of the images in the reported content that you believe are illegal
  • Why you believe the statements or images are illegal

Please note that you must specify the law you believe has been violated for your report to be processed.

To complete your report submission you will be asked to confirm your email (if you are logged-in) or provide an email (if you are not logged-in), and verify that the information provided is truthful by checking a box at the bottom of the form.

Notifying You of Our Decision on Your Report

After you file a report, a number of things happen, which are detailed in our How to File a User Report help page. In addition to what is described there, for EU residents, once we have made a decision on your report, we will send you an email informing you of our decision.

Appealing Our Decision On Your Report

If you would like to appeal our decision on your report, you can request another review by clicking the appeal link provided in your report outcome email. This link will take you to a “Request Another Review” form that will include the reference number and additional details, when available, from your original report. Here, you can provide additional information explaining why you believe we should reconsider our decision. You will also be asked to provide your email if you are not logged-in.

Your appeal will be automatically linked to your original report. Note that only EU residents may appeal our decisions on their reports, and reporter appeals will not be processed if filed from outside the EU.

Once we have made a decision on your appeal, we will send you an email informing you of our decision. If you wish to contest our decision further, you may be able to utilize other legal methods for seeking redress, including the out-of-court dispute settlement process established by the DSA. To access this settlement process, you must first contact a certified out-of-court dispute settlement body. The European Commission publishes and updates a list of certified out-of-court dispute settlement bodies which can be found here.

Illegal Content Enforcements & Enforcement Appeals

Evaluation & Processing of Illegal Content Reports

When content is reported for any reason other than “Other Illegality,” a member of our safety team will evaluate the report under our Community Guidelines. For “Other Illegality” reports, the report will first be evaluated under our Community Guidelines, and then, if necessary, under the law(s) specified in the “Tell Us More” section.

  • Community Guidelines Review: We will always review the reported content under our Community Guidelines. If the content violates our Community Guidelines, we will issue an appropriate enforcement, including sending an enforcement notice. Please see our detailed About Account Enforcement and Chat Bans help page for additional information on Twitch enforcements and their consequences.
  • Illegality Review: If we determine that the reported content does not violate our Community Guidelines, we will then review it to determine whether it violates the provisions of the law(s) specified in the report. If we determine the content violates the cited provisions, the content will be removed from our service, and we will send a notice to the user whose content has been removed. No enforcement action will be issued.
Appealing Illegal Content Enforcements

If you believe an enforcement against your account was issued incorrectly or that your content was removed in error, you may file an appeal through our regular appeals procedures, which are described in detail in our About Account Enforcement and Chat Bans help page.

Once we have made a decision on your appeal, we will send you an email informing you of our decision. If you wish to contest our decision further, you may be able to utilize other legal methods for seeking redress, including the out-of-court dispute settlement process established by the DSA. To access this settlement process, you must first contact a certified out-of-court dispute settlement body. The European Commission publishes and updates a list of certified out-of-court dispute settlement bodies which can be found here.

Discovery Feed

The discovery feed is a scrollable feed in the Twitch mobile app that shows users a personalized mix of clips and live streams to help viewers find content to enjoy quickly and help streamers get discovered, even when they’re not live.

Scan the below QR code to download the new Twitch mobile app for iOS on the App Store or for Android on Google Play.

Make sure you’ve updated your app to the latest version to see the new experience today.

How does the feed work?

Whether you’re looking to lock in for a live stream or to catch up with the latest on Twitch throughout your day, the discovery feed will show you a mix of personalized content from streamers you already love and new communities we think you’ll enjoy.

There are two tabs within the feed – a live feed, and a clips feed. Scroll vertically through preroll-free previews of live streams in the feed and tap the streamer’s avatar to enter theater mode and join the live stream. We’re working on making it possible to enter a live stream just by tapping the screen in the near future!

If you discover a new channel you like while you’re scrolling but don’t have time to watch the stream, you can follow them and sign up for notifications for upcoming streams directly from the feed.

See a clip you like in the clips feed? Press the share button to share the moment with your own community. You can also press the thumbs up button to signal that you like the clip, to help us better personalize your feed. This information is only shared with Twitch and the streamer and clip creator are not notified.

The live feed will autoplay on mute by default when you open the app. Adjust the volume using the mute button directly on the feed for more control as you scroll. You can also change your mute and autoplay preferences in your app Settings under “Preferences.”

How does content get featured in the feed?

All live streams and clips are automatically eligible to appear in the feed if they meet our content guidelines. To foster a safer viewing experience, unless a viewer is following a channel that is streaming content with a content classification label applied, some streams with content classification labels applied will be restricted from appearing in the feed.

Featured Clips will be prioritized in the Clips feed over non-featured Clips, so select clips after every stream to increase your chance of being discovered.

Will there be ads in the feed?

The discovery feed lets you preview dozens of live streams without having to watch pre-roll ads before you even know if the stream is the right fit for you. You will see ads between content in the feed as you scroll, but these ads are scrollable just like any other content in the feed, to ensure a non-intrusive experience. We may continue to experiment with exactly how ads show up in the feed over time.

These ads operate much like the ads that can be seen on other discovery surfaces today, like the home page headliner or display ads in Browse. Since ads in the feed aren’t directly on a streamer’s channel, streamers will not receive ad revenue. However, these ads still benefit streamers indirectly: these help Twitch maintain its service and can incentivize advertisers to bring more of their business to Twitch. More advertisers mean more potential ad revenue for streamers if they decide to run ads through our service.

Once a viewer enters a live stream from the feed, any ads that are shown during the live stream will function the same way as they do on live streams across web and mobile surfaces (streamers will receive a revenue share for video ads and stream display ads run on their channels).

Using Subfeeds to Discover Content

The discovery feed now includes subfeeds, which allow you to quickly browse content by specific category or other collection type. Subfeeds appear as a horizontal scrollable shelf at the top of both the Live and Clips feeds.

By default, your feed shows a mix of personalized content. Additional subfeeds may include popular categories, or featured collections. Tap any subfeed to view content specific to that category or collection. You can only have one subfeed selected at a time.

Frequently Asked Questions

How can I get my content into the discovery feed?
Streamers can not directly upload any content to the discovery feed. Your live streams and clips are automatically eligible to appear in the feed if they meet Twitch’s content guidelines. Some content with content classification labels applied will not be eligible for the feed. Featured Clips will be prioritized in the feed over non featured clips, so continue to feature your Clips for discovery.
How do I enter a live stream from the feed?
  • You can click on the streamer’s’ avatar from the live feed to enter the live stream (4/30).
  • After 5/20, you’ll be able to tap anywhere on the screen in the live feed to enter the live stream.
Can I chat and join in on the streams from the feed?
When you find a stream you might want to join, you can tap the streamer’s avatar to go to theater mode, and that’s when you’ll be able to see chat and interact with the stream.
Does the Discovery Feed only support horizontal video?
Only horizontal video is supported in the Live feed, but we’re exploring supporting vertical video in the future. Portrait clips are eligible to be shown in the feed. To edit your Clips to portrait, use the Clips Editor in your Clips Manager and feature your Clip to prioritize it in discovery.
Is there a limit to the number of clips or live streams I can scroll in the feed?
There is no limit to the amount of either clips or live streams you can watch in the feed. If you experience an error or end screen when scrolling, please refresh your app. If the issue persists, please leave feedback in UserVoice.
Are only Featured Clips eligible to show up in the Discovery Feed?
Featured Clips are prioritized over other Clips in the feed, but the feed is not limited to only Featured Clips. Learn more about featuring clips.
Will I see ads in the feed if I have Turbo?
Twitch Turbo users will not see ads in the feed. If you’d like to enjoy Twitch ad free, sign up for Turbo here.
Will I see any content or streams with content classification labels applied in my feed?
Some content with content classification labels applied will be restricted from appearing in the feed to foster a safer viewing experience. Mature games and profanity mature content types will still be eligible to show up in feed. If a viewer is following a channel streaming content with a content classification label applied, they will still be able to see that content in the feed, and be prompted to consent to view if the content requires a content classification label be applied.
What is the difference between collections, or featured collections in subfeeds, and creator collections?
In the discovery feed, “collections” refers specifically to the browsable Twitch curated collections of content. Most often, this content is grouped by category, but Twitch may also feature other collection types. Creator collections are playlists of videos you wish to highlight on your channel. Creator collections are not featured anywhere outside of your own channel page. Learn more.

DJ Program FAQ

The Twitch DJ Program is a first-of-its kind offering that makes it possible for DJs to livestream millions of tracks representing the vast majority of popular music, and benefit from new promotional and discovery opportunities. Since we announced the program, we’ve seen a ton of interest and questions. In this guide, we will present answers to common questions received from DJs, and the DJ-curious.

Was this content helpful? Let us know! Tell us what information may be missing by voting at the bottom of this article 👇. You can also give feedback at twitch.uservoice.com, or join us every third Wednesday of the month at twitch.tv/twitch for Patch Notes.

What is the DJ Program?

Note: The DJ Program contains a ton of important information. For details about the program, please read the DJ Program Terms.

DJs who enroll in the DJ Program will be able to livestream millions of tracks representing the vast majority of popular music without risk of takedowns, and will qualify for opportunities on Twitch we haven’t been able to previously offer. This is made possible by a first-of-its-kind partnership with hundreds of companies, including all of the major labels–Universal Music Group, Warner Music Group, Sony Music, and a large number of independent labels and other rights holders represented by Merlin.

When you enroll your account in the DJ Program, you agree to new terms that make this offering possible. We encourage you to review the DJ Program Terms to understand what will change with your account before you enroll in the program. Here’s an overview of highlights:

  • Earnings Sharing - We set aside a portion of earnings generated by your channel to be paid to musicians via the music companies that represent them. Twitch is splitting these costs 50/50 with you.
  • VODs, Highlights, and Uploads disabled; Clips allowed (no music) - Due to contractual restrictions, VODs, Highlights, and Video Uploads are disabled for the DJs category. Clips are available but must not contain music from the DJ Music Catalog. Clips are automatically scanned, and those detected as containing music will not be published. We are creating additional promotional and discovery opportunities to extend the reach and impact of DJ content.

Additionally, viewers on mobile are able to watch DJ streams, except the option for Audio Only listening will be disabled due to program requirements.

It’s crucial that DJs understand the status quo on Twitch was not sustainable, and that any viable future for the community required we find a solution that recognized the contributions of musicians who create the music being streamed in DJ sets. The DJ program is opt-in, and you are not required to join. You are also free to opt-out after you join. But if you live-stream DJ sets and you don’t have the necessary rights or authority to do so outside of the program, you will need to join the DJ program or be exposed to the risks of DMCA takedowns and account enforcement, including strikes and bans.

Who Can Join the DJ Program?

In the Twitch DJ Program, anyone* can be a DJ if they want to live stream themselves playing recorded music for the enjoyment of their Twitch viewers. This program is not just limited to dance or electronic music, but applies to any channel that is using music as a primary focus of their live stream where they are mixing pre-recorded music where they do not have the rights. This program applies to anyone who wants to DJ, and makes that activity the main focus of their streams. You can be a DJ no matter how frequently you stream, regardless of whether you know anything about mixing, remixing, or creating mashups.

If you are not primarily a DJ streamer but stream DJ content occasionally, we recommend creating a separate, additional account dedicated to your DJ streams, so the DJ Program Terms apply to your DJ content. If you DJ for the majority of your streaming time, we recommend keeping a single account. If you are already an affiliate or partner, and aim to create a secondary DJ account, please visit our guide with instructions on how to link your accounts.

How enrolling in the program impacts your account:

Earnings Sharing - We set aside a portion of earnings generated by your channel to be paid to musicians via the music companies that represent them.

VODs, Highlights, and Uploads disabled; Clips allowed (no music) - Due to contractual restrictions, VODs, Highlights, and Video Uploads are disabled for the DJs category. Clips are available but must not contain music from the DJ Music Catalog. Clips are automatically scanned, and those detected as containing music will not be published.

*Due to contractual restrictions and other requirements, the DJ Program is not available worldwide. If you reside in the following countries, you may be unable to enroll in the DJ Program: Belarus, Russia, China, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, South Korea, and Syria.

Variety Streamers Who Stream Occasional DJ Content

This program is designed to enable DJ streams, and for monetizing DJs, as it requires a revenue sharing arrangement to cover the costs associated with music used specifically in DJ streams. If most of your streaming is not as a DJ playing recorded music we recommend setting up two channels, one for your DJ performances and another for your non-DJ performances. Learn more about secondary accounts and the DJ Program here.

How to Join the DJ Program

The DJ Program is open for enrollment. To enroll in the program, make sure you are logged in to your account, visit this page, and review the DJ Program Terms. Then click the enroll button to agree to the terms and join the program. You’ll see a success message in the next screen and receive a welcome email shortly thereafter.

How Does the DJ Catalog Work?

The Twitch DJ Music Catalog is a searchable database that contains millions of track titles that streamers who enroll in the program are allowed to live stream on their channels as part of their DJ performances. This catalog is constantly updated with new releases, offering a real-time look at all of the tracks that DJs are allowed to stream as part of this offering. It does not contain music files, and is designed to be a reference for DJs to search and understand, with certainty, which tracks they are allowed to stream as a part of this offering, and which tracks are blocked.

You are not limited to performing DJ sets with music tracks from the catalog, but if you choose to venture beyond the catalog, you are responsible for ensuring you have the necessary rights or authority to use the music. The information about what tracks are included in the catalog is intended to serve as a definitive reference point that gives you clarity as to what music is covered for you to perform as a part of the DJ Program under Twitch’s deals with music companies. If you stream music that is not included in the catalog, including tracks which do not appear in the catalog database or which are not marked as allowed, you do so at your own risk and may be subject to DMCA claims and enforcement actions if you lack the necessary rights or authority to use the music.

You Still Use Your Own Music Audio! Once you’re opted-in to the program, you’ll stream similarly to how you’ve streamed in the past, using the same streaming software and channel settings, and using your own music files, vinyl, or physical media. Please use the DJ Music Catalog to see what music is covered by Twitch’s deals to stream as a part of this offering, but you will stream the music from your software/hardware.

Restricted Artist List

As a supplemental quick-reference resource for DJs, we have compiled a list of artists whose tracks are generally marked as Restricted (and are excluded from the catalog). We will be updating this Restricted Artist List, but it is not exhaustive and we recommend you search the catalog as the ultimate source of truth for what tracks you are allowed to perform as part of the program.

What Music Can I Play?

The Twitch DJ Music Catalog contains millions of tracks representing the vast majority of popular music, hundreds of thousands of independently released tracks, niche sub-genres, and more. Our agreements with rights holders allow you to livestream these tracks in your DJ sets. If you stream music that is not marked as allowed or that does not appear in the catalog, you do so at your own risk and may be subject to DMCA penalties and enforcement actions if you don’t have the necessary rights or authority to use the music.

Use the catalog search function to see which songs you are allowed to stream as a part of this offering. Please note that the track catalog may vary depending on where you are located when you enroll as a DJ.

Do Not Play Pre-Release or Unreleased Music

Our program does not allow you to stream pre-release tracks (music that has not been released by the rights holder to the public on a digital music service or in physical media). You can use the catalog search functionality to understand which tracks you are allowed to perform in DJ sets. If a track is not marked as allowed or does not appear in the catalog, our program does not allow you to perform that music in your DJ sets.

If you stream pre-release tracks, your channel may be subject to enforcement and penalties including termination of your stream and suspension of your channel. For more information, please refer to the Music Guidelines, Reporting Process for Participating Music Rights Holders, and the DJ Program Terms.

What if a Label WANTS me to Play an Unreleased Song as a Part of Their Promotional Strategy?

We understand that many labels distribute pre-released music to DJs for promotional purposes. Pre-release restrictions are in place to respect the wishes of musicians and their copyright holders. If you’re working with a label that allows Twitch streamers to play their music as part of the Twitch DJ Program and generally restricts pre-releases, and that label wants you to perform their music in a DJ set on Twitch prior to the release date, have them reach out to their Twitch contact to set up an exception to pre-release restrictions.

I am not enrolled in the DJ Program, but a music rights holder has allowed me to play their track in my stream – even though that track is part of the DJ catalog or is a pre-release or unreleased track. If I receive a channel enforcement for playing this track, how do I submit an appeal?

We may issue an account enforcement when Twitch systems detect certain music uses in a stream. Learn more.

If you would like to appeal an account enforcement, you can sign in to the Appeals Portal to submit an appeal. In the description box labeled Tell us why you are submitting an appeal, please include the statement I was authorized by the rights holder(s) to stream the music I included in my stream, and provide the following information:

  • Artist name
  • Track title
  • Rights holder(s): If you are the rights holder, please list yourself.
  • Name of rights holder(s) representative(s)
  • Contact details of rights holder(s) representative(s): Please provide name, email, and/or phone number
  • Your name
  • Your channel name
  • Your phone number
  • Your email address

If you’re working with a label that allows Twitch streamers to play their music as part of the Twitch DJ Program, and that label wants you to perform their music in a DJ set on a Twitch channel that isn’t enrolled in the DJ Program, you can also have the label reach out to their Twitch contact to make advance arrangements related to channel enforcement.

I believe I have the right or authority to stream a track from the DJ Music Catalog on Twitch. Why did I receive a channel enforcement for playing that track in my stream?

We cannot provide legal advice about whether you have the right or authority to stream music on Twitch under your agreements with rights holders. However, we can tell you that:

  • Being able to stream recorded music on a global service like Twitch can involve often obtaining permissions from multiple rights holders;
  • Obtaining an agreement with a rights holder can sometimes only cover certain copyright uses, and streaming music on Twitch may not necessarily be a covered use – for example, a license from a performing rights organization such as ASCAP or BMI may not be sufficient to cover streaming music globally on Twitch; and
  • Subscribing to a music service or buying a CD or digital audio download typically does not by itself allow you to share that music on Twitch – so we encourage you to review each service’s terms of use and our relevant legal pages before including that music in your Twitch streams.

We recognize some streamers may choose to not enroll in the DJ Program because they play music that they created or have sourced authorized music. Streamers who do include music from the DJ Music Catalog in their streams, but do not have agreements with rights holders, may enroll in the DJ Program and stream under Twitch’s contracts. Twitch pays the rights holders based on the music played by DJs enrolled in the program, which makes it possible for musicians to be paid.

Understanding DJ Program Earnings

To cover the music rights costs associated with the Twitch DJ Program, we set aside a portion of earnings generated by your channel to be paid to music companies for the benefit of the musicians they represent. These costs will be a percentage of total revenue. That means this earnings share required to cover music rights costs is proportional to the amount of money you earn. A streamer that earns very little revenue will pay the same percentage of their earnings as a larger streamer who earns more. There are no upfront fees to enroll in the Twitch DJ Program.

Non-Monetizing DJs

Twitch is covering the music rights costs for DJs who aren’t yet monetizing. Streamers will not be financially impacted until they become eligible to monetize.

DJ Promotions & Clubs

DJs enrolled in the program are eligible to be included in front page promotional shelves and other recurring promotional initiatives. Much of this promotion happens automatically and through our systems that surface relevant content to viewers. If you are enrolled in the program and are streaming in the DJs Category, you’re optimizing your opportunities for exposure. Twitch is also creating bespoke marketing initiatives for DJs that will be announced and launched on an on-going basis. Enrolled DJs will be notified of these promotions through Creator Home messages, social media, and email.

In addition to increased promotional opportunities, Twitch has launched the DJ Creator Club, an exclusive community for DJs on Twitch who are enrolled in the program. Hosted on Discord, this is your chance to connect with fellow DJs, learn from each other, and elevate your craft. As a member, you’ll have access to interactive workshops, creator and industry panels, and exclusive networking events. Plus, you’ll get unique opportunities to collaborate and grow alongside other passionate DJs on Twitch. Apply to the DJ club (or any other club you’re interested in) here!

Giving Feedback in the Feedback Forums

This article is part of a series on giving feedback about Twitch.

You can give feedback in the Twitch feedback forums in a few different ways:

  • Vote on an idea
  • Comment on an idea
  • Post a new idea

This guide explains how to post an idea, and includes tips on providing actionable feedback.

Getting Started

The Twitch feedback forum requires a Twitch account to post an idea, vote, or comment on an existing idea. You do not need a Twitch account to lurk.

First time in the feedback forums? Let us show you around: Navigating the Feedback Forums. To learn more about voting and commenting on an existing idea, visit this guide.

Posting a New Idea

Choose a relevant forum & category for your idea and navigate the input field where it says, Enter your idea.

Type out your feedback into this field. Similar ideas will surface in the list below. Please review existing ideas first! If an idea pops up that reflects the feedback you wish to provide, increase its chances for consideration with your vote.

If you’re unsure which category might be best-suited for the idea you’re looking to post or where to look into similar suggestions to vote/comment on, you can utilize the search feature to get a better picture of where relevant, existing ideas live.

Not seeing anything close to what you had in mind? Share your ideas with us!

  • Name your idea clearly and treat the title like a summary! Opt for something that would be easy to search for others. For example: Instead of, “New chat feature”, something like, “Allow users to react to/like individual chat messages” would help get the idea across and surface it better in a search.
  • Titles that are unclear or unnecessarily vulgar may be reworded to better reflect the request for ease of discovery by other users.
  • Although the description input mentions this part as optional, please use this space to flesh out your idea in detail. It’s also important to note that the contents of your description will be shown as comments in the event your idea is merged into another idea. To learn more about merging, please refer to our FAQs.

Be sure to share your suggestions with others to gain more support.

We cannot guarantee action on an idea.

Tips For Giving Good Feedback

An actionable idea:
  • Has a clear title that summarizes the main point of the feedback.
  • Is detailed but easy to read for all (neatly formatted if long).
  • Addresses why and how it should/can be implemented.
  • Adheres to Twitch Community Guidelines

As a community, we are passionate. Feedback should not be offensive, or target certain individuals or groups.

Considerations when providing actionable feedback:
  • Describe the feature would you like to see and where. How would it function? Provide examples and give insight on how this feature would help you/the community.
  • Please ensure that you are not providing a suggestion/feedback for a third-party feature/service. That feedback is best left for the developer of that feature/service.
  • Got multiple suggestions? Feel like putting them all into one idea? Please don’t. It becomes unclear which aspect of your idea people are voting on and makes it impractical to share with our teams for consideration.
  • If you see an issue with something? Describe what or why it is not working and offer solutions to how it can or should function otherwise.
  • Reporting a bug? Be sure to specify where on the site (including links where possible is helpful or referencing the terminology used on-site relevant to the feedback). What error messaging are you seeing, if any are present? Describe the behavior you expect vs. the behavior you’re observing. For some features/functions, it’s perfectly fine to report bugs on UserVoice; however for certain issues (such as those related to video playback), it’s best to use more direct methods (referenced here).

Suggestions without actionable feedback (those that offer little to no insight/are non-constructive), appeals or commentary on suspension decisions, support requests, and suggestions disparaging others will be closed without comment.

Example Actionable Feedback

“Increase the artist role limit beyond 5 - Many streamers have multiple artists for different aspects of the stream (emotes, Vtuber models, alerts, overlays, screens, etc.). Considering the number of VIPs & Moderators you can assign, it doesn’t make sense to limit the artists you’d like to recognize to only 5. This would really help bring recognition to work these artists have done to help streamers develop their channel brand/style. (Reworded example from idea art badges).

  • Feedback came in through a relevant category/forum.
  • Explained why it was important and brought in specific examples of why additional roles would be necessary.
Example That Lacks Actionable Feedback

“Add more places for the artist role.”

  • Feedback came in through an irrelevant category/forum and was not detailed enough to easily determine what the user might be asking for or why.
  • Feedback does not explain how it can help the user or community.

More Resources

Learn more about what status updates mean in the Twitch feedback forums in our guide: Understanding Status Updates FAQ

Want to browse or filter other ideas? Learn how to navigate the feedback forums here: Navigating the Feedback Forums

Was this guide helpful? Let us know by voting below.

Guide to Cheering with Bits

Bits are a virtual good you can buy on Twitch that give you the power to encourage and show support for streamers, get attention in chat through animated Cheermotes, Power-ups, get recognition through badges, leaderboards, with even more possibilities in Extensions.

A Cheer is a chat message that uses Bits. Bits can be used one by one, all at once, or anything in between. Using many Bits at once shows more support through cool animations called Cheermotes. You can pin your message so it stays visible in chat.

So go celebrate amazing moments, show support for streamers, and be recognized!

Looking for a walkthrough on streamer’s Bits settings? Visit Cheering: For Partners & Affiliates

How to Cheer

You need Bits in your inventory to Cheer, and you can only Cheer towards channels that have Bits enabled. Purchase Bits via the Bits icon in the top nav bar, or in a creator’s chat. For more detailed help purchasing Bits, including FAQ and answers to common problems, visit How to Purchase Bits.

To Cheer, type or select Cheermote options from the Bits menu. Cheers can be sent alone, or with a message. You can chain multiple cheer messages together.

No matter how you select your Cheermote + amount, you can enter a message along with your Cheer. For example, if you type: “cheer100 Love your stream!”, your message will appear like this:

To Cheer without the Cheermote menu, type cheer into chat + the amount of Bits you wish to contribute. You can do this with any Cheermote, including custom Partner Cheermotes.

Add an extra 0 by mistake? Don’t worry! Cheers of 1000 Bits or higher (cheer1000) allow a 5-second countdown to click Cancel before Bits are removed from your inventory.

To Cheer using the Cheermote menu, press the Bits icon in the chat window. Select the number of Bits you wish to use from the default gem Cheermotes menu. Send your Cheer by hitting enter or send!

Under the Cheermote picker, you can see if this Cheer will earn you a chat badge!

Creators can set a Minimum Bits Emote (the smallest Bit emote allowed in chat) and a Minimum Bits to Cheer (the minimum total Bits required to send a Cheer message). When you send your message, make sure you aren’t hitting any limits set by the channel owner. You’ll know you hit the limit by the error below: This channel has set a minimum of 100 Bits to use a Cheer emote in chat.

Creators can set minimum pinned cheer limits.

Customize Cheer

There are a variety of different Cheermotes to choose from. The higher the number of Bits, the cooler and more expressive the animation.

To see additional options including custom Partner Cheermotes,(or one of several Cheermotes based on popular global emotes), select the number of Bits you want to use from the menu, or edit the message to type in a custom amount of Bits. Send your Cheer by hitting enter or send!

Gem Cheermotes are default gems.

Custom Partner Cheermotes are available to Partners. If a channel has custom Cheermotes enabled, they will appear to the right of the default Cheermote gem in the Cheermote menu. To cheer with a streamer’s custom Cheermote, select it in the Bits card, or type the Partner’s custom Cheermote prefix + any amount of Bits in chat.

Global emote Cheermotes are animated versions of your favorite default emotes. Cheer with animated Kappa, Kreygasm, Swiftrage, 4Head, PJSalt, MrDestructoid, NotLikeThis, FailFish, and VoHiYo with many more. To Cheer with Kappa, just type Kappa and the number of Bits you want to use into chat, e.g. Kappa5000. An animated version of the Kappa emote will appear in chat.

Pinned Cheers

You can pin your cheer to the top of chat, if the streamer has this feature enabled. Pin duration scales with the amount of Bits cheered.

The option to pin is disabled if your cheer is below the channel’s minimum threshold.

Your Cheering History

Visit your Bits History for a record of your Cheering activity and Bits use. Use this record to see where your Bits have gone. The tab to the left, Payments History, contains additional information about your purchases.

Learn more in this article referring to our Guide to Bits History.

Cheering Rewards

As you Cheer in a channel, you earn rewards including custom Bits chat badges, leaderboard position, and exclusive emotes.

For further explanation on custom Bit Badges, reward slots, FAQ and more, visit Custom Bit Badge and Emote Reward Slots and Emote Slots.

Cheering: for Moderators

All Cheers and Cheer messages appear in chat – including when chat is in sub-only or slow mode – unless the Cheerer is banned or timed out.

However, all Cheer messages are fully moderatable, and subject to Auto-Mod. Channel owners and their moderators can ban or timeout any chat comment, even if it includes Bits. Note that bans and timeouts will delete the Cheer message as it would a chat message, but Bits that are used cannot be unused.

Ways to ensure unwanted Cheer messages are removed:
  • All Cheer messages will follow banned words lists already in place (global and channel).
  • Banned and timed out users will not be able to use Bits to send Cheer messages.
  • You can also moderate Cheer messages or have your moderators do so for you in the same manner as regular chat messages. Remove by clicking on the user and selecting the timeout or ban symbol or by typing /clear to clear the chat and remove all messages from the chat room, /timeout username seconds in the chat box to purge the message, or /ban username to ban the user from the channel.
  • If overlays are used, the overlay provider may have a way for the broadcaster to dismiss Cheer messages or to preview these messages before they show up on stream.

Frequently Asked Questions

I’m having issues with my Bits purchase, what should I do?
Sorry to hear you’re having trouble! Visit our Bits Purchase Troubleshooting guide here for more help:
I can’t Cheer in a certain channel. What should I do?
First, make sure the channel you’re attempting to cheer in is that of a monetized streamer by looking for a subscription button. Second, make sure that you are not bypassing any limits set by the channel owner on total Bits per Cheer, or minimum Cheermote. Finally, verify that you do not reside in a country that does not support Bits. Additionally, if you have been banned from chat by the channel’s moderation team or streamer, or if your account has a chatting suspension, you will not be able to Cheer. Learn more about account enforcements and chat bans.

If after trying these options you still do not find success, please contact us at Twitch Support.

What is the distinction between Bits and Cheering?
Viewers buy and use Bits to Cheer. Cheers are chat messages that include Bits.
Can I Cheer when using Twitch on mobile web?
No, Cheering is not available when using mobile web. However, Cheering is available in the Twitch Mobile App.
Do I need to subscribe to Cheer or purchase Bits?
No, Cheering is a way to support a channel even if you are not subscribed. By Cheering, you may participate in chat, earn a chat badge, or help kick off a Hype Train!
A channel I am watching has a Cheermote minimum. My total Cheer exceeds this limit. Why can’t I complete my Cheer?
Streamers can set two different limits: a Minimum Bits to Cheer (the minimum total Bits required to send a Cheer message) and a Minimum Bits Emote (the smallest Bit emote that can be used). The Cheermote minimum applies per emote, not for the entire Cheer.

For example, if a streamer’s Cheermote minimum is 100, you could not cheer25 cheer25 cheer25 cheer25 for a total of 100 Bits. One single Cheermote would need to be 100 Bits, so Cheer100 or higher.

I sent a Cheer message, but my message disappeared! What gives?
Your message may have been held by Moderators reviewing chat, or it may have scrolled past quickly in a busy chat. To confirm your Cheer went through, check your Bits History for a record of the transaction. If the Cheer appears in your history, it was successfully processed — even if you didn’t see it in chat. If it does not appear in your Bits History, the transaction may not have completed. Try again, and if the issue persists, contact Twitch Support.
My Cheer message did not appear on the streamer’s overlay. Why might that be?
Overlays and alerts are managed by the streamer using third-party tools. Not all streamers use overlays, and those who do may configure them to display only certain Cheer amounts or types. If your Cheer does not appear on the overlay, it does not mean your Bits were lost. Check your Bits History to confirm the Cheer was processed.
Do I have to use Bits? Can I support a streamer in other ways?
Yes, viewers are free to support streamers in other ways, including third-party services and tools. We understand how important these services are to a streamer’s livelihood and to creating interactions between them and their communities. Our focus as an organization is making sure that our streamers succeed. We believe that Cheering provides a completely new value to the Twitch community, and our goal is to take your feedback and make it a critical component to a streamer’s success.
Does Cheering support third-party integrations?
Absolutely! Third parties can build cool stuff around Cheering through chat messages and through Twitch’s PubSub system.
Are there restrictions to using Bits?
Yes, Bits are subject to our Acceptable Use Policy. Bits have no monetary value, so users cannot make a purchase, donate, or tip with Bits.
How do I give feedback about Cheering or Bits?
If you would like to send us feedback, ask a question, share an idea, request, random thought, or report a bug, please submit it here!

How to Contact an Extension Developer

Twitch does not support Extensions. For help, contact the developer directly via your Extensions Manager. Generally, developers wish to hear from you, so make sure you contact them for specific assistance.

Extensions are third-party apps that are developed using Twitch APIs, but not managed by Twitch. If you need to report an issue or contact the Extension developer, you can do so from the details page of any Extension.

Overlay or Component Extensions

For Extensions that utilize a video overlay or component, hover over the video player. If the channel you’re viewing is Extension Enhanced, you will see the Extension bar on the right side of the player.

Using these controls, you can hide or report the Extension, or add it to your own channel.

Contact information for the developer can by found by selecting “Add to my Channel” and opening the Extension’s info page. Take this step for troubleshooting problems, as Twitch Support cannot assist with Extension troubleshooting.

Only report Extensions when their content or conduct violates the Twitch Terms of Service.

Panel Extensions

Some panel Extensions allow you to manage their settings from the panels below a channel’s video player. Below the panel you will find a bar that contains the name of the Extension.

Click the name of the Extension to be taken to the Extension details page. The details page displays information about the Extension, including a contact method for the developer which you can use to provide feedback or report an issue.

Click the 3 Vertical Dots to see more information about the Extension and access the report tool by clicking the flag.

Only report Extensions that are violating the Twitch Terms of Service. For issues with a specific Extension, or problems, use the Extension page’s contact page to contact the developer.

Mobile Extensions

If enabled, you will see a mobile Extension’s icon under the video player. To report or contact the developers, select the 3 Vertical Dots menu icon and select the Report or View Details option. You also can control whether or not this Extension has access to your information.

Frequently Asked Questions

I contacted a developer with a question and there was a problem with their contact information.

Contact Twitch Support and send us a link to the Extension in the Extension store. Let us know the specific developer contact email that you encountered issues with.

I spent Bits in Extensions, or made some other purchase and am having an issue.

Please contact the Extension developer directly.

How to Contact Twitch Support

Need help? Contact Twitch Support 24/7 via email at help.twitch.tv/s/contactsupport.

We usually provide an initial response within 24 hours. However, some issues do require additional time for us to respond. For fastest assistance, monitor your email in case we need more information from you.

How to Contact Support

  • All users, logged in or out, should visit our help form
  • If you have a Twitch account, click Log In at the top-right of the page or in the middle of the Contact Us form. Make sure that you provide the correct username for the account you are attempting to recover, so we can verify your account ownership.

If you don’t have a Twitch account, you can still file a ticket. Just complete the required fields, including selecting the Category and Sub-Category related to your issue. You can skip the Login button.

  • Add additional information about the issue you are experiencing
  • Submit your ticket

Twitch Partners or Affiliates may contact Twitch Support via Live Chat, instead of filing an email ticket.

  • Click Login at the top-right of the page.
  • Click the circular chat icon at the bottom-right of the page.
  • Start the conversation!

If you’re already chatting with our virtual assistant, you can request a transfer to a live specialist directly in that conversation.

Self-Help Guidance

Search your question in the help center, or browse for articles in our topic catalog.

If a help article doesn’t answer your question, let us know. You can:

  • File a ticket, especially if you still need further help. Select Contact Support at the bottom of any article, and then follow the steps above.
  • At the bottom of the page, mark the article as Not Helpful. Choose Missing Information, and let us know what you were looking for.
  • Let us know on UserVoice .

If you did find the answer you were looking for, we appreciate the feedback. You can click Like on an article.

Self-Help Tools

Account Access Recovery: Use our recovery tool if you need help logging into your Twitch account.

Data Request: You can request your data from Twitch.

Broadcast Issues: Check out Twitch Inspector for rich broadcast troubleshooting information.

Frequently Asked Questions

When can I expect a response to my ticket?
If you’ve filed an email ticket, usually we provide our initial response within 24 hours. However, some issues do require additional time for us to respond. If you’re a Twitch Partner or Affiliate using Live Chat, someone should be with you as soon as we’re able.
It’s urgent! What can I do?
For help with immediate safety issues during a live stream, use Twitch’s on-site reporting tools instead of contacting Twitch Support. You can report live streams, past broadcasts (VODs), chat messages, user profiles/channels, Whispers, and more. Twitch provides many safety tools for viewers, streamers, and community members that can help mitigate harm of immediate issues. Learn more.

If your issue relates to stream playback, broadcast health, network quality, or troubleshooting audio or video issues, browse our self-help guides (Broadcast Guidelines, Guide to Twitch Inspector, Playback Issue Troubleshooting). Twitch Support may not be able to help you with detailed broadcast or network troubleshooting. Twitch Inspector is a great self-help tool available to all users to diagnose broadcast issues.

If the urgent issue relates to account access or unrecognized charges, we’ll be in touch as soon as possible. We may ask for additional identification or clarification of your issue to process your request further. Please monitor your email for any response we may send.

For all other matters, we’ll get to your case as soon as possible and usually within 24 hours. Creating duplicate requests does not accelerate response time.

I forgot to add important information in my support request. What should I do?
Don’t worry - if you need to add more information after you filed your ticket, you can let us know by replying to the confirmation email after your initial ticket. Please do not create another new ticket.
The help form is signed in to the wrong account, or I can’t log in. What should I do?

For your security, we can only discuss account details when you contact us from the account the request is about.

  • Signed in to a different account: Open a private or incognito browser window, log in to the account you need help with, then submit your request.
  • Can’t log in: Open the help form in a private or incognito window, skip logging in, and enter the username and email address for that account.
I need help about a suspension or appeal decision. What should I do?
For assistance regarding suspensions and appeals, visit our Appeals Portal instead of contacting Twitch Support.

How to Delete and Manage Clips

In this guide you will learn how to delete clips you have made, and clips made of your channel.

How to Manage Clips

Visit your Clips Manager from your Creator Dashboard (Content ->Clips)

Here, clips are presented in a table along with relevant information like the title, channel of the creator featured, the streaming category, when it was created, and the number of times it’s been viewed.

Sort clips by views and recency by clicking the corresponding column header. You can also filter clips by category or channel by using a keyword in the search bar.

Clicking on a clip provides a number of options. You can Moderate, Delete, Share, or Watch the clip. You can also edit the clip title.

Toggle between Clips I’ve Created or Clips of My Channel at the top of the screen.

Optimize clips of your channel for sharing on social media with the Clip Editor. Learn more in our guide: link.twitch.tv/HowtoClip

How to Delete Clips

If a clip you created has been featured, it must be unfeatured before you can delete it.

To delete a clip you’ve created, or clip of your channel:

  • Visit the Clips Manager in your Creator Dashboard (Content->Clips)
  • Click on the clip you wish to delete
  • Click the Trash Can icon
  • Click Delete if you wish for this clip to be permanently deleted

To delete multiple clips you’ve created, or clips of your channel:

  • Click the checkbox next to each clip in your Clips Manager
  • Click Delete Selected

To delete all the clips you have created, or of your channel:

  • Click the 3 Vertical Dots menu (located upper-right)
  • Select Delete All Clips of My Channel

Deleting clips is permanent, and cannot be undone.

Clips of My Channel

Unique to Clips of My Channel are Moderation options, located under the sword icon.

Option

Description

Timeout User (24 hr.)

Ban the creator of the clip from your channel for 24 hours.

Ban User

Ban the creator of the clip from your channel.

Followers Only

When enabled, followers must follow you for the specified amount of time before they are allowed to make clips of your channel.

Subscribers Only

Only allow subscribers to make clips of your channel.

Delete All Clips From Video

This will remove every clip made from the original broadcast.

To delete multiple clips at a time, click the checkbox next to each clip and then click Delete Selected, which should have appeared at the top of the table. To delete all the clips of your channel, click the 3 Vertical Dots menu icon above the top right corner of the table, and you will see the option to Delete All Clips of My Channel. This option will permanently delete all clips ever made of your content, so please be absolutely sure before choosing this option.

If you’ve assigned the Editor role to someone, they’ll also be able to review, search, sort, and delete (including mass delete) clips on your behalf. For more information, please see our knowledge guide: link.twitch.tv/ManagingRoles

How to Earn the Social Media Badge

Content in this article is relevant to all streamers regardless of monetization status and their viewers. This feature is currently in Beta. Learn more.

The social media badge is a channel-level badge that recognizes viewers who share clips on social media and helps their favorite streamers go viral. The badge shows other viewers in chat that you helped the creator’s clips get discovered off Twitch.

The badge is progressive, and has 3 levels. Each level is unlocked by reaching a new viewership milestone and provides recognition for the support to the streamer’s content.

Who Can Earn the Social Media Badge?

The Social Media Badge can be earned by any viewer in a channel where viewer exports are enabled. The viewer must not be banned in the channel, and must not block or be blocked by the streamer. Learn more.

How to Earn the Social Media Badge

To earn the social media badge, share clips from participating streamers on TikTok, Instagram or YouTube, then let us know by submitting the links to your posts. We’ll keep track of how many views your social posts get, and award you with a badge when the total view count across all your social posts, per streamer, reaches the view count threshold.

Once you submit the link to us, you can lean back and relax while we continue to monitor views for you. Your badge upgrades as you get more views!

Step 1: Share Clips on Social Media

Share clips from participating channels on your linked social media accounts. You can download the clip, or share a link. Learn more.

Step 2: Submit your Posts

Visit our viewer submission form here, and submit the social media post URL. You’ll need to tell us which streamer is featured in the clip.

If you haven’t already linked your Twitch account to your social media accounts, you’ll be prompted to do so before you can submit.

To help you track your total view count progress towards badge levels, a summary of your submitted posts is available just below the submission field. Progress is shared across all clips and social media platforms.

Equip Your Badge

Once you reach the viewcount threshold, we’ll notify you when a badge is available. You can then equip the badge and it’s yours to keep.

Posts must be from the same social media account linked to your Twitch account. Posts cannot be older than 30 days when submitted. View counts are updated every 2 days to track your progress towards badge levels.

Badge Levels
  • Icon: Earned at 100 total views across your shared clips, per streamer.
  • Pro: Earned at 10,000 total views across your shared clips, per streamer.
  • Legend: Earned at 100,000 total views across your shared clips, per streamer.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I submit social posts of any channel’s clips to earn the Social Media badge?
No, the channel must have viewer exports enabled on clips to participate. Participating channels feature a banner below the video player indicating social media badges can be earned for viral posts of its clip content. However, this banner may not always be visible, if the channel is running certain other promotions at the same time. If a channel’s name does not appear when searching in the submission form, they are not participating.
How long do I have to earn Social Media badges?
During the beta period, all streamers are eligible to participate by enabling viewer exports of clips in their Clip Settings. After the beta period, participants can still keep any badges earned.
Which social media platforms are supported?
Currently, YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram are supported. You must link your accounts for these platforms to your Twitch account to participate. To do so, visit your account settings here.
Am I eligible to earn the Social Media badge?
You’re eligible if you’re a subscriber or have been following a participating channel for at least 3 months, and the channel has viewer exports enabled. The feature is currently in Beta with select channels.
What is the difference between the Top Clipper badges, and the Social Media badges?
Top Clipper badges are awarded for clipping the most-viewed clip in a channel during a leaderboard cycle, where the views are on the Twitch clip itself. Social Media badges are awarded for sharing clips on social media, and those social media posts gaining certain thresholds of views, where the views are on the social media platform itself.
How are views counted toward my badge progress?
View counts are pulled directly from the social media platforms where you posted, using those companies’ public APIs. Views are updated regularly (approximately every two days) without you needing to do anything!
How long does it take to receive the badge after earning it?
Badges are awarded automatically when you reach the view thresholds. The badge will appear in your chat badge selection the next time you visit the channel where you earned it. We’ll also send you a notification when you’ve earned a new badge!
What are the rules for submitting social media posts?
Posts must be from your linked social media account, cannot be older than 30 days, and cannot have been previously submitted.
Can the same clip be submitted by multiple users?
Yes, the same clip can be submitted by multiple users. However, the same social media post cannot be submitted by multiple users. Only the individual who posted it to social media can submit that post to us.
Can I earn the Social Media Badge for sharing a clip that someone else created?
Yes! You do not need to be the original creator of a clip. You can share any clip, regardless of who created it. So long as you’re the one who shared it on social media, you can submit it to us for view count progress tracking towards badge levels.
Can I wear my Social Media badge on other channels?
No, the Social Media badge is a channel badge. This means you can only equip it in the channel where you earned it. If you share clips for multiple participating channels, you’ll earn separate badges for each.
Will I lose my Social Media badge, once I earn it?
No. Once you earn the Social Media badge, it is yours to keep.
I’m having issues with my Social Media badge. How can I get help?
For technical issues with badge display or submission problems, contact Twitch Support with details about your account, the channel, and the specific issue you’re experiencing.

How to Link Your Amazon and Twitch Accounts

You must link your Amazon and Twitch accounts to access Prime Member Perks page on Twitch, including your monthly free Twitch channel subscription, chat color options, emoticons, and chat badge.

Link Your Accounts

Follow these steps to connect your Amazon and Twitch accounts from your settings page:

  • Visit the Prime Member Perks page
  • Select Connect
  • Sign in to your Amazon account when prompted

Follow these steps to connect your Amazon and Twitch accounts from a channel page:

  • Open the Support Panel
  • Select Sign Up
  • Select Connect
  • Sign in to your Amazon account when prompted

When you connect your Amazon account, profile information from your Amazon account (including your name) may be used by Twitch. Twitch will not publicly display your Amazon account information.

You may need to refresh the channel page to use your Prime subscription.

Unlink Your Accounts

To disconnect your Amazon and Twitch accounts:

  • Visit the Prime Member Perks page, or your connections settings
  • Select Disconnect

Unlinking your accounts will remove access to all Prime Member Perks page on Twitch, including your monthly free channel subscription, exclusive emotes, and Prime chat badge.

Troubleshooting

If you’re having trouble linking your accounts, try these steps:

  • Clear your browser cache and cookies, then try linking again
  • Try a different browser or use an incognito/private browsing window
  • Disable browser extensions that might interfere with the connection process
  • Ensure you’re signed into the correct Amazon account that has an active Prime membership

Need Additional Help?

For issues with account linking, or using your Prime perks once your accounts are linked, Prime membership status, or billing questions, contact Amazon Customer Support directly. Amazon handles all Prime-related account and subscription issues.

Twitch Support cannot assist with Amazon account or Prime membership problems.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why can’t I use my Prime subscription on my iOS device?
At this time, Prime channel subscriptions cannot be redeemed directly in the Twitch app on iOS devices. Depending on your region, you may able to redeem your Prime subscription by redirecting to subs.twitch.tv in your mobile browser. If this option is available, you’ll see it when you select the Subscribe button when viewing a channel.
Why do I need to link my Amazon and Twitch accounts?
Linking your accounts is required to access Prime Member Perks page on Twitch, including your monthly free channel subscription, exclusive emotes, expanded chat colors, and the Prime member chat badge.
Can I use a Prime Trial to get a free Twitch subscription?
Depending on your region, Prime Trial members (including Prime Student) may be eligible to receive one free Twitch channel subscription during their no-cost trial. This is a one-time perk — it can only be redeemed once, even if you start a new trial later. If you’ve previously redeemed a free Twitch subscription through a Prime Trial, you will not be eligible again during subsequent trials.
What information does Twitch access from my Amazon account?
Twitch may use profile information from your Amazon account, including your name, but will not publicly display your Amazon account information.
I’m getting an error when trying to link my accounts. What should I do?
Try the troubleshooting steps above first. If the issue persists, contact Amazon Customer Support as they handle all Prime membership and account linking issues.
Can I link multiple Amazon accounts to one Twitch account?
No, you can only link one Amazon account to your Twitch account at a time. To link a different Amazon account, you must first unlink your current one.
Will unlinking my accounts cancel my Prime membership?
No, unlinking only removes access to Prime perks on Twitch. Your Amazon Prime membership remains active. Contact Amazon Customer Support for Prime membership questions.
Who should I contact if I have problems with my Prime membership?

Contact Amazon Customer Support for Prime membership issues, billing questions, or account problems. Twitch Support cannot assist with Amazon account or Prime membership matters.

If you believe your Prime subscription was redeemed to a channel without your permission (for example, you see a subscription you didn’t make), contact Twitch Support to report unauthorized use of your Prime token.

How to Opt-Out of the DJ Program

Per the DJ Program Terms, participation in the DJ program is voluntary. You may opt out of the DJ program via your Creator Dashboard or, if this option is not currently available, contact Customer Support.

About Account Types

Certain account types on Twitch have certain permissions, abilities, and access to certain features and tools.

After opt-out, DJ account status indicators are removed immediately, including access to the Twitch DJ Music Catalog and DJ badge. If you are a monetized streamer, Music Costs deductions will no longer apply at 12AM UTC the day after you opt-out. Your prior VOD, Clips, Highlights, and Upload storage settings will be restored. Refer to the table below for full details.

Opting Out

Re-Joining

Allowed to stream tracks from the DJ Music Catalog.

Existing VODs, Clips, and Highlights remain available. (Uploads not available to non-monetized accounts).

Future VODs, Highlights, and Uploads are disabled. Clips are enabled but must not contain music from the DJ Music Catalog.

DJ badge available to be equipped in chat and visible on channel page.

No longer allowed to stream tracks from the DJ Music Catalog. If you live-stream DJ sets outside this program without rights to do so, you expose yourself to risk of DMCA takedowns and/or account enforcement.

Future VODs, Clips, and Highlights are enabled

DJ badge removed as equipable option, and from channel page.

Affiliate or Affiliate/Developer**

DJ Badge removed (from channel and chat badge option)

Future monetization not subject to earnings share

About secondary accounts: If a secondary account you control was granted Partner or Affiliate status as part of the DJ program, opting out of the DJ Program will remove the status from that secondary account. The account status of your secondary account will be updated 30 days after you opt out. You will need to contact Twitch Support to opt out.

Opt Into the DJ Program

After opting-out, you can decide to re-enroll in the DJ Program at any time. However, the Affiliate or Partner status of your secondary account is not automatically reinstated. Refer to Secondary Accounts and the DJ Program help article for additional detail

*Opting Into the DJ Program means you agree to be bound by the DJ Program Terms.

**Affiliates and Partners may also join the Developer program at Twitch (Affiliate/Developer, Partner/Developer).

Creator Dashboard Self-Service

Follow the instructions below to opt-out of the DJ Program from your Creator Dashboard.

If your secondary account was granted Partner or Affiliate status as part of the DJ Program, you will need to contact Twitch Support to opt out rather than using the self-service option.

  • Visit the DJ page in your Creator Dashboard
  • On this page, select Opt-out of DJ Program.
  • Click to Opt-Out

Contact Twitch Support

Contact Twitch Support if the option to opt-out via the Creator Dashboard is not currently available, or if you encounter any issues using the automated process.

You must file a ticket from the account that is currently enrolled in the DJ Program.

  • Click here to open a case with Twitch Support.
  • Choose Category -> DJ Program, Sub-Category -> General Questions.
  • In the ticket body, let us know you want to opt out of the DJ Program.
