How to Provide Feedback

There are a few different ways you can provide Twitch with feedback, report a bug, participate in brand surveys, or inquire about issues.

If Something Seems Broken…

If something appears broken or not working the way it should, try these basic troubleshooting steps. For playback issues (audio and video) visit our dedicated troubleshooting guide here.

On web:

  • Refresh your tab or web page
  • Check for updates to your web browser
  • Quit and re-open your browser

On mobile:

  • Quit and re-open the app
  • Check for updates to the Twitch Mobile App

If you’re still encountering an issue, report it to us at help.twitch.tv. Choose the category option that best fits the issue. It helps to include a screenshot replicating the issue. You can also send us console error information.

How to Send Error Information:

On Google Chrome:

  • Open your developer console in Chrome. You can do this one of three ways:
    • Right-click your mouse. Choose Inspect
    • Press F12,
    • In the upper right-hand of your browser, select 3 Vertical Dots menu icon > More tools > Tools > Developer Tools,
    • or Press Ctrl + Shift + I
  • Navigate to the Console and Network tabs of your tools.
  • In each window, refresh the page you are having issues with (press F5).
  • Let each page load
  • Screenshot any errors in red
  • Send error log screenshots to us.

On Mozilla Firefox:

  • Open your developer console in Firefox. You can do this one of three ways:
    • Right-click your mouse. Choose Inspect
    • Press F12,
    • Go to Hamburger menu icon (or Tools) > Web Developer > Toggle Tools,
    • or Press Ctrl + Shift + I
  • Navigate to the Network tab of your tools.
  • In that window, load the page you are having issues with (press F5).
  • Let the page load, then sort by Status.
  • Screenshot any errors in red
  • Send error log screenshots to us

You can also check our status page or @ us on Twitter.

How to Redeem Drops Codes and Rewards

Drops campaigns offer rewards to Twitch users for taking certain actions on Twitch. Twitch works with companies like Roblox, Discord, Duolingo, or Crunchyroll (and more!) where watching streams or subscribing to certain channels can earn you a code to redeem on that partner company’s website or service.

In this guide, we’ll explain how to claim these code-based rewards that require manual entry on a third-party or partner website.

Twitch Support can only help with issues that occur on Twitch (earning and claiming rewards). For issues with redeeming codes on partner websites or rewards not appearing in games, you must contact the promotional partner directly. You can find their contact info in your Drops Inventory page

For questions on redeeming in-game items automatically delivered to your connected game accounts, visit our guide here.

Who Can Help You?

Need help with drops and rewards? Before you start troubleshooting, it’s important to know who to contact for help:

Twitch Support CAN Help With:

Twitch Support CANNOT Help With:

  • Earning or qualifying for Drops on Twitch
  • Claiming rewards from your Drops Inventory
  • Receiving your redemption code from Twitch
  • Understanding campaign requirements

Contact Twitch Support: link.twitch.tv/Contact-Us

  • Redeeming codes on partner websites
  • Codes not working on partner sites
  • Rewards not appearing in games or apps
  • Issues with partner website functionality
  • Expired or already-used codes

Contact the promotional partner directly. Find their contact info on your Drops Inventory page.

In other words.. if your issue happens on Twitch (earning, claiming, receiving codes), contact Twitch Support. If your issue happens off Twitch (redeeming codes, rewards not appearing in games), contact the promotional partner.

Types of Drops Rewards

Your Drops Inventory page shows all available campaigns and clearly indicates which type of reward is offered. No matter which reward type is offered, you must meet the requirements to earn the reward.

Type 1: Automatic In-Game Rewards

Type 2: Code-Based Rewards

When the requirement is met, go to your Drops Inventory page to claim the rewards. After claiming, the rewards are automatically added to your connected game account.

Reward Examples: In-game items, skins, or currency that appear directly in your game inventory.

How to Redeem: No additional steps required after (1) completing the drop requirements on Twitch and (2) claiming from the Drops Inventory page on Twitch.

After taking these two steps, if the reward does not appear in your connected game account, contacted the game developer or promotional partner, not Twitch. You can find the promotional partner’s contact info in your Drops Inventory page.

When the requirement is met, you receive a notification from Twitch delivering a unique redemption code, to enter on a partner website or app.

Reward Examples: Early access or beta codes for video games, codes for in-game items, checkout discount codes and more.

How to Redeem: Manual entry required on partner website or app.

In this guide, we’ll talk about Type 2 code-based rewards.

How to Redeem Codes

Exact redemption steps vary by campaign. Check your Drops Inventory page for specific reward redemption details.

Common redemption locations may include an external (not managed by Twitch) Redeem / Enter Code webpage provided by the company or promotional partner, a checkout page or shopping cart when completing a purchase, or another settings page designated by the company or promotional partner delivering the reward. Code formats may vary.

Some rewards or offers may require subscription sign-up with a credit card. Check your Drops Inventory page for specific reward redemption details.

Troubleshooting

The issues described in this section are meant to give a general series of steps that you can take to try and resolve an issue. Check your Drops Inventory page for specific details of the campaign you’re having issues with if these steps do not help.

Depending on the specific issue you’re facing, if these troubleshooting steps do not resolve your issue, you should contact Twitch Support or the promotional partner directly.

Code Not Received

If you have not received the reward code after fulfilling the requirements, double-check the specifics of the campaign and ensure you’re following the necessary qualification steps.

If you’re 100% sure you’ve fulfilled the requirements, contact Twitch Support so we can take a closer look!

Code Not Working

If you enter the code into the promotional website and there is no response, check for any typos, that the code has not expired, or that you reside within an eligible territory.

Contact the promotional partner for further assistance. These details would be available in your Drops Inventory page.

Why can’t Twitch Support help? Twitch delivers the code to you, but the promotional partner controls whether codes work on their website. Only they can troubleshoot redemption issues, reactivate expired codes, or grant rewards.

Code Already Used

Each reward code can typically only be used once. Check if the reward was already applied to your account.

Contact the promotional partner for further assistance. Their details would be available in your Drops Inventory page

Why can’t Twitch Support help? Once you’ve successfully redeemed a code on a partner website, Twitch’s role is complete. Only the game developer or promotional partner can grant in-game items or troubleshoot their delivery systems.

Frequently Asked Questions

What’s the difference between automatic Drops rewards and code-based Drops rewards?
Automatic Drops are added directly to your connected game account when claimed. Code-based rewards provide a redemption code that you must manually enter on a third-party website or app.
How can I tell if a campaign offers automatic rewards, or code-based rewards?
In your Drops Inventory page, the campaigns you’re currently tracking towards will specify the reward type.
Why do I need to redeem codes on other websites?
Some of our partners prefer to handle redemption through their own systems, which allow them to ensure a better experience for you.
What do I do if my code expires before I can use it?
Expired codes can’t be reactivated. Check your Drops Inventory page for specific details of the campaign you are trying to earn rewards for, including any expiration dates.
What do I do if there’s an issue with the third-party / external website?
Check your Drops Inventory page for contact information of that company. You may need to contact them for further assistance.
Who do I contact for help with Drops issues?
Contact Twitch Support if:
  • You didn’t receive your code from Twitch after completing requirements
  • You can’t claim a reward from your Drops Inventory
  • You’re unsure if you qualified for a campaign

Contact Twitch Support here

Contact the promotional partner if:
  • Your code doesn’t work on their website
  • The code says “already used” or “invalid”
  • You redeemed the code but didn’t receive the reward
  • The partner website has technical issues

Find partner contact information on your Drops Inventory page.

How to Use Emotes

What’s that emote? Emotes are images that appear in chat, and play a big part in the chat experience on Twitch. This guide will explain what emotes are, and how to use them.

What Are Emotes?

Emotes are small pictures that are used in place of a word or comment to express the emotion of the individual posting the emote.

Some examples of Twitch emotes include:

Name

Emote

Meaning

Kappa

Sarcasm or wry humor. Kappa is our signature emote.

HeyGuys

A casual greeting. Used when joining chat, or when welcoming someone to a stream.

LUL

Laughter. The emote version of Laugh Out Loud.

Jebaited

For when someone is “baited or tricked”. Often used in games where the player is surprised or lured into a trap.

This is not a complete list of Twitch emotes. Emotes are a unique language created, adopted by, and forever evolving alongside the community.

How to Get Emotes

There are multiple ways to obtain emotes for use in Twitch chat.

Global Emotes

Global Emotes are emotes that every user on Twitch has access to.

Learn more about Global Emotes in our guide: help.twitch.tv/s/article/global-emotes

Follower Emotes

Follower Emotes are custom emotes that can be unlocked for free by following a qualifying streamer, Partner, or Affiliate channel that has them available. Viewers will see a call out in Chat once Follower Emotes have been added.

Call out as seen by a viewer that hasn’t followed the channel

Call out as seen by a viewer that’s already following

Thanks to your feedback, Follower Emotes can now be used by subscribers in any channel on Twitch. Followers who are not subscribers may continue to use Follower Emotes only within that channel itself.

Qualifying streamers, Partners, and Affiliates can learn more about uploading Follower Emotes in our guide here: help.twitch.tv/s/article/follower-emotes

Subscription Emotes

Subscriber emotes are custom emotes that can be unlocked by subscribing to an qualifying streamer, Partner, or Affiliate channel that has them available. Viewers who have active subscriptions to their channel will have access to their custom emotes. Subscriber emotes can be used across any channel at Twitch.

Your subscription tier will determine which of the channel emotes you will have access to.

Bits Tier Emotes

Bits Tier Emotes are custom emotes that can be unlocked by Cheering certain Bits amounts in qualifying streamers, Partners, and Affiliates channels that have Bits enabled. Qualifying streamers, Partners, and Affiliates can learn more about Bits Badge Emote Rewards in our guide: help.twitch.tv/s/article/custom-bit-badges-guide

Event Emotes

Event emotes can be unlocked by participating in celebrations or events within a channel, like Hype Train. Other event emotes can be earned during Twitch events like the Glitch emote Drops from GlitchCon 2020.

Some event emotes are temporary. Some can be used across all channels on Twitch. Most do not require a purchase to unlock, but may require event participation, or another action.

How to Use Emotes

Using emotes in chat is easy whether you use Twitch on desktop or the Twitch mobile app.

Selecting From Your Emotes

In the chat box, click or tap the Emotes icon to open the emotes picker. The emote picker shows emotes available to you.

Once you have found the emote you want to post, click or tap to place it in the chat field. Send your chat message.

Sometimes an emote is worth a thousand words. You can send an emote alone, or add other text.

Use Emote Code

You can type the name of an emote if you prefer not to make a selection from the emote picker.

To do this, type a colon : in chat and begin to type an emote name. A list of available emotes will populate for you.

Select the emote you want, and continue any addition you want to add to your comment. Then post like you would for any other comment in chat.

Frequently Asked Questions

How can I get a certain emote?
Interact with an emote to see information on where it is from, and how to get it. On desktop, click the emote. In the Twitch mobile app, tap the emote.
I should have access to an emote but don’t. What do I do?

All Emotes - Make sure you have onboarded to monetization in order to access emotes. Follow the steps here to complete.

Global Emotes - Contact Twitch Support here with details on the Global Emote you believe you are missing.

Custom Emotes (Follower/Bits Tier/Subscriber Emotes) - Make sure you have followed the channel in question, Cheered the required amount of Bits, or successfully subscribed to the channel. If you are sure of these steps, contact Twitch Support here with details of the emote you are missing.

Event Emotes - Depending on the event, there could be different requirements to unlock. Contact Twitch Support here with details of the event you believe you participated in.

For Hype Train emote questions, visit our guide: help.twitch/tv/s/article/hype-train-guide

What do I do if I see an emote that makes me uncomfortable?
Custom emotes must respect Twitch policies, and abide by our Emote Guidelines and the Community Guidelines.

Learn how to report an emote, in our guide: help.twitch.tv/s/article/emote-guidelines

Language on Twitch.tv

To display twitch.tv in your language:

  • Click your profile picture in the top-right hand corner of the website
  • Click Language

Twitch will remember your language selection, and automatically display your language when you log in to the Twitch app on several devices (LG, Samsung, Fire TV, Android TV) and platforms (Nintendo Switch, twitch.tv in a mobile browser).

If you notice a translation error or mistake on our site, please let us know on our UserVoice forum!

When browsing Twitch, you’ll be shown streams that match your site language first, but will also have the option to filter by other languages, or browse all channels regardless of language.

To browse live channels where the streamer is speaking specific languages:

Mobile App Language

To change your Twitch mobile app language, set your language settings within your mobile device. Setting your language on twitch.tv does not impact your Twitch mobile app language.

Console Apps Language

Apple TV, PS4/PS5, and Xbox apps have language settings that are independent of twitch.tv site language or device languages in the Twitch mobile app.

Stream Language

The Stream Language setting can be found on the Stream Manager section of your dashboard, and is not set by Site Language.

To set your stream language:

  • Click the drop-down menu on the Stream Info panel
  • OR, Click Edit Stream Info in Quick Actions

Setting your stream language will apply a label to your channel that will allow people using the site or filtering via that language to find you easily.

If your language isn’t available on the drop down menu, please choose Other.

Add custom tags to your stream to indicate additional languages available to viewers beyond your primary Stream Language. To do this, set your primary stream language and add custom tags for additional languages to communicate to those browsing that you speak these languages.

Invoices Language

When you successfully complete a purchase on Twitch, we email you an invoice.

Depending on the payment provider you use, your invoice language will either be in your site language, or the tax jurisdiction of your payment method. Change your payment method, or your site language to adjust your invoice language.

Managing Your Phone Number

Adding a phone number to your Twitch account adds a layer of security, and some features on Twitch require a verified email address or phone number before you can use them.

In this guide, you will learn how to add, edit, or remove your phone number, and how to use one number on more than one account.

What are you trying to do?

  • Add a phone number for the first time → Adding a Phone Number
  • Change your existing phone number → Editing a Phone Number
  • Use a number that’s already on another account → Using a Phone Number on Multiple Accounts
  • Not receiving the verification code → Not Receiving a Verification Code
  • Remove phone number from account → Deleting a Phone Number

Adding A Phone Number

You can add a phone number even if it’s already linked to another Twitch account. Learn more.

If you don’t have a phone number added to your Twitch account, visit twitch.tv/settings/security.

  • Click Add a number
  • Choose your area code
  • Enter your phone number
  • Click Save
  • Confirm your number

A 6-digit verification code will be sent to the phone number you entered, so make sure it is correct. Message and data fees may apply to messages sent by Twitch.

  • Enter your verification code
  • Success!

Editing A Phone Number

To change your phone number, visit twitch.tv/settings/security.

  • Click the pencil icon next to Phone Number under Contact
  • Choose your area code
  • Enter your phone number
  • Click Save
  • Confirm your number
  • Success!

Deleting A Phone Number

To delete your phone number, visit twitch.tv/settings/security.

  • Click the trash can icon next to your phone number
  • Confirm you wish to delete this number
  • Success!

If this phone number is also linked to other accounts, it’s only removed from this account.

Using a Phone Number on Multiple Accounts

You can add the same phone number to more than one Twitch account. It doesn’t matter which other accounts already have the number, or whether those accounts are active, disabled, or deleted. You don’t need to change any settings on your other accounts. Add the number as usual (see Adding A Phone Number) and enter the code we send.

All of your accounts must follow our Community Guidelines and Terms of Service. Creating a new account to evade an existing suspension is a violation and may result in additional enforcement action.

You Don’t Recognize an Account Linked to Your Number

To see every Twitch account that uses your phone number, use the Account Recovery Tool:

  • Go to twitch.tv/user/account-recovery
  • Select your country code, then enter your phone number
  • Click Continue
  • Click “I Don’t Know My Username”
  • We’ll text you a list of ALL accounts linked to this phone number

If one of these accounts is yours and you’ve forgotten the password, use the password reset tool. If you don’t recognize an account, contact Twitch Support with that username, your phone number, and your current username.

Not Receiving a Verification Code

If your 6-digit code doesn’t arrive, see Not Receiving Verification Codes for step-by-step troubleshooting, including carrier issues and rate limits.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why should I add a phone number to my Twitch account?
Adding a phone number to your Twitch account can provide an additional layer of security. It also gives us another way to contact you with important messages about your account, such as payout information changes, password changes, and login attempts. Plus, some channels require a verified phone number or email be added to your Twitch account before you can send messages.
Why can’t I add a VoIP number to my Twitch account?
For security purposes, Twitch only accepts mobile phone numbers on a cellular network. VoIP numbers (like Google Voice) are not supported.
Can I use the same phone number on multiple Twitch accounts?
Yes. Add and verify the number on each account. You don’t need to change any settings on your other accounts. See Using a Phone Number on Multiple Accounts.
Why can’t I change my phone number without receiving an SMS code?
For security reasons, Twitch requires verification of your current phone number before allowing changes. If you no longer have access to your old number, see our guide: How to Change Your 2FA Phone Number for instructions on using Authy’s Phone Change Form.

Mobile App Troubleshooting

If the Twitch app keeps crashing, won’t open, or a page or button isn’t working on your iOS or Android device, this guide walks you through general troubleshooting steps that resolve most common issues.

This guide is for more general troubleshooting. If you already know the root of your issue, check our guides:

  • Playback Issue Troubleshooting or How to File a Video Playback Issue
  • Low Latency Video
  • Mobile IRL Broadcasting or Mobile Game Broadcasting

General Troubleshooting Steps

Most mobile app issues can be resolved with the steps below. Try them in order.

  • Update the Twitch app. Make sure you’re running the latest version from the App Store (iOS) or Google Play (Android).
  • Update your device’s operating system. Make sure your iOS or Android version is up to date.
  • Try a different network. If you’re on Wi-Fi, switch to mobile data (or vice versa) and try again.
  • Restart the app. Fully close the Twitch app (swipe it away from your recent apps), then reopen it.
  • Restart your device. Power your phone or tablet off completely, wait a moment, then turn it back on.
  • Try the same action somewhere else. See whether the issue also happens on another device, or on twitch.tv in a web browser. This helps show whether the problem is specific to the app on your device.

If your issue is still happening after these steps, try the platform-specific steps below for your device.

iOS: Reinstalling the Twitch App

Reinstalling the app clears out stored data that may be causing problems.

  • In the Twitch app, tap your profile icon, then tap Account Settings. Scroll down and tap Log Out.
  • On your iPhone or iPad, open Settings → General → iPhone Storage (or iPad Storage).
  • Select the Twitch app and tap Delete App. This removes the app and its stored data.
  • Restart your device.
  • Reinstall the Twitch app from the App Store and log back in.

Android: Clearing the App Cache

On Android, clearing the app’s cache and data often resolves issues without a full reinstall.

  • On your Android device, open Settings → Apps (or Manage Applications).
  • Select the Twitch app.
  • Tap Storage (or Storage & cache), then tap Clear Cache. If the issue continues, tap Clear Storage (Clear Data on some devices). This logs you out, so have your login details ready.
  • Reopen the Twitch app and log back in if needed.
  • If the issue continues, uninstall the Twitch app, then reinstall it from Google Play.

Still Need Help?

If you’ve worked through the steps above and the issue is still happening, contact Twitch Support. To help us resolve your issue faster, please include:

  • Your device model and operating system version (for example, iPhone 15 running iOS 18, or Samsung Galaxy S24 running Android 14)
  • The Twitch app version you’re running (iOS: Settings → General → iPhone Storage → Twitch; Android: Settings → Apps → Twitch)
  • A description of what happens, and what you were doing when it happened
  • Which troubleshooting steps you’ve already tried

Frequently Asked Questions

Will clearing the cache or reinstalling the app delete my account or followed channels?
No. Your account and follows are tied to your Twitch account, not the app on your device. Clearing the cache, reinstalling the app, or logging out and back in won’t affect them. Some app preferences saved on your device may reset. You will need to log back in afterward, so have your login details ready.
The app works fine on Wi-Fi but not on mobile data (or the other way around). What does that mean?
This usually points to a network issue rather than a problem with the app. If the issue is on Wi-Fi, restart your router. If it’s on mobile data, your carrier may limit video streaming. See Playback Issue Troubleshooting for carrier streaming limits.
Why does the app work on my phone but not my tablet (or the reverse)?
Each device has its own app version, operating system version, and storage. An issue on one device but not another usually means that device needs an app or OS update, or a cache clear. Run through the general troubleshooting steps on the device that isn’t working.

Navigating the Feedback Forums

This article is part of a series on giving feedback about Twitch.

Does Twitch listen to feedback? Yes! Submit your ideas on how Twitch can improve using our feedback forums. There, Twitch Staff identify trending ideas to surface to various teams within Twitch for consideration as we continually develop and improve Twitch.

While we can’t address or act on every single suggestion we receive, we’ll do our best to provide information in responses when updating statuses.

This article covers how to support ideas you like, and to make your own suggestions.

Feedback Forum Structure & Layout

On the homepage of the feedback forums, there are tiles for different forums that house suggestions for the many features and functions of Twitch.

In general, the structure is forum > category, with ideas within.

  • Forums cover broad aspects of Twitch, such as large features, or a particular function of the website.
  • Categories within that forum focus on particular aspects of that forum.
  • Comments for certain ideas can be found on their individual, detailed view pages.

As an example, ideas relating to finding streamsthrough Twitch’s recommendations on the Front Page, the Browse page, or the Channel List sidebar can be found in the Discovery forum.

Filtering Options

By default, when entering a forum, all ideas will show, regardless of the category they are in, sorted by the highest number of votes (Top Ideas). There are a few other ways to filter Ideas:

Filter by Category

You can narrow in on a specific category within a forum using the left-hand Categories panel.

Filter by Trending

You can filter displayed ideas by New or Hot to explore! A hot idea is one that has a lot of activity in a short period of time - both votes and comments. Although these ideas are really taking off, they don’t necessarily mean that Twitch will take action.

Browse by Status

You can browse Ideas by their status. Learn more: Understanding Feedback Forum Statuses FAQ

Connect Your Twitch Account

Now that you have honed in on the ideas you want to support, you can amplify its potential by voting, or commenting.

Similar to chatting in a channel, the feedback forums rquire a Twitch account to engage (vote or comment on ideas). You do not need a Twitch account to lurk.

  • Click “Twitch” at the top of the screen.
  • Enter your Twitch username/password

You may need to enter a two-factor authorization code to complete account connection.

Vote on an Idea

Now that you have connected your account, vote on an idea you wish to support!

Ideas in certain statuses, such as Closed or Completed cannot be voted on.

Just because an idea might have a high vote count, doesn’t mean that it will necessarily be implemented. Learn more: Understanding Feedback Forum Statuses FAQ

Comment on an Idea

Have something else to add to an idea you voted on?

Click the idea title to be taken to the idea detail page where you can leave a comment (or mosey your way around the conversation of other users).

Reporting a Comment or Idea

Sometimes you might see offensive comments or ideas; and even while there are spam filters in place, some spam might fly under the radar. In both cases, you can report such content. To report an idea, click on its title to navigate to the idea detail page. From there, you will see the option to Report… a Report cue will also appear for each comment.

Translating Feedback in the Forums

Polyglot or not, we have you covered for when you run into ideas in languages that you might not understand. The localization widget translates ideas and comments. To enable it, click on the round button located on the top, right-hand side of the screen (pictured below for reference).

Select your preferred language, and turn on Translate Ideas and Comments. A blue toggle indicates translation is activated. You might notice that the forum/category titles are not supported with this tool (so they’re shown in English, by default).

More Resources

Ready to submit your own ideas? Learn how to give actionable feedback in the Twitch feedback forums. Read our guide: Giving Actionable Feedback in the Feedback Forum

So you posted an idea…. now what? Learn more: Understanding Feedback Forum Statuses FAQ

Was this guide helpful? Let us know with the upvotes or downvotes below.

Not Receiving Verification Codes?

If you’re not receiving SMS text messages, email codes, or 2FA codes from Twitch, the solution depends on why you’re trying to receive the code.

First, identify your situation below. Each scenario has specific troubleshooting steps.

Setting Up 2FA for the First Time

If you’re trying to set up Two-Factor Authentication and not receiving SMS codes:

Check Your Phone Number
  • Verify you entered the correct phone number with country code
  • Make sure it’s a cellular number, not a VoIP number (Google Voice won’t work)
Wait Between Attempts
  • Wait at least 60 seconds before requesting another code
  • Too many requests can trigger rate limiting
About Authenticator Apps

After successfully verifying your phone number via SMS, you can optionally set up an authenticator app (like Authy, Google Authenticator, or Microsoft Authenticator) as an additional verification method. However, SMS verification is required first — you cannot skip SMS setup and go directly to an authenticator app.

If you cannot receive SMS codes at all, the troubleshooting steps above may help. If none of them resolve the issue, contact Twitch Support for assistance with 2FA setup.

Logging In from a New Device

If you’re trying to log in from a new device and not receiving the verification code via email:

Check Your Email
  • Check your spam/junk folder
  • Search for emails from “Twitch” or “no-reply@twitch.tv”
  • Wait 5 minutes - email delivery can be delayed
Verify Your Email Address
  • Make sure you’re checking the correct email address
  • If you disabled your email, you won’t receive codes - re-enable it first
Use “Resend Code”

On the login screen, click the “Resend code” option to request a new code.

Disabled Email? If you disabled your email address, you won’t receive verification codes. You must reactivate your email OR use your phone number for recovery. See Can’t Access Your Account?

Recovering Your Account

If you’re trying to recover your account and not receiving codes:

Check Both Email AND Phone

If you have 2FA enabled, you will only be able to log in with the code provided by your authenticator app or by SMS. Only accounts without 2FA enabled are able to receive recovery codes via email.

  • Recovery codes can be sent to either your email or phone
  • Check both locations, including spam folders
  • Wait 5 minutes for delivery
Verify You’re Using the Correct Username
  • Make sure you’re entering the right username for recovery
  • Use the Account Recovery Tool to find your username
If Neither Email Nor Phone Works

If you’re not receiving codes on either method:

  • Your email may be disabled - re-enable it first
  • Your phone number may have changed - see Can’t Access Your Account?
  • If you’ve lost access to both, see the “Lost Both” section in the account access guide

Getting a 2FA Code to Log In

If you’re trying to log in with 2FA and not receiving codes, start by identifying how you get your codes:

If You Use an Authenticator App (Authy, Google Authenticator, etc.)
  • Open your authenticator app
  • Find your Twitch account in the app
  • Enter the 6-digit code shown
  • Authenticator apps generate codes without internet or cell service, so they work even when SMS won’t
If You Get Codes by SMS (Text Message)
  • Make sure your phone has signal and can receive texts
  • Wait a few minutes, then use the resend option to request a new code
  • If codes still aren’t arriving, see Common Issues (All Scenarios) for delivery problems like carrier delays, spam filtering, and unsupported number types
If You Lost Access to Your Authenticator App
  • Use your backup codes if you saved them when setting up 2FA
  • If you don’t have backup codes, request a code by SMS instead — because SMS is set up first when you enable 2FA, every account can fall back to a text code
If You Lost Your Phone or No Longer Have Your Old Number

If you can’t receive codes by app or SMS because you no longer have access to your phone or old number:

  • Fill out Authy’s Phone Change Form
  • This applies to all Twitch users with 2FA, even if you don’t use the Authy app for authentication
  • Authy will process your request within 24-48 business hours

When you enable 2FA on Twitch, an Authy account is automatically created for you, regardless of which authenticator app you use. Learn more about 2FA and Authy.

Verifying a New Account

If you’re trying to verify a new Twitch account and not receiving codes:

Check Your Email Spam Folder
  • Verification emails often end up in spam
  • Search for “Twitch” or “no-reply@twitch.tv”
  • Mark as “Not Spam” to receive future emails
Verify Phone Number Format
  • Include country code (e.g., +1234567890 or +1-234-567-8900)
  • Must be a cellular number (not VoIP like Google Voice)
Wait Between Attempts
  • Wait at least 60 seconds before requesting another code
  • Too many requests can trigger rate limiting

Common Issues (All Scenarios)

These issues can affect code delivery regardless of your scenario:

SMS Codes Delayed or Never Arrive

If SMS codes arrive hours late or not at all, this can happen due to:

  • Carrier delays - Some mobile carriers have slow SMS delivery, especially during high traffic periods
  • International numbers - Twitch SMS may not reach all countries reliably
  • VoIP numbers - Google Voice, Skype numbers, and other VoIP services don’t receive Twitch SMS
  • Blocked sender - Check if you’ve blocked messages from short codes or unknown senders
  • Carrier spam filters - Some carriers aggressively filter automated messages

Alternative: Use Authenticator App Instead

If SMS is unreliable, switch to an authenticator app for better reliability:

  • Log in to Twitch (if possible)
  • Go to Security Settings
  • Enable “Two-Factor Authentication” with an authenticator app (Authy, Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator)

Can’t log in to change settings? Contact Twitch Support

Carrier Delays
  • SMS delivery can take up to 5 minutes
  • High network traffic can cause delays
  • Carrier spam filters may block messages
Device Settings
  • Turn off “Do Not Disturb” mode
  • Check that you haven’t blocked messages from Twitch
  • Ensure your device has sufficient signal strength
  • Restart your device and try again
VoIP Numbers Not Supported
  • Google Voice, Skype numbers, and other VoIP services don’t work
  • You must use a cellular phone number
Regional Restrictions

Currently, Russia is the only region blocked from SMS for 2FA. Russian users must use an authenticator app instead.

Frequently Asked Questions

What do I do if I’m rate limited?
If you’ve made too many code requests, you’ll need to wait 24 hours before trying again. This is a security measure to prevent abuse.
Why should I use an authenticator app instead of SMS?
Authenticator apps are more reliable than SMS because they work without cell service, can’t be intercepted, and aren’t affected by carrier delays or spam filters. We strongly recommend using an authenticator app for 2FA.
What if I don’t have access to my old phone number anymore?
If you’ve lost access to your phone number, see our guide: Can’t Access Your Account? The solution depends on whether you can still log in and whether you have 2FA enabled.
Can I use a landline for 2FA?
No, 2FA requires a mobile phone number that can receive SMS text messages. Landlines and VoIP numbers (like Google Voice) are not supported.
I’m still not receiving codes after trying everything. What now?
If you’ve tried all the troubleshooting steps for your specific scenario and still aren’t receiving codes, contact Twitch Support for assistance. Include details about which scenario applies to you and what you’ve already tried.

Parental Controls in the Family Center

Parental Controls gives parents visibility into their teen’s activity and the ability to manage key settings. Teens ages 13-17 can invite a parent or guardian to link accounts, giving both parties a shared space to manage oversight. Once the accounts are linked, parents can manage what their teen accesses, how long they spend on Twitch, and stay informed about their activity — all from the Family Center.

How to Link Parent & Teen Accounts

Teens can initiate linking to a parent or guardian’s account through the Family Center page in account settings or during sign up.

Both teen and parent accounts can manually unlink at any time.

As a teen, to link accounts with a parent, begin by logging in to your Twitch account and navigating to settings.

  • Select Family Center
  • Locate the shareable link
  • Copy the link and send to the parent you wish to link accounts with

Once linked, both accounts will appear in the Family Center.

How to Set Parental Controls

Once linked, access the Parental Controls dashboard from the Family Center to toggle settings on or off. Customize anytime to stay flexible around your teen’s life.

Settings to monitor and customize on linked teen accounts include:

  • Streaming & Video Uploads
    • Teens can be prevented from going live and streaming their own content
    • Disable the ability to create Stories or upload VODs
  • Disable DMs
    • Teens can be blocked from sending or receiving Whispers (direct messages).
  • Protect from Sensitive Content
    • Teens have a restricted ability to discover or be recommended content with certain Content Classification Labels (CCLs) that may contain sensitive content, with the option for parents to modify at their discretion.
  • Enact Time Limits
    • Parents can set daily time limits for Twitch across all their teen’s devices.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do parents or guardians need a Twitch account to access Parental Controls?
Yes. Parents or guardians must first create their own Twitch account in order to link with their teen’s account and access Parental Controls.
Can my teen see what controls I’ve set?
While teens cannot see the Parental Controls dashboard, they may discover a restriction when they try to use a feature you’ve disabled or when they reach their time limit.
How do I unlink my account as a parent/guardian or teen?
Both parents/guardians and teens can unlink, or re-link, their respective accounts at any time through the Family Center page. Parents and guardians are notified via email if their teen unlinks from their account.
As a parent, how many accounts can I link my account to?
Parents can link up to 10 teen accounts to their account.
What happens when a teen with Parental Controls enabled turns 18?
When a Twitch user turns 18-years-old, any accounts they are linked to with Parental Controls will automatically unlink.
How many parent or guardian accounts can a teen link with?
Teen accounts can only be linked to one parent or guardian account.
How often can the Parental Controls settings be changed?
Parents or guardians can adjust the Parental Controls settings as often as they’d like — there are no limits in place.
Are these settings able to be controlled on mobile?
Yes, the Family Center dashboard and Parental Controls are available on mobile.
What time limits can I set for my teen’s account?
Parents and guardians can set as big, or as small, of a daily time limit for their teen as they like — from one minute to 24 hours per day.
Are parental controls mandatory for Twitch users ages 13-17?
Not at this time. As regulatory requirements evolve around the world, we look forward to continuing to be good partners with various regulatory agencies and exploring how we can potentially utilize Parental Controls to achieve their respective goals and objectives.

If you’re experiencing issues with Parental Controls or linking accounts, contact Twitch Support here.

Playback Issue Troubleshooting

If you’re experiencing disruption while watching Twitch, this guide will walk you through troubleshooting steps to help resolve your issue.

Twitch streams vary based on each broadcaster’s setup and settings. As a result, playback issues can have multiple causes—some within your control (like internet speed or device settings) and some outside of it (like the broadcaster’s configuration). This guide will help you identify and address the most common issues within your control.

Recommended Internet Speeds for Viewing Twitch

A stable internet connection is required for the best Twitch viewing experience. Our recommended download speeds are:

Quality

Recommended Speed

1440p60 (2k) (Not available everywhere. Learn more.)

9-18 Mbps, or higher

1080p60

7-12 Mbps, or higher

720p60

3-6 Mbps, or higher

480p

1.1-3 Mbps, or higher

360p

0.7-1.5 Mbps, or higher

About Download Speed and Upload Speed

When watching Twitch, your download speed determines video quality. Download speed measures how fast your internet connection receives data like videos and streams. Even if you have high upload speed (used on Twitch for broadcasting), low download speed can cause playback issues when watching streams.

Mobile Carrier Considerations

If you experience buffering on mobile devices, check your carrier’s plan for video streaming limitations. Many mobile carriers cap streaming speeds or quality:

  • 480p streaming: Some carriers (like T-Mobile/Mint Mobile) cap streaming at 1.5 Mbps, which supports 480p quality
  • HD streaming (720p, 1080p): May require an HD video streaming add-on or upgraded plan
  • Higher quality (1080p60+): May require 4K video streaming options from your carrier

Contact your mobile carrier to learn about your plan’s video streaming capabilities and available upgrades.

General Troubleshooting

Video playback issues related to unstable internet can interrupt your experience on Twitch. Examples of video playback issues include:

  • Audio and video stutter
  • Video stutters, but audio is fine
  • Video is completely black, or doesn’t load
  • Audio and video aren’t synced
  • Fullscreen playback doesn’t work

Regardless of how you watch Twitch, most video playback issues can be resolved by:

  • Refresh the page in your web browser (or restart your app/player)
  • Attempt to view another live stream as a test
  • If twitch.tv is not the only site not loading, you may be experiencing an internet connection issue
  • Attempt to watch the stream on another network, such as a cellular network

Why Some Streams Play Fine, and Others Don’t

Twitch receives a wide variety of broadcast configurations from streamers all over the world. Our video infrastructure handles the vast majority of broadcast configurations smoothly. However, if one stream works and another doesn’t, the issue may be related to misconfigured broadcast settings from that specific streamer.

Examples of broadcast configurations that can cause playback issues include:

  • Extremely high bitrate streams that exceed recommended settings
  • Encoder misconfigurations (incorrect keyframe intervals, unsupported codecs)
  • Unstable upload connection from the streamer’s broadcast location
  • Resolution or framerate settings set by the streamer that do not match their internet capacity

If you’ve tried the troubleshooting steps above and are still experiencing issues with a specific stream, try watching other channels to determine if the problem is specific to one stream, or affecting your viewing of all streams on Twitch.

For persistent issues across multiple streams, contact Twitch Support.

Common Playback Error Code Solutions

If you get one of these error codes, try the possible solutions listed below.

Error Code 1000 (Not Supported Error)

What’s happening?

The Error Code 1000 may appear when your web browser, or the application you are using to access Twitch can’t play the video due to compatibility issues.

Common Causes:

  • Your browser is outdated
  • Browser extensions
  • The stream is using features not supported by your browser or not available in your region

Solutions:

  • Try updating your browser to the latest version
  • Disable any browser extensions that block ads, as those may affect playback. You can also try opening Twitch in an incognito window with all extensions disabled.
  • Some streams may not be available in your region. Check if the stream is available in your region.
Error Code 2000 (Not Supported Error)

What’s happening?

Error Code 2000 appears when there’s a problem with your internet network. It is not sufficiently strong, stable, or configured to deliver Twitch video to your device.

Common Causes:

  • Slow or unstable internet connection
  • Router or modem connectivity issues
  • Browser extensions

Solutions:

  • Check internet connection speed and stability. Restart your modem and router (unplug for 30 seconds then reconnect).
  • Ensure Twitch video quality is set to Auto. To do so, click the Settings icon on the player, then click on quality and ensure Auto is selected
  • Check and disable browser extensions, including ad blockers
  • As another potential solution, open Twitch in an incognito window with all extensions disabled.
Error Code 3000 (Decode Error)

What’s happening?

Error Code 3000 appears when the device you’re using to access Twitch is having trouble decoding and displaying the video stream.

Common Causes:

  • Outdated browser version
  • Hardware acceleration issues
  • Browser extensions

Solutions:

  • Update your browser to the latest version
  • Toggle hardware acceleration OFF in browser settings
    • Chrome: Settings > System > Use hardware acceleration when available
    • Firefox: Settings > General > Performance > Use hardware acceleration when available
  • Update your GPU (Graphic Processing Unit) drivers
  • Restart your browser
  • Check and disable browser extensions, including ad blockers
Error Code 7005 (DRM Error)

What’s happening?

Error Code 7005 appears when Digital Rights Management (DRM) settings in your browser are preventing protected content from playing.

Common Causes:

  • DRM is disabled in your browser settings
  • Browser doesn’t support required DRM technology
  • Browser extensions

Solutions:

  • Ensure that your browser has DRM enabled
    • Chrome: “Sites can play protected content” and “Sites can use identifiers to play protected content” should be enabled
    • Firefox: “Play DRM-controlled content” should be enabled
    • Microsoft Edge: “Allow sites to play protected content” should be enabled
  • Try playing the stream on a different device
  • Check and disable extensions, including ad blockers

Frequently Asked Questions

I have gone through every piece of troubleshooting possible, and still no luck.
We understand it’s frustrating to experience video playback issues, and not know exactly why. To help you understand where issues can occur, here’s how streaming works:

The Streaming Pipeline:

  • Broadcaster’s Setup: The streamer creates content using their device, encoder, and internet connection
  • Upload to Twitch: The stream travels from the broadcaster’s location through their ISP to Twitch’s servers
  • Twitch Processing: Twitch receives, processes, and distributes the stream
  • Delivery to You: The stream travels through the internet to your ISP
  • Your Connection: The stream travels from your ISP through your home network to your device

Issues can occur at any of these points. In most cases, playback problems are caused by:

  • The broadcaster’s upload connection or encoder settings (Step 1-2)
  • Your internet connection, home network, or device (Step 4-5)

If you’ve tried all troubleshooting steps and the issue persists, it’s often related to factors outside of Twitch’s control—either on the broadcaster’s end or in the “last mile” delivery to your device. Often, waiting and trying again can resolve most issues.

Can I report a video playback issue on Twitch?
Yes, please do so! You can learn more about how to do this here: help.twitch.tv/s/article/how-to-file-a-video-playback-issue
Why do I have issues viewing Twitch, but my friend can view Twitch just fine?
Every person’s device and network settings may be different. Even if you reside in the same household on the same network, there could still be considerations in your device that causes issues when watching Twitch, that are not shared by another person.
Why does choosing the Auto video quality setting provide a better viewing experience?
The Auto setting automatically adjusts your video quality based on your current network conditions. This is especially helpful if you have spotty, or inconsistent internet connection. Auto will select the best quality that works for your connection in real-time, reducing buffering and interruptions. Manually selecting a quality (like 1080p60) can result in a worse viewing experience if your network can’t consistently support that quality level.

Political Onboarding

What is considered a political channel?

A political channel on Twitch includes accounts owned by candidates, elected officials, campaign committees, political action committees (PACs) , government entities, and political party committees.

A political channel is NOT a content creator that discusses politics, special interest groups, media organizations, or journalists.

What is the process for political channels on Twitch?

All political channels on Twitch undergo a standard process to ensure that they are treated equally, and that Twitch remains in compliance with campaign finance laws. This includes disabling ads and monetization tools on political channels in line with our Terms of Service and legal requirements. We also activate purple checkmarks to indicate that the channel is run by a political entity.

Twitch expects all users to comply with the Community Guidelines and does not make exceptions for political entities. If you see a political channel violating our Terms of Service or Community Guidelines, please file a user report.

Political Channel Requests

If you would like to establish a political channel on Twitch, you must email politics@justin.tv with the subject line “Political Onboarding” before streaming. In your email, include the following information:

  • Channel name
  • Name of the political entity (candidate name, elected official, etc.)
  • Proof of identity
  • Official website and any supplemental documentation verifying authenticity

Once your request is reviewed and approved, you may go live.

Helpful Resources

At Twitch, our goal is to provide the best shared livestreaming experience where streamers and communities can interact safely. All Twitch users are required to agree and abide by our Community Guidelines, and we expect everyone who connects on Twitch to participate in a way that promotes a positive experience for our global community. We do not make public interest exceptions to our rules, including for statements made by public figures. Please see the below list of resources to aid in setting up your political channel and creating a safe streaming experience:

  • Twitch Terms of Service
  • Community Guidelines
  • Fundraising Guidelines
  • User Reporting Guide
  • Moderation Settings
  • Creator Camp (to help you get started)
  • Off-Service Conduct Policy
  • Trademark Usage Guidelines

Requesting Your Data From Twitch

You have the right to access, review, update/correct, transfer, or delete your information on Twitch. Learn more.

Who Can Request Data?

Any logged-in user may request and download a summary of their user data for that account through their user settings page. This feature is available for users on desktop. Those who are not logged in or no longer have access to their account may still request their data by filling out the Contact Us form.

Can’t log in? See our FAQ

Requesting Your Data

To download your user data directly, visit your Security and Privacy settings from your Settings page. Follow these steps:

  • Navigate to your Privacy Settings
  • In the Download Your Data section, click Request a Copy of Your Data
  • Select the categories of data to include in your report.
  • Customize the date range of your report
  • Submit your request

The date range of your report can be as recent as today, or as far back as the date you opened your account.

Once a request has been submitted, you won’t be able to make changes until your report is completed.

Receiving Your Data

Reports are completed within 14 days. You will receive a notification on Twitch when your report(s) are ready to be downloaded.

Return to your Privacy Settings page where the report was requested. Click Download a Copy of your Data.

Understanding Your Data Report

When you download your data, you will receive your report broken down into different subfolders with files named after the event or action they track. These different files can help you sort through your data based on category.

Data Category

Folder Name

Description

Account History

accounts

A log of account actions you’ve taken, such as logging in and out, enabling two-factor authentication, or changing your name and email.

User Information

users

Data about your Twitch account, such as username, login information, account creation date, and last login/broadcast date.

Ad & Commercial Breaks History

ads

A history of ads viewed by you, your ads consent preferences and commercials that were run on your channel.

Bits & Subscriptions History

commerce

A log of your purchases of Bits and Cheers made, as well as which subscriptions you have purchased on Twitch.

Developer History

developer

A log of events that describe the authorizations you have provided to developer accounts

Follows History

community

A history of follow/unfollow actions for channels and games.

Extensions

extensions

A history of extensions you have installed, interacted with, and made purchases from.

Viewing & Chat History

site_history

A log of your viewing and chat activity across all channels for both live and VOD content, as well as any searches you performed from the browse page.

VODs History

vod

A history of changes to you made to VODs on your channel.

Each folder contains a number of files, named after the event or action it tracks. For example, the folder, site_history, includes 6 files with the following names:

  • chat_messages.csv - a list of chat messages you have sent in various channels
  • minute_watched.csv - a log of how many minutes you’ve watched per day, per channel.
  • minute_broadcast.csv - a log of how many minutes you’ve broadcast.
  • search_query.csv - your search history on Twitch.
  • pageview.csv - a log of all the different pages you visited on Twitch.

Frequently Asked Questions

I no longer have access to my Twitch account. How can I request a copy of my data?
You may contact Twitch Support here by email and request your data access report directly.
Why do I need to request a copy of my data?
You don’t need to. However, you have several rights regarding your personal information, including the right to access a copy of your data, request its deletion, correct any inaccuracies, limit certain uses, or request a portable copy that can be shared with other services. Learn more about your rights in our Privacy Notice.
How can I delete the data you have about me?
To delete your Twitch data, you must delete your Twitch account. Learn more in our guide here: help.twitch.tv/s/article/delete-twitch-account
I have a question about data in my access report. What should I do?
Depending on the type of info you request, we may or may not be able to provide additional information or support. Contact Twitch Support here, and we’ll see what we can do.
If I have multiple Twitch accounts, must I request my data from each account individually?
Yes.
I don’t recognize some of the activity in my data report. What should I do?
First, make sure that you have secured your account with 2FA. If you think your account has been compromised, contact Twitch Support here. Learn more in our knowledge guide: help.twitch.tv/s/article/two-factor-authentication
Some of the data in my report is missing. What should I do?
Please note that these reports do not include some of your personal information maintained by Twitch which you can access yourself by logging into your Twitch or Amazon account, such as your Twitch Purchase History. Twitch is also unable to provide data relating to alleged violations of our Community Guidelines as part of your data access request in order to preserve the rights of other users on Twitch.

It’s also possible that you have other Twitch accounts. You can recover your account information using this form.

There was an error when attempting to process my request. What do I do?
Contact our support team here and let us know what happened.
Someone is requesting that I send them the information in my data report. Should I do it?
The information in this report should never be shared, or downloaded on a public computer or device.
Can I request my Whispers history?
Whispers history is not supported in this data report.
Can I request another report before I receive my first report?
No. You must wait for your first requested report to complete before you can request another, or make any alterations.
Why do I have a subscription with an end date so far in the future?
In your Subscriptions History, you may notice a subscription with an end date far into the future. You could be a recipient of a lifetime subscription from a Partner. Learn more about lifetime subscriptions in our knowledge guide: help.twitch.tv/s/article/lifetime-subscriber-guide-for-partners

Signing Up For or Logging Into Twitch with Your Google, Apple, or Amazon Account

Twitch supports the ability to sign up and log in using your Google, Apple, or Amazon account (“social login”). This option provides a fast and secure way to create or access your Twitch account — including support for multiple Twitch accounts linked to the same email.

What You Need to Know

Signing Up For A New Twitch Account With Your Google, Apple, or Amazon Account

Learn more about creating a Twitch account here.

When creating a new Twitch account, you can sign up with your choice of the following social login providers:

  • Sign up with Google
  • Sign up with Apple
  • Sign up with Amazon

Sign in to your selected provider and authorize Twitch to access your name and email address.

Twitch will start your account with your social login email, but it won’t be created until you enter a valid date of birth and choose a username.

You can link your Twitch account to Google, Apple, and Amazon simultaneously, but you cannot link multiple accounts from the same provider (e.g., two different Google accounts). If the email address you choose already matches an existing Twitch account, you’ll be signed into that account instead. If no match is found, you will be prompted to create a new Twitch account using that social login.

Connect Your Existing Twitch Account to Your Google, Apple, or Amazon Account

When signing in to your existing Twitch account, you can connect your choice of social login providers to that account. On your first attempt, we’ll link your Twitch account with your chosen social login provider. You’ll be asked to enter a one-time password (OTP) code sent to your email to verify your account.

Once this step is completed, that social login is now associated with your Twitch account. In the future, you can click on the provider you used during sign-up:

  • Continue with Google
  • Continue with Apple
  • Continue with Amazon

If you’re already signed into that provider on your device, Twitch will log you in automatically without asking for your credentials.

If you’re not signed in, you’ll be redirected to the provider’s login page to enter your credentials.

Complete any additional verification steps, such as two-factor authentication (2FA), if prompted.

Once verified, you’ll be logged in to your Twitch account without needing to enter your Twitch password.

Make sure you’re signed into the correct Google, Apple, or Amazon account before clicking to log in, especially if you have multiple accounts with these providers.

Using Social Login with Multiple Twitch Accounts

If you have multiple Twitch accounts that share the same email address, you can link them all to a single social login provider (Google, Apple, or Amazon). This lets you access any of your Twitch accounts through social login without needing to remember separate passwords.

How It Works

When you use social login and have multiple Twitch accounts with the same email:

  • Sign in with your social login provider (Google, Apple, or Amazon).
  • Verify your identity with a one-time password (OTP) sent to your email.
  • You’ll see a list of all your Twitch accounts associated with that email. Select the account you want to link during this session.
  • After linking, you’ll be logged into that account.
The Multi-Account Picker

After your first linking session, signing in with your social login provider will show you the multi-account picker — a page displaying all of your Twitch accounts associated with that email. The picker separates your accounts into two groups:

  • Selectable accounts — Twitch accounts you can log into or link during this session
  • Already linked accounts — Twitch accounts that are already connected to your social login provider

From the multi-account picker, you can:

  • Select which account to log into
  • See your username and profile picture for each account
  • Link additional Twitch accounts that share the same email

Your most recently used account will appear first on the list. If you don’t see your account listed, select Don’t see your account? for help.

To switch between accounts, you’ll need to log out from your current account via settings and sign in again with your social login provider to return to the multi-account picker.

Linking Additional Accounts

If you have Twitch accounts that aren’t linked yet, you can add them from the multi-account picker by selecting Link an existing account. You’ll go through the OTP verification process again to confirm ownership before the account is linked.

Only Twitch accounts with a verified email address matching your social login provider’s email can be linked through the login flow. You can link your Twitch account to a social account with non-matching emails through settings while logged into the Twitch account. If your Twitch account’s email isn’t verified, verify it first in your account settings.

Managing Your Social Login Accounts

Viewing Your Linked Social Login

To view your linked social login:

  • Go to Settings in your Twitch account.
  • Click on the Security and Privacy tab.
  • Scroll down to Login Options to see your connected providers. Connected providers will show a Disconnect button, while unconnected providers will show Connect.
Linking a Social Login Provider from Settings

You can link a social login provider to your account from the settings page:

  • Go to Settings > Security and Privacy > Login Options.
  • Select the provider you want to link (Google, Apple, or Amazon).
  • Complete the verification process to confirm your identity.

Your session will not be interrupted — you’ll remain logged in while linking completes. You’ll see a confirmation message at the bottom of the screen with an Undo option in case you linked the wrong provider.

Unlinking a Social Login Provider

If you want to disconnect a social login provider from your Twitch account:

  • Go to Settings > Security and Privacy > Login Options.
  • Select the option to unlink your connected provider.
  • You’ll see a confirmation dialog explaining the consequences — after unlinking, you’ll need to use your username and password to log into this account.
  • Confirm to complete the unlinking.

When you unlink a social login provider, you’ll receive an email notification confirming the change. If you didn’t initiate this action, secure your account immediately.

Changing Your Email Address

Changing the email address on your Twitch account will unlink any connected social login provider, since social login relies on matching email addresses.

Before the change takes effect:

  • You’ll see a warning explaining that your social login will be disconnected.
  • If your account doesn’t have a password set, you’ll be required to create one before the email change can proceed.
Lost Access to Your Social Login Provider

If you lose access to your Google, Apple, or Amazon account, you’ll need to recover it through your provider before you can use social login on Twitch. Visit your provider’s help center:

  • Google Account Help
  • Apple ID Support
  • Amazon Account Help

About Apple’s “Hide My Email” Feature

If you sign up for Twitch using Sign in with Apple and choose the Hide My Email option, Apple will generate a unique, random email address (e.g., random@privaterelay.appleid.com) that automatically forwards Twitch communications to your real email inbox. This email address, provided by Apple, is unique to your Twitch account.

To view the unique, random email address associated with your Twitch account:

  • Open Settings on your Apple device.
  • Tap Apple ID > Password & Security > Apps Using Apple ID.
  • Select Twitch to view the relay email address used.

Apple’s Hide My Email feature can sometimes filter or block automated messages like confirmation or OTP (one-time password) emails. Please check your junk, spam, or email filters.

Frequently Asked Questions

Common Social Login Issues and What to Do
What should I do if I get an “Account not found” error?
This means you’re using a social login email that doesn’t match an existing Twitch account. Try signing up instead of logging in, or verify you’re signing in using the correct provider.
Why did I sign into the wrong Twitch account when I used social login?
You’re likely logged into a different provider account than expected. Log out of the current Google/Apple/Amazon account and sign in with the correct one before retrying. If you have multiple Twitch accounts linked, make sure you’re selecting the correct one from the multi-account picker.
Why can’t I change my email or password?
If your account was created via social login, changing your email or password may disconnect your linked social login provider. Contact Twitch Support here for further assistance.
I forgot which social provider I used to sign up. How can I find out?
Try each social login option (Google, Apple, Amazon), or check your email inbox for Twitch emails to identify which provider was used during signup. You can also visit Login Options in your Twitch account settings.
I don’t recognize the email address Twitch is using for my Apple account. What’s happening?
If you used Apple’s “Hide My Email” feature, Apple generated a unique relay address for your account. Follow the steps in the “About Apple’s Hide My Email Feature” section above to locate your relay email in Apple ID settings.
Can I use the same email for multiple Twitch accounts with social login?
Yes. If you have multiple Twitch accounts that share the same verified email address, you can link them all to a single social login provider. When you sign in, you’ll see a multi-account picker that lets you choose which account to log into. See Using Social Login with Multiple Twitch Accounts for details.
What should I do if Google, Apple, or Amazon login services aren’t working?
The provider’s login services may be experiencing outages or slowdowns. Wait and try again later, and check the provider’s service status page for updates on any known issues.
Why does Twitch warn me before changing my email?
Changing the email or enabling additional account creation can break the link between your Twitch account and the login provider. For the best account experience, Twitch needs the email address on your account to always match the email from the social login provider. If your account doesn’t have a password set, you’ll be required to create one before the email change can proceed.
Can I link my Twitch account to a social login provider from the settings page?
Yes. Go to Settings > Security and Privacy > Login Options to link or unlink a social login provider. See Managing Your Social Login Accounts for step-by-step instructions.
I chose Apple’s “Hide My Email” option when signing up for a Twitch account, and didn’t receive the confirmation or OTP email in my inbox. Why?
Apple’s “Hide My Email” feature can sometimes filter or block automated messages like confirmation or OTP emails. Please log in to the Mail inbox and check your Junk, Spam, or filtered folders.
How do I disconnect my social login account?
You can unlink your social login account from your Twitch account in Settings > Security and Privacy > Login Options. You’ll see a confirmation dialog before the change takes effect. After unlinking, you’ll need to use your username and password to log in. See Managing Your Social Login Accounts for details.
What happens if my account fails to link?
If linking fails, you’ll see an error message with the option to retry. Make sure your email is verified on the Twitch account you’re trying to link, and that you’re using the correct social login provider. If the issue persists, contact Twitch Support here.
Will creating a new Twitch account with the same email automatically link it to my social login?
No. New accounts created with a username and password are not automatically linked to an existing social login, even if they share the same email. You can add the new account to your social login from the multi-account picker or from your settings page.

Stories on Twitch

Stories on Twitch give you an easy way to stay top of mind and deepen connections with your community directly on Twitch by sharing short-form, ephemeral content with your followers. Stories are easy to catch up on at any time, even when viewers’ schedules may not align with tuning in for a stream, proving that stories can be a powerful way to engage your community beyond going live. Anyone can view stories. However, the ability to create stories is limited to qualified monetized streamers. Stories can only be posted using the Twitch mobile app. Learn more.

Streamers: How to Create a Story

Eligible Affiliates and Partners can create or post stories to their followers using the Twitch mobile app. To create a story, tap the + (plus) button in the bottom navigation bar and select Create Story from the menu. When creating a story, you can tap the info icon on the top right to customize when your story expires. You can pick from 1, 12, 24, and 48 hours.

There are three core content types on stories: Select from Camera, Clip, or Canvas

Camera: Photo or Video

To create a story using your phone’s camera, take a photo within stories, or upload an existing image from your photo gallery. You can also record and upload videos to stories.

Canvas

Twitch has designed a number of canvas backgrounds that can be used to create stories. Choose from various gradients, solid colors, or seasonal backgrounds.

Clips

Clips in Stories have moved. You can no longer share Clips directly to your story. To share Clips from your streams with your community, add them to your Stream Recap.

Add @Mentions, Texts, and Emotes

Once you’ve selected your content type, personalize your story by adding emotes, @mentions, and text! Mentioned users will be notified when they are mentioned in your story. Settings can be adjusted to change who can mention you. Clicking on a mentioned channel opens a popup that takes you to that user’s stream (if live) or channel page. Any channel can be mentioned, including non-streamers, and users can change who can mention them or opt-out of mentions entirely.

Post Your Story

Post your story by selecting “Your Story” to share to everyone or “Subscribers.” to share exclusive content with subscribers only. Please note that targeting stories to your subscribers only is limited to streamers who meet eligibility requirements.

Stories Inspiration For Creators

Need some inspiration on the types of moments to share? There are so many ways to make your stories work for you!

Bring your viewers with you when you’re on the go

Taking a break from your usual stream schedule or traveling to a fun event? Use stories to check in with an update and take them behind the scenes with you.

Run a Poll & Get your community involved

Learn more about what your viewers want and think by asking a question and encouraging them to take a poll using the Reactions feature.

Spread the love

@mention another streamer in your story to send your viewers their way!

Those with access to video can create personalized videos with @mentions to shout out new subs and viewers to make them feel welcome.

Build your brand

Have projects you’re working on outside of Twitch? Share the latest updates, press coverage, restock-announcements or whatever else you have going on.

Keep them up to date

Post time-sensitive announcements about your stream and schedule changes, highlight an upcoming guest stream, or share exciting life updates!

Pro tip: Use shorter expiration times for updates that may not be relevant the next day.

In case you missed it: Recap your streams

Viewers have busy lives and don’t always get a chance to tune in for a live stream. Your Stream Recap shares Clips from your recent streams so your community can catch up.

Viewing and Reacting to Stories

Viewers can see stories from streamers they follow in a few ways:

  • From the stories shelf at the top of the home page on the mobile app
  • On the following page on web
  • On the left nav on web
  • By clicking on any streamer’s avatar on their mobile channel page

Tap to go through multiple stories in a single channel or swipe to go through different followed channels’ stories. If a streamer is live when you view their story, you can also tap their avatar to go to their stream and join chat!

Viewers can like a story by pressing the heart button or long press on the heart to see a range of emotes to react with. When you react to a story, your favorite streamers can now see which emote you reacted with.

Resharing Stories

Re-sharing other streamers’ stories to your own story is a great way to acknowledge them and cross-promote content, leading to increased visibility.

Streamers with stories creation access can reshare other streamers’ stories to their own story if they are mentioned in the story, or if they have set their settings to allow anyone to reshare their stories.

If you are mentioned in a story and have permission to reshare the story, you’ll see a button to reshare the story to your own story. If a streamer has enabled stories resharing for any user, even if they are not mentioned or tagged, you’ll see the option to reshare their story when clicking on the three dot icon at the top right of the story.

When you reshare a story to your story, the original creator of the story will be notified. You can manage this in your notification settings.

Streamers can manage who can reshare their stories in their stories settings. Please note that being “mentioned” in a story means being @mentioned.

Stories Notifications

By default, sharing a story sends a push notification to your Followers. Story notifications follow an individual’s device, app, or channel notification settings. Learn more.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who can create stories?
At launch, eligibility to create a story will be limited to Partners and Affiliates with at least one stream of 45 minutes or longer in the last 30 days. Some Streamers will also be able to post stories to their subscribers only (if eligible). Only someone who follows your channel will see your stories appear in their Stories shelf in the Following page.
How can I leave feedback, report a bug, or share ideas on stories?
If you have suggestions or ideas on stories, visit link.twitch.tv/UVStories, or contact Twitch Support here.
Can I hide stories from certain streamers?
Currently you can not hide stories from channels that you follow from appearing in the stories shelf on the Following page.
Can I turn off notifications from certain streamers?
Yes. Navigate to the streamer’s channel page and select the notification icon. From here, you can manage notification settings for this streamer.
I’m not receiving story notifications. What should I do?
To receive push notifications when a channel posts a new story, you must be following the channel. If you’re already following the channel:
  • Check your mobile device system settings
    • Are Do Not Disturb/Focus modes enabled?
    • Have you allowed notifications from the Twitch mobile app?
  • Check your Twitch mobile app settings
    • Have you disabled story notifications? In the mobile app, tap your portrait -> Settings -> Notifications -> verify if you have enabled notifications about new stories.
    • Have you disabled notifications from the channel? In the mobile app, navigate to the channel you are following. Select the notification icon, and verify if you have enabled notifications about the channel.
  • Update notification settings for that channel
    • Twitch does not send a notification for every single story a channel shares unless a user has changed the settings for that channel to “Always.”
    • To make sure you always get notified for a channel; navigate to the channel you are following, select the notification icon, and choose “Always” as your setting

In the Twitch mobile app notification settings, the toggles in Per Channel affect live notifications only. Select the notification icon on a channel page to manage story notifications from that channel.

I’m a monetized streamers, and I’ve streamed for over an hour in the last 30 days. Why don’t I have access to create stories when I open the Twitch app?
Make sure you are using the latest version of the Twitch app and reload the app.
What statistics can I see about stories?

Engagement statistics for stories are available for each story. Visit the Content tab in Creator Mode to see:

  • Views per story
  • Emote reactions per story
    • Types of emote reactions used per story
    • Who reacted
How can I see prior stories I created?

You can view your active stories simply by clicking on your own stories on the Following page. If you’d like to view your history of stories beyond what’s active, visit the Content tab in Creator Mode and select All Your Stories.
