Browser Extensions & Twitch

If something doesn’t look right on Twitch, there are quick, simple troubleshooting steps you can take that may resolve the issue. The most basic is to refresh your web page or app– yes, really. Another tip includes temporarily disabling 3rd party browser extensions.

This guide will explain how extensions interact with Twitch, and why Twitch Support may ask you to disable browser extensions when assisting you.

Looking for Twitch Extensions? Visit our how-to guide here.

On this page:

  • What are browser extensions?
  • Common Issues
  • Your Privacy
  • Frequently Asked Questions

What are browser extensions?

Browser extensions (or add-ons) are small pieces of software made by 3rd party developers that modify how a website loads and functions. When you enable a browser extension, you give it permission to modify how Twitch looks and behaves. This relationship is one-way: Twitch code does not interact with the browser extension; it is the browser extension that is modifying your experience.

Like any piece of software, browser extensions can have bugs or problems. Developers build their browser extensions based on the current state of Twitch. Since we constantly update and improve Twitch, there may be occasions that the browser extension experience of Twitch behaves unexpectedly. (For example, the extension code may be looking for a button that doesn’t exist anymore, or has moved).

Temporarily disabling browser extensions and reloading your page can solve common issue types in the following categories

Common Issues

  • Emote, badge, and chat display issues.
  • Payment currency/pricing issues.
  • General issues viewing video

If disabling browser extensions solves your issues, there is no requirement to leave the extension disabled. Be aware that the issue may persist until the 3rd party developer issues a fix.

If disabling browser extensions doesn’t solve your issue, you can:

  • Attempt the operation again in incognito mode
  • Refresh the page
  • Troubleshoot on another device.

If you still need help, contact Twitch Support. Let us know what troubleshooting steps you’ve completed and other details such as the platform you’re experiencing the issue.

Your Privacy

Your use of 3rd party browser extensions is not covered under Twitch’s Privacy Notice. Before granting a browser extension access to your information and permission to change your systems, it never hurts to do research and consider where you are downloading it from. Use caution and consider any risk. Happy viewing!

Learn more about your data choices on Twitch with Your Privacy Choices.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I keep using my 3rd party browser extensions?

Of course. The purpose of this guide is to help self-solve certain categories of issues you encounter.

What’s the difference between browser extensions (or add-ons) and Twitch Extensions?

Twitch Extensions are live interactive experiences that can be integrated into the Twitch video stream. Browser extensions are add-ons for a web browser like Firefox, Opera, or Chrome. Both are developed by 3rd party developers, but Twitch Extensions are built with officially supported APIs provided to developers.

What information does Twitch get from my internet browser, regardless of if I use browser extensions?

Learn more about the data we collect and what we do with it in our Privacy Notice

Does Twitch have any 3rd party applications they recommend?

We aren’t able to endorse anything that we did not create or support.

Channel Page Setup

Setting up your channel page is one of the most important aspects of being a creator. Your channel page will be where your viewers and other users can find information about you and your streams.

Profile Picture and Profile Banner

Set your channel apart by uploading a Profile Picture and Profile Banner.

The profile picture and profile banner are two of the most prominent features on your profile. Whether it’s a favorite picture of yours or dedicated branding that you want to use, these images will be one of the first impressions you make on viewers.

Adding a Profile Picture
  • To get started, log in and go to Creator Dashboard by clicking your profile icon in the upper right, and selecting Creator Dashboard from the drop-down menu.
  • Click on Settings and then Channel in the side menu. Then select the Brand tab.
  • Under the heading Profile Picture, click Add Profile Picture and upload an image from your computer. Must be JPEG, PNG, or GIF and cannot exceed 10MB.
Adding a Profile Banner
  • In your Channel area of your Creator Dashboard make sure you’ve selected the Brand tab.
  • Under the heading Profile Banner, click Update. You will be prompted with an Upload a Photo pop-up where you can select an image from your computer.

The recommended size for a profile banner is 1200x480px. Twitch pages (and your banner art) scale based on the width of each user’s browser window. Images shorter or taller than 480px will be scaled to 480px high. Images will also be stretched if a user’s browser window is open wider than the width of the image. To ensure a consistent look across all monitor resolutions, it is best to make your image as wide as possible and concentrate the graphics on the left.

Profile Accent Color and Video Player Banner

You can highlight your personal brand around Twitch by choosing an accent color and uploading a video player banner, which will appear when your channel is offline. The profile accent color that you choose will be used to highlight your content on Twitch and be displayed on your channel’s elements.

Choose Accent Color
  • To choose an accent color, log in and go to Creator Dashboard by clicking your profile icon in the upper right, and selecting Creator Dashboard from the drop-down menu.
  • Click on Settings and then Channel in the side menu. Then select the Brand tab.
  • Choose a color using the color picker on the left; customize your color by using the slider; enter a specific color code if you have one (e.g. #00C7AC).
  • Click Save Changes to save your color and update your profile.
Upload a Video Player Banner

Animated video player banners are not natively supported on Twitch.

  • To add a video player banner, log in and go to Creator Dashboard by clicking your profile icon in the upper right, and selecting Creator Dashboard from the drop-down menu.
  • Click on Settings and then Channel in the side menu. Then select the Brand tab.
  • Choose a color using the color picker on the left; customize your color by using the slider; enter a specific color code if you have one (e.g. #00C7AC).
  • Click Save Changes to save your color and update your profile.
Delete a Video Player Banner
  • To delete your banner, click the trash icon next to Update to remove the banner.

Bio and Social Links

Writing a bio and linking to your social media accounts helps to introduce yourself to viewers and provides them with an opportunity to check out your other media to get a sense for who you are. These also help improve your channel’s discoverability by providing content for SEO that a search engine can read and then use when people are searching for you or other similar content.

Add a Bio
  • To add a bio, log in and go to Creator Dashboard by clicking your profile icon in the upper right, and selecting Creator Dashboard from the drop-down menu.
  • Click on Settings and then Channel in the side menu. Then select the About tab.
  • Under the heading Profile Settings you’ll see the box to fill in your bio information beneath Username and Display Name settings.
  • Once you’ve written your bio, be sure to click Save Changes to publish the bio to your channel page.
Bio Best Practices

A bio should speak from your own voice and give potential viewers more information about yourself. This could include games you like to play and more about your personality on-stream. You have max 300 characters so make it short and sweet.

Add social links

Social media handles appear in search results! Add up to 5 social links that will display on your channel profile.

  • To add social links, log in and go to Creator Dashboard by clicking your profile icon in the upper right, and selecting Creator Dashboard from the drop-down menu.
  • Click on Settings and then Channel in the side menu. Then select the About tab.
  • Enter the name of the social link in the first box (e.g. Follow me on Twitter!)
  • Enter the full URL for the social link in the second box (e.g. twitter.com)
  • When you’re finished, click Add to add the link to your channel.

If you add social links, we’ll automatically tag your handle if you or your viewers share clips to YouTube or TikTok!

Edit Social Links
  • To edit a social link, enter the new text in the first or second box (depending on which you’d like to change).
  • Click Save to keep those changes and update your link.
Delete Social Links
  • To delete a social link, click the trash icon next to Save for the link that you want to delete.

Stream Schedule

Stream Schedules appear on the Following page and the search results page, so be sure to set up your schedule and keep it relevant!

We recommend listing the days and times you usually stream so your viewers know when to tune in. It’s okay if this changes, just keep your schedule up to date.

Add Stream Schedule
  • To add a Stream Schedule, log in and go to Creator Dashboard by clicking your profile icon in the upper right, and selecting Creator Dashboard from the drop-down menu.
  • Click on Settings and then Channel in the side menu. Then select the Schedule tab.
  • Select Add Stream to popup the options and set up your first schedule.
  • Select all of the options that are relevant for your stream and enter the corresponding information.
  • Title:
  • Create a title that is helpful for viewers to know what your stream will be about as well as interesting to set it apart from other streams.
  • Category:
  • What are you going to be doing on stream? Which game(s) will you be playing?
  • Start time:
  • This can be an estimate of when you plan to start streaming.
  • Duration:
  • This can be an estimate of your stream duration. You can always go shorter or longer.
  • Frequency:
  • Select multiple days of the week if you plan to play the same game or want to cover all of the days you plan to stream. You can always edit individual days and stream info as needed.
  • Specific Day:
  • Select a specific day you plan to stream. This is only available for Affiliate and Partners.
Edit Schedule

It’s easy to change the date and time of upcoming individual scheduled streams, or make changes to your recurring scheduled altogether.

  • Once you’ve set a schedule, you can edit the individual streams by selecting the Edit icon next to each stream.
  • You can edit any/all of the specifics for each stream.
  • Click Save to update the stream info or click the trash icon icon to delete that specific stream from your schedule.
Cancel an Individual Stream
  • You can cancel an individual stream if you aren’t able to stream that day, by toggling on the Cancelled button and saving. The stream will stay cancelled until you uncancel or edit the other information about the stream.
Delete Schedule
  • If you want to delete your entire schedule you can select Delete schedule located at the top of the Stream Schedule section, next to Create New. You’ll get a confirmation that you actually want to delete your schedule.
Vacation Mode
  • Select Vacation Mode using the toggle button at the top of the Stream Schedule section to let viewers know that you’re away.
  • Set the Start and End dates for your vacation time.
  • Click Save to update your schedule.

Channel Trailer

Channel Trailers are currently only available to Affiliates and Partners. Upload a channel trailer here.

Channel Trailers are short videos to introduce yourself to new viewers while you’re offline. Your trailer will show up at the top of your offline channel page when a new viewer visits. Keep it short and sweet, this quick introduction video can be up to 60 seconds. And keep it classy - Trailers must follow the Twitch Community Guidelines, are reportable content and subject to review.

Trailer Best Practices

First and foremost, be yourself! Introduce yourself, tell viewers what types of content you typically stream, and remind them to follow you and turn on notifications so they’ll be notified the next time you go live. If you stream regularly, consider sharing that schedule.

If you don’t stream regularly, consider pointing viewers to your stream schedule to know when to tune in next.

Your trailer should be 60 seconds or less, keep it short and sweet! If you include music in your trailer please make sure that any music in your trailer follows Twitch’s DMCA guidelines and is approved for use.

There’s plenty of cleared music out there, like Anjuna’s playlist curated exclusively for Twitch and its community.

Trailer Technical Requirements

Your channel trailer needs to be stored in your VOD library.

  • MP4, MOV, AVI and FLV file formats
  • AAC audio
  • h264 codec
  • Up to 10Mbps bitrate
  • Up to 1080p/60FPS
Setting a Channel Trailer

You can set your trailer from the Channel Settings under the Featured Content tab.

  • Under the Channel Trailer heading select Choose a Video
  • Review the onboarding tips then dismiss the welcome message.
  • If you need to upload a trailer: Select Video Producer at the top of the setup page.
  • Click Upload and select the video to upload from your computer
  • Once the upload is complete, click the 3 Vertical Dots menu of the upload you wish to set as a trailer, review it and the trailer title and then select Set as Trailer and you’re done!
  • If you already have an uploaded trailer: Select the video from your library. Review it and the trailer title and then select Set as Channel Trailer and you’re done!
Removing a Channel Trailer

Removing your trailer does not delete the video from your VOD library.

  • Once a trailer is set, it can be removed as your trailer from Channel Settings by clicking the Remove button under the Channel Trailer heading and confirm by clicking Remove Trailer.
  • A Trailer can also be removed from Video Producer by first filtering to see your Channel Trailers, then clicking the 3 Vertical Dots menu icon of your trailer and selecting Remove as Channel Trailer and confirm by clicking Remove Trailer in the confirmation box.
Deleting a Channel Trailer
  • To delete a trailer from your VOD library, follow the steps to delete your a video in the Videos on Demand article.

Info Panels

A space for broadcasters to customize their channel with information, links and images using the editing language, Markdown. File sizes for images must be under 2.9 MB, and should be no larger than 320px wide and 300px high, otherwise they automatically resize to these maximums.

For more information about info panels, check out our How to Edit Info Panels article.

Suggested Channels

Your suggested channels list allows you to showcase another channel in your video carousel when you’re offline. This is a great way to support other streamers and introduce your community to channels you enjoy.

For more information check out our article What Are Suggested Channels?

Chat & Events Beta For Twitch Streamers

The best moments on Twitch occur when streamers and their viewers connect, interact and come together to co-create live content and experiences. Being a streamer is hard — it takes a lot of energy and focus to entertain, interact with viewers, and manage the many tools and windows required to make this magic happen.

We want to make engaging with your audience easier so that you can focus on creating the best stream experience possible. To do this, we are introducing a new tool called Chat and Events. Chat & Events brings Twitch engagement activities together in a single, portable window. This is the first step in moving towards a unified tool to help streamers monitor engagement across chat and events, as well as live audience and participation insights. Chat and Events includes the following key components:

  • Combined chat and events feed. The tool uses a side-by-side display of recent events and chat. Each section has filters to easily see the number of recent events or chat activity by event or message type (e.g. all subs, first time chatters, or mentions), with the option to dive deep into a particular event category or message type.
  • Portability to multiple surfaces. You can dock or embed the dashboard into Twitch’s stream manager, 3P clients such as OBS Studio, or use it as a stand-alone popped-out browser.
  • Live and upcoming events. Chat & Events will provide a creator centric view and management of active channel activities such as a Poll or Prediction, and upcoming events and insights, such as an upcoming Ad break without taking up space in chat or requiring you to click into prompts to see more details.

How to Enable Chat and Events (beta)

Chat & Events was designed to be portable. If you are eligible for the Beta, you can access the tool within Stream Manager, from OBS Studio or as a popped-out experience. If you are enrolled in the beta, a first-time user experience will guide you through the process to upgrade to Chat & Events.

From Stream Manager

You can access the Chat & Events panel from Stream Manager as a new layout, add it as a new panel to an existing layout, or replace an existing panel, such as Chat and/or your activity feed.

As a Pop-out

You can also use creator Chat & Events as a pop-out panel to place elsewhere in your setup. To access the pop-out, go stream manager -> Chat & Events -> Three Dot Menu -> Pop-out Chat & Events.

From OBS Studio

Finally, for streamers that use chat as an embedded dock in OBS, the Chat & Events beta includes an upgrade flow to upgrade the default OBS Twitch Chat dock to creator Chat & Events. To enable the new experience:

  • Open OBS with the existing Twitch Chat dock open
  • When the upgrade modal appears, select “Upgrade Now.”
  • Recommended: Expand the width of the existing dock to at least 600px

If you want to switch back to the default Twitch Chat dock in OBS, there is an option to do so in the Chat & Events menu -> Exit Chat & Events. You can re-enable it any time within Chat settings -> Upgrade to Chat & Events.

Customizing Chat & Events

Every Streamers setup is different, so you can customize Chat & Events to meet your needs.

Adjusting size and width

You can adjust the height and width of the Chat & Events tool using the existing panel controls in stream manager, or using the dock layout controls within OBS Studio.

You can also adjust the width of the split between the chat and events columns. To do so, highlight the divider between the columns and drag to the left or right to increase the width of one side.

Changing Event Views

You can swap between different views of the event feed while using Chat & Events.

Category View: This view groups events by the event type. You can select any category in this view to see all events in that category. For example, all Follow events will be grouped under Follows. When grouped you will see the most recent event and the total number of these events that have occurred during your stream. You can change the order of the categories in the events filter menu.

List View: This view lists events in the order in which they occurred during your stream.

Changing Event order

By default, Chat and Events uses a bottom to top sorting order with the newest event appearing on the bottom to mirror the direction of Chat.

You can switch between bottom-to-top or top-to-bottom ordering by selecting the “Sort Event Order” control at the top of the events section.

Using Event Filters

You can select the types of events that appear in the events section by toggling on or off individual categories from the events filter. When you turn off an event category, the quick filter will no longer appear and any events in that category will not display in your events view.

You can also change the order of your quick filters from the events filter menu by dragging a category up or down the list.

Chat & Events allows you to filter for third-party events triggered by services such as Streamlabs, StreamElements, and more.

Using Quick Filters

Quick Filters are available for both Chat and Events categories to allow you to focus on a specific message or event type. Quick filters can be disabled from the three dot menu.

Chat Quick Filters: Chat quick filters allow you to see all messages of specific type such as First Time Chats, Raiders, or @mentions. Selecting a Chat quick filter will open a filtered view of chat in the right column and only show messages of that type while open. While filtered chat is open, the event space will resize to accommodate the new view. Your unfiltered Chat will remain visible even when a filter is applied. You can resize or close the filtered chat view at any time.

Event Quick Filters: Event quick filters allow you to quickly switch between event types. For example, selecting subscriptions will display all subscription events that have occurred since your last stream.

A maximum of 200 recent events can appear within Chat & Events currently.

Live Events

The Chat & Events tool features a Live Events section that will appear whenever a Poll or Prediction event is active on the channel. This interaction will replace the notification on the top of chat and allow you to monitor and manage the live poll or prediction at a glance. You can minimize the live event at any time.

Swapping Columns in Chat & Events

You can swap the Chat column to appear on the left or right side of the tool by opening the three dot menu and selecting “Switch Columns”

Frequenty Asked Questions

Can I keep using the default Chat experience?

Yes! The default chat layout is still available to streamers in the Beta and you can continue to use that in Stream Manager or wherever you use chat.

I’ve upgraded to Creator Chat but I want to go back to using classic chat. How can I revert to default Chat?

Stream Managers Users: Use the panel control settings to switch back to default Chat.

OBS Studio or Pop-out Users: Select the Chat & Events three dot menu and select “Exit Chat & Events.” You can return to Chat & Events at any time through the chat settings options.

What is the minimum recommended width for Chat & Events?

We recommend a width of 600px or greater for Chat and Events.

What event types are supported in the new Live Events section?

During the beta, Polls, Predictions and Ad breaks will be supported. All other events will continue to appear at the top of chat. We are exploring adding more event types in the future.

Can I keep using the stand alone Activity Feed?

Yes! The Twitch Activity Feed is available for use in all existing locations.

Is Chat & Events available for Mods or Viewers?

No, Chat & Events is designed specifically with streamers in mind. We may evaluate extending it to other Twitch users in the future.

When will Chat & Events be available for all streamers?

Chat & Events is currently in beta so we can continue to build and improve the feature to ensure it meets the needs of Twitch streamers. We do not yet have a timeline for general availability, but will keep the community informed as we move forward.

Copyrighted Audio Detection & Warnings

As part of Twitch’s ongoing efforts to help you understand when unauthorized copyrighted material may be included in the content you stream, we proactively employ an audio recognition system that scans VODs and clips for copyrighted audio. When copyrighted audio is detected in these videos, that portion of your VOD is muted and associated clips are deleted.

You can take action on these VODs in the Video Producer.

How it Works

If our audio recognition system detects multiple instances of copyrighted audio in your VOD(s) in 24 hours, you will receive a notification on Twitch and an email sent to the address associated with your account. Copyrighted audio warnings are enabled by default but can be disabled in the Stream Settings page of your Creator Dashboard.

We hope these warnings can help you make more informed decisions regarding what type of content to include on your channel moving forward. These advance warnings are not copyright strikes, and accruing them will not result in your account getting banned.

How to Use

  • If the audio recognition system detects 3 or more cases of copyrighted audio in your VODs in a 24-hour period, we will send you a notification on Twitch and send you an email. The email will include more information about the copyrighted material that was detected in your VOD(s).
  • You can also review these details in the Video Producer section of your Creator Dashboard. Navigate to the VOD(s) and click the corresponding row to open up the editing pane. The portions of the VOD that were muted should show up in the video timeline with red lines. You can appeal muted audio.
  • In your Stream Settings, Always Publish VODs will be toggled off in your VOD settings. This change will not be retroactive for your existing VODs, but will prevent new VODs from being published by default.
  • To publish your VODs by default and for future broadcasts, go to the Stream Settings page in your Creator Dashboard, and toggle Always Publish VODs in VOD settings.
  • You can also choose not to be notified again if you trigger the match threshold in the future by toggling off Copyrighted audio warnings.

Creator Dashboard

Although the Creator Dashboard is available to all Twitch users, some features and settings described in this guide are available to Affiliates and Partners only.

The Creator Dashboard is the home for streaming on Twitch. You can manage your live-stream, organize your content, edit safety preferences, or access resources to help you improve your stream.

In this guide, we’ll first explain how you can easily navigate the Creator Dashboard. Then, we’ll provide a detailed overview of the tools and settings at your disposal.

We’ve been working hard to update the Creator Dashboard, we hope you like it and look forward to your feedback!

Navigation

Navigate the Creator Dashboard using the left-hand menus or the Dashboard Search in the top bar. In Dashboard Search, enter search terms for quick access to settings and resources. Press enter for more detailed results, or click a suggestion to go straight to the feature.

You can focus search using Ctrl+/ on Windows and Cmd+/ on Mac. Start typing to see search suggestions, then use arrow keys and enter to navigate to the suggested page or search results page.

Home

Creator Home is the default landing page for all streamers in the Creator Dashboard. It will provide you with the most relevant tools, tips, guidance, and inspiration you need to thrive at various stages of your streaming journey on Twitch – all in one place. Your personalized landing page experience will show you things such as important announcements, stats from your most recent stream, helpful tips, and actionable insights based on your streaming journey.

Stream Manager

Stream Manager is the control panel for your stream.

For more information check out our article for the Stream Manager.

Creator Updates

We use this space to share the latest product changes and policy updates that impact the creator community, so you don’t have to check anywhere else.

To see if there are any new updates, look out for the sparkles icon at the top right-hand corner of your Creator Dashboard, which will be green if you have any new updates.

Alerts

Set up custom stream alerts by Twitch. Alerts highlight your communities’ actions, driving awareness and engagement with your audience.

Learn more about Alerts in our guide: Twitch’s Alerts

Analytics

Your Analytics provide a comprehensive and customizable overview of your stream’s revenue, engagement and viewer statistics over a date range you define. These detailed breakdowns allow broadcasters to make informed decisions to improve their stream.

Get to know each page more here, or visit your Analytics.

Community

The Community section contains four key features:

  • Roles Manager - Manage the roles of your community members
  • My Assigned Roles - View your assigned roles in other communities
  • Activity - Check out the updates you’ve made to Ad Breaks, Category, and Stream Title
  • Followers List - See all of your current followers

To view your followers, navigate to Community > Followers List in the Creator Dashboard.

For more info on the different roles that can be assigned to your community members, visit the Managing Roles For Your Channel help article.

Content

Organize and curate your streaming content in these four sections:

  • Video Producer - Manage past broadcasts (VODs), Highlights, and Uploads in the Video Producer. You can also review your copyright strike status.
  • Collections - View collections you’ve curated of your own content.
  • Clips - Review Clips of your channel, and Clips you’ve created.
  • Copyright Claims Manager - Keep track of copyright claims on your channel.

For more tips on how to manage your content, check out the Video on Demand, How to Use Collections, and How to Create, Edit, and Share Clips help articles.

Monetization

If you are a Twitch Partner or Affiliate, find options here pertaining to your monetization settings.

  • Ads
  • Bits & Cheering
  • Community
  • Subscriptions
  • Sponsorships
  • Monetization Onboarding Settings - If you are a monetized creator, you’ll find onboarding information in this section.

Learn more about these settings in our Affiliate Settings Guide or Partner Settings Guide.

Moderation

Set controls for your channel via AutoMod and manage what is allowed in your Chat, such as by blocking hyperlinks or setting up personalized Chat Rules. For more details on how to moderate your channel, visit the Setting Up Moderation for Your Twitch Channel help article.

In the Moderation Analytics section, review a post-stream report of all moderation actions that took place during your streams. Learn more.

Settings

Access your stream key, manage your VODs and clips settings, and edit your permissions in the Stream section. Manage your profile settings and customize your channel (such as through adding a profile photo or setting a custom background) in the Channel section. You can also add your social links or set a streaming schedule here. For a comprehensive guide to setting up your channel page, visit the Channel Page Setup help article.

Partners and Affiliates can also access the Streamer Community Survey in the Streamer Survey section. Check out this help article to learn more about the Streamer Community Survey.

Viewer Rewards

Manage Power-ups & Channel Points.

Manage your Drops preferences in this section of the dashboard. Keep an eye out for the latest Drops and connect your Twitch account to your game accounts to grant rewards to your community. Please note that your viewers will not be eligible for Drops if Drops are disabled on your channel. For an overview on Drops and how they work, check out the How to Discover and Claim Drops on Twitch help article.

If you are a monetized creator, you can also manage your Emotes preferences in this section. The Emotes section is your one-stop location to manage subscription emotes, Bits tier emotes, and Cheermotes (Partners only). Visit Creator Camp to learn more.

Streaming Tools

View the most common streaming tools to set up your stream and go live in this section, or in the Recommended Software for Broadcasting help article.

Charity

Support the causes you care about with the Charity Tool. Learn more about setting up a charity stream.

Extensions

Extensions provide interactive experiences that are built by third-party developers. Extensions can help streamers drive engagement, create integrations with top games, share important information, and even earn additional revenue. Manage your installed extensions or discover new extensions in this section of your dashboard.

For more info on how to install and use extensions, visit the How to Use Extensions help article.

Check out the Safety Center.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I access my moderation tools?
To access your channel moderation tools click Moderation, and then Settings (Moderation). You can also access Mod View (a comprehensive channel mode for moderators) for your channel by navigating to twitch.tv, where you can click on Moderate Your Own Channel at the bottom of the page.
What Quick Actions are available? Are more coming soon?
Edit Stream Information, Clip That, Clear Chat History, Start Watch Party, and Add Stream Marker are a few of the available Quick Actions. We’ll continue to add new quick actions as new products launch and based on feedback from the community. There is also a “New Quick Actions” section within the Quick Actions modal where you can see all recently released Quick Actions.
How does the dashboard work with Twitch Studio?
Anyone can access the Creator Dashboard on the web to manage their streams and both the Creator Dashboard and Twitch Studio include features designed to make it easier for newer streamers to get started. Our goal is to make the tools streamers rely on easy to access and we’ll continue to find ways to do this in the future based on feedback.
Which streamers will see the Creator Home?
Creator Home is currently available for streamers who are not yet Affiliates or Partners.
Can I use this as an Editor of a channel?
Yes, Editors are able to access a channel’s dashboard and help streamers manage their channel. For more information on the type of actions you can perform as an Editor of a channel, check out the Managing Roles For Your Channel article.
Where can I report bugs or provide feedback?
All bugs and feedback can be reported from inside the Creator Dashboard by clicking the ? in the top right corner, or go here.

Earnings Analytics

Visit your Earnings page in Analytics to review how much you earn on Twitch, get a breakdown of your revenue sources, and take a look back at your payout history.

With the exception of the Earnings page, stream data throughout your Channel Analytics is displayed in your local time zone. Subscription data on the Earnings page is displayed in UTC to match payouts which are UTC based.

Subscriptions

As a monetized streamer, your standard subscription revenue split with Twitch is 50/50. This means that after applicable deductions (such as taxes, payment processing fees, and currency conversion fees), you and Twitch each receive half of the remaining subscription revenue. Eligible creators may qualify for enhanced revenue share rates through the Plus Program.

Subscription Breakdown

This panel is a static report of the exact number of subscribers that you have in the current moment. Using this, you can find out how many subscribers you have today. The information on this panel does not necessarily correspond to the information on the Subscriptions By Location panel and does not update when you change the date range at the top of the page.

On the bottom of this panel is the View details button. This allows you to see detailed information about your subscriptions, including a breakdown of subscription purchases to your channel by country.

Subscriptions By Location

View this panel to understand where your subscription purchases are from. Creators who have a sufficient number of subscribers from at least two countries will see a country-by-country summary of subscription purchases to their channel.

In some cases, where the location data is unavailable, the country will be listed as “Unknown Country.”

To see other date ranges, you may change the date selector at the top of the screen. If you do, the chart and breakdown will update to include all subscriptions during this time period.

From this page, Partners can also download their subscriber list:

Why Subscriptions Lapsed

This panel allows you to see aggregated, anonymous information about the reasons your subscribers gave for canceling their subscriptions. Learn More or See Your Settings.

Founders Badge Holders

In this panel, review information about and manage Founders Badges held by your most dedicated supporters.

Learn More about Founders Badges.

Revenue Breakdown

Revenue Sources

This panel provides details on revenue received during the time period selected at the top of the page. This information will update dynamically as you select different date ranges at the top of the page.

Mousing over Paid Subs will provide a breakdown of how much of your paid subscription revenue came from Tier 1, 2 or 3 subscriptions. Mousing over Gifted Subs will provide the same breakdown for gift subs. Underneath this panel is the View Payout History button. Clicking this button will allow you to view your Payout History.

Ads & Twitch Turbo includes ad impression revenue earned from ads and revenue earned from viewers who are subscribed to Turbo, our ad-free product. Turbo revenue is pro-rated daily over the subscription period for accurate day-by-day tracking.

About Revenue Sources Timing

It takes about 24-48 hours for recent Subscription, Bits, Turbo, and other revenue types to appear in your Revenue Sources. Revenue from ads may appear in as soon as 12 hours.

How Turbo Revenue is Calculated: Turbo revenue is pro-rated daily, meaning 1/30th of a Turbo subscription’s revenue is recognized per day over the subscription period. This provides an accurate day-by-day view of your earnings and is consistent with how other revenue types are displayed in your Earnings Analytics.

Frequently Asked Questions

How is Turbo revenue calculated in my Earnings Analytics?
Turbo revenue is pro-rated daily over the subscription period. When a viewer subscribes to Turbo, 1/30th of the subscription revenue is recognized per day, rather than showing the full amount upfront. This gives you an accurate day-by-day view of your earnings. During the transition to this calculation method, you may notice differences in how Turbo revenue appears month-to-month as the system adjusts from the previous upfront calculation to the new daily pro-rating.
What else can I learn with Channel Analytics?
Dive in by visiting your Analytics, or click here for an overview.
Where can I leave feedback on Analytics?
Browse these pages and let us know your feedback or suggestions in UserVoice.
My revenue split seems lower than it should be. Why is that?
There are many factors that can influence your share of the revenue that you earn. Here is a shortlist of the most common points of confusion:
  • Tax Withholding — If you are a non-US creator, some tax withholdings might have been applied to your revenue due to expired or invalid tax information on your account. You can use the withholding widget in your Creator Dashboard to keep track of the status of your tax information.
  • Local Subscription Pricing — Due to Local Subscription Pricing, different subscriptions can earn you different amounts of revenue. A subscription can cost less than $1 and vary by country all the way up to $5.99. This means that the price for a subscription (and thus your earned revenue for that subscription) depends on which subscription it is and who purchased it. You can get a general idea of where your subscribers come from any time by going to your Analytics > “How many subscribers do I have today?” widget > View details.
  • Discounted Gift Subscriptions — When looking at your revenue, also take into account that when gifting subscriptions in bundles of 5 or more, viewers can purchase them at a discounted price. Revenue received from these subscriptions is shared between Twitch and the streamer after the discount.
What if my revenue split still seems off?
As explained above, there are certain costs, taxes, and fees that must be accounted for before you receive subscription revenue, including localized subscription pricing, gift sub bundle pricing, and promotional subscription discounts, which might generate a lower revenue per subscription than what you are using for your calculations. Before the revenue split between you and Twitch takes place, deductions are made from the full price of the subscription, including taxes, payment processing fees, bank fees, currency conversion fees, etc. After the split takes place, we still account for required tax withholding, which is reflected in the payout you ultimately see on your dashboard. If you still have questions, contact Twitch Support.
Why is my ad revenue lower than expected?
Several factors can cause ad revenue to vary from day to day, even with the same average viewership:
  • Revenue reporting delay — Revenue from ads may take up to 12 hours to appear in your Earnings Analytics.
  • Seasonal trends — Advertiser demand fluctuates throughout the year, which affects how much ad revenue channels earn.
  • Ad blockers — Viewers using third-party ad blocking software will not generate ad impressions for your channel.
  • Regional ad availability — Depending on where your viewers are located, ads may not always be available in their region at that time. If no ads are shown, no revenue is earned.
Why are no ads playing on my channel?
If ads are not playing on your channel, consider the following:
  • Content Classification Labels (CCLs) — The type of content you stream can affect your ad revenue. Brands align their ads with content that reflects their brand values. Advertisers use Content Classification Labels to decide which streams to show their ads alongside. Certain brands may choose not to run ads on streams with specific labels applied.
  • Recent suspension — Receiving a temporary account suspension for brand safety-related Community Guidelines violations (including sexual content, nudity, gambling, hateful conduct, or violence) may result in ads being removed from your channel for a short period. If you appeal a suspension and the appeal is accepted, your previous ad eligibility will be restored.
If you believe ads should be running on your channel and they are not, contact Twitch Support.

Geoblocked and Region-Locked Content

This premium content is not available in your region is an error meaning you cannot access that particular live stream.

What is Geoblocking?

Geoblocking refers to Twitch’s ability to limit viewing of a live Twitch stream to certain countries. This can be because of laws in that country, or the content is not legal in other areas. This can be applicable to Clips or VODs depending on the laws of the country the content is served. If a stream is set up to be geoblocked, viewers who are outside of the allowed countries will be presented with an error message in the player saying that they are not allowed to view the stream. This is true for viewers on all platforms (web, mobile, smart TVs, etc).

Frequently Asked Questions

When will a geoblocked channel go back to normal?
Some channels will broadcast content that requires them to always be blocked to other regions. However, some channels may request geoblocking for specific rights-protected content for a certain period of time. In these cases it depends on what the channel owner has requested for that particular broadcast. You should contact the channel owner directly if you encounter this error.

For example, If you were showing rights-protected content that was scheduled to end at a certain time, you may continue with post-event streaming that is unblocked. The channel does not need to stop and restart their stream.

If a channel is geoblocked, but wasn’t previously, what does that mean?
Geoblocking content usually happens for a set amount of time, for example if there is a specific campaign or otherwise. The channel can set the geoblocking window to whatever they need.
Why is the channel I am trying to watch geoblocked? They aren’t normally geoblocked?
This can happen if the channel has decided to set up geoblocking in specific circumstances.
How can I request geoblocking of my channel?
In some cases, premium partners may request this through Partner Help or through their partnerships manager.
How does Twitch detect the location of viewers?
When you watch a live stream on Twitch, your web browser or phone app sends a request to Twitch. That request includes your public IP address, which is used to determine your approximate location. Learn more about your Privacy Choices.
What happens if viewers use a VPN or another anonymising service?
If we detect you using a VPN, you’ll see an error. This is the error that you will see.

Getting Started on Twitch - Mobile Streaming

Mobile streaming is a powerful way to connect with your audience, offering the flexibility to stream from anywhere without a computer. This guide suggests leading apps, as well as tips for setup and engaging with your chat. With the right tools, you’ll be ready to start streaming and growing your community on Twitch.

  • Streamlabs Mobile (iOS, Android) — A feature-rich app designed for Twitch integration, offering customizable overlays, alerts, and tools like Collab Cam. Ideal for creators seeking a robust all-in-one streaming solution. Free and paid options.
  • PRISM Live Studio (iOS, Android) — A user-friendly app with multi-platform streaming, adaptive bitrate, and real-time effects. Perfect for beginners and creators looking for stability and versatility. Free.
  • IRL Pro (Android) — An Android-only streaming app that combines multiple internet connections (like WiFi & cellular) to ensure a stable broadcast, and helps you create high-quality streams even with poor reception. Free.
  • Camo Studio (iOS, Android) — Turn your iPad into a fully-featured streaming machine. Connect your cameras and console, choose a scene template, build your own, or import your favorite web-based overlays. Then stream directly to Twitch or record at resolutions up to 4K. Free and paid options.

Getting Started

  • Set Up Your Twitch Account: Create an account, personalize your profile, and set moderation rules. Remember, your content and conduct on Twitch must adhere to the Community Guidelines.
  • Choose and Install a Streaming App: There are many mobile-streaming solutions out there. However, we recommend Streamlabs Mobile, PRISM Live Studio, IRL Pro (Android), or Moblin (iOS).
  • Set Up Alerts and Emotes: Start with Alerts for follows and subscriptions. Try default emotes to engage your audience.
  • Test Your Stream: Perform a test stream to check video quality, alerts, and connectivity. Use strong Wi-Fi and cellular connections for stability for the best mobile-streaming experience, if possible.
  • Promote Your Streams: Share your Twitch channel link on social media with the date and time of your stream, either before or during our broadcasts.
  • Go Live: Set a clear stream title and category. Actively engage with chat to create a welcoming experience.

Key Tips

  • Focus on the Essentials First: Start with follow and subscription alerts to ensure you thank your audience in real time. Start with Twitch’s Default Emotes to make your chat more interactive—these are ready to use and require no custom design. Learn more about emotes.
  • Engage with Your Chat: Engage with your chat: Respond to questions, greet new viewers, and create conversations. Watch and learn how from other streamers!
  • Learn As You Go: Don’t worry about perfection! Authentic and real is what appeals. Focus on creating a welcoming, engaging atmosphere for your audience.
