Delete Clips

Click this icon to delete this clip. To mass delete clips, select the 3 Vertical Dots menu in your Clips Manager, or utilize the checkboxes in the main clip list view.

You can delete clips you’ve made of other channels up until the channel owner edits, features, or export the clip themselves.

Landscape and Portrait Clips

Clips are saved in two formats, landscape and portrait. When reviewing clips in your Clips Manager, landscape and portrait versions appear side by side.

How to Edit Clips

Use the Clip Editor to re-edit the title, trim, or portrait layout of any clips of your channel at any time. To edit your clips, please visit your Creator Dashboard -> Content -> Clips.

  • Select a clip from the Clips Manager.

  • Click Edit (scissors) to open the editor

  • When you open the clip editor, your clip starts with an automatic suggested crop applied based on where your cam and gameplay appear in the frame. If the creator has not previously set layout preferences, auto crop is applied by default. If the creator has previously set layout preferences, auto crop is off by default so their preferences are respected. You can accept, adjust, or dismiss the crop at any time.

  • To manually edit the layout, select Edit Layout to edit the portrait version of your clip.

  • When editing your portrait version clip, select from 2 layouts: Stacked, or Full. Stacked splits your screen into 2 boxes, which is ideal if your stream captures both face cam and gameplay. You can adjust the horizontal line in the Stacked layout to change the size of each box. Full uses 1 box.

Full Layout

Stacked Layout

On the right side of the editor, preview your current layout selections.

  • Once you’re done editing, Apply changes, and Save Clip. If you were editing an existing clip, you’ll need to agree to overwrite the existing clip.

Editing and Removing Captions

Clips created via the Clip That Quick Action or Auto Clips include captions by default. For other clips, captions are included if “Add Captions” was selected at creation. You and your channel editors can edit the caption text, or add or remove captions, on any clip of your channel within 30 days of creation. To manage captions on a clip:

  • Go to Creator Dashboard > Content > Clips
  • Find the clip you want to update
  • Toggle captions on or off, or select Edit (pencil) and then Edit Text to correct the caption wording
  • Select Save to apply your changes

When you edit caption text, the updated captions are reviewed by AutoMod. You won’t see explicit language masked as you type, but it is automatically masked and censored in the final clip.

After 30 days, captions can no longer be changed on that clip.

When using the new picture-in-picture clip creator, the portrait layout editing experience works the same way directly within the overlay.

If a streamer edits a clip of their own channel, that locks the clip from further editing by the viewer who created it.

How to Share Clips

You can share clips from any location they can be watched, including your channel page, the Clips Manager, and at the end of clip creation.

Select the Share button next to the clip and you get the menu of all the ways you can share.

YouTube Shorts

Directly post your clips to YouTube Shorts. The title and description fields are pre-populated with recommended text to optimize your post for visibility and drive viewers back to your stream. If you prefer different text, you can replace the recommended text by typing into the field.

If a streamer has turned on the setting, you can also directly post their clips to your YouTube account. Auto-hashtagging of your Twitch channel name is not supported to YouTube.

TikTok

Directly post your clips to TikTok. The title and description fields are pre-populated with recommended text to optimize your post for visibility and drive viewers back to your stream. If you prefer different text, you can replace the recommended text by typing into the field.

If a streamer has turned on the setting, you can also directly post their clips to your TikTok account. The streamer’s channel name will be auto-hashtagged in your post and it cannot be removed.

Instagram

Directly post your clips to Instagram. The title and description fields are pre-populated with recommended text to optimize your post for visibility and drive viewers back to your stream. If you prefer different text, you can replace the recommended text by typing into the field.

If a streamer has turned on the setting, you can also directly post their clips to your Instagram account. The streamer’s channel name will be auto-hashtagged in your post and it cannot be removed.

Snapchat

Directly post your clips to Snapchat Stories or Spotlight.

If a streamer has turned on the setting, you can also directly post their clips to your Snapchat account.

X.com / Twitter

Quickly post a link to your clip, with pre-filled text.

Facebook

Quickly post a link to your clip, with pre-filled text.

Reddit

Quickly post a link to your clip, with pre-filled text.

Download Clips

Download landscape or portrait mode clips.

If a given clip does not offer a portrait version for download, this means a portrait version has not been created yet for this clip. You can create one by clicking Edit Clip, and adjusting the portrait layout using the steps above, and Saving Clip.

Copy Embed Code

Share clips to your website, by utilizing embed codes. Learn more in our developer portal here.

Clips you and your channel editors make are added to your Stream Recap automatically, unless you’ve turned this off in your Clips Settings. To add any other clip of your channel, select Add to Recap in your Clips Manager.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who can create clips?
All logged-in viewers and streamers can create clips of any channel, provided that:
  • The streamer has enabled clips to be made from their live streams and VODs in their Clips Settings: link.twitch.tv/ClipSettings.
  • The streamer has not enabled additional clip creation settings, such as Followers-only or Subscribers-only.
  • The streamer has not blocked the user attempting to create clips.
How can I update the aspect ratio of my clips?
We recently tested the ability for users to edit the aspect ratio of their portrait clips and discovered that Clips that were not 9x16 aspect ratios caused bugs in areas like the Discovery Feed and Stories. We are going to delay the launch of this feature while the team works to find a solution that ensures a smooth experience.
Why do all my portrait clips appear as landscape clips with black bars behind them?
If you are seeing this, please go to your Clips Manager and click the scissor icon next to any clip to edit the portrait layout. You only have to do this once and we will save your layout preference for all future clips. This allows portrait clips to automatically generate the most optimal layout for you. You can always update your layout preferences again by editing the portrait clip layout before publishing a clip.
As a streamer, can I re-edit clips my viewers created of my channel?
Yes. You can always re-edit the trim, title, and portrait layout of any clip in your Clips Manager.

You can also toggle captions on or off, or edit the caption text, for any clip of your channel within 30 days of when it was created. After 30 days, captions can no longer be changed.

Streamers have the ability to control who can make clips of their content. They also see clips you make, and have the ability to ban you or time you out or delete your clip.

My volume of clips has drastically decreased since the update. Why is that?
With this change, you may notice the overall number of clips created by viewers decrease. We heard your feedback that a lot of clips are created unintentionally. To create clips, be sure to click “Publish” and include a title. This will help limit accidental clips, leaving only intentional clips so it’s easier for you to find quality clips to share. With that being said, the team is exploring ways to increase the supply of high quality, intentional clips.
Why are only landscape clips available to download in my Clips Manager?
If you don’t have the option to download a portrait version, that means a portrait version of the clip has not yet been created.

To create a portrait version of this clip,

  • Edit the clip
  • Choose Edit Layout, then make a change or adjustment to the captured range of content.
  • Apply and Save Changes.

Wait a minute for the newly edited clip to render. Now, you can download this clip in portrait mode.

What happened to the ‘Default to final selections’ checkbox for my portrait layout?
Moving forward, Twitch always remembers your preferences automatically, so you don’t have to. If you edit the portrait layout of any clip of your channel, the next time you or your viewers create a clip of your channel the portrait layout will default to your last used settings.
I don’t see the toggle that lets me add my Channel Name overlay to my Clip. Where did it go?
We have removed the Channel Name overlay with this update. The team is actively evaluating the best ways to showcase your Twitch channel name and looking into making it more customizable, as we heard your feedback that streamers were dissatisfied with the inability to move the logo around and resize.

One great way streamers can continue adding their channel name on their exported clip is via hashtags. When a viewer posts your clip directly to TikTok, Instagram, or Snapchat, we automatically insert your Twitch channel name as a hashtag so potential viewers know where to find you. Auto-hashtagging on clip export is not supported to YouTube.

Are viewers able to go back in and edit the Clip they created? What if I don’t want that Clip to change and want it to remain as is?
Yes a viewer has the same edit functionality as you do for the clips they created. They can go back in and edit the trim, portrait crop, and title. However, the viewer will no longer be able to edit the clip if you have: Featured, edited, exported, or shared a link to it. This is to prevent the clips you care about from being changed.
As a viewer, why don’t I see the same “Share” options outlined in this article?
The clip Share menu is smart, and will only show you the options that apply to you. For example, channel owners see TikTok, YouTube, Instagram, or Snapchat in the menu alongside the link sharing options, whereas a viewer would only see link-sharing options if the streamer has enabled this setting.
Can I create clips on mobile?
Yes! You should be able to find the ‘Clip’ button on the top of the stream. Once you click, you’ll need to add a title. You can edit the clip before publishing, or save it first and then edit it. Have fun creating cool highlights!
Can I edit clips on mobile?
You can trim and title clips during creation on mobile. Portrait clip editing is not yet available on mobile.
Why can’t I create a clip for a particular live stream?
There are a few reasons you may get an error if you try to clip a channel.
  • This channel cannot be clipped - The streamer has disabled the ability to create clips of their channel generally, or the category they are currently streaming.
  • You do not have permission to create a clip - Streamers control who can make clips of their channel. These controls include limiting by follow duration and subscription status.
  • Hmm.. Something went wrong - This error is generally caused by technical issues. Click retry, refresh the page, close and re-open the app or browser, disable browser add-ons or extensions, and check your network connection.
  • If you attempt to make a clip the first 1:30 of a VOD, you may experience an error or unpredictable behavior.
As a streamer, how can I recognize Top Clippers in my channel?
If you have enabled Top Clipper Leaderboards in your channel, your Top Clippers will be automatically displayed at the top of chat. Learn more.
Can I expand the clip creator to full screen?
Yes. To expand the clip creator to full screen, click the Expand View button in the clip creator overlay to open the clip creation flow in a new tab, and close the clip creation modal on the channel page.
Can I switch back to the old clipping experience?
Yes. If you prefer the previous clipping experience, you can switch back by using the toggle in the top-right corner of the clip creator overlay. This will open the clip creation flow in the traditional full-screen format.
Why does my stream audio mute when I start creating a clip?
When you open the clip creator, we automatically mute stream audio so you can focus on the clip audio. You can unmute the stream if needed, which will result in both audio sources playing simultaneously.
What happens if I navigate away from the clip creator, without creating a clip?
If you try to navigate away from the clip creator while creating a clip, we’ll remind you to save your clip first. If you choose to navigate away without saving, your clip will not be saved.
What happens if an ad starts playing while I’m creating a clip?
If an ad starts playing while you have the clip creator open, the clip creator will remain open where it was before the ad started playing. The audio that was playing before the ad started will continue to take precedence.
Can I automatically add clips to my Stream Recap?
Yes. Clips you and your channel editors make are added to your Stream Recap automatically. This is on by default. To change it, go to Creator Dashboard > Settings > Stream and, under Clips Settings, use the Automatically include Clips created by me or my editors in Recaps toggle.
How do I enable captions for my community?
Go to Creator Dashboard > Settings > Stream > Clips Settings. When enabled, viewers who create clips of your channel will see the option to add captions in the Clip Creator. You can change this setting at any time. Turning it off won’t remove captions from clips that were already created with them.

Clips created via the Clip That Quick Action or Auto Clips include captions by default. The Clips Settings page controls captions for both viewer-created clips and Auto Clips. If you disable this setting, future Auto Clips will be created without captions.

Auto Clips created before July 14, 2026 have captions permanently embedded in the video and cannot be removed.

Can I remove captions from a clip after it’s been created?
Yes. You can toggle captions on or off for any clip of your channel within 30 days of when it was created. After 30 days, captions can no longer be changed. Visit your Clips Manager to manage captions.
Can I edit the caption text on a clip?
Yes. You and your channel editors can correct the wording of captions on clips of your channel within 30 days of creation. In your Clips Manager, select the clip, choose Edit (pencil), then Edit Text to make your changes and Save. Edited captions are reviewed by AutoMod. You won’t see explicit language masked as you type, but it is automatically masked and censored in the final clip. After 30 days, captions can no longer be changed.
Why don’t I see the “Add Captions” option when creating a clip?
The “Add Captions” option only appears in the Clip Creator if the streamer has enabled captions for their channel. If you don’t see it, the streamer hasn’t turned on this setting yet. Clips created via the Clip That Quick Action or Auto Clips include captions by default — you won’t see a separate toggle in the Clip Creator for these clip creation methods.
What is the crop suggestion I see when creating a clip?
When you create a clip, you’ll see a suggested crop that keeps your cam and gameplay in frame. You can accept it, adjust it, or dismiss it. Choose any aspect ratio from landscape (16:9) to portrait (9:16) — empty space is filled with a blur effect. If your cam or gameplay can’t be confidently identified, you’ll see a centered crop as a starting point.
What happens if auto crop can’t detect my cam?
If auto crop can’t confidently detect a face cam or gameplay region (for example, during IRL streams, music streams, or content without a standard overlay), it defaults to a centered crop at the selected aspect ratio instead of showing a bad suggestion. You can adjust from there or switch to a different ratio.
Does Auto Crop use facial recognition?
No. Auto Crop looks to see if a face is in the frame, but does not perform identification or recognition. After the crop is made, no data about your face is saved, stored, or used beyond that moment.

How To Give A Shoutout

Shoutouts are a great way to show your support for another streamer and help them grow. Shoutouts let you promote another channel to viewers who are not following them, so they can follow the channel without leaving your stream.

How Do Shoutouts Work?

Using the shoutout command prompts your viewers to follow a channel and lets the streamer know how many viewers saw the shoutout.

For You And Your Mods

To initiate a shoutout, type /shoutout followed by the name of the channel you wish to share with your viewers. For example, to give OtherStrimmer a shoutout, you’d type /shoutout OtherStrimmer.

The shoutout chat command can only be used once every two minutes while your stream is live.

Shoutouts can only be given to the same person once every hour.

For Your Viewers

When you give a shoutout it appears in chat.

Viewers who do not follow the channel will see a pop-up Follow button that lets them follow the channel directly from your page. More information about the channel is shared in the expanded view of the pop-up (when available).

If the channel has an upcoming scheduled stream, the pop-up will show the date/time/title of the stream, including a Reminder button. This reminder enables a one-time notification when the streamer goes live.

If the channel does not have a future stream scheduled, their 3 most recently streamed categories will be shown instead.

For the Channel Receiving the Shoutout

The channel is notified about the shoutout in the activity feed of their stream manager. The notification lets them know who gave them the shoutout, how many viewers were present, and how long ago it happened.

For the Mods & Broadcaster

A record of the shoutout will appear in the actions panel of mod view. This log will share when the shoutouts happened, who called the shoutout, and which channel was shouted out. Only successful shoutouts will appear in this log. If multiple mods try to shout someone out, only the first will go through and be recorded.

How to Report a Shoutout

If you receive a shoutout that is offensive or inappropriate, you have the option to report that channel. To do so, click the 3 Vertical Dots menu next to the shoutout notification in your activity feed and select Report. If a mod gave a shoutout that you do not approve of, please address this with them personally as the channel owner.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I shoutout my own channel?

You cannot give yourself a shoutout. It’s not necessary to do this, as a follow button is embedded in your channel page, always visible to viewers.

Can a moderator shout themselves out?

Yes! We know lots of you shoutout your mods as a way to show them love, but we also know you are often relying on them to help you out while you are live.

Who can see shoutouts?

Everyone in your chat can see the shoutout, but only those who are not following that channel will also see the pop-up with the follow button. The channel you shouted out can also see a record in their activity feed, including how many viewers were there when you shouted them out. Finally, the broadcaster and mods for that channel can check past shoutouts in the mod logs.

If a user I blocked is given a shoutout, will I see their name?

Within a few weeks after launch, you should not see shoutouts given to users that you have blocked.

When should I use shoutouts?

A great reason to give a shoutout is when another streamer joins your stream or says something in chat, but a streamer does not need to be present in your chat to receive a shoutout. You can also give a streamer a shoutout before you raid their channel so that viewers who are not able to participate in the raid have an easy way to follow the channel so they can check it out later.

How to Use Collections

Collections are playlists which let you organize and show off your best work. You can create Collections for any set of videos you want to highlight on your channel, whether it is a general introduction reel, a recurring show, each game you stream, or creative projects that span across multiple streams on your channel.

Managing Collections

To begin, navigate to your dashboard. Once there, click the Hamburger icon to open the menu. Under Content, click Collections.

Creating Collections

To create a collection, enter the desired name of your collection into the Title field at the top of the page. Then, click the Create Collection button.

A channel can have up to 100 collections, and a collection can have up to 200 videos.

Editing Collections

Creating a collection or clicking an existing collection will open the Edit Collection screen. Here, you can edit the Title and Description of your collection. You can also click the Share button in the bottom left-hand corner to access a direct link to your collection and a number of other options for sharing.

To add a video to your collection, click Add Videos in the bottom left-hand corner. Doing so will bring up a list of eligible videos to add to your collection, starting with the most recent. Scrolling will load more videos, and you can use the Search your videos field to look for a specific video.

Once you’ve added videos to your collection, they’ll appear below the Edit Collection panel. To change the order the videos in a collection will play, click and drag each video up or down the list using the dotted anchor point on the left-hand side. Clicking the 3 Vertical Dots on the right hand side of a video will allow you to use that video as the thumbnail for the collection, or remove it from the collection entirely.

Deleting Collections

To delete a collection, click the 3 Vertical Dots next to the relevant collection on the Collections page and select Delete. You can also delete a collection by clicking on the trash can icon in the bottom left-hand corner on the Edit Collection screen.

Featuring Collections

Collections can be featured on your channel’s video page along with your Clips, VODs, highlights, etc. Click the Feature Collections button in the top right-hand corner of the Collections page to be taken straight to the layout customization for the Featured section of your video page. To access customization from your channel page, click Customize Layout when filtering your video tab by Featured. To add a collection to your page:

  • Click Add Section.
  • Scroll to your chosen collection and click Add.
  • Click and drag your new section to the desired place on your video page using the dotted anchor point on the left-hand side of the panel.

To remove a collection, click the 3 Vertical Dots on the right-hand side and select Remove.

How to Use Go Live Notifications

Notifications for viewers are important and sometimes you may just want to add a little bit of a personal touch into your going live notifications. Whether it’s a meme, information about the broadcast, or just a more personalized notification you’re looking to send to your viewers; Go Live Notifications have got you covered!

About Go Live Notifications

To get started with sending a custom Go Live Notification simply head to the Stream Manager section of your dashboard. Here, click Edit Stream Info under the Quick Actions panel.

If you’d like to be able to access your Stream Info settings at all times, click the Edit icon on the top left-hand corner of your Stream Manager page. This will open the Edit Stream Manager Layout panel. You can drag panels you’d like to add or remove to and from the page here.

We’ve given you 140 characters to play around with! Go Live Notifications are reviewed by AutoMod and won’t send if you enter anything you wouldn’t say to grandma.

You’ll also want to make sure that your Go Live Notification text is correct as you will only be able to send one Go Live Notification per broadcast. Once you go live the notification will be sent to all of your followers that have notifications enabled - your custom notification will also be visible in going live emails and push notifications.

Make sure to write a custom message with your Go Live notifications. If you leave the notification field blank, viewers will only see a default message: “User is now live”. Adding a custom message can help with engagement and increase the click-through rate of your notifications.

Go Live notifications are limited to one per 4 hour broadcast session. You may resend another notification 4 hours after the last one and after restarting your broadcast.

Frequently Asked Questions

What happens if I don’t enter anything into the Go Live notification field?
If you don’t enter anything into the Go Live notification field we will send out standard live notifications to your viewers. You are free to add or remove custom notifications at anytime!
Why won’t it let me use my custom message?
If you are unable to use a custom message it is likely due to the message being over the 140 character limit or your message was flagged by AutoMod. Please see the information noted in red below the Go Live notification field for more information on why your message is not being accepted.
Can I use global or sub emotes in my custom message?
Unfortunately, you cannot use emotes in your custom Go Live notification.
Is there any analytical data I can see to see engagement on my custom Go Live notification?
Yes! Please see the How have my custom go live notifications performed? panel of your Channel Analytics for information on your notification engagement. For more information about Channel Analytics, please see our help article.
How can I report inappropriate custom Go Live notifications?
Go Live notification messages are currently served through email notifications and push notifications.

To report an inappropriate notification sent via email, open the notification email. At the bottom of this email you will find a link that will take you to a report page.

To report an inappropriate notification sent via iOS push notifications simply swipe left on the notification and select the report option.

If you are unable to report via any of the above processes, you may file a report on the channel directly by following instructions located in our article on how to file a user report.

How to Use Polls

Polls can be created by streamers and voted on by viewers. Polls are a great way for streamers to gauge feedback from their community, figure out what game they should play next or even just ask their community how they’re doing today. Streamers can start a poll at any time and viewers can begin to vote on their option.

The ability to create Polls is exclusive to monetized streamers. Learn more.

On this page:

  • Voting in Polls
  • Creating Polls
  • Using the Poll overlay
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Voting in Polls

When a Poll is created a modal will be displayed at the top of the chat window. You can expand the poll to see what the question and selection of choices are by clicking the Arrow Down icon. Options can be voted on by selecting the option and clicking the Vote button. Alternatively, you can vote using chat commands by typing /vote and the number of your desired option.

For example: /vote 2 would vote for “Level” on the poll in the screenshot below.

Polls can be configured by the streamer to be:

  • Additional votes with Channel Points (not available on mobile)

Eligible voters, depending on the Poll settings, will be able to vote once for free on their answer choice. If the Poll has been configured to accept additional votes using Channel Points you may continue to vote using Channel Points for each consecutive vote.

Channel Points used for voting in Polls are not anonymous and are non-refundable to your Channel Points balance. Be sure to verify you have selected the correct option before proceeding to vote.

Once a poll has ended, the results will be displayed for one minute and additional votes will not be accepted.

Creating Polls

Polls can be created by streamers from the Dashboard and new Creator Dashboard.

On your Dashboard for your first Poll click the Create a New Poll button if you have never created a Poll before. If you have created a Poll previously you will see the last Poll you started with the option to view the results and start a new Poll with the New Poll button.

On the new Creator Dashboard, you will first need to add the Manage Poll quick action by adding a new quick action and selecting the Manage your poll option under the Grow Your Community section. From there you can click Manage Poll in your quick action list and clicking New Poll.

Start by creating a title (i.e. the question you’d like to ask) for your Poll such as “What game should I play next?” or “How was everyone’s day?”. There is a 60 character limit for the title so keep it short and concise!

Next add the options that your viewers can vote on, a Poll needs a minimum of 2 options and you can add up to 5 total.

Each option is limited to 25 characters.

Polls can be configured with various settings. Below is a description of each setting:

Setting

Description

Allow Voting with Channel Points

If enabled, this allows viewers to make additional votes using Channel Points on top of the 1 regular vote they get. You will need to set the amount of Channel Points needed per additional vote on the Poll.

Duration

The duration of time the Poll will run before ending.

Once you’ve configured your Poll, click the Start Poll button and watch the results come in on your Creator Dashboard.

On the Poll panel you will be able to see a real time breakdown of your Poll results and the option to end the Poll early on your Dashboard.

Once a Poll has ended a Poll breakdown will be made available to you. The breakdown will be available at:

[twitch.tv](https://twitch.tv/popout/yourusername/poll)

Click Vote Breakdown and you will find an outline of the final results, number of voters and how many Channel Points were contributed if Channel Points voting was enabled. You’ll also be able to see the top contributors from voting with Channel Points.

Using the Poll overlay

The Poll overlay allows you to display the currently active Poll on your channel onto your stream. You can do this by adding a browser source into your active scene and using the following URL - replace yourusername with your own username:

[twitch.tv](https://www.twitch.tv/popout/yourusername/poll)

Frequently Asked Questions

Where can I use Polls?
Polls are available to monetized streamers via the Creator Dashboard.
How many Polls can I run consecutively?
Only one Poll can be ran at a time.
I voted on the wrong option using Channel Points, can I be refunded my Channel Points?
Unfortunately not, all votes using Channel Points are final and cannot be returned.
Can my Moderators and Editors start a Poll for me?
Channel Moderators and Editors can create and manage a Poll through the /poll command in chat which will bring up the Poll module. Channel Moderators and Editors can also end and delete polls with /endpoll and /deletepoll respectively.
I don’t want to vote in the Poll, how can I dismiss it?
While a Poll is running it may be collapsed by clicking the arrow icon. When a Poll has ended it can be dismissed / closed out from your chat view.
I don’t think the Poll question / answers were appropriate, how can I report?
You may report a Poll by clicking the 3 Vertical Dots icon and selecting the option to Report Poll.

How to Use Raids

Using Raids, any creator (regardless of Affiliate or Partner status) can send viewers over to another channel after a stream. Raiding can be a great way to make connections and network with other broadcasters by sharing audiences and growing your communities.

On this page:

  • How Do Raids Work?
  • Choosing a Raids Recipient
  • Managing and Moderating Raids
  • Frequently Asked Questions

How Do Raids Work?

A raid sends everyone connected to chat at the time of the raid to the recipient channel.

Raids can be started from mobile. To start a raid, type /raid followed by the name of the channel you wish to raid. For example, to raid the TwitchPresents channel, you’d type /raid TwitchPresents.

If you aren’t sure who to raid, you can easily preview a suggested list of channels by clicking the Raid Channel quick action in your Creator Dashboard. You can also type /raidbrowser to bring up the same menu. The Raid Browser is not available in the Twitch mobile app. Learn more.

Once you initiate a raid, a pop up at the top of the chat tracks the number of participants and begins a countdown to the raid start. Viewers will be able to opt out of joining before the raid begins. After 10 seconds (or when everyone’s ready to go), click Raid Now to redirect everyone connected to chat to the target channel. If Cancel or Raid Now is not clicked before the purple countdown bar at the bottom depletes, the raid will automatically begin.

Raids are best used at the end of your broadcast. If you raid another channel while online, your viewers will be redirected from your channel to the new channel. However, any new viewers entering your page will see your stream, not the target raid channel.

When a channel is raided, a message in chat notifies everyone on the target channel about the raid and the number of participating raiders.

The broadcaster can see recent raids from their Stream Manager in the Activity Feed as well.

Moderators and broadcasters can review recent raids via the Settings cog in the bottom right-hand corner of the chat panel. Select Tasks -> Review Recent Raids

Choosing A Raids Recipient

Quickly identify a channel to raid using the Raids Browser.

Select the Raid Channel Quick Action in the Creator Dashboard, or use /raidbrowser to open a dialog displaying a searchable, filterable channel browser.

From this module, review channel name, stream title, current category, viewer counter, video thumbnail, uptime, tags, and other information. Use the following filters to refine your search:

  • For You (Default) - A curated list of channels that Twitch has created for you, including creators you follow, you’ve watched, or that could be a good fit for your community.
  • Same Category - The For You list, but filtered only to channels streaming the same category as you.
  • Following - A list of channels you follow that are live right now.
  • Raided You - Channels that have Raided you in the last 30 days.
  • Events - (Special events like Streamer-versary, Charity, Drops enabled, Stream Together)
  • Similar or Similar Size - A list of channels with similar or smaller viewership than yours.

You can sort results by:

  • For You (Default) - In order of our best suggestions for you.
  • Viewers (low to high)
  • Viewers (high to low)
  • Channel Name (A to Z)
  • Uptime (low to high)

You may not attempt to raid a channel that has blocked yours. An error message will be shown instead.

Before clicking Start Raid you can preview a stream.

Managing and Moderating Raids

While raids are intended to be a positive, collaborative experience, it’s important that broadcasters are able to maintain control over their channel. There are a number of tools available that can help broadcasters manage incoming raids.

Incoming Raid Settings

Click here to manage who can raid your channel. Your Raid settings offer a variety of options for who is allowed to raid you. You can customize the following:

Viewer count limitations:

When another channel raids you, they must have a viewer count that falls into the range you have listed. This will be the total number of viewers they have at the time they select you to raid, and not the total number of viewers who will ultimately participate in the raid. If you edit the minimum or maximum number of viewers, offline channels will not be able to raid you.

Account age limitations:

For a channel to raid you successfully, their account must have been created x number of days ago, where x is the number of days you select in your settings.

Additional Groups:

Finally, you can select from a list of checkboxes. Selecting these groups is completely optional. If you check any boxes, any incoming raid must meet only one of the chosen requirements, not all, and the raiding channel must meet the viewer and account age thresholds.

Creators in multiple teams who select My teammates will only receive raids from members of their main team. Click here to manage your main team.

If you would like to allow any and all raids, do not select any of the optional groups, leave your minimum viewer count at 1 and maximum at “No max” (don’t enter anything) and drop the account age to zero.

Only the channel owner has permissions to view and edit these settings. These settings are for your comfort and safety, so we do not suggest sharing your selections with anyone.

Managing Incoming Raids While You Are Live

You can temporarily deny all incoming raids for up to an hour. To do so, you will need to add the Stop Raids for 1 Hour quick action to your stream manager and enable raids in your raids settings. Use this quick action at any time during your stream to disable all incoming raids. To re-enable raids, either let the timer run to 0 or use the quick action to accept raids before the hour is over.

You can edit your incoming raids settings by clicking the Settings icon at the top of the quick action. Any changes you make will be enabled as soon as you save, even if you are live.

Managing Raids Via Chat Settings

Using chat moderation settings, you can reduce spam from an incoming raid or - if need be - shut the raid down entirely. To access these settings, click the cog in the bottom right-hand corner of the chat window and look for CHANNEL MODES

  • Emotes-Only: Emotes-only chat prevents anyone from posting anything other than emotes while enabled.
  • Subscribers-Only: In this mode, only your subscribers can post in the chat (requires Partner/Affiliate status).
  • Followers-Only: In this mode, only your followers can post in the chat. You can set the duration a person needs to be following your channel before they can post.
  • Slow Mode: This mode requires users to wait a set amount of time (customizable by you) between sending messages. Subscribers can be exempted via your Partner/Affiliate settings.
Report or Chat Ban a Raiding Channel

If an offensive or inappropriate raid is sent to your channel, you have the option to report or chat ban the raiding channel. To do so, click the Settings cog in the bottom right-hand corner of the chat window, then click Review Recent Raids under the Tasks section. Click Report or Ban as appropriate. People that you have banned will not be able to raid your channel in the future.

Managing Individual Harassment in Chat

Broadcasters and their channel moderators can timeout or ban individual raiders as necessary, or turn on Auto-Mod to manage chat messages. To learn more about general moderation tools available to you, please see our help articles on How to Manage Harassment in Chat and How to Use AutoMod.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I choose which channel to raid?
You can raid any channel you want, so long as the recipient’s settings allow you to raid them. Raiding your peers can be an easy way to share audiences and raiding a smaller streamer just might make their day! If you’re not sure who to raid, you can use the Raids Browser to help you find a few good options quickly. Try out ‘streamer-versary’ or ‘raided you’ quick filters to help you find the right channel to raid.
I tried to Raid a channel, and it won’t let me. Why is that?
If you attempt to Raid a channel, you will see a notice preventing you from doing this. The channel you are intending to Raid has enabled settings that do not allow you to raid them.
Do my raid settings affect participating raiders, or the channel that is initiating the raid?
Your incoming raid settings impact the channel that initiates the raid, not participating raiders.
How do I respond to incoming raids?
Visit our Safety Center if you need help with an unwanted raid.

If you get raided, here are a few tips to capture the attention of the raiders:

  • Thank the streamer and raiders for joining.
  • Introduce yourself to the raiders - keep it short, be genuine and talk about what your channel is about. If you know the person raiding you, introduce them to your community too.

With a bit of luck, the raiders will stick around or even follow you. The next time you stream, try using the /raidbrowser ‘raided you’ filter to find channels that have raided you and are live to share the fun.

Do raids work on mobile?
As a streamer or editor, you can start or join raids as a viewer on mobile devices. As a viewer, you can join raids on mobile devices. Incoming raids settings are managed on web.
Will viewers coming from a raid see pre-roll ads?
No. When a raid begins, neither the raiding creator nor their audience sees pre-roll ads upon arrival at the raided channel. Depending on the channel, some viewers can still receive mid-rolls if one is actively playing when joining via raid. Learn more about pre-rolls and mid-roll ads.

Creators may see pre-rolls when browsing channels to raid, but these do not appear once the raid begins.

How to Use Suggested Channels

On October 3rd, 2022, we deprecated the /host and /unhost command. Visit the FAQ for more info. We encourage you to use the Raid feature instead. If you’re looking for information about the Raids feature, please see our How to Use Raids help article!

Autohost is now called suggested channels, and no longer interacts with host mode. Suggested channels no longer appear in the “live” view of the channel page.

Suggested channels is a channel feature available to all users across the site. Suggested channels allow broadcasters to choose a list of channels to be featured on their offline channel page.

Suggested channels are picked from your suggested channels list. Any broadcaster can suggest another channel, and any channel can be suggested. It works just like using an embedded video player on another website, except that the embed is located in your channel page’s carousel.

Using the suggested channels feature, you can set your channel to automatically suggest a list of pre-approved channels when you are not live. Suggested channels are a great way to support your fellow broadcasters and help grow your community.

On this page:

  • Adding to your Suggested Channels
  • To Disable Suggested Channels
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Adding to your Suggested Channels List

Suggested channels are enabled by default, so all you need to do is add channels to your list, and set the priority.

To add specific channels to your suggested list:

  • Visit your Creator Dashboard.
  • Click Settings
  • Click Channel and then Featured Content.
  • Select Suggested Channels

On this page, use the search box to find and add channels to your suggested list. Once you’ve populated your list, you can change the order by dragging and dropping channels up and down the host list.

Suggested Channel Priority

There are two settings to determine priority of your suggested channels: If Display channels in an order personalized to each viewer is selected, the order of the list will determine suggestion priority.

If Display channels in an order personalized to each viewer is selected, the priority will be determined based on the viewer, not the order of the list.

Suggested channels will only display channels from the existing, curated list of channels selected by the suggesting streamer, regardless of which priority mode is selected.

To remove specific channels from your suggested channels:

To remove a channel from your suggested channels list, click the trash can next to their channel name.

To Disable Suggested Channels

If you ever toggle suggested channels off, your existing settings will be saved.

To disable Suggested Channels:

  • Visit your Creator Dashboard.
  • Click Settings
  • Click Channel and then Featured Content.
  • Under the Suggested Channels section, click the Suggested Channels toggle to OFF.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is changing with Host Mode, and when is it happening?

Host mode is going away on October 3, 2022. After this date, the “/host” chat command and the “Host Channel” Stream Manager quick action will no longer be available. In addition, “Autohost” will be changed to “Suggested Channels” in your channel settings.

Why are you deprecating Host Mode?

We introduced host mode in 2014 to make it easy for streamers to give their viewers another stream to watch when they went offline. Since its launch, we’ve learned that streamers want to share their viewers with other streamers to help them grow and have introduced features that help you do that.

We made the decision to deprecate this feature because the experience it delivers to viewers doesn’t match their expectations when they come to Twitch. Viewers want to interact with a streamer when they’re live and host mode blocks this from happening. Preventing viewers from interacting with the streamer they’re watching also limits a streamer’s growth potential because they’re not able to build meaningful connections with those new viewers.

What should I do to help support the growth of other streamers once Host Mode is removed?

As a streamer, the most effective way you can help another streamer grow is by promoting them to your viewers when you’re live. You can also endorse their channel on your offline channel page.

  • Give them a shoutout to help them gain more followers*. Use the chat command /shoutout [channel] to share a follow button in chat so that your viewers can follow them without leaving your stream. If the streamer has a stream schedule set up on their channel, the shoutout will also highlight their next scheduled stream with a button to set a reminder to watch.
  • Send your viewers to their channel at the end of your stream. Use the chat command “/raid [channel]” to send everyone on your channel to their channel. Not only is it a great way to connect and network with other streamers, you’re also helping your viewers form connections with other communities.
  • Suggest their channel to viewers when you’re offline. Add them to the Suggested Channels list in your channel settings (formerly known as your “Autohost list”) to endorse their channel to those who visit your channel when you’re offline. When their channel is live, their stream will appear in the carousel at the top of the page. You can also display your suggested streamers list in your streamer shelf.

What’s the difference between raiding and hosting?

When you raid a channel, all of the viewers currently watching on your channel page are redirected to the target channel page. This is different from Host Mode, which embeds the target channel’s video directly on your channel page. Host Mode does not redirect anyone currently on the page at the time of the host, keeping them on your page and in your chat. In terms of use cases, raiding is a great thing to do at the end of your broadcast to send all of your viewers over to another channel to spread the love and hype, while Host Mode is better used as a showcase tool for content you wish to share with your viewers while your stream is offline. For more information about Raids, please see our How to Use Raids help article.

Does adding channels to my suggested channels list change what viewers see if my channel is embedded on an external site?

No, suggesting channels does not affect what viewers see on any embedded version of your broadcast.

Do the channels I suggest receive viewers when viewed from my channel page carousel?

Yes. Suggested channels receive credit for viewers who view from your channel page carousel. The suggested channel will see those viewers included in their channel analytics overview.

How does advertising work when suggesting channels on my channel page carousel?

Viewers of the hosted channel will see advertising from that channel while you have suggested channels turned on, exactly as if they were on that channel’s page directly.

Who gets ad revenue from ads shown by the suggested channel?

The suggested channel will receive credit for ad impressions viewed from the suggesting channel’s carousel.

Can moderators from a suggested channel mod in the channel that is suggesting them?

No. The chat remains as the chat of the host channel. The rules for that chat do not change.

Will I receive notifications when someone adds me to their suggested channels list?

No.

Can I manage my suggested channels list on mobile?

No - you will need to manage this list via the website or desktop app.

How can I remove a suggested channel from my channel page carousel?

If you wish to stop suggesting a certain channel, you may delete the channel from your suggested channels list, or turn off suggested channels in your channel settings. This can be accessed by navigating to your Channel Settings and clicking Featured Content.

Leaderboards Guide

Leaderboards are a great way to give your viewers recognition and kudos for supporting your channel through gifting, cheering, or creating top clips of a stream.Usernames of your top supporters will be pinned to the respective leaderboard at the top of the chat window, if enabled by channel owners. Leaderboards are only available on monetized channels today. Monetized streamers can choose to enable or disable one or more of the leaderboards for their channel. Read more about the different types of Leaderboards and how to manage Leaderboard settings below.

Leaderboards on Twitch

Leaderboards help streamers recognize and reward top supporters on their channel. Streamers can set leaderboard refresh daily, weekly, monthly, or keep them set for all-time. There are three different Leaderboards on Twitch today: Top Cheerers, Top Clipper(s), and Top Gifters.

Top Gifters: Earn a spot on the leaderboard for gifting the most subs during a leaderboard cycle.

Top Cheerers: Earn a spot on the leaderboard for sending the most Cheers during a leaderboard cycle.

Top Clippers: Earn a spot for clipping the most-viewed clip of that channel during a leaderboard cycle.

The top 3 usernames on each leaderboard will be pinned to the top of chat and earn a channel-level chat badge for as long as they hold their top 3 spot during the leaderboard cycle.

Leaderboards can be found at the top of the chat window on eligible channels. If more than one leaderboard is enabled, viewers can click the arrows on either side of the leaderboard(s) to switch between them. Viewers can click each leaderboard to expand it and see the full leaderboard (up to 5 for Top Clippers and up to 10 for Gifters and Cheerers).

Leaderboards Settings

Leaderboard settings can only be managed on desktop in your Creator Dashboard.

Monetized streamers may access Leaderboards settings in the Creator Dashboard. There, in the left-hand panel, click Monetization -> Community -> Leaderboards, or search for “Leaderboard Settings” using the search bar.

Within your settings, you can toggle the Top Cheerers, Top Clippers, or Top Gifters Leaderboards at any time by clicking on the toggle next to Enable Top Cheerers, Enable Top Clippers, or Enable Top Gifters.

Using the Default Leaderboard setting, you can pick which leaderboard will display by default on your channel by clicking the drop down menu.

The Leaderboard Time Range setting has the following options as radio buttons:

  • Daily
  • Weekly
  • Monthly
  • All-Time

Choose Daily for a leaderboard that automatically resets every day at 12:00AM PT. Choose Weekly for a leaderboard that automatically resets every Monday at 12:00 AM PT. Choose Monthly to reset every 1st day of the month. Choose All-Time for a leaderboard that tracks the Top Gifters, Top Clippers, and/or Top Cheerers in your channel for all time, starting from when Gifts launched in November of 2017, and when Bits launched in June of 2016.

Frequently Asked Questions

If I make one of the top 3 spots on a leaderboard and unlock a badge, how long do I get to keep it?
If you unlock a badge, you keep it for as long as you keep that ranking. Leaderboard badges are granted and auto-equipped immediately. For example, if you are in the #1 spot and someone overtakes you, they will get the #1 badge right away. At that point, you would then have the #2 badge until you are overtaken again, or overtake the person in the #1 slot. If the creator has their leaderboards set to ‘weekly’, the leaderboard resets every 7 days on Monday at 12:01 AM PT, at which point all 3 badges disappear until someone again qualifies to take one of the top 3 spots.
As a streamer, how can I turn a leaderboard off?
Streamers may turn off each Leaderboard in their Creator Dashboard. In your Leaderboards Settings (found underneath the Monetization -> Community -> Leaderboard), you’ll find an option to disable or enable individual leaderboards.
When does an “All-Time” Top Clipper Leaderboard begin tracking?
The All-Time Leaderboard allows you to see Top Clippers over your entire channel’s history.
As a streamer, how can I remove a clip from my Top Clipper Leaderboard?
To remove a clip from your Top Clipper Leaderboard, delete the clip.
What happens when a Top Cheerer, Clipper, or Gifter is banned / unbanned from a channel?
When a Top Cheerer, Clipper, or Gifter is banned from a channel’s chat, their Top Cheer, Clipper, or Gift count will be removed from the leaderboard and everyone below the banned user will move up a spot.

If the previous Top Cheerer, Top Clipper, or Top Gifter is unbanned, they will be eligible to receive their position again should they still qualify. As banned users are not able to Cheer or gift subscriptions, their position may have changed.

Please note that only permanent chat bans affect leaderboard standings. Timeouts do not affect leaderboards placement.

As a viewer, what if I don’t want to be included on a leaderboard?
Viewers who have turned on Hide Progressive Gifter Badge and Gifts Given Count in their Security and Privacy settings (or who have gifted anonymously) will not appear on Gifting leaderboards. You cannot remove yourself from Top Cheerer leaderboards. To remove yourself from the Top Clipper leaderboards, delete the clip you created.

You cannot delete a clip if it has been featured.

Low Latency Video

Low Latency mode is a feature that allows a broadcaster to reduce the delay between their broadcast and their viewers. This feature allows broadcasters to respond more quickly to their chat and fosters closer interactions between broadcasters and their community.

In March 2019, Low Latency mode changed from an opt-in to an opt-out model after overwhelmingly positive feedback from the community. Low latency mode is now enabled on most channels by default, but you can still choose to turn it off if you encounter issues or interactivity is not a focus of your channel.

On this page:

  • Low Latency Settings
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Low Latency Settings

To disable or enable low latency on your channel, head to your dashboard. Click the Hamburger icon, then open the Preferences drop down menu and select Stream. Latency mode settings can be found under the Stream Key & Preferences section at the top of the page. Here, you can pick Low latency or Normal latency.

You will need to restart your stream in order for the changes to take effect.

Frequently Asked Questions

What browsers/platforms are supported for low latency?

We currently support low latency on desktop Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and the Twitch desktop app. We also support low latency on the Android Twitch mobile app, Android TV, Xbox One and PS4.

What should I, as a broadcaster, do if I’m seeing unusually poor quality of service while using low latency mode?

If you’ve recently enabled low latency and are now seeing issues with your broadcast, please try disabling low latency to see if this resolves the issue.

What should I, as a viewer, do if I’m seeing unusually poor quality of service when viewing in low latency?

As a viewer, you can disable low latency locally. To do so, click the Settings icon on the bottom right corner of the video player, then click Advanced. You can toggle low latency on and off in this section.

How can I check the latency for a channel I’m currently viewing?

You can check your Latency to Broadcaster and Latency Mode (along with a number of other stats) by toggling Video Stats under the Advanced menu on the Settings icon on the bottom right hand corner of the video player.

Managing Roles For Your Channel

There are currently six roles that you can assign to people. Depending on the role, the individual will get a chat badge to display next to their name in your channel’s chat. In addition, some roles give the individual access to restricted areas or privileges on your channel.

Types of Roles

Role

Description

Editor

Editors can access a channel’s Creator Dashboard and use most creator tools on the channel’s behalf, including:

  • Stream info: Edit the title, category, tags, and content classification labels, and edit the stream schedule
  • Ads: Run commercial breaks, manage Ads Manager settings, and view and snooze scheduled ads
  • Raids: Start, cancel, and pause raids, find channels to raid, manage raid settings, and view recent raids
  • Engagement: Create polls and Community Goals, and add stream markers
  • Collaboration: Manage Stream Together settings
  • Channel page: Edit featured content shelves, the channel trailer, and social links
  • Videos: Edit video info, upload videos, create highlights, manage collections, start reruns, and download past broadcasts
  • Clips: Review, search, sort, and delete clips (including mass deleting), and set clipping permissions
  • Activity Feed: View and pin events

Moderator

Moderators help manage a creator’s chat to help ensure that it stays safe, welcoming, and fun by performing the following actions:

  • Warn, time out or ban users
  • Enable slow, Emote-only, Subscriber-only, or Follower-only chat modes
  • Start, manage, and end polls
  • Start, manage, and end Predictions

Lead Moderator

Lead moderators can perform all the actions that regular moderators can, as well as the following actions:

  • Manage the mod team (adding or removing other moderators)
  • Add or remove the VIP role for other users
  • Access all channel moderation settings (regular moderators will not have access to certain settings). Note: The one exception is that private blocked terms will remain visible only to the channel owner.
  • Delete mod comments (including by other lead mods or the channel owner).

VIP

VIPs are valuable members of a creator’s community who are recognized with a special badge. VIPs can perform the following actions:

  • Chat without being affected by slow, sub-only, or followers-only modes
  • Chat without being affected by rate limits
  • Post links in chat even when links are disabled

Artist

Artists are members of a creator’s community who are recognized for their contributions to the brand/style of the creator’s channel, such as through emotes, overlays, avatars, and more. There are five (5) artist badges available for each channel.

Business Manager

Business Managers receive access to a creator’s dashboard to help them manage their business. A Business Manager will have access to the following pages in the Creator Dashboard:

  • Analytics Overview
  • Stream Summary
  • Earnings Analytics
  • Sponsorships Portal, including Creator Profile

Business Managers cannot view the Revenue/Payouts section of the Creator Dashboard or change a creator’s payout method.

If the creator has joined the Sponsorship Program, the Business Manager will also be able to accept and decline sponsorship opportunities within a creator’s dashboard on behalf of the creator and receive notifications (both on-site and via email) when new offers are available. Certain campaigns can only be accepted by the creator themselves, for example when the payout amount surpasses a certain threshold.

After a creator appoints a user as their Business Manager, that user will need to accept the role the next time they access the creator’s dashboard before they can view the contents of the pages listed above.

How to Manage Roles

To manage the roles of your community members, go to your Creator Dashboard. Click on the Community option in the menu, then Roles Manager. You will see a list of all the individuals who currently have a role (e.g., Editor, Moderator, Lead Moderator, VIP, Artist, and/or Business Manager) on your channel.

Adding Roles

If you have not assigned any roles on your channel you will be greeted with a popup to help you quickly assign your first role. Simply click Add a Role.

If you already had individuals assigned to roles on your channel, a list of those will populate instead. You will need to click on the Add New button.

Next, you will search for the individual you want to assign a role to. Once you find them, check which role from the drop down you want to assign, and click the Save button.

Additional Steps for Adding Business Managers

Business Managers have enhanced access to your Twitch channel and personal data. For that reason, there are a few additional steps that need to be taken before you can add someone to that role in your channel.

First, we will ask you to review the Business Manager role details, and confirm that you want to add the selected user to the role:

After you confirm, and their role has been added, your Business Manager must accept before being granted enhanced access to your channel.

To accept the role, your new Business Manager must first navigate to your Creator Dashboard at dashboard.twitch.tv. Then, they must navigate to a page in the Creator Dashboard that requires the Business Manager role to access, such as the Sponsorship Portal (https://dashboard.twitch.tv/CHANNEL/monetization/sponsorships/browse).

Business Managers must replace CHANNEL in the above link with the username of the channel they manage. For channels with localized display names (Arabic, Chinese, Korean, or Japanese characters), use the English username, not the display name.

To accept the role, your Business Manager must confirm that they are at least 18 years old and are authorized to take actions on your behalf, and acknowledge that the Twitch Terms of Service apply to all actions they take on Twitch as a Business Manager.

As a channel owner you can unassign the Business Manager role from appointed users at any time. You can add a maximum of five Business Managers to your channel.

Editing Roles

If you need to change an individual’s roles, locate them in the list. Click the Add button next to their name, and check the box next to the role you wish to add from the menu.

To remove a role from an individual click on the Remove button next to the role to remove it from the individual.

Only the channel owner can add or remove Lead Moderator, Editor, and Artist roles.

Chat Commands

You can also use chat commands to add or remove moderators and VIPs.

Command

Description

/vip username

Adds the VIP role to the user.

/mod username

Adds the mod role to the user.

/unvip username

Removes the VIP role from the user.

/unmod username

Removes the mod role from the user.

/vips

Will post a list of the users with your channel’s VIP role.

/mods

Will post a list of the users with your channel’s mod role.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I unlock more VIP badges?
Creators can unlock more VIP badges by getting more viewers to chat during streams. Specifically, getting 10/15/20/25/50/100/200 unique chatters in a stream will unlock 20/30/40/50/60/80/100 additional VIP badges.
Can VIPs be moderated?
Yes. While VIPs are immune to Twitch chat option settings including AutoMod, Block Hyperlinks, and slow/sub-only/follower-only modes, they are not immune to actions by channel moderators.
Can I customize what the VIP badge looks like for my channel?
No, VIP badges are channel badges that don’t allow for customization.
Can someone be a VIP and a moderator at the same time?
No, a user can only be either a VIP or a moderator. It is, however, possible for a user to be a VIP, an editor, and an artist at the same time.
Do VIPs have the same status as subscribers?
VIPs are not granted access to a channel’s sub badge and sub-only emotes. It is, however, possible for a subscriber to be granted VIP status.
Can a viewer have both a VIP and a subscriber badge?
Yes, viewers who are both subscribers and have been granted VIP can have and equip both badges.
Can lead moderators use both the regular mod badge and the lead mod badge?
The default badge for lead moderators will be the lead mod badge, but lead moderators can choose to use the regular mod badge instead. They can not equip both badges at the same time. To change which badge you have displayed, just click on your current badge in the chat box, which will open up a badge selector menu.
How can I manage my role in other peoples’ channels, or communities?
To manage your roles in other communities, visit your Creator Dashboard. Click on the Community tab, then My Assigned Roles. Here, you can filter by role, and locate channels from which you may remove your role assignment.

Mobile Game Broadcasting

Mobile Game broadcasting allows anyone to easily broadcast mobile games to Twitch directly from their mobile phone or tablet. The Twitch app can be found on the iOS App Store and Google Play Store.

For best performance, and to reduce potential data charges, make sure you are connected to WiFi and stream only from a WiFi connection.

Where can you find it?

You can access mobile game broadcasting in the Twitch app:

  • Tap the + (plus) button in the bottom navigation bar.
  • Select Stream (Stream from this device) from the menu that appears.
  • Your camera opens with a preview. At the bottom of the screen, select Stream Games (instead of Stream IRL).

Features

Android & iOS devices allow different functionality for mobile devices. The article attempts to denote features that are Android only with the phrase “[Android Only]” in the text.

If this is your first time streaming, you’ll be asked to give permissions for the microphone which is necessary to capture your voice & game audio for your stream.

[Android Only] We’ll also ask you for permissions to overlay content - which allows you to view chat & alerts in a notification bubble without leaving your game.

When streaming from your mobile device, EVERYTHING that appears on your screen will be captured, including notifications. Be careful not to display personal or sensitive information like phone numbers, emails, or addresses as this will be broadcast to the audience. Do not type passwords while streaming, as users can also see the letters being typed on the keyboard even if the text is obscured. It’s always best to turn “Do Not Disturb” mode on before streaming to prevent notifications from showing.

The system will automatically detect your network settings and automatically broadcast with the most appropriate quality. You can always adjust these settings by tapping the triple dot menu on this screen.

You’ll be asked to select the game you want to stream. Common mobile games and (for Android only) games installed on your phone will show here. If you don’t see the game you want, you can search for it and select it.

[iOS Only] Tap the red record button to begin capturing your stream. Make sure to switch apps to the game you want to stream.

If the button to start your stream is greyed out on iOS, you need to add stream information such as a title and category first. Once your stream info is filled in, the button will become active.

[Android Only] After adding your stream into, tap Launch game which should automatically open the game you selected and open the stream manager. The stream manager is the best place to change your settings or get detailed information from alerts for follows, bits, and subs or to view chat. You can chat directly with your audience by tapping the message button on the bottom right corner of the stream manager. Tap Start Stream to start broadcasting. Tap the X in the bubble to close the stream manager and play your game.

When you’re finished streaming, make sure to manually end the stream so to stop capturing the screen & audio. Tap the stream manager and then tap the red End Stream button to end the stream.

Settings

Game Audio

There are two audio levels available - the first one adjusts your game volume and the second one adjusts your microphone volume. These audio levels are provided to ensure there is no clipping, or audio distortion, during your live stream

During a live stream, the Stream Info screen will indicate any audio distortion in yellow or red. If both levels are in green, the volume isn’t too loud or distorted. If one of your audio levels reaches yellow, it means the volume level is close to reaching critical levels. If one of your audio levels reaches red, it means that volume has reached critical level and clipping will occur.

Chat Notifications (iOS only)

On iOS, you can now follow what’s happening on chat by enabling push notifications when you are live streaming. In order to do that, you need to do two things:

  • Open Settings > Notifications > Screen Sharing > Enable Allow Notifications
  • Enable the Stream Notifications toggle in the Stream setup screen. The Stream setup page will appear when you click the Stream icon to go live.

Custom Focus Mode - Enables Gaming App Notifications only

In order to see just Twitch gaming push notifications, enable a custom Focus Mode in Settings. You can do this by opening your device Settings > Focus and then selecting the Plus icon in the top right corner.

Setup your custom focus mode and add the Twitch app to the Allowed Apps for Notifications.

Any app added here will show notifications when your Focus Mode is enabled.

Enabling Your Custom Focus Mode

When you’re about to go live on Twitch, enable your custom focus mode. Open Control Center and select Focus, then select your custom Focus Mode from the available options.

If set up correctly, this will ensure only notifications from the Twitch app are seen during your broadcast.

Tips & Tricks

Stream from WiFi:

For best performance, and to reduce potential data charges, make sure you are connected to wifi and stream only from WiFi.

Be headphone-free:

Keep bluetooth and wired speakers disconnected to capture all game sounds & voice for your stream.

Keep the microphone clear:

Audio is captured through your microphone. Make sure your hand isn’t covering it.

Turn off notifications & protect your privacy:

Put your phone in Do Not Disturb mode to prevent notifications from appearing. Everything you see on your screen will be streamed. Use caution when changing apps, or what you open on the screen.

Stay unlocked while live:

If your device locks, the stream will end.

Frequently Asked Questions

What devices are supported?
Broadcasting will work on tablet or phone on all devices that support the Twitch app, from low-end to high-end.
Can I broadcast from the camera and screen at the same time?
At this time, you cannot broadcast both from the camera and capture your screen at the same time. If you’d like to use your front or back facing camera to stream - choose “Stream IRL” in the first screen. If you want to broadcast a mobile game, choose “Stream Games”.
Can I set my overlays?
At this time, we do not support overlays when broadcasting from mobile.
Are there other ways to broadcast mobile games to Twitch?
There are several other options located here dashboard.twitch.tv. If you have a PC, a mobile cable, and a way to mirror your screen on your PC, you can also use PC based streaming tools.

On-Demand Content on Twitch

Utilizing on-demand content, such as Past Broadcasts (VODs), Clips, Highlights, and Collections can help grow your channel and also allow your community to watch content they may have missed otherwise.

Types of On-Demand Content on Twitch

There are a few different on-demand content types on Twitch.

Past Broadcasts (VODs)

Past Broadcasts, commonly referred to as VODs, are recordings of your past live streams. Once a broadcast is saved, you can find it in your Video Producer, where you can review it, create Highlights and Clips, or download it to repurpose elsewhere. If you don’t see your past broadcasts there, check that Past Broadcast storage is turned on in your Stream Settings before your next stream.

Twitch Partners, Prime and Twitch Turbo users will have past broadcasts saved for 60 days before being deleted. Twitch Affiliates have their past broadcasts saved for 14 days. All other broadcasters will have their past broadcasts saved for 7 days before they are deleted. If you want to save your past broadcasts beyond the 7 or 60 day limits, download or export them before the 7 or 60 day window.

For streamers who stream in Dual Format or Vertical: The vertical version of your VOD will expire 7 days after your stream, after which the horizontal version will be available for the remainder of your existing retention period (60 day retention for Prime, Turbo, and Partners and 14 day retention for Affiliates). Learn more about dual format streaming.

For streamers who stream in 2K: Please note that the 2K quality version of your VOD will expire 7 days after your stream, after which the 1080p quality version will be available for the remainder of your existing retention period (60 day retention for Prime, Turbo, and Partners and 14 day retention for Affiliates). Learn more about 2K streaming.

Highlights

The Highlighter tool allows you to use segments of your Past Broadcasts (VODs) to create a new content type, called a Highlight. Highlights can serve as a highlight reel to show off your best moments to new viewers who land on your channel page. There is a 100-hour storage limit across all Highlights and Uploads, including unpublished Highlights and uploads. Read more about creating Highlights and adding stream markers here.

Uploads

Uploads allow you to upload content you may have created, saved, or edited elsewhere onto Twitch. Use the button on the right above the video list and select the file you’d like to upload from the window that opens. Uploading videos is limited to Affiliate or Partners at this time. We support file uploads using H264 video compression. There is a 100-hour storage limit across all Highlights and Uploads, including unpublished Highlights and uploads.

Channel Trailer

Channel Trailers are short videos that serve as an introduction to new viewers who visit your channel while you’re offline, and are currently only available to Affiliates and Partners. Read more about channel trailers here.
