Mod Club Founder’s Badge (2026) — Not to be confused with the channel Founders Badge. This badge celebrates the founding members of the Twitch Moderators Club. Members were eligible to receive it if they applied, were accepted, and completed the required Mod Club onboarding by June 30, 2026. Members who applied or completed onboarding after this date were not eligible to receive the badge.

Some badges from events may be yours to use forever, and some may only be accessible during the event. Once event badges are gone, they’re gone and cannot be issued. For time-limited badges from community programs, see the event badges listed above.

How to Get Badges

There are several different ways for viewers to obtain badges on Twitch.

Global Badge

These badges are available for all viewers to have access to. The only exceptions are the Turbo and Prime badges, which require the viewer to have Turbo or have their Twitch account linked to an Amazon Prime account, respectively.

Channel Badges

Channel badges are different. Some you earn based upon your support of a specific channel with bits, gifted subs, and/or longevity of subscription.

Badges like the VIP or Artist badge are granted to you by the streamer. These two, along with the Founders badge, are limited in number per channel.

Event Badges

Event badges are badges that are obtained through different types of events such as live events like TwitchCon or online events like r/place 2023 Cake. When event badges are gone, they’re gone, and can’t be reissued.

How to Use Badges

Using badges in chat is easy. Start by clicking on the icon in the left of your chat box to open your Chat Identity.

Click on the badges you want to display next to your name in chat. You can set both your global badges as well as the badges for the channel you are currently in.

View Other Badges

You can view other badges you see in chat by clicking on the badge. This will bring up a larger view and more details about the badge.

Frequently Asked Questions

What do I do if I am missing a certain badge?

Attention, troubleshooters: Most missing badge issues can be resolved by refreshing your page/app, or waiting a few moments.

VIP Badge – Qualifying streamers, Partners, and Affiliates who have met the requirements for initial and additional VIP slots may need to wait 24-36 hours due to metrics lag time.

Founders Badge – Viewers who are missing Founders Badges may have had them removed by the qualifying streamers, Partners, and Affiliates. Learn more in our guide.

Artist Badge – Artists that are missing their badges must first ensure they have reviewed and approved any attribution sent to them by creators. Learn more in our guide.

Event Badge – Depending on the event, you must meet certain conditions to unlock your reward. Ensure you have met these requirements.

If you need further help with a badge-related issue, contact Twitch Support here. Tell us details of the badge you’ve earned, including the channel name in question, or any purchase invoice.

Shared Chat

Shared Chat makes it easy for collaborating streamers to bring their communities together into a combined chat experience. You can start and manage Shared Chat right from your chat, Stream Manager, or your channel page. In this article, we explain what streamers, moderators, and viewers can expect during a Shared Chat.

Want to collaborate with audio and video too? You can add Audio/Video to any collaboration with Stream Together. Learn more about hosts, guests, and Stream Together in our guide.

Before You Start Shared Chat

A collaboration is when you team up live with other streamers on Twitch. When you start a collaboration, you choose what to share:

  • Shared Chat: Combine your chats. This also combines your view counts (Shared Viewership) and lets you run a Shared Hype Train.
  • Audio/Video: Join a Stream Together call so you can see and hear each other on stream.
  • Or both.

Twitch also supports other ways to stream together, like Co-Streaming a special event. This article covers Shared Chat.

In a collaboration, only the host can start Shared Chat. You must be live to start or join a Shared Chat. Guests can leave a Shared Chat at any time, and the host can end Shared Chat for everyone at any time. Hosts can also remove guests from the collaboration, which removes them from the Shared Chat.

Before joining or initiating Shared Chat, hosts and guests should know:

  • In a Shared Chat, your chat is jointly moderated as described below in the “Moderating Shared Chat” section. Also, your chat is accessible to any third-party applications operating in the channels of other streamers participating in the Shared Chat session. This means, for example, that other streamers’ chatbots and extensions may read and send messages in the chat, see chat data and activity (including moderator information and activity), and take Shared Chat moderation actions (as described below). You can leave a Shared Chat session at any time and your community will leave with you.
  • Your collaborators may invite and admit other users, and anyone with the invite link can join, regardless of your collaboration settings. Keep your invite links safe and share them only with trusted users. Links only expire when you regenerate them or the collaboration ends.

Shared Chat on Web

Hosts: Starting Shared Chat on Web

You must be live to start Shared Chat. You don’t need to start an audio/video call. You can start or manage Shared Chat from any of these places:

  • Stream Manager chat: Click Modes at the top of your chat panel, then click Start Shared Chat. This also works in Mod View on your own channel.

  • Stream Manager Quick Actions: Add the Shared Chat Quick Action (in the Community category of Add Quick Actions), then click it to start or manage Shared Chat.

  • Stream Manager Collaboration panel or the Stream Together dashboard page: Click Invite to Collaborate.

  • Your channel page chat: Open your chat settings and click Start Shared Chat, or click Start or Manage on the “Combine your communities?” card in the Community tab.

  • Chat command: Type /sharedchat in your chat.

  • Another streamer’s channel page: Open the drop-down menu next to the Knock button and click Invite to Shared Chat. This starts a collaboration with Shared Chat and invites that streamer.

  • Open Shared Chat from any of the places above. If you’re not already in a collaboration, click Enable Shared Chat and Invite.

  • In the Invite and Start a Collaboration window, make sure Shared Chat is checked. Check Audio/Video too if you also want to start a Stream Together call.

  • Search for the streamers you want to invite, or pick them from your Favorites, Recents, Followers, Subscribers, or Team, then click Send Invite.

  • Once a guest joins, a temporary banner appears at the top of the chat column for all participants to confirm that a Shared Chat has begun. “Shared Chat” stays at the top of the chat column while you’re in a Shared Chat.

Guests must be live to join a Shared Chat. Invited guests who aren’t live can join once they go live.

Hosts: Managing Shared Chat on Web

Open Shared Chat from any of the places above, or click “Shared Chat” at the top of your chat. The Manage tab shows everyone in your collaboration and whether they’re using Shared Chat, Audio/Video, or both. From here, you can:

  • Invite more streamers: Click the + next to the participant count.
  • Remove a guest: Click Remove next to their name. This removes them from the collaboration.
  • Add audio and video: Click Join Audio/Video to open the Stream Together window. If you close that window, you stay in Shared Chat.
  • Change collaboration settings: Click the Settings icon.
  • End Shared Chat for everyone: Hover over Shared Chat is Enabled and click End Shared Chat. Shared Chat also ends when your stream ends.
Guests: Joining Shared Chat on Web

You must be live to join a Shared Chat. To join:

  • Open Shared Chat from any of the places above, and go to the Invites tab. Invites you’ve received are listed newest first, with who sent them and when.
  • Click Join next to the invite. If the host is in an audio/video call, this opens the Stream Together window. Otherwise, you join the Shared Chat directly.
  • Got an invite link instead? Click Join with invite link, paste the link, and click Join.

To leave a Shared Chat, open the Manage tab and click Leave. When you leave, your community leaves with you.

Learn more about Dropping in / Knocking here.

Hosts & Guests: Viewing Shared Chat

Shared Chat can be viewed in all existing locations that streamers can currently see chat, including within Stream Manager, as a pop-out, or embedded in broadcasting software such as OBS.

Streamers will see visual indicators for viewers from their own channel, in order to make it easier for them to engage with and recognize members of their own community. The profile image of the source channel will be displayed for each message, while messages from the streamer’s own channel will show the streamer’s Profile icon highlighted.

Shared Chat on Mobile

Hosts: Starting a Shared Chat on Mobile

You can start and join Shared Chat from the Twitch Mobile app whether you’re streaming from the app, from your desktop, or with third-party mobile apps like Streamlabs Mobile, PRISM Live Studio, IRL Pro, or Camo Studio (learn more).

Your channel must be live to host a collaboration using Shared Chat on mobile.

From Mobile Creator Dashboard Stream Manager:

  • (Live channels only) Open the Twitch Mobile App. Tap the red button at the bottom of the screen for quick access to your Stream Manager.
  • In your Stream Manager, select the speedometer icon to view your Quick Actions.
  • You may need to add, remove, or reorder the widgets in your Creator Dashboard for easy access.
  • Tap on the Start or Manage Shared Chat button.

You now find yourself in the collaboration Backstage. From here, you can manage collaboration settings, including inviting other collaborators, Connect to Audio and Video, or enable Shared Chat. Learn more.

Hosts: Inviting Guests to Collaborate & Join Shared Chat

It’s time to add some guests. Your Shared Chat won’t start until at least one other participant joins your collaboration.

Once you start a collaboration from the Twitch Mobile App, we’ll automatically copy an invite link to your clipboard. You can also share the invite link directly through other messaging apps by tapping Share Invite Link once Shared Chat is enabled.

Your guests must be live to join your collaboration, and the Shared Chat. They can be live using a third-party streaming app from their phone, or a computer.

Hosts: Managing Collaborators From Mobile Backstage

As guests join your collaboration, they’ll appear in your Backstage window. Guests can enable their chat, their audio and video, or both. Key Backstage functions include:

  • Add or Remove Collaborators From Mobile Backstage - Backstage, hosts see all collaborators in their session. Both guests and hosts can share the invite link to add more collaborators to the session. Hosts may remove collaborators from the session, which removes them from both Shared Chat and Audio/Video (if enabled).

  • (Mobile-Only) Connect to Audio and Video - From Backstage, hosts and guests have the option to connect audio and video by tapping Add Audio Connections and following the prompt. Once connected, note that your mic and camera are off by default. You remain connected while the screen is open, but if you leave the Twitch app or exit the Backstage window, you will be disconnected from audio and video.

  • You won’t hear participants until you connect audio!

If you are collaborating using audio and video for the first time on the Twitch App, you must grant the Twitch App access to your Microphone and Camera.

  • Disable Shared Chat and End the Collaboration - As host, disabling Shared Chat ends the Shared Chat session, and removes guests from the collaboration if they are only connected to Shared Chat, and not connected to audio or video. To proceed, tap Shared Chat is Enabled at the top of the Backstage window. Confirm by tapping Yes, End Now.

Collaboration hosts and guests may leave Backstage any time by tapping the X in the top-left corner of the Backstage window. Shared Chat stays active in the background, and can be managed any time via your Quick Actions in the mobile Creator Dashboard.

You’ll know Shared Chat is enabled when the Start or Manage Shared Chat Quick-Action button is highlighted.

Hosts: Managing Collaborations Between Mobile and Web

Switch between Stream Manager on desktop or your mobile device to manage collaborations on either mobile or web.

Guests: Joining a Shared Chat on Mobile

To join a Shared Chat, you must be live. Hosts can share invite links to you directly via a messaging app, or on Twitch via your notification inbox.

To join the collaboration session:

  • Click the invite link sent to you by the Host
  • Click Join Session to enter the Backstage window
    • If all participants are using Shared Chat without audio or video enabled, you will first see all participants in the collaboration session.
    • If at least one participant has enabled audio or video, instead you will first see the audio/video Backstage view. Your mic and camera will be turned off by default when you enter. You’ll need to tap the microphone icon to turn on your mic, and the camera icon to turn on your video.
Guests: Leaving Shared Chat on Mobile

Guests can leave a Shared Chat at any time by doing one of the following from the Backstage window:

  • Tap Exit This Collaboration Session at the bottom of the window
  • Tap the Shared Chat is On button at the top of the window
  • End your stream
  • Turn on Shield Mode

Minimizing or closing the Twitch Mobile App will disconnect you from audio/video, but will not disconnect you from Shared Chat.

What happens when you leave depends on whether you’re connected to audio or video:

  • If your audio or video is connected, you will only be removed from the Shared Chat, but you’ll stay in the collaboration session connected to audio and video.
  • If you’re not using audio or video, you will be removed from the entire collaboration session.

If you leave your Shared Chat session, your community leaves with you.

Moderating Shared Chat

Moderation in Shared Chat is intended to be a jointly moderated experience while maintaining the principle that a streamer and their mods are in control of their channel and the relationship with their community.

  • Moderators will see an onboarding card the first time they are in a Shared Chat session. Additionally, a “Shared Chat” indicator at the top of the chat column will provide confirmation that a chat is shared.
  • Like streamers, mods will see visual indicators for viewers from their own channel to help them more easily identify members of their own community
  • Mod actions taken by mods against viewers from the channel they moderate work the same in a Shared Chat as in regular chat. Mods can also take mod actions against viewers from other channels during the Shared Chat session, which will always be reflected in their own channels. Those mod actions will not always be reflected in other channels participating in the Shared Chat. For example, mod actions such as timeouts and bans only impact viewers in other channels for the duration of the Shared Chat.
  • More details available below:

Mod actions taken on viewers in the channel you moderate

Impact on viewers in the channel you moderate during Shared Chat

Impact on viewers in the channel you moderate after Shared Chat

Deleting messages

Messages will be deleted in your channel and all other channels in the Shared Chat

Messages remain deleted

Chat Warnings

User will receive a warning and will need to acknowledge it prior to chatting again

User will receive a warning and will need to acknowledge it prior to chatting again

Timeouts

Users will not be able to chat for the duration of the timeout

Users will not be able to chat for the duration of the timeout

Bans

Users will not be able to chat or watch the stream

Users will not be able to chat or watch the stream

Mod actions taken on viewers from other channels in the Shared Chat

Impact on viewers in other channels during Shared Chat

Impact on viewers in other channels after Shared Chat

Deleting messages

Messages are deleted only in the channel you moderate for, but remain visible in the other channels

Messages are not deleted in other channels

Chat Warnings

User receives a warning and must acknowledge it to chat again

Users in other channels can chat normally

Timeouts

Users can not chat for the duration of the timeout

The timeout will no longer impact users in other channels after the Shared Chat ends

Bans

Users can not chat for the duration of the Shared Chat but can watch the stream and participate in channel events (such as Polls)

Users can not chat for the duration of the Shared Chat but can watch the stream and participate in channel events (such as Polls)

The user remains banned in the channel where the ban originated.

To see mod actions taken by mods from other channels during the Shared Chat that affect the channel you moderate for, you can refer to the Mod Actions panel in Mod View.

  • Moderation and chat settings for each channel only apply to their respective communities during a Shared Chat. For example, a channel’s AutoMod level and blocked terms only apply to messages sent from that channel. Messages sent from other channels in the Shared Chat must follow the moderation and chat settings set in those channels.

How Shared Chat Works For Viewers

Viewers will see a prompt if they are in a collaborating channel when a Shared Chat is beginning.

When visiting the channel page of a streamer that is currently in a Shared Chat, viewers will see a “Shared Chat” indicator at the top of the chat column as well as under the video player to indicate Shared Chat is active, and who the collaborators are.

During a Shared Chat, viewers can hover over each other’s usernames or badges to see what communities they are from if they are watching on desktop.

On the Twitch mobile app, viewers can tap on the user’s name in chat to bring up their profile card and see what channel they are chatting from.

During a Shared Chat session, moderators from other channels within the Shared Chat can take certain mod actions on viewers from each participating channel, including warning, timing out, and banning viewers. Viewers who are banned by mods from other channels during a Shared Chat will no longer be able to chat for the duration of the Shared Chat, but can still watch the stream and participate in channel events (such as Polls).

GIF messages sent via the GIF Keyboard work in Shared Chat. Tier 2 and Tier 3 paid subscribers can send GIFs in any participating channel where GIF keyboard is enabled, and GIF messages are visible to all viewers across the Shared Chat.

Frequently Asked Questions

As a streamer or moderator, will chat highlights such as First Time Chatter or Suspicious User show up for chatters from other channels?
In most cases, only messages sent from the channel you are the moderator or streamer for will have highlights applied to them. The @mention highlight will still apply to messages sent from any channel within the Shared Chat.
How do chat modes work in Shared Chat?
Each channel has control over their own chat mode settings. For instance, if two channels are in a Shared Chat and one of them is set to “Emote Only” mode, then all messages sent from that channel will follow “Emote Only” rules. The other channel would not be affected by the chat mode change.
Does revenue from cheers or subscriptions get shared across channels in Shared Chat?
All subscriptions, cheers, and other Twitch monetization tools apply only to the channel where the transactions occur. Though chat messages about these activities may be shared across other channels for visibility to everyone in the Shared Chat, the activities and any associated revenue only apply to the source channel.
Will all events initiated in each channel be shared to all channels in the Shared Chat?
No. The only events shared in each channel in the Shared Chat are Shared Hype Trains. Learn more.

A number of other events only appear in the channel they were initiated in, including: Power-Ups effects, Shout Outs, Polls, and Predictions. Pinned Messages and Highlighted Messages will also appear as regular chat messages outside of the channel they were initiated in. In the future, we may explore sharing these events to all channels within the Shared Chat.

How does Shared Chat work with third-party tools like chat bots or other chat clients?
Twitch provides APIs that 3rd party tools can use to integrate with Shared Chat. If your favorite 3rd party tool does not integrate with Shared Chat, you can contact the developer and ask them to add that integration.
Does Mod View on the Twitch mobile apps support Shared Chat?
Not at this time. When accessed from a desktop browser, Mod View supports Shared Chat.
How does Shared Chat work with Drop-Ins?
When you open the drop-down menu next to the Knock button on another streamer’s channel page, you can choose Knock with Message to ask to join their collaboration, or Invite to Shared Chat to start a Shared Chat with them. Knocks you receive while you’re not in a collaboration appear at the top of your Invites tab in Shared Chat. Learn more about Drop-Ins here.
How do chat bans work during a Shared Chat?
Users who are banned during Shared Chat cannot participate in chat for the duration of the Shared Chat. Once the Shared Chat is over, users will only remain banned in the channel from which the moderation action came from. If you’d like to ensure all users banned during the Shared Chat can’t return to your stream even if your channel was not the channel that applied the ban, it can be helpful to enable Shared Ban Info between your channel and the other channels in the Shared Chat session. Shared Ban Info allows users banned in one channel to appear flagged/restricted in other channels.
How do unban requests work in Shared Chat?
Provided the channel owner has the option enabled, if you are banned in chat, you can request to be unbanned. Learn more.
Will I remain in the collaboration session if I exit out of the Twitch App?
If you have your audio and video connected, exiting out of the Twitch App will automatically remove you from the collaboration session. If you are the host, this will end the collaboration session for everyone. If you are only using Shared Chat, leaving the Twitch App will not remove you from the collaboration session.

Shared Viewership

Shared Viewership is a collaboration feature on Twitch, and represents a significant change to one of the most important Twitch metrics. You can read more about how and why we decided to make these changes on our blog post.

What is Shared Viewership?

Shared Viewership is the combined view count of a collaboration on Twitch, and is automatically enabled with any Shared Chat session. This view count is displayed to viewers on your channel page and in the Followed Channels list. Shared Viewership shows how many people your collaboration is reaching, and it helps your stream appear higher on your followers’ Following page when they sort by Viewers (High to Low).

The Shared Viewership Metric

Shared Viewership is a metric that shows the total unique count of concurrent viewers across all channels collaborating. It displays on your channel page and in the Followed Channels list.

How Shared Viewership Affects Sorting

When viewers sort their Following page by Viewers (High to Low), channels in a collaboration are ranked by Shared Viewership, because it is the truest representation of what a viewer can expect to experience when they decide to join a stream.

When viewers browse a category, such as Just Chatting, and sort by Viewers (High to Low), each channel is ranked by its own viewer count, not Shared Viewership. Stream previews in the category also show each channel’s own viewer count.

Individual CCV

CCV is an industry-standard metric that means “Concurrent Viewers.”

Viewers and streamers can see both viewership numbers on each channel. Individual CCV is the viewer count used when viewers sort a category by Viewers (High to Low), when evaluating Path to Partner and Path to Affiliate, and when measuring ad payouts.

What Qualifies For Shared Viewership?

Shared Viewership is designed to highlight collaborations where the streamers are creating new content together and their communities can engage as one. Examples that do not meet that bar will not qualify, even if they may technically involve multiple channels streaming at the same time. Importantly, we understand brand promotions and brand channels to be a necessary exception, as there are instances where a streamer and brand will benefit from streaming the same content across multiple channels while sharing chat & viewership.

Shared Viewership turns on automatically when you’re in a Shared Chat with another streamer. You don’t need to use Audio/Video. Learn more about Shared Chat and Stream Together in these articles.

Viewership Tampering - Review the existing guidance in our Community Guidelines around Viewership Tampering when using Shared Viewership. There, you may also find outlined examples of the policies involving Shared Viewership and Viewership Tampering.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I enable Shared Viewership during my next collaboration?
Shared Viewership turns on automatically for all channels in a Shared Chat.
How will you prevent misuse of the system?
We understand the concern about potential misuse, which is why we are spending the time to clearly define the guidelines for what is permissible and restricting it to collaborations with Shared Chat turned on. We will be actively enforcing our policies to retain trust in the feature.
How will infractions be dealt with by Twitch?
On enforcement your first infraction will be a warning. On additional offenses users will receive a violation.
Does this punish streamers who don’t collaborate regularly?
No, this is us remedying a flaw in collaboration on Twitch. Streamers have told us that collaboration is important, but the current experience doesn’t feel truly co-op. Shared Viewership is designed to fix that problem by providing a more accurate representation of the collaborative experience - for both streamers and viewers.
What does Shared Viewership affect?
Shared Viewership determines where your stream appears on your followers’ Following page when they sort by Viewers (High to Low), as it is the best representation of what a viewer should expect to experience. It does not affect where your stream appears when viewers browse a category and sort by viewer count. Categories use each channel’s own viewer count. In the future we plan to add these metrics to Stream Summaries so streamers can understand how collaborations impact their growth and reach.
Will it affect Path to Partner or ad payouts?
No, Shared Viewership does not affect Path to Partner or ad payouts. We want to first understand how creators utilize the tool before applying it more widely as a metric.
Why are there no shared monetization features?
We believe there is significant value in better supporting the monetization of collaborative content, and we are actively exploring opportunities to do so in the near future. Our focus right now is on providing the foundational tools like Shared Viewership to enhance the overall collaborative experience on Twitch.
Will I be penalized for the activities of my collaborators?
We understand there are risks around safety when collaborating with others. Collaborating on Twitch helps mitigate those risks as every collaborator is logged into their Twitch account and responsible for their own behavior and can be individually reported. However, we encourage all creators to be mindful of their collaborators. Collaboration hosts need to condemn behavior that violates our Terms of Service and remove a guest who engages in that behavior from the collaboration.

Watch Streaks

Watch Streaks show your dedication to a channel by tracking consecutive streams you’ve viewed. They’re a way to demonstrate loyalty, earn bonus Channel Points, and show off your commitment to your favorite creators. In this guide, we’ll explain how Watch Streaks work and how to maintain them - including how to recover them if you miss a stream.

What Are Watch Streaks?

Watch Streaks track how many consecutive streams you’ve watched from a channel. They’re more than just a number - Watch Streaks are a form of recognition and reward that shows your dedication to a creator beyond just earning Channel Points.

Watch Streaks can be earned on monetized channels where Channel Points are enabled. Viewers must be logged in to their Twitch account to build and maintain Watch Streaks. As your Watch Streak grows, you’ll automatically earn additional Channel Points for each consecutive broadcast you watch.

Learn more about how Watch Streaks impact Channel Points earnings in our Channel Points Guide.

Watch Streak Milestones

Twitch celebrates your dedication with milestone notifications in chat when you reach certain Watch Streak levels:

  • Watch Streak 2: Earn bonus points for 2 consecutive streams
  • Watch Streak 3: Earn bonus points for 3 consecutive streams
  • Watch Streak 4: Earn bonus points for 4 consecutive streams
  • Watch Streak 5+: Earn bonus points for 5+ consecutive streams

How to Build Watch Streaks

Building a Watch Streak is simple: watch consecutive broadcasts from the same channel. Here’s what you need to know:

Requirements for Watch Streaks
  • You must be logged in to your Twitch account
  • The channel must have Channel Points enabled
  • Each stream must be at least 10 minutes long
  • At least 30 minutes must pass between the end of one stream and the start of the next
  • You need to watch each consecutive broadcast to maintain your streak

Watch Streaks are unique to each channel. You can have different Watch Streak levels with different creators simultaneously.

What Breaks a Watch Streak

Previously, missing even one stream would reset your Watch Streak to zero. However, Twitch now offers Watch Streak Recovery for meaningful streaks (3+ consecutive streams), giving you a second chance to maintain your dedication.

How to Recover Your Watch Streak

Watch Streak Recovery allows you to maintain your streak even if you miss a stream. This feature recognizes that life happens, and you shouldn’t lose weeks or months of dedication because you missed one broadcast.

Eligibility for Recovery

You can recover your Watch Streak if you originally had a Watch Streak of 3 consecutive streams or more with that channel. If your eligible Watch Streak is at-risk, we’ll send a notification about 45 minutes after a missed stream ends.

Recovery Process

To recover your Watch Streak, watch recorded content from the missed stream, or watch another live stream from the channel. Whichever you choose, do so within 24 hours from when the first missed stream ended. You’ll see a confirmation message when your Watch Streak has been successfully maintained.

Recovering your Watch Streak maintains your current streak count but does not increase it. Watch the next live stream to increase your streak.

Don’t Miss Out

You have exactly 24 hours from when the first missed stream ended to complete your recovery. This window gives you flexibility while maintaining the meaningful nature of Watch Streaks.

What Content Helps Recover Your Watch Streak

It’s easy to find content that will help restore your streak – look for the Watch Streaks icon in various places around Twitch on web and mobile.

Stories (Recommended)

In the Twitch mobile app, browse the story shelf on the home tab. Look for stories marked with the Watch Streaks icon. The Watch Streaks icon indicates that the story contains clips from the stream you missed. Watch at least 5 seconds of any story with the Watch Streaks icon to restore your streak.

On Twitch on web, click “Open Stories” in the upper corner of the left navigation bar. You can now browse for stories with the Watch Streaks icon.

Clips

Channel Page Clips (Recommended): You can identify which clips are eligible to aid Watch Streak recovery without needing to click into every video. Navigate directly to the channel page of the channel you’re going to lose the watch streak with. Select the Clips tab to browse clips from that specific channel. Look for clips marked with the Watch Streaks icon – this icon appears on both the channel page clips tab and individual clips, so you can tell which ones are eligible before clicking into the video. You can also check the Home tab of the channel page, which displays a shelf with eligible clips.

Clips Feed (Alternative): In the Twitch mobile app, you can also browse the Clips feed from the home tab. Look for clips marked with the Watch Streaks icon. However, this method is less optimal since you don’t know what clips you’ll be served and you have to scroll through them one by one. Watch at least 5 seconds of any clip with the Watch Streaks icon to restore your streak.

On-Demand Content (VODs)

Highlights of the missed stream, or content from collections do not count towards Watch Streak recovery.

Navigate to the channel whose Watch Streak you wish to restore. Choose Videos → Past Broadcasts (mobile app) or Recent Broadcasts (web). The Watch Streaks icon appears on the VODs tab of the channel page, so you can tell which VODs are eligible before clicking into the video. Watch at least 5 minutes of the VOD of the missed stream to restore your streak.

Live Streams

If the creator goes live again within your 24-hour recovery window, watching at least 5 minutes* of the new stream will also recover your streak. We’ll notify you in chat!

*Do note that some users report needing to watch significantly longer (1-3 hours).

Watch Streak Recovery Notifications

Twitch will help you stay on top of your Watch Streak recovery with timely notifications. Make sure you have Recommended Live notifications enabled from Twitch!

About 45 minutes after a stream ends (if you missed it), you’ll receive a Watch Streak recovery notification letting you know which channel your Watch Streak is at risk with, and how long your current Watch Streak is. Interact with the notification to view content that can help you recover your Watch Streak.

Success Confirmation

When you successfully recover your Watch Streak, you’ll receive a confirmation notification in your notifications inbox.

Disabling Watch Streak Recovery Notifications

If you prefer not to receive notifications that your Watch Streaks will expire, you must disable Recommended Live notifications in your Notification Settings.

Troubleshooting Watch Streak Issues

If you’re experiencing problems with Watch Streaks, you’re not alone. Here are solutions to the most commonly reported issues:

My Streak Reset Even Though I Watched the Stream

This is a known technical issue that can occur due to several factors:

  • Mobile app limitations: Watching on mobile may not always register properly
  • Casting to TV: Streaming to smart TVs or casting from devices often doesn’t count toward streaks
  • Browser issues: Ad blockers, inactive tabs, or network interruptions can interfere with tracking
  • Short streams: Streams lasting less than 5 minutes may cause tracking problems

Recommended solution: For most reliable streak tracking, watch directly in a web browser on desktop with the tab active.

VOD Recovery Not Working

If watching VODs isn’t recovering your streak:

  • Watch longer: As mentioned, while we state 5 minutes, some users report needing to watch significantly longer (1-3 hours)
  • Check timing: Ensure you’re within the 24-hour window from when the stream ended
  • Verify eligibility: Look for the Watch Streaks icon on the VOD
  • Wait for processing: Recovery may take several hours to register
Notification Settings Issues

Known Issue: The current instructions for disabling Watch Streak notifications may not work correctly. We’re working on a fix.

If you’re still receiving notifications after disabling “Recommended Live notifications,” try these additional steps:

  • Check your browser notification settings
  • Disable notifications in the mobile app separately
  • Clear your browser cache and cookies
Streaks Not Appearing on Some Channels

Watch Streaks are still rolling out and may not be available on all channels. Factors include:

  • Channel must have monetization and Channel Points enabled
  • Feature release is gradual - not all channels have it yet
Recovery Notifications Leading to Wrong Content

If recovery notifications direct you to short clips instead of full VODs:

  • Navigate directly to the channel’s Videos page
  • Look for “Recent Broadcasts” or “Past Broadcasts”
  • Find the VOD with the Watch Streaks icon
Channel Points or Streamer Settings Affecting Streaks

Your Watch Streak may reset if:

  • The streamer disables Channel Points (which also disables Watch Streaks)
  • The streamer disables Watch Streaks
  • The channel loses Partner/Affiliate status
When to Contact Support

Contact Twitch Support if:

  • You were actively chatting and participating but still lost your streak
  • You performed moderator actions during the stream but it didn’t count
  • Multiple channels reset simultaneously
  • You get “No Content Eligible” errors within the 24-hour window
  • You experience the “There was an error sharing your watch streak” message

When contacting support, include: the channel name, your approximate watch time, whether you were chatting, and your device/browser information.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do Watch Streaks work?
Watch Streaks track consecutive streams you’ve watched from a channel. Each consecutive broadcast increases your streak and earns you bonus Channel Points. You must be logged in and the channel must have Channel Points enabled.
What watch streaks are eligible for recovery?
Only Watch Streaks of 3 or more consecutive streams are eligible for recovery. This aligns with our definition of a meaningful Watch Streak with a channel.
How long do I have to recover my Watch Streak?
You have exactly 24 hours from when the first missed stream ended to watch eligible content and recover your streak.
Will recovering my Watch Streak increase the count?
No, recovering your Watch Streak maintains your current count but doesn’t increase it. For example, if you had a 4-consecutive day streak and recover it, you’ll still have a Watch Streak of 4. You’ll need to watch the next live stream to increase that streak to 5 days, and beyond!
What happens if I miss multiple streams within 24 hours?
Content from any stream you missed within the 24-hour recovery period can help you recover your streak. This gives you more opportunities to maintain your streak if a creator streams multiple times.
Can I recover Watch Streaks for DJ category streams?
Yes. Streams from creators enrolled in the DJ Program can now have non-music Clips. As a result, you can recover a broken Watch Streak on a stream in the DJs category by watching a Clip from the missed stream, or by watching a Story that contains a Clip from the missed stream. VOD-based Watch Streak recovery is not available for DJ streams. Learn more about the DJ program here.
What if there are no clips or VODs available from the missed stream?
If no recorded content is available from the missed stream, you won’t receive a recovery notification and your streak will reset. This can happen if the creator doesn’t enable VODs or if no clips were created from the stream.
How do I know which content will help recover my streak?
Eligible content will be marked with the Watch Streaks icon. You’ll receive notifications directing you to specific content that can help recover your streak.
Can I turn off Watch Streak recovery notifications?
Yes. To disable Watch Streak recovery notifications, disable Recommended Live notifications in your Notification Settings.
Do I need to watch the entire VOD to recover my streak?
No, you only need to watch at least 5 minutes of the VOD from the missed stream to recover your Watch Streak.
Can I have Watch Streaks with multiple channels?
Yes! Watch Streaks are unique to each channel. You can maintain different Watch Streak levels with different creators simultaneously.
What if I watch a live stream during my recovery period?
If you watch a new live stream from the same channel within your 24-hour recovery window, watching at least 5 minutes will recover your streak. However, you must still recover your streak first before the new stream will count toward increasing your streak count.
Why did my streak reset when I was actively chatting and participating?
This is a known technical issue. Even active participation (chatting, moderator actions, gifting bits) doesn’t guarantee streak tracking will work properly. If this happens repeatedly, contact Twitch Support with specific details about your viewing session.
Do Watch Streaks work when casting to my TV?
Casting from mobile devices or using smart TV apps may not reliably count toward Watch Streaks. For best results, watch directly in a web browser on desktop or mobile.
Why do I get “No Content Eligible” even though I’m within 24 hours?
This error can occur if the stream was very short (under 5 minutes) or if there are technical issues with the recovery system. Contact support if you receive this error within the valid recovery window.
I watched hours of VOD but my streak didn’t recover. What’s wrong?
While we state 5 minutes is sufficient, some users report needing to watch much longer. Try watching more of the VOD, ensure you have the Watch Streaks icon visible, and wait several hours for the system to process your recovery.

What Are Global Emotes?

Learn how to use emotes in our guide here: help.twitch.tv/s/article/how-to-use-emotes

Global Emotes are available to every user on Twitch. They can be used in any channel: you do not need to follow, subscribe, or otherwise do anything to unlock or earn them.

Occasionally, Twitch will add Global Emotes for special events and holidays. Many Global Emotes are yours forever. Some Global Emotes may come and go.

Global Emotes

To locate global emotes, select the Emoticons All icon in your emote picker, or scroll to the end.

Learn how to select emotes in our guide: help.twitch.tv/s/article/how-to-use-emotes

How to Use Emotes

Visit our guide on how to use emotes: help.twitch.tv/s/article/how-to-use-emotes

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I tell if an emote in chat is a global emote?

Interact with the emote to see information on where it is from, and how to acquire it. On desktop, click the emote. In the Twitch mobile app, tap the emote.

Some Global Emotes come and go. If an emote is a Global Emote, it does not necessarily mean it is available forever.

What can I do if I don’t wish to see global emotes in my channel?

Adding certain emote code names to your AutoMod settings prevents global emotes from being used in your channel.

For example, adding Kappa or :kappa: to your blocked terms will prevent the emote from being used in your chat.

Can I create and upload emotes to my channel that mirror global emotes?

No. Emotes based on Twitch Global Emotes are not allowed. Partners and Affiliate should refer to our Emote Guidelines here: help.twitch.tv/s/article/emote-guidelines

What is the Chat Bot Badge?

Content in this article is relevant to all streamers who use 3rd-party chat bots. Learn more about chat bots, how they can help your stream, and how to build one in our developer documentation here.

The Chat Bot badge is automatically applied to authorized 3rd-party bots when they send messages in your channel. Unlike other badges, streamers cannot manually apply this badge to accounts.

How To Add the Chat Bot Badge

The Chat Bot badge appears automatically on 3rd-party bot accounts you authorize to perform actions in your Twitch channel. Grant the 3rd-party bot access your Twitch account, through the bot provider’s website. Once authorized, the bot will also appear in the Chat Bots section of your Community Tab (users list).

The third-party bot must have their API set up correctly for the badge to appear. For developers, setup information is available in the Twitch Developer Documentation.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I remove the Chat Bot badge from a bot?
To remove the Chat Bot badge from a bot in your channel, revoke the bot’s authorization through the developer’s dashboard. Once access is revoked, the badge will stop appearing and the bot will no longer be listed under “Chat Bots” in your chat’s Community Tab. It may take up to 48 hours from authorization removal for this to occur.
Can I manually add the Chat Bot badge to an account?
No, the Chat Bot badge is only applied automatically when a third-party bot is properly authorized, connected to your channel through the official authorization process, and sends a message.
Why might I see multiple badges on the same account?
Depending on your stream setup, you may appear as a moderator, and chat bot simultaneously depending on how you are accessing and using certain bot functionality.
The bot is authorized but the badge isn’t showing. What’s wrong?
3rd-party bot developers need to set up their API correctly for the badge to appear. Refer them to the Twitch Developer Documentation for proper implementation.

Getting Started: Twitch Account

Delete My Twitch Account

There are many reasons why you may wish to disable or delete your Twitch account. Deleting and disabling your Twitch account are separate actions.

Disabling your account is a temporary solution if you need a break. This prevents your account from being accessed. You can recover a disabled account.

Deleting your account is a permanent action that wipes your data in accordance with Your Privacy Rights. A deleted account cannot be recovered.

Ready to delete your account? Delete your account now or continue reading to learn more.

Disabling Your Twitch Account

Disabling your Twitch account temporarily deactivates your channel and content from anyone trying to view it. If you change your mind at a later time, you can reactivate your account by simply logging back into your account. Learn more about Account Reactivation.

If you choose to reactivate your account, your user information remains intact.

  • To disable your Twitch account, click on your Profile icon in the up right corner to open the dropdown menu, and then click on your Profile icon a second time.
  • In your Profile Settings, scroll down to Disabling Your Twitch Account and click on Disable Account
  • Make sure you are disabling the correct account, enter a reason for disabling, and then click on Disable Account.
  • Explaining why you are disabling your account is optional and not required to disable your account.

Deleting Your Twitch Account

There is no reversing Twitch account deletion. If you need a break from Twitch, we recommend you disable your account. Disabling your account is temporary, and can be reversed.

If you no longer wish to maintain your Twitch account, you can permanently delete it. This will delete all your content and profile information including clips, highlights, user rewards, and settings. Within 90 days of your request, Twitch will permanently erase all your content and close your account. The deletion process will terminate if you log back into your account while we still are processing your deletion request.

Deleting your account also stops the processing of new personal data, deletes your profile and other identifying data such as usage data, and user generated content, in accordance with Your Privacy Rights.

Unless required by law or in the case of certain legal claims, Twitch will not retain your content, your contact information, or your username. In some cases, Twitch may retain limited personal data for legal, security and other reasons permitted or required under applicable law.

To delete your Twitch account, visit the Delete Account page.

  • Make sure you are deleting the correct account, enter a reason for deletion, then click Delete Account.

Providing a reason as to why you’re deleting your account is optional.

Partners and Affiliates

Before a Partner or Affiliate account can be deleted or disabled it must first be offboarded. Please contact Customer Support here for assistance with offboarding.

Frequently Asked Questions

I disabled my account a while ago, and it’s not deleted. Why?
Disabled accounts may be purged after a period of time.
What happens to my subscriptions (and other community rewards) when I delete or disable my account?

If you temporarily deactivate your Twitch account, your subscriptions are set to cancel, and Twitch will not attempt to collect payment. You may receive updates about your subscription status by email. If you reactivate your account before your subscriptions expire, you will need to continue those subscriptions to maintain tenure streak and sub benefits.

If you permanently delete your Twitch account, your subscriptions are canceled. After the account deletion process is complete, all data is wiped and you cannot restore your subscriptions.

I have a multi-month subscription towards a creator. What happens to their revenue if I delete my account?
If your deletion request is processed before the final month of your multi-month subscription, the creator will not receive that revenue.
Why don’t I have the option to delete/disable my account?
Partners and Affiliates must complete the creator offboarding process before deleting or disabling their account. Please contact Twitch Support here for assistance with offboarding. If you are still having issues, contact us for help.
What happens to my username when I delete my account?

In most cases, if you close one account you will not be able to immediately reuse or transfer that username to a different account. After you delete your account, your old username will be recycled. It will take a minimum of 6 months for this process to complete. Eventually, that username will be added to the pool of available usernames. In most cases this means you cannot rename one account to the name of another account you own.

For more information about our username rename and recycle policy please check out our Username Rename and Recycling Policies article.

How do I restore my Twitch account after I disable it?

If you have chosen to temporarily disable your Twitch account, all you need to do is log back into it to restore your account. Please give us 24-36 hours to restore your account to its prior state. If you have questions about your account after this period, please contact Twitch Support here. Learn more about Account Reactivation.

How to Customize Content You See on Twitch

With so much great stuff on Twitch, it can be tough to choose what to watch. That’s why we feature content recommendations across Twitch based on what you’ve previously enjoyed watching.

Have you ever wondered how to better manage content types and recommendations served to you on Twitch? This guide is for you.

On this page:

  • Removing Recommendations
  • Content Display Preferences
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Removing Recommendations

Let’s start on the front page of Twitch (twitch.tv):

Front-Page Carousel

At the top of Twitch’s homepage (twitch.tv), visitors will find our Front-Page Carousel, which gives a preview of live channels or upcoming events. The carousel features content that has been curated by Twitch Staff; it is not populated through an automated system or your interactions with Twitch.

Twitch may highlight particular segments of our content creators, upcoming Twitch events, or content sponsored by our advertisers. Twitch’s carousel varies by region to account for geographic differences in creators and their content, such as languages spoken.

To remove or hide a channel you don’t want to see from this Carousel, block the channel. After you block the channel, it will be removed from the Carousel for you and will not appear again anywhere we show you content.

Front-Page Shelves

Immediately below the carousel, you will find a number of different scrollable horizontal lists of content, which Twitch refers to as “shelves.” We will always show you shelves with channels and categories that we think you will like, and we may also show you other shelves that may be curated by Twitch Staff. Shelves are selected for you based on your language, device, browser, your engagement with Twitch, and whether or not you are logged in. If you have visited Twitch before, the shelf order and the channels within the shelves are also personalized for you based on your watch history. This means we use information about channels and categories you have watched on Twitch in the past to recommend new content we think you will enjoy. For all Twitch shelves, live channels are more frequently given higher priority than non-live channels.

To train our algorithm that you don’t wish to see content similar to the channel or category, select the 3 Vertical Dots Icon then Not Interested and we will remove the category, streamer, or section you don’t like from the shelf or collection where it appeared. We’ll also give you improved recommendations the next time you return to your front page.

Block a channel to remove it from your recommendations permanently.

Left Navigation Bar - For You (Followed & Recommended Channels)

To the left of the carousel and shelves, Twitch users see the “left navigation” bar. There, logged in users will see a list of the channels they have followed, with live channels listed first, and then offline channels in order of the number of new videos available. After you follow channels, you will see recommended channels, again selected based on your region, language, interaction behavior, and watch history. Once you select a channel to view, the left navigation bar will update to include a third list, after recommended channel, which listing similar channels to the one you are currently watching.

To remove a channel from the recommended channels list, you will need to block the channel.

Let’s move now to some other pages or surfaces:

Following Page

Click Following at the top left of the screen to view shelves of channels you follow. The shelf of recommended channels shown here mirrors the listed recommended channels in your left navigation bar. You cannot remove these recommendations from your Following Page or front page left navigation bar without blocking the channel. In your Following Page, we also show you completed streams that you may have watched earlier. If you see an unexpected or unrecognized channel in your Continue Watching shelf on your Following Page, you may have watched a live stream somewhere by Twitch such as the Front-Page Carousel. To remove channels from your Continue Watching shelf on your Following Page, block the channel.

Browse Page

From the Twitch homepage or any channel page, viewers may always click Browse at the top left of the screen to find additional content. On Twitch’s Browse page, you can look for content either by Category, which is selected by broadcasters, or by Live Channels. You can then sort the categories or channels by Twitch’s recommendations or by the number of viewers from high to low.

Search Bar

From the Twitch homepage or any channel page, users may also search for content in the search bar in the top middle of the screen. When you begin to type a word, you will see Twitch’s search suggestions, which are suggested search terms based on direct matches for the word being typed and the popularity of the category or channel, with live content always listed first. If you pick a search suggestion, you will go directly to the category or channel suggested. If you elect to go to the search results page, instead of picking a search suggestion, the search results you see will be ordered based on live channels, popularity, and search query matches.

Learn more about how search works.

Content Display Preferences

Click here to manage your Content Display Preferences. You can use these settings to either hide or blur content that has been labeled with Content Classification Labels (CCLs). Your Content Display Preferences can be found under your Profile settings, under Content Preferences.

Hide Content With Content Classification Labels

You can control how content labeled with Content Classification Labels is displayed across Twitch by selecting the respective toggle for each CCL category. Streams labeled with the CCLs that you have chosen to filter out will not be recommended to you, and will not show up when you browse categories or search for content. If you follow a streamer, their content will be exempt from these settings and will still be shown even if labeled with a CCL that you’ve chosen to filter out. If you go to a channel page directly, you will still be able to view that content in full.

For users under the age of 18, content labeled with Sexual Themes; Drugs, Intoxication, or Excessive Tobacco Use; Violent and Graphic Depictions; and Gambling will be filtered out by default; users under the age of 18 may adjust their default content preferences from their Content Display Preferences settings.

For logged out users, any content labeled with a Sexual Themes or Gambling CCL will be filtered out from Twitch discovery surfaces. Logged out users can choose to hide all labeled content by visiting their Profile dropdown menu and toggling on the “Hide Labeled Content” setting. To have more control over the types of content seen while on Twitch, users will need to log-in or create an account in order to see the full set of filtering options within the Content Display Preferences menu.

If you cannot change your Content Display Preferences settings, it might be because they’re being controlled by your account or device based on your location. For example, some regions prohibit certain content and in those cases Twitch must comply with any local requirements.

Blur Content Labeled As Including Sexual Themes

You can choose to blur preview thumbnails for content that is labeled as including Sexual Themes. Blurring is enabled by default for all users, and can be adjusted in your Content Display Preferences.

When the blur feature is enabled, thumbnails of content labeled with a Sexual Themes CCL will be blurred while browsing categories, viewing recommendations, or searching for content. If you follow a channel, that content will not be blurred even if this setting is on.

Frequently Asked Questions

What if I mark something as ‘not interested’ on accident?

Right after you mark something as ‘not interested’, you’ll see an option to undo your feedback or you can always change your recommendations feedback from your settings page.

Can I still watch a channel or category I mark as ‘not interested’?

Yes, you can still watch content you mark as ‘not interested’. We just won’t recommend it to you on your home page.

What if I mark a lot of content as ‘not interested’?

If you mark too many streamers, categories, or shelves as ‘not interested’ you may not receive any recommendations.

Are Content Display Preferences enabled for viewers by default?

For users under the age of 18, content labeled with Sexual Themes; Drugs, Intoxication, or Excessive Tobacco Use; Violent and Graphic Depictions; and Gambling will be filtered out (hidden) by default; users under the age of 18 may adjust their default content preferences from their Content Display Preferences settings here.

For all users, content labeled with Sexual Themes is blurred by default. Users may adjust this default content preference here.

What is a Twitch discovery surface?

That’s our name for the various places across Twitch where you may discover new channels, live streams, or VODs (video on demand). Many of the discovery surfaces across Twitch are defined in this article. Additional discovery surfaces may include the Feed in Twitch Mobile Apps. Learn more.

When do streamers need to apply Content Classification Labels (CCLs) to their content?

We require streamers mark their stream with a label to indicate if their content may not be appropriate for everyone, (while still maintaining our Community Guidelines). Learn more.

New Device and Location Verification

As an added layer of protection, when you log in from a device we do not recognize, you may be prompted to enter a login verification code.

Can’t access your account? If you’ve lost access to your email or phone number, forgot your password, or need help recovering your account, visit our Account Access & Login Issues Guide for complete recovery options and troubleshooting.

What Are You Trying to Do?

This article covers the New Device Verification process. In case you landed here because you’re having an issue with new device and location verification, let’s get you to the right place. Select your situation below, or visit Account Access & Login Issues Guide:

Your Situation

Where to Go

I’m not receiving the verification code

See Troubleshooting below for email delivery issues

I don’t have access to my email anymore

Account Access Guide → “Lost Access to Email”

I don’t have access to my phone anymore

Account Access Guide → “Lost Access to Phone”

I received a code I didn’t request

Someone may be trying to access your account - secure it immediately

The code isn’t working or expired

See Troubleshooting below

I’m receiving codes successfully

Continue reading How It Works below

How New Device Verification Works

When a new login attempt is made from an unrecognized device, a six-character verification code will be sent via email (if you have a verified email address and don’t have 2-Factor Authentication enabled).

If you received a code for a login you did not make, please see this article for immediate next steps to secure your account.

If you did not receive your code, be sure to check your spam folder or select the “Resend code” option on the login screen.

Enter and submit your code on the login screen. The device you logged in with will now be recognized and authorized for future access. Any new devices may require an additional login verification.

Troubleshooting

Code Received But Doesn’t Work (“Something Went Wrong” Error)

If you’re entering the correct code but getting “Something went wrong” or “Invalid code” errors:

  • Wait 2-3 minutes - The code may have expired. Request a new code using “Resend code”
  • Check for extra spaces - If you’re copying/pasting, make sure there are no spaces before or after the code
  • Try a different browser - Some users report issues with specific browsers. Try Chrome, Edge, Safari, or Firefox
  • Clear browser cache and cookies - Old session data can cause conflicts:
    • Chrome/Edge: Settings → Privacy and security → Clear browsing data
    • Firefox: Settings → Privacy & Security → Clear Data
    • Safari: Safari menu → Clear History
  • Try incognito/private browsing mode - This eliminates browser extension conflicts
  • If same code keeps arriving - Wait 10-15 minutes before requesting a new code. The system may be rate-limiting

Still not working? Contact Twitch Support and provide: your username, the email address receiving codes, a screenshot of the error message, and the browser/device you’re using.

Code Never Arrives

If you’ve checked spam, verified your email address is correct, and still don’t receive codes:

For Email Codes:

  • Add Twitch to your email contacts - Add no-reply@twitch.tv and account-notifications@twitch.tv to your contacts or safe senders list
  • Check email provider settings - Some email providers (Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo) may have aggressive spam filtering. Check your provider’s blocked senders list
  • Verify email storage isn’t full - Full inboxes block new messages. Delete old emails to free up space
  • Check email forwarding rules - Automated rules may be redirecting Twitch emails
  • Wait 10-15 minutes - Email delivery can be delayed during high traffic periods

For SMS Codes:

  • See our guide: Not Receiving SMS or 2FA Codes

Other Twitch emails arrive but not 2FA codes? This suggests a delivery issue specific to automated verification codes. Contact Twitch Support for assistance.

Verification Required on Same Device Repeatedly

Twitch may prompt for verification even on familiar devices if:

  • You cleared your browser cookies
  • You’re using incognito/private browsing mode
  • Your IP address changed significantly (VPN, mobile network, ISP change)
  • It’s been a long time since your last login on that device
  • You’re accessing from a VPN or proxy

Verification helps protect your account from unauthorized access. If you suspect unauthorized account access, change your password immediately. If you see charges you don’t recognize, contact Twitch Support immediately.

Rate Limits

If you’ve requested too many codes in a short period, you may be temporarily rate-limited. Wait 24 hours before trying again.

Lost Access to Email or Phone

Need complete account recovery help? Our Account Access & Login Issues Guide provides step-by-step instructions for recovering your account when you’ve lost access to your email or phone, including Account Recovery Tool usage, password reset options, and what to do if you can’t remember your username.

If you no longer have access to your email or phone number:

  • Try Account Recovery Tool - twitch.tv/user/account-recovery may help you regain access using alternate contact methods
  • Contact Twitch Support - link.twitch.tv/Contact-Us and explain:
    • Your username
    • The old email/phone that’s no longer accessible
    • Any other account details you remember (creation date, linked accounts, subscription history)

Important: You’ll need to verify your identity to regain access to your account.

Frequently Asked Questions

1. How do I find which account is linked to my phone number?
Use the Account Recovery Tool to see all accounts linked to your phone number:
  • Go to twitch.tv/user/account-recovery
  • Select your country code, then enter your phone number
  • Click Continue
  • Click “I Don’t Know My Username”
  • We’ll text you a list of ALL accounts linked to this phone number
2. What if I don’t receive the verification code?
If you’re not receiving your email verification code:
  • Check your email spam/junk folder
  • Verify your email address is not disabled in Settings
  • Use the “Resend code” option on the login screen
  • Wait 5 minutes - email delivery can be delayed
  • Add no-reply@twitch.tv and account@twitch.tv to your safe senders list
3. What if I can’t access my email or phone anymore?
If you’ve lost access to your email or phone number, see our guide: Account Access Guide for recovery options.
4. How long is the verification code valid?
Verification codes expire after 5 minutes. If your code has expired, click “Resend code” on the login screen to receive a new one.
5. Why am I being asked for a code every time I log in?
This can happen if:
  • You’re using private/incognito browsing mode
  • Your browser is clearing cookies automatically
  • You’re logging in from different devices
  • Your IP address changes frequently (VPN, mobile network)
Once you successfully verify a device, it should be remembered for future logins.
6. Can I disable new device verification?
No, new device verification is a security feature that cannot be disabled. However, once you verify a device, you won’t be asked again on that device unless you clear your browser cookies or log out.
7. What if I’m traveling and need to log in from a new location?
You’ll receive a verification code via email when logging in from a new location. As long as you have access to your email, you can verify the login. If you’re traveling without email access, consider enabling 2FA with an authenticator app before your trip.

We highly recommend you enable 2FA (Two-Factor Authentication) on your account for added security. For more information, see our 2FA setup article.

Smart Notifications

To help make Twitch notifications as effective and efficient as possible, we use smart notifications to ensure you get the right notifications in the right places and aren’t informed about the same thing twice.

On this page:

  • What are Smart Notifications?
  • Enabling/Disabling Smart Notifications

What are Smart Notifications?

When smart notifications are enabled, notifications are sent based on where you are. If you’re active on Twitch, you’ll receive an on-site notification when a channel you’re watching goes live. When you’re not using Twitch, you’ll receive a mobile OR email notification. Without smart notifications, every time you get a notification from Twitch, we send it to every notification channel you have turned on (onsite, mobile, and email). You could get the same notification 3 different times!

How does it work?
  • When you’re active on Twitch, you’ll get an on-site or in-app notification to let you know when a channel you follow goes live.
  • When you’re not active on Twitch, if you subscribe to mobile notifications from Twitch, you will only get a mobile notification when a channel you follow goes live. You will not also get an email when that channel goes live.
  • If you do not get mobile notifications from Twitch, you will continue to get emails when a channel you follow goes live and you are not active on Twitch.

Enabling/Disabling Smart Notifications

You can update your notification preferences on the Notifications tab of your account settings.

To disable smart notifications, click the toggle next to the Smart notifications section. For more information about customizing the events you receive notifications for, please see our Twitch Account Settings help article.

Lost Access to Email

Can you still log into your Twitch account?

Your Situation

What to Do

Yes, I can log in

  1. Go to twitch.tv/settings/security

  2. Change your email address

  3. Verify your new email

No, I can’t log in

If you added a phone number/email address to your account, use it to reset your password

If you disabled your email address, you won’t receive password reset emails. You must reactivate your email first OR use your phone number/email address for recovery.

I need to contact support

Go to Contact Support and select:

Account/Login Issues → Email Verification

If you’re a creator, please contact support.

Lost Access to Phone Number

If you no longer have access to the phone number on your Twitch account, your options depend on whether you can still log in and whether you have 2FA enabled.

Can you still log into your Twitch account?

Your Situation

What to Do

Yes, I can log in

  1. Go to twitch.tv/settings/security

  2. Remove old phone number

  3. Add new phone number

No, I can’t log in (no 2FA)

• Use your email for password reset

• Once logged in, update your phone number

No, I can’t log in (2FA enabled)

• Use your authenticator app to log in

• If you lost your authenticator: Fill out Authy’s Phone Change Form (Even if you did not use Authy for your authenticator).

• Processing time: 24-48 business hours

• This applies to ALL 2FA users (not just Authy app users)

ALL Twitch users who set up 2FA have an Authy account automatically created, regardless of which authenticator app you use. If you lose access to your phone, you’ll need to contact Authy to change it.

For more details, see: How to Change Your 2FA Phone Number

Lost Access to Both Email and Phone

If you’ve lost access to both your email and phone number, your options are limited.

Can you still log into your Twitch account?

Your Situation

What to Do

Yes, I can log in

Update both immediately:

  1. Go to twitch.tv/settings/security to update email

  2. Go to twitch.tv/settings/security to update phone

  3. Verify both new contact methods

No, I can’t log in

• If you have 2FA enabled: Use your authenticator app

• If you saved backup codes: Use those

• If neither works: Contact Twitch Support

Always keep your email and phone number up to date. Enable 2FA and save your backup codes in a secure location.

Phone Number Linked to Another Account

You can add a phone number that’s already linked to another Twitch account, including a disabled or deleted one. You don’t need to change any settings on the other account. Add the number and enter the verification code we send.

If the code doesn’t arrive, see Not Receiving Verification Codes. To see which accounts use your number, or if you don’t recognize one of them, see Managing Your Phone Number.

Forgotten Password or Username

Forgotten Password

Have you forgotten your password? No worries! We have a self-service Password Reset Request tool to help you regain access to your account. You will be prompted to enter your email or phone number associated with your account, and then your username. Once you submit your request, an email or an SMS will be sent to you with a link to reset your password.

If you need help creating a strong password, please follow our tips for Creating a Strong Password.

Password reset requests may take a few minutes to process and appear in your inbox. If you haven’t received your password reset email, please be sure to check your spam folder. If this doesn’t resolve the issue, please Contact Support.

Forgotten Username

If you’ve forgotten your username, you can use the Forgot Your Username? form to retrieve a list of the username(s) associated with your email address or phone number.

To use this form:

  • Go to twitch.tv/user/account-recovery
  • Select your country code, then enter your phone number/email address
  • Click Continue
  • Click “I Don’t Know My Username”
  • We’ll text/email you a list of ALL accounts linked to this phone number/email address

Username reminders may take a few minutes to process and appear in your inbox. If you haven’t received your username reminder, please be sure to check your spam folder.

Not Receiving Verification Email

Email is complicated. Occasionally our emails get blocked by email providers even before they go to your spam folders, so you may need to try these steps several times over a few days:

  • Head over to your Settings Page.
  • Enter a fake email address in the email field.
  • Click Save.
  • Refresh the page/leave and navigate back to your Settings Page.
  • Enter your actual email address in the email field.
  • Click Save.

If you still haven’t received the email after following these steps, we recommend adding no-reply@twitch.tv and account@twitch.tv to your allow/safe senders list to help prevent your provider from blocking emails from us.

Frequently Asked Questions

1. How do I change my email address?
After logging in to your account, you can change your email address and verify on your Settings Page.
2. How do I know which email address the password reset was sent to?
The password reset email is sent to the verified email address tied to your Twitch account. If you don’t remember which Twitch account is tied to your email address, you can use our Forgot Username flow and enter your email address.
3. What if I’m not receiving any codes at all?
First, identify what you’re trying to do (see the “Not Receiving Verification Codes” section above). The troubleshooting steps depend on your specific situation. If you’ve tried all relevant troubleshooting and still aren’t receiving codes, contact Twitch Support. Let us know specifically what you’re trying to do, and what hasn’t worked so far.
4. Can I use the same phone number on multiple Twitch accounts?
Yes. Add and verify the number on each account, even if another account using it is disabled or deleted. You don’t need to change any settings on the other account. See Managing Your Phone Number for details.
5. How long does it take to change my 2FA phone number?
If you submit the Authy Phone Change Form, processing typically takes 24-48 business hours. This applies to ALL Twitch 2FA users, regardless of which authenticator app you use.
6. What should I do if I lost access to both my email and phone?
If you can still log in, update both immediately in your settings. If you cannot log in, try using your authenticator app or backup codes. If neither works, contact Twitch Support.

We highly recommend you enable 2FA (Two-Factor Authentication) on your account for added security. For more information, see our 2FA setup article.

Passkeys

A passkey is a secure, phishing-resistant alternative to your password that lets you sign in to Twitch using your device’s fingerprint, face, or screen lock. It works alongside Two-Factor Authentication, rather than replacing it.

  • Add, view, or remove your Twitch passkeys in your Passkey settings. Avoid adding one on a shared or public device.
  • Passkeys are created, stored, and synced by your device or password manager.
  • For device-level issues (such as biometrics or syncing across devices), manage passkeys on your device and contact Apple Support or Google Support. Twitch settings only manage passkeys for your Twitch account.

Sign Out Everywhere

This will log you out of Twitch everywhere you’re logged in, including third party applications. If you believe your account has been compromised, we recommend you change your password.
