Frequently Asked Questions

What are “generative AI content models,” and what does it mean for my content to be used to train them?
Generative AI content models are AI tools that can help create or synthesize content outputs like text or images when given instructions or prompts because they are also trained on content. When you allow training, that means that your content may be used for future Gen AI model improvements. An example of what happens when you allow your content to be used for training a GenAI content model is that your audio might help refine models that create speech to text, which would help improve captions at Twitch but would also help improve captions across Amazon.
What exactly does opting out cover? What doesn’t it cover?
If you opt-out and decide to not allow your channel content to train Generative AI content models, your streams, VODs, clips, stream chats, and pictures and text on your channel will not be used in future training of a model developed by Amazon whose purpose is to generate or synthesize text, audio, images, or video.
Opting-out of training generative AI content models does not opt you out of all AI or machine learning uses at Twitch. For example, Twitch will still run AutoMod, which helps keep our community safe, but does not retain your data and use it to produce content. Twitch may also still use your data to run AI-supported features, like captions, which automatically generate captions for your Clips but does not retain your stream or your clips to train a model that can generate new content.

Manage opt-out settings at twitch.tv/settings/security

If I opt out, will other AI-powered features like Captions or safety tools still work on my channel?
Yes. There are two important differences between Generative AI content models and AI-supported features at Twitch.
1) AI-supported features at Twitch do not retain your content and then use it to train models that create new videos, images, or text.
2) Twitch users have separate controls for many of the AI-supported features we’re releasing. For example, streamers can turn on AutoMod and can adjust captions settings.

Manage opt-out settings at twitch.tv/settings/security

Why can’t I opt-out of all AI uses at Twitch?
Where AI works to help you create content or to help viewers understand your content, you do have controls over how it is used, and you can manage those in your settings.
Other AI works differently. Some of it runs the service itself, the same way our servers and our code do. Some of it keeps the service secure. And some of it, like AutoMod, protects the whole community. Turning those off for one person would weaken safety and security for everyone else on the platform, so they are not individual settings.
What channel content (clips, chat, metadata, etc.) is eligible to be used for generative AI training?
Your stream and the stream’s chat, your VODs, your Clips, Highlights, and any text or images on your Channel may be used. If you chat on someone else’s stream, their opt-out preferences govern if that chat can be used for training.

Twitch Experiments

Don’t miss Patch Notes, our monthly product update show, available the third Wednesday of each month at twitch.tv/twitch

We’re always working on new ways to improve Twitch for streamers and viewers. Experiments are an important part of that mission, and we want to be clearer with the community about how they work, who’s selected to participate in them, and which experiments we’re currently running. This page will answer those questions and more.

Experiments are valuable because they help us evaluate the potential impact of a product change before we release it broadly to the community. For example, we ran an experiment with Hype Train, and in six weeks we learned that it was effective at helping streamers earn more revenue. These insights give us the info we need to refine our approach, or, in some cases, switch our focus to something more useful.

Current Experiments

Play on Luna (desktop)

Some viewers on desktop see a Play on Luna button in the stream window when a streamer is playing a game available on Amazon Luna. Some also see Play on Luna games in the left navigation and on the Home page. Selecting Play on Luna opens Amazon Luna in a new browser tab.

Luna is an Amazon service. For questions about playing on Luna, including who can play, where it’s available, and your Amazon account, visit Amazon Luna Help & Customer Service.

Experiments FAQ

What are experiments?

An experiment is when we release a product or feature to a subset of our community to see how it affects their experience. By using a limited release, we can compare this experience to our wider community and measure impact. Experiments are generally introduced for a limited period of time so that we can test whether or not our ideas about a feature or tool could go into full product development.

Experiments have helped shape some of the tools and features you see on Twitch today, like Pinned Chat and Chat Highlights. During the four-week Pinned Chat experiment, we saw streamers connect with and celebrate their communities more easily by pinning announcements, promotions, and highlights in chat. This helped confirm the benefit to the community so we decided to make it a permanent feature. Chat Highlights were built upon the first chat highlight feature, First-Time Chatter, which helped streamers engage with viewers while they are live. We saw great chat engagement and return visits from first-time chatters during the experiment. Based on those results, we made First-Time Chatter Highlights available to all streamers and rolled out additional Chat Highlights including VIP, raiders, subscribers, and more.

Results from experiments uncover data and insights that help us iterate on our products. To do this, we introduce a new or different experience to a limited number of users so we can measure the impact. As a result, users who are taking part in our experiments will have a different experience on Twitch than the wider community for a limited time. We’re always listening to feedback from the community, and experiments are one of the ways we can test potential solutions to the community’s challenges.

How long do experiments last?
It varies. The duration of an experiment is determined by the audience size required to get us unbiased test results. Some experiments run longer than others because it takes more time for us to accumulate the traffic required to reach our sample size.
How are experiments different from an Alpha or Beta?

Experiments: An experiment is a way for us to gather early learnings about whether a tool or feature we’re testing has the potential to become a full product. Not all features at Twitch start as experiments, but we do use data to inform all of our product and feature development. Additionally, not every experiment becomes an Alpha or Beta and not every Alpha or Beta begins as an experiment.

Alpha: The Alpha is the earliest stage of product development and may have a limited feature set. We test Alpha products with very small groups of users to gain early feedback that will inform subsequent iterations.

Beta: The Beta stage is when we refine and finalize the feature set in preparation for launch. We release Beta products to more users to help uncover and squash bugs before the full product release–which is often called General Availability (GA).

How do streamers know if they’re part of an experiment?
Most of the time, streamers will not be informed that they are in an experiment because it may negatively affect the results. But if that is not the case, streamers may be notified via an email or a notification on Twitch. They may also see the below icon, which denotes that a product change is part of an experiment:
How do we select streamers for experiments?
Selection for an experiment is random within a set of parameters that make sense for the specific experiment. For example, experiments that require us to evaluate a high volume of viewer feedback may be limited to larger streamers’ channels so that we can gather data quickly and roll out a product to the community sooner. Other enrollment factors, like the size of the group we want to test, the time period we’re running the experiment, and regions all contribute to selection, and we are unable to assign specific accounts to an experiment.
Is every feature or tool Twitch is experimenting with listed on this page?
Many will be, but no, not all. We’ll list out experiments that are community-facing for streamers and viewers that would affect the day-to-day experience of using Twitch. To ensure we gather unbiased data and insights that reflect how members of the community use a tool or feature we’re testing, there may be scenarios where active experiments will not be listed on this page and users will not see the experiment icon.
Can streamers get out of an experiment or opt out of experiments altogether?
Experiment participants are selected at random to remove bias. We cannot select individual users to be included in an experiment or remove them once they’ve been selected, and users cannot opt-out of experiments.

Username Transfer Policy

Twitch usernames are provided to the first individual to register an open and available username either during account creation or through a username change in their profile settings. To be clear, usernames are claimed on a first-come, first-served basis on Twitch.

However, a username may be transferred or reclaimed by Twitch, without notice, if it:

  • infringes another’s trademarks (please note that merely registering a username that is also a trademark is not necessarily infringement, and please visit Twitch’s Trademark Policy for more information); or
  • is involved in an active impersonation (keep in mind that merely registering a username that is the same as your name is not an act of impersonation)

We reserve the right to change this policy and to transfer, change, reclaim, or remove a username at any time.

With any transferred username, Twitch will reassign the username from the original account holder to the new account holder. This means that any personal data and private content associated with the original account will not be accessible to the new account holder.

On this page:

  • Important things to note before you change your username
  • How to Change Your Username
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Important Things to Note Before You Change Your Username

Before changing usernames, all streamers should be aware of a few key facts and known issues that may impact your account:

  • Your channel URL will not redirect to your new name. You will need to update the URL anywhere you are using it.
  • If you are an Affiliate or Partner, your revenue will not be impacted. We want to stress that a username change will lead to absolutely no loss of revenue.
  • If you are a Partner, your old username will not be made available again to anyone else.
  • Usernames must be at least 4 characters long.

Note for Affiliates and Partners: Changing your username will not change your ticket product name, which is used in the URL to directly link to your subscription page. The ticket product is a unique ID taken from your registration username. It cannot be changed, even after a name change has been performed.

How to Change Your Username

  • Navigate to your Settings page, scroll down to Profile Settings, and click the Edit icon on the far right side of the username field to edit your username. Enter your desired username in the username field. If your desired username is available a green checkmark will be present.
  • You will be prompted to confirm your password in order to proceed with the username change. Enter your password, and click Verify.
  • Upon entering and verifying your password, your username will be changed. Please note it may take several minutes to take effect across the site.

Twitch users may change their usernames once every 60 days, but username changes will not be allowed during an active broadcast or when an active VOD upload is pending.

Remember that all requests to obtain a username already registered to another user are subject to our Username Transfer Policy above.

To change your username:

You must have a verified email in order to change your username. If you do not have a verified email, you will be prompted to verify. Once you have a verified email:

As stated above, Partner usernames will not be reassigned.

Frequently Asked Questions

If my username is transferred to another user by Twitch, will the new username owner have access to my information?
No. The new owner of the username will never have access to any of your data, including credit card information, settings, or viewing history.
Will people be able to change their username in order to circumvent channel or community timeouts/bans?
No, they will not be able to circumvent bans or timeouts by changing their username.
My old name still shows up in Google. Can you do anything about this?
Unfortunately, Twitch cannot remove search results for your old username.
Can I switch names with another account I own?
No, account usernames cannot be swapped between two accounts you own. Once you change the username of your first account, the original username will not be available for rename on your other account, because usernames that are abandoned by non-Partnered accounts will take at least 180 days before they are available to reclaim again through self-service.

Twitch Support does not revert accidental name changes.

What does and does not change with my Twitch account when I change my username?
Your channel URL will update immediately to your new username. Your username will change anywhere that your stream or video is shown on Twitch. In addition, your subscription name changes for new subscribers moving forward. However, long-time supporters with active subscriptions may continue to see your old username on invoices until they next cancel and resubscribe.

What does not change:

  • The prefix for your emotes does not update automatically. Partners may be able to request a change to their emote code.
  • Links to your old profile may not redirect, so be sure to update the link wherever it may be.
  • You may need to regenerate a stream key.
  • Besides your username, no profile information, settings, or history changes when you update your username. This includes any content on your channel page, followed channels/followers, notification, privacy, connection settings, and more. Changing your username does not remove or change any prior enforcements for violating our Terms of Service and/or Community Guidelines.
  • No rewards, benefits, or unlocks are removed from your account when you update your username. This includes channel points, emotes, Drops, tenure, subscriptions/subscribers, and more.
Can I approach the account owner of a username that I want and attempt to swap usernames?
No. Swapping usernames with another account owner is not supported, and may result in both account owners losing their account usernames.
Does changing my username affect my display name? (Ex: I no longer want a CJK display name)
Display names do not change when you change your username. Learn more about display names here
I logged back into my Twitch account and don’t recognize the username. What can I do?
Contact Twitch Support right away.
How do name changes affect third-party apps (ex: loyalty bots)?
Some third-party apps may not be able to recognize your account anymore once you have changed your name. You should contact the developer of the application to make sure they support name changes. Many developers will have some public information regarding this.
If I change my username, will I lose my followers, view count, followed channels, or subscriptions?
No.
I no longer want my new name. Can I change back?
For non-Partnered accounts, if you changed your username and would like to change it back, unfortunately we cannot facilitate this. You can change your name again in 60 days, but your original name will not become available again for at least 180 days.

For Partnered accounts, as stated above, Twitch Support can assist you once with changing your username. This one-time benefit can be used to change your username back to the one you previously had.

Can I have a name associated with a channel that has been banned?
In general, usernames associated with a channel that was banned by Twitch are excluded and permanently inaccessible, except in limited circumstances decided by Twitch. Twitch does not release information about TOS banned accounts to users seeking usernames, or provide details on whether an account was banned
Where can I find information on safety-related username policies and enforcement?
Please visit the Safety Center for more information on our safety-related username policies regarding account usernames and display names.

Where Are My Notifications?

We frequently hear from users that they don’t get Twitch’s “Go Live” notifications. We’ve found there are a few common reasons why that users can fix themselves - this article is the ultimate guide to help you debug your notifications and get them immediately.

Not getting notifications for a specific channel? Check if that channel is set to Personalized (the default). Personalized notifications may skip some notifications based on your viewing habits. To get all notifications, change the channel to Always in your Notification Settings under Manage Channel Notifications.

Hey, Streamers! If viewers aren’t getting your go-live notifications, tell them to visit twitch.tv/settings/notifications, find your channel under Manage Channel Notifications, and change the setting from Personalized to Always.

Where are notifications sent?

When a streamer starts their broadcast (goes live), we send out notifications to up to 3 different notification channels, depending on your settings:

  • Temporary onsite notification on web / within the mobile app
  • Push notifications on mobile
  • Email notifications

Twitch uses “smart” notifications – instead of sending notifications to all 3 destinations, a notification is sent based on where the recipient is active. If a person is on the site, they receive a notification there. If they’re offsite and have the Twitch mobile app and mobile notifications enabled, we send a push notification. If neither of those cases are true, then we send them an email.

If you’d like to receive notifications on all channels regardless of where you’re active, you can turn smart delivery off by heading over to your Notifications Settings and toggling the radio button under Smart Delivery to off.

For more information about smart delivery, please see our help article.

Common Reasons for Missed Notifications

Here are four common reasons that users don’t receive notifications:

Per Channel Notifications

Notification settings can be customized individually for each channel you follow. If you’re missing notifications for a specific channel, check your notification preference for that channel.

Each channel has four notification options:

  • Always: Receive all notifications for the channel (go-live, catch-up, subscriber updates)
  • Personalized: Receive select notifications based on your viewing preferences and habits (default setting)
  • Go Live Only: Only receive notifications when the streamer goes live
  • Off: No notifications for this channel

If your channel is set to Personalized, you may not receive every notification. Twitch curates which notifications you receive based on your viewing history, time of day, and recent notification frequency. To receive all notifications for a channel, change the setting to Always.

For more information about these settings, see About Personalized Channel Notifications.

On desktop, navigate to your Notifications Settings and expand the Manage Channel Notifications section. In this section, you can adjust notification preferences for any channel you follow.

On mobile, tap your display icon in the top left-hand corner and then tap Account Settings -> Notifications -> Manage Channel Notifications. Tap each channel to adjust its notification settings.

Alternatively, navigate to the relevant channel. Underneath the video player, tap the bell icon to change notification settings.

Notifications On

Notifications Off

Twitch Notifications Settings

We provide options to set your onsite, push, and email notifications - make sure the notification channel you want is turned on. In order to receive Live Ups notifications for channels you follow, you must make sure the Live category is turned on for your desired notification channel.

You can update your notification preferences on your Notifications Settings page. On mobile, tap your display picture in the top left-hand corner of the app, then tap Account Settings -> Notifications.

Mobile Notification Settings & Email Verification

Email and push notifications require your permission before we can send them.

For mobile push notifications, please ensure that notifications are enabled for the Twitch app on the system level for your mobile device. Generally, this can be done via your device’s application or notification settings. If you have disabled notifications for the Twitch app, you will be prompted to enable them when visiting the Mobile Settings section of your Twitch app Account Settings.

Android

iOS

In order for you to receive email notifications, the email address attached to your account needs to be verified. To check whether your email address is verified (and to verify it if it isn’t), head over to your Settings and click the Security and Privacy tab.

Smart Delivery

Smart (notification) delivery makes it easier for users to receive notifications in the most relevant destination (i.e., onsite, push, or email). We only deliver to one destination, instead of all three. You can turn smart delivery OFF by adjusting your settings on your Notifications Settings page.

For more information on smart delivery, see this article.

Moderation & Safety

About Account Enforcements and Chat Bans

Account Enforcements

When content is reported to us, we issue enforcements against accounts that we determine to have violated our Terms of Service and/or Community Guidelines.

We take a number of factors into consideration when we review reports of violations, including the intent and context, the potential for or actual harm to the community, legal obligations, and more.

Depending on the nature of the violation, we take a range of actions including a warning, a streaming suspension, a chatting suspension, and for more serious offenses, an indefinite suspension. Violations may result in loss of privileges, such as being featured on the home page or in marketing campaigns, participation in programs and events, ability to monetize your content, and/or access to features such as automated emote approvals.

Whenever we make an enforcement decision, we notify the account holder both via email. They can view details about the enforcement reason in the Appeals Portal. Out of respect for the privacy of individuals, we do not disclose details of specific enforcements with the wider community. Should the account holder wish to share this information with their community they are free to do so.

Warnings

A warning is a courtesy notice for some violations. We may also remove content associated with the violation. Repeating a violation you have already been warned for, or committing a similar violation, may result in a suspension.

Suspensions

Streaming suspension

A streaming suspension is issued when a violation occurs on stream or in a VOD/clip. If your account is suspended from streaming, you will not be able to access certain features related to streaming, including going live, creating Stories, participating in Stream Together sessions, or uploading VODs. Streaming suspensions are temporary and will last between 24 hours to 30 days.

Chatting suspension

A chatting suspension is issued when a violation occurs in chat, Whispers, or other forms of writing on Twitch. If your account is suspended from chatting, you will not be able to access certain features related to chatting, including chatting on other channels (you will still be able to chat on your own channel), sending Whispers, Cheering, redeeming Channel Points, purchasing Power-Ups, or sending custom sub/resub messages (you can still use the default sub message when subscribing to a channel). Chatting suspensions are temporary and will last between 24 hours to 30 days.

For violations that are more severe (such as hate speech), you will receive both a streaming suspension and chatting suspension regardless of where the violation occurred.

Indefinite suspension

For the most serious offenses, we will immediately and indefinitely suspend your account. You may also receive an indefinite suspension if you accumulate multiple suspensions over time. We keep a record of past violations.

On bot accounts: While we welcome bots that add new features to Twitch chat and Whispers, bot accounts that spam unwanted messages will be banned indefinitely. Bots that exceed messaging rate limits will automatically be blocked from sending more messages. To ensure your bot is not banned, please visit this link to our developer documentation to learn about message and command rate limits and how to register your bot.

Restrictions
Streaming and Chatting Suspensions

If your account receives a streaming suspension or chatting suspension, you will only lose access to the specific features related to your violation. For either type of suspension, you can continue to watch streams, follow channels, and use other Twitch features not restricted by your suspension type.

Indefinite Suspensions

If your account is indefinitely suspended, you may not access or use Twitch services, including:

  • Watching streams
  • Going live
  • Chatting
  • Using items you have purchased to use on Twitch, including Bits and subscriptions. Any recurring subscriptions you have purchased will not renew.
  • Creating other accounts
  • Appearing/participating in another user’s channel. If a suspended user appears in a third-party channel while being suspended, this could cause the suspension of the channel they appear in.

If you are a monetized streamer who receives an indefinite suspension, you will not be able to utilize Twitch monetization tools during your suspension and existing recurring subscriptions to your channel will not renew.

Expiration

Expiration is different from your suspension duration. Your suspension duration is how long you lose access to specific features (between 24 hours and 30 days). Expiration is how long the violation remains on your account record. Your suspension ends first, and you regain access to your account, but the violation stays on your record until it expires.

Most violations will expire and drop off of your account after a set period of time. Lower severity violations will expire in 90 days, and higher severity violations expire in 1 or 2 years. You can track when your violations will expire in the Appeals Portal. The expiration date shown in the Appeals Portal refers to when the violation is removed from your record, not when your suspension ends.

Escalating Consequences

In order to hold users accountable for repeated harmful behavior, there are escalating consequences if you violate within the same policy category multiple times before the initial violation expires (in 90 days, 1 year, or 2 years depending on the violation). This means that the length of suspension you receive for each subsequent violation will increase, even if the severity of the violation itself has not increased.

Ad Restrictions

Receiving temporary account suspensions for brand safety-related Community Guidelines violations (including sexual content, nudity, gambling, hateful conduct, or violence) may result in a removal of ads from your account for a short period of time. If you appeal a suspension and that appeal is accepted, your previous ads eligibility will be restored. We are making this update to ensure that we are meeting the needs of our advertisers.

Streamers who successfully request reinstatement after an indefinite suspension and are reinstated on Twitch, will have no ads for at least a month following return. In some cases, we may indefinitely disable ads on an account for ongoing brand safety concerns. You will be notified if this occurs.

Forced Username Reset

Usernames that are flagged as violating our Community Guidelines, and do not result in an indefinite suspension, will be forced to rename. When this occurs, the account is locked and cannot be recovered until the account owner completes the username reset process. Once complete, the channel owner will regain access to their account including followers, Bits, and subscriptions.

Note: DMCA notifications are not handled by our Trust & Safety team, and copyright strikes are tracked separately from enforcements issued for violations of our Community Guidelines. As we explain in our DMCA Guidelines, if we receive a complete DMCA notification against content you’ve shared on Twitch, we will generally remove or disable access to the claimed infringing material, and we may disable your livestream and/or temporarily suspend your account. We will also take note of this incident under our repeat infringer policy, and will terminate your account if you are determined to be a repeat infringer of copyrighted works.

Appealing an Account Enforcement

Appeal Types

We will review and consider appeals that satisfy one of the following categories:

  • If you believe you did not violate the Community Guidelines, or if you believe we enforced against your account incorrectly, you may appeal. You may apply for an appeal in this category, regardless of the nature of the violation for up to 6 months following the enforcement.
  • If you have served an indefinite suspension for more than 6 months, toward an enforcement that was correctly applied, you may submit a request for reinstatement. We will review requests for reinstatement following indefinite suspensions for most Community Guideline violations. We will not consider reinstatements for violations of high severity harms, such as violent content. Only one request for reinstatement will be granted per user.
Appeals Eligibility

For potential enforcement errors:

You can view enforcements applied to your account in our appeals portal. From here, if you believe you did not violate our Community Guidelines, or if you believe we enforced against your account incorrectly, you can appeal your enforcement for up to 6 months following the enforcement. There is no waiting period required to submit appeals of this type.

For requests for reinstatement while serving indefinite suspensions:

You are able to view enforcements applied to your account in our appeals portal. From here, you can appeal your indefinite enforcement.

  • You must wait at least 6 months from the date you were indefinitely suspended before requesting reinstatement. If you have previously requested reinstatement and were denied, you must wait 6 months before reapplying.
  • Requests must include taking responsibility for your actions and an acknowledgement that you violated the Community Guidelines.
  • If you have previously requested and received reinstatement, you are not eligible to make another request (only one request for reinstatement will be granted per user).
  • Upon reinstatement, you will be on probation for a period of up to 6 months following reinstatement. During this probationary period, any new violations may result in longer suspension lengths than normal, and may lead to another indefinite suspension.
Appealing a Suspension or Warning

To submit an appeal, go to our appeals portal located at appeals.twitch.tv. Appeals can be requested for enforcements issued within the last six months, or for your most recent enforcement if you are currently serving an indefinite suspension. Appeals sent via any other means will not be considered, except for suspensions related to your age (see below).

If your account was suspended for a reason related to your age and you are older than the minimum age required in your region, appeal through our contact form using the “Privacy Questions” category and “Age Suspension Appeal” sub-category. Learn more in Date of Birth Changes.

Appeals are reviewed by our Safety Operations team in the order in which they are received. There is no guarantee that enforcements will be overturned. For suspensions of 30 days or less, you may only submit 1 appeal per enforcement. For indefinite suspensions, you may only submit 1 appeal in a 6-month period per indefinite enforcement. Only the owner of the account in question may appeal an account suspension or warning. Abusing or spamming the appeals process, including repeatedly submitting unfounded appeals, may lead to additional penalties, or revoking of appeal privileges.

  • To view your recent enforcements and submit an appeal, log in to the appeals portal using the Twitch account for which you wish to appeal an enforcement. You will still be able to access the appeals portal even if your account is currently suspended.
  • Select the enforcement that you wish to appeal. The enforcement date and enforcement reason will be included alongside each enforcement, along with the suspension length or enforcement type.
  • Your user information will be pre-populated in the form at the bottom of the page. Use the description box to provide more details explaining why you would like to appeal the enforcement.
  • After your appeal has been submitted you will receive an on-screen confirmation acknowledging receipt of your appeal. The status of your appeal in the appeals portal will also be updated to “Pending.”
  • Once your appeal has been reviewed, you will receive an email notification containing our decision on your appeal, and the status of your account(s). The status of the appeal will also be updated in the appeals portal to reflect our decision. This will complete the appeals process.
  • If you are a resident of the European Union (EU) and you wish to contest our decision further, you may be able to utilize other legal methods for seeking redress. Please review our Digital Services Act (“DSA”) help page for more information.
Appealing Forced Username Resets

If you do not believe that your username violates our Community Guidelines, you may appeal the forced rename. In order to appeal, go to our appeals portal located at appeals.twitch.tv. Appeals sent via any other means will not be considered.

  • To submit an appeal, log in to the appeals portal. You will be able to log into the portal with your account even if it is currently flagged for a username reset.
  • Your user information will be pre-populated in the form at the bottom of the page. Use the description box to provide more details explaining why you believe you were incorrectly flagged for a username reset.
  • After your appeal has been submitted you will receive an on-screen confirmation acknowledging receipt of your appeal. The status of your appeal in the appeals portal will also be updated to “Pending.”
  • Once your appeal has been reviewed, you will receive an email notification containing our decision on your appeal, and the status of your account(s). The status of the appeal will also be updated in the appeals portal to reflect our decision. This will complete the appeal process.
  • If you are a resident of the European Union (EU), and you wish to contest our decision further, you may be able to utilize other legal methods for seeking redress. Please review our Digital Services Act (“DSA”) help page for more information.

To regain access to your account while you wait for your appeal, you must complete the username reset process. If your appeal is successful, you may then revert to your old username.

Account Enforcements Due to Copyright Infringement

As we explain in our DMCA Guidelines, if we receive a valid DMCA notification against content you’ve shared on Twitch, we will generally remove or disable access to the claimed infringing material, and we may disable your livestream and/or temporarily suspend your account. We will also take note of this incident under our repeat infringer policy, and will terminate your account if you are determined to be a repeat infringer of copyrighted works.

DMCA notifications are not handled by our Trust & Safety team, and copyright strikes are tracked separately from enforcements issued for violations of our Community Guidelines. To learn more about how Twitch processes DMCA notifications and your options for responding to a notification, including sending a counter-notification or requesting a retraction, please review our DMCA Guidelines.

Filing a Channel-Specific Unban Request

If you have been banned from chatting in a specific channel, you can request to be unbanned using the Unban Request feature, providing the channel owner has this option enabled. Banned users can submit a one-time unban request through the Chat column, which channel owners and moderators can review and take action on anonymously. Channel owners can also set a cooldown period which newly banned users must adhere to before they can request to be unbanned.

When reviewing unban requests, chat message logs only show messages from the past 3.5 years. Moderator actions and comments from any time period remain visible to help inform decisions.

How to file an Unban Request:

  • Navigate to the chat column of the channel you are currently banned in.

  • Click “Request Unban” and send your unban request message via the chat column interface. Note that once you have sent your unban request, you cannot edit it.

  • After you submit your request, you will receive an on-screen confirmation that your request was sent and that it is under review. You can view whether your request has been granted or denied by the channel owner/moderators via the chat column.

Date of Birth Changes

Most users don’t need to change their Date of Birth (DOB). Changing your DOB is typically only needed when appealing an account suspension related to your age. However, you may request that Twitch update your DOB at any time.

Contact Twitch Support to update your date of birth.

  • Visit help.twitch.tv/s/contactsupport
  • Select Category -> Privacy -> Data Request -> Correcting my date of birth
  • Fill out the details.
  • Verify your account by providing the following:
    • Email address on the account
    • Your Date of Birth
    • Last 4 digits of the phone used to set up 2FA
    • Current IP address
    • Attach a copy or piece of photo identification to verify your DOB and identity
  • After review, Twitch Support will inform you that your DOB is updated. There is nothing further you need to do.

If you are unable to verify your identity, we will not be able to assist you. Requests sent via any other method will not be reviewed.

If your account was suspended for a reason related to your age and you are older than the minimum required age in your region, you can appeal. Submit a request through our contact form using the “Privacy Questions” category and “Age Suspension Appeal” sub-category. Do not include attachments containing private information — if an attachment is needed, you will be informed how to send it securely.

Updating the Date of Birth on Your Monetization Onboarding

This section applies only if you have set up monetization — that is, you have completed your monetization information (whether or not you are an Affiliate or Partner yet). If you have not set up monetization, or you just need to correct the Date of Birth on your account, use the Support process described at the top of this article instead.

If you have set up monetization, you can edit your onboarding details directly from your Creator Dashboard → Monetization — you do not need to restart onboarding. Editing your information this way does not affect your monetization status and does not clear your tax forms or payout method. For the exact steps for your account, see:

  • Affiliate Onboarding Guide
  • Partner Onboarding Guide
  • About Monetization on Twitch (if you have set up monetization but are not an Affiliate or Partner yet)

If your Date of Birth field is locked

Your Date of Birth field is locked if you previously verified your age with Twitch (see Age Verification on Twitch). To change it, use the correction request at the top of this article — contact Twitch Support under Privacy → Data Request → Correcting my date of birth, and note that your Date of Birth is locked from age verification. You will need to verify your identity with the items listed above.

Payouts begin processing before the 15th of each month. If you need to update payout-related information, it’s best to do so before the 10th of the month to avoid delays. If you have earned revenue or a payout pending and you’re unsure about timing, contact Twitch Support before making changes.

Parent Inquiry

To comply with local laws, Twitch has minimum age requirements that vary by region. Read about our parental precautions in Guide for Parents and Educators

Guardians appealing the DOB of their child must first download the Parental Relationship Form.pdf, complete the answer, and attach it to your Support request.

Parents looking to delete their child’s account, visit How to Delete Your Twitch Account.

Your Data & Privacy

Your privacy is important to us. Any personal information requested by Twitch for verification purposes will only be used in connection with your request. Twitch will never ask for your personal information outside of support ticket correspondence with an official “@twitch.tv” email address or another official Twitch channel for customer communications. Please visit our Privacy Notice and Privacy Choices page for more information about Twitch’s data practices.

We require certain pieces of information from you in order to provide you a service. Your DOB is part of a category of information that you provide Twitch. You give us this information when you Create a Twitch Account. We use this information to verify you are who you say you are.

If you wish to delete your DOB or remove it, you can delete your Twitch account. This will permanently erase your content and account data within 90 days of your request. In some cases, Twitch may retain limited personal data for legal, security and other reasons permitted or required under applicable law. For more information, please refer to our Privacy Notice.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does Twitch share my DOB with any third-parties?
No. Your DOB is never shared with third parties. Your DOB is used only by Twitch to verify your account identity, and for tax purposes. Guard this information carefully.
What can parents request of Twitch on behalf of their children?
Parents may request the closure of a child’s account if that child is between the ages of 13-16. Parents may appeal the suspension of a child’s account if the child was mistakenly suspended for being under 13, and the child is aged 13-16.
Why do you need my information?
In order to make changes to your account, Twitch must verify your identity. If you are unable to verify your identity, Twitch cannot assist you further.
How old do you need to be to use Twitch?
The Twitch Services are not available to persons under the age of 13, the age of 16 in Australia, or the minimum age required for use of the Twitch Services in your jurisdiction of residence if that age is older than 13 (the “Minimum Age”).
Can Twitch Support tell me the date of birth on my account?
No. For security purposes, Twitch Support cannot read back or confirm the date of birth on your account. To update your date of birth, submit a correction request with your correct date of birth and valid photo identification. You do not need to know the current value on your account to request a change.
Why can’t I edit my Date of Birth during onboarding?
Your Date of Birth is locked if you previously verified your age with Twitch (see Age Verification on Twitch). To change it, contact Twitch Support under Privacy → Data Request → Correcting my date of birth and note that it’s locked from age verification.

How to File a User Report

If you come across a broadcaster or user on Twitch whom you feel has violated Twitch’s Terms of Service (ToS) or Community Guidelines (CG), you have the ability to send a report to our Moderation team for review.

How to File a Report on Desktop

Reporting a Channel
  • Click the 3 Vertical Dots icon in the bottom right below the video player on the channel to report the live stream itself (using Report Live Stream) or other attributes of the user such as their username or their avatar (using Report Something Else).
  • You can also initiate a report for a user’s chat messages or Whispers under the Report Something Else menu, but we recommend reporting directly from the chat message or the Whisper so that our team knows exactly what message you are reporting.
  • To report a VOD, highlight, or clip, please submit your report directly from the actual piece of content you are trying to report.
  • Clicking on either Report Live Stream or Report Something Else will open the reporting flow.
  • Follow the report flow to select the most appropriate category for your report and write a detailed description of the violation in the Tell Us More field. If the correct category isn’t listed on the first page of the form, you can select Search in order to search for the reason category.
  • Click Submit Report, and a confirmation will appear confirming that your report has been submitted.
Reporting a User in the Chat
  • Click on the user’s name in chat.
  • Click the 3 Vertical Dots icon at the bottom right and then the Report option. This will open the reporting flow.
  • Follow the report flow to select the most appropriate category for your report and write a detailed description of the violation in the Tell Us More field. If the correct category isn’t listed on the first page of the form, you can select Search in order to search for the reason category.
  • Click Submit Report, and a confirmation will appear confirming that your report has been submitted.
Reporting a Whisper
  • Click the Cog located in the top right of your Whisper window.
  • Click the Report option.
  • Follow the report flow to select the most appropriate category for your report and write a detailed description of the violation in the Tell Us More field. If the correct category isn’t listed on the first page of the form, you can select Search in order to search for the reason category.
  • Click Submit Report, and a confirmation will appear confirming that your report has been submitted.

How to File a Report on Mobile

Reporting a Channel
  • Tap the 3 Horizontal Dots icon in the top right corner.
  • Android
  • iOS
  • Select Report from the menu that appears on the bottom of the screen.
  • Select the most appropriate report reason from the menu that pops up. If the correct category isn’t listed on the first page of the form, you can select Search in order to search for the reason category.
  • Type out a detailed description in the Tell Us More field and tap send.
  • Confirmation will pop up stating that your report has been sent.
Reporting a User in the Chat
  • Tap on the username in the chatroom.
  • Android
  • iOS
  • Select Report from the menu that appears.
  • Select the most appropriate report reason from the menu that pops up. If the correct category isn’t listed on the first page of the form, you can select Search in order to search for the reason category.
  • Type out a detailed description in the Tell Us More field and tap send.
  • Confirmation will pop up stating that your report has been sent.
Reporting a Whisper
  • Tap the Cogicon next to the user that you are reporting from inside the whisper screen.
  • Android
  • iOS
  • Select Report from the menu that appears on the bottom of the screen.
  • Select the most appropriate report reason from the menu that pops up. If the correct category isn’t listed on the first page of the form, you can select Search in order to search for the reason category.
  • Type out a detailed description in the Tell Us More field and tap send.
  • Confirmation will pop up stating that your report has been sent.

Please note that abuse of the User Report Tool constitutes a violation of our Terms of Service and Community Guidelines. Accounts associated with such activity may be suspended. Mass or repeatedly reporting the same content will not increase the speed in which a report is investigated.

How to Use the Batch Reporting Tool

During a stream, streamers and moderators often need to keep a close watch on chat and may not have the time or attention to submit reports to Twitch in real-time. With the Batch Reporting Tool widget within Mod View, streamers and their moderators can now easily view a list of recently banned or timed out users and submit reports to Twitch in bulk at a time that makes sense for them, such as during a lull in the stream or after the stream has ended.

  • Select the Batch Reporting Tool widget from the left side vertical nav within Mod View.
  • If you’d like to add it to your Mod View layout, you can drag it out towards where you’d like it to be placed.
  • You can filter the list of viewers by the mod actions that were taken against them: “Everything”, “Bans”, or “Timeouts”; or by who took the mod actions against them: “By Everyone” or “By You”. You can also hide specific users from the list by clicking the to the right of each user.
  • Using the drop-down menu at the left of each viewer in the list, select the most appropriate report reason.
  • Use the Tell Us More field to provide additional details and context on why you’re submitting the report, which will help our team take action on your report faster.
  • Click the Report button at the bottom right of the widget to submit your report(s).

Users will be shown in the Batch Reporting Tool for 8 hours after being banned or timed out. Users that have already been reported will be shown with a check mark.

Reporting Best Practices

When filing a report, select the most appropriate category. This ensures that your report is processed as quickly and effectively as possible. Selecting a more severe report reason than is appropriate will not increase the likelihood of enforcement.

In your report, please include as much context as possible in the Tell Us More field. We’ve provided some guidance on the most helpful kinds of additional information that you can include.

  • Date, time (including time zone), and description of the violation
  • Where the violation occurred and/or the target of the violation
  • For example: The username of the person being harassed, the name of the channel in which the violation occurred
  • Timestamps (if applicable)
  • Game names
  • This is useful for reporting in-game cheating or prohibited games.

The more information and context you provide, the more effectively our specialists can process your report. After reporting a user you will be presented with an option to block them. If your report pertains to user harassment, please also see our help article for more information on how to manage harassment in chat.

Report Feedback

After you’ve filed a report, you will receive a confirmation email that the report was received. If action was taken on the account you reported for the reason you provided you will also receive an email confirming that action was taken. If you don’t see this email, make sure to check your Spam folder.

You will not receive the action confirmation email if:

  • No action was taken.
  • Action was taken for a different reason than the one you reported (i.e. you reported for harassment and the infraction/violation was spam)
  • Action has already been taken for the same content you reported (i.e. the reported user has already been suspended) OR
  • The report relates to alleged criminal behavior.

Please know that even if you do not receive a notification, each report you submit is reviewed by a member of our moderation team.

If you are a resident of the European Union (EU), there may be additional circumstances under which you’ll receive an enforcement confirmation email. Please see our Digital Services Act (“DSA”) help page for additional information.

To protect the privacy of those involved we do not disclose details about the specific enforcement action to the user(s) who reported the violation.

To report conduct that occurred off Twitch, visit our Safety Center reporting guide for instructions on how to submit a report to our Off-Service Investigation Team.

Moderation & Safety: Account Security

Authy Desktop App Shutdown

On March 19th, 2024, the Authy desktop app will shut down, and no longer provide valid two-factor authentication (2FA) temporary one-time password (TOTP) codes on Twitch. The Authy app is provided by Twilio. Read Twilio’s announcement here.

We recommend that you install and log into the Authy mobile app, available here for both iOS and Android. Authy desktop users who enable Backups before the shutdown will instantly have access to 2FA codes when logging into the Authy mobile app.

If you are on an M1/M2 Apple Mac device, you are able to install the Mac OS version of the Authy desktop app, which will continue to be supported. Identify your MacBook Pro Model here.

If you can’t log in

Most Authy desktop app users can simply log into the Authy mobile app, without interruption. However, Twitch users without access to the phone number they used to create their account may experience disruptions.

We strongly suggest that Twitch users without access to their original phone numbers sign into the Authy mobile app before the Authy desktop app is shut down. After March 19, 2024, those Twitch users without access to their original phone numbers will not be able to sign into Twitch or modify their 2FA settings without Twilio modifying the old phone number to a new, working number.

To contact Authy for a phone number change, follow the recovery instructions in Authy’s guide.

If you don’t hear back from Twilio

  • Monitor your email inbox (including your spam folder) for emails from noreply@authy.com.
  • Contact Twilio directly, or review this resource.

If you require further assistance

Contact Twitch Support at the link below if you require account access to manage an upcoming subscription renewal, or other time-sensitive issues.

Creating a Strong Password

Secure your Twitch account by using a strong and unique password created with a password manager like LastPass or 1Password. Turn on two-factor authentication to protect your account even more!

  • Make your Twitch password as unique as you. Don’t reuse the same password across multiple sites. If you have a favorite password that you created for another site, please don’t use it here!
  • Make your password longer and more complex. If you use a password manager (such as 1Password or LastPass), you’re in luck, it can do this for you. If you aren’t using a password manager, here’s what you need to know. Your passwords should be at least 8-10 characters long, but the longer the better. Your password can be more than one word! It is easier to remember “easier to remember” than Password1, or 987654321 and it is a better password.
  • Your password can be too easy (it doesn’t have enough characters), too weak (not complex enough), just fair (we recommend that you make it longer), or strong. Choose a combination of letters, numbers, and special characters to make your password stronger. Do not reuse a previous password.
  • Be creative! Don’t use single dictionary words. Avoid simple words, phrases, and patterns that are easy to guess. Passwords with obvious words and phrases like “password”, “twitch”, or “1234” put your account at risk.

How to Change Your 2FA Phone Number on Twitch

2FA protects your account from unauthorized logins. When you enable 2FA on your Twitch account, an Authy account and ID are created for you, and linked to that phone number, regardless of the authenticator you use.

Lost access to your account? If you can’t log in to your Twitch account, have lost access to your email or phone, or need help recovering your account, visit our Account Access & Login Issues Guide before attempting to change your 2FA phone number.

Authy Account:

  • Why do I have an Authy account?
  • Can I delete my Authy account?
  • What if I have multiple Twitch accounts associated with multiple Authy accounts?
  • What do I do if I requested a phone change from Authy?
  • How can Authy help me?
How do I change my 2FA phone number on Twitch?

When you enable Two-Factor Authentication on Twitch, an Authy account is automatically created and linked to your phone number. This happens regardless of which authentication method you use (Authy app, Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, SMS codes, etc.).

If you still have access to your old phone number and your Twitch account:

  • Go to twitch.tv/settings/security
  • Click Edit Two-Factor Authentication
  • Enter the 2FA code from your authentication app or SMS
  • Click Modify next to Text Message (Backup)
  • Choose your new phone number’s country code, then enter the number
  • Enter the verification code sent to your new number
  • Click Submit

Your 2FA will now be linked to your new phone number.

What if I don’t have access to my old phone?

All Twitch users with 2FA enabled have an Authy account, regardless of which authentication method you use (SMS codes, Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, Authy app, etc.).

If you still have access to your Twitch account but lost your old phone:

  • Use a backup code to log in (if you saved them when setting up 2FA)
  • Go to twitch.tv/settings/security
  • Follow the steps in the above FAQ, How do I change my 2FA phone number?

If you cannot access your Twitch account (lost phone/authentication device):

  • Fill out Authy’s Phone Change Form
  • Authy will process your request within 24-48 business hours
  • Once approved, you can log in with your new phone number

If you see charges you don’t recognize or suspect unauthorized account access, contact Twitch Support immediately. Do not use the Authy phone change process for fraud or unauthorized purchase issues.

The above process applies to ALL Twitch 2FA users, not just those using the Authy app.

What if I don’t have access to my Twitch account?

If you cannot log in to your Twitch account because you lost access to your phone number or authentication device:

  • Fill out Authy’s Phone Change Form
  • Provide your old phone number and new phone number
  • Authy will verify your identity and process the change within 24-48 business hours
  • Once approved, you can log in to Twitch using your new phone number

All Twitch 2FA users have an Authy account automatically created, regardless of which authentication app you use. This process works for everyone with 2FA enabled.

Need more account recovery help? Our Account Access & Login Issues Guide covers lost passwords, lost email/phone access, Account Recovery Tool instructions, and complete troubleshooting for all login scenarios.

For additional help, see: Can’t Access Your Account?

What if I don’t have a new phone number?

You must have a new phone number to change your 2FA phone number. Twitch requires a valid phone number for Two-Factor Authentication.

Your options:

  • Get a new phone number: Obtain a mobile phone number from a carrier
  • Use an authenticator app instead: If you have access to your account, you can continue using your current authentication app (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, etc.) without changing your phone number
  • Use backup codes: If you saved backup codes when setting up 2FA, you can use those to log in

Note: VoIP numbers (Google Voice, Skype, etc.) and landlines are not supported for 2FA verification codes.

What if I only have a VoIP (Voice over Internet Protocol) number?

VoIP numbers (such as Google Voice, Skype, WhatsApp, or other internet-based phone services) are not supported for Twitch Two-Factor Authentication.

Why VoIP numbers don’t work:

  • VoIP numbers cannot reliably receive SMS verification codes
  • They are more vulnerable to security risks
  • Twitch requires a mobile carrier phone number for 2FA

Your options:

  • Get a mobile phone number: Obtain a phone number from a mobile carrier (AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile, etc.)
  • Use an authenticator app: You can use Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, or Authy app instead of SMS codes. These apps work without requiring SMS delivery.

To set up an authenticator app, visit: Setting up Two-Factor Authentication

What if I only have a landline?

Landline phone numbers are not supported for Twitch Two-Factor Authentication. Twitch requires a mobile phone number that can receive SMS text messages.

Why landlines don’t work:

  • Landlines cannot receive SMS text messages
  • 2FA verification codes are sent via SMS
  • Voice calls for verification codes are not supported

Your options:

  • Get a mobile phone number: Obtain a phone number from a mobile carrier
  • Use an authenticator app: You can use Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, or Authy app instead of SMS codes. These apps generate codes without requiring a phone number for SMS delivery.

To set up an authenticator app, visit: Setting up Two-Factor Authentication

What if there is an error confirming my code?

If you’re getting an error when entering your 2FA verification code:

Common issues and solutions:

  • Code expired: 2FA codes expire after 30 seconds. Request a new code and enter it immediately.
  • Wrong code: Make sure you’re entering the most recent code from your authentication app or SMS.
  • Time sync issue: If using an authenticator app, ensure your device’s time is set to automatic. Go to your device settings and enable “Set time automatically.”
  • Typing error: Double-check you’re entering the code correctly with no spaces.
  • Rate limit: If you’ve requested too many codes, wait 24 hours before trying again.

Still not working?

  • Try using a backup code (if you saved them when setting up 2FA)
  • See our troubleshooting guide: Not Receiving Verification Codes?
  • If you’ve lost access to your phone, see the earlier FAQ: What if I don’t have access to my old phone?
Why do I have an Authy account?

All Twitch users who enable Two-Factor Authentication automatically have an Authy account created. This happens regardless of which authentication method you choose to use.

How it works:

  • When you enable 2FA on Twitch, an Authy account and Authy ID are automatically created in the background
  • This Authy account is linked to your phone number
  • You have an Authy account even if you use Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, SMS codes, or any other authentication method
  • You don’t need to download the Authy app to have an Authy account

Why Twitch uses Authy:

  • Authy provides the backend infrastructure for Twitch’s 2FA system
  • This allows you to recover your account if you lose access to your phone
  • It enables phone number changes through Authy’s verification process

For more information about setting up 2FA, visit: Setting up Two-Factor Authentication

Can I delete my Authy account?

You cannot delete your Authy account separately from your Twitch account. Your Authy account is automatically created when you enable 2FA on Twitch and is tied to your Twitch account.

Your options:

  • Disable 2FA on Twitch: Go to twitch.tv/settings/security and turn off Two-Factor Authentication. This will disable your Authy account for Twitch. (This step is not recommended).
  • Keep 2FA enabled: We strongly recommend keeping 2FA enabled for account security. Your Authy account provides important account recovery options.

If you disable 2FA, you will lose access to exclusive 2FA emotes and your account will be less secure.

What if I have multiple Twitch accounts associated with multiple Authy accounts?

Each Twitch account with 2FA enabled has its own Authy account linked to a phone number. If you have multiple Twitch accounts, you can:

Option 1: Use the same phone number for all accounts

  • You can link multiple Twitch accounts to the same phone number
  • Each account will have its own separate Authy ID
  • You’ll receive 2FA codes for whichever account you’re logging into

Option 2: Use different phone numbers for each account

  • Each Twitch account can be linked to a different phone number
  • Each will have its own Authy account
  • Useful if you want to keep accounts completely separate

To find which accounts are linked to a phone number:

  • Go to twitch.tv/user/account-recovery
  • Select your country code, then enter your phone number
  • Click Continue
  • Click “I Don’t Know My Username”
  • We’ll text you a list of ALL accounts linked to this phone number
What do I do if I requested a phone change from Authy?

If you submitted a phone change request through Authy’s Phone Change Form:

What to expect:

  • Processing time: Authy typically processes phone change requests within 24-48 business hours
  • Verification: Authy will verify your identity before approving the change
  • Notification: You’ll receive confirmation once the change is complete

After your phone change is approved:

  • Go to twitch.tv
  • Click Log In
  • Enter your username and password
  • When prompted for 2FA code, use your new phone number to receive the code
  • Enter the verification code

If it’s been more than 48 business hours:

  • Check your email for updates from Authy
  • Visit Authy’s Help Center for support
  • Note: Twitch Support cannot expedite or modify Authy phone change requests
How can Authy help me?

Authy provides the backend infrastructure for Twitch’s Two-Factor Authentication system. Authy can help you with:

Phone number changes:

  • If you lost access to your old phone number and cannot log in to Twitch
  • Submit a request at: Authy Phone Change Form
  • Processing time: 24-48 business hours

Authy app support:

  • If you’re using the Authy app and need help with app features
  • Backup and restore questions
  • Multi-device setup

Authy resources:

  • Help Center: help.twilio.com
  • Phone Change Form: forms.authy.com/phones/change

What Authy cannot help with:

  • Twitch account access issues unrelated to 2FA
  • Twitch account suspensions or bans
  • Twitch billing or subscription issues

For Twitch-specific issues, visit: Can’t Access Your Account?

More Resources

If you haven’t yet set up 2-Factor Authentication, you can do so here: twitch.tv/settings/security. Read our guide on turning on 2FA here: help.twitch.tv/s/article/two-factor-authentication

Not receiving SMS messages or 2FA codes? Visit our troubleshooting guide here: help.twitch.tv/s/article/not-receiving-sms

How to Change Your Password

Contact Twitch Support here right away if you suspect unauthorized access to your account. Learn more.

Changing your Twitch account password periodically can help prevent access from bad actors. Make sure your new password is strong and unique.

Changing your password will result in the invalidation of your stream key, and the revocation of existing account credentials issued to 3rd party services. In other words, once you reset your password, you will need to re-add and re-link all 3rd party services to your Twitch account such as Prime, or game accounts for Drops.

Changing Your Password on Desktop

To change your password on desktop, click here.

  • Visit your Account Settings
  • Click the Change Password link (You may need to re-authenticate)
  • In the next window, enter your old password, a new password you wish to use, and a confirmation of your new password.
  • Make sure your password is strong and secure. Learn more.
If You Can’t Change Your Password

Contact Twitch Support right away.

Changing Your Password on Mobile

You cannot change your password while logged into the Twitch mobile app. To change your password in the Twitch mobile app, log out, log in, then select Trouble Logging In.

  • Enter your email, or phone number instead.
  • Enter the username of the account you wish to change the password for
  • Select Send my password reset link

If you entered a phone number instead of an email, you’ll need to enter a verification code sent by SMS. Confirm your old and new password, and you are done!

If you entered an email instead of a phone number, you’ll need access to the email associated with your Twitch account to proceed. Choose and confirm your new password.
