Setting up Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)

Twitch offers two-factor authentication (2FA) to protect your account from unauthorized logins. Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) means two different methods of verification will be required to log in to your Twitch account: your password and your mobile phone. If your password is compromised, your account will be inaccessible without the unique code sent to your phone.

Important: When you enable 2FA on Twitch, an Authy account is automatically created and linked to your phone number. This happens regardless of which authentication app you use (Authy, Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, etc.). If you lose access to your phone number, you’ll need to contact Authy to change it.

To get started as an Affiliate or Partner, you need to turn on Two-Factor Authentication (2FA). Learn more about becoming an Affiliate.

This article will walk you through setting up Two-Factor Authentication via SMS and TOTP (temporary one-time password) for your Twitch account.

If you need further information including troubleshooting and answers to other frequently asked questions regarding 2FA and Authy, check out this article for more information.

Enabling Two Factor Authentication (2FA) on Twitch

When you enable 2FA, you will be logged out of Twitch on all devices except for the one used to do so.

To begin set-up of Two-Factor Authentication the email tied to your Twitch account must be verified.

Once your account is verified and you’re ready to set-up 2FA head to your Security and Privacy settings page. From there, follow these steps:

  • Select Set Up Two-Factor Authentication
  • Select Enable 2FA
  • Enter your phone number (we do not recommend using VOIP numbers) and select Continue
  • Enter the 7 digit verification code you receive via text message and select Continue
  • After verifying your phone number via SMS, you can optionally set up an authenticator app for TOTP (“temporary one-time password”). If you have a preferred authenticator app, scan the QR code displayed using your phone camera. Note: SMS verification is always required first, even if you plan to use an authenticator app. If you’re enabling Two-Factor Authentication on the Twitch mobile app, you will need to use SMS.
  • If you do not have an authenticator app, you will need to download one from your phones respective app store. You may also opt to use SMS as your primary 2FA, if you are unable to use an authenticator app.
  • You can scan the QR code with multiple apps and devices to have a backup in the case you lose access to your primary authentication device / app.
  • Once you have scanned the QR code, enter the 6 digit verification code generated in the authentication app and select Submit.

If you have followed all steps correctly, your account should now be secured with Two-Factor Authentication (2FA), and TOTP (“temporary one-time password”).

Please see our Authy 2FA Management & FAQ article for helpful advice on managing, securing, and recovering your 2FA account via Authy.

Authenticator Backups (TOTP)

If you lose your mobile device or access to it, having backups enabled for your authenticator will allow you to easily regain access to your account. Some authenticator apps do not support backups, however below we’ve listed a few that do.

Authy

Authenticator Backups are an opt-in feature for Authy and will not be enabled by default. Click here to learn more about Authenticator Backups on Authy.

Duo Mobile

Duo Restore is an opt-in feature for Duo Mobile that can be easily enabled. Click here to learn more about Duo Restore on Duo Mobile.

Microsoft Authenticator

Cloud Backup is an opt-in feature for Microsoft Authenticator. Click here to learn more about Cloud Backup on the Microsoft Authenticator app.

Another alternative that supports multiple device syncing is an application called 1Password, which also inherently helps to keep you safe by creating and saving strong random passwords for you too!

If you choose to use an alternative authentication app, be sure to check if backups are supported. Enabling them will help to save a lot of hassle should you ever lose your device or access to it.

Receiving 2FA Emotes

Once you have successfully enabled 2FA SMS and TOTP, you will be rewarded with exclusive emotes!

  • Navigate to the “Unlocked” section of the emote picker within chat.
  • You should now see all 6 exclusive emotes available.

Your emotes will be removed whenever 2FA SMS or TOTP are disabled, including when you switch from one authenticator app to another. When you complete setup or re-enable 2FA in your authenticator app, the emotes will return. Keep your accounts protected!

Frequently Asked Questions

How can I change or remove my authentication app (TOTP)?
You can change or remove your authentication app by going to your Security and Privacy settings and selecting “Edit Two-Factor Authentication.” Then:
  • Click Modify
  • Read the warning about removing 2FA, then click Continue
  • Enter your password
  • You will see the Two-Factor Authentication setup screen with 3 steps: download an authenticator app, scan the QR code, and verify the code
  • Scan the QR code with your new authenticator app and submit the verification code to complete the switch
To switch to SMS instead of an authenticator app: On the setup screen, select the option to skip and use SMS.
What can I do if I lose access to my device and / or phone number?

Important: When you set up Two-Factor Authentication on your Twitch account, an Authy account is automatically created for you and linked to your phone number. This happens regardless of which authentication app you choose to use (Authy, Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, etc.).

If you lose access to your device and have backups enabled for your authentication app, you can quickly recover access by utilizing the backup / restore feature. For more information on backups, click here.

If you no longer have access to your old phone number: You will need to contact Authy to change the phone number associated with your Authy account. Fill out Authy’s Phone Change Form to recover access to your account. This process applies to all Twitch users with 2FA enabled, not just those actively using the Authy app. For more information, please visit their Help Center.

What authentication app should I use?
In short, you can use any app that supports TOTP (Time-based One-Time Password) authentication. Some examples are: Authy, Microsoft Authenticator, Last Pass and Duo Mobile.
Will I keep the exclusive emotes if I disable Two-Factor Authentication on my account?
No, if you disable Two-Factor Authentication on your account you will lose access to the exclusive emotes until it is re-enabled.

What can I do if someone else accessed my account?

If you believe your account has been inappropriately accessed, you can take action to regain control and prevent future abuse. It is very important that you change your password as soon as possible. We also highly recommend immediately setting up Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) to provide an additional layer of security.

How do I know my account was inappropriately accessed?

Some of the more obvious signs of your account being inappropriately accessed include:

  • Any changes to your account settings or profile that you didn’t make.
  • Unrecognized purchases.
  • Unable to login with your credentials.
  • Receiving notifications for creators that you didn’t follow.
  • Whispers/chat messages that you didn’t send.
  • Changes to your payout method or other account information that you don’t recognize.
  • Your account was unexpectedly suspended.
  • Your language selection has changed.

What can I do to recover/regain control of my account?

In order to secure your account, we recommend following the steps below:

  • Sign Out Everywhere - If you suspect your account has been accessed elsewhere without your permission, you can sign out everywhere via your security settings at twitch.tv/settings/security
  • Delete Payment Methods - If you’ve noticed unrecognized purchases, we highly recommend deleting any currently saved payment methods. This will help protect against additional purchases being made while your account is being secured.
  • (Monetized Creators Only) Check Your Payout Method - If you are a monetized Creator, ensure your payout method is still set to yours. Change your payout method in the Onboarding Info section of your Affiliate or Partner Settings. Select Change Payout Method. More info in this help article.
  • Review all installed Browser Extensions - Remove any that you do not recognize or trust.
  • Browser
  • Directions
  • Chrome
  • Go to chrome://extensions in your address bar.
  • Firefox
  • Go to about:addons in your address bar, and click on Extensions on the left.
  • Edge
  • Go to edge://extensions in your address bar.
  • Safari
  • Go to Safari in the top left, click Preferences…, and click on the Extensions tab.
  • Opera and Opera GX
  • Go to opera://extensions in your address bar.
  • Review all installed programs / apps on your computer or other device you use to access Twitch - Remove any you do not recognize or trust.
  • Scan your computer/device for viruses and malware - Scan your computer or other device using trusted antivirus software or Windows Defender, which is built into Windows Operating Systems.
  • Remove Connections - In the past, you may have allowed 3rd party apps limited access to your account. In order to secure your account completely, we recommend disconnecting all apps under the Other Connections section of your Connections Settings.
  • Check your account email - Check within your Twitch security settings to make sure the email on the account is still your correct email address. If it is not we recommend attempting to change the email address back to the one you have access to as soon as possible.
  • Secure your email - To better protect your Twitch account we recommend you change your password on the email associated with your Twitch account. This is especially important if your Twitch account password was the same as your email password. We also recommend setting up Two-Factor Authentication on your email if it is available through your email provider.
  • See the step below for additional information on this and how to set it up.
  • Reset your password - Use a unique password you have not used anywhere else. A combination of letters, numbers and symbols, as well as significant password length, are contributors to having a strong password.
  • Check out this article for more tips.
  • Set up Two-Factor Authentication - 2FA provides an additional layer of security for your account. It is a great tool to help ensure access to your account is limited to just you.
  • See our article on Setting up Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) for your Twitch account for more information.
  • Contact Us - If after completing all of the necessary steps above you do not have control of your account or have unauthorized payments charged to you, please open a ticket with us so that we can assist you.
  • To ensure that your case is handled in the fastest way possible, please choose from the correct contact options based on what is happening.
  • If you notice suspicious or unrecognized transactions after securing your account using the steps above, contact us at this link.
  • If you can not login after you suspect your account has been accessed by someone else and you have followed the above steps already, file your case under Account/Login Issues > Logging In > My account has been hacked or stolen (without charges).
  • If you’re noticing unauthorized charges after your account was accessed by someone else, please file your case under Purchases > Unrecognized / Unauthorized Charges.

What if I can’t find or don’t have access to my account?

If you cannot find your account or do not have access to your account and believe it has been inappropriately accessed, we recommend you first try to request a password reset. If you do not receive an email with instructions on resetting your account password the email on the account may have changed.

If you are unable to access your account after requesting a password reset, you can contact us by opening a support ticket.

Receiving 2FA requests when you haven’t logged in recently?

If you already have 2FA enabled, and you’re receiving 2FA login requests when you haven’t logged in recently, this is likely an indication that your password has been inappropriately accessed. Fortunately, 2FA is helping to keep your account secure by blocking the unexpected login attempt. In a situation like this, we recommend that you change your password, and leave 2FA enabled.

Moderation & Safety: Channel Moderation

About Bans, Blocking, and Suspensions

On Twitch, the terms “ban,” “block,” and “suspension” have specific meanings. While some members of the Twitch community may use these terms interchangeably, understanding the differences can help you navigate the platform and our help articles more easily.

For more information about enforcements and safety on Twitch, visit the Safety Center.

Bans

On Twitch, a ban refers to being removed from a specific channel’s chat. Channel owners and moderators can ban users from participating in their chat. When you are banned from a channel:

  • You cannot send messages in that channel’s chat
  • You cannot comment on that channel’s clips, and any existing comments you’ve made are hidden
  • You can still watch the stream (unless the channel owner has enabled additional restrictions)
  • The ban only applies to that specific channel

Bans can be temporary (called “timeouts”) or permanent. A timeout is a temporary ban that lasts for a set period of time, after which you can chat again.

If you’ve been banned from a channel and the channel owner has enabled Unban Requests, you can request to be unbanned. Learn more about filing an Unban Request.

Community Usage

In casual conversation, some members of the Twitch community may use “ban” to refer to account suspensions. However, in Twitch’s official communications and help articles, we use “ban” specifically for channel-level chat restrictions.

Blocking

Blocking is a personal privacy tool that allows you to stop interactions with specific users across Twitch. When you block someone:

  • They are removed from your followers/following list
  • They are prevented from following you, and vice-versa
  • You won’t see their messages in any chat
  • You won’t see them in channel recommendations across Twitch, and vice-versa
  • They cannot send you whispers (direct messages)
  • They won’t be able to subscribe to your channel
  • They won’t be able to purchase gift subs for other users in your channel
  • They cannot comment on your clips, and their existing comments are hidden (Learn more)
  • The block works in both directions—they also won’t see your messages
  • The blocked user is not notified that you’ve blocked them

Blocking is different from a ban because it’s an action you take for yourself, not something a channel owner or moderator does. Many tools and experiences on Twitch are designed to prevent users from being able to interact with you if you block them. You can block and unblock users at any time from your Security Settings.

Learn more about blocking users.

Suspensions

A suspension is an enforcement action taken by Twitch against an account for violating our Terms of Service or Community Guidelines. Suspensions are site-wide and affect your entire Twitch account.

Learn more about account enforcements and how to appeal.

Frequently Asked Questions

What’s the difference between a ban and a suspension?
A ban (commonly “chat ban”) is a channel-specific action taken by a streamer or their moderator that prevents you from chatting in one particular channel. A suspension is a site-wide enforcement action by Twitch that, depending on where the violation occurred, restricts your entire account from using the site; or restricts access to certain features such as chatting or streaming.
If I block someone, can they still see my streams?
No. Blocking someone on Twitch prevents them from viewing your livestreams, in addition to preventing chat and whisper interactions. There is also a separate channel setting that allows you to decide whether banned chatters can view your stream. Blocked users are always prevented from viewing, regardless of that setting.
Can I appeal a ban from someone’s channel?
If the channel owner has enabled Unban Requests, you can submit a one-time request to be unbanned. The channel owner or their moderators will review your request and decide whether to grant it. Twitch does not get involved in channel-specific bans.
Will someone know if I block them?
No. When you block someone on Twitch, they are not notified. They may notice that they can’t see your messages or send you whispers, but they won’t receive a direct notification about the block.

How to Handle Viewership Botting and Fake Engagement

At Twitch, the concerns and welfare of the community as a whole are taken very seriously. We are always investigating artificially inflated viewers, chat activity, and follower counts, and are constantly collecting information on users that are utilizing these bots.

On this page:

  • What is fake engagement
  • What is view-botting?
  • What is follow-botting?
  • Why is botting bad?
  • How to deal with fake engagement
  • How to deal with someone else being botted

What is fake engagement?

Fake engagement is artificial inflation of channel statistics, such as views or follows, through coordination or 3rd party tools. This behavior is characterized by the creation of incidental or duplicitous views or follows. One common form of this activity is often referred to as view-botting. Another, when done in a coordinated manner, is sometimes identified as “Follow 4 Follow” (F4F), “Lurk 4 Lurk” (L4L), or Host 4 Host (H4H), which involve a mutual exchange of interaction intended to increase visibility of both channels over those with legitimate interaction. Using services that promise higher visibility in exchange for lurking in a large number of channels or viewing streams on pages with several unrelated, active embedded streams, is considered a form of fake engagement and is not permitted on Twitch services.

What is view-botting?

View-botting is the practice of artificially inflating a live view count, using illegitimate scripts or tools to make the channel appear to have more concurrent viewers than it actually does. It is important to not confuse this with a legitimate rise in concurrent viewership, such as being hosted, the channel being embedded elsewhere, or some other promotional source.

View-botting may also be accompanied by chat activity bots, which attempt to imitate streamer/viewer interaction.

What is follow-botting?

Follow-botting is when a channel is followed by a number of fake accounts. These accounts are usually controlled by a computer or script, and will attempt to look as ‘real’ as possible while following the target account en masse. These fake accounts are generally made and detected in batches, meaning that if you have been the victim of follow-botting, you may notice a sudden dip in followers from time to time as the batches are removed.

Why is botting bad?

Artificial engagement and botting limit growth opportunities for legitimate broadcasters and are damaging to the community as a whole. False viewer growth is not conducive to establishing a career in broadcasting because the ‘viewers’ do not contribute to a healthy, highly engaged community.

As a reminder, fake engagement and artificial inflation of channel statistics are violations of our policies. Participating in, organizing, and/or running these services will lead to an enforcement issued on your account, including and up to indefinite suspension.

How to deal with fake engagement

Twitch will not punish a user for the actions of another. If you are not responsible for botting, Twitch will not take action against you.

If you believe you are being targeted, we recommend following the steps below.

  • Report: You may report any user(s) claiming to be responsible or offering botting services to you by filing a user report. For more information on how to file a user report, see this help article.
  • Don’t Panic: While being botted may be stressful and a distraction, try not to panic and carry on as you would otherwise.
  • Stay Civil: Botting can bring a lot of attention and you may be asked about your viewership. Feel free to calmly explain the situation or ignore such questions altogether.

Educate your mods and regular viewers on how to handle viewer reactions to your channel being botted and how to handle them on a case by case basis, answering the questions about view-bots in the same manner as described above. You are the broadcaster and you set the tone, but your community pillars can help you along the way.

How to deal with someone else being botted

It is very important to remember that just because a channel is having its view count artificially inflated, it does not necessarily mean the channel owner is behind it. The most important thing in reporting a channel for view-botting is having evidence. While screenshots and sounds or video recordings hosted on 3rd party websites can be (and have been) faked and are not used as conclusive evidence, it is still good to attach it to your report in addition to any evidence that is hosted on Twitch (i.e. Clips, VODs), as it helps in the moderation process.

How to Manage Harassment in Chat

Harassment comes in many forms and can be taxing to deal with. Fortunately, Twitch provides you with a number of tools to make dealing with this easier. This article covers all of the different methods at your disposal to deal with harassment.

Overview

Harassment can be frustrating, demoralizing, or scary. It’s also against the rules, and we’re here to help. Anytime you feel someone is breaking Twitch’s Terms of Service or Community Guidelines, you can report them (see File a User Report below). Our Safety Ops specialists are on duty 24/7, and review every report.

You also have options you can use immediately. When you are being harassed, there is no one right answer or best approach, only the one that works for you and your situation. Many choose to deny the harasser any attention and quickly timeout or ban them, while others choose to handle it differently. If your go-to approach is not effective for a given harasser, you may experiment with another one. Ultimately, your reaction is up to you.

The most important thing to remember is that you are in control. You have the power to take any of the actions described in this article, and to appoint moderators and empower them to take action; the right combination is whatever makes you feel safe and positive.

If you are a streamer, you may want to find a trusted person to give moderator status if you haven’t already. Your moderators can help manage your chat, leaving you to focus on your broadcast!

Use The Ignore Feature

What if you are being harassed in somebody else’s channel where you are not the moderator, or through Whispers? With a click of a button or a single chat command, any user can be ignored, which means that their messages will no longer appear on your screen. You can use this command in any chat room on Twitch, and can ignore any user. The feature ties chat and whispers, meaning that if you ignore somebody through one of them, they are ignored in both.

To use this feature in chat, click the ignore button on their user card that appears when you click their username, or type:

/ignore username

To unignore someone, click on the unignore button which replaces the ignore button, or type:

/unignore username

To use this feature in a whisper, click on the Cog icon at the top of the whisper window, and then on Block username.

There is one condition when you will still see messages from users that you have ignored. If you are a moderator of a channel, you must see all messages sent in that channel, including from ignored users, so you can perform your duties effectively. You will still not receive whispers from those ignored users, and will not see their messages in channels in which you are not a mod.

Block Other Users on Twitch

You can prevent harassment on Twitch by blocking other users. To block a user, click on their username and then the 3 Vertical Dots menu. Select Block Username.

You can see a list of who you’ve blocked, unblock or remove blocked users in the Privacy section of your Security Settings page.

Blocking Users

By blocking another user on Twitch you:

  • Remove them from your followers.
  • Prevent them from following you in the future.
  • Prevent them from whispering you.
  • Prevent them from watching your livestreams.
  • Prevent them from seeing your channel in recommendations across Twitch.
  • Prevent them from subscribing to your channel.
  • Prevent them from purchasing gift subs for other users in your channel.
  • Filter their messages out of the chats you don’t moderate.
  • Prevent them from commenting on your clips and hide their existing comments. (Learn more)

You can always see which users you currently have blocked by going to the Privacy section of your Security Settings page.

Blocking Strangers

A “stranger” is anyone who does not have a relationship with you or with Twitch: you have not followed them; they are not an editor or mod in your channel; you have not whispered them previously; and they are not a partner, Twitch staff member, or Safety Ops specialist.

The Block Whispers from Strangers setting will prevent strangers from initiating Whisper conversations with you, and is effective in preventing spam messages as well as any harassing messages. The setting will be enabled by default and you can manage it from your Security & Privacy Settings.

Turn on Chat Filters

Hide unwanted messages in any chat across Twitch with Chat Filters, your personal AutoMod. You can set your global chat filters preferences directly from your Chat settings on any channel. There are settings for Discrimination, Sexually Explicit Language, Hostility, and Profanity.

File a User Report

Twitch is committed to fighting harassment along with you. If you believe a user is breaking Twitch’s Terms of Service or Community Guidelines, you can file a user report. For example, if a harassing user is continually creating new accounts, please report them. By reporting an account, you directly notify our moderation team that somebody is breaking the Terms of Service and Community Guidelines of Twitch, which lets them react swiftly and take appropriate action.

For more information on how to file a report, see How To File a User Report. If someone is violating the Terms of Service or Community Guidelines via whispers and you wish to report them, see How to File a Whisper Report.

For reports about users repeatedly harassing or evading chat bans, use the Harassment or Chat Ban Evasion categories respectively. In the description, note any details such as other usernames you suspect them of using, which channel it happened in, and at what time. Do the same for any new account used by the person to harass you.

Always be sure to provide as much information as possible and never abuse the reporting tool. Doing so is a violation of the Terms of Service. Be aware that some conduct may not violate Twitch’s Terms of Service or Community Guidelines, and thus may not lead to the suspension of the reported account. To ensure you are protected, we suggest that you use the other tools and methods described in this article in addition to reporting.

GIF messages sent via the GIF keyboard can be reported like any other chat message through the standard reporting process. Streamers and moderators can also delete individual GIF messages and take moderation action against the sender.

Appoint Moderators

Moderators pay attention to your chat, so you can pay attention to your stream. Mods have the power to use most of the tools described in this article — responding to messages caught by AutoMod, setting chat modes, and timing out or banning users — and can help make sure your chat follows your rules. A good mod does more than timeout and ban: they interact with chat, welcome new people, cheer you on, and set a good example for everyone else to follow. If that sounds like a member of your community, it’s never too early to ask them to be your mod.

To appoint them, click the mod icon (the lightning bolt icon) on their user card that appears when you click their username, or type in chat:

/mod username

To remove them as a mod, click the unmod button that replaces the mod button, or type in chat:

/unmod username

To learn more about building a team of moderators, check out our Guide to Building a Moderation Team.

Require Users to Agree to Chat Rules

Under your Moderation Settings in the Creator Dashboard you can write your chat rules. This will show your chat rules as a pop-up to first-time viewers and require them to click Agree before they can type in the chat, ensuring that new viewers are aware of your rules and are more likely not to violate them.

Be sure to type one rule per line so the rules show up formatted correctly to your viewers.

Prevent Banned Users from Viewing Your Livestreams

If you’re the channel owner, you can prevent banned users from watching your livestreams. You can find this feature in your Moderation Settings, and opt in by toggling the Stop banned users from viewing stream setting on.

Banned users can still watch livestreams from an incognito window or while logged out, and will still be able to access VODs, highlights, and clips.

Stop Raids for 1 Hour

You can temporarily deny all incoming raids for up to an hour. To do so, you will need to add the Stop Raids for 1 Hour Quick Action to your Stream Manager and enable raids in your raids settings. Use this Quick Action at any time during your stream to disable all incoming raids. To re-enable raids, either let the timer run to 0 or use the Quick Action to accept raids before the hour is over. Learn more about How to Manage Raids.

Manage Incoming Raid Settings

Manage who can raid your channel with viewer count, account age, and other customizable settings. Click here to manage your raid settings, or learn more about managing incoming raids.

Consider a Moderation Bot

In addition to AutoMod, many channels use bots developed by Twitch community members for additional moderation. They look like any other user in chat, but are typically moderators and often (but not always) have “Bot” in their username. These bots can reduce nuisance messages such as excessive uses of Twitch emotes or symbols, repetitive messages, ALL CAPS, and other annoyances. A variety of bots are available with many different features: from moderation, to scheduled chat messages, to loyalty points and games, and more. Talk to others on Twitch to find a bot or bots that are right for you.

These bots are developed by third parties and are not affiliated with Twitch.

Send a Chat Warning

Next are the other tools specifically designed to help in a harassment situation, and are available to all streamers and their moderators.

We often hear from streamers and mods that they use an informal three-strike system when managing poor behavior from chatters in their communities - first a warning, then a timeout, and then a ban. You can use the Chat Warnings feature to anonymously send warnings to chatters, which specify the specific chat rules they have broken or display a customizable reason that you enter. Chatters who receive a warning will need to acknowledge the warning before they will be able to chat again. This is a useful tool to manage minor or first-time offenses.

To send a Chat Warning, you can click on a user’s viewer card and click the “Warn” button. You can also use the chat command /warn USERNAME, or send a warning via the mod action buttons on chat messages if you have them enabled.

Timeout a User

The timeout feature is your bread and butter for dealing with harassment. This feature will prevent the harasser from sending messages to your channel for 10 minutes by default, which means they are forced to take a moment to cool off while they wait for this timeout to expire, or they will simply leave due to impatience.

The timeout feature can be used by clicking the clock symbol either directly in chat or on the user badge which appears when clicking on a username, or by typing in chat:

/timeout username seconds

The seconds amount can be any number, so feel free to create your own length of time a timeout should last for if you wish for something other than 10 minute intervals. If you accidentally timeout somebody, all you need to do is to type in chat:

/timeout username 1

This will overwrite the old timeout with a new one lasting only 1 second, immediately allowing them to chat once again.

Ban a User

If a user does not stop their harassment after being timed out, you can implement a ban. This works as an indefinite timeout, and will prevent the user from chatting in your channel for as long as they are banned.

The Ban feature can be used by clicking the ban user button directly in chat, or on the user badge which appears when clicking on a username. You can also use this feature by typing in your chat:

/ban username

You can see a list of any banned users in your Moderation Settings, and hovering over the name will display which moderator issued the ban. If you then wish to unban them, all you need to do is either click the unban user button which replaces the ban user button, or by typing:

/unban username

Enable Follower-Only Mode

Activating Followers-Only Chat allows you or your mods to restrict chat to all or some of your followers, based on how long they have followed - from 0 minutes (all followers) to 3 months. If you are the recipient of an unwanted raid, or if someone is creating new accounts to evade your chat ban, turn on 10-minute or 30-minute Followers-Only Chat to stop the unwanted visitors from chatting (and please report any harassing conduct). Use longer durations, like 1-month or 3-month Followers-Only Chat, to reward longtime community members.

Turn it on from the chat settings menu by clicking the Cogwheel icon. You can turn on the chat mode and select the minimum time a viewer must follow in order to chat. You can also use the /followers chat command to set it. A public notification will show in chat when this feature is enabled or disabled so that the viewers are informed of the change.

Here are a few example commands, which can be any length of time, up to 3 months:

/followers 30m or /followers 30 minutes

/followers 1h or /followers 1 hours

/followers 2d or /followers 2 days

/followers 1w or /followers 1 week

/followers 3mo or /followers 3 months

To disable followers only mode, use the Cogwheel icon or type in chat:

/followersoff

Customize AutoMod

AutoMod uses machine learning and natural language processing algorithms to hold risky messages from chat so they can be reviewed by a channel moderator before appearing to other viewers in the chat. Moderators can approve or deny any message caught by AutoMod. With AutoMod, broadcasters can establish their own reliable baseline for acceptable language and around-the-clock chat moderation, a way to create a more positive experience for themselves and their communities. Read more about how to configure AutoMod here or customize it via the Moderation Settings page.

Set a Non-Moderator Chat Delay

Under the Moderation Settings page, there is an option to set a non-moderator chat delay which, if enabled, prevents all chat messages from appearing for 2, 4, or 6 seconds. Any message that is timed out or banned will completely remove the message, even from third-party chat features. Therefore swift-acting moderators can stop harassing messages from even appearing to anyone other than other moderators and the channel owner.

Require Chatters to be Email or Phone-Verified

There are options to require all chatters in your chatroom to be email verified or phone verified on Twitch. This means that anyone that would like to send messages to your chat room must first verify their email address or phone number. Enabling this can help to lower the likelihood that someone creates a “throwaway” account just to harass you or your viewers.

Require Followers to be Email or Phone-Verified

There are also options to require all or some users to be email verified or phone verified on Twitch before they can follow you. This means that anyone that would like to follow your channel must first verify their email address or phone number. Enabling this can help to lower the likelihood that someone attacks you using harassing usernames, and also make it more difficult for followbots to target your channel.

Add blocked Terms and Phrases

Add blocked terms and phrases via the Moderation Settings page. To use this feature, type the word you wish to have blocked from your channel, choose whether to mark it as Public (so that your mods can view it) or Private, and click the “Add” button. You may add terms containing multiple words, and messages that contain all words in the term will be blocked, without blocking messages that contain only one word in the term (e.g. adding “hi there” as a term will not block messages containing only “hi” or “there”, but it will block “hi there”, and “there hi”). The number of terms you can filter is in the tens of thousands, so you do not need to worry about reaching the cap.

Messages containing channel-blocked terms will not be posted to your chat.

This filter also has wildcard functionality, so all variations are effectively banned from the chat. This means you do not need to input every variable of a word you wish to remove, just the core of the word and the ban filter will censor all variations of that word. Just add wildcard, “”, at the start or end of a word and it will match any characters there. For example, adding the word ”shoot” would also filter “shooting”, “shoots” and other variations.

It is recommended that aside from any words you find offensive or wish to protect your viewers from, that you add any words which might be rare and tied to your personal information. However, while adding such words to your filter is a good way to hide sensitive personal information, it can also confirm whether or not that information belongs to you which is why it is best to only filter out words that are not commonly used (for example, do not add your house number to the filter, but perhaps add your street name or last name). Another good strategy to protect your personal information is to add several false-positives so no one can try to figure out your information through trial by error.

There is also a globally banned words filter which is enabled by default. These are words that Twitch has removed because they are the most commonly banned.

Manage Links in Chat

Clicking the Block Hyperlinks toggle on the Moderation Settings page will send messages containing links to the AutoMod queue for moderator review, instead of appearing directly in chat. The message sender will see a “Your message is being reviewed” notification. Moderators will see the held message in the AutoMod Queue with a reason indicating a hyperlink was detected. Links posted by you, your moderators, admins, or VIPs will always pass through without being held for review.

You can also add specific URLs or domains to your Blocked or Permitted Terms for more granular control. When you enter a term that looks like a link, you’ll be asked whether to block or permit the exact URL or any URL from that domain.

Enable Uniquechat Mode

Uniquechat is designed to block repeated messages. This is a great tool to use if multiple users repeatedly send the exact same message in chat.

Uniquechat can be turned on by typing:

/uniquechat

and turned off by typing

/uniquechatoff

Enable Slow Mode

The feature is turned on or updated by typing:

/slow

or turned off completely by typing

/slowoff

When enabled, it blocks users from sending messages within 120 seconds of each other by default. You can also edit the slow mode duration to be longer or shorter than 120 seconds by adding an amount at the end of the command, like this:

/slow number

A public notification will show in chat when this feature is enabled or disabled so that the viewers are informed of the change.

Partnered streamers can also enable an option via their Partnership tab on their dashboard to allow their subscribers freedom from slow mode.

Enable Sub-Only Mode

The sub-only mode should only be used in special circumstances, as it only allows users subscribed to your channel and moderators to chat, preventing all other messages. If you are not a Twitch Partner or Affiliate, this means that only your moderators will be able to talk. Nonetheless, it is a powerful feature that may be useful in critical situations such as unwanted raids. A public notification will show in chat when this feature is enabled or disabled so that the viewers are informed of the change.

Enable Emote-Only Mode

This command allows you to set your chat so only messages that are 100% emotes are allowed. This is an effective mode to remove messages that could be harassing but still allows viewers to participate in chat, just with emotes only.

When Emote-Only Mode is active, GIF messages via the GIF keyboard are also prevented.

This mode can be turned on by typing:

/emoteonly

and turned off by typing:

/emoteonlyoff

A public notification will show in chat when this feature is enabled or disabled so that the viewers are informed of the change.

Clear the Chat

If something harassing has been said in chat by several people in a short span of time, the fastest way to remove all comments is to clear the chat.

This command will allow the streamer and moderators to completely wipe the chat history that can be visible by scrolling up (up to 200 lines). To use this command, type:

/clear

However, please note that users with IRC or browser add-ons may not see the chat get wiped due to history saving features and logging.

Viewer Card Mod Logs

On your channel, or on channels you moderate, you’ll see channel-specific details about each user in chat that will help you make more informed moderation decisions without leaving Twitch.

Viewer cards display chat messages from the past 3.5 years. While older messages aren’t visible, moderator actions and comments from any time period are preserved to maintain moderation context.

How Does it Work?

You can click a username in chat or use the /user chat command to open a person’s profile card. From there, you’ll be able to:

Description

See when they made their account:

You’ll know at a glance if someone has been around for a while or if they’re using a brand new account.

View the user’s channel-specific chat (including messages caught by AutoMod), timeout, and ban history:

When you’re on the fence about taking moderation actions, you can check whether someone generally brings a positive or not-so-positive attitude to the channel.

Share channel-specific comments about your moderation choices:

You can explain why you did or didn’t take a moderation action and collaborate with your fellow mods without leaving Twitch.

Unable to View Moderation Logs

Under rare circumstances, you might open a person’s profile card, but find that you are unable to view logs. This can happen for the following reasons:

  • The streamer may have disabled moderator access to logs. The streamer can change this setting from their dashboard.
  • The user may have disabled their account or it may have been suspended. You will see this explained in a banner over the viewer card.
  • You can still ban the user, which will prevent them from being able to chat even if their account is reinstated.
  • The user’s account may have been deleted or you may have attempted to open user details for an account that does not exist. In this case, you will not be able to take any action from the viewer card, and a banner will tell you that we could not fetch details for the user.

Activate Shield Mode

Shield Mode is a tool to customize and pre-set powerful safety settings that can be quickly activated to stop hateful messages from being spammed in your channel and instantly ban harassers. You can use this feature to protect against sudden chat abuse.

When Shield Mode is active, GIF messages via the GIF keyboard are automatically disabled.

We recommend that you customize Shield Mode’s settings prior to activation so that you’re ready to go whenever you anticipate needing stronger protection, but the settings can also be updated while Shield Mode is active. Shield Mode’s settings include channel modes (such as Followers or Sub-Only chat, as well as a new mode exclusive to Shield Mode: No First-Time Chatters), chat verification options (Phone or Email), and AutoMod levels. The settings you choose will be turned on when Shield Mode is active, and when Shield Mode is disabled, your settings will go back to how they were before Shield Mode was activated.

Shield Mode can be activated using the following chat command:

/shield

and turned off using the following chat command:

/shieldoff

There will also be a Shield Mode shortcut enabled by default on your channel page and a Quick Action that you can add to your Stream Manager. Shield Mode is also integrated into Mod View, just click on the shield icon in the top navigation menu to enter the Shield Mode layout, where you can easily activate Shield Mode.

Once Shield Mode is activated, you can add harmful terms and phrases to the “Terms and Phrases” tab in order to instantly bulk ban the chatters who use those terms. You can also keep an eye on your chat from directly within the Shield Mode modal. Once chatters are banned due to using your added terms or phrases, you can review them in the “Banned Chatters” tab to determine if you want to unban them, keep them banned, or report them to Twitch. Banned terms and phrases will reset after every Shield Mode session.

Both streamers and their moderators will have full access to activate Shield Mode and manage its settings.

Parents and Educators: For comprehensive guidance on setting up moderation tools and keeping teens safe on Twitch, see our Guide for Parents and Educators.

How to Use AutoMod

AutoMod uses machine learning and natural language processing algorithms to hold risky messages from chat so they can be reviewed by a channel moderator before appearing to other viewers in the chat. Moderators can approve or deny any message caught by AutoMod. With AutoMod, streamers can establish their own reliable baseline for acceptable language and around-the-clock chat moderation, and a way to create a more positive experience for themselves and their communities.

On this page:

  • How AutoMod Works
  • How to Configure AutoMod
  • Blocked and Permitted Terms and Phrases
  • Frequently Asked Questions

How AutoMod Works

AutoMod is a moderation tool that blocks inappropriate or harassing chat with powerful moderator control. AutoMod detects misspellings and evasive language automatically.

When a user sends a message that AutoMod flags as potentially inappropriate, the message is held and shown to moderators to Allow or Deny. If allowed, the message will be sent to chat.

Streamers can configure AutoMod by selecting one of four levels. These levels affect how aggressively AutoMod holds back messages under five categories: discrimination and slurs, sexual content, harassment, profanity, and Smart Detection. These settings can only be changed by the streamer, while the dictionary of terms each setting contains is managed by Twitch.

AutoMod does not timeout, ban, or mute users from any channel; it merely withholds comments that fall within the streamer’s chosen moderation settings to be either approved or denied by the streamer’s moderators.

Users with messages held by AutoMod will receive a notification that their message is being held for review, as well as a notification if the message was approved or denied. If approved, the message will instantly appear in chat as the next message.

Streamer and their moderators will also still see all the same timeout and ban options on those messages, so even if the message was denied, they will still have the ability to timeout or ban the user.

How to Configure AutoMod

We recommend you discuss with or inform your moderator team what settings you have used and perhaps which words or phrases you care most about filtering, in order to ensure they adhere to your preferences when they are prompted by AutoMod to review chat messages for approval or denial.

Configuring AutoMod
  • Go to your Creator Dashboard and click Moderation, then Settings (Moderation).
  • Under AutoMod & Message Filtering, you can adjust your AutoMod settings.
  • On this page, click Turn On AutoMod. You will be defaulted to Level 1, the lowest active setting. Drag the slider bar to choose the setting most appropriate for you, from Level 0 (no filtering) to Level 4 (the strongest setting). To tailor AutoMod to your own custom settings, you can use the drop down menus to update each moderation category individually.

You can see how strictly AutoMod will filter based on how many shields are displayed in each moderation category, from zero (no moderation) to four (a lot of moderation).

If you haven’t turned on AutoMod manually, AutoMod will also be enabled automatically when you receive your first chat message in your channel. AutoMod will be enabled at Level 1 if you have at least one mod assigned in your channel, and at Level 2 if you have no mods assigned in your channel.

AutoMod Moderation Categories

Category

Description

Discrimination and Slurs

Includes race, religion, gender-based discrimination. Hate speech falls under this category.

Sexual Content

Words or phrases referring to sexual acts and/or anatomy.

Harassment

Provocation and bullying, sexual harassment.

Profanity

Expletives, curse words, and vulgarity. This filter especially helps those who wish to keep their community family-friendly.

Smart Detection

Detects unwanted messages (including spam) based on mod actions taken in your channel.

What AutoMod catches at each level

Level

Description

Level 0

No filtering.

Words and terms you have added to your channel’s blocked terms will still be blocked even if AutoMod is turned off. This can prevent messages from being sent.

Level 1

Some filtering on discrimination, and Smart Detection only.

Level 2

Some filtering on discrimination, sexual content, and Smart Detection, more filtering on harassment.

Level 3

More filtering on discrimination, sexual content, harassment, and Smart Detection.

Level 4

More filtering on discrimination, sexual content, profanity and Smart Detection, and most filtering on harassment.

Hate speech, bullying, and sexually explicit content are not allowed under Twitch’s Community Guidelines. If you see it, please report it.

AutoMod and Channel Moderators

Channel moderators can also access and update AutoMod settings by opening the Chat Settings in the channel via the settings cog on the bottom right hand corner. From there, select Manage Moderation Settings. This will open the moderation preferences page for the channel, where they can update the AutoMod level, create a custom level, and update terms in the blocked and permitted terms list.

Blocked and Permitted Terms and Phrases

In addition to AutoMod’s machine learning and language processing, you can manually list terms to block or permit in your chat. To do so, click Blocked terms and phrases or Permitted terms and phrases under AutoMod & Message Filtering. Blocked and Permitted terms can also be added via Mod View under the Channel Actions menu.

When you enter a term that looks like a link, you’ll be asked whether to block or permit the exact URL or any URL from that domain. Blocked links will be sent to the AutoMod queue for moderator review regardless of your Block Hyperlinks toggle setting. Permitted links will always pass through without being held, even when Block Hyperlinks is enabled.

Blocked Terms

Blocked terms are words or phrases that you wish to completely filter out from your channel. This can be useful for protecting your personal information, reducing toxicity, or protecting against spambots.

Adding Blocked Terms Manually

When adding a word or phrase to your blocked items, you can choose to set it to Public or Private. Setting a term to Private will prevent it from being viewable to your channel’s moderators. Once you have added a term, you can click the Edit icon to edit it, or the Delete icon to remove it from your blocked terms list.

When you add a term consisting of multiple words to your block list, messages that contain all of the words in that term will be blocked without blocking messages that contain only one word in the term. For example, adding “hi there” as a term will not block messages containing only “hi” or “there” but will block messages containing “hi there”. The number of terms you can filter is in the tens of thousands, so you do not need to worry about reaching the cap.

You can add global and sub emotes to your blocked terms. To block an emote from your channel, add the exact emote name to your blocked terms. For example, adding “Kappa” to your blocked terms would prevent the Kappa emote from being posted in your chat.

When adding blocked terms, you can also use wildcards by adding a “” to your term. For example, adding ”hate” to your blocked terms will also cause “haters” and “hateful” to be blocked. You can also use this feature to filter any variant of a url. For example, “someurl.com*” would filter someurl.com, someurl.com, someurl.com, etc. This can protect your chat from variations of links that are unwelcome.

In the “Occurrences” column, you can see the number of times that each term has successfully blocked a chat message from appearing in your channel. Only occurrences after 5/25/2024 will be counted.

Adding Blocked Terms from the AutoMod Queue

When you deny a word or phrase held by AutoMod in the AutoMod Queue within Mod View, you’ll have the option to add that term to your Blocked Terms list. This gives you full control over which terms are blocked on your channel by ensuring that terms are only added when you explicitly choose to add them.

You do not need to have AutoMod filtering enabled to add or enforce blocked terms on your channel.

Messages Containing Blocked Terms

When chatters attempt to send messages that contain your channel’s public blocked terms, those messages will be held from chat and will be surfaced via AutoMod for you and your moderators to allow or deny. If you deny a message, you will also see an option to warn, timeout, ban, or report the user sending the message. These messages will also be stored in users’ chat logs which you can access through their viewer cards.

If chatters attempt to send messages that contain your channel’s private blocked terms, those messages will be held from chat as well, but will only be surfaced to the channel owner for their visibility. Moderators will not see when a message was attempted using a private blocked term.

When you allow messages containing blocked terms from the AutoMod Queue in Mod View, you will see an option to remove blocked terms that you no longer want.

Permitted Terms

Permitted terms are used to set exceptions for specific words or phrases and bypass AutoMod’s filters. Adding terms or phrases to your permitted terms will prevent AutoMod from catching messages containing those terms (provided those messages do not contain other terms caught by AutoMod or your Blocked Terms). For example, if AutoMod catches an innocuous phrase as a false positive, you can add this phrase to your permitted terms so that it is not caught again. When you allow a word or phrase held by AutoMod in the AutoMod Queue within Mod View, you’ll have the option to add the flagged term to your Permitted Terms list, giving you control over which exceptions are made for your channel.

Permitted terms do not support wildcards.

Frequently Asked Questions

What languages is AutoMod available in?
AutoMod is generally available in: English, German, Spanish, (Spain) Spanish (Mexico), French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese (Portugal), Portuguese (Brazil), Russian, Slovak, Turkish, Chinese (Simplified) and Chinese (Traditional).

The exceptions are the Sexual Harassment category (which is currently available in English only) and the Smart Detection category, which is available in Arabic, Chinese (Simplified), Chinese (Traditional), Dutch, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese (Portugal), Portuguese (Brazil), Russian, Spanish (Spain), Spanish (Mexico), and Turkish.

How will AutoMod operate as new meanings and slang words grow on the internet so frequently?
Twitch will be regularly reviewing how moderators use AutoMod to maintain its effectiveness on a site-wide and per channel basis. The feedback from your moderators approving and denying messages, as well as removing other messages not caught by AutoMod, will help to grow our understanding of how language used on Twitch evolves. Our goal is for a streamer’s chosen AutoMod setting to reflect how they want to run their chat.
Can my moderators update AutoMod?
Yes, moderators can update your AutoMod level, create a custom level by fine-tuning each moderation category, and update terms in your blocked and permitted terms lists. To access AutoMod settings in the Creator Dashboard, mods can click Manage Moderation Settings in the Chat Settings menu.
What if I want to customize my AutoMod settings even further, like with an allowlist or blocklist for words the settings I have chosen do not include?
We support blocked and permitted terms. Each term can be more than one word, and AutoMod will also try to fix misspellings or evasive language when checking a message. For more information about blocked and permitted terms, please see our Blocked and Permitted Terms section.
Can moderators see all my blocked terms?
By default, moderators can see blocked terms in your channel. If you’d like to keep a blocked term private, set that term to Private when blocking the term or by editing the term using the Edit icon on its entry in the Active Terms list.
What other tools and options are there to ensure a quality chat experience for viewers?
For an overview on the tools available and the best ways to set up moderation for your channel, please see our help article.

Mod View

Mod View is a customizable channel view that includes everything you need to moderate channels on Twitch. Featuring movable and resizable widgets, Mod View can be tailored precisely to your needs so that you can moderate without losing sight of the stream or chat.

To access Mod View, click the Sword icon at the bottom of the chat for any channel you moderate for. You can also navigate to twitch.tv in order to view a list of any live channels you mod for, or append the relevant channel name after the twitch.tv URL to go to that channel’s Mod View directly. A mobile version of Mod View can also be accessed within the iOS and Android Twitch apps.

Customizing Mod View

Mod View on desktop consists of 4 sections:

  • A central grid for high-priority tasks.
  • A left side dock that displays relevant stats, and houses other, less-frequented tasks.
  • A panel for viewer details and quick actions.
  • A top navigation bar for insights, stats, and switching layout states.

When you first access Mod View, you’ll be shown a tutorial that walks you through the basics of how to use Mod View and how the different parts work. To view this tutorial again at any time, click the Moderator Help & Feedback icon in the top right corner and then click Rewatch Tutorial.

For Mod View in the iOS and Android apps, you can customize the order in which widgets are displayed or choose to hide widgets from the dock.

Shield Mode Integration

Shield Mode is fully integrated within Mod View, and you can switch into the Shield Mode layout by clicking the shield button in the top nav. Once you are in the Shield Mode layout, you can manage your settings and be ready to activate Shield Mode with a single click, while continuing to have visibility over the stream, chat, and mod actions. Widgets that are not shown in the Shield Mode layout will be accessible from the left-side dock. To return to the regular Mod View layout, just click the shield button again.

Moving Widgets

Widgets within mod view can be moved around to your liking by clicking and dragging the top of the desired widget. The purple outline represents where and how the widget will be placed when it is released based on your current cursor position. To adjust the sizes of widgets in relation to each other, click and drag the space between widgets.

Adding and Removing Widgets

To remove or add widgets, click the Add/Remove Widgets button in the left side dock. Click the Close icon on any panel in the central grid or left side dock to remove it from Mod View.

When in Add/Remove Widgets mode, the panel on the right hand side will store any unused widgets. Click and drag them back into the central grid or the left side dock to use them again. When you’re finished, click Save.

Your personal Mod View layout is stored locally in your browser. You’ll need to reconfigure Mod View when using different browsers, but all channels you mod for using the same browser will keep your custom layout.

Desktop Mod View Widgets

Mod View on desktop includes a number of widgets, many of which you can add or remove as you like.

Widget

Description

Other Channels You Mod For

This widget is located in the top nav and tracks other channels you also mod for, outside of the channel whose Mod View you’re currently viewing.

Channels You Follow

This widget is located in the top nav and displays channels that you follow, as well as their live status.

Mod Actions

This widget tracks actions taken by moderators such as timing out users, deleting messages, and changing chat modes. Raids are also shown here. To filter out actions from being shown here, click the Filter button next to the 3 Vertical Dots menu in the top right-hand corner of the panel and click the checkbox next to the relevant alert.

AutoMod Queue

If the channel has AutoMod enabled, any messages held by AutoMod for review will appear here. Click the 3 Vertical Dots menu in the top right-hand corner for options to clear the widget of messages, review Blocked/Permitted terms, and access AutoMod’s settings.

Predictions

Located in the left-hand dock, this widget allows you to create new predictions or manage prior ones. Clicking the 3 Vertical Dots will pop-out the tool, or move it to the grid with your other widgets.

Suspicious User Activity

Located in the left-hand dock, this widget allows you to manage shared ban information between channels. Monitor or Restrict users, manage filters, or manage the display modes of the widget via the 3 Vertical Dots menu.

Chat

The chat panel shows the channel’s chat, which functions as it does on the main channel page. Clicking the 3 Vertical Dots menu will bring up your chat settings. Clicking any username in chat will bring up their information in the Community panel on the right.

Chat message logs in viewer cards display messages from the past 3.5 years. Moderator actions and mod comments are retained indefinitely.

Community

Located on the far right of Mod View, this section shows all users currently connected to the chat. Clicking on a username from this list or in the Chat widget will bring up a summary of information of that user. This summary includes:

  • Subscription time / tier (if relevant)
  • Account creation date
  • A lot of that user’s messages in the channel
  • Any mod actions (timeouts, bans) taken against this user
  • Comments left by moderators
  • Whether a user is marked as suspicious by that channel’s mods, whether they are a suspected ban evader, or whether they are banned in a channel you share ban info with.

Below the chat log is a list of moderation actions that can be taken upon the user. When you’ve finished reviewing a user, click the Close icon in the top right-hand corner to return to the user list.

Unban Requests

Unban requests from banned chatters are listed in this widget. Unban Requests can be sorted using the drop-down menu on the right-hand side. If you choose to deny an unban request, that user will not be able to submit another request. To ignore this feature or continue using a 3rd party unban solution, click the Close icon when in Add/Remove Widget mode to remove the widget.

Active Mods

This widget shows any mods currently connected to the chat.

Activity Feed

This widget shows all activity for the channel; follows, subs, bits, raids, etc. To filter out what is shown here, click the Filter button next to the 3 Vertical Dots menu and select the relevant categories.

Whispers

This widget shows your received whispers/conversations.

Reward Requests Queue

This widget shows a list of outstanding Channel Point Reward requests. For more information about Channel Points and rewards, please see our Channel Points article.

Batch Reporting Tool

This widget shows a list of recently banned or timed out users so that streamers and mods can easily submit reports to Twitch in bulk at a time that makes sense for them, such as during a lull in the stream or after the stream has ended. Users will be shown in the Batch Reporting Tool for 8 hours after being banned or timed out.

Mobile Mod View Widgets

A mobile version of Mod View can be accessed within the iOS and Android Twitch apps, and currently includes the following widgets. You can enter Mod View through the callout that you will see whenever you visit a channel where you have the moderator role, or via the channel’s chat settings.

Chat

The chat panel shows the channel’s chat, which functions as it does on the main channel page. Clicking the 3 Vertical Dots menu will bring up your chat settings. Clicking any username in chat will open up their viewer card in a modal.

Chat message logs in viewer cards display messages from the past 3.5 years. Moderator actions and mod comments are retained indefinitely.

Quick Actions

Perform different actions (e.g. clip the stream, activate Shield Mode, start a poll) at the click of a button.

Activity Feed

This widget shows all activity for the channel; follows, subs, bits, raids, etc. To filter out what is shown, click the 3 Vertical Dots menu and select the relevant categories.

AutoMod Queue

Mod Actions

To filter out actions from being shown here, click the 3 Vertical Dots menu in the top right-hand corner of the widget and click the checkbox next to the relevant alert.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I access Mod View?
To access Mod View on desktop, click the Sword icon in the bottom right-hand corner of the chat panel in any channel you moderate. Alternatively, you can append the name of the channel you want to moderate to twitch.tv providing you have moderator permissions in that channel. A mobile version of Mod View can also be accessed within the iOS and Android Twitch apps.
Who can use Mod View?
Streamers, their moderators, and lead moderators can use Mod View to moderate a channel.
Can I continue to moderate from chat if I don’t want to use Mod View?
Yes! Moderator actions are still available to use within a channel’s chat.
Can I continue to use my 3rd party solution for moderation?
Yes.
Will I be able to chat with other moderators in Mod View?
Not at this time.
Can I use Mod View for multiple channels?
Mod View can only show one channel at a time. To switch between the channels you moderate on desktop, click the Sword icon in the top right corner to access the Other Channels You Mod For menu and select the desired channel. For Mod View in the iOS and Android Twitch apps, in order to switch views you will need to navigate to the other channel and then enter Mod View from there.

Setting Up Moderation for Your Twitch Channel

Content on this page is relevant to any streamer or moderator.

Good moderation is key to successfully managing your Twitch community and maintaining compliance with the Twitch Community Guidelines. It’s also a critical element to preserving a safe chat experience during busy events. This article provides an overview of the various tools and options available to help you efficiently and effectively moderate your channel, as well as recommendations on moderation best practices.

On this page:

  • Moderation Preferences
  • Chat Commands
  • Managing Channel Mods
  • Privacy Settings

Moderation Preferences

Features described in this section may not be available to everyone yet. Stay tuned!

To access these moderation settings, navigate to your Creator Dashboard, click Moderation, and then Settings (Moderation).

Chatter Permissions

In the Chatter Permissions section, you can manage settings that determine how and when your community participates in chat.

  • Email & Phone Verification to Chat: Set up Email & Phone Verification on your channel to prevent users without a verified email or phone number from posting in your chat. This is strongly recommended to reduce spam and harassment.
  • Followers-only & Subscribers-only Mode: These two options allow you to limit who can talk in your chat based on whether or not they are following or subscribed to your channel. For followers-only mode, use the dropdown menu to set the amount of time an account needs to be following your channel before they can speak in chat.
  • Channel moderators are immune to both of these modes.
  • Non-Mod Chat Delay: A short delay can be added to chat messages appearing in your channel. This gives chat moderators and bots a chance to remove them before viewers can see the message. A good setting for allowing moderation without a noticeable impact on the viewer experience is 2 seconds.
  • Block Hyperlinks: Enabling this setting will send messages containing links to the AutoMod queue for moderator review, instead of appearing directly in chat. The message sender will see a “Your message is being reviewed” notification. Moderators will see the held message with a reason indicating a hyperlink was detected. The channel owner, moderators, and VIPs are exempt — their links always pass through. If you’d like to allow specific URLs to bypass the queue while this setting is enabled, you can add them to your permitted terms. It is recommended that you use some form of link management in your channel, be it via this setting or a chat bot.
  • Chat Rules: You can create a custom set of rules for the channel to educate new viewers on what behavior is expected in your chat. First-time chatters will have to agree to the chat rules before they can start chatting.
AutoMod & Message Filtering

In the AutoMod & Message Filtering section, you can manage settings that automatically screen and hold potentially offensive or inappropriate messages from appearing in chat.

  • AutoMod: AutoMod is an automated method of catching potentially risky messages in chat so they can be reviewed by a channel moderator before appearing to others. When a user sends a message that AutoMod flags as potentially inappropriate, the message is held pending approval or denial by your moderators.
  • Blocked Terms: Add terms and phrases that you wish to have blocked from your channel. This can be useful for protecting your personal information, reducing toxicity, or protecting against spambots.
  • Permitted Terms: Permitted terms are used to set exceptions for specific words or phrases which will then bypass AutoMod’s filters. Adding terms or phrases to your permitted terms will prevent AutoMod from catching messages containing those terms (provided those messages do not contain other terms caught by AutoMod or your blocked terms).

Learn more about both AutoMod, and blocked/permitted terms in this help article.

Channel Protection

In the Channel Protection section, you can manage how others can engage with your channel in order to prevent trolls and harmful users.

  • Follower Verification: You can require all or some users to be email verified or phone verified on Twitch before they can follow you. This means that anyone that would like to follow your channel must first verify their email address or phone number. Enabling this can help to lower the likelihood that someone attacks you using harassing usernames, and also makes it more difficult for followbots to target your channel.
  • Harmful Chatter Detection: When enabled, this setting can help detect potential ban evaders or harassers and flag them for moderators to review.
  • Stop Banned Users from Viewing Stream: If you’re the channel owner, you can prevent banned users from watching your livestreams by toggling the Stop banned users from viewing stream setting on.
  • Banned Users List: This is a list of users that have been banned from chatting in your channel. Hovering over a banned user’s username will display who banned the user and when. To unban someone, type /unban in your channel’s chat, or you can also make use of the Unban Requests feature, which allows banned users to submit an unban request through the Chat column for channel owners and moderators to review and take action on, anonymously.

Moderators, visit Mod View to see unban requests for channels you moderate. Streamers may view unban requests for their own channel from the Stream Manager by searching “unban requests panel” in the Creator Dashboard, or manage their unban requests settings by visiting Moderation > Settings (Moderation) > Channel Protections.

Moderator Management

In the Moderator Management tab, you can see your current list of moderators and lead moderators, and add new ones, as well as manage the actions that moderators can take on your channel.

  • Moderator tools in chat: Enabling this option will allow your moderators to view the chat and ban history of chatters in your channel, as well as leave and view comments left on users. This allows you and your moderators to take into account any past history on a particular chatter and make informed decisions in regards to time outs, bans, or warnings.

Understanding Message Retention: Chat message logs in moderation tools show messages from the past 3.5 years. Moderator actions and mod comments are retained indefinitely to preserve moderation history.

  • Pin message: Enabling this option will allow your moderators to pin messages in chat.

Listed below are actions moderators can automatically take on your channel:

  • Send a Chat Warning
  • Timeout a User
  • Ban a User
  • Enable Follower-Only Mode
  • Customize AutoMod
  • Set a Non-Moderator Chat Delay
  • Require Chatters to be Email or Phone-Verified
  • Require Followers to be Email or Phone-Verified
  • Add blocked Terms and Phrases
  • Disable Links in Chat
  • Enable Uniquechat Mode
  • Enable Slow Mode
  • Enable Sub-Only Mode
  • Enable Emote-Only Mode
  • Clear the Chat
  • Viewer Card Mod Logs (this is not automatic but is on by default)
  • Activate Shield Mode

Moderators can also delete comments and ban users from clip comment sections. Comment moderation is managed separately from chat — see Comments on Clips for details.

Chat Commands

Additional chat settings can be set and managed in real-time via chat commands. This includes setting chat to follower or subscriber only mode, emote only mode, slow mode, and much more. Some moderation actions, such as /clear, are only available through chat commands.

For a full list of chat moderator commands and how to use them, click here.

Managing Channel Mods

Even with all of the tools above, there is still a need for a human to moderate your channel. It is impossible for a bot or an automated system to catch everything or to be 100% accurate. However, selecting the wrong channel mods can be just as detrimental to a viewer’s chat experience as not having any at all.

  • Pick someone reliable. When you make someone a moderator of your channel, you are showing your community that you trust this person.
  • Communication is key. As a channel owner you will expect a certain behavior in your chat. You and your mods should be on the same page about what type of environment you want to achieve within your community and have mods who are open to evolving their skills to your needs.
  • Moderation/chat bots. AutoMod and live human mods can do great work, but to have a fully dynamic chat experience, there are chat bots that can fill in the extra gaps. It is ideal if one or more of your moderators can operate one of these bots to keep it calibrated for your specific needs. It can catch words, symbols, caps, message length, etc. These can be necessary while dealing with a very fast chat when human moderators would have a difficult time keeping up, or to discourage malicious raids.

To mod a user and add them as a moderator, go to the channel’s page and use the command:

 /mod username

You can use /mods to see a full list of the modded users in the channel and check the viewer list to see what mods are currently in the chat. You can read more about building a moderation team here.

Privacy Settings

Block Whispers from Strangers

Checking this setting will let you block incoming whispers from users you don’t follow. This setting can be found in the Security and Privacy tab of your channel settings. We strongly recommend this is turned on when running large events.

Suspicious User Controls

Suspicious User Controls are customizable tools to enable moderators and streamers to detect, identify, monitor, and restrict chat privileges from suspicious users in their channels. Moderators can manually add users for monitoring, or rely on a Twitch-provided warning.

What is Ban Evasion Detection?

Ban Evasion Detection relies on machine learning to flag “Possible” or “Likely” channel-ban evaders who enter your chat. By default, “Likely” evaders will be put into restricted mode, and “Possible” evaders will be put into monitoring. Streamers may alter or disable these default settings while still allowing moderators the control to manually remove these flags.

Ban Evasion Detection identifies users attempting to evade channel-specific chat bans set by you or moderators. This is different from site-wide chatting suspensions issued by Twitch. Learn more About Bans, Blocking, and Suspensions.

Monitoring Ban Evaders

By default, messages sent by Possible Ban Evaders will automatically be Monitored. Messages sent by monitored accounts will appear in chat, but flagged in the chat panel and Mod View widget for moderators and streamers to review. Moderators and streamers may monitor and unmonitor individual users freely, or rely on Twitch’s default settings.

Restricting Ban Evaders

By default, messages sent by Likely Ban Evaders will automatically be restricted. Messages sent by restricted accounts will be displayed only to the streamer and their moderators, both in chat and in the Mod View widget. As with the monitoring state, moderators and streamers may restrict and unrestrict users freely.

How to Use Ban Evasion Detection

We’ve enabled these as default settings for all channels so streamers and moderators can focus on other important aspects of the stream, but you can always turn it off or update how you want to use these signals from your moderation settings page.
