To manage your Ban Evasion Detection setting, visit your Moderation settings in the Creator Dashboard.

Streamers may access Suspicious User Controls by visiting their Creator Dashboard > Moderation > Settings (Moderation) > Harmful Chatter Detection.

Moderators may access the Moderation Settings page via links in Chat Settings and in Mod View for channels they moderate.

From here, you can control the level of detection for “Likely” or “Possibly” ban-evading users. This level of detection still allows moderators and streamers to manually add or remove the flag on users who appear in your chat.

Choose the best level of protection based on the needs of your moderation team and your channel.

Manually Add Users

You can also manually add individual users that you’d like to monitor more closely from their Viewer Card, even if Twitch doesn’t detect them as ban evaders.

Manually Remove Users

When the default setting is enabled, Twitch will automatically flag users as “Likely” or “Possible” ban evaders. In the case of a false positive, moderators can remove this flag to stop monitoring the user’s messages and allow them to chat freely.

What is Shared Ban Info?

Shared Ban Info builds upon the Suspicious User Controls system and provides a simple way for you to share information about who you’ve banned in your channel with other streamers so you can collaborate to help keep serial harassers out of your communities.

Sending a share request

To get started, you can initiate a sharing request from the Shared Ban Info section of the Moderation Settings in your Creator Dashboard. Once initiated, an on-site notification will be sent to the channel you’ve requested to share ban information with. When you request another channel’s ban information you are also consenting to share yours with that channel. Once they’ve accepted your request, you’ll receive an on-site notification letting you know.

Receiving a share request

You can choose to accept share requests from anyone or limit it to specific groups: Partners, Affiliates, or mutual follows. Once both channels mutually consent to share their ban information you will have a sharing relationship.

You can currently have a maximum of 50 sharing relationships.

Sharing mod comments

The Share Mod Comments setting will be toggled on by default, and allows you to share mod comments made in your channel with the channels you are sharing ban information with. If this setting is turned on, you can still choose whether you want to share new individual mod comments when you add them, or keep them private. If the setting is turned off, any mod comments that were previously shared will be made private until the setting is turned back on.

Mod comments can help provide helpful context on why users were banned, and help prevent serial harassers from going on to harass other communities

Using shared ban information

Similar to Ban Evasion Detection, you can choose a default action for how flagged users are treated in your channel — monitoring or restricted. Unless you adjust your settings, flagged users will be restricted by default.

Once a user is flagged, you can continue monitoring/restricting them, ban them, or change them back to trusted. Flagged users’ first chat messages are clearly marked with a red border and include details on which channel they are banned from. Their messages are also queued in the Suspicious User Activity Mod View widget for additional visibility.

Once you’ve established a sharing relationship, any new channel bans will continue to be flagged as suspicious users on your respective channels. You can always manually change their status by clicking on their viewer card. And of course, if you feel that a user shouldn’t be allowed on Twitch at all because they’ve violated our Community Guidelines, be sure to report them so we can take action.

Ending a sharing relationship

If you want to end a sharing relationship, you can do it at any time. Either side can do so by going to your Shared Ban Info settings.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I turn Ban Evasion Detection off? Why is this on by default?
Yes, you can turn it off at any time from your moderation settings page. As an important safety feature, we wanted to make sure it was enabled before channels needed it.
Do I need to add people as suspicious users?
You do not need to manually add users, but you may do so if you want to keep an eye on a new chatter who sends a borderline message.

By default, Twitch will flag users to you who are “Likely” or “Possibly” evading a channel-level chat ban.

How do I remove people from being designated as suspicious users?
Users can be manually moved between monitoring and restricted or removed from suspicious user handling either on their messages in the Mod View widget or from their Viewer Card.

Message History Scope: User message history displays chat messages from the past 3.5 years. Moderator actions and comments remain available from all time periods.

Since moderators and streamers can take actions on a user, how will I know who did what?
Streamers and moderators may review Mod Actions taken against a user from that user’s Viewer Card. This information is also gathered for you in the Mod Actions widget in Mod View.
What’s the difference between “Likely” and “Possibly” suspicious users?
Our machine learning model relies on several signals to determine whether a user may be evading a ban, and while we cannot reveal the exact signals used, we have grouped its classifications into two “buckets” to assist with moderators’ decision-making. When we flag a potential ban evader as Likely, it means that that user is much more likely to be a true ban evader, and not a false positive. However, as machine learning is not perfect, streamers and moderators have the ability to monitor or restrict these flagged users, or remove the flag entirely.
What do I do if I believe I am a false positive?
Ban Evasion Detection works on a channel-by-channel basis, and only detects evasion of channel-specific chat bans (issued by streamers and moderators), so it’s very unlikely that you will be held as a false positive in more than one channel. If you are held, your best bet is just to behave well, as moderators can always override Twitch’s detection if they don’t find you suspicious. In the event that you are wrongfully banned, you can submit an Unban Request in channels that have enabled this feature.
Can Ban Evasion Detection be used on mobile?
This feature is not available on mobile devices at this time.
What if I want to share ban information with more than 50 channels?
If you would like more than 50 sharing relationships please let us know at UserVoice. We’re always open to your feedback and may be able to implement your suggestions in future updates.
If the users being flagged by Shared Ban Info could be serial harassers, why wouldn’t Twitch just suspend them altogether?
Rather than making decisions on your behalf, our goal with this tool is to provide you with the information you need to make informed and personalized decisions about who can participate in your community. We want to strike a balance between protecting streamers from harassers while still giving streamers control over who is allowed to participate in their communities. You’re the expert when it comes to your community, and you should make the final call on who can participate.

Our Hateful Conduct and Harassment Policy prohibits harassment anywhere on Twitch, so if someone is breaching this policy in your channel, please report them so that we can take action against their Twitch account. We know that sometimes, harassers may move faster than user reports can, by making new accounts or moving rapidly between different channels. We hope that together, Ban Evasion Detection and Shared Ban Info will offer more instant, proactive support while we review your reports and take more conclusive action.

What if I can’t find anyone who wants to share their ban information with me?
Stay tuned, our team will be working on future updates that make it easier to identify suspicious users and there will be more to come on this front.
Sometimes I temporarily ban users from my community as part of a shared joke. Can I exempt people from my shared ban information?
No, you cannot exempt people that are banned in your channel from your shared ban information. However, even if users have been flagged through Shared Ban Info, they can still be manually marked as trusted by the channels who you have shared ban information with.
Will Shared Ban Info help prevent hate raids against my channel?
“Hate raids” are attempts at targeted harassment against a community member. They can come in a wide variety of forms—from a batch of bot accounts created in one swoop, to a group of individuals coordinating off Twitch to act in unison.

No single tool or technology can stop “hate raids” altogether, but using a combination of tools like Phone-Verified Chat and Followers-only mode has proven extremely effective for a lot of our streamers, and we’ve made it easier to pre-set and activate a variety of safety settings using Shield Mode. We believe Shared Ban Info adds an additional layer of protection, particularly against any raids orchestrated by individuals acting in tandem. That said, we encourage you to try out this and other tools, to find the combination of settings that best meets your needs.

Partner Program

Channel Skins

Channel Skins are a feature of the Sponsorship product on Twitch. It is a clickable branded experience that surrounds the stream and is seen by all of the viewers on the channel, including Turbo and subscribers.

The channel skins are made up of 4 animated graphic elements.

  • The frame and ribbon surrounding the video player.
  • Above chat (on web)
  • Branding in your channel information
  • Follower promotion on the left navigation bar (on web)

Channel Skins are an Ad product on Twitch and we measure impressions, unique viewers, click-through rate and more, which we share with the sponsoring advertiser after the campaign. All metrics are captured automatically.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need to upload any graphics into my broadcasting software (i.e OBS, Streamlabs, Stream Elements) for a Channel Skins campaign?
You do not. The brand provides all the assets and Twitch manages the logistics for uploading and changing graphics. Everything is done on our end.
I don’t like one of the placements, can I choose not to use it?
No. Channel Skins placements are pre-set during the agreed livestream.
Can I turn Channel Skins off during my stream?
If you need to take down the ongoing channel skins you can click cancel in the Sponsorship Tool. This will reset your progress and allow you to start over.
Can I run ads during a Channel Skin campaign?
Yes! You can run video ads like you normally would during a campaign. Channel Skins will disappear while a viewer is watching a video ad and reappear when the ad has finished running.
Do I have to do anything to remove the Channel Skins assets after the campaign finishes?
No. These assets will disappear after the agreed-upon timing.

Contacting Partner Help

If you are a Twitch Partner, you have access to a priority support queue where you can ask for help regarding the Partner program, payment inquiries, subscriber-only features, and more. To contact Partner Help. please submit a ticket while logged into your Partnered account. Your ticket will be automatically routed to the Partner Help queue.

Please ensure you are logged in while submitting a ticket. If you are not logged in, your ticket may be routed to our general support inbox and this may cause a delay in processing your request.

If you are a Twitch Partner and are having issues accessing or logging in to your Partnered account, please submit a ticket on the same page and make sure to enter your Twitch ID and select Account/Login Issues as your category. Please provide as many relevant details as possible to help expedite processing.

Creator Profile Setup Guide

Let brands know what you’re looking for in a partnership with your Creator Profile.

Available to all Partners and Affiliates globally, your Creator Profile is how brands discover you for sponsorship campaigns on Twitch. It allows you to share details about your channel, your audience, and your brand sponsorship interests in one place. A completed Creator Profile increases your chances of being matched with sponsorship opportunities.

New to Creator Sponsorships? Affiliates can access Creator Sponsorships on Twitch after completing Creator Certification. To get started: accept the Portal Terms, complete Certification, and fill out your Creator Profile below. Once set up, you’ll start receiving campaign invitations when brands match with your profile.

In this guide, we’ll walk you through your Creator Profile, how it works, and how to set it up.

What Is Your Creator Profile?

Your Creator Profile is a professional showcase of your channel, interests, profile picture, and new audience demographic data. Twitch Partners and Affiliates can easily compile this information to share with brands.

Creator Profiles allow Partners and Affiliates to fill out their preferences and channel information. This information helps brands and agencies working directly with Twitch to find your channel for opportunities. When you have an opportunity to work with a sponsor, you’ll be notified and can choose to accept it directly in your sponsorships tab.

Your Creator Profile differs from your channel page, which is the front door to your stream and community for all viewers.

How to Create Your Creator Profile

To access your Creator Profile:

  • Click here.
  • Navigate to your Creator Dashboard and select Monetization > Sponsorships

The first time you visit this page, you’ll be prompted to click the sponsorship portal terms of service. Once those terms have been signed, you’ll find your Creator Profile.

Twitch Partners globally can fill out their Creator Profile.

Filling Out Your Creator Profile

The Creator Profile includes the details brands want to know about you. This feature allows you to share what information you want brands to know.

Before you dive in, please note:

  • You must read and accept the sponsorship portal terms of service.
  • You won’t be able to delete the info in your Creator Profile once you submit it (unless you delete your Twitch account). We’re adding this functionality shortly so you can edit your Creator Profile.
  • Only brands with an advertising relationship with Twitch will see your Creator Profile.
  • You will soon be able to download your Creator Profile as a shareable infographic and share that information outside of Twitch.
  • Any information shared within the Creator Profile can be shared with Twitch advertising clients.
  • Any content you submit that violates Twitch’s Terms of Service or Community Guidelines can result in removal from Twitch’s sponsorship program, including loss of access to Creator Profile.
A Tour of Your Creator Profile

Profile Picture

This picture does not replace your channel profile picture, but it can be the same if you want.

Bio

An opportunity to present yourself and your community. There is a 100 word count limit.

Brand Categories

Select what kind of brands you are interested in partnering with.

Sponsorship Highlights

Select and customize which clips appear on your Creator Profile. Sponsorship Highlights let you feature clips that showcase the type of sponsored content you can create — this helps brands understand your style and what you can deliver. You can select and update your Sponsorship Highlights in the Clips Manager at any time.

Top Categories

We automatically populate these based on your stream data for the last 365 days.

Current Sponsors

We know a lot of creators have current commitments. This is a chance for you to let us know! Share whatever you are comfortable with.

Previous Sponsors

Previous commitments showcase your experience with brands, and can catch the eye of brands looking for creators to work with. Additionally, if you have completed a creator sponsorship campaign through Twitch in the past 6 months, these will be automatically populated here.

Restricted Advertising Categories

Not all creators may wish to be associated with certain restricted advertising categories. This is the chance for you to let us know.

Community Stats

If your average daily viewers is less than 25 in the last 90 days, we won’t show your audience demographic stats.

What’s Next?

After you have filled out your Creator Profile, you will be notified when you have a campaign opportunity to review via your Creator Dashboard and email. Be sure to enable sponsorships emails in your Email Notification Settings.

  • Visit the Sponsorship Portal to browse available campaigns
  • Complete Creator Certification to become eligible for campaign invitations (required for Affiliates)
  • Go deeper with Creator Camp for in-depth guidance on maximizing sponsorship opportunities

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I get access to my Creator Profile?
Great news, if you are a Twitch Partner or Affiliate, you automatically have access to your Creator Profile. Visit your Creator Dashboard today to set it up.
Can I share my Creator Profile directly with brands I’m interested in working with? If so, how?
Yes! We encourage you to use this to help you expand your overall sponsorship opportunities. In a few weeks, it’ll be a downloadable infographic, so you can share it with any potential sponsor off of Twitch. Until then, we’ll share your profile with Twitch advertising clients, and you can print or screenshot your Creator Profile to share it with brands not in our sponsorships ecosystem. However, when utilizing this interim method, exercise good judgment regarding sharing personal details of your account.
Where exactly does the information go that I provide in the Creator Profile?
The information in your Creator Profile is shared with our Ads team and vetted brands and agencies, who are looking for creators for sponsorship campaigns. By filling out your Creator Profile, you are more discoverable to potential sponsors.
What should I put in my bio?
Help brands know who you are, what you do, and what you’re looking for. It could also be helpful to include times your channel is live.
Can I alter or change which stats are included automatically in my Creator Profile?
At this time, no. However, we’re working hard to make changes and improvements to this tool in the future.
Can Creator Profile be updated or managed on mobile?
No, at this time Creator Profile can only be updated on Desktop.
Why should I fill out my Creator Profile?
Filling in your Creator Profile will help surface richer data in our advertiser search tool, thereby increasing the chances your profile will match the criteria for a brand’s campaign. Adding a bio and a profile picture makes it easier for the brand to connect with you, and increases the chances your channel will have opportunities to participate in campaigns.
Can I delete my Creator Profile?
At this time, you can only delete your Creator Profile by deleting your Twitch account. However, you can edit any sections, and we are working on building the ability to delete just your Profile.
Will my profile be visible to viewers?
None of the information you choose to share on your profile will be visible to viewers.
I don’t see any demographic statistics in my profile, why?
We only show audience demographic data to streamers with more than 25 average concurrent viewers in the past 90 days.
Some of the stats you have provided for my channel do not match third-party or community tools that I have previously used for this purpose. Why?
Third-party tools can be helpful in some respects, but ultimately Twitch’s data is most representative of your channel’s true performance. A key benefit to filling out your Creator Profile is the ability to rely on official Twitch audience and demographic data when connecting with brands.

Custom Bit Badge and Emote Reward Slots

Affiliates and Partners can replace Bit Badges with their own custom designs and names for their channel, starting with the 1 and 100 Bit Reward Tier and beyond. Users are eligible to start receiving emote rewards only at the 1,000 Bit Reward Tier, as Emote Reward slots are progressively unlocked starting from the 1,000 Bit Reward Tier up to the highest tier.

This is an opportunity for you to further customize the rewards for your community, and to have those rewards align with the vision for your channel.

On this page:

  • Managing Bits Badges
  • Emote Reward Slots
  • Managing Emote Rewards
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Managing Bits Badges

To manage your Bits reward tiers, head to your dashboard. On the left-hand sidebar, click Monetization, then Bits & Cheering. There, visit Bits Tier Badges.

Search “bits” in the creator dashboard search field to quickly navigate to your Bits & Cheering settings.

Here, you can choose which Bits Badges are enabled on your channel. Viewers unlock badges based on total Bits used to Cheer for you. The highest unlocked enabled badge will appear next to viewers’ names. All badges are on by default, but you can choose which chat badges your channel supports by deselecting the Badge Tiers you would like to ignore.

Uploading Bits Badges

You will need each badge image as a .png in the following three sizes:

  • 18 x 18px
  • 36 x 36px
  • 72 x 72px

To upload a badge:

  • Click Edit on your desired Bits reward tier.
  • If you’d like to change the name of your bit badge, enter it under the Badge Name field.
  • Under Badge Image, click or drag and drop the appropriately sized file onto each box.
  • Click Save.

Once uploaded, your custom badges will be immediately available on the site. Any viewers that already have a Bit badge will have to Cheer once for their badge to be updated to the new custom design.

To reset a Bits badge back to default, click Reset to Default underneath your custom badge, then click Save.

Emote Reward Slots

To strengthen the bond between your channel and community, your viewers have the opportunity to unlock special emotes when they reach certain Bits Reward Tiers. Once an emote slot is unlocked, viewers can use the emote in that slot anywhere on Twitch, just like any other standard subscriber emote.

Emote slots are available beginning at the 1,000 Bits Reward tier. To get you started, the first 3 emote slots are automatically unlocked for you:

  • 1,000 Bits Reward Tier
  • 5,000 Bits Reward Tier
  • 10,000 Bits Reward Tier

If higher Bits Reward tiers have been achieved in your channel these emote slots will also be unlocked, as will the slot for the next highest tier. Your community will progressively unlock emote slots as new Bits Reward tiers are reached.

You can upload new, custom emotes into these slots or re-use existing subscriber emotes - remember that emote names are unique so the artwork can be the same but you may need to choose a different emote name. Once a slot is unlocked you can also change the emote in that slot at any time. When you change an emote reward, viewers at that tier will lose access to the original emote and be rewarded with the new emote.

Managing Emote Rewards

To manage your Bits tier emotes, head to your dashboard. On the left-hand sidebar, click Viewer Rewards, then Emotes. Here, scroll down to the Bits Tier Emotes section.

The size limitations and guidelines for emote rewards are the same as subscriber emotes. As a rough guideline, your emote rewards will need to meet the following requirements:

  • 112x112px image size. If uploading in Manual Mode, you will also need your emote in 56x56px and 28x28px sizes.
  • The file size of your emote cannot exceed 1 MB.
  • Your emote must be a .png.

For more information about the Rules & Guidelines for emotes on Twitch, please see our Emote Guidelines.

To add an emote reward, click the + on any open slot to open the upload menu. Once uploaded, your emote will be added to the slot and saved to your Library so that it can be used later should you decide to remove it from the slot in the future. You can also upload directly into your Library instead of a specific slot by clicking on Upload New.

You can upload your emote in one of two ways:

Auto-Resize Mode

Auto-resize mode is an easy, streamlined way to upload your emotes. You’ll need a single, square .png that is at least 112x112px. This image will then be converted automatically into our other required sizes.

  • Click the Upload icon within the square on the left hand side to select the appropriate file. Your emote will automatically be converted into 56x56px and 28x28px.
  • Within the Emote Code field, choose a name for your emote (e.g: Love). Your emote’s full code will be your emote prefix combined with your emote code (e.g: prefix + Love = prefixLove).
  • Once you’ve uploaded your file and selected your code, click Upload Emote.
Manual Mode

Deactivating auto-resize mode allows you to upload three separate sizes (28x28, 56x56, 112x112px) rather than having them automatically scaled. If the automatic conversions made via auto-resize mode are not to your liking and you want more control on each of the sizes, manual mode allows for image-by-image control for each size. Please note that the three sizes you supply for each emote must be of the same image.

  • Deactivate the Auto-Resize toggle.
  • Click the Upload icon within each square to select the appropriately sized file (specified underneath the box) for each.
  • Within the Emote Code field, choose a name for your emote (e.g: Love). Your emote’s full code will be your emote prefix combined with your emote code (e.g: prefix + Love = prefixLove).
  • Once you’ve uploaded your files and selected your code, click Upload Emote.

Once uploaded, your emote will be saved to your library. If you uploaded directly into a slot, it will be assigned to that slot by default.

As with subscriber emotes, your emote rewards will need to be reviewed and approved by Twitch before they can be used on the site. However, Partners in Good Standing and Affiliates who meet certain criteria are eligible for instant emote upload — your emotes go live right away without manual review. See our Emote Guidelines for eligibility details.

Emote rewards earned by unlocking Bits Reward Tiers can only be used by the channel owner and viewers who have unlocked the corresponding badge tier through Cheering.

The Emote Library

Whenever you upload an emote, it is saved within your Library. The Library allows you to save and manage your emotes independently from slots. Emotes within your library will be grayed out if they are assigned to a slot or lit up if they are available. If your emotes are pending approval, they will have a watch icon. You can have a pending emote assigned to a slot. Just note that your viewers will not be able to see it until it is approved and the watch icon disappears.

Your Library will automatically expand as you open more emote slots. As your Library of emotes expands, the ability to sort, filter, and search will allow you to quickly find the emotes you’re looking for.

Library capacity for standard emotes is equal to 2x Subscriber Emote Slots + 10. For Partners, the Library capacity for Animated emotes is 10.

You can assign or reassign an emote from the Library to a slot by clicking on an emote and selecting Slot Assignment. The dropdown will provide a list of options for assignment. Once you’ve made your selection, the emote will be added to the end of the active emote slots for that assignment.

If the slots for a given assignment are full, the option will be grayed out. You can fix this by removing emotes from slots, which will make them unavailable to viewers but will still save them in your library should you choose to use them later. You can remove an emote from a slot either directly through the Library or by clicking on Remove from Slot on the slot itself.

At a certain point, you may reach your Library capacity, which will prevent you from uploading additional emotes until some are deleted. You can delete an emote from your Library by clicking on an emote and selecting Delete from Library. This will permanently remove the emote from your Library and any slot it is currently assigned to upon confirmation.

Frequently Asked Questions

Are these features available for Affiliates and Partners?
Both Affiliates and Partners may customize their Bit Badge images and names and upload Bits Emote Rewards.
What if I find an offensive badge or emote image?
As with all user-uploaded content, these images are subject to the Terms of Service and Community Guidelines. Please report the channel with as much information as possible. Partner’s Custom Bit Badges can be reset to the global default if found necessary by staff.
Are animated Bits badges and Bits reward emotes supported?
No. Static PNG images only
Why are the higher Bits tiers of emotes locked?
If a Bits tier has not been reached in your channel that emote slot will remain locked. Once a new Bits tier is reached by one of your viewers, that tier’s emote slot and the one above it will be unlocked and you will be able to upload emotes in those slots.
Do my Bits emote rewards have to be approved like my subscriber emotes?
Your Bits emote rewards will need to be reviewed and approved by Twitch before they can be used on the site. However, Partners in Good Standing and Affiliates who meet certain criteria are eligible for instant emote upload — your emotes go live right away without manual review. See our Emote Guidelines for eligibility details.
How is my Library capacity determined?
Library capacity for standard emotes is equal to 2x Subscriber Emote Slots + 10. This means that as a new Affiliate, you will have a Library capacity of 16 and Partners with all emote slots unlocked will have a capacity of 150. See the Subscriber Emote Guide for further details.
Can I upload multiple emotes with the same name into my Library?
Yes, but you cannot have two emotes with the same name assigned to slots at the same time. Example: You can have two “Happy” emotes in your Library, but only one of them can be assigned to your emote slots.
Can I upload an animated emote as a Bits tier reward?
Animated emotes are a subscription benefit. They can only be added as Tier 1 subscription emotes.
An earned Bits Badge is not showing up, how can I select it?
In your Chat Identity settings, you can choose to Use Custom Badge For This Channel. This lets you pick a badge that is different from your global badge. If you enable this option, your channel badge will override your global badge choice.

Partner Cheermote Guide

For Partners, Cheermotes are a great way to further customize their channel with their unique style and branding.

Each channel with Cheering enabled can now create a progressively more exciting Cheermote for each tier of Bits used: 1, 100, 1,000, 5,000, and 10,000. Viewers will be able to see your customized Cheermote in your channel when they click the gem icon in the bottom right hand corner of the chat.

Viewers can use the format prefixCheer# (for example: bobrossCheer1000) to Cheer with a channel’s custom Cheermote. Cheers made with a custom Cheermote will still count towards cheering features such as Top Cheerers. For more information about Cheering, please see our Guide to Cheering with Bits.

Your Partner Cheermote can only be used in your channel.

CHEERMOTE GUIDELINES

Our Twitch Community Guidelines and Terms of Service apply to all user-generated images, including Cheermotes, badges, and emotes.

Specific content prohibited from use in Cheermotes includes the following:

  • Nudity, and obscene or sexually suggestive content.
  • Drugs or drug paraphernalia.
  • Hate speech, racist, derogatory, and harassing words or imagery.
  • Explicit words or gestures.
  • Images of single letters (sub badges may have single letters if it represents the brand of the channel).
  • Violations of Twitch Brand Assets.
  • Violations of any third party intellectual property or privacy rights, such as copyrights, trademarks, or rights of publicity. Remember, these may be subject to DMCA take-downs or other requests for removal by the rights holders.

For further information on guideline enforcement, please see the Frequently Asked Questions section below.

CHEERMOTE REQUIREMENTS

Cheermote images must be:

  • Between 112x112px and 4096x4096px. If using manual mode, you will need three sizes when uploading your Cheermote: 28x28, 56x56, and 112x112px.
  • When using auto-resize, the size of the image cannot exceed 1MB. When using manual mode, each image cannot exceed 512KB
  • Each image cannot contain more than 60 frames.
  • Must not flash or flicker more than 3 times within a 1 second period.
  • The images must comply with the Twitch Community Guidelines, Terms of Service, and DMCA Guidelines.

UPLOADING YOUR CHEERMOTE

To manage your Cheermotes, head to your dashboard. On the left-hand sidebar, click Viewer Rewards, then Emotes. Here, scroll down to the Cheermotes section.

Click on the + sign under each Cheer tier to upload your image for that tier. All images must be uploaded in order to enable your Cheermote.

There are two ways to upload your Cheermotes:

Auto-Resize Mode

Auto-resize mode is the default upload experience and allows you to upload a single 112x112px animated .GIF which is then converted into all the required sizes for you. Auto-resize mode uses the first frame of each .GIF as the static image. To manually set your static image, deselect the Use the first frame for thumbnails option.

Manual Mode

Deactivating auto-resize mode allows you to upload three separate sizes (28x28, 56x56, 112x112px) rather than having them automatically scaled. If the automatic conversions made via auto-resize mode are not to your liking and you want more control on each of the sizes, manual mode allows for image-by-image control for each size. Any missing images will mean your Cheermote will not go live.

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

Does this replace the Bits gem cheering in my channel?

No. Cheermotes are in addition to the standard Bits gems and tiers.

Will my Cheermotes be available for my viewers immediately upon uploading all tiers?

Yes. Unlike emotes, Cheermotes can only appear in your channel and therefore do not require manual approval before they appear to your audience.

I uploaded my Cheermote but I can’t use it on my channel! What gives?

If you believe your Cheermote has been successfully uploaded but still isn’t usable on the site, please submit a ticket via help.twitch.tv so that we can investigate. When submitting a ticket, please log into your Partnered account so that your ticket is routed correctly.

My Cheermote disappeared from my Partner settings. What happened?

You should have received an email regarding the reason why your Cheermote has been removed (check your spam filter). If you did not, simply file a ticket via help.twitch.tv to inquire (be sure to log in so that your Partnership status is noted for expedited assistance). Remember that all Cheermotes must comply with the badge and emote guidelines. To resolve this, you may alter the Cheermote so that it does not violate any of these rules, or submit a different Cheermote altogether.

I think a Cheermote violates Twitch’s rules. How do I report it?

If you find a Cheermote you believe violates the rules, please report it via the User Report feature. You can report a channel by clicking the three dots on the bottom right hand side underneath the video player. From there, use the path Somewhere Else -> On Twitch -> Emotes or Badges then pick the most appropriate reason from the list.

Does this work with my third-party alerts?

Yes. Third party devs are able to get new Cheermote assets to customize Bits-related alerts.

How many Cheermotes can each Partner create?

One set with five tiers.

What is the revenue I receive when a viewer uses my Partner Cheermote?

When your viewers Cheer with your Partner Cheermote in your channel, you receive the same revenue from the Bits used as with global Cheermotes or regular gem Bit emotes.

Partner Settings Guide

This article provides an overview of the various settings and customizations available to Twitch Partners. Twitch Partners can find their Partner settings on the Creator Dashboard. To navigate to your Partner settings, click the hamburger menu icon on the top left hand side of your dashboard to open the navigation menu, then click Preferences, then finally Partner. You can also use this direct link.

You must be a Partner in order to see this tab on your dashboard.

Onboarding

The Onboarding section is where you need to be to update or view the information on your Partnered account.

Partner Onboarding

To update your address or personal information (email, etc.), edit your details directly from your Creator Dashboard → Monetization → Partner. To redo a tax interview, use the Retake option next to the relevant interview. You do not need to restart onboarding. For more information, please see our Partner Onboarding Guide.

Payout Method

You can change your payout method here. For information on how to do this, the payout methods we support, or general payout queries, please see our Partner Payout FAQ.

View Active Partner Agreement

You can view your active Partner Agreement here.

Subscriptions

This section contains options for customizing your subscriber benefits. Subscription settings are located in your Monetization preferences.

Subscription Name

Here you can set a custom name to refer to your subscription product by. This can be edited at any point, does not require approval to show immediately, and can include any characters. Explicit words and hate speech are prohibited - the Subscription name must comply with our Terms of Service and Community Guidelines.

Emotes

You can upload, modify, or remove emotes for your subscriptions by clicking on the redirect link to our Emotes page. You can also access the page directly through navigation via Viewer Rewards -> Emotes on the left-hand sidebar. Partners in good standing do not need to wait for manual approval for their emote to go live on the site. Partners are considered to be in “good standing” if they have not had a conduct infraction within the last 60 days. A conduct infraction is defined as any behaviour that breaks the Terms of Service or Community Guidelines.

For more information on subscriber emotes (including content guidelines, format requirements and how to upload them), please see our Emote Guidelines and Subscriber Emote Guide.

Partners in good standing can also change their emote prefix via the Emotes page every 60 days. Please note that emote prefixes:

  • Cannot begin with a number
  • Must be alphanumeric (no special characters)
  • Must be between 3 and 10 characters long
  • Cannot use capital letters

If you were previously a Twitch Affiliate, your previously automatically assigned prefix will carry over. Once you’ve become a Partner, you may request a one time manual prefix change by opening a ticket. Your requested prefix must follow the same guidelines noted above. Please provide multiple options within your ticket in case your initially requested prefix is taken.

Subscriber Badges

You can upload custom badges to denote subscribers and their subscription length here. Unlike emotes, badges will only appear in your channel and therefore do not require manual approval before they appear to your audience. For more information about Subscriber badges, please see our Subscriber Badge Guide.

Ad-Free Viewing

Toggle this option to allow subscribers to watch your channel ad free.

If you enable ad-free viewing for subscribers, your ad revenue will be calculated based only on the number of non-subscribed viewer impressions when you ran the ad. When the ad-free option is enabled, channel Subscribers will not be included in the impression counts used to calculate ad revenue. However, Twitch Turbo Subscribers who are also channel subscribers do count as ad impressions contributing towards ad revenue.

With ad-free viewing for subscribers enabled, you should only see a minimal change in ad revenue (up to about 3%), and for most Partners, this will be balanced by higher subscription rates as viewers see the added value of their purchase. You can also fine-tune your ad revenue by adjusting the timing and frequency of the ads you play during your streams or choosing to opt-out of offering ad-free viewing for subscribers on your channel.

Ignore Slow Mode

Toggle this option to allow subscribers to bypass slow mode. Your chat moderators will always be immune to this mode.

Subscriber-only Chat

Toggle this option to only allow subscribers to chat in your channel. This setting can also be toggled via chat commands (/subscribers and /subscribersoff) from the Partner or their moderators. Your chat moderators will always be immune to this mode.

Subscriber-only Archives

Toggle this option to only allow subscribers to view your past broadcasts and highlights.

If this option is enabled, you will not be able to make clips from your VODs.

Bits & Cheering

This section contains configuration and customization settings for Bits & Cheering on your channel. This section is located in your Monetization preferences.

Minimum Bits to Cheer

This is the smallest total of Bits that a cheer must meet in order to cheer on your channel. For example, setting this to 50 would mean that the sum total of the Bits used in your channel must be equal or greater to this amount.

Minimum Bits Emote

This is the smallest individual Bit Emote that can be used to cheer on your channel. For example, setting this to 50 would mean that no individual Bit Emotes under 50 (1, 25, etc) could be used in your channel.

Enable/Disable Pins

Disable or enable pinned cheers. This setting is enabled by default.

Minimum Threshold to Pin

By default, the minimum threshold to pin is 100 Bits, or the amount selected in Minimum Bits to Cheer (whichever is higher). You can lower this setting, which will lower your Minimum Bits to Cheer.

For further info on both of these settings, please mouse over the ‘i’ icon next to each one.

Bits Tier Badges

Here you can upload, modify, or remove custom Bits badges for viewers that reach cheering milestones on your channel. Unlike your subscriber emotes, badges can only appear on your channel and do not require manual approval before they become available to your audience. Your Bits badges must abide by our Terms of Service and Community Guidelines. For more information, please see our Custom Bit Badges Guide. To upload or remove Bits Tier Emotes, head to our Emote page via Viewer Rewards -> Emotes on the left-hand sidebar.

Cheermotes

You can upload, modify, or remove a custom Cheermote that viewers can use when Cheering on your channel by clicking on the redirect link to our Emote management page. You can also access the page directly via Viewer Rewards -> Emotes on the left-hand sidebar. These do not require manual approval before going live on your channel. However, your Cheermote must still abide by our Terms of Service and Community Guidelines. For more information, please see our Partner Cheermote Guide.

Community

This section is dedicated to options that allow you to provide recognition and give back to supporters of your channel. This section is located in your Monetization preferences.

Hype Train

This menu allows you to customize various settings and enable or disable the Hype Train feature. For a full run down of these settings, please see our Hype Train Guide.

Leaderboards

This menu provides the option to enable or disable the leaderboard that displays Top Cheerers and Top Gifters at the top of your chat.

Ads

This section contains options for ads on your channel. Locate these settings in your Monetization preferences.

Preroll Ads

This option allows you to disable or enable prerolls when you run midroll ads on your channel.

Preroll Notifications

This toggle dictates whether or not you receive dashboard alerts when preroll ads are disabled/enabled on your channel.

Stream Display Ads

This toggle enables Stream Display Ads on your channel.

Revenue share for Advertisements

View your revenue share for playing advertisements on your channel.

For more information about preroll and midroll ads, please see our Disabling Prerolls article.

Streamer Community Survey

Improving inclusivity within our product and program designs is a priority at Twitch. In order to make that happen, we need a measurable way to understand how a creator’s identity might influence their experience.

The Streamer Community Survey - developed in partnership with international survey experts PSB Insights - consists of seven questions that provide us with data about different aspects of a creator’s identity including gender, race, sexual preference, and ability. By collecting this data, we can study the differences in creator experiences based on their identity. We can also build and improve tools that promote safe and equitable experiences, and ensure our programs and initiatives support a diverse set of creators.

We understand that identity is very personal and some creators may not feel comfortable revealing certain aspects of their identity. The information creators choose to share in the survey is not accessible to the public. We will only use a creator’s data for the purposes to which they consent. All questions within the survey are optional and can be edited or deleted at any point in the future should you change your mind.

On this page:

  • Taking the Survey
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Taking the Survey

Twitch Partners and Affiliates can access the Streamer Community Survey in their Creator Dashboard. On the left-hand sidebar, click Settings, then Streamer Survey.

On this page, you’ll find the following options:

Your Level of Participation

You have the option to answer all, some, or none of the questions in the survey.

If you do not wish to participate in the survey, click the box next to Opt-out. This will disable responses from being entered into the survey, as well as deleting any responses you’ve previously given.

Open Ended Responses

We strive to provide inclusive representation in the survey, and with your help, we can learn and make improvements over time. If your identity is not represented in the list, choose the “Not Listed” response option and let us know what’s missing.

Data Use Preferences

Use the toggles to give or withdraw your permission for each use of your demographic data.

  • Study the differences in creator experiences based on their identity.
  • Build and improve the tools that promote a safe and equitable experience for creators.
  • Recruit creators for participation in research studies.
  • Invite creators to be featured in events, promotions or sponsorships.
Change or Delete Responses

For privacy purposes, your responses are cleared from the page after you click Submit. To edit your responses once they’ve been submitted, simply complete and resubmit the survey. Choosing Prefer not to answer will delete a previously submitted response.

To delete all of your prior responses, click the box next to Opt-out.

To provide suggestions or feedback about the Streamer Community Survey, visit our UserVoice page.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can everyone that works at Twitch view the responses shared in the Streamer Community Survey?

No. The data collected from the Streamer Community Survey has additional layers of security to ensure that it is only used for the purposes to which you provide consent.

Will the information I share in the survey be visible to the public?

No. Unlike Tags - which are displayed on your channel to help viewers discover your content - the information you provide in the Streamer Community Survey is never shared publicly and your demographic information will only be used for the purposes to which you consent.

Why is the survey only available to Partners and Affiliates?

We believe that limiting survey participation to Partners and Affiliates will allow Twitch to conduct meaningful research and programs, however, availability may expand in the future.

How will this data be used by Twitch?

We will only use the data for the purposes to which you consent. Generally speaking, however, Twitch is collecting this data to study the behaviors, interactions and differences in creator experiences based on their identity, to build and improve tools that promote a safe and equitable experience for creators, and to ensure our programs and initiatives support a diverse set of creators.

This survey is missing a specific attribute, will you be updating the survey?

If a specific attribute is missing from the list, please use the open-ended response option in the survey to let us know. This data will inform future iterations of the survey.

Will this data be used for Recommendations on the Twitch home page?

No, this data will not impact your individual Recommendations, and will not be used to make recommendations to others.

Streamer-Read Ads

Streamer-read Ads are live readouts of branded talking points across multiple streams for a preset time frame (ex: 4 readouts across 2 weeks). Streamer-Read Ads allow brands to work with streamers to increase the awareness and understanding of their products and services.

Streamer-read Ads are often included as part of Sponsorship campaigns and can be completed while you are live with a Sponsored Subscription or channel skin.

Frequently Asked Questions

I forgot to click “Start Streamer-Read Ad” when doing the read out, can I still count it as completed?
No. Clicking “Start Streamer-Read Ad” is how we start a campaign and monitor performance. A campaign therefore can’t be completed until you click this button. If you realize after finishing one or more read-outs that you didn’t press the button, you will have to re-do those read-out(s) after clicking the button to complete the campaign.
I’m using OBS/Stream Elements/Streamlabs and I can’t find the quick action. Where is it?
Quick actions embedded in third-party apps are not currently available for Streamer-Read Ads. Keep your Twitch Stream Manager open in order to trigger the quick action.
I’m getting an error and/or unable to click “Start Streamer Read Ad”, what’s going on?
If you’re unable to click the button or getting an error, please check to make sure you’re live, not running a midroll ad, and didn’t click Start Streamer-Read Ad more than once. These factors will inform whether you can move forward.
Will ads be able to play during my readout?
Ads should not play while you are reading a Streamer-Read Ad. If an ad (e.g., a mid-roll ad that you activated) is running before you initiate a Streamer-Read Ad, you will receive an error and need to wait until the ad has finished. We recommend verifying you do not have a scheduled ad running when you plan on beginning your Streamer-Read Ad. Once a readout has started, ads will be declined for two minutes during the readout.
During the readout, I made a mistake and would like to request a re-do. What should I do?
Please reach out to the Twitch team member working with you on the campaign.
Will users with channel or Turbo subscriptions see the sponsored overlay logo even if they normally enjoy ad-free viewing?
Yes, users who subscribe to our ad-free products are still able to see sponsorships that involve their favorite streamers, so your viewers will see the experience.

Twitch Ambassador Program Overview

What is the Twitch Ambassador Program?

The Twitch Ambassador program empowers a dynamic community of passionate leaders committed to fostering collaboration, driving positive change by amplifying the voices of our global community and brand advocacy. Ambassadors embody the fundamental values of the program’s pillars. Read on to learn more.

What do Twitch Ambassadors Do?

Twitch Ambassadors actively embody the program pillars: Fostering Collaboration, Positive Change & Brand Advocacy.

Fostering Collaboration: Twitch Ambassadors are empowering and inspiring leaders within the community with a unique ability to bring people together. They have a proven track record of creating impactful moments and events, driven by a deep understanding of the Twitch community. By sharing their knowledge and experience, Ambassadors empower others, foster growth, and pave the way for the next generation of creators.

Positive Change: Twitch Ambassadors drive positive change by amplifying the voices of the community and advocating for its needs. They provide valuable feedback on all things Twitch, participating in roundtables with various Twitch teams. Ambassadors are also included in the Twitch Safety Advisory Collective. Their contributions help embody our commitment to the creator experience at the heart of Twitch.

Brand Advocacy: Twitch Ambassadors are passionate champions of the service who proudly “bleed purple.” As trusted community leaders, they are among the first to showcase and provide new education on new Twitch tools to the community. Twitch Ambassadors are also showcased across Twitch marketing and campaigns, highlighting their influence as authentic advocates for the service.

How Do I Know Someone is a Twitch Ambassador?

Twitch Ambassadors can be identified by their unique chat badge:

Find current and past year Ambassadors in the Ambassador Team Page.

Who Can Apply to the Ambassador Program?

The Ambassador Program is open to individuals who meet the following criteria:

  • Be a Twitch Partner.
  • Be at least 18 years of age.
  • Global applications are welcome. We wish to bring on Ambassadors that can work on our programming and events globally.

How to Apply to the Ambassador Program?

Submit your Application to be considered.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the benefits of being a Twitch Ambassador?

Ambassador benefits include but are not limited to:

  • Unique chat badge.
  • Streamlined communication between Twitch community programs such as Unity Guilds, MeetUps, and Creator Camp.
  • Early access to Twitch service updates & product testing.
  • Marketing and PR opportunities.

How long does a Twitch Ambassador remain in the program?

Twitch Ambassadors remain in the program permanently unless they choose to opt out or are removed for a violation of Terms of Service (TOS) or Community Guidelines (CGs).

Do Ambassadors need to be Twitch Partners?

Yes, all Twitch Ambassadors must be Twitch Partners.

Is there a minimum follower or viewer count required to become an Ambassador?

As long as you are already a Twitch Partner, there’s no specific follower or viewer count required to become an ambassador. Our selection process focuses on an applicant’s community impact and alignment with the program mission, rather than metrics.

How long are you accepting applications for the Twitch Ambassador program?

Our Ambassador application is open year-round, allowing individuals to apply whenever they feel ready. We recognize that everyone’s journey is unique, so there’s no set deadline. Apply whenever the time feels right for you!

Can I recommend someone to be a Twitch Ambassador?

Recommendations can be made within the Ambassador Application! If you know someone who would be a great fit, we encourage you to submit them within your application.

Do I need to resubmit or reapply each year?

No, you do not need to resubmit your application or reapply each year. You can log in and edit your submission at any time to update your information or make changes as needed.

Will I be notified if my application is not accepted?

Due to the high volume of applicants, we are unable to send individual denial emails. If you have not heard back after a certain period, it is safe to assume that your application was not selected at this time. We encourage you to continue creating impactful content or editing your previous submission.

Twitch Partner Discord Server

All Twitch Partners can now connect with other Partners, and stay up-to-date on Twitch news, and by joining their local Twitch Partner Discord server. Discord is a messaging platform that connects communities through combined chat rooms, or servers. Many streamers already keep in touch with their Twitch communities utilizing Discord or other social media tools.

In this guide, we’ll walk you through how to join the Twitch Partner Discord Server, benefits of joining, and what to expect once you join.

How to Join the Twitch Partner Discord Server

First, Twitch Partners must link their Partner account to their Discord account via Discord’s user settings. Learn more in Discord’s Help Center here. For help, contact our friends at Discord.

Step 1: Visit your Creator Dashboard, and click the Discord server invite in Creator Home.

Partners, visit your Creator Dashboard here!

Partners may join Twitch Partner Discord servers outside of their geographic region. Server links are contained in the #server-guide section of all servers.

  • English-language North America
  • English-language Asia Pacific
  • English-language Europe, Middle East & Africa
  • Spanish
  • German
  • French
  • Japanese
  • Traditional Chinese
  • Portuguese
Step 2: (In Discord) Authorize Twitch’s account verification bot access to your Twitch account.

After you accept an invite to the Twitch Partner Discord server, you’ll need to grant our authentication bot access to your Twitch account. This bot verifies your identity as a Twitch Partner.

Twitch’s authentication bot is called Verification Bot. Check for the verified bot badge in Discord. Twitch’s authentication bot is hosted at help.twitch.tv.

Use caution when granting bots, services, or tools access to your Twitch account. Additionally, do not click links from anyone claiming to represent Twitch Staff that approaches you via Discord Direct Messages, or Twitch Whispers.

If you have multiple Twitch accounts connected to your Discord, this is usually the reason for verification errors. We recommend temporarily removing all other Twitch accounts from your Discord during the verification process. You should then be able to join with no issue!

Agree to the Twitch Partner Discord Server Rules:

When you join the Twitch Partner Discord Server, you are subject to both Twitch’s Community Guidelines and Terms of Service, and Discord’s Community Guidelines and Terms of Service. Terms of your Partner contract apply to your conduct in the Twitch Partner Discord server. You must also follow the server rules listed below.

  • Twitch’s Terms of Service and Community Guidelines apply in this server.
  • Discord’s Terms of Service and Community Guidelines apply in this server.
  • This server is not an official Twitch Support channel. For assistance with your account, please visit twitch.tv/help. Do not ping or DM Twitch Staff, admins, or moderators. For security, do not share any information associated with your account.
  • Harassment of any kind will not be tolerated. Be respectful of server members, including fellow Partners, moderators, and Twitch Staff.
  • Keep discussions relevant to the channel descriptions. In addition to content covered in Twitch’s Community Guidelines, refrain from engaging in topics that are harmful to members of the community.
  • Any discussion regarding on-service enforcement or off-service allegations, including speculation concerning specific accounts or users, is strictly prohibited. If you wish to appeal enforcement actions taken against your account, please utilize appeals.twitch.tv
  • Inappropriate or impersonating profiles are prohibited (including usernames, nicknames, avatars, etc.).
  • Advertising content and recruiting (including advertising and recruiting of competing services), as well as spamming (sending repetitive messages, emojis, images, or reactions) in the server or DMs is prohibited
  • Feedback in dedicated channels must be constructive or contribute to fostering constructive discussion. Explore our Help Portal for tips on giving constructive feedback.
  • To maintain a safe environment, we depend on server members to report any rule violations or situations that make them feel unsafe. Please prioritize reporting incidents to discord.com/report first. Then, utilize the #report-a-user channel to submit a ticket to promptly inform our server moderators. If you suspect a violation of the Off-Service Conduct policy, please reach out to the Twitch Off-Service Investigations team for assistance.
  • This server is meant to be a safe and fun space for Twitch Partners to connect. Do not screenshot or otherwise store or share anything from this server without Twitch’s written permission.
  • We offer servers in multiple languages, with moderators who are fluent in that language. For moderation purposes, some servers may set communication in one language only. If you’re looking for a server in another language, please read the #server-guide channel.
  • Upon joining this server, you agree to abide by the rules. Failure to comply may result in removal from the server. Rules are subject to change and we may notify the server accordingly. It’s your responsibility to review and adhere to the rules.

Last updated: May 2024

Frequently Asked Questions

Who can join Twitch Partner Discord Servers?
Any Twitch Partner can find an invitation to their region’s Discord server in their Creator Dashboard
When do I go to Discord for help, and when do I go to Twitch for help?

Something not right in the Twitch Partner Discord server? To file a report, always start by reporting to Discord first, then report to the Twitch server moderator in the #report-a-user channel.

Contact our friends at Discord support for help with:

  • Connecting your Twitch and Discord accounts
  • Make sure you are logging into the right Twitch and Discord accounts

Contact Twitch Support for help with:

  • Issues with our verification bot
  • Issues with our invitation link in your Creator Home
  • Issues with your Twitch account
How many Twitch Partner Discord Servers can I join?
Twitch Partners are welcome to join as many regional Twitch Partner Discord servers as they like. However, be aware that some regional servers may set communication in one language only.
Why is Twitch using Discord for Twitch Partners?
We want to meet our community members where they are. We launched Twitch Partner Discords to provide a space for Partners to come together and build communities. In addition to creating spaces for Partners to connect and collaborate, we use these channels to share relevant updates, get feedback, and highlight new opportunities for Partners.
Is it safe to connect my Twitch account and Discord account?
For more information, visit our Privacy Notice.
Am I required to join the Twitch Partner Discord server?
No. Joining the Twitch Partner Discord server is not a requirement of the Twitch Partner program. The server is available as an extra benefit, and we welcome you to join!
How active do I need to be in the Twitch Partner Discord server?
There are no specific requirements for participating in the Twitch Partner Discord server.
If I don’t join the Twitch Partner Discord server, am I missing out on opportunities to advance my Twitch channel?
By organizing the servers around shared languages, we believe we can unlock new opportunities for Partner networking and collaboration across regions. By being part of the Twitch Discord servers, you not only receive relevant Twitch information like news and product updates, but you will also be able to connect with fellow Partners in your region and around the world. You may also be able to participate in networking and collaboration sessions facilitated by the Twitch Partnerships team, designed to bring Partners together around similar interests and streaming categories.

Twitch Partner Onboarding Guide

Congrats on being invited to the Partner program! This guide walks you through completing Partner Onboarding. If you’re already a fully onboarded Affiliate, the process is very quick — your account details, tax interviews, and payout information carry over.

If you have questions throughout this process, contact Twitch Support here.

Coming From Affiliate? (Fast Path)

If you were already a fully onboarded Affiliate, the Partner upgrade process is simple. Your account details, tax interviews, and payout method all carry over from your Affiliate setup.

To complete your Partner upgrade:

  • You’ll receive a Partner Invite Extended notification. Click Accept Now.
  • You’ll be taken to your Creator Dashboard (Monetization → Partner). All three steps should show green checkmarks if your Affiliate onboarding was complete.
  • Verify your information is correct, then click the Become a Partner button at the top of the page.
  • You’ll see a “Partner Status: Unlocked!” confirmation. Welcome to the Partner Program!

If any steps do not show a green checkmark, you’ll need to complete them before you can click Become a Partner. See the full step-by-step guide below.

You may also be invited to take an optional Streamer Community Survey. This helps Twitch learn more about who you are so we can source you for opportunities in the future. You can take it now or find it later in your Creator Dashboard settings.

Access and Overview

Once accepted into the Partner program, you’ll complete onboarding from Creator Dashboard → Monetization → Partner.

Complete the following steps:
  • Enable Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)
  • Complete Your Account Detail
  • Start Earning Revenue

All steps must be fully completed in order to begin monetizing your channel as a Partner.

Didn’t come from the Affiliate program? If you haven’t previously completed tax interviews and payout setup, you’ll need to complete all steps in full — including tax interviews and payout method. The process is the same as Affiliate Onboarding, with the same tips and troubleshooting guidance.

Step 1 — Enable Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)

Partners are required to use Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) for account security. If you already have 2FA enabled (most Affiliates will), this step will show as complete and you can proceed to Step 2.

If you need to enable 2FA, click Enable and follow the prompts. For detailed instructions or troubleshooting, see our Two-Factor Authentication guide.

Step 2 — Complete Your Account Detail

Provide your details and accept the Monetized Streamer Agreement to get started. If you completed this step during Affiliate onboarding, it will show as complete with your existing information.

Complete the following fields:

  • Legal Full Name — Enter your first, middle (optional), and last name exactly as it appears on your tax documents. Do not alter your legal name to match the form.
  • Email — Pre-filled from your account. You can edit this if needed.
  • Business Name (optional) — For business tax reporting only. Match your business name to tax filings and payout method.
  • Country of Residence — Select your country.
  • Date of Birth — Enter your date of birth. If this field appears locked, you’ve previously verified your age with Twitch. See Date of Birth Changes to learn how to update it.
  • Monetized Streamer Agreement — Read and agree to the Twitch Monetized Streamer Agreement. If you are over 13 but under 18, your parent or legal guardian must agree on your behalf.

Common issue — mismatched details: The information you enter here (name, address, country) carries forward to your tax interviews and payout setup in Step 3. Mismatches between these areas are the most common cause of issues. Enter your information accurately and use the same details throughout.

Address formats differ around the world. If you’re outside the US and have trouble entering your address, the form may expect US formatting conventions (such as house number before street name). Do not alter your legal address to match the form. If you’re having trouble, contact Twitch Support.

Step 3 — Start Earning Revenue

Fill in your information to get paid out and access your Spendable Balance. This step includes your tax interviews and payout method selection. If you completed these during Affiliate onboarding, they may already show as complete.

Tax Interviews

You’ll see one or more tax interviews listed (such as Royalty Tax Interview and Service Tax Interview). Depending on your region, you may see additional required interviews (e.g., DAC7 for EU-based streamers). Complete all interviews that appear for your account.

Twitch is a subsidiary of Amazon. We use certain Amazon tools to help Partners get paid, including the tax information forms in the onboarding process. Please refer to the Amazon Tax Information Interview Guide if you need help with the definitions for any individual field.

Click Start next to a tax interview to begin. You may be asked to re-authenticate (log in again and enter a verification code). This is normal — you’re handling sensitive personal information.

You’ll then see a screen asking you to authorize Amazon Tax Central to access your account. This is expected — Twitch uses Amazon tools for tax processing.

The tax interview form is managed by Amazon and may look different from Twitch. This is expected. Twitch Support cannot provide tax advice or help you fill out the form. For field-by-field guidance, see the Amazon Tax Information Interview Guide. If you need tax advice, contact a local tax professional.

In some cases, a subsequent tax interview may not require you to fill out additional information if your details from a previous interview carry over. Complete whatever the form asks you to do.

Processing Timeline:

  • Tax forms typically take 24-48 hours to validate
  • In some cases, validation can take up to 72 hours (3 days)
  • If your forms are still processing after 72 hours, wait 2-3 weeks for validation to complete
  • This process cannot be expedited

Additional Tax Resources:

  • If you need help filling in either tax information interview, contact your local tax professional.
  • EU residents, learn more about DAC7 requirements and how they impact you here.
  • CA residents, learn more about Canada Tax Interview requirements and how they impact you here.
Payout Method

Select how you want to be paid. You may need to confirm your password before proceeding. Some fields may be pre-filled from your account details.

Data consistency reminder: Ensure the name and details shown here match what you entered in Step 2 and in your tax interviews. Mismatches can cause payout issues.

We accept the following payout methods:

Payout Method

Timing

Direct Deposit / ACH (U.S Only)

3-5 Days

eCheck/Local Bank

1-4 Days

PayPal

1-2 Days

Check

1-2 Weeks

Wire Transfer

1-3 Days

Hold Payouts

N/A

Our payout processor requires a minimum balance for payout. The minimum amount for most payout methods is $50, and $100 for wire transfer. Learn more in Payout Balance FAQ.

Choose Hold Payouts if you want to control how often you are paid and consolidate transaction fees. Otherwise, you will be paid automatically with the method you select.

Partners enjoy no transaction fees on most payout methods. For details on payout fees, see Payout Details FAQ.

This section may also ask you to submit a scanned copy of your government ID such as a passport.

Updating Your Information

If you need to update your name, address, tax information, or payout method after completing onboarding, you can edit your information directly.

Visit your Creator Dashboard → Monetization → Partner to view and edit your current details.

Payouts begin processing before the 15th of each month. If you need to update your payout information, do so before the 10th of the month to avoid delays. If you have earned revenue or a payout pending and you’re unsure about timing, contact Twitch Support before making changes.

Frequently Asked Questions

What do I do if I need to change my information later?
You can edit your information directly from your Creator Dashboard → Monetization → Partner page. See Updating Your Information above for details.
When will I get paid?

The minimum payout threshold is $50 for most payout methods, or $100 for wire transfer. Learn more in $50 Minimum Payout Threshold.

Payouts are made 15 days after the end of the month of revenue being earned. For example, if you earn at least $50 with most payout methods or $100 with wire transfer on April 5th, the payout will be initiated 15 days after April 30th, which is May 15th. After the payout is initiated and depending upon the payout method, it may take several days for payouts to settle within your bank. Eligible payout methods for the $50 threshold include ACH/direct deposit, eCheck/local bank, PayPal, and check.

For details on payout timing, visit our help article When Do I Get Paid?

Why is my payout taking so long?
Typical payout timing by method:

Payout Method

Timing

ACH

3-5 days

PayPal

1-2 days

Check

1-2 weeks

eCheck (outside of U.S.)

1-4 days

Wire

1-3 days

For details on payout timing, visit our help article When Do I Get Paid?

How come my payout keeps failing?
Ensure your payout information is accurate and consistent across all steps. For PayPal, it is important that your country information, legal name, and PayPal email account match what you provided to PayPal directly. Mismatches between your account details, tax interviews, and payout setup are the most common cause of failed payouts.
Why am I seeing a reduction in my payout?
This could be a result of how your tax interview questionnaire was filled out. Review your tax information to ensure all details are correct.

For questions on your payout balance, visit Payout Balance FAQ.

When do changes to payout preferences take effect?
Once you submit payout method changes, any changes made after the 8th of the month will not be reflected in the current month’s payout. Make all payout method changes as early in the month as possible so this process does not interfere with any due payout.
Are there any payout threshold settings?
Your channel must accrue at least $50 with most payout methods or $100 with wire transfer before each payout is eligible to be initiated.
Still Stuck?
Tax forms validation taking longer?
Though typical time for tax forms validation is up to 3 days, in a few cases forms validation can take more time. If your tax forms are under review for more than 3 days, please wait 2-3 weeks to see if the validation will be complete. Twitch Support is unable to provide resolution for cases less than 2-3 weeks old. Contact support if tax form validation is pending for more than 3 weeks.
Payout verification taking longer?
If you are stuck in the payout verification step, try using an alternate payout method. If you prefer not to change the payout method, wait up to 48 hours for verification to complete. Contact support if you have been waiting more than 48 hours.
How do I leave the Partner Program?
Partners can contact Twitch Support to request offboarding. You will need to verify your identity before your request can be processed. Once offboarding is complete, all features related to your Partner status are removed from your channel, and active subscriptions towards your channel are cancelled. Subscribers are notified that their subscription has been canceled, but are not told the reason for the cancellation.

If you voluntarily leave the Partner Program, you can contact Twitch Support to rejoin the Affiliate Program — you cannot rejoin the Partner Program directly. If you were removed from the program by Twitch, your eligibility to rejoin may be restricted. Contact Twitch Support for more information.

What happens to my unpaid earnings when I leave the Partner program?
If you’ve reached the payout threshold ($50 for most users) and your payout method is valid, we will issue payment to you on the next payout cycle. If your payout method isn’t valid, we’ll hold your balance until you update to a valid payout method. If your unpaid accruals haven’t reached the payout threshold, no payout will be issued. That balance remains on your account. To receive a payout, you’ll need to rejoin as a Twitch Affiliate or Partner and your accruals need to reach the payout threshold.

If you can’t find an answer here, contact our support team using this form.

Twitch Partner Program Overview

The Twitch Partnership Program is for those committed to streaming and ready to level up from Affiliate. Twitch Partners are creators who stream various content, from games, music, talk shows, and art, to just about anything else you can imagine. If you love sharing what you do with a live community and have built up a sizable audience on Twitch or other services, we want to hear from you! If you want to learn more about how to grow your channel on Twitch, visit Twitch Creator Camp.

Monetization

Type

Description

Channel Subscriptions & Emotes

Twitch Partners can earn revenue by accepting subscriptions from their viewers. The subscription options are Tier 1, Tier 2, Tier 3, or the Prime free subscription. Revenue received from a subscription may vary depending on the country in which a subscriber lives. To learn more about local subscription prices read more here. Partners can also unlock up to 60 channel emotes.

Bits

Bits are a virtual good viewers can buy to Cheer on your channel, allowing them to support you without having to use an external website or third party. Twitch provides participating Partners a share of the revenue Twitch receives from Bits equal to 1 cent per Bit used to Cheer for them. As a Partner, you can customize your Cheermote and Bit Badges.

Ads

Partners earn a share of the revenue from any ads on their channel. In addition, partners can determine the length and frequency of mid-roll advertisements through their dashboard.

Special features

Channel Customization

Feature

Description

Custom Chat Badges

Partners can create custom chat badges for subs based on sub tenure.

Custom Emotes

Partners can unlock up to 60 emote slots based on the total amount of subscriber points you have.

Custom Emote Prefix

Partners can customize the prefix code in front of their emotes.

Custom Bit Badges, Bits Reward Emotes, and Cheermotes.

Verified User Badge

Chat badges allow you to showcase a part of your identity in channels on Twitch.

Lifetime Channel Subscriptions

Two lifetime channel subscriptions for your chatbot.

Additional Lifetime Channel Subscriptions

Up to 3 additional free lifetime channel subscriptions to friends and family. These are unlocked based on your total amount of subscribers.

Partner Username Change & Revert

As a Twitch Partner, you have access to two one-time username benefits through Partner Help:

  • Name Change — If you’d like to change your username and your desired name is not available through the self-service tool, the Partner Help team may be able to change it for you, based on availability.
  • Name Revert — If you’d like to revert to a username you previously held on the same account, the Partner Help team may be able to restore it for you.

Both are one-time benefits — Partners may request one name change and one name revert through Partner Help.

VOD Features

Feature

Description

Extended VOD Storage

Partners have VODs stored for 60 days, vs the standard 7 Days*.

Reruns and Premieres

Rebroadcast past content and show off new videos to your audience.

  • 7-day storage (formerly 14) beginning September 1, 2022 for channels that are not a Partner, Affiliate, Amazon Prime, or Twitch Turbo user. For more information, visit Video On Demand.
Subscriber Streams
