Subscriber Streams allow Creators to host a stream for some of their most dedicated community members: subscribers, VIPs, and moderators. Learn more about Subscriber Streams.

Priority Support

Twitch Partners have access to a dedicated support team. Visit our support portal while logged in to your Partner account, and you should receive an answer from the Partner Help team in 1-2 business days.

Twitch Partner Discord Server

Twitch Partners may join a Discord server for their geographic region, or others. Learn more.

Twitch Team Creation

Twitch Partners may create their own Twitch Team by requesting one through Partner Help.

Access to Partner-Only Opportunities

Partners will be considered for special promotional opportunities such as Partner Spotlights, Meet & Greets, Partner Panels, Streamer Zones, and more.

Guaranteed Video Transcodes

Partners will always have first-priority access to quality options for their channel. Quality options allow viewers to adjust the quality they view a broadcast for the best experience. While non-partnered channels receive transcodes depending on the capacity available, Partners are guaranteed transcodes for all their broadcasts.

Who qualifies

We are looking for Partners who can act as role models to the community and meet the following criteria. If you do not meet these qualifications, consider the Affiliate Program, obtainable through the Path to Affiliate achievement. You can also learn more about how to grow on Twitch via Creator Camp, the go-to strategy guide for all things Twitch.

Viewership from Front-Page Promotions, or Embeds does not count towards viewership requirements calculations.

Twitch Partnership Criteria
  • Complete the Path to Partner achievement. In addition, for the past two consecutive months prior to your application, have at least 6 individual streams that meet the minimum requirements of 75 average viewers per 30 day period.
  • Broadcast content that conforms to our Community Guidelines, Terms of Service, and DMCA Guidelines. We also consider suspension history when evaluating applications.
  • There are certain circumstances where we may accept applications outside of these criteria. Some instances may include exceptional viewership growth, or an established audience on other platforms.

Completing the Path to Partner achievement in your Dashboard will unlock a button to apply for Partnership. Please note that applying does not guarantee Partnership.

Username Change & Revert

As a Twitch Partner, you have access to two one-time username benefits through Partner Help:

  • Name Change — If you’d like to change your username and your desired name is not available through the self-service tool, the Partner Help team may be able to change it for you based on availability.
  • Name Revert — If you’d like to revert to a username you previously held on the same account, the Partner Help team may be able to restore it for you.

Both are one-time benefits — Partners may request one name change and one name revert through Partner Help.

Partner Manager

A Twitch Partner Manager supports streamers in navigating their streaming careers on Twitch by providing one-to-one support. Partner Managers are available globally, with teams offering conversations in English, Spanish, Portuguese, German, Italian, French, Japanese, and Traditional Chinese.

Working with a Partner Manager is by invitation only, with eligibility reviewed periodically based on size of a channel, languages, and countries where Partner Managers are available.

Partners can expect their Partner Manager to be a supportive guide within Twitch. A Partner Manager is not responsible for growing your channel. Twitch’s dedicated Partner Help team, available 24/7 via Live Chat or Email, ensures technical issues are addressed promptly and consistently.

If you’ve received an email letting you know your Partner Manager becomes unavailable, you will continue to receive comprehensive support through our Partner Help resources via live chat or email at any time. The Partner Help team is equipped to handle any inquiries you previously directed to your Partner Manager, including but not limited to issues regarding account/login, username changes, payment questions or front page requests.

You will also continue to receive access to regional and global programming opportunities (e.g. TwitchCon) and various marketing and promotional campaigns. Look out for our emails and invitations to sign up and express your interest. By joining our Partner Discords you can also connect and collaborate with other Partners and stay informed on the latest Twitch news and product updates and provide your feedback.

The Plus Program

The Plus Program offers two levels of enhanced subscription net revenue share rates for qualifying Affiliates and Partners: Level 1 (60/40) and Level 2 (70/30). Learn more about the Plus Program.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I request a name change through Partner Help if I haven’t tried the self-service tool first?
No. The self-service username change tool should always be your first option. Partner Help can only assist if the username you want is unavailable through the self-service tool.
Can I use both the name change and the name revert benefit?
Yes. These are two separate one-time benefits — you can request one name change and one name revert. However, each can only be used once.
Can I revert to a username I held on a different account?
We do not allow name swaps between accounts. However, if you currently hold a username on another account and would like to have it on your Partner account, the Partner Help team may be able to assist you in reserving it. Please contact Partner Help with the details of both accounts.
What if the username I want is taken by an inactive account?
Partner Help may be able to assist based on availability, but there is no guarantee. Usernames held by other accounts — even inactive ones — may not always be released.
What is a Partner Manager?
A Twitch Partner Manager supports streamers in navigating their streaming careers on Twitch by providing one-to-one support.
How can I work with a Partner Manager?
Working with a Partner Manager is by invitation only, with eligibility reviewed periodically based on size of a channel, languages, and countries where Partner Managers are available. We can’t share specific qualification criteria as these are subject to change.
How often are Partners considered to work with Partner Managers?
Partner Managers review their portfolios of accounts twice each year and we aim to assign a Partner Manager for a minimum period of 6 months. We will periodically make it possible for you to express your interest in working with a Partner Manager, and invite you when you’re eligible to participate. We will make sure to notify you by Email and on Twitch so you don’t miss out.
What happens when I’m notified I no longer have a Partner Manager?
If you’ve received an email letting you know your Partner Manager becomes unavailable, you will continue to receive comprehensive support through our Partner Help resources via live chat or email at any time.
What subscription revenue share do Partners receive?
The Plus Program offers two levels of enhanced subscription net revenue share rates for qualifying Affiliates and Partners: Level 1 (60/40) and Level 2 (70/30). This enhanced net revenue for subscriptions is earned in connection with recurring monthly subscriptions and gift subs.

Purchase Support

About Twitch Invoices

After a successful purchase, your receipt or transaction ID is sent to your email. For most web purchases, this email is the email associated with your Twitch account. For in-app purchases, check the email address associated with your respective app store.

Your billing and payment information is private. Only you can see your billing details. Streamers only see your username when you subscribe or make a purchase, unless you purchase gift subscriptions anonymously.

Identify or change the email associated to your Twitch account in your Security & Privacy settings here: twitch.tv/settings/security

  • Bits Purchase Issues
  • Subscriptions Purchase Issues

Providing Feedback

How can we improve Twitch’s purchase management? Let us know in UserVoice here.

Locating Your Invoice For a Web Purchase

Successful web purchases generate an invoice that is sent to the email associated with your Twitch account. In most cases, searching your email inbox for the name of the streamer you contributed towards will locate your most recent invoices.

If you are not sure the email inbox that your purchase was sent to, you can review your purchase history to see what payment method was used.

Locating Your Invoice For a Mobile Purchase

Twitch purchases made on Twitch iOS Apps are managed in their respective App Stores.

Successful mobile purchases generate an invoice that is sent to the email associated with your App Store account. For the Twitch App for Android, check the email address associated with your Google Play account. For the Twitch App for iOS, check the email address associated with your iOS account.

Correcting or Updating Your Billing Information

Twitch invoice details, such as billing information, are retrieved from the details of your credit card or other payment method at time of purchase. If you receive a Twitch invoice with outdated information such as legal name or billing information, the invoice cannot be resent or altered. To change this billing information for future purchases, update your billing information with the payment method used for this purchase.

In some cases, you may need to cancel your active subscription and re-subscribe to apply billing information changes made through your payment method. If you add a billing instrument to a payment platform such as Amazon Pay or PayPal, you may need to contact these companies to complete this change.

Learn more about updating your payment information here.

About Other Payment Systems

Twitch accepts payments from services including PayPal, Xsolla, Amazon Pay, and others. You may receive a transaction ID directly from these services that is separate from, or references your Twitch invoice ID.

What Does an Invoice ID Look Like?

Depending on the payment method used, invoice IDs will have different formats:

  • Google Play invoice IDs begin with “GPA.” followed by groups of numbers and letters separated by dashes (example: GPA.1234-5678-9012-34567)
  • Apple invoice IDs are alphanumeric (example: MSXH6MDFH4)
  • PayPal and credit card invoice IDs will consist of a series of numbers
  • Amazon Pay and Xsolla invoice IDs may appear in transaction confirmations from those services

If your invoice ID doesn’t match these formats, check your email for any transaction confirmation and contact support with the details you have.

More Resources

For questions on completing purchases on Twitch, visit our Purchase Support FAQ

For information on how to update your payment information, visit our guide here.

Failed Payments for Subscriptions

We understand it can be frustrating to face a payment error when trying to purchase subscriptions or support your favorite creators. This article addresses billing and payment processing issues for Twitch purchases. Below are common resolution steps for problems completing purchases on Twitch.

Frequently Asked Questions

Have you been making frequent purchases?
Some banks will attempt to limit the frequency of your spending online. If you are having difficulties, and if all else fails, please contact your bank to see if there are any issues.
Refresh the page and try to complete your purchase again
You may have experienced a temporary problem that has now been resolved.
Review the details of your chosen payment method
Have your personal details been entered correctly, or have they changed? Does your payment method match your country of residence? Are you using a VPN, that may be interrupting your connection to Twitch?
I was charged, but I did not get a subscription!
In some cases, you might see a delayed fulfillment of the item you purchased. In order to verify that your subscription is active, you can visit twitch.tv/subscriptions to see all current and expired subscriptions. You can also check if you have access to subscriber benefits, such as the subscriber badge. A streamer’s channel configuration can affect the viewing experience and the benefits enjoyed by subscribers.

If you were charged and did not receive any subscriber benefits, please Contact Support

You can also update your payment method from your subscriptions page, or from the Manage Your Sub button on impacted channel(s).

If you have another payment method available, select Change Payment Method to try it.
This can help determine if the problem is with one payment method or provider, or if it is a larger issue.
Try to complete the purchase with your same payment method in a different browser or incognito / private browsing window.
This can help narrow down if your browser’s cookies/cache are causing a problem.
Double-check that your bank is able to complete the purchase.
Ensure that your bank account has enough funds or that you have not exceeded some spending limit. (You may need to contact your banking institution directly).
Delete and re-add your payment method. (This is different than changing existing payment methods)
  • This can be done through PayPal here.
  • This can be done through Amazon Pay here.

If you are deleting a saved credit card on Twitch you can do this at twitch.tv/payments (note you may first need to cancel any recurring subscriptions that rely on this payment method)

Delete your billing agreement with your purchase provider (such as Amazon Pay or PayPal) through the provider’s website. Attempt your purchase again.
  • This can be done through PayPal here.
  • This can be done through Amazon Pay here.
What is a billing agreement?
Essentially, your billing agreement is a handshake that authorizes a payment system such as PayPal and Amazon Pay to complete purchases on your behalf on Twitch each time you complete a purchase. If you’ve ever logged into PayPal or confirmed your PayPal details before completing a payment on Twitch, you “agree” that Twitch may bill these companies on your behalf. Removing that agreement, then going through the purchase flow again can sometimes resolve purchase issues.

While you’re here…

Have you secured your Twitch account with 2FA? You can earn cool emotes, and more importantly, keep your account secure.

If you believe that you have been hacked or experiencing fraud, please contact Twitch Support immediately here.

Still having issues?

We’re here to help! Our team is available to help you troubleshoot any further billing issues that you may be having. Contact Twitch Support here. Please include any troubleshooting steps that you have attempted.

How to Purchase Bits

This article walks through how and where to purchase Bits on desktop and mobile.

Purchase Bits on Web Browser

Click the bits icon in the chat window of any Cheer-enabled channel.

Web browser users may also visit twitch.tv/bits.

Select the bundle of Bits you wish to purchase. Larger bundles offer a better value per Bit.

After you’ve made your selection, double check your order details. You can change your payment method, adjust bundle quantity, or use your Twitch Gift Card balance to purchase Bits.

After completing your purchase, your Bits will be added to your Bits total balance.

The receipt from your purchase will be sent to the email you have on file with Twitch. You may begin using your new Bits right away!

For help Updating Payment Information, visit our help article.

Visit the Bits Purchase Troubleshooting Guide for help resolving payment errors.

Twitch Mobile Apps & Third-Party Software

Payments for Bits on Twitch mobile apps are processed by the Google Play Store or the Apple App store. Due to this, additional platform processing fees may be applied to the purchase and lead to a higher price for Bits purchases on mobile apps. You have the option to purchase bits at web browser prices on your mobile device by going to bits.twitch.tv in your mobile web browser or by visiting twitch.tv on a web browser.

To purchase Bits on mobile devices, follow the same steps as Purchasing Bits on a web browser. Please note that your invoice will be sent to you via your mobile device.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why didn’t I get my Bits? In most cases, refreshing your web page or mobile app after experiencing a fulfillment delay will resolve the issue. For detailed Bits purchase troubleshooting help, visit our help article.I was charged more than once for my Bits purchase.
If you experience a fulfillment delay after your first Bits purchase, try not to complete it again! Please also make sure that your second payment is not a pending payment (which calls off in 3-5 business days). If you require further assistance, please contact Twitch Support here.
Why was my payment declined? In most cases, attempting another payment method can resolve this issue. For Bits purchase troubleshooting help, visit our help article.Why don’t I see a Bits button on the channel I want to support?
If a channel does not have this button, it’s likely they are not a monetized streamer. You can tell a channel is a monetized streamer if they have a Subscribe button under their video player.
I bought Bits, but don’t want them. Can I get a refund?
No. There are no refunds for Bits purchases unless it is mandated by law. Limited exceptions apply. For more, visit our help article.
Where can I see my Bits History?
You can review your Bits purchase history, Cheering, and other Bits actions in your Twitch Wallet. Use the “Location” drop-down to toggle between your on-site and Extensions Bits actions.

How to Subscribe

Our subscription options let monetized streamers reward and interact with their audience. Some of the benefits for subscribers are: access to custom emotes that can be used across all of Twitch; Subscriber Badges, which can change with your tenure if the channel has set up loyalty badges; and other perks we allow Creators to enable like ad-free viewing. Subscription benefits are selected by streamers, and may change or be canceled at any time.

Your billing and payment information is private. Only you can see your billing details. Streamers only see your username when you subscribe or make a purchase, unless you purchase gift subscriptions anonymously.

When you resubscribe to any channel or subscribe for the first time with your Prime subscription, a Share button will appear at the top of chat. This button will allow you to send a customized message to the broadcaster and trigger any alerts that they have set up.

How to Subscribe with Prime

With Prime, you have a channel subscription which can be used on any monetized channel at no cost. Click the Subscribe button on a channel to begin.

Need to connect your accounts? If you’re having trouble accessing your Prime subscription, you may need to link your Amazon and Twitch accounts. See our How to Link Your Amazon and Twitch Accounts guide for help.

Prime Trial members (including Prime Student) may be eligible to receive a free Twitch channel subscription during their no-cost free trial, depending on their region. This is a one-time perk. If you’ve used a Prime Trial previously, you aren’t eligible to receive a Twitch channel subscription during subsequent no-cost Trials. Availability and benefits vary by region—refer to your Prime membership terms for details.

If you are not currently enrolled in Prime, you will see a shortcut to start your trial at the bottom of the subscription window.

Existing Prime members will instead see a checkbox that will allow them to apply their sub towards the current channel.

If you do not have a Prime Subscription available yet, the button will be grayed out showing the date when it next can be used.

Learn more about Prime Subscriptions here.

How to Subscribe with Payment

Click Tier 1, Tier 2, or Tier 3 to choose which price/tier to subscribe at.

Subscriptions are a monthly recurring product that can be purchased with Credit / Debit cards, Twitch Gift Cards, PayPal, Amazon Pay and various local payment options, such as paysafecard via Xsolla. Payment Methods offered are subject to regional availability.

However, if you click More Methods beside the payment options at checkout, you can pay for 1 month, 3 month, or even 6 month increments.

See More Methods will allow you to also choose from a wide range of Xsolla options, including Apple Pay, bank transfer, paysafecard, and digital cryptocurrency depending on your region.

When you click Complete Purchase you will be able to verify the final amount that we will charge your payment method which may include tax in some locations. If you have a Gift Card Balance in your Wallet then we will automatically apply those funds for purchases that you make on twitch.tv website. You will need to have a saved payment method, in order to be able to spend with your Gift Card Balance.

Upon a successful purchase you will be notified and your payment method will be saved for automatic subscription renewals and any future payments.

You may manage your saved payment methods at any time through your Payment Management page. Keeping an active payment method will mean we can have it ready for you to make any additional subscription purchases a much quicker process.

For more information on your Payment Management page please see our article on it here.

Depending on where you live, the price of a subscription may vary. To learn more about local subscription prices, please see our help article.

After you have added a payment method to Twitch, you can get back to the stream as quickly as possible by using 1-click checkout to complete your purchases, if available in your region.

Subscribing through Mobile Devices

Information and guidance on how to subscribe through your mobile devices can be found on our Subscriptions on Mobile article.

iOS users: Save 25% by purchasing through our external browser instead of the iOS or Android app.

Subscribing through subs.twitch.tv

Subscribing to your favorite streamer through mobile and desktop has never been easier than now with subs.twitch.tv.

When you visit subs.twitch.tv on a mobile or desktop web browser, you can use the search bar to search for specific streamers. If you’re logged in, you’ll also see a list of monetized streamers you follow. Clicking on any of the channels presented will take you to their respective subscription page where you can complete the subscription process.

Once you are done selecting your chosen channel, you can either use your Prime subscription or choose a Tier (Tier 1, Tier 2 or Tier 3). If choosing a tier, you will be presented with available payment methods. Select the payment method you wish to use to purchase the subscription with and follow the on-screen instructions presented to you.

Monetized streamers can link to their subscription page easily by simply replacing “channel” in the following URL with their channel name: subs.twitch.tv channel. This link can be posted on social media, or anywhere the streamer would like to promote subscriptions. The link works across mobile devices and desktop.

Tier 2 and Tier 3 Subscription Benefits

Purchasing a Tier 2 or Tier 3 subscription comes with a number of benefits for both you and the channel you subscribe to. The additional benefits that may be offered by a channel for a Tier 2/Tier 3 subscription are listed on the Higher Tiers section shown when purchasing a subscription. Subscription benefits are selected by streamers, and may change or be canceled at any time.

Emotes

A Tier 2 or Tier 3 subscription will give you access to additional emotes providing they have been added by the channel. All Partners have 5 additional emote slots at Tier 2 and Tier 3, while all other monetized streamers have 1 additional emote slot on Tier 2 and Tier 3.

GIF Keyboard

In channels where the streamer has GIF keyboard enabled, Tier 2 and Tier 3 paid subscribers can search for and send GIF messages in chat using the GIF keyboard. Learn more about the GIF keyboard on Twitch.

Badge Flair

For channels with badge flair enabled, Tier 2 and Tier 3 subscribers will receive a special flair overlaid on top of their subscriber badge. If badge flair is enabled on a channel, you’ll be able to see a preview of your subscriber badge with a badge flair when reviewing the benefits of a Tier 2 or Tier 3 subscription.

To disable your badge flair at any time, head to any channel and click the Chat Identity button on the left-hand side of the chat box.

Under the Channel Badges section, you can toggle badge flair on and off globally for all channels you subscribe to.

Modified Emotes

Subscribing to Partnered channels gives you access to emote modifiers providing they’ve been enabled by the channel. Modifiers include fun effects like horizontally flipping an emote, or adding sunglasses. Modifiers are chosen by the channel and any emote with an available modifier will be shown with a small black triangle in the bottom right-hand corner of the emote in the emote picker (accessed by clicking the smiley face in the bottom right-hand corner of the chat window). Hovering your mouse cursor over an emote will show the available modifiers.

Multi-Month Subscriptions

We offer subscriptions that recur at various intervals. Our default subscription recurs every month and you are charged on a monthly basis to keep your subscription to the streamer you are supporting. For multi-month subscriptions, you are charged every 3 or 6 months (whichever plan you choose) until you choose Cancel Subscription. This option can be found by clicking on the settings cog of the relevant subscription on your Subscriptions page.

You can select the frequency of your subscription charges in the subscription window and complete your checkout as you would with a standard, monthly subscription.

For more information about multi-month subscriptions, please see our FAQ.

Frequently Asked Questions

General Questions
I currently subscribe to a channel at Tier 1. How do I switch over to Tier 2 or Tier 3? Do I need to wait till the end of my subscription cycle?
You can switch over by going to the channel page, clicking the green Subscribed button in the upper right corner, and selecting your new option. You do not need to wait till the end of the cycle, but there is no proration. You will be charged the new amount immediately, and will not receive any refund for the remainder of the Tier 1 if your subscription month is not over.
I subscribe to a channel using a Prime Subscription. Can I switch over to Tier 2 or Tier 3, and how? Do I need to wait till the end of my subscription cycle?
You can switch from the Prime Subscription at any time by going to the channel page, clicking the green Subscribed button in the upper right corner, and selecting your new option. You do not need to wait till the end of the subscription cycle, but you will not get another subscription to use until the following month.
Where can I see my currently active subscriptions?
You can see a list of all your currently active subscriptions on your subscriptions page which can be found at: twitch.tv.
Where can I see expired subscriptions?
You can see a list of your most recent 100 inactive subscriptions on your subscriptions page, under expired subscriptions: twitch.tv.
I purchased a subscription but I don’t see it as active on my account, what do I do?
Don’t panic, some payment methods can take a little longer to process than others. If you don’t see your subscription activated within 5 minutes please reach out to our purchase support team by opening a ticket and selecting your issue as Purchases > Subscriptions > Purchase not received.

Make sure to log in at the top of the ticket submission page to ensure we have all of the information required to assist you.

I’m not from the US, will I be charged in USD?
We now support localized pricing and will attempt to charge you in your local currency.
How do I use my Gift Card Balance to make a purchase?
If you have a Gift Card Balance in your Wallet then we will automatically apply those funds for purchases that you make on twitch.tv website. If the cost of your purchase exceeds your Gift Card Balance, we will charge the additional amount to your saved payment method. If you do not have a saved payment method then you will be prompted to add one.
In which countries will I be able to subscribe using Twitch’s Android app?
Albania, Australia, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, India, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Morocco, Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Russian Federation, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Korea, Spain, Sweden, Taiwan, United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, United States of America, Hong Kong, Japan, Brazil, Mexico, Bahrain, Canada, Georgia, Indonesia, Iraq, Kuwait, Liechtenstein, Morocco, Myanmar, Malaysia, Philippines, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, Thailand, Turkey, South Africa, Rwanda, Gabon, Argentina, Colombia, Chile, Costa Rica
In which countries will I be able to subscribe using Twitch’s iOS app?
Afghanistan, Albania, Argentina, Austria, Australia, Belgium, Bulgaria, Brazil, Canada, Switzerland, Chile, China, Costa Rica, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Germany, Denmark, Estonia, Spain, Finland, France, United Kingdom, Greece, Hong Kong, Croatia, Hungary, Indonesia, Ireland, India, Iceland, Italy, Japan, South Korea, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Latvia, Malta, Mexico, Netherlands, Norway, New Zealand, Philippines, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Saudi Arabia, Sweden, Singapore, Slovenia, Slovakia, Thailand, Taiwan, United States, South Africa.
Why should iOS users subscribe through the external browser instead of the app?
iOS users can save 25% by subscribing through the external browser instead of the iOS app, while receiving the same subscription benefits.
Multi-Month Subscription Questions
Do multi-month subscriptions recur?
Yes. Just like single month subscriptions, they automatically renew at the end of the subscription interval (every 3 or 6 months) unless you choose to Cancel Subscription under the settings cog for that subscription on your Subscriptions page.
How often am I charged for a multi-month subscription?
You are charged every 3 months for 3 month subscriptions and every 6 months for 6 month subscriptions.
Does the streamer see all 3 or 6 months that I paid for up front?
No, they will see the revenue listed monthly over the course of 3 or 6 months. For example, if you were to purchase a 3 month multi-month subscription in May, the streamer would see the revenue for your subscription once each month in May, June and July.
How do discounts for multi-month subscriptions work?
Multi-month subscriptions with recurring discounts will renew at the original, discounted price. Multi-month discounts that are non-recurring will only have the discount applied to the first recurrence (first 3 or 6 months) of a subscription. When the subscription automatically renews, it will renew at the full price. In both cases, a cancelled recurring subscription will be eligible for the discount when repurchased at a later date.
I just purchased a multi-month subscription but now I want to upgrade to a higher tier. How do I do that?
Head to your Subscriptions page, click the Settings icon and select Change Subscription Tier. Alternatively, click the Gift a Sub button on the relevant channel and scroll down to Your Subscription to select and purchase your new tier. Please note that this purchase would be in addition to your existing multi month subscription.
I currently have a monthly subscription but I want to purchase a multi-month subscription. How do I do that?
On your Subscriptions page, click the Settings icon for the subscription you would like to modify and select Cancel Subscription. Then, choose to continue your subscription for multiple months at a time. You will be charged at the new rate when your current subscription benefits expire if you’ve continued at the current tier. If you’ve upgraded to a higher tier, you will be immediately charged for your new benefits.
I currently have a Prime/Gift sub to the channel, how do I purchase a multi-month subscription?
You can select Continue Sub and select the tier you would like to continue your sub at. You will be charged at the new rate when your current subscription benefits expire if you’ve continued at the current tier. If you’ve upgraded to a higher tier, you will be immediately charged for your new benefits.

How to Update Payment Information and View Transaction History

This article provides an overview of how to update your existing payment information for web purchases and view a history of your previous transactions.

Your billing and payment information is private. Only you can see your billing details. Streamers only see your username when you subscribe or make a purchase, unless you purchase gift subscriptions anonymously.

You must access Twitch on a web (or mobile) browser to manage these settings.

If you’re looking for your Twitch invoices, click here.

On this page:

  • Existing Payment Management
  • Adding a Payment Method
  • Deleting your Payment Information
  • Payment and Bits Usage History
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Existing Payment Management

To begin, head over to your Wallet page by clicking your Profile icon in the top right hand corner and selecting Wallet from the menu. Once there you will see a list of your current payment methods and a list of the subscriptions currently utilizing those payment methods.

If you have never made a purchase before on Twitch and are trying to add a payment method on the Wallet page, please instead add a payment method during checkout of your desired product. It is not possible to manage payment methods on Twitch without associating that payment method to a specific purchase.

Once you update the payment method, all of the subscriptions renewing under the previous payment method will now be charged to the new one.

Most payment methods can be managed and updated via this page using the Update Payment Info button next to the payment method. Other payment methods may require you to manage them via an alternative page provided by the payment provider.

For iOS/Android app subscriptions, you can update payment methods via your Apple App Store or Google Play settings.

Adding a Payment Method

If you have never made a purchase before on Twitch, you must first add a new payment method during checkout of your desired product.

To add a payment method during checkout, select the product you wish to purchase, at which time you will be prompted to select your preferred payment method from credit / debit card, Amazon Pay, Apple Pay and PayPal. You may also select “See More Methods” at this stage for additional options.

Not seeing your preferred payment method? Select “See More Methods” during checkout to view all available payment options for your region.

If you have used Xsolla to make purchases on Twitch, you may add a payment method to Xsolla at any time via your Payment Management page. To get started, click the “Manage With Xsolla” button and select your preferred payment method from credit / debit card, Amazon Pay, PayPal, with many more options available.

Deleting your Payment Information

You may delete a payment method at any time from your Wallet page by selecting Delete on the desired payment method. Other payment methods may require you to manage them via an alternative page provided by the payment provider.

Please note that by deleting a payment method you will be cancelling further renewals of all subscriptions under that payment method. An alternative would be to update your payment method with one that is preferred thus allowing your subscription renewals to remain unaffected.

Payment and Bits Usage History

This page cannot be accessed on the Twitch Mobile app. Please use Twitch on a desktop computer.

On the Payment History tab you can filter your transactions by date by using the Start and End fields in the top left-hand corner above the table. Clicking Date or Amount at the top of the table will sort the results by the chosen category.

If you see any purchases that you do not recognize, or if you believe that your account may have been compromised, we recommend immediately reviewing this account security article.

You can also check your Bits usage history by clicking the Bits Usage History tab. Here, you’ll see the channel on which you used your Bits, the amount used, and when. To filter your Bits usage history by date, use the Start and End fields in the top left-hand corner above the table. Clicking Date or Amount at the top of the table will sort the results by the chosen category.

Toggle between On-Site and Extension usage on the top right hand corner to filter for the according usage of your Bits.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is it possible to change checkout currency?
It is not possible to change, set, or swap checkout currency on Twitch. Checkout currency is set via an automatic process that references information about your payment method. To ensure you’re billed in the correct currency, add a locally issued credit or debit card to your Twitch account, and choose that payment method during checkout.
How can I change my billing information shown in Twitch invoices?
It is not possible to alter billing information in your Twitch invoice after a purchase is made. To change the billing address shown in your Twitch invoice for future purchases, use a different payment method or update your billing information with your banking institution.

Twitch invoices receive your billing information from the payment method used for the purchase in question, at the time the purchase is made. You may need to remove and re-add the payment method from Twitch before new billing information is shown in your invoice.

In some cases, Twitch may receive your billing information from online payment systems like PayPal or Amazon Pay. Please update your billing information in those systems before completing a purchase on Twitch.

Where is my invoice sent after a successful purchase?
After a successful purchase, your receipt or transaction ID is sent to your email. For most web purchases, this email is the email associated with your Twitch account. For in-app purchases, check the email address associated with your respective app store. Learn more.
I am having issues adding or updating my payment method — what can I do?
For a step-by-step troubleshooting guide, please see our help article on Failed Payments for Subscriptions.

Managing Multi-Month Subscriptions

By default, subscription renewal is monthly. However, as you have recently upgraded or modified your sub, you can extend your renewal period to every 3 or 6-months.

For your convenience, you can purchase multiple months of subscriptions in advance for yourself or another user through gift subs. Multi-month subscriptions offer a discount of 10% off 3-months and 15% off 6-months subscriptions.

Special promotional/limited-time multi-month discounts that are non-recurring, like SUBtember, for example, will only have the discount applied to the first recurrence (first 3 or 6 months) of a subscription. When the subscription automatically renews, it will renew at the standard full price with the regular multi-month discount (10% for 3 months, 15% for 6 months). In both cases, a cancelled recurring subscription will be eligible for the standard discount when repurchased at a later date.

Purchasing Multi-Month Subscriptions

New subscribers can select their renewal period (1, 3, and 6-months) during checkout. Your Total will reflect your multi-month discount.

Purchasing a multi-month subscription does not award subscription tenure rewards such as chat badges in advance.

Check out our Purchasing Gift Subscriptions article to learn more about purchasing multi-month subscriptions for others!

Managing Multi-Month Subscriptions

Subscriptions renew monthly by default. As long as you have yet to recently upgrade or modify your sub, upgrading to a higher recurring period is easy without interrupting your experience.

You can extend your subscription renewal period in two places:

From the Support Panel
  • Visit the corresponding channel page.
  • Click Manage My Sub.
  • Choose from renewal options of every 3 or 6-months.
  • You may also change subscription Tier (Tier 2 or Tier 3) at this time if you choose.
  • Click Update Subscription.

Don’t see the recurral period upgrade menu when you click Manage My Sub? Check out the FAQ.

From the Subscriptions Management Page
  • Visit your Subscriptions page.
  • Identify the subscription in question.
  • Click Continue Sub.

Don’t see Continue Sub on your desired subscription? Check out the FAQ.

Completing Your Purchase

After selecting a renewal period update, you will come to the checkout page. Carefully review the details of your purchase. Once you click Agree & Subscribe, this information is unavailable again before billing.

You will not be charged today. No digital record is sent to you for this future-dated invoice, so it is critical to note the information presented during checkout.

After you have added a payment method to Twitch, you can get back to the stream as quickly as possible by using 1-click checkout to complete your purchases.

Future Billing Date

You may wish to review details of your upcoming charge. View the future date your changes will take place in two places:

From the Support Panel
  • Visit the corresponding channel page.
  • Click Manage My Sub.
  • Note the Sub Expires date.

The Sub Expires date does not indicate an unsuccessful update. Instead, the Sub Expires date refers to when your previous renewal terms expire. Therefore, if you have initiated an update, it will occur after this date.

For example, if you previously had a monthly recurring subscription, that subscription will “expire” on Aug 29. Charges for your “new” 3 or 6-months subscription will occur on Aug 29. There is no risk to your sub-streak in this seamless process.

From the Subscriptions Management Page
  • Visit your Subscriptions page.
  • Identify the subscription in question.
  • Note the Recurring Sub continues date.

Your new recurring subscription will be charged on this date. It should match the Sub Expires date in the Support Panel of the corresponding channel in the previous point.

These locations are the only place to track your future billing date. There is no place to track your future billing amount, duration (3 or 6-months), or billing instrument. So, be sure to take note of this at time of upgrade to avoid surprises.

Lowering Your Renewal Period

Make changes to your renewal period at any time before the date you are charged (Sub Expires date or Recurring Sub continues date). Review the prior section to find this date.

To make changes to your renewal period, visit your Subscriptions page and locate the subscription in question. Click the cogwheel icon, and select Don’t Renew Subscription.

This action will update your subscription with a Canceled On date, and a Benefits Expire On date.

Do nothing at this point, and your subscription benefits will expire on the Benefits Expire On date. To resume your benefits and adjust your desired recurral period, click Continue Sub.

If you’d like to make changes to your subscription tier at this time check out our Managing Subscription Tiers article.

Frequently Asked Questions

How often do multi-month subscriptions renew?
While a single-month subscription renews monthly, a multi-month subscription automatically renews at the end of your chosen subscription interval (3 or 6-months).
What payment options are available for upgrading or extending a multi-month subscription?
Checkout for upgrading or extending a multi-month sub is the same as making any other purchase on Twitch.
How will I be billed for multi-month subscriptions?
You will be billed for all months purchased up front.
I got an email informing me that my subscription will be renewing soon. Why am I being charged the wrong price or more?
Depending on the payment provider/method selected, your renewal notice may not reflect the 10% / 15% multi-month discount price. Check your billing statement once you are charged — if there are any concerns or questions, Contact Support.

Special promotional/limited-time multi-month discounts (e.g., SUBtember) apply only to the first recurrence (first 3 or 6 months). Upon auto-renewal, subscriptions renew at standard full price with regular multi-month discounts (10% for 3 months, 15% for 6 months). Cancelled recurring subscriptions remain eligible for standard discounts when repurchased later.

How do I gift multiple months of subscription to a specific viewer?
Select Gift a Sub and then Gift to a specific viewer. You may select the number of months to give a specific user from 1, 3, 6, and 12-months. Learn more about Gifting Subscriptions by checking out our Purchasing Gift Subscriptions article.
Does the streamer receive revenue up front from all 3 or 6-months that I paid?
No, creators receive this revenue monthly over time. For example, if you were to purchase 3 months of subscription in May, the streamer would receive revenue for your subscription once each month in May, June and July.
Can I purchase multi-month subscriptions through the Twitch Mobile App?
You can learn more about subscriptions on mobile devices with our Subscriptions on Mobile article.
Who is eligible to receive a multi-month single gift?
Anyone without an active subscription in a given channel is eligible to receive a multi-month sub gift. Find out more about Gifted Subscriptions at our Purchasing Gift Subscriptions article.
I forgot about my renewal. Can I get a refund?
While we don’t allow refunds in most cases, you can refer to our refund guidelines. You may be applicable to request a refund.
Does increasing my renewal grant me additional tenure?
Tenure is accumulated as time passes, not in advance. Buying a 3 or 6-month subscription does not add +3 or +6 to your tenure or sub streak.

Managing Subscription Tiers

Upgrade your subscription from Tier 1 to Tier 2 or Tier 3 without canceling your existing subscription on web.

Subscription Tier upgrades are charged immediately, unlike Gift-to-Paid, Prime-to-Paid, or renewal period updates, which charge at the end of your billing period.

Twitch doesn’t pro-rate Subscription Tier upgrades: you pay the full price of your new Tier on the day you upgrade. As a result, it is always more cost-effective to cancel your existing subscription, then upgrade Tiers once your benefits expire.

Choosing A Subscription Tier

Subscription Tier benefits are configured by the individual streamer. Learn more about Subscription Tier benefits.

Tier 2 and Tier 3 subscribers gain access to additional benefits such as extra emotes, badge flair, modified emotes, and GIF Keyboard (in channels where the streamer has this feature enabled).

Raising Your Subscription Tier

As long as you have not upgraded or modified your sub recently, it’s easy to upgrade to higher tiers without interrupting your experience. You can raise your subscription Tier in 2 places. Each requires different steps:

From the Support Panel
  • Visit the corresponding channel page
  • Click Manage Your Sub.
  • Under Sub tier, choose Tier 2 Subscription or Tier 3 Subscription. Review What happens next? to see what you’ll pay today and when your new plan renews.
  • You can change the recurral period (every 3 or 6 months) at this step as well.
  • Click Update Subscription, choose your payment method, and click Complete Purchase.

Visit the FAQ if you don’t see the Tier upgrade menu when you click Manage Your Sub.

From the Subscriptions Management Page.
  • Visit your Subscriptions Management page
  • You will be brought to the subs page for the channel: twitch.tv.
  • Identify the subscription in question.
  • Click the Settings icon.
  • Select Change Subscription Tier
  • Select Go above and beyond, and choose your desired Tier upgrade.

Not seeing Change Subscription Tier? Visit the FAQ.

Completing Your Purchase

You will be brought to checkout after selecting a Tier upgrade. Carefully review the details of your purchase before you click Complete Purchase.

You will be charged the day of the upgrade.

A Purchase Successful screen lists your new benefits. Close it when you’re done.

Your new sub benefits are yours to enjoy right away. You now have two sub cards side-by-side, one at your new (higher) Tier, and one at the previous Tier.

You’ll get two emails: a receipt for your new Tier, and a cancellation confirmation for your previous Tier. Your previous Tier won’t renew, but its benefits continue until the end of its billing period.

Subscription benefits are selected by streamers, and may change or be canceled at any time.

Enjoy!

Lowering Your Subscription Tier

You cannot lower your Subscription Tier without setting the subscription to cancel. Once your benefits have expired, you can subscribe again at a lower Tier.

Mid-cycle upgrades create two side-by-side cards in Subscriptions Management. Cancel your subscription via Settings icon of leftmost (or higher Tier) subscription.

Managing Tiers Between Platforms

Subscriptions purchased in the Twitch app on iOS and Android are managed in the app, not on web. You can upgrade a mobile subscription from Tier 1 to Tier 2, or from Tier 2 to Tier 3, in the app. Upgrades take effect immediately, and you’ll receive a prorated refund or discount toward the new tier. You can’t downgrade a mobile subscription to a lower tier.

If you’d rather manage your subscription to a channel on web, set your mobile subscription to cancel. The benefits must expire completely before you can purchase a subscription to that channel on web.

Frequently Asked Questions

What payment options are available for upgrading or extending a Multi-Month subscription?
Checkout for upgrading or extending a Multi-Month Sub is the same as making any other purchase on Twitch.
I upgraded my subscription. Why did I get a cancellation email?
When you upgrade, your previous Tier is set to not renew, so you’ll get a cancellation confirmation for it along with a receipt for your new Tier. Your previous Tier’s benefits continue until the end of its billing period. You don’t need to do anything.
I clicked Manage Your Sub on the channel’s page to upgrade my sub Tier. I see this screen instead. What gives?

Upgrading Subscription Tier is easy, if you have not recently made changes to your subscription. If you see this screen when you click Manage Your Sub, you may have recently made changes.

Visit your Subscriptions Management page and review the sub in question. The Sub Expires date should match your Recurring sub begins date.

You cannot make further changes to your subscription until your current billing period expires (and your pending upgrades are billed) OR you cancel the pending subscription upgrades. Cancel your pending upgrade if you would like to immediately complete a Subscription Tier upgrade.

I clicked the Settings icon on my sub in Subscriptions Management, but I don’t see options to Change Subscription Tier. Why is that?
This can happen for a variety of reasons:
  • Are you trying to upgrade the subscription Tier of a pending Gift Sub upgrade? If so, you must wait for the Gift Sub to expire, and your paid recurring subscription to begin before you can make changes to your Subscription Tier. Learn more.
  • You already committed to a pending sub upgrade. You can only have one pending sub upgrade at once. You’ll know this is the case if you see Cancel Recurring Subscription under the Settings icon instead of Change Subscription Tier. To make your desired subscription Tier upgrade, cancel your recurring subscription.
  • You may have already completed a Tier 3 subscription. If you already have a Tier 3 subscription, you must set this subscription to cancel to make further subscription Tier changes. You’ll know if you did this previously because subscription upgrades appear side-by-side with your prior upgrade if you made your upgrade during your billing cycle.
  • You are trying to manage a subscription purchased in the Twitch mobile app. Upgrade it in the app instead.
Does the streamer receive revenue up front from all 3 or 6 months that I paid?
No, creators receive this revenue monthly over time. For example, if you were to purchase 3 months of subscription in May, the streamer would receive revenue for your subscription once each month in May, June and July.
Why doesn’t my tenure or anniversary increase when my Tier subscription rolls over?
Subscription tenure is based on time past, not time purchased or Subscription Tier purchased.
I set my Tier 2 or Tier 3 subscription to cancel. Why can’t I complete a purchase of a Tier 1 subscription?
You must wait for the date that your Tier 2 or Tier 3 subscription expires before you can make further changes.
I started my subscription on mobile. How can I upgrade my subscription Tier?
Upgrade it in the Twitch app on iOS or Android. Upgrades take effect immediately, and you’ll receive a prorated refund or discount toward the new tier. Mobile subscriptions can’t be upgraded on web, and you can’t downgrade a mobile subscription to a lower tier.
I forgot about my renewal. Can I get a refund?
While we don’t allow refunds in most cases, you can refer to our refund guidelines.

Purchase Support Guide

If you are having an issue with, or have a general inquiry regarding subscriptions, the Twitch Support team is here to help. We understand that users want a hassle free purchase experience and we strive to provide that.

For more information, please read the Twitch Terms of Sale from the Twitch Terms of Service which apply to your use of and purchases made through Twitch.

You can contact us anytime via our contact form. When contacting us, please state in your email what the problem is and try to include as much useful information as possible, such as your on-site username and any related transaction or invoice IDs from your email receipt for the purchase you need help with. Please note that we are unable to use Amazon Pay and Paypal Transaction ID’s to locate purchases but rather only the specific Invoice/Order ID included within the email receipt from Twitch.

When contacting us about a bug or error related to purchases, please provide a screenshot of the problem and/or error message so that we can investigate the issue as quickly and effectively as possible.

Below is a summary of frequently asked questions regarding purchases and subscriptions. If your question is not answered in the FAQs below, please get in touch!

On this page:

  • General Subscription FAQ
  • Purchases and Payments FAQ

General Subscription FAQ

How do channel subscriptions work? Are subscriptions a one-time or recurring payment?
Many Twitch channel subscriptions are recurring monthly charges that will be billed in advance for the following month. On the checkout page for a subscription, you’ll be provided with information about the price and its renewal frequency. For some subscriptions, you’ll also have the additional option to pay in 3 or 6 month installments.

Some subscriptions are a one time purchase. When purchasing these subscriptions, you’ll be shown the price, duration and the One-time purchase text alongside it on the checkout page.

How do I purchase a subscription on my mobile device?
Subscribing on mobile is simple. This article provides an overview of how you can support your favorite broadcasters through mobile subscriptions.
How do I cancel a subscription’s recurring monthly payment?
You may cancel your recurring monthly payment at any time by going to your Subscriptions page, locating the subscription you wish to cancel, and clicking the Cog on the right-hand side. Here, you will be able to select Don’t Renew Subscription.

Clicking on the Don’t Renew link will set your subscription to expire at the end of the currently billed period and ensure you are not billed in the next payment cycle. If applicable, your subscriber badge will still appear in that channel for the remainder of the paid period.

If you started your subscription through your Android device on Google Play or iOS device on Apple App Store, you can cancel its recurring payment by following the steps as outlined here.

What is Xsolla and why are they charging me?
Xsolla is one of our payment processors. If you have any questions regarding a payment made to them, please contact them directly via their support portal or by emailing them at support@xsolla.com.

If you have feedback regarding Xsolla, please feel free to contact us directly by using our Contact Form and choosing Purchases and the relevant subcategory under the drop-down menus.

Can I transfer my subscription to another Twitch account?
It is not possible to transfer a subscription from one account to another. This also includes transferring your subscription streak to another account.
I cancelled my subscription’s recurring payment. Will I lose my channel subscription streak / anniversary?
If you re-subscribe within 7 days of your subscription expiring you will see no break in your subscription streak / anniversary.

Purchases and Payments FAQ

I paid, but my channel subscription is not active!
Please get in touch with us so we may investigate further for you.

You can contact us directly by using our contact form and selecting Subscriptions as your issue.

Please include your invoice / transaction ID, your on-site username and the subscription you attempted to purchase.

I am being charged on an account I cannot access.
Firstly, to regain access to your account, we recommend going through our account recovery flow. Once you’ve regained access to your account (and if you haven’t done so already), we recommend enabling Two Factor Authentication. If you are unable to regain access to your account, please get in touch so we may assist you further.

Please include your invoice / transaction ID. You can contact us directly by using our contact form and selecting Subscriptions as your issue.

If you need assistance recovering your account, we will ask for additional information to verify you are the account owner.

How do I remove/change my payment information?
To update or remove your active payment method, visit your Wallet. Please note that if you have multiple subscriptions under one payment method you will be updating the payment method for those subscriptions too.
Am I able to see a list of my subscription payments?
You may find a list of subscription payments by heading to your Wallet and selecting the Payment History tab at the top. On the Payment History tab you can filter your transactions by date by using the Start and End fields in the top left-hand corner above the table. Clicking Date or Amount at the top of the table will sort the results by the chosen category.

Note: For more information about managing your payment information and viewing your payment history, please see our help article.

My payment was declined, why?
There can be a number of causes for this issue. To troubleshoot, please follow through the list below of steps below:
  • Attempt to remove, then re-add the payment card from your Twitch account and try the purchase again. If you’re paying through a credit/debit card that’s been directly added to Twitch, this can be modified through the Payments page, here. If you’re paying through Amazon Pay or PayPal, you can update the linked payment method through their respective sites.
  • Attempt to contact your credit/debit card issuer to ensure that they’re not blocking transactions from Twitch and indeed that you have a sufficient balance on the card to complete the purchase in its entirety.
  • If you have any other Debit / Credit Cards you could try to use to complete the purchase, it may be worth adding the card and trying to make the purchase again.
  • Some payment providers have limits as to how many purchases you can make within a given amount of time. If you’ve recently made several transactions, try to make the purchase again later.

If you are still having issues after going through all these steps, please get in touch so that we may investigate further for you.

I cancelled my subscription’s recurring payment, so why am I still being charged?
If you have cancelled your subscription’s recurring payment and are still being charged, please get in touch so that we may investigate the issue further for you.

Please include your invoice / transaction ID, your on-site username and the subscription you were charged for. You can contact us directly by using our contact formand selecting Subscriptions as your issue.

What is “JTI*TWITCHTV SUB SRVCS” and why is it showing up on my statement?
“JTI*TWITCHTV SUB SRVCS” is how Twitch charges may appear on your bank statement.

If you are seeing unrecognized / unauthorized charges on your statement please get in touch with us directly so we may assist and investigate further.

We take all unauthorized/unrecognized/fraudulent charges extremely seriously and comply with all legally issued subpoenas.

You can contact us directly by using our contact form and selecting Purchases > Unrecognized / Unauthorized Charges as your issue. Please include any invoice / transaction ID and any additional information which may help us (i.e. the date of the charges and amounts).

How does this work with the Prime free subscription benefit?

Prime is a premium experience on Twitch that is included with an Amazon Prime membership. Your Prime membership comes with a ton of awesome benefits that will power your experience on Twitch, such as an Amazon Prime free channel subscription.

If you’re having trouble accessing your Prime benefits, you may need to link your Amazon and Twitch accounts. See our How to Link Your Amazon and Twitch Accounts guide for help.

More information surrounding Prime can be found here.

How do I upgrade to a higher-priced subscription option?
You can upgrade to a new option by clicking on the Subscribe button, selecting All Paid Tiers, and then picking the price point that you want to support the streamer at.

If you subscribed in the Twitch mobile app (iOS or Android), upgrade your subscription in the app. Mobile upgrades take effect immediately, and you’ll receive a prorated refund or discount toward the new tier. Learn more in Managing Subscription Tiers.

On the Twitch website, we do not currently support the proration (partial-refunds) of subscriptions. That means if you upgrade Tiers on the website before the end of a billing cycle, you will not receive credit for the remaining amount throughout the rest of the billing cycle. If this is a concern, we recommend upgrading at the end of the billing cycle.

How do I downgrade to a lower-priced subscription option?
To downgrade your subscription, first set the existing subscription to Do Not Renew on your Subscriptions page. Once the subscription has expired, you’ll then be able to manually subscribe at a lower tier. If you resubscribe using any payment method within 7 days of your subscription’s expiry, you should not see a break in your sub streak anniversary. Even if you aren’t able to resubscribe within that period, you will NOT lose your loyalty badge progress.
I made a purchase through the Android app. Who handles refunds?
Twitch Support handles all refund requests for purchases made through the Android app or Google Play Store. Contact Twitch Support at this link. Do not contact Google Play support for Twitch purchase refunds. When submitting your request, include your Google Play invoice number from your email receipt (format: GPA.1234-5678-9012-34567).
I made a purchase through the iOS app. Who handles refunds?
Apple handles refund requests for purchases made through the iOS app. Contact Apple support for help with iOS app purchase refunds. For technical issues with subscription benefits (emotes, badges, ad-free viewing), contact Twitch Support.

Refunds on Twitch

Have an issue with a purchase and would like to request a refund? Here’s how you can submit a refund request.

Not all purchases on the Twitch services are refundable. See our Terms of Sale for additional information.

Recurring Subscriptions

Twitch makes certain offerings – for example, channel subs and Turbo – available to users on a subscription basis with recurring payments. You may cancel existing subscriptions up to 24 hours before your Sub Renew Date (which can be viewed on your Subscriptions page) to avoid being charged for the next renewal period. To do so, select the “Do Not Renew” option under your Subscription settings.

We may share reasons subscribers choose to cancel their subscriptions with streamers in an anonymous, aggregated way to help streamers better understand their community.

We may offer limited refunds on purchases of recurring subscriptions. When reviewing refund requests, we primarily look at historical refund requests from purchasers’ accounts and actions taken with respect to those requests. Decisions whether to refund a subscription purchase are solely within Twitch’s discretion.

Outside of the example above, we do not offer refunds for recurring subscriptions (including channel subscriptions and Turbo) except in circumstances where technical issues impact the purchase or benefits relating to a subscription, where the purchase of a subscription was fraudulently made, or where otherwise required by law.

Gift Subscriptions

When you purchase a gift subscription for another user, the recipient will be notified and subscription benefits will become available to them immediately after your purchase is completed. Gift subscriptions are not refundable except where the purchaser experienced a technical issue with the purchase, the purchase was fraudulently made, or where otherwise required by law.

Bits

If Bits are purchased and Cheered, this action cannot be reversed / refunded except for technical issues, suspected fraudulent activity with a particular purchase, or where otherwise mandated by law.

Please see our Terms of Sale for additional information.

Gift Cards

Twitch does not collect retailer purchase information, and cannot process refunds for unredeemed gift cards purchased from third-party retailers. If you have questions about a return or refund for the gift card itself, please contact the retailer where you purchased it. Any refund would be subject to that retailer’s policies.

If you made a purchase on Twitch using your wallet balance funded in whole or in part by a redeemed gift card, the standard refund policies in our Terms of Sales and on this page apply to that purchase. Contact Twitch Support for assistance.

Unauthorized transactions

If you notice suspicious or unrecognized transactions that do not match your regular purchasing history, contact us immediately at this link. Provide as much detail as possible so our Support team can review the incident. We may refund transactions that we determine were made without the user’s authorization, and take appropriate action against the originating account of the unauthorized transaction(s).

As part of the process of investigating your refund request, we may need to ask for information about the payment method(s) used and/or other information to locate the underlying account.

Technical Issue with Purchase

If you experienced a technical issue with completing or receiving your purchase or benefits, please raise a case with us and provide as much detail as possible so our team can assist you. Examples of technical issues include duplicate purchases, specific error messages, missing benefits, or other outages. Please be sure to include any additional information about your issue, including screenshots, error codes, and (if applicable) which Twitch channels are involved.

Abuse of refund policy

Twitch reserves the right to restrict purchase access or suspend accounts that are found to be in violation of our refund policies.

Please see our Community Guidelines, and Terms of Service for additional information.

Submitting a refund request

How you submit a refund request depends on where you made your purchase. First, identify your purchase type by checking your invoice or receipt:

Identifying Your Purchase Type

Your invoice ID format tells you where the purchase was made:

  • Google Play purchases: Invoice IDs begin with “GPA.” followed by groups of numbers and letters separated by dashes (example: GPA.1234-5678-9012-34567)
  • Apple purchases: Invoice IDs are alphanumeric (example: MSXH6MDFH4)
  • Web purchases: Invoice IDs consist of a series of numbers

Your invoice is sent to the email associated with your Twitch account (for web purchases) or your app store account (for mobile purchases). Check your email inbox or spam folder for your receipt.

Purchases Made on Web or Android App

To submit a refund request for purchases made on the Twitch website or through the Twitch Android app, make sure you’re logged into the Twitch Help Portal and visit this link. You may need to select the relevant dropdown entries (e.g., for a recurring subscription refund request, select “Subscriptions” then “Refund Request.”).

Android/Google Play purchases: Twitch Support handles all refund requests for Twitch products purchased through the Android app or Google Play Store. Do not contact Google Play support for Twitch purchase refunds. When submitting your request, include your Google Play invoice number from your email receipt (format: GPA.1234-5678-9012-34567).

Purchases Made on iOS App

If you would like to request a refund for a purchase made through the Twitch iOS app, please contact Apple support for help. Apple handles support matters regarding such purchases directly, and Apple’s refund policy will apply.

Refund Timeline

If a refund is issued, funds will be issued to your original payment method within 10 business days.

Subscriptions on Samsung Smart TVs

Subscribing or gifting subscriptions through the Twitch App on Samsung Smart TVs is simple, in this article we’ll go over how to purchase and gift subscriptions as well as answer some frequently asked questions.

Purchasing a Subscription

To access the Subscription option navigate to the channel in the Twitch App on your Samsung Smart TV. Select the Subscribe button.

If you already have a subscription to the channel Subscribe will be replaced with Gift a Sub.

A QR code will be presented that will need to be scanned on your mobile device.

Once scanned, you will be directed to the subs.twitch.tv for the channel on your mobile device. Select the Subscribe option.

If you are not logged into Twitch on your mobile device you will need to login. Make sure it matches the same account as you are logged into on your Samsung Smart TV.

Follow the on-screen instructions to complete your payment through the payment flow.

Gifting Subscriptions

To gift a subscription on a Samsung Smart TV, navigate to the channel in the Twitch App. Select the Subscribe button.

If you’re already subscribed to the channel, this button will show Gift a Sub instead.

You will be presented with a QR code that will need to be scanned on your mobile device.

Once scanned, you will be directed to the subs.twitch.tv page for the channel via your mobile web browser. Select the Gift a Sub option.

You may now select the subscription tier, amount of gifts, and theme of the gift. You can also select a specific viewer, and don’t forget you can also Gift Anonymously if you prefer.

After selecting the gift tier, theme and whether it’s a gift to a specific viewer or an anonymous gift, proceed to select the number of subscriptions you’d like to gift or enter a customer amount at the bottom and follow the on-screen instructions to complete your payment through the payment flow after clicking the respective price button.

Frequently Asked Questions

I don’t have a Twitch account, can I create one?

If you’d like to create an account you’ll have to visit Twitch.tv on a computer or mobile device. Once created, you’ll be able to login on a Samsung Smart TV with your new account.

I don’t have a Samsung account, do I need one?

You will need a Samsung account to install the Twitch App onto your Samsung Smart TV.

Do I need to have a Twitch account?

You can watch Twitch livestreams on a Samsung Smart TV without an account. You won’t have access to account features, like following a channel or Chat, but you will still be able to watch all of the content.

Will all Samsung Smart TVs have the option to subscribe?

You can subscribe on any Samsung Smart TVs with the Twitch App.

Can I manage my Twitch subscriptions through a Samsung Smart TV?

You cannot manage your subscriptions through your Samsung Smart TV. To manage your Twitch subscription, you can use the desktop or mobile web version of Twitch or the Twitch mobile app . Then, head over to your Subscription page and click on the Cog icon for options to manage your subscription.

How do I report a bug?

Report bugs by filing a Support ticket here.

SUBtember 2026 FAQ

SUBtember is an annual celebration that offers discounts on subscriptions for new or upgrading subscribers, plus some other surprises. This year, SUBtember includes recurring subscription discounts, a mid-month Bonus Bits offer, a Bonus Gift Subs finale, and an exclusive event chat badge to unlock.

Additional Terms and Conditions apply. Check our blog for more information.

Recurring Subscription Discounts

  • 25% off new 1-month subscriptions
  • 25% off new 3-month subscriptions
  • 30% off new 6-month subscriptions

The purchase price of gift subs is not discounted during this event.

Frequently Asked Questions

Before you purchase or upgrade, check your purchase details including the subscription tier, renewal terms, amount, and payment method. This information is not available after you complete check out. Learn more about managing multi-month subs, managing subscription Tiers, and upgrading gift subs.

How long does SUBtember last?
This year, SUBtember has a few components: discounted subs, a mid-month Bonus Bits offer, a Bonus Gift Subs finale, and an exclusive event chat badge to unlock.

SUBtember discounted subs begin August 28, 2026 at 10AM PT / 5PM GMT / 2AM (August 29) JST and conclude October 1, 2026 at 10AM PT / 5PM GMT / 2AM (October 2) JST.

What purchases are eligible for discounts?
You can start a new subscription, upgrade a Prime sub or gift sub, extend your commitment length, and level up your tier to be eligible.

SUBtember 2026 includes purchases of:

  • Upgrading a Prime sub to a 1-month, 3-month, and 6-month recurring sub at any tier

On which platforms are discounted purchases available?

Which subscription purchases are not discounted?
  • Existing recurring subscriptions

How can I tell if my purchase will earn the SUBtember discount?
Before purchase, viewers will see a SUBtember promotional banner under the video player and within the support panel of all monetized channels. During checkout, the SUBtember discount is noted in the price breakdown.
How can I get help with an issue related to SUBtember?
If your answer is not found in this article, please feel free to contact us. When filing a ticket, select Category -> Purchase, Sub-Category -> SUBtember, Detail Category -> I didn’t get the discount.
Who is eligible for SUBtember?
SUBtember discounts are available on all monetized Twitch channels. Monetized streamers do not need to opt in to SUBtember and cannot opt out. SUBtember discounts can be redeemed by any viewer, as long as you have a valid payment method and reside in a country where subscription purchases are allowed.
How can streamers learn more about SUBtember?
Check out tips in our SUBtember Creator Camp.
How long does the discount last?
SUBtember discounts apply to the first term of the subscription (i.e., the first month of a monthly sub, the first 3 months of a 3-month sub, and the first 6 months of a 6-month sub). After that, the subscription renews at the regular price. Outside of SUBtember, we offer 10% off regular price for 3-month subs and 15% off regular price for 6-month subs, which you’ll receive upon renewal.

For example, purchasing a new 1-month subscription to a channel will reduce the price for the first month of the subscription by 25%, and thereafter renewals will be charged at the full price.

Are there any other benefits to SUBtember?
Yes! This year, SUBtember offers a few more surprises, including a mid-month Bonus Bits offer on Custom Power-Ups, a Bonus Gift Subs finale, and an exclusive event chat badge!
I’m not sure I received the correct discount. What do I do?
Before purchase: During checkout, you’ll see the SUBtember discount line noted in the price breakdown of eligible purchases.

After purchase: You’ll see the SUBtember discount line noted in the Twitch invoice that is emailed to you.

If you don’t see the SUBtember discount noted in either of these places, the purchase was not eligible for SUBtember discounts. SUBtember 2026 discounts include:

  • 25% off new 1-month subscriptions
  • 25% off new 3-month subscriptions
  • 30% off new 6-month subscriptions

This includes subscriptions at any tier.

Turbo subscriptions and existing recurring subscriptions are not eligible for SUBtember.

Existing Subscriber FAQ
I recently purchased a new recurring subscription or initiated an upgrade before August 28, 2026. Can I request a refund in order to receive the promotional price?
No, we do not offer retroactive refunds.
I have an active multi-month subscription. Is there any way I can get the SUBtember discount on that channel?
Thanks for supporting our streamers! If your current multi-month subscription’s benefits are set to expire during SUBtember, you can purchase a new sub at the discounted rate after the sub benefits expire. If you have a 3-month subscription, you can upgrade to a 6-month subscription and receive the discount. At any subscription length, you can upgrade to a higher tier subscription and receive the discount.

If your current multi-month subscription will continue through SUBtember, you will not be able to subscribe at the discount on that particular channel. However, you can enjoy discounted new multi-month subscriptions on any monetized channels.

Gift Sub Upgrades FAQ
My gift sub expires during SUBtember. How can I participate in SUBtember?
As long as you purchase the recurring subscription during the promotional period, you’ll qualify for the SUBtember promotional price. Even if your gift sub expires before you continue the subscription, you can subscribe at a discounted rate before October 1, 10AM PT.
I just bought a ton of gift subs for my favorite streamers. Why don’t I see my gift sub badge reflecting this?
As a first step, click here to ensure you have not toggled off Hide Progressive Gifter Badge and Gifts Given Count at twitch.tv/settings/security. You may need to refresh your page. As a streamer, how can I learn more about how gift subs affect my revenue?
You can learn more here.
I tried to purchase a gift sub for an individual user, but the Gift A Sub button is grayed out. Why?
