Are SUBtember Bonus Gift Subs available on purchases to specific viewers?
No, Bonus Gift Subs are available on purchases of community gift subs only. Community gift subs allow you to distribute a bundle of gift subscriptions to a group of people in a channel.
Are SUBtember Bonus Gift Subs available for all subscription Tiers?
Yes. Bonus Gift Subs will match the Tier of qualifying gift subscription purchases.
Is there a limit to how many Bonus Gift Subs I can purchase during SUBtember?
There’s no limit to how many gift subs you can share with the community throughout SUBtember, however the maximum amount of gift subs that can be purchased in a single transaction is 200.
Do SUBtember Bonus Gift Subs work with multi-month gift sub purchases?
No. SUBtember Bonus Gift Subs only apply to single month gift subs, not including 3-, 6-, or 12-month gift subs.
If SUBtember discounts apply to the first term of my subscription, how much will I pay after my SUBtember discount for multi-month subscriptions ends?
Year-round, multi-month discounts are available at the following rates:
  • 3-month multi-month subscriptions save 10% off what a single-month subscription would cost over 3 months.
  • 6-month multi-month subscriptions save 15% off the cost of a single-month subscription over 6 months.

During SUBtember, the deeper discounts of 25% off 3-month and 30% off 6-month apply to the first term only. You’ll receive the regular 10% or 15% discount on subsequent renewals.

Learn more about managing multi-month subs, managing subscription Tiers, and upgrading gift subs.

How does SUBtember impact streamers?
SUBtember encourages even more viewers to support their favorite streamers with discounted prices. Even though viewers pay less for subs during SUBtember, streamers will still get the payout for a full-priced sub.
As an existing subscriber, how can I participate in SUBtember?
Thank you for supporting our streamers! SUBtember 2026 does not include the renewal of recurring subscriptions for existing subscribers. However, upgrading to a higher tier or a longer subscription period will qualify your purchase for SUBtember discounts.

In addition, SUBtember features a Bonus Gift Subs finale from September 25 at 10AM PT until October 1 at 10AM PT.

If my recurring subscription expires in the middle of SUBtember, can I purchase a new subscription at the discounted rate?
Yes. This only applies if you resubscribe during SUBtember after your benefits have fully expired.
How can I tell if my existing subscription or gift sub is going to expire during SUBtember?
Visit Subscription Management to review upcoming renewal and expiration dates, as well as subscription benefits.

Twitch Apps: Mobile & Console Apps

Dual Format Streaming on Twitch

Dual Format Streaming is now available to all streamers on Twitch! Partners and select Affiliates also get server-side transcode support, which takes strain off your PC and helps with smooth stream performance — learn more about what this means and if you are eligible on your Creator Dashboard.

Need help with setup or want to leave feedback? Join the Dual Format Discord group to connect with staff and other streamers who can help!

Dual format streaming allows streamers to broadcast in both horizontal (traditional) and vertical (mobile-optimized) formats at the same time. This feature helps you reach more viewers by delivering an optimized experience regardless of whether they’re watching on web or mobile. With more and more viewers coming to Twitch from their phones, dual format streaming ensures your stream looks its best everywhere.

What is Dual Format Streaming?

As more and more viewers come to Twitch on mobile, optimizing your stream for both web and mobile devices becomes key to reaching and engaging new audiences.

Dual format sends two versions of your broadcast to Twitch at once: a standard horizontal stream and a full-screen vertical stream. Viewers automatically get the right one for their device.

  • Desktop & TV viewers — your usual horizontal stream.
  • Mobile viewers — a full-screen vertical view when holding the phone upright, or the horizontal view when they rotate it. They can tap to switch anytime.

Viewers on mobile will see a new, full-screen vertical view of your stream if they hold the phone vertically, or a full-screen standard horizontal view if they rotate their phone horizontally.

How to Start Dual Format Streaming

Watch this short video to get set up in less than 5 minutes! We’ve also included written instructions below.

Follow these instructions to stream in Dual Format with OBS and Aitum Vertical — the most common setup. Using different software? Click on your software of choice for set up instructions: Meld, Streamlabs, Streamrun, or XSplit. Please note that most modern GPUs (NVIDIA GTX 900+, AMD RX 5500+, or Apple M1+ and more) and systems can handle Dual Format streaming. See detailed system requirements.

  • Download and Install Aitum Vertical Plug In
  • Open OBS and adjust your settings.
    • Go to Settings > Stream > Check the “Enhanced Broadcasting” box under “Multitrack Video.”
    • In the same settings window, set Additional Canvas to Aitum Vertical. If you don’t see this as an option, close and reopen OBS, then try again.
    • [Recommended] In the Aitum Vertical Dock, click the gear icon at the bottom of the panel and uncheck Backtrack runs while streaming/recording. This is optional and helps reduce strain on your PC.
  • Set Up Your Vertical Layouts & Link Your Scenes
    • Enable Vertical Scenes and Vertical Sources in Docks from the top menu
      • Create your vertical scenes — no need to start from scratch. Click the “+” button in the Vertical Sources panel to add your existing scenes, game capture, webcams, and alerts, then customize each for the vertical canvas.
        • Skip chat overlay. Twitch adds chat to the vertical view automatically.
        • Start with 2-3 scenes. You don’t need a vertical version of everything on day 1.
      • Link your vertical and horizontal scenes: In the Vertical Scenes panel, right-click your vertical scene, select Linked Scenes, and choose the desired horizontal scenes to link. Linked scenes switch together, so you don’t have to adjust separately every time you switch. Here’s a detailed video from Aitum on how to set up and link your vertical scenes to your existing horizontal scenes.
    • Preview your vertical layout to confirm your camera, overlays, or alerts fit the vertical frame. See the best practices on safe zones below
  • Press “Start Streaming” to go live in both formats!
  • Pressing Start Streaming in OBS will go live in Dual Format — no need to press the green “Go Live” button in the vertical canvas.

How to know it worked:

  • Run a quick test stream and watch it on your phone in the Twitch mobile app. Ensure all key elements display properly.
  • In Stream Manager on desktop, click the orientation icon next to the gear icon in Stream Preview to see your vertical stream.
  • Check your stream health at inspector.twitch.tv. Learn more about Twitch Inspector.

Best Practices for Setting Up Your Dual Format Stream

The vertical canvas is 1080 × 1920 (9:16). Twitch overlays its own interface (chat and controls) on top of the mobile view, so keep important visuals in the center safe zone.

  • Center your critical visuals (gameplay HUDs, camera, etc) so they read on a phone. Drag and adjust on the canvas to find the right fit or right-click a source and choose “Transform” to fine-tune. See the safe zone and overlay template above.
  • Link your scenes for seamless transitions and switch from the primary (horizontal) scene menu, not the vertical scenes menu.
  • Skip chat overlay for vertical canvas. Twitch adds a chat overlay for your vertical video in mobile automatically.
  • Set up a few layouts for different games and content types. See these live Dual Format streams for inspiration (open on mobile).
  • Monitor stream performance at inspector.twitch.tv. Streaming both formats requires more resources. Watch your CPU/GPU and adjust accordingly.
  • Hitting encoder limits? Lower the maximum bandwidth under Multitrack video (Settings → Stream → Multitrack video), or reduce maximum video tracks to 5 or 4.

Need more help or want to leave feedback? Streamers can get help or share their feedback in the Discord group. Viewers watching dual format streams can share their feedback with us here.

What You Need To Know About Enhanced Broadcasting and Dual Format Performance

Dual Format and 2K streams use Enhanced Broadcasting, which encodes multiple quality variants from your broadcast software. This can put strain on some systems, but most modern GPUs can handle this!

To reduce strain on your system and improve performance, Twitch also provides added server-side transcode support for these streams for Partners and select Affiliates. Added server-side transcode support lets us utilize your GPU to encode the highest-resolution horizontal and vertical streams, while using server-side transcoding to fill in all the lower resolutions.

Added server-side transcode support does two main things:

  • Reduced encode limitations. Transcode support helps offset the high encoder utilization and encoder slot limitations by offloading to server-side transcoding, freeing slots and reducing utilization. Your viewers will now get the full quality ladder for both horizontal and vertical with this approach. Prior to this change, Dual Format vertical streams typically only got 1080 and 360 — viewers will now get 1080 source, 720, 480, 360, 160p. This also applies to the horizontal 16:9 stream as well.
  • Reduced network upload bandwidth requirements. The minimum required upload bandwidth for streamers using Dual Format and 2k with Enhanced Broadcasting was 22.5 Mbps. With the additional transcode support, we can cut this upload bandwidth nearly in half, lowering the requirement to ~14 Mbps for 2K + Dual Format (~9 Mbps for 2K only, ~12.5 Mbps for Dual Format 1080p only).

Ultimately, this results in your viewers getting a higher-quality experience across all formats. Partners and select Affiliates with access to this added server-side support do not have to encode all variants of the stream on their own system, so previous concerns around performance, strain on system, and dropped frames have been addressed. Check your Advanced Broadcast Settings on the Stream Settings page in your Creator Dashboard to see if you have access to added server-side transcode support for Dual Format and 2k streams.

Minimum System Recommendations for Dual Format Streaming

Below are the minimum requirements to get started with dual format streaming. You may need higher requirements if you’re also streaming in 2k, or have additional broadcast activities requiring bandwidth. See the system requirements section for a more detailed look at the system requirements Twitch recommends if you’re streaming in 2k and Dual Format at the same time.

Broadcast Software: OBS Studio 32.0.0 or newer, Streamlabs, Streamrun, XSplit, Meld

Vertical Plugins for OBS: Aitum Vertical latest version or StreamElements

Minimum GPU and Driver Version

  • NVIDIA: GTX 900 Series, GTX 1050 variants, GTX 1060 variants, GTX 1650 variants or newer.
  • AMD Radeon RX 5500 or newer
  • Mac M1 or Newer

Operating System: Windows 10/11 or macOS

Upstream Bandwidth Bitrate: 12.5 Mbps when streaming in 1080p. Test your upload speed at speedtest.net or fast.com.

Maximum Video Tracks: up to 4 tracks when streaming at 1080p or lower. Up to 5 tracks when streaming at 1440p (2k).

Vertical Canvas: 1080x1920 ** Your horizontal 16:9 stream will use your regular settings, while your vertical 9:16 stream will be configured separately in your Broadcast software or via the vertical plugin (typically 720x1280 or 1080x1920).

Not sure how to find information on your system requirements? Check the FAQ.

All Partners have access to added server-side support for Dual Format streams that will help with performance and reduce strain on your system. Not a Partner? Check your Creator Dashboard for the Advanced Broadcast Settings on the Stream Settings page to see if you have access to added server-side transcode support.

  • Will my VODs and Clips be available in Dual Format?
What if I don’t use OBS? Can I still stream in Dual Format?

Most Twitch streamers use OBS with the Aitum Vertical plugin to stream in Dual Format, so we’ve simplified this help article to focus on set up with OBS and Aitum. However, you can also stream in Dual Format using Meld, Streamrun, Streamlabs, or Xsplit (no plugin required).

  • OBS users may follow instructions in this Twitch guide to set up OBS with Aitum Vertical.
  • Streamrun users, click here to get set up.
  • Streamlabs users, click here to get set up.
  • Meld users, click here to get set up.
  • XSplit users, click here to get set up.
  • To use StreamElements plugin with OBS, click here.

Mobile streamers that use cloud OBS and advanced set ups can stream in Dual Format. We are working on adding more Dual Format support for IRL streamers over time.

I need help with setting up my dual format stream. How can I get staff support?
Streamers can get real-time troubleshooting support, tips on vertical layouts, or share feedback by joining the Dual Format Enhanced Broadcasting Discord group. Also check the Troubleshooting section at the bottom of this help article for some simple pointers.
Who has access to dual format streaming?
Dual format streaming is now available to all streamers on Twitch!
Will all of my viewers be able to watch my stream if I stream in dual format?
Yes, all viewers will be able to watch your dual format stream. There are no regional restrictions on dual format streams. Reminder: There are still regional limitations on 2k(1440p) viewing, so streamers using both dual format and 2k should be mindful of these limitations.
Will my viewers know that I’m streaming in Dual Format?
Viewers watching your dual format stream on mobile will be notified that you are streaming in Dual Format and be informed of their option to switch views. They will only see this message once when first seeing a Dual Format stream. Otherwise, they will just see your vertical view by default and can tap the screen to switch between classic split and vertical view at any time.
Do I need to stream at two different resolutions?
Yes. Your horizontal stream will use the base canvas resolution while your vertical stream’s largest resolution is usually configured separately. For example: If using OBS and Aitum, your horizontal stream will use OBS Settings > Video > Base (Canvas) Resolution and Output (Scaled) Resolution (e.g., 1080p or 2K if supported), while your vertical stream’s largest resolution will be configured separately in OBS via the Aitum Vertical plugin (typically 720x1280 or 1080x1920). Enhanced broadcasting will automatically configure the stream resolution, framerate, bitrate, codec, and encoder settings to optimize for horizontal and vertical viewing experiences.
Will my PC be able to handle streaming in both formats?

Dual Format and 2K streams use Enhanced Broadcasting, which encodes multiple quality variants from your broadcast software. This can put strain on some systems, but most modern GPUs can handle this!

To reduce strain on your system and improve performance, Twitch also provides added server-side transcode support for these streams for Partners and select Affiliates. This added server-side transcode support lets us utilize your GPU to encode the highest-resolution horizontal and vertical streams, while using server-side transcoding to fill in all the lower resolutions. Ultimately, this results in your viewers getting a higher-quality experience across all formats.

Check your Advanced Broadcast Settings on the Stream Settings page in your Creator Dashboard to see if you have access to added server-side transcode support for Dual Format and 2k streams.

What is added server-side transcode support?

Dual Format and 2K streams use Enhanced Broadcasting, which encodes multiple quality variants from your broadcast software. To reduce strain on your system and improve performance, Twitch also provides added server-side transcode support for these streams for Partners and select Affiliates. This added server-side transcode support lets us utilize your GPU to encode the highest-resolution horizontal and vertical streams, while using server-side transcoding to fill in all the lower resolutions. Ultimately, this results in your viewers getting a higher-quality experience across all formats.

Check your Advanced Broadcast Settings on the Stream Settings page in your Creator Dashboard to see if you have access to added server-side transcode support for Dual Format and 2k streams.

Does Dual Format streaming always require Enhanced Broadcasting?
Yes. Dual Format streaming always requires using Enhanced Broadcasting, even if you have added server-side transcode support.
How will I know if I qualify for this additional transcode support for Dual Format Streams?

All Partners and select Affiliates will qualify for additional transcode support for Dual Format Streams. Check your Advanced Broadcast Settings on the Stream Settings page in your Creator Dashboard to see if you have access to added server-side transcode support for Dual Format streams.

Please note that this added server-side transcode support is specific to Dual Format and 2k streams that use Enhanced Broadcasting and is entirely separate from transcode support for any other regular stream. Read more about transcode support for regular streams here.

Why can’t everyone have access to added server-side transcode support for Dual Format and 2k Streams?
These resources are limited. We do our best to provide additional server-side transcode support to as many Dual Format and 2k streams as possible. However, not every stream on Twitch will have this added support, and we can only guarantee it for Partners at this time. Check your eligibility status for added transcode support in stream settings.
If I qualify for transcode support, will I benefit from this transcode support on every stream?

Yes, if you qualify for transcode support, you will have the added server-side transcode support on every 2k and/or Dual Format Enhanced Broadcasting stream. It will not be available for regular non-enhanced-broadcasting streams or Enhanced Broadcasting streams that are not in 2k or Dual Format. For those streams, your standard transcode support will apply. Read more about transcode support for regular streams here.

Please note: Twitch may stop providing added transcode support for your 2k or Dual Format streams for select reasons, such as if you are inactive for long periods of time or lose Partner or Affiliate status. You can always check your access to added transcode support for Dual Format and 2k streams in your Stream Settings.

I have additional transcode support but I still experienced performance issues during my stream. Why is that happening?
  • Double check your qualification by visiting your Advanced Broadcast Settings on the Stream Settings page in your Creator Dashboard.
  • Some performance issues may not be related to Enhanced Broadcasting, Dual Format, or 2k and may be caused by temporary issues with your network provider.
I’m a mobile-first or IRL streamer. How do I set up Dual Format on mobile?

If you stream directly from the Twitch mobile app, Dual Format isn’t available yet. You can stream vertically via the app, but your viewers won’t be able to switch to horizontal, and desktop viewers will also see a vertical feed.

However, if you have an advanced mobile cloud setup and meet the Enhanced Broadcasting requirements, you may be able to run Dual Format.

Can I simulcast / multistream when streaming in dual format?
Yes. You can still stream to an existing restreaming service to enable restreaming to other platforms in addition to streaming directly to Twitch with Enhanced Broadcasting.
Will dual format streaming affect my viewers’ ability to chat or support the stream?
No. Viewers can chat, subscribe, gift subs, cheer, and use all standard Twitch engagement features regardless of whether they’re watching your horizontal or vertical stream. Viewers can also adjust chat to show more, less, or no chat by tapping on the screen in vertical view on mobile.
Can I opt out of dual format streaming once I start?
Yes. You can continue streaming in horizontal-only format at any time. If you want to continue using Enhanced Broadcasting for horizontal-only streaming, simply select None for Additional Canvas. Alternatively, you can disable Enhanced Broadcasting altogether by unchecking “Enable Enhanced Broadcasting”.
Will my VODs and Clips be available in Dual Format?
Yes. Please note that the vertical (portrait) format version of your VOD will expire 7 days after your stream, after which the classic horizontal (landscape) format version will be available for the remainder of your existing retention period (60 day retention for Prime, Turbo, and Partners and 14 day retention for Affiliates). Clips from Dual Format streams will be available in both vertical and horizontal formats and will not expire. If you are streaming in both Dual Format and 2k(1440p), please note that the 2k quality version of your VOD will expire 7 days after your stream, after which the 1080p quality version will be available for the remainder of your existing retention period. Clips from 2k streams will be available in 2k quality and will not expire. See more about VOD and Clip storage here.
How do I find out what GPU and driver I have?
On Windows, right click the task bar on the bottom of your screen and open task manager. Click the icon on the left that shows a square with a squiggly line. Then click GPU to see your GPU information at the top of the task manager.
How can I find out which operating system I have?
On Windows, open the start menu and click the Windows button in the bottom-left corner of your screen. Click the Settings icon to open settings, click on “system”, and scroll down to click on “about”. Under “windows specifications” you’ll be able to find the edition and version of your Windows operating system.

Viewers FAQs

  • Can viewers switch between the new vertical view and the classic horizontal view?
  • Can I still watch a vertical stream in full screen when I’m holding my phone horizontally?
  • How can I adjust chat to see more or less of chat on my screen?
Can viewers switch between the new vertical view and the classic horizontal view?
Yes. Viewers watching a dual format stream on mobile will see the vertical stream by default, but they can switch back to the classic split by tapping the video and pressing on the classic split icon on the right of their screen.
Can I still watch a vertical stream in full screen when I’m holding my phone horizontally?
Yes. Viewers can rotate their phone to see the full screen horizontal view for streamers streaming in dual format.
How can I adjust chat to see more or less of chat on my screen?
Viewers can tap on chat to bring up chat controls on the right-hand side of the screen that let you adjust chat to see more, less, or no chat while you watch the stream.

Troubleshooting Dual Format Streaming

We’ve included some common troubleshooting tips here for streamers using OBS and Aitum. You can also reach out to Aitum, OBS, Streamlabs, StreamElements, Streamrun, Meld, or XSplit for more help with your setup.

Join our Discord to get support from Twitch staff and other Dual Format streamers.

Get real-time troubleshooting support and feedback by joining the Discord group.

My vertical stream isn’t appearing on Twitch

For streamers using OBS and Aitum: Ensure you’ve enabled Enhanced Broadcasting and selected “Aitum Vertical” from the Additional Canvas dropdown. Finally, check that the correct Aitum Vertical plugin is installed, enabled, and connected to your Twitch account in OBS.

The vertical stream isn’t using the right layout

Open the Aitum Vertical dock in OBS and confirm that the correct vertical scene is selected. Make sure your sources (camera, gameplay, overlays) are properly arranged within the vertical frame. If needed, create vertical-specific scenes optimized for mobile viewing rather than reusing your horizontal layout.

I’m experiencing high CPU or GPU usage

You can try a few things to help with this:

  • Reduce the maximum bandwidth in your OBS settings under Multitrack video
  • If you’re running into encoder limits from hardware, local recording, or multistreaming issues, you may need to reduce the auto setting for the maximum video tracks down to 5 or 4.
  • Close unnecessary background apps or browser windows while streaming.

To reduce strain on your system and improve performance, Twitch also provides added server-side transcode support for these streams for Partners and select Affiliates. This added server-side transcode support lets us utilize your GPU to encode the highest-resolution horizontal and vertical streams, while using server-side transcoding to fill in all the lower resolutions. Ultimately, this results in your viewers getting a higher-quality experience across all formats. Check your Advanced Broadcast Settings on the Stream Settings page in your Creator Dashboard to see if you have access to added server-side transcode support for Dual Format and 2k streams.

My vertical stream has no audio or mismatched audio
  • Check that the same audio sources (mic, desktop audio) are added and linked to both your horizontal and vertical scenes in OBS.
  • Verify your audio monitoring settings in OBS and ensure they are consistent across scenes.
  • If using virtual audio cables or third-party routing software, confirm it’s correctly assigned to both outputs.
OBS says “failed to connect” for my vertical stream
  • Confirm your internet connection is stable and meets the minimum requirements to support dual output streaming.
  • Ensure you are logged into Twitch within OBS and have selected Aitum Vertical as your additional canvas in settings.
  • Restart OBS and try again. If the issue persists, reinstall the Aitum Vertical plugin.
I don’t see the Aitum Vertical plugin in OBS
  • Verify you are running the latest version of OBS. Older versions may not support the plugin.
  • Verify that you have the correct Aitum plugin link.
  • Reinstall the latest version of the plugin and restart OBS. You can also reach out to Aitum Support or OBS support for more help.

Subscriptions on Mobile

Save 25% by purchasing on our external browser instead of in the Twitch app.

Subscribing or gifting subscriptions through the Twitch iOS and Android Mobile Apps is simple, in this article we’ll go over how to purchase and gift subscriptions as well as answer some frequently asked questions.

Your billing and payment information is private. Only you can see your billing details. Streamers only see your username when you subscribe or make a purchase, unless you purchase gift subscriptions anonymously.

Purchasing a Subscription

When a channel is live, you can find the subscription button below the video player.

If you are already subscribed to the channel the Subscribe button will be replaced with the Gift a Sub button.

Tapping Subscribe will open up a prompt. This prompt will show the subscription tier you’re purchasing, the monthly cost of the subscription, the emotes available as a part of that subscription, and any other benefits offered. You can scroll or swipe to see detailed information about the benefits the creator offers to subscribers.

The Subscribe button is also available on a channel’s profile page, accessible regardless of whether the stream is online or offline.

Android
iOS

You can purchase Tier 1, Tier 2, and Tier 3 subscriptions in the Android and iOS Twitch Mobile Apps. You can also upgrade a mobile subscription to a higher tier in the app. Upgrades take effect immediately, and you’ll receive a prorated refund or discount toward the new tier. You can’t downgrade a mobile subscription to a lower tier. Learn more in Managing Subscription Tiers.

Follow the on-screen instructions to complete your payment through the Google Play or Apple App Store. If it’s available in your region, you can also use your Prime Subscription to subscribe on Android.

At this time, Prime subscriptions are not able to be used to subscribe to a channel on the iOS Twitch Mobile App. However, you can still use Prime subscriptions on your mobile device via subs.twitch.tv in your phone’s internet browser, or you may complete your Prime subscription use from twitch.tv on a desktop.

For more information on using subs.twitch.tv, check out our How to Subscribe article.

Gifting Subscriptions

To gift a subscription on Android or iOS, tap the video player on your chosen channel to access the Subscribe button.

If you are already subscribed to the channel the Subscribe button will be replaced with the Gift a Sub button.

Once you’ve done so, navigate to the Gift tab.

Here, you can choose how many gift subscriptions you’d like to purchase for the community.

If you’d like to purchase a gift subscription for a specific user, you can do so by tapping their name in the chat and selecting Gift A Subscription.

Gifted Subs through the Twitch Mobile App are for single-month, Tier 1 only at this time.

Once you’ve chosen either your gift number or gift recipient, follow the on-screen instructions to complete your purchase.

Multi-month Subscriptions

For more information about multi-month subscriptions check out our Managing Multi-Month Subscriptions article.

By default, subscription renewal is monthly. As long as you have not upgraded or modified your sub recently, you can extend your renewal period to every 3 or 6-months.

For your convenience, you can purchase multiple months of subscriptions in advance for yourself. Multi-month subscriptions offer a discount of 10% off 3-months and 15% off 6-months Tier 1 subscriptions. Your subscription will also renew at the discounted price, too!

Multi-month option is available for both Android and iOS through the Twitch Mobile App. However, multi-month discounts, through the Twitch Mobile App, are only available for iOS.

Managing your Subscriptions

Active subscriptions can be managed through the channel page and your profile. For the best experience, we recommend that you use the Android or iOS Twitch Mobile App to manage your mobile subscriptions instead of the Google Play or Apple App Store Subscription Manager.

Subscriptions purchased through the Twitch mobile app cannot be managed on Twitch’s website (twitch.tv/subscriptions). Use the Twitch mobile app to manage all your mobile subscriptions — including those purchased through Google Play or the Apple App Store.

To view the renewal date of your mobile subscription and your subscription badge on offline channels, tap the Subscribed button on the respective channel. For a live channel, tap the Gift a Sub button underneath their video feed and switch over to the Subscribe tab.

To manage your subscriptions from your profile tap on your profile picture in the top left hand corner of the app to access your profile. There, select Subscriptions.

Android
iOS

Tap on a specific subscription to manage it. From this screen, you’ll be able to cancel your subscription should you choose to do so. You may also choose to disable the benefits of a gift subscription by tapping Disable Gift Benefits under that subscription.

Android
iOS

If you have any active subscriptions via another platform (such as web), you will see them in the Other Subscriptions section. These subscriptions cannot be managed from your Android or iOS device; you’ll need to manage these subscriptions through the web browser at twitch.tv/subscriptions.

Once a subscription is successfully cancelled we’ll let you know what day your benefits will expire. If you didn’t mean to cancel your subscription to a specific channel, don’t worry - you’ll be able to subscribe again once your current subscription expires.

Can’t access your device?

If you’ve lost access to the device you subscribed on and need to cancel, first check where the subscription was originally purchased:

Subscribed on twitch.tv (web or desktop):

You can cancel from any device by visiting twitch.tv/subscriptions in any browser. No mobile device needed.

Subscribed through the Twitch mobile app:

You can manage your subscription from the Twitch app on any Android or iOS device — it does not need to be the same device you originally subscribed on. Simply log in to the Twitch app, tap your Profile, then the Settings icon, then Subscriptions.

If you cannot access the Twitch app at all:

As a last resort, you can cancel through the platform’s web-based subscription tools:

  • Google Play: Visit play.google.com/store/account/subscriptions and sign in with the Google account used for the purchase.
  • Apple: Visit appleid.apple.com, sign in with your Apple Account, and navigate to Subscriptions.

If none of the above options work, contact Twitch Support for assistance.

Getting Help with Mobile Subscriptions

Need help with a subscription purchased through a Twitch mobile app? How you get support depends on which platform your purchase was made:

Twitch Android App (Google Play) Purchases

Contact Twitch Support for all issues with subscriptions purchased through the Twitch Android app, including:

  • Refund requests
  • Technical problems with subscription benefits
  • Billing questions
  • Missing emotes or badges

Twitch Support handles all support requests for Twitch products purchased through the Android app or Google Play Store. Do not contact Google Play support for Twitch purchase issues. When contacting support, include your Google Play invoice number from your email receipt (format: GPA.1234-5678-9012-34567).

iOS App Purchases

For refund requests: Contact Apple support for refund requests for purchases made through the iOS app.

For technical issues: If you’re experiencing problems with subscription benefits (emotes, badges, ad-free viewing), contact Twitch Support.

Frequently Asked Questions

Below we have answered some frequently asked questions regarding subscriptions and subscribing on the Android and iOS Twitch Mobile Apps.

Can I subscribe at Tier 2 or Tier 3 in the Android and iOS Twitch Mobile Apps?
Yes. You can purchase a Tier 1, Tier 2, or Tier 3 subscription in the Android and iOS Twitch Mobile Apps, or upgrade your mobile subscription to a higher tier. In the apps, multi-month subscriptions are available for Tier 1 only. You can also subscribe at any tier, including multi-month options, on your mobile device by going to subs.twitch.tv in your mobile web browser or go directly to the streamer’s subscriptions landing page by visiting:
[twitch.tv](https://www.twitch.tv/subs/STREAMER’S) USERNAME
I am having issues completing a payment on the Android app — what do I do?
If you’re trying to make an in-app purchase but the transaction is declined or the payment won’t go through, try to fix payment issues on Google Play.
I was charged for an Android purchase, but I didn’t get the subscription — help!
If your in-app purchase doesn’t show up, please try these troubleshooting steps.
Why do subscriptions cost more on the Android and iOS apps?
There are costs associated with selling subscriptions within mobile platforms. We want to offer you the option to subscribe in our apps, while preserving the same payout to streamers when you subscribe, and in order to do that, the price has to reflect the added costs. You always have the option to subscribe at desktop prices on your mobile device by going to subs.twitch.tv in your mobile web browser or go directly to the streamer’s subscriptions landing page by visiting:
[twitch.tv](https://www.twitch.tv/subs/STREAMER’S) USERNAME

Payments for subscriptions on Android are processed by the Google Play Store and on iOS are processed by the Apple App Store. As such, additional platform processing fees may be applied to the purchase.

Why am I being charged a different currency in the Android and iOS apps vs. the Twitch website?
We recently rolled out international subscription pricing to make it more affordable to support your favorite Creators all over the world. If you do not see your desired local currency during checkout in the Android or iOS app, please ensure that your payment method attached to your account is locally issued.
I was already able to subscribe on my Android device before. What changed?
Before, Android’s Twitch Mobile App users were able to subscribe through a mobile web browser, but it was not a native mobile app purchase. We wanted to provide our Android users a seamless experience, so we’ve updated the Android’s Twitch Mobile App to include native in-app purchase.

Unfortunately, due to tax reasons, some countries like Canada are not supported with this new integration. If your country is not supported with our new in-app purchase flow, you always have the option to subscribe at desktop prices on your mobile device by going to subs.twitch.tv in your mobile web browser or go directly to the streamer’s subscriptions landing page by visiting:

[twitch.tv](https://www.twitch.tv/subs/STREAMER’S) USERNAME
I was previously able to subscribe on iOS with Sub Tokens, why the change?
We’re replacing Tokens with recurring subscriptions to make it easier and less confusing to subscribe to your favorite creators. Now subscriptions behave the same across all of your devices whether you’re a mobile user or a desktop user.
What happens to my subscriptions if I subscribed on my Android device before in-app purchases became available?
Any recurring subscriptions purchased before the update to the Android’s Twitch Mobile App will continue at their original price at the time of purchase. You can manage your subscriptions at twitch.tv.
What happens to my subscriptions if I subscribed using Tokens before recurring subscriptions were available?
You will continue to be subscribed to channels you’ve already subscribed to using your Tokens until your subscription(s) runs out. At that point in time, you may re-subscribe to that channel using the new, recurring subscription feature.
I accidentally cancelled the wrong subscription, can I reactivate it?
You won’t be able to reactivate your subscription immediately, but don’t worry. You’ll be able to re-subscribe once your current subscription benefits expire. Furthermore if you re-subscribe within 28 days, using any payment method, you won’t see a break in your tenure or subscription notification anniversary.
Can I manage my web subscriptions through mobile?
Web subscriptions must be managed by logging into a web browser and heading to your subscription management page.
How can I tell which subscription is for which channel in the Google Play Store subscription management?
Google Play’s subscription manager does not display specific channel names for Twitch subscriptions, which can make it difficult to identify the correct one. For the best experience, use the Twitch mobile app to manage and cancel your subscriptions — it shows each subscription by channel name.

See Managing your Subscriptions above for step-by-step instructions. If you’ve lost access to your device, see Can’t access your device? for alternative options. If you need further help, contact Twitch Support.

In which countries will I be able to subscribe using Android’s Twitch Mobile App?
Albania, Australia, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, India, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Russian Federation, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Korea, Spain, Sweden, Taiwan, United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, United States of America, Hong Kong, Japan, Brazil, Mexico, Bahrain, Canada, Georgia, Indonesia, Iraq, Kuwait, Liechtenstein, Myanmar, Malaysia, Philippines, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, Thailand, Turkey, South Africa, Rwanda, Gabon, Argentina, Colombia, Chile, Costa Rica
In which countries will I be able to subscribe using iOS Twitch Mobile App?
Afghanistan, Albania, Argentina, Austria, Australia, Belgium, Bulgaria, Brazil, Canada, Switzerland, Chile, China, Costa Rica, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Germany, Denmark, Estonia, Spain, Finland, France, United Kingdom, Greece, Hong Kong, Croatia, Hungary, Indonesia, Ireland, India, Iceland, Italy, Japan, South Korea, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Latvia, Malta, Mexico, Netherlands, Norway, New Zealand, Philippines, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Saudi Arabia, Sweden, Singapore, Slovenia, Slovakia, Thailand, Taiwan, United States, South Africa
Why should iOS users subscribe through mobile web instead of the app?
iOS users can save by subscribing through mobile web instead of the iOS app, while receiving the same subscription benefits.

Watching Twitch on Android Devices

There are two options for you to watch Twitch content on your Android device. You can view live Twitch video directly in your preferred Android browser, or simply by visiting twitch.tv in your mobile browser.

For a tailored mobile viewing experience on Android devices, use the Twitch App, available from the Google Play Store.

Using the Twitch Android App

Once you have downloaded the Twitch Android App, you will need to log in to your existing Twitch account or create a new one.

Having an account will allow you to keep track of all the broadcasters you are following, as well as receive push notifications when they go live.

The App also allows you to view Twitch streams across cellular data and WiFi networks, participate in chat, utilize Airplay or Chromecast to watch your favorite streams on the big screen and so much more.

Following

In the Following tab you will be presented with the Categories you are following, Channels you are following that are currently Live, Recommended Channels, Continue Watching, and a list of the Channels you are following that are not currently streaming.

Discover

Discover will introduce you to channels that are currently live. These are recommended live channels from different categories or types.

Browse

In the Browse tab you will be presented with the games you follow at the top for ease of browsing. Below you find a list of all games ordered by the total number of viewers watching live content for that game.

By default we have started reordering the streams in the browse directory by the language your device is set to. You can turn this off in your app settings.

Esports

Esports is

  • live streams
  • Plus replays
  • and highlights for Esport events as well as ProStreamers streams.

Theatre Mode

Once you enter a stream you will be able to swipe left and right to go to the next or previous stream.

Pulling down on the player will reveal the playlist you are swiping through! It is based on where you started playing the stream from, if you enter the stream through the Overwatch directory you will be able to swipe through all the top Overwatch streams.

Pressing the down arrow on the player will take you to the mini player! From here you can continue watching your favourite streamers while continuing to use the app. To dismiss the mini player you can just swipe it off the screen.

Light and Dark Mode

The Twitch app now supports both a light and dark mode, you can switch between light and dark mode in your app settings!

To toggle between the modes, click on your profile picture in the upper left side of the app.

Find the Account Settings and then Preferences.

Click on Enable Dark Mode to toggle it on or off.

Purchase Bits and Subs

Supporting your favourite streamers has never been easier with our purchase flow for Bits and Subscriptions via the Android app.

Subscription

Subs may be purchased in-app by opening the sub menu. This can be done by clicking the Subscribe in the Stream details. Once you have the sub menu open you’ll find the option for subscribing.

If you don’t see the Stream details under the stream video (i.e only chat) tap on the video to display the stream details.

Bits

Bits may be purchased in-app by opening the Cheer menu. This can be done by clicking the Bits icon in the right side of the text chat field. Once you have the Cheer menu open you may find the Buy Bits button at the bottom past the Cheermotes.

After clicking this button you will be presented with the currently available Bits purchase options. The purchase flow is very similar to many other apps and you will be able to pay with a variety of options supported by Apple Pay.

For any payment issues please reach out to our purchase support team via the help form and select the respective issue for Bits or Subscriptions.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why do Bits cost more in the mobile apps?

There are costs associated with selling items on mobile platforms. We want to offer you the option to buy Bits in our apps, while preserving the same 1 cent per Bit that is paid out to streamers when you Cheer with Bits in their channels, and in order to do that, the price has to reflect the added costs. You always have the option to buy Bits at desktop prices on your mobile device by going to bits.twitch.tv in your mobile web browser.

Twitch Studio

Collaborating With Stream Together

Drop Ins is a Stream Together feature that makes spontaneous collaboration easier than ever. With Drop Ins, you can “knock” on the door of any streamer you follow who is live, and if they’re available, join their stream instantly through a Stream Together session. No need for lengthy planning or scheduling—just seamless, improvisational streaming. This feature lets you control who can request to collaborate, ensuring your streaming experience remains enjoyable and uninterrupted. Whether you want to drop in for a quick chat, plan a Drop-In party with friends, or support smaller streamers, Drop Ins brings the fun and creativity of live collaboration to a new level.

Key Features:

  • ‘Knock’ to request collaborations with other streamers who are live: You can ask to start a spontaneous collaboration from the channel page, your Following list, or the Collaboration Panel in Stream Manager
  • Easily manage incoming requests: You can accept or decline collaboration requests directly from the request notification.
  • Control which streamers you’re open to collaborating with: You decide who can request to collaborate with you through your Favorites settings, your personal list of trusted friends and collaborators. Pause collaboration requests in your settings to temporarily restrict incoming requests if you’re not open to collaborating.
  • Integrated safety features: As with all Twitch collaboration features, you’re protected against harassment with integrated moderation, request cooldowns, reporting, and channel block/ban features.

This article focuses on collaborating live with other streamers and managing these collaborations. To learn more about other features of Stream Together, and how to set it up, check out this article.

Managing Your Collaboration Settings

Collaboration Settings allow you to control who can ask to drop in and collaborate with you. You always have the option to accept or decline incoming requests to join your stream.

Where to Manage your Collaboration Settings

You can manage your Collaboration Settings in the Collaboration Panel in Stream Manager, from your Stream Together call, or with the Settings icon in Shared Chat. If you’re using the default Stream Manager layout, the Collaboration panel has already been added for you.

If you’re using a custom Stream Manager layout, you can find the Collaboration panel and add it to your Stream Manager by clicking the + button and finding Stream Together in the list of Panels.

Collaboration Settings can only be accessed from Desktop.

Understanding Your Collaboration Settings

Permissions: These settings control who can knock and request to collaborate with you when you’re live. At minimum, these permissions can be set to Favorites, though you can choose to expand access to additional networks like Channels you follow, all partners, or all affiliates.

  • Favorites: Your Favorites are your trusted network of friends and collaborators. When you are open to collaborating these streamers can always knock and request to drop in. You can learn more about Favorites in the following section.
  • Channels I Follow (optional): By enabling this option, any channel you follow will be able to knock and ask to drop in.
  • Partners (optional): By enabling this option, any channel with Partner status will be able to knock and ask to drop in.
  • Affiliates (optional): By enabling this option, any channel with Affiliate status will be able to knock and ask to drop in.

Pausing Collaborations: You can pause collaboration requests at any time. When you have paused collaborations, no one will be able to knock and request to collaborate with you. You have the option to pause collaboration requests for 1 hour, or the remainder of the stream.

Build Your Network With Favorites

Favorites are your trusted network of friends and collaborators. When you are open to collaborations, your Favorites can knock and request to collaborate with you, unless you have temporarily paused all incoming collaboration requests using the ‘Pause’ setting.

You can manage your Favorites from your Collaboration Panel in Stream Manager or from the Stream Together Creator Dashboard page.

To add a Favorite, search for their username via the search bar. You can remove a Favorite anytime by clicking the Delete icon next to their username in your list of Favorites.

How to Answer When Collabs Come Knocking

When you are open to collaborations and someone “knocks” to request to join your stream, you will be notified in your Chat and your Collaboration Panel. Knocks also show up in Shared Chat: in the Invites tab, or next to the person on the Manage tab if you’re already in a collaboration. You can manage the collaboration request directly from the notification. Stream Together Moderators cannot accept or decline these requests on your behalf.

When you receive a knock, you have a few ways to manage the incoming request:

  • Accept the collaboration request
    • If you are not already in an active Stream Together call, accepting the request will automatically start a Stream Together session with the person who knocked.
    • If you are already in an ongoing Stream Together session, accepting will add the requester to your existing session.
  • Decline the collaboration request
  • Preview the requester’s channel page before collaborating with them

How to Drop In on a Stream

Drops Ins make it easy to initiate or join collaborations with other live streamers. When a streamer has indicated that they are open to collaborate with you, you will see the “Knock” button enabled directly on their channel page, as well as within your Left Navigation and Collaboration Panel. To request to collaborate with a streamer, click the ‘Knock’ button on any of these surfaces. To start a Shared Chat with them instead, open the drop-down menu next to the Knock button on their channel page and click Invite to Shared Chat. Learn more about Shared Chat. Your request will be sent to the streamer, and they have the option to accept or decline your request.

If they accept, you will be invited to join a Stream Together call with them.

Safety

A number of safety measures are built directly Stream Together collaborations:

  • Reporting: You can report streamers via their channel page or from the Stream Together session. Streamers are responsible for their own actions, you will not be held accountable for the behavior of others, provided you address the behavior appropriately by removing them from your stream and/or reporting it.
  • Cooldowns: To prevent spamming, automatic cooldowns limit the number of times a streamer can knock and request to drop in
  • Banned/Blocked users: Banned and blocked users are never able to request to drop in, regardless of your collaboration settings.

Frequently Asked Questions

I am not interested in collaborating, how do I turn this off?
If you are not interested in collaborating, you can “Pause Requests” in the new Collaboration panel in Stream Manager. You can update this setting at any time before or during your stream.
What happens when I click the ‘Knock’ button?
When you click ‘Knock’ a private request will be sent to the streamer you have selected. They will then be able to preview your stream, accept, or decline.
What happens when I accept a knock?
When you accept a knock, the requesting streamer will be prompted to start an audio-only call with you. You can then choose to add video with a few additional steps detailed here.
What do I need to connect over audio?
Just ensure you have desktop audio capture enabled in your streaming software and call audio will come through the moment you accept an invite and join.
I understand it’s easier than ever to connect with audio, but how do I add video when dropping in?
You can easily add video and show your collaboration on your stream by setting up a browser source. For step by step instructions on getting setup with both video and browser sources check out our help article.
I’m open to collaborating but worried about being interrupted at a bad time, what can I do?
When someone knocks, you can preview the streamer, accept, or decline the request. You can also proactively pause requests within Stream Manager if you know you don’t want to collaborate during a given stream.
I only want my friends to be able to request to collaborate with me, what can I do?
If you want to limit who can knock, you can add specific streamers to your Favorites and set your Permissions to Favorites Only from the new Collaboration panel in Stream Manager.
How can I provide feedback?
We love your feedback! You can give us feedback on collaborating with Stream Together through UserVoice.

Turbo Overview and FAQ

Turbo is a monthly subscription program offered on Twitch.tv. Turbo subscribers receive the following benefits:

  • Ad-free Viewing Across Twitch - Watch your favorite streamers without video or banner ads, except as part of channel sponsorships. You may still see streamer-enabled promotions on channels and Twitch-promoted content on non-channel pages.
  • Expanded Emoticon Set - Choose from 2 additional sets of emoticons. Glitch or monkeys; (you can always change it later).
  • Custom Chat Username Colors - Stand out in chat with a custom username color.
  • Chat Badge - Represent Turbo proudly with an exclusive chat badge.
  • Extended Broadcast Storage - Save your past broadcasts on Twitch for 60 days instead of the standard 7 Days.

On this page:

  • Purchasing Turbo
  • Turbo Benefits
  • Turbo Pricing
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Purchasing Turbo

Purchase Turbo at twitch.tv/turbo or via the Get Ad-Free button in the top-right on twitch.tv

Turbo can also be purchased on mobile devices.

Turbo is a monthly recurring subscription. You can manage your Turbo subscription by visiting your Subscription Management -> Turbo: twitch.tv/subscriptions?tab=turbo

Benefits

Ad-Free Experience across Twitch

With Turbo, you can watch your favorite streams without video or banner ads, except as part of channel sponsorships. You may still see streamer-enabled promotions on channels and Twitch-promoted content on non-channel pages. Plus, Twitch Partners and Affiliates still earn ad revenue from Turbo subscribers who watch their channel.

Exclusive Emoticons and Customizable Chat Colors

Turbo subscribers can set their own custom chat color by toggling a set of 3 sliders. Members also can change basic emoticons from the standard robots to a cool set of purple glitch emotes. At time of purchase, you are presented with these options, and can change at any time by visiting your Turbo settings (users who have also linked their Amazon Prime account will see a combined tab called “Prime”).

Exclusive Turbo Badge

Get recognized! Turbo members get access to the Turbo supercharged Global chat badge.

Expanded VOD Storage

Turbo subscribers have their past broadcasts saved for 60 days, instead of the 14 days for Affiliates or the 7 days for non-monetized channels. For more information about VOD settings, visit our guide: help.twitch.tv/video-on-demand

Pricing

As of May 25th, 2023, the price of Turbo has been adjusted to make it locally appropriate for subscribers across many parts of the globe.

You can review the price and currency for Turbo subscriptions in your region here: link.twitch.tv/TurboPricing

Viewers with existing Turbo subscriptions as of May 25th, 2023 should have received an email from Twitch describing their options.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I purchase Turbo on mobile?
Yes. Turbo is available for purchase on mobile devices. Learn more about subscription prices on mobile here. If you experience an error completing this purchase on mobile, try a different payment method or contact Twitch Support here.
Can I purchase Turbo more than 1 month in advance?
At this time, Turbo may only be purchased as a monthly recurring subscription. If you’d like to buy Turbo months in advance, you may suggest it here: UserVoice.
Can I gift Turbo to someone else?
Yes. You can gift Turbo to another user on web (twitch.tv). You’ll find the Gift Turbo option in the top navigation bar or on the Turbo page. Gifting Turbo is currently available on web only.
How much does Turbo cost?
Turbo is available at locally appropriate prices and currencies in many regions across the globe. If your region does not have local Turbo pricing available, the monthly cost of Turbo will be $11.99 USD/month if purchased on web. To see how Turbo is priced in your region, visit our guide: link.twitch.tv/TurboPricing. Try Turbo for free for 7 days, with valid payment method at time of sign-up.
What happens to my Turbo subscription if I delete my Twitch account?
If you temporarily disable your Twitch account, your recurring channel subscriptions (including Turbo) are set to cancel, and Twitch will not attempt to collect payment. Learn more in our guide here.
As a Turbo subscriber, do I have the same benefits to a channel I would if I directly subscribed to them?
Turbo and channel subscriptions are similar in that they both renew monthly. However, a Turbo subscription primarily allows you to not see most video or banner ads across Twitch. Channel subscriptions offer additional benefits such as access to emotes, badges, and more. A subscription to a particular channel may allow you to not see most video or banner ads on that channel, only if the streamer has enabled Ad-Free Viewing for subscribers.
I want to support my favorite streamers - how does my Turbo subscription impact them?
Turbo subscribers get to watch their favorite streamers without interruptions* from ads, and it’s reasonable to ask what this means for streamers who rely on ad revenue. We built Turbo with this question in mind, and streamers continue to earn revenue from ads that Turbo subscribers miss. For streamers – revenue you receive from Turbo subscribers who watch your channel is reflected in your “Ads” revenue estimate in your payout analytics. Learn more.
Can streamers see how much they earn from Turbo?
Yes, streamers can see how much they earn from Turbo in the Analytics section of their dashboards. As a reminder, streamers earn revenue for missed Turbo ad impressions from viewers in their channels.
How do streamers see Turbo revenue in their dashboard?
Streamers can view Turbo revenue in their Earnings Analytics under “Ads & Twitch Turbo.” Turbo revenue is pro-rated daily (1/30th per day) over the subscription period, providing an accurate day-by-day view of earnings consistent with other revenue types. Learn more.
What does ad-free mean?
With Turbo, you can watch your favorite streamers without video or banner ads, except as part of channel sponsorships. You may still see streamer-enabled promotions on channels and Twitch-promoted content on non-channel pages. If you experience ads while being an active Turbo subscriber outside of these circumstances, the issue can be commonly resolved by disabling third-party extensions or browser add-ons.
  • Have you confirmed that your Turbo subscription has not recently expired? Check if you have access to other Turbo benefits like emote sets or chat badges, or visit twitch.tv/subscriptions -> Turbo Subscriptions
  • Are you using the Twitch video player? Alternate players may not correctly log into your Twitch account to retrieve your Turbo status and ad-free benefits.
  • Try another browser, as some may have ad blockers built in.
If after disabling add-ons and completing the previous step you still require assistance, please contact Twitch Support here and let us know you attempted the steps in this article.
Why are my Turbo settings called Prime Perks?
If you are a Prime member, and also a Turbo subscriber, your Turbo settings and Prime Perks settings will be combined into one page called “Prime.” For more questions on Prime, visit Prime Support.
Why do I see ads despite my active Turbo subscription?
If you see ads despite having an active Turbo subscription, there are a few things you can try:
  • Refresh the page or update the app if you’re using a mobile or desktop app. It may be a temporary issue with fetching your current subscription status.
  • Confirm your Turbo subscription has not recently expired.
  • Check if you are using an alternate Twitch player. Alternate players may not correctly log in to your Twitch account to retrieve your Turbo status.
  • Try to disable any ad blocker you’re using. We believe there may be a conflict with some ad blockers which is causing the issue.
  • Try another browser, as some may have ad blockers built in.
Why am I not able to get the free Turbo sub?
If you already took part in a free Turbo trial, you will not be able to resubscribe to a free trial, unless otherwise indicated in the promotion. If you are unsure whether you had already taken part in a prior promo, you can check on this in your subscription history here: twitch.tv/subscriptions
Why is my gift card not working to purchase Turbo?
If you have a gift card balance in your Wallet, we automatically apply those funds to purchases you make on twitch.tv. If the cost of your purchase exceeds your gift card balance, we will charge the additional amount to your saved payment method. If you do not have a saved payment method then you will be prompted to add one before you can proceed with your purchase.

Twitch Brand Sponsorship Portal Description of Measurement Methodology & Reporting Procedures

This page is intended for brand advertisers and agency partners using the Twitch Brand Sponsorship Portal.

The following includes a general description of Twitch creator sponsorship measurement methodology and reporting procedures for the Twitch Brand Sponsorship Portal.

Standard Reporting

The following standard reporting is provided with every campaign:

  • Brand Name: Name of brand
  • Campaign Level Channel Count: Total participating channels
  • Clickable Impressions: Impressions that included the brand CTA (Channel Skins Impressions)
  • Non-Clickable Impressions: Impressions that did NOT include the brand CTA (e.g., follower promotion, front page, branded chat notices)
  • CTR (Average): Clickthrough rate on clickable assets (clicks/impressions)
  • Unique Viewers: Number of unique viewers who saw the sponsored assets across Twitch
  • Total Hours Watched: Total hours of sponsored assets watched by viewers on the channel during the activation time period
  • Average Minutes Watched per Viewer: Average minutes watched of sponsored assets by viewers on the channel during the activation time period. This does not include any viewing activity on the Twitch front page
  • Total Subscriptions Purchased: Number of subscriptions, both recurring and gift, that were purchased during the campaign
  • Channel Level % Change in Subs Purchased: Overall lift in subscriptions purchased on a sponsored channel by the sponsorship (compared to how many would have sold otherwise) — this is a good indicator for positive brand sentiment

Frequently Asked Questions

How are impressions measured?
Twitch’s sponsorship logic considers whether elements of the creative have loaded before firing the impression pixel. Impression events captured through the pixels are logged within Twitch’s servers and are parsed, processed, and aggregated for further traffic validation, measurement reporting, and billing.
How are clicks measured?
Once the ad is clicked, the measurement pixel fires a request, and asynchronously logs the click as a single event. These click log files are processed, undergo invalid traffic filtration, are filtered for clicks outside the staleness window, and aggregated for advertising reporting.
What are the limitations?
  • Ad Blockers: Ad-blocking software is capable of preventing ad creatives from being rendered. Some front-end ad blockers that disable images, JavaScript, HTML5 elements, and/or Flash are capable of preventing ads from being displayed. When these situations occur, there’s no impression served, and corresponding clicks can’t be generated nor counted.
  • JavaScript disabled: For Safeframe, ads won’t render and instrumentation (impressions, viewability, measurability) won’t fire. For light ads, depending on the placement ads may or may not render, but instrumentation won’t fire.
  • Images disabled: Whether an ad renders or not depends on the creative (whether it has images). Instrumentation won’t fire as image requests are generally blocked and Twitch’s impression measurement methodology wouldn’t detect images.
  • document.visibilityState not supported: Would result in no impression events fired.
How is traffic validated?
  • Matchmaking fraud filtering: Channel traffic validity is factored into the suitability filtering within the matchmaking tool for each creator.
  • Post-campaign fraud filtering: For view-based payouts, view counts undergo supply quality filtering before final counts are calculated.

Twitch X (Twitter) “@TwitchSupport” FAQ

The Twitch Support Twitter account is currently monitored Monday through Friday between 10am and 6pm Pacific Standard Time for trending technical issues within the community. This account is used to communicate known site issues, announce new products and features, and educate the community on Twitch-specific topics.

Twitch Support on Twitter is not a substitute for ticket support. While we may offer troubleshooting advice from time to time, actual account issues, especially anything requiring personal information to verify or discuss, will require a support request through the Twitch Help site.

Other knowledgeable and experienced Twitch users sometimes reply to questions and provide support to those who tweet at @TwitchSupport. Note that while these individuals may provide the general community with answers to common questions, they do not speak for or represent Twitch officially.

On this page:

  • Issues we cannot assist with via Twitter
  • Moderation Concerns
  • Other Official Twitch Twitter accounts

Issues we cannot assist with via Twitter

  • Suspension Appeals
  • Questions or concerns about enforcement actions taken on an account
  • Inquiries on how long a submission will take (appeals, Partnership applications, Affiliate tax review, emote submissions, existing support tickets)
  • Account access, including 2FA (managed by Authy)
  • Payout inquiries
  • Prime (managed by Amazon)
  • Purchases

Moderation Concerns

Twitch Support only monitors and assists with troubleshooting technical issues specific to the user who contacts us on Twitter. We cannot comment on or assist with suspension appeals, calls for banning users, or any direct harassment you or another user may be receiving. If you feel a user is breaking the Twitch Community Guidelines, please use the on site reporting tool located on the user’s channel page, or within the whisper box to report the user to the Safety Operations team for review. If you have feedback in regards to our Community Guidelines or safety operations, please voice those concerns on our feedback forum, Uservoice.

For suspension appeals, please go here and log in with the suspended account.

Safety Operations does not accept appeals on another user’s behalf.

If you are unable to login to appeal your suspension, you will need to recover your account through Support’s account recovery options first, selecting Account/Login Issues > Logging In > I have forgotten my password.
